title: Assam To Get 3 Data Centres, Bharti Airtel Signs Deal With State Government
description: The Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) was signed at Lok Sewa Bhawan in Guwahati in the presence of Chief Minister Himanta Biswa Sarma, Bharti Airtel Chairman Rajan Bharti Mittal, state ministers and senior government officials.
author: Ratnadip Choudhury
content:
Assam will get three data centres after the state government and Bharti Airtel signed an agreement on Wednesday, in a move to strengthen the state's digital infrastructure and attract fresh investment.
The Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) was signed at Lok Sewa Bhawan in Guwahati in the presence of Chief Minister Himanta Biswa Sarma, Bharti Airtel Chairman Rajan Bharti Mittal, state ministers and senior government officials.
Speaking at the event, Mittal said the proposed data centres would bring data storage facilities closer to consumers in the region and help reduce dependence on infrastructure located outside the state.
"The data centres will bring data storage closer to customers and help localise data within the state," he said.
Mittal also spoke about Airtel's plans to expand its 5G network and fibre-optic connectivity across Assam. He said the expansion of the company's network, along with the proposed facilities, would create employment opportunities, both directly and indirectly.
He pointed out that better connectivity could make a difference in the delivery of essential services, particularly in areas where access to healthcare, education and government services remains a challenge.
Chief Minister Himanta Biswa Sarma said the agreement was part of Assam's efforts to build a stronger presence in India's growing technology sector.
Referring to the changing nature of infrastructure, Sarma said digital connectivity and data management had become increasingly important, alongside conventional infrastructure such as roads, bridges, railways and electricity. He also referred to the growing demand for data centres with the expansion of artificial intelligence, cloud computing and other technology-driven services.
Big news for Assam's tech story! We just signed an MoU with @airtelnews for two new Data Centres, one in Jorhat and one in Silchar. Add the one coming up in Guwahati, and that's 40 MW of capacity and ₹705 crore of investment for Assam's digital future. Now, I know the world is busy debating data centres. But here's why Assam needs them 👉 Your data stays closer to home 👉 Apps and online services get faster across the Northeast 👉 Three locations mean there's always a backup 👉 And it's exactly what digital-first companies look for before they invest The best part? More jobs for our youth and smoother digital services for everyone.
— Himanta Biswa Sarma (@himantabiswa) November 25, 2026
The Chief Minister said Assam should not remain merely a consumer of digital services but should also participate in the development of India's expanding digital economy.
Sarma cited Assam's geographical location, connectivity, existing infrastructure and skilled workforce as factors that could help the state attract further investment in the sector.
The agreement with Bharti Airtel marks another step in Assam's push to attract technology-related investments, with the proposed facilities expected to support the growing demand for data storage and digital services in the Northeast.

title: Allahabad High Court Quashes Uttar Pradesh APO Prelims Result, Orders Fresh Mains
description: The Allahabad High Court held that the Uttar Pradesh Public Service Commission (UPPSC) lacked the legislative competence to issue such a policy directive.
author: Press Trust Of India
content:
The Allahabad High Court on Wednesday quashed the preliminary examination result for the 2025 Assistant Prosecution Officer recruitment, ruling that meritorious candidates from reserved categories cannot be excluded from the open category at any stage of the selection process. The court held that the Uttar Pradesh Public Service Commission (UPPSC) lacked the legislative competence to issue such a policy directive.
The ruling emphasised that the "open/unreserved category" is accessible to all candidates based on merit at every stage of recruitment and should not be regarded as exclusive to general category candidates.
The court directed the commission to conduct the mains again based on revised preliminary examination results and to proceed with the selection process accordingly. This order followed a writ petition filed by Pankaj Verma and two others.
Justice Manish Kumar Nigam also struck down the commission's Office Memorandum (OM) dated January 9, 2020, which restricted the adjustment of meritorious reserved category candidates into the unreserved pool solely to the final selection stage.
"An open/general category is open to all and is not reserved only for general category candidates. If a reserved category candidate, even though he has obtained more marks than the cut-off marks of the general category candidate, is excluded and ousted from the process of selection at the stage merely for the reason that he belongs to a reserved category. In my considered opinion, it would be the worst form of discrimination wholly impermissible under Articles 14 and 16 of the Constitution," Justice Nigam observed.
The recruitment drive was initiated on September 16, 2025, for 182 APO posts, comprising 27 unreserved, 67 Scheduled Caste (SC), 9 Scheduled Tribe (ST), 61 Other Backward Classes (OBC), and 18 Economically Weaker Sections (EWS) vacancies.
Following the preliminary test on March 22, 2026, the UPPSC declared the result on April 30, 2026, shortlisting 2,856 candidates (15 times the number of advertised posts) for the mains held between June 28 and June 30, 2026.
While interviews were ongoing in October, the high court, through an interim order on September 28, 2026, stayed the declaration of the final results.
During the proceedings, supplementary affidavits filed by the commission revealed that 321 OBC candidates and 43 SC candidates had secured higher marks than the last shortlisted candidate in the unreserved category in the preliminary examination.
However, citing its January 9, 2020, OM, the UPPSC restricted all 364 high-scoring candidates to their respective reserved category lists instead of placing them in the open pool. This action prevented an equal number of reserved-category aspirants ranked lower from qualifying for the mains.
According to the petitioners, treating the unreserved list as an exclusive preserve for non-reserved applicants converted the open pool into a form of "communal reservation", violating Articles 14 and 16 of the Constitution and Section 3(6) of the UP Public Services (Reservation for SCs, STs and OBCs) Act, 1994.

title: UGC-NET December 2026 City Intimation Slip Out, Download Link Here, Exam From December 14
description: UGC-NET December 2026: The examination will be conducted in Computer-Based Test (CBT) mode from December 14 to 18 and on December 21, 2026.
author: Rahul Kumar
content:
UGC-NET December 2026: The National Testing Agency (NTA) has released the examination city intimation slip for the University Grants Commission-National Eligibility Test (UGC-NET) December 2026 session. Candidates can now check their allotted examination city and download their city intimation slip from the official website, ugcnet.nta.nic.in.
The NTA will conduct the UGC-NET December 2026 examination in Computer-Based Test (CBT) mode from December 14 to 18 and on December 21, 2026. The examination will be conducted in two shifts, from 9am to 12pm and 3pm to 6pm. The examination will be of 180 minutes (three hours), with no break between Paper 1 and Paper 2.
UGC-NET is conducted to assess the eligibility of Indian nationals for the award of Junior Research Fellowship and appointment as Assistant Professor; appointment as Assistant Professor and admission to PhD; and admission to PhD only in Indian universities and colleges.
Pattern Of Examination
The test paper will comprise two sections, both consisting of objective-type, multiple-choice questions. The medium of the question paper will be English and Hindi only, except for language papers.
Marking Scheme
- Candidates must choose one option as the correct answer.
- Each question carries two marks.
- Candidates will be awarded two marks for each correct response.
- There will be no negative marking for incorrect responses.
- Questions answered or attempted will be evaluated irrespective of whether they are marked for review.
- Questions that are unanswered or unattempted will not be evaluated, irrespective of whether they are marked for review.
The information bulletin states that while every effort will be made to ensure that each question has only one unique answer, if a question is found to have more than one correct option, it will be dealt with in the following manner:
a) If more than one option is found to be correct, two marks (+2) will be awarded only to candidates who have marked any of the correct options.
b) If all options are found to be correct, two marks (+2) will be awarded to all candidates who have attempted the question.
c) If none of the options is found to be correct, or a question is found to be wrong or dropped, two marks (+2) will be awarded only to candidates who have attempted the question. This could be due to a human or technical error.
Since there is no negative marking, candidates should choose the most appropriate option as the correct answer.
Candidates facing difficulty in downloading the examination city intimation slips are advised to contact the NTA Helpdesk at 011-40759000 or email ugcnet@nta.ac.in.

title: 'Zero tolerance for terrorism': EAM Jaishankar remembers 26/11 victims on attack anniversary
description: NEW DELHI: External affairs minister S Jaishankar on Thursday paid tribute to the victims of the 26/11 Mumbai terror attacks, remembering the innocent
author: Abhishek Mishra
content:
NEW DELHI: External affairs minister S Jaishankar on Thursday paid tribute to the victims of the 26/11 Mumbai terror attacks, remembering the innocent lives lost and the security personnel who made the supreme sacrifice while fighting the terrorists.Marking 18 years since the attacks that shook the country, Jaishankar reiterated India's commitment to combating terrorism in all its forms and bringing those responsible to justice."Remember innocent lives lost & salute the brave security personnel who made the supreme sacrifice during 26/11 Mumbai terror attacks. Committed to combating terrorism in all its forms & manifestations and bringing those involved to justice. Zero tolerance for terrorism," Jaishankar wrote in a post on X.
This year marks 18 years since 10 Pakistan-backed Lashkar-e-Taiba (LeT) terrorists launched a series of coordinated attacks across Mumbai, targeting some of the city's busiest locations.Commonly known as 26/11, the attacks began on the night of November 26, 2008, when the terrorists entered Mumbai by sea. Over the next four days, they carried out strikes at several locations, killing 166 people and injuring around 300.
Among the targets were the Taj Mahal Palace Hotel, the Oberoi-Trident Hotel, Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj Terminus, Nariman House, Cama Hospital, Metro Cinema and Leopold Cafe. Several of these locations were frequented by foreign nationals and Mumbai's workforce.
The attacks left a lasting impact on the city, with the memories of the siege continuing to haunt survivors and families of those killed. Bullet marks at Leopold Cafe and Nariman House, along with memorials honouring the security personnel who lost their lives, remain reminders of the tragedy.Nine of the 10 terrorists were killed during the security operation, while the lone surviving attacker, Pakistani national Mohammad Ajmal Amir Kasab, was captured. Assistant Sub-Inspector Tukaram Omble played a crucial role in apprehending Kasab before succumbing to his injuries.Kasab was sentenced to death in May 2010 and hanged at Yerawada Central Prison in Pune on November 21, 2012.
Abhishek Mishra is a Digital Content Producer at The Times of India, working with the news desk. He writes with a keen eye on foreign policy, defence developments, and the shifting currents of geopolitics-and yes, Indian politics always finds a way onto his radar too.

title: Thirupparankundram Deepam row: Tamil Nadu governor Rajendra Arlekar seeks explanation from TVK govt
description: NEW DELHI: Tamil Nadu governor Rajendra Vishwanath Arlekar has sought an explanation from the TVK government over the alleged non-compliance with a
author: Abhishek Mishra
content:
Tamil Nadu Governor seeks explanation from TVK govt
NEW DELHI: Tamil Nadu governor Rajendra Vishwanath Arlekar has sought an explanation from the TVK government over the alleged non-compliance with a Supreme Court directive to light the traditional Karthigai Deepam at a stone pillar atop the Thirupparankundram hill in Madurai, official sources cited by news agency PTI.The governor has written to the Vijay-led government seeking an official account of the matter, including details of the specific police instructions issued and followed on the ground, the sources told PTI.The Karthigai Deepam was lit on Tuesday at the customary Deepa Mandapam near the Uchi Pillayar Temple, instead of the stone pillar on the hill, where the Supreme Court had earlier directed that the lamp be lit on a one-time basis.
The Supreme Court on Wednesday said it would hear, in a day or two, applications seeking directions for lighting the traditional lamp at the stone pillar.A bench of Justices Aravind Kumar and Vipul M Pancholi said the registry would verify the filing of the applications, including contempt petitions, and examine whether they could be listed for hearing on Thursday or Friday.Hours after the lamp was lit at the customary location on Tuesday, bypassing the court-directed spot, the temple's Board of Trustees defended the decision, asserting that long-standing religious traditions must take precedence.However, the temple priests, known as Sthanikars, distanced themselves from the Board's decision.

title: ‘Could be something good’: NCP (SP) leader Supriya Sule strikes softer tone on delimitation Bill
description: NEW DELHI: NCP (SP) national working president Supriya Sule struck a softer tone on the Centre's proposed delimitation Bill, saying it would be premature
author: Abhishek Mishra
content:
NEW DELHI: NCP (SP) national working president Supriya Sule struck a softer tone on the Centre's proposed delimitation Bill, saying it would be premature to oppose the legislation before its details are known.Her comments come amid broader opposition resistance to the NDA government's push for delimitation."Let the bill come. Perhaps there could be something good in the Delimitation Bill," she told news agency PTI."Whether a bill is in the country's interest or not, opposing it just because you are in the opposition, or blindly supporting it because you are in power, is wrong for a healthy democracy. It is not necessary to oppose everything. We can also suggest improvements and say what changes should be made. There could be something good in it," Sule said.
The NCP (SP) leader added that her party would discuss the legislation once it was introduced and support it if it served the country's interests.Her remarks on the Bill come at a time of heightened speculation over the possibility of Sharad Pawar's Nationalist Congress Party faction moving closer to the BJP-led NDA, triggering political chatter about a possible realignment in Maharashtra.
Sule, however, sought to brush aside speculation about her party joining the ruling alliance or her getting a ministerial berth at the Centre or the Maharashtra chief minister's post, dismissing the claims as "gossip".Speaking to reporters in Karad on Wednesday, she said such speculation had followed her for years.
"For the last 12 years, I have been taking an oath as a minister. Don’t do this injustice to me. Since 2014, I have been made a minister," Sule told reporters.
Sule rules out merger speculation after Ajit Pawar's death
Meanwhile, speculation about a possible merger between the two NCP factions led by Sharad Pawar and his nephew Ajit Pawar has also resurfaced.Sule had earlier said that the possibility of a merger had ended with the death of her cousin Ajit Pawar in an air crash. The two factions had been at the centre of discussions over a possible political reunion before his death.

title: Constitution Day LIVE updates: Priceless heritage of Indian democracy, says PM Modi
description: Follow The Hindu LIVE for the latest updates on Constitution Day as Prime Minister Narendra Modi says the Constitution is a priceless heritage of Indian democracy, while the Congress will hold ‘Samvidhan Raksha’ marches across the country as part of its campaign against alleged electoral roll manipulation.
author: The Hindu Bureau
content:
- November 26, 2026 09:48CJP leaders visit Deekshabhoomi ahead of ‘Save Democracy, Save Constitution’ rally Ahead of their ‘Save Democracy, Save Constitution’ rally in Nagpur, Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) founder Abhijeet Dipke and co-convenor Ashutosh Ranka visited Deekshabhoomi in Nagpur on Thursday (November 26, 2026). Speaking to the media after visiting Deekshabhoomi, Dipke said, “Today is a very holy day for everyone in the country because, on this day, Dr Babasaheb Ambedkar gave us the Constitution, on which our country is running and moving forward.” Dipke said he wanted to begin the day by paying his respects to Dr Babasaheb Ambedkar at Deekshabhoomi on this sacred occasion. Deekshabhoomi is a Buddhist monument and pilgrimage site in Nagpur, commemorating the conversion of Ambedkar and hundreds of thousands of his followers to Buddhism on October 14, 1956. The CJP leader said that they would participate in the ‘Save Democracy, Save Constitution’ rally at 4 pm, which would also be attended by Ranka and actor Prakash Raj. -- PTI
- November 26, 2026 09:45The systematic erosion of political equality in India On November 26, 2026, India marks 77 years since the Constituent Assembly adopted the Constitution in 1949. That founding charter made a bold promise for a poor, deeply stratified country emerging from colonial rule. Every adult citizen, regardless of property, caste, gender, or creed, would stand equal at the ballot box. Today, that core principle of political democracy, which B.R. Ambedkar placed at the heart of the Republic, is being systematically erased in practice.
- November 26, 2026 09:45Take constitutional patriotism to the people Every November 26, on Constitution Day in India, a striking visual emerges on the political landscape. Opposition leaders, civil rights activists, and citizens step into the public space clutching pocket-sized editions of the Constitution of India — often bound in bright red. Waving these slender volumes is a powerful symbolic gesture that signals a collective resolve to defend the Republic against majoritarian consolidation and the erosion of democratic norms.
- November 26, 2026 09:44Constitution is an inseparable part of our life journeys On November 26, 1949, the Constituent Assembly adopted our Constitution. Today, we remember Dr. Rajendra Prasad, Dr. Babasaheb Ambedkar, and every member of the Constituent Assembly. Their greatness lay in drawing extensively from the rich traditions and civilisational wisdom of Bharat while framing a modern Constitution. For a nation as diverse as Bharat, with its numerous faiths, languages, customs, and schools of thought, it is important that the Constitution has a resonance far beyond the precincts of Parliament and the courts. Our endeavour has been to deepen its connect with the collective consciousness of our people, especially our youth and strengthen the spirit of unity essential to India’s bright future. That is why over a decade ago, our government decided to mark November 26 as Constitution Day.
- November 26, 2026 09:42Why is November 26 celebrated as Constitution Day in India Constitution Day, also known as Samvidhan Diwas, is observed every year on November 26 to commemorate the adoption of the Constitution of India in 1949 by the Constituent Assembly. The Constitution came into force on January 26, 1950, two months later, making India a republic. However, November 26 is celebrated as the Constitution Day to commemorate the moment the Constitution of India was formally adopted for “We, the People of India”.
- November 26, 2026 09:38Constitution is a strong and living document, says former President Ram Nath Kovind
- November 26, 2026 09:37We should pledge to uphold for a stronger, united nation: Sonia Gandhi
- November 26, 2026 09:36Let us carry values forward in action as we strive for a Viksit Bharat, says Arjun Modhwadia
- November 26, 2026 09:35Government is working relentlessly to realize the aspirations and vision of Babasaheb Ambedkar, says Kumaraswamy
- November 26, 2026 09:32Govt.’s endeavour has been to deepen Constitution’s connect with people, strengthen unity: PM Modi Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Thursday (November 26, 2026) highlighted the Constitution’s role in strengthening democracy and promoting social and economic justice, while outlining his government’s achievements through welfare schemes and constitutional amendments. He said collective efforts guided by “India First” thinking, duties in action and constitutional values would realise Viksit Bharat by 2047.
- November 26, 2026 09:31Constitution a living, sacred document that safeguards citizens’ rights: Himanta Assam Chief Minister Himanta Biswa Sarma on Thursday (November 26, 2026) said the Constitution is not merely a legal framework but a “living sacred document” that safeguards justice, liberty, equality and fraternity for every citizen. In a social media post on the occasion of Constitution Day, Sarma recalled the contributions of the members of the Constituent Assembly who laid the foundation of the country’s vibrant democracy. The Constitution empowers institutions, guarantees fundamental rights and reminds citizens of their duties towards nation-building, he said. “As we march forward in this Amrit Kaal, let us reaffirm our collective commitment to upholding constitutional values, strengthening the nation’s unity and serving the motherland with an unwavering dedication,” he added. -- PTI
- November 26, 2026 09:28Constitution of India is our pride, says Prakash Ambedkar
- November 26, 2026 09:27J&K Lieutenant Governor calls for commitment to constitutional values Jammu and Kashmir Lieutenant Governor Manoj Sinha on Thursday (November 26, 2026) greeted the people on Constitution Day, reaffirming the importance of upholding the constitutional values of justice, liberty, equality and fraternity. In a message posted on X, Mr Sinha said the Constitution stands as the supreme guiding light of India’s democracy and enshrines its timeless values. “Greetings on Constitution Day. Our Constitution stands as the supreme guiding light of our democracy, enshrining the timeless values of justice, liberty, equality and fraternity,” he said. He called upon people to reaffirm their commitment to upholding these ideals and fulfilling their fundamental duties to build a stronger and Viksit Bharat. -- PTI
- November 26, 2026 09:26Priceless heritage of Indian democracy: PM Modi Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Thursday (November 26, 2026) greeted all fellow citizens on the occasion of Constitution Day and said the Constitution is a priceless heritage of Indian democracy, one that will continue to guide in realising the resolve of a developed India. Mr. Modi also said that it is a day to pay homage to the makers of the Constitution and an occasion to reaffirm the commitment to strengthening the values enshrined in it. “Warmest greetings on Constitution Day to all fellow citizens,” he said in a social media post. -- PTI
- November 26, 2026 09:25Country could face a ‘blood revolution’ unless the Constitution is saved: Prakash Ambedkar Vanchit Bahujan Aghadi (VBA) chief Prakash Ambedkar on Wednesday (November 25, 2026) warned that the country could face a “blood revolution” unless the Constitution is saved and people are allowed to choose their own representatives. Speaking at the Samvidhan Samman Sabha, held ahead of Constitution Day, Mr. Ambedkar said it is “unfortunate” that the ideals of the Constitution were under threat as Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh (RSS) and the BJP is doing everything to be in power.

title: Supreme Court issues notice on bail pleas by Umar Khalid, Sharjeel Imam in 2020 Delhi riots case
description: SC notices bail pleas of Umar Khalid, Sharjeel Imam in UAPA Delhi riots case; hearing on interim bail after protected-witness issue.
author: Aaratrika Bhaumik
content:
The Supreme Court issued notice on Wednesday (November 25, 2026) on the bail pleas of former JNU scholar Umar Khalid and activist Sharjeel Imam, accused in the larger conspiracy case linked to the 2020 Delhi riots. The court, however, declined to take up their pleas for interim relief, saying a three-judge Bench would be set up to decide whether prolonged incarceration and delay in trial can override stringent bail curbs imposed by the Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act (UAPA), 1967.
A Bench comprising Chief Justice of India (CJI) Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V. Mohana sought the Delhi Police’s response to the bail pleas by December 14. It also directed the Registry to place the matter before the CJI on the administrative side for the constitution of a larger Bench in light of the court’s May 22 judgment in Tasleem Ahmed v. State Government of NCT of Delhi.
“Issue notice, returnable on 14.12.2026. The Registry is directed to put up the matter before Hon’ble the Chief Justice of India, on the administrative side, for constitution of a three-Judge Bench in light of the judgment dated 22.05.2026,” the Bench said.
The May 22 reference arose from divergent interpretations by coordinate Benches of the law governing bail under the UAPA. In its January 5 verdict, a Division Bench comprising Justices Aravind Kumar and P.B. Varale had granted bail to five other accused in the case but denied relief to Mr. Khalid and Mr. Imam on the ground that the roles attributed to them stood on a “qualitatively different footing”. The court permitted them to renew their bail pleas after a year or upon completion of the examination of protected witnesses, whichever was earlier.
Subsequently, on May 18, a Bench comprising Justices B. V. Nagarathna and Ujjal Bhuyan, while granting bail to an accused in a narco-terrorism case, expressed reservations about the January 5 judgment, observing that it had failed to correctly apply the binding principles laid down in the court’s 2021 ruling in Union of India v. K. A. Najeeb. In Najeeb, the court had held that the stringent bail embargo under Section 43D(5) of the UAPA could “melt down” where prolonged incarceration and delay in trial infringed an accused’s fundamental rights.
Following this, Justices Kumar and Varale referred the matter to the CJI on May 22 for the constitution of a larger Bench to ensure “parity and consistency” in the application of binding precedents by coordinate Benches. The Bench, however, granted six months’ interim bail to Tasleem Ahmed and Abdul Khalid Saifi, two other accused in the conspiracy case, observing that they “cannot be made to suffer” merely because a question of law awaited authoritative settlement.
Also read | The continued custody in Delhi Riots cases is an injustice
‘Conflicting interpretations’
At the outset of Wednesday’s hearing, senior advocates Kapil Sibal and Siddhartha Dave, appearing for Mr. Khalid and Mr. Imam, respectively, urged the court to consider their pleas for interim bail, pointing out that both had been in custody for over six years. Mr. Dave argued that the prayer for interim relief was distinct from the larger question of law referred to the CJI on May 22.
“Only the main matter on the legal issue is under reference. Let the issue of interim come up for hearing,” Mr. Sibal submitted, seeking an early hearing.
The CJI, however, said he would have to first examine the conflicting interpretations of the Najeeb ruling, which he had authored.
“…in the light of the conflict of observation, I have to apply my mind. It was my judgment (Najeeb case) which is being discussed. So, I am feeling a little embarrassed. One bench says Najeeb means this; another bench says it does not mean… I am being told what I have said,” the CJI remarked.
Solicitor General Tushar Mehta, representing the Delhi Police, pointed out that the May 22 reference had arisen from bail proceedings involving other accused in the same conspiracy case.
‘Unjustified delay’
The two activists have challenged a September 30 ruling of the Delhi High Court rejecting their fresh bail pleas, contending that the case remains at the stage of framing of charges and that the trial is yet to commence.
A Division Bench of the High Court had held that judicial discipline prevented it from modifying the conditions imposed by the Supreme Court in its January 5 judgment.
“These two conditions would show that the specific liberty is clear and conditional, and this Court would not be in a position to modify the condition,” a Bench comprising Justices Prathiba M. Singh and Dinesh Bhatt had said.
In his petition filed through advocate Fauzia Shakil, Mr. Imam pointed out that despite his incarceration for over six years, not one of the more than 900 prosecution witnesses named in the case had been examined. Of these, 47 are protected witnesses.
Given the pace of proceedings, he contended, “On no fair assessment can examination of protected witnesses be expected to commence, much less to conclude, before January 5, 2027, or for a considerable period thereafter.”
Mr. Imam further argued that his continued detention had ceased to serve a procedural purpose and had become “punitive by reason of unreasonable and unjustified delay”.
Of the 18 accused in the conspiracy case, five, including Mr. Khalid and Mr. Imam, remain in custody. Gulfisha Fatima, Meeran Haider, Shifa Ur Rehman, Mohammad Saleem Khan and Shadab Ahmed were granted bail on January 5.
The Delhi Police have booked the accused under the UAPA and various provisions of the Indian Penal Code (IPC), alleging that they conspired to orchestrate the communal violence that broke out in northeast Delhi on February 23, 2020, amid protests against the Citizenship (Amendment) Act. The riots left 53 people dead and hundreds injured.
Mr. Imam was initially arrested on January 28, 2020, before the riots, while Mr. Khalid was taken into custody in September that year.
Published - November 25, 2026 11:52 am IST

title: Country could face a ‘blood revolution’ unless the Constitution is saved: Prakash Ambedkar
description: Prakash Ambedkar warns of a potential “blood revolution” unless India’s Constitution is protected amid alleged RSS/BJP threats and North-South divides.
author: The Hindu Bureau
content:
Vanchit Bahujan Aghadi (VBA) chief Prakash Ambedkar on Wednesday (November 25, 2026) warned that the country could face a “blood revolution” unless the Constitution is saved and people are allowed to choose their own representatives.
Speaking at the Samvidhan Samman Sabha, held ahead of Constitution Day, Mr. Ambedkar said it is “unfortunate” that the ideals of the Constitution were under threat as Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh (RSS) and the BJP is doing everything to be in power.
Constitution Day LIVE updates
“They have this mindset of paying Pakistan and get bomb thrown at the country,” said Mr. Ambedkar, alleging that BJP and RSS were returning to communal politics to win elections, with an agenda built on being “anti-Muslim and anti-Pakistan.”
Referring to the Pulwama attack, he asked whether any country had stood behind India, and said European nations had backed Iran. He also asked why Nepal’s Prime Minister had visited India and what happened in Sri Lanka meeting, urging people to “understand the game plan.”
North-South balance
Mr. Ambedkar said India’s unity rested on a balance between North and South. He cautioned that RSS and BJP want to create the divide by increasing the dominance of North. Hinting on delimitation bill, he said, “A mechanism built over 70 years ensured there was a balance between northern and southern dominance. BJP and RSS are trying to break this arrangement out of greed. The day the South feels its dominance in Delhi is weakening, it won’t stay.”
After Independence, he said, the country chose nation over religion. The BJP, he alleged, had instigated a North-South divide to break India into pieces, put religion at the centre once more, and run the country through corporates such as Adani and Ambani.
Opposition criticised
He also criticised Shiv Sena (UBT) Chief Uddhav Thackeray and Congress leader Rahul Gandhi for not asking questions on these issues. He also advised Shiv Sena chief Eknath Shinde to be alert as Mr. Thackeray wants to be in power.
He called NCP-SP supremo Sharad Pawar’s friend of Dawood Ibrahim, saying “I know everything about these leaders and RSS has documented the history.”
Rafale, national security
Questioning the government on defence, Mr. Ambedkar said India was reported to have taken delivery of 36 Rafale jets, but the count on the ground was 32. He demanded to know how many the country actually has, and, if a jet had been shot down in conflict, where the pilot was: “with them or in the country.”
He further claimed that the Prime Minister’s “56-inch” image had suddenly shrunk and that he had “taken refuge at America’s feet.”
Drought warning
Mr. Ambedkar also spoke on the drought, warning that after December, rural Maharashtra would begin migrating to Pune, Mumbai and other metros.
Published - November 26, 2026 09:22 am IST

title: Uncovering the 'Major General Sahab' from 26/11
description: Listed only by rank in the Mumbai Police039s chargesheet on the 2611 attacks this shadow Pakistani commander oversaw one of the deadliest terror strikes against India
author: Sandeep Unnithan
content:
Uncovering the 'Major General Sahab' from 26/11
Listed only by rank in the Mumbai Police's chargesheet on the 26/11 attacks, this shadow Pakistani commander oversaw one of the deadliest terror strikes against India.
"Fire! Fire!" the Pakistani Major General shouted as the ten recruits stood with their AK-47s pointed at a row of cardboard targets on the firing range. That was the signal for the recruits to empty their magazines. Three hundred bullets echoed across the Lashkar- e-Taiba's Baitul Mujahideen camp nestled in the rugged Chelabandi Hills near Muzaffarabad in Pakistan-occupied Kashmir (PoK).
The Major General walked to the targets and inspected them closely. His eyes stopped at target number 4. "Who fired at this target?" he asked.
A short, stocky recruit, Ajmal Kasab, raised his hands. "This is how to shoot," the general said, before walking away. Kasab's bullets had completely destroyed the target.
A few weeks later, Kasab and his nine 'fedayeen' or suicide commando comrades executed one of the Pakistani deep state's deadliest attacks against India -- an assault on its commercial capital Mumbai that killed 166 people and injured over 500. Kasab and his partner Ismail Khan killed over 60 persons in a murderous rampage that began at the CST station, through the Cama Hospital, the Rang Bhavan lane where they ambushed Maharashtra Anti Terrorism Squad (ATS) top brass, chief Hemant Karkare, Additional CP Ashok Kamte and Inspector Vijay Salaskar.
Their killing spree ended at a police checkpoint near Marine Drive where an unarmed police officer, ASI Tukaram Ombale, heroically grappled with Kasab, capturing him alive but falling to his bullets. Kasab was to later recount to the Mumbai Police in graphic detail the levels of training by the LeT and the Pakistan Army that converted him into a pitiless killing machine all under the shadowy supervision of a 'Major General Sahab'.
THE MYSTERIOUS MAJOR GENERAL
That the 26/11 attacks were supervised and launched by the Pakistan Army is beyond doubt -- detailed statements made to the National Investigation Agency (NIA) by David Headley aka Daood Gilani, who recced the targets in Mumbai, point to serving Pakistan Army officers behind the attack. From Major General Muhammad Khalid Rao and Colonel Sadatullah of the Special Communications Organisation (SCO), who set up the secure networks with voice over internet or VOIP phones, to David Headley's handler, Major Iqbal, and Major Iqbal's boss, Lt Col Hamza.
'Every LeT official had a handler from the Pakistan ISI,' Headley told Indian interrogators from the NIA in Chicago two years after the attacks. During the team's training in PoK, Headley was introduced to a Pakistan Navy frogman, an officer in his mid-30s. The frogman, 'Abdul Qadir', who Indian officials believe was from the SSG-Navy (Pakistan's equivalent of India's Marine Commandos) spent several days in Muzaffarabad with nautical charts and a GPS set, plotting the 10-man attack team's 1000-km sea voyage to Mumbai and letting the LeT know where to land the boat.
But an enduring mystery of the attack is the "Major General Sahab". This mysterious two-star officer, identified only by his rank, and who keeps cropping up phantom-like in all the 26/11 chargesheets and trial papers. Identified as 'Accused number 20: Major General Sahab - Name not known', the officer is the only one among 32 Pakistanis not named in the Mumbai police's 2009 chargesheet.
But who is he?
No police artist sketch of the Major General was taken based on Kasab's description. In the absence of this, the only clues lie in Kasab's police interrogation report.
That the officer was a serving officer is beyond doubt -- Kasab's statement mentions the general as the one who brought Pakistan Army trainers to the camp. The 'Major General sahab' was a regular visitor and keenly supervised the training of the 10-man team and commanded the respect of the LeT senior cadres, receiving sharp salutes from the trainers, most likely serving personnel from the Special Service Group, the Pakistan Army's special operations force.
Like any other general in charge of a high-stakes operation, this officer was keen to know whether his highly-trained recruits could deliver -- by killing the maximum number of people in Mumbai, as efficiently as possible.
When the attacks were underway, intercepted communications between the attackers and their handlers referenced the Major General saheb. The boss was clearly in the loop.
It is clear the officer was from the ISI -- but not its chief -- the spy agency is headed by a serving Lt General. Under the ISI chief are around a dozen departments dealing with everything from intelligence analysis to counter-intelligence, policy and planning and special operations and political intelligence. Each of the ISI's 12 departments is headed by a Deputy Director General (DDG), a two-star officer who's either a Major General, Air Vice Marshal, or Rear Admiral.
THE ISI'S SINISTER DIRECTORATE S
Of all the ISI's 12 directorates, one stands out for being particularly secretive and sinister -- the S branch.
Directorate S, as it is also called, functions as an agency within an agency. Its actions are known to few even within the ISI, and for good reason. This Directorate handles external covert actions, which includes training terrorist organisations and liaising with the agency's regional militant proxies targeting India, Afghanistan, Iran, and Central Asia. The S branch's actions have led countries like India to name Pakistan a state-sponsor of terrorism.
This directorate, headed by a two-star officer, almost always a serving Army Major General, had its origins in the Afghan Bureau during the proxy war against the Soviet Union in Afghanistan between 1980 and 1988. The bureau armed, trained and equipped the Mujahideen -- a searing account of which was detailed by the then bureau chief Brigadier Mohammed Yusuf in his explosive 1992 book 'The Bear Trap'.
Yusuf's successors carried the war into India from the late 1980s onwards, first with Khalistani groups and then Kashmiri militant groups, as the expanded bureau oversaw a covert war against India through militant proxies like the LeT and the Jaish-e-Mohammed.
During the 20-year US presence in Afghanistan from 2001, Pakistan ran with the hares and hunted with the hounds. The Pakistan Army and the ISI pretended to help the Western coalition fight the Afghan Taliban, even as its Directorate S armed and trained the Taliban. The S branch practically runs groups like the LeT and Jaish, along with another directorate, DDG (North) also known as Joint Intelligence North, in charge of ISI actions within Jammu and Kashmir.
THE MUSHARRAF CABAL
When the attacks in Mumbai broke out on the night of November 26, 2008, the ISI was headed by Lt General Ahmed Shuja Pasha. The S branch chief then was Major General Mumtaz Bajwa. But, interestingly, the duo were not in charge when the attacks were being planned and the ten terrorists were being trained between 2007 and 2008.
Between 2006 and 2008, Indian security agencies began receiving a gush of intelligence alerts, 23 in all, warning of a major terror attack on five-star hotels and a Jewish centre in Mumbai. The last alert in 2008 gave out the exact coordinates of an LeT vessel off Karachi carrying ten terrorists.
Many of these alerts came to Indian agencies from US intelligence agencies, but the full picture of a major attack was never given -- a fact later noted by India's then National Security Adviser MK Narayanan.
In 2007, as the alerts kept pouring in, a close Musharraf aide was appointed as DG ISI -- Lt General Nadeem Taj. He was personally loyal to the dictator and was his wife Sehba's relative. Taj was Musharraf's Military Secretary and onboard the fateful Colombo-Karachi flight carrying Musharraf in 1999. When the aircraft was refused permission to land, the Army staged a coup and overthrew Nawaz Sharif's government.
In 2003, Taj was also in the convoy when a powerful bomb targeted Musharraf's cavalcade in 2003. "He was just a bag man for Musharraf, a guy nobody trusted," the author Steve Coll quotes a US intelligence officer in his 2018 book 'Directorate S'.
Musharraf resigned as President on August 18, 2008, to avoid impeachment. He had ruled Pakistan for nine years. The commando general had launched the 1999 Kargil War against India and during his nine-year rule as dictator, terror attacks against India soared.
Under Musharraf, the Pakistani deep state unleashed fedayeen attacks across the country. Pakistani terrorists struck India's parliament in 2001 and across Indian cities -- Bengaluru, Ahmedabad, Delhi, Hyderabad, and even the Ram Janambhoomi shrine in Ayodhya. Over 4,000 people died in a single year in Jammu and Kashmir in 2001, the state's most violent year.
A month after Musharraf's exit, in September 2008, the ISI began cleaning house, reportedly under US pressure. Coll quotes the US as being furious at multiple terror attacks in Afghanistan and Pakistan with ISI fingerprints on them. The Indian embassy in Kabul was hit by a suicide bombing on 8 July 2008 -- the attack killed 58 people, including India's defence attache Brigadier RD Mehta and an IFS officer V Venkateswara Rao. On September 20, a Pakistani suicide bomber detonated a truck bomb at the Marriott in Islamabad, killing 54 people including two Americans.
Shortly after these attacks, Taj was moved out and Pasha brought in. One other officer was shunted out of the ISI - the Deputy Director General of the notorious 'S branch', Major General Asif Duraiz Akhtar.
'The head of operations (handling relations with Mujahideen groups in Kashmir and other similar groups), Major General Asif Akhtar, and the head of the internal wing dealing with counter-terrorism and political issues inside Pakistan, Major General Nusrat Naeem, are reported to have been superseded for promotion by junior officers and moved to other jobs in the army itself,' Pakistani author Shuja Nawaz wrote of the changes in 2008.
Two months later, as the savage 26/11 attacks unfolded, the Pakistani state went from extending cooperation to outrightly denying it. In 2018, former PM Nawaz Sharif admitted Pakistani nationals were involved, but steered clear of naming the army.
Musharraf, in particular, performed a volte-face in his statements. At the India Today conclave in March 2009, he called the 26/11 attacks 'most unfortunate', 'a terrorist act' and said that 'terrorists have no nationality.' In later years, he called for cooperating in punishing those responsible, denied the involvement of the ISI and, in later years, rejected the idea that Hafiz Saeed or the LeT were behind the attacks.
Musharraf acolytes Taj and Akhtar have never been quizzed about the attacks.
Few photographs exist of the duo on the internet, particularly of Akhtar, who evidently had a more storied career than Taj. Major General Akhtar was commissioned into the 13 Punjab regiment sometime in the late 1960s and saw action in the 1971 war with India on the western front. In 1993, Akhtar was the Deputy Force Commander of the Pakistani UN contingent in Somalia that rescued US special forces stranded after their helicopter was shot down in Mogadishu (popularised by the 2001 Hollywood movie 'Black Hawk Down').
In 1999, he commanded the Peshawar-based 7th Infantry Division before going on to take over as the Director General Logistics for the Pakistan Army during the Musharraf years, between 2000 and 2003. After leaving the army, he served as Pakistan's High Commissioner to Nigeria between 2009 and 2011.
The few photographs available show Akhtar as a short, slim officer with bushy eyebrows and a hooked nose. Akhtar's LinkedIn profile has no photograph and lists him as 'Retired General / Ambassador, dealing in Oil and Gas Equipment, trading, consultation, Insurance and expertise in logistics.'
Eighteen years later, Taj and Akhtar could hold the answers to one of the last great mysteries of the 26/11 attacks: Who in Pakistan authorised the savage attacks and why? And, more importantly, who is the 'Accused number 20' in the Mumbai police chargesheet.

title: Singur's 997 acres: Said Tata to Nano 20 years ago, will welcome Ashok Leyland now
description: Singur was where then West Bengal CM Buddhadeb Bhattacharya039s ambitious industrialisation drive unravelled in 2006 forcing Tata Motors to abandon its Nano factory Two decades later CM Suvendu Adhikari is looking to turn the same 997 acres in Singur into an industrial hub starting with an Ashok Leyland truck-manufacturing factory
author: Shounak Sanyal
content:
Singur's 997 acres: Said Tata to Nano 20 years ago, will welcome Ashok Leyland now
Singur was where then West Bengal CM Buddhadeb Bhattacharya's ambitious industrialisation drive unravelled in 2006, forcing Tata Motors to abandon its Nano factory. Two decades later, CM Suvendu Adhikari is looking to turn the same 997 acres in Singur into an industrial hub, starting with an Ashok Leyland truck-manufacturing factory.
On November 21, Union Minister Sukanta Majumdar announced that commercial vehicle maker Ashok Leyland would set up a manufacturing plant in West Bengal's Singur. A day later, West Bengal Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari said the state's industrial development corporation was acquiring 997 acres of land in the town, without specifying why. While a new factory is significant for a state often seen as hostile to big industry, there is another important detail.
It was exactly 997 acres of land on which the erstwhile Left Front government had attempted to build a Tata Motors factory, only to see the Nano project collapse amid a sustained Trinamool Congress-led farmers' agitation in 2006.
West Bengal has long struggled with an image of being inhospitable to big industry. While states such as Tamil Nadu and Gujarat rapidly industrialised, Bengal went through decades of de-industrialisation. The 34 years of Left Front rule saw the state's industrial base steadily weaken, a trend that the Mamata Banerjee-led Trinamool Congress government failed to reverse during its 15 years in power.
It is this reputation that the Suvendu Adhikari-led BJP government is now looking to overturn, with plans to bring a new vehicle manufacturing plant in West Bengal.
As West Bengal's Finance Minister said on Wednesday, "The industrial and investment policy has already been announced. Ashok Leyland has shown interest in Singur. Alongside it, several chemical companies have also expressed interest. However, everything is still at a preliminary stage, and nothing has been finalised yet," reported The Times of India.
And what could be a better symbol of that change in attitude than Singur?
Nearly 20 years ago, then Chief Minister and CPI(M) veteran Buddhadeb Bhattacharya embarked on an ambitious industrialisation drive. Its centrepiece was a Tata Motors plant on 997 acres in Singur, intended to manufacture the Tata Nano, then billed as the world's cheapest car.
The current BJP government's bid to revive Bengal's industrial fortunes through a vehicle manufacturing plant in Singur appears to be retracing the very path taken by the Left Front, whose own industrial ambitions unravelled in the same town.
So why did the Left's attempt to bring about an industrial renaissance in Bengal fail? And can Suvendu Adhikari succeed in bringing an Ashok Leyland factory to the very land once earmarked for Tata Motors?
THE CPI(M) ATTEMPT TO SET UP A TATA MOTORS PLANT IN SINGUR
The Tata Motors plant at Singur, a small town in West Bengal's Hooghly district, was the centrepiece of CM Buddhadeb Bhattacharya's ambitious bid to reverse the state's industrial decline.
On May 18, 2006, the day Bhattacharya was sworn in as CM for a third consecutive term, Tata Group Chairman, Ratan Tata announced that the group would set up a plant to manufacture the Tata Nano in Singur.
It must be noted that Bhattacharya's push for private investment was a significant departure from the traditional ideological position of the CPI(M), which had for long been wary of big capital and private corporations. In fact, he went against a whole lot of CPI(M) leaders to push forward his plan.
The project ran into serious problems right from the get-go, mainly around the acquiring of 997 acres of fertile agricultural land in Singur.
Within days of Ratan Tata's announcement, farmers were demonstrating over what they termed "forcible" acquisition of land, while Bhattachrya was soon taking fire from his own party colleagues, including ex-CM Jyoti Basu for "mishandling" the land acquisition.
The protests soon snowballed into a major political confrontation, with the Singur Krishi Jami Raksha Committee and Mamata Banerjee's Trinamool Congress (TMC) spearheading the agitation against what they termed forcible land acquisition.
Banerjee accused the Left Front government of forcibly taking away farmers' land and demanded its return. The movement gathered momentum through rallies, road blockades and an indefinite hunger strike by Banerjee in December 2006, which lasted 26 days.
Despite Bhattacharya's efforts to salvage the project, the agitation continued, with violence and clashes around the factory site further escalating tensions.
After a brief breakthrough in September 2008, when negotiations brokered by then Governor Gopal Krishna Gandhi led to an agreement to examine the return of land to unwilling farmers, the deadlock returned.
Mamata Banerjee insisted that 400 acres be returned, while the Bhattacharya government refused to part with land from the main factory site.
The Trinamool Congress resumed its agitation, and Tata Motors suspended construction work on September 3, 2008, while exploring alternative locations.
On October 3, 2008, Ratan Tata announced that the company was pulling the Nano project out of Singur and the company subsequently shifted the project to Sanand in Gujarat, then ruled by the BJP, under Chief Minister Narendra Modi.
CAN THE BJP SUCCEED WHERE THE LEFT FAILED?
To say that Tata Motors' pullout from Singur was a setback would be an understatement.
It shattered Buddhadeb Bhattacharya's aim of re-industrialising West Bengal and cemented the state's image of being hostile to big industry in front of private investors. It also contributed to the Left Front's electoral collapse in the 2011 Assembly elections, which led to Mamata Banerjee ruling as the CM for the next 15 years.
The TMC, of course, failed to attract industry, which the now Suvendu Adhikari-led BJP government has set out to do in West Bengal.
There's also the hard-to-miss fact that the now CM and BJP leader, Suvendu Adhikari, was a card-carrying member of the Trinamool Congress, who rose to prominence leading his own land acquisition movement against a proposed chemical hub in Nandigram district.
Singur has featured prominently in the BJP's plan to bring industry back to the state. The CM had previously stated that he would do "something for Singur", and last week came the announcement that Ashok Leyland, India's second-largest commercial manufacturer, would set up a truck-manufacturing plant there.
The symbolism is hard to miss. Singur and the 997 acres that became the symbol of West Bengal's perceived hostility to heavy industry and derailed the Left Front's plan to reinvigorate the state, is now at the centre of the BJP's push to attract investments to the state.
A fully operational truck factory in Singur would demonstrate that West Bengal is finally ready for business. It might be a long way before everything falls into place.
Ashok Leyland is yet to present a detailed investment plan of their own, even if they have "shown interest in Singur. As state finance minister Swapan Dasputa put it, "everything is still at a preliminary stage, and nothing has been finalised yet".
There is also the sensitive issue of land acquisition. Even if the same 997 acres that had been earmarked for Tata Motors and now rendered unsuitable for agriculture are to be bought for Ashok Leyland, the acquisition will have to be made carefully. The Left Front and Tata Motors had to deal with the consequences of a "mishandled" land acquisition in 2006.
The challenge for Suvendu Adhikari is to pull off what Buddhadeb Bhattacharya failed to do nearly 20 years back. Singur had bid an unceremonious farewell to Tata Motors and its Nano. It is planning to welcome Ashok Leyland, and exactly on 997 acres in Singur. The journey will be worth watching, and have a strong bearing on West Bengal's future.

title: Man gets berth 54 in a 52-berth coach. How Railways allotted a non-existent berth
description: A passenger set to take an overnight train from Varanasi to Gorakhpur was allotted berth number 54 in an AC 2-tier coach After boarding he found that the coach had only 52 berths and berth number 54 didn039t exist The Railways blamed a software glitch What could have led to the mix-up
author: Sushim Mukul
content:
Man gets berth 54 in a 52-berth coach. How Railways allotted a non-existent berth
A passenger, set to take an overnight train from Varanasi to Gorakhpur, was allotted berth number 54 in an AC 2-tier coach. After boarding, he found that the coach had only 52 berths and berth number 54 didn't exist. The Railways blamed a software glitch. What could have led to the mix-up?
Getting a confirmed train ticket might be a struggle for many in India, but for Ishan Bajpai, the struggle began after he got a confirmed ticket and boarded the train late at night. Bajpai found that the berth allotted to him didn't exist at all. On November 22, Bajpai was travelling from Varanasi City to Gorakhpur Junction and had been allotted berth number 54 in an AC 2-tier coach (A1) that had only 52 berths.
After Bajpai registered a complaint through railway helpline 139 and flagged the issue on X, the Indian Railways responded. The Senior Divisional Commercial Manager (Sr DCM) of the Varanasi Division of the North Eastern Railway (NER), which operates the Varanasi City-Nepalganj Road Express (Train No 15132), told India Today Digital that "the discrepancy was due to a software glitch and corrective action had been taken".
The Sr DCM of the Varanasi Division said that "Bajpai wasn't the only passenger affected by the glitch. He and another passenger were subsequently provided alternative berths in the same coach".
Bajpai had discovered the discrepancy at around 10.45 pm and shared a video of himself looking for his berth inside the coach, along with a screenshot of his confirmed ticket, on X.
While the incident triggered a flurry of jokes on social media, it raised the question of how could the Railways' computerised reservation system allot a berth that did not physically exist?
TWO PASSENGERS GOT NON-EXISTENT TRAIN BERTHS
The screenshot of the ticket shared by Bajpai showed his reservation status as CNF/A1/54/SU. This meant that he had a confirmed reservation for side-upper berth number 54 in the A1 coach of the Varanasi City-Nepalganj Road Express.
"Travelling on Train 15132 tonight. My ticket confirms A1/54, but the coach has only 52 berths. Being left without your confirmed seat at 10:45 PM, on an overnight journey, is extremely frustrating. Complaint raised on 139. How can this happen?" Bajpai wrote on X on November 22.
Railway Seva, the official grievance redressal handle of the Indian Railways, responded to Bajpai's post, saying the matter had been escalated to the official concerned.
The Senior Divisional Commercial Manager (Sr DCM) of the Varanasi Division of the North Eastern Railway (NER) acknowledged the software glitch, speaking to India Today Digital.
"The inconvenience was caused by a software glitch which is being addressed. Both passengers were provided alternative berths in the same coach," the official said.
WHY SOME AC TWO-TIER COACHES HAVE 52 BERTHS AND OTHERS 54
So, how did that happen? The answer could lie in the different configurations of railway coaches of the same category. Not all railway coaches belonging to the same travel class have an identical number of berths. Their capacities vary depending on their design and configuration.
For example, conventional Integral Coach Factory (ICF) AC two-tier coaches, the old blue-or-biscuit-coloured ones, generally have 46 berths. The newer Linke Hofmann Busch (LHB) coaches, typically having a red-grey coloured configuration, have a higher capacity.
Interestingly, official documents of the Indian Railways list both 52 and 54 as the berth capacities of LHB AC two-tier coaches.
The June 2022 Revised LHB Maintenance Manual, available on the website of the Research Designs and Standards Organisation (RDSO), listed 52 berths each in AC two-tier coaches bearing the codes LWACCW and LWGACCW, the coach classification codes for two variants of LHB AC two-tier coaches.
However, technical examination material from 2020 of the North Eastern Railway, the same railway zone that operates the train Bajpai was travelling on, mentions 54 as the berth capacity of an LHB AC two-tier coach.
Therefore, a 52-berth AC two-tier coach is not an anomaly and both configurations (52-and 54-berth) for 2 AC LHB coach co-exist. In newer LHB AC two-tier coaches, which have 52 berths, the space meant for two additional passenger berths has been repurposed as a storage compartment for linen, including bedsheets, blankets and pillows for passengers.
HOW RAILWAYS COULD HAVE ALLOTTED A NON-EXISTENT BERTH
The Indian Railways' computerised Passenger Reservation System (PRS) allocates berths based on the coach configuration and berth inventory registered in its database. For the system to function correctly, this digital inventory must correspond to the actual berth capacity of the coaches attached to the train.
Such discrepancies can arise when the coach configuration registered in the reservation system differs from that of the coach actually attached to the train. Just days before Bajpai's ordeal, another passenger travelling from Hadapsar in Pune to Pandit Deen Dayal Upadhyaya Junction in UP was reportedly allotted berth number 79 in a sleeper coach that had only 78 berths, according to a report in the Hindustan Times.
"The matter has been examined, and it occurred due to a technical issue. The passengers were accommodated at berths 73 and 76 in the same coach S-10 ex-HDP by the on-board Ticket Checking staff," the report quoted IRCTC as responding to the complainant.
According to the reservation rules published by the North Central Railway, the allocation of berths is done by computers using predefined logic. For the system to allot berths correctly, the digital inventory of berths must correspond to the physical configuration of the coaches attached to a train.
Suppose the reservation system has 54 berths registered against coach A1, but a coach with 52 berths is attached to the train. So, unless the discrepancy is corrected in the system, the software could treat berths 53 and 54 as available for reservation even though they do not exist.
Such a mismatch arises when a coach is replaced for operational or maintenance reasons and the corresponding reservation inventory is not updated correctly. An incorrect coach configuration registered in the reservation system could also result in such an error.
While the Railways has acknowledged a software glitch in Bajpai's case, it has not specified whether a coach was replaced or the inventory of berths in the system caused the problem. Until such discrepancies between the Railways' digital berth inventory and actual coach configurations made in coaching yards are addressed, even a confirmed ticket might not guarantee a berth. Because it exists only on the papers.

title: National Security Guard trains state anti-terror units to deal with 26/11 type attacks
description: The federal counter-terrorism force will train anti-terror units of other state police forces in the coming months | India News
author: Prawesh Lama
content:
Prawesh Lama, an Associate Editor at Hindustan Times with nearly two decades of frontline reporting experience across India’s conflict zones, border regions, and disaster-hit areas. He writes on internal security, insurgency, the Northeast, and Left-wing extremism and has reported from India’s hinterland and some of the most sensitive and strategically critical regions.
National Security Guard trains state anti-terror units to deal with 26/11 type attacks
The federal counter-terrorism force will train anti-terror units of other state police forces in the coming months
The National Security Guard (NSG), the federal counter-terrorism force, has completed six weeks of police commando conversion courses for personnel from the anti-terror units of Maharashtra, Telangana, West Bengal, Gujarat and Uttar Pradesh as part of plans to ensure states have commando teams to respond to a 26/11-type terror attack, officials aware of the programme said.
The NSG will train anti-terror units of other state police forces in the coming months. Officials, who asked not to be named, said the Union home ministry is tracking the training programmes conducted at the NSG’s Manesar headquarters.
“There is a 6-week course... police personnel from different anti-terror units stayed with the NSG and were trained. The [Union home ministry] has said the training should be completed for all anti-terror units. The personnel are trained in hostage rescue and counter-terror operations, as the NSG does. There is a module that prepares the unit to work alongside the NSG if such a situation arises. While staying at [Manesar]...the NSG shares its training with the people from the anti-terror units,” an officer said.
The officer added that a major part of the training is focussed on hostage rescue during terror incidents. “Conducting such a hostage rescue in a house or a few rooms becomes a challenge. During the Mumbai attacks, the teams had to check hundreds of rooms on different floors at the Taj Mahal Hotel and also other buildings while fighting was on. NSG and special forces are trained for this. The home ministry’s idea behind the programme is to train the police forces on this and show them the best practices.”
A second officer said that state police anti-terror units have some of the best personnel, but their primary expertise is often in intelligence gathering and investigating terror cases. “The idea is to have one battle-ready commando unit in every anti-terror unit. The main component of the training is hostage rescue in different situations and neutralising attackers.”
The officer said refresher courses will be done once the first round of training is over. “This will ensure that all major states have a team that is trained specifically for this purpose as the first responders, even as the NSG is already expanding its presence.”
The NSG was the country’s only specialised force trained to handle counter-terrorism and anti-hostage operations at the time of the 26/11 terror attacks in Mumbai 18 years ago. The force, which draws its personnel from the Army and central armed police forces, maintains teams under its Counter Terrorist Task Force (CTTF).
These teams train throughout the year. One CTTF team, usually Team 1, is kept on standby for any national emergency. Its weapons, equipment, and even the batteries in its communication and operational devices are kept ready to ensure that commandos can mobilise as soon as possible.
Even when one commando from the unit is on leave, someone from the other CTTF teams is immediately brought to CTTF 1 and readied for any emergency.
The NSG is used only in exceptional cases. It was used during the 26/11 Mumbai attacks in 2008 and then the 2016 Pathankot Air Force station terror attack. The NSG was modelled on the UK’s SAS and Germany’s GSG-9. It has two complementary elements: the Special Action Group (SAG), including Army personnel, and the Special Ranger Group (SRG), comprising personnel from central armed and state police forces. Over 90% of the personnel in the SAG component are from the Army’s Special Forces.

title: HT morning brief Nov 26: 4 in 5 Agniveers wanted to stay on, India rejects US excess capacity claims and more

content:

HT morning brief Nov 26: 4 in 5 Agniveers wanted to stay on, India rejects US excess capacity claims and more
From Agniveer report, India's response to fresh US tariffs, Gukesh's World Championship clash and the Ramayana collection, here are today's top stories.
Good morning, readers! Here are the top developments from India and across the world, covering news, international affairs, sports and entertainment.
HT Exclusive: 4 in 5 Agniveers wanted to stay on before Agnipath’s revamp
About 80% of the Indian Army’s first batch of 19,000 Agniveers wanted to stay on beyond their four-year tenure after being asked whether they wished to continue or leave, weeks before the government unveiled a revamped Agnipath scheme in early November offering short-term soldiers a full career in the armed forces, officials familiar with the matter said Wednesday.
Deep Dive
The Agnipath announcement came weeks before the three services were set to release 75% of Agniveers from their first batch, retaining only the 25% selected on merit for another 15 years under the scheme’s earlier provisions.
Crucial assembly elections are scheduled early next year in five states, of which Uttar Pradesh, Uttarakhand and Punjab contribute substantial numbers to the forces and where the Agnipath scheme was a significant poll issue. Read the full story here.
India rejects US excess capacity claims, says no structural overcapacity in any sector
The government of India on Wednesday said it was examining a notice issued by the United States Trade Representative (USTR) as part of a probe into manufacturing capacity across 14 economies, including India, and reiterated that the country does not have structural excess capacity in any sector. The USTR has proposed tariffs of up to 25% on Indian goods under the Section 301 investigation.

title: Ministers, lawmakers put travel plans on hold amid uncertainty surrounding Parliament session
description: There are no explicit instructions, but there is an understanding that a session may be announced at short notice | India News
author: Smriti Kak Ramachandran
content:
Ministers, lawmakers put travel plans on hold amid uncertainty surrounding Parliament session
There are no explicit instructions, but there is an understanding that a session may be announced at short notice
Ministers and lawmakers of the ruling National Democratic Alliance (NDA) have put their travel plans on hold amid expectations that the schedule for the Parliament session could soon be announced, people aware of the matter said on Thursday.
The monsoon session has not yet been prorogued, stoking speculation that a short special sitting may be announced ahead of the winter session that typically takes place in November-December.
A lawmaker said there are no explicit instructions, but there is an “understanding” that a session may be announced at short notice and therefore lawmakers should be prepared. “There are indications that the session may be convened in the first week of December…” said the lawmaker.
The opposition has questioned the delay in proroguing the monsoon session. There has been no explanation from the government. Parliament affairs minister Kiren Rijiju has said there is nothing unconstitutional about the delay.
The delay comes against the backdrop of the government’s keenness to pass the delimitation and the Constitution amendment bills to implement 33% women’s reservation in the Lok Sabha and state assemblies by 2029, and to convene a special session.
The Union government has reached out to opposition parties to set aside political differences to pass the bills that seeks to increase the number of Lok Sabha seats by 50%. It has assured that proportional representation of states will be maintained.
The proposed amendment seeks to increase the Lok Sabha’s strength from 543 to a maximum of 850 through delimitation. The bills are a prerequisite for rolling out 33% reservation for women.
The opposition has stuck to its demand that the assurances be incorporated into the bills. Some parties have also suggested that the government should roll out reservation based on the current strength.
A new session requires the President to summon Parliament. Lawmakers generally receive at least a couple of weeks’ notice. The government can extend the existing monsoon session at short notice without requiring any fresh summon from the President.

title: Rooftop solar rules: Centre proposes net-metering charges, battery storage for larger systems; key changes exp
description: The Union Power Ministry proposed changes to India rooftop solar rules, allowing charges on excess power sent to the grid and mandating energy storage for systems above 10 kW starting April 2028.
author: CNBCTV18.com
content:
Rooftop solar rules: Centre proposes net-metering charges, battery storage for larger systems; key changes explained
- Published OnNov 26, 2026 | 09:36 IST
- Last Updated OnNov 26, 2026 | 09:36 IST
The government is restructuring rooftop solar regulations to impose grid charges on surplus power exceeding designated thresholds and mandate battery storage for larger installations, aiming to protect distribution netwo
The Centre has proposed a set of changes to India's rooftop solar rules that could alter how consumers use the electricity grid, including by allowing charges on excess solar power fed into the grid and requiring larger rooftop systems to have energy storage.
The Union Power Ministry issued a revised draft of the Electricity (Rights of Consumers) Amendment Rules, 2026 on November 23. The proposals are aimed at addressing the growing impact of rooftop renewable energy on electricity distribution networks as India's clean-energy capacity expands.
Under the proposed rules, State Electricity Regulatory Commissions (SERCs) would be allowed to set a threshold for net metering. Consumers would not face the proposed additional charges up to that limit.
For rooftop solar systems above the threshold, state regulators could impose charges taking into account the cost of energy storage and network losses. The proposal effectively seeks to ensure that consumers who use the electricity grid to export surplus solar power and subsequently draw electricity from it bear a greater share of the associated system costs.
Battery storage proposed for larger rooftop solar systems
The draft also proposes allowing state regulators to prescribe a capacity threshold above which rooftop renewable-energy systems would have to be equipped with energy storage systems (ESS).
Where a state regulator does not prescribe its own threshold, the requirement would apply to rooftop solar systems with an installed capacity of more than 10 kW.
The proposed storage capacity would be at least 20% of the system's total daily generation, unless a different requirement is specified by the state regulator. The energy-storage provision is proposed to take effect from April 1, 2028.
The move would encourage larger rooftop solar users to store part of their generation rather than sending all surplus electricity into the grid during periods of high solar generation.
Rooftop solar capacity could exceed sanctioned load
The proposed amendments would also give consumers, including commercial and industrial users and MSMEs, greater flexibility to install rooftop renewable-energy capacity above their sanctioned electricity load.
However, the amount of electricity that can be injected into the distribution grid would generally remain capped at the consumer's sanctioned load unless the distribution company permits a higher limit.
Electricity injected beyond the permitted limit would not be eligible for payment or compensation and could attract a penalty determined by the state regulator.
Changes to time-of-day tariffs
The draft also proposes changes to time-of-day (ToD) tariffs, under which electricity prices vary depending on when power is consumed.
The implementation of ToD tariffs for consumers with a maximum demand above 10 kW is proposed from April 1, 2028, while other non-agricultural consumers would be brought under the framework from April 1, 2029.
State regulators would also be able to determine the relevant solar and peak-hour periods based on local conditions.
Faster electricity connections, abnormal-bill checks
The proposed amendments extend beyond rooftop solar.
The draft seeks to reduce the maximum timeline for providing new or modified electricity connections in municipal corporation areas to three days.
It also proposes additional safeguards for abnormal bills. If a consumer's electricity consumption is more than five times or less than one-fifth of the average consumption over the previous six billing cycles, the distribution company would have to examine the bill and resolve the matter within a specified timeframe.
The rules also propose a framework for demand response, allowing consumers to reduce or shift electricity consumption during periods of high demand.
