title: Tradwife Influencers in India: The Politics of Women’s Choice
description: Tradwife influencers turn marriage and homemaking into aspirational content. Caste, class, and unpaid care expose the inequalities behind this ideal.
author: Jagisha Arora
content:
A woman in her early 20s, visibly married, makes tea or breakfast in her kitchen with the tagline: “A day in my life as a married girl”. Several content creators put the tagline on videos that document cooking, cleaning, and other household chores. “Love Life of a Sarkari Bahu [government daughter-in-law]” is the caption on the videos of Baishali Karmakar, a 22-year-old Bengali content creator based in Bhubaneswar, Odisha.
Her videos typically show her waking up, preparing breakfast, seeing her husband off to work, and cooking lunch for him in the afternoon. “I am the eldest daughter in my family, so I had to take care of everything. That’s why I quit my job,” she said. Managing household responsibilities and creating content was difficult alongside an office job. Karmakar earns an income from brand collaborations built on this content.
Such videos centre marriage, homemaking, and domestic responsibility, and creators often present them as aspirational lifestyles and personal choices. Academics and feminist creators question the ideals of womanhood they promote.
Tradwife is short for “traditional wife”. The term emerged online in the 2010s and spread widely on Instagram and TikTok from around 2020. Creators record, curate, and post their everyday domestic routines for online audiences. Caro Claire Burke’s debut novel, Yesteryear (2026), is a satire of American tradwife influencers. Its protagonist, Natalie Heller Mills, builds her online identity around being a devoted wife, mother, and homemaker. Her curated videos celebrate cooking, raising children, and caring for her husband as an ideal way of life. When Natalie wakes up in 1855, she must live the domestic life she once romanticised, without modern appliances. The novel sets the online presentation of domesticity against the restrictions and inequalities traditionally imposed on women.
Also Read | Film review: 'The Great Indian Kitchen' discusses gender issues and patriarchal values in relationships
The ideal of the traditional wife is not entirely new to India. Indian television serials and films have long portrayed women as responsible for holding families together and creating a sense of security within the household. The same narratives now circulate through social media, said Deepika Singh, assistant professor of political science at the GITAM School of Humanities and Social Sciences, Hyderabad.
Referring to television serials produced by Ekta Kapoor in the early 2000s, Singh said many of these shows portrayed women as responsible for managing households, maintaining relationships, and undertaking almost every domestic responsibility.
She also pointed out a contradiction between the ideals being promoted and the lives of those producing these representations. While the serials promoted traditional wives, early marriages, and women’s domestic responsibilities, their makers were themselves participating in the market economy and earning money from these narratives.
“The growing popularity of content promoting traditional gender roles needs to be understood within India’s patriarchal social structure,” said Muskan Madaan, a digital content creator who focusses on feminist conversations and self-awareness. “When you grow up in that patriarchal environment and encounter content that tells you that whatever you have been taught is right, that you are meant to cook, be someone’s wife, and make somebody else’s home your own, it reinforces the same ideas,” she said. “Before a young woman gets exposure to a new city, a different lifestyle or other possibilities, she might come across this content and begin to believe that this is what she should aspire to. It encourages young women to limit their ambitions when they already have societal expectations weighing on them.”
Singh also pointed out that the democratisation of content creation has allowed younger women to participate in the production and circulation of these narratives. Although they have greater exposure to educational and professional opportunities, they continue to be influenced by the ideas and gender norms circulating within their families and social environments.
Singh cautioned that repeated exposure to such content could normalise traditional gender roles, particularly among younger women and those without access to higher education. When certain ideas circulate repeatedly through reels, jokes, and everyday conversations, they could gradually become accepted as normal, and women could internalise these narratives and reproduce them through their own content. She added that such content is also popular among male audiences, whose engagement contributes to its circulation.
At the same time, Singh pointed out that social media gives exposure to different perspectives. Unlike television, which largely circulated a dominant narrative, social media allows people to express opposing opinions. Comment sections also provide space for women to challenge such representations and point out that domestic work is not solely their responsibility.
Choice and consent
Many creators describe early marriage, motherhood, and a life centred on domestic responsibilities as their right to choose. This perspective, commonly known as “choice feminism", frames every choice a woman makes as a feminist one, as she chose it for herself.
Does choosing a traditional lifestyle give a woman control over the conditions in which she lives? Understanding agency here requires examining a woman’s power to question and alter the arrangement, said Shivani Nag, assistant professor at the School of Education Studies, Dr. B.R. Ambedkar University Delhi. “What can she refuse or renegotiate? Is the man’s exemption from care ever questioned? Does she have control over money, and can she change course later? Calling the decision an expression of agency does not settle what it does to the division of labour and power,” Nag said.
Consent also depends on the possibility of refusal, Nag said. If saying no to a domestic role means losing financial support, facing hostility from family, or being judged a bad mother, those consequences form part of the agreement. Consent alone cannot settle whether the relationship is equal. Women’s agency operates within these relationships and can develop through negotiation, refusal, and efforts to change an arrangement.
Another content creator, Tanya Baliyan, who posts as Soul by Tanya on Instagram, has built her online presence around domesticity, marriage, and relationships. Her Instagram bio describes her as a relationship coach, offering one-on-one sessions to women to help them become better wives. Some of her content also conveys the idea that a woman’s life remains incomplete without her husband.
The debate around tradwife culture cannot be reduced to whether a woman chooses to stay home and take on domestic responsibilities. The economic and social conditions within which that choice is made, and the long-term security it offers women, also need to be examined. Many tradwife influencers seem reluctant to engage with these questions, said Ashima, a corporate professional who has been observing this trend for years.
She pointed to a contradiction in the way this lifestyle is marketed. Many of these influencers argue that women should prioritise domestic responsibilities while men take charge of earning. Yet they themselves generate income through brand collaborations, social media engagement, and monetising content that promotes this very division of labour.
The market’s role
Estimates of the money behind such collaborations vary widely. Kofluence, an influencer marketing platform, valued India’s influencer marketing industry at Rs.3,000-3,500 crore in 2025, while the agency KlugKlug estimates that actual spending has crossed Rs.10,000 crore. Both firms sell influencer marketing services.
Nag said many influential ideas of respectable womanhood have treated the home as a space whose intimacy and sanctity women must preserve. A reel makes selected parts of that world available to a public audience, and a woman who promotes domestic life speaks publicly, builds a following and, where the account earns revenue, takes part in a commercial economy. “What happens to the idea of the ‘traditional wife’ when domestic life becomes a public, potentially commercial activity?” she asked. Traditional domestic roles may be affirmed, while the boundary between private domestic life, public visibility, and commercial activity is reworked.
For a creator, presenting domestic life may become work and a source of income, she said. Income from representing domestic life, however, does not establish that care within the household has become paid or more equally shared. What audiences and advertisers encourage creators to show, and whether earning from that image makes domesticity more attractive, are open questions. The language of choosing tradition can serve several purposes at once: making sense of one’s own life, negotiating family expectations, and building a persona that attracts a following. How these combine has to be examined case by case, Nag said.
Nag also connected this trend to the privatisation of care under neoliberalism. “When the state withdraws from providing services, or leaves families to arrange care themselves, the work still has to be done. It usually falls to women. Could the tradwife ideal make that withdrawal of public responsibility easier to accept by presenting women’s return to unpaid care as a desirable personal choice?” she asked.
Caste, class, gender, and labour
In India, caste and class have historically shaped women’s relationship with domestic labour. Nag argued that this history cannot begin with a generalised woman confined to the home: caste helped secure domestic seclusion and respectability for some women by extracting the labour of others.
Caste required Dalit women and women from other historically marginalised castes to work in fields, in service, and in other households, and restricted where they could enter, what work they could do, and on what terms they could be present. Work outside their own homes did not necessarily bring them freedom of movement or equal standing.
The domestic respectability of one group and the compelled labour of another were connected arrangements, she said. “This distinction is essential to understanding the promise of ‘returning home’. Many women have never had the material possibility of withdrawing from earning. Others have worked in someone else’s home while struggling to meet their own needs. An ideal presented as women’s natural way of life can depend on labour that makes that life impossible for other women,” she added.
Women make up 49.7 per cent of students in Indian higher education, but their participation in the workforce remains low. Female enrolment rose 42.2 per cent between 2014-15 and 2023-24, to 2.24 crore, according to the Ministry of Education’s All India Survey on Higher Education.
In September 2026, the labour force participation rate for people aged 15 and above stood at 55.5 per cent across India, but was 34.6 per cent among women, according to the monthly bulletin of the Periodic Labour Force Survey, published by the Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation.
Explaining how individual agency operates within patriarchal structures, Nag said, “Take a household in which both partners earn, but childcare is assumed to be the woman’s responsibility. Her job has to accommodate the child’s needs; his is treated as the job that must continue uninterrupted. If affordable care is unavailable and her wages are lower, leaving employment may become the arrangement the household can manage. Describing this as her choice to prioritise family conceals the inequalities that made her employment the one to be sacrificed. Why was his job never up for discussion?”
A wider economy sits behind that private decision, she said. Someone has to cook, raise children and look after people who are ill, and employers depend on that work to have workers who can turn up each day. Households carry much of its cost, and when public care is unavailable, families absorb more of it. “A woman’s unpaid labour can become the way everyone else’s demands are accommodated.”
Also Read | Women working the invisible double shift
Expectations of the good wife or mother reinforce these pressures, Nag said. A father who works late is praised for providing for his family, while a mother who does the same is accused of neglecting hers. The woman may come to experience giving up her job as the right thing to do. “Economic inequality and internalised expectations strengthen one another; they are working through the same decision,” she said.
Beyond individual choice
The structural inequalities shaping the division of domestic labour explain why individual choice needs to be understood through broader social conditions. To explain these inequalities, Singh discussed the American feminist philosopher Nancy Fraser’s work on three dimensions of justice: recognition, representation, and redistribution.
The first is recognition, which concerns the invisibility of care work. Singh said society often describes a woman as a housewife, as though she does no work, yet domestic work is a 24-hour responsibility, seven days a week.
The second dimension is representation, which examines women’s participation in the public sphere and workplaces. Singh explained that the traditional expectation that women should remain at home and undertake care responsibilities has restricted their participation in public life.
The third dimension is redistribution, which concerns the equal distribution of care work between genders.
Singh argued that choice can be meaningful only in an equal society. If men and women had equal rights and opportunities, a woman could genuinely choose to take care of the household. But when domestic responsibilities are treated as a woman’s duty and she is judged a bad woman for not performing them, it becomes difficult to describe that arrangement as an “individual choice”.
Jagisha Arora is a Delhi-based journalist covering social, gender, cinema, and political issues.

title: Statue of Unity to Gandhi Ashram: How Modi’s Politics Repackages History and Hides Reality
description: The Statue of Unity, Gandhi Ashram redevelopment and electoral-roll controversies point to a politics of distraction that obscures history and democratic accountability.
author: URVISH  KOTHARI
content:
You have probably heard of the Statue of Unity, the world’s tallest statue, if its sheer scale has not already impressed itself upon you. Erected in memory of Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel—a leader whom the right-wing narrative often portrays as having been wronged by Gandhi and Nehru—the monument was completed in 2018, its outer bronze cladding cast at a foundry in China.
A visit to the Statue of Unity offers an array of attractions: the Jungle Safari (Sardar Patel Zoological Park), botanical gardens, river cruises, Tent City accommodation, aarti ceremonies, and more. In recent years, lakhs of tourists have visited the site, making it one of Gujarat’s top ten tourist destinations. Visitors frequently praise these attractions. Yet very few speak of what the site teaches them about Patel himself, or of his achievements and legacy. They leave carrying memories of safaris, cruises, gardens, and entertainment, but scarcely any understanding of his life and work.
Thus, a nearly Rs.3,000-crore project supposedly conceived to remedy the alleged historical injustice done to Patel ends up accomplishing the opposite of its stated purpose. Rather than highlighting his legacy, it obscures it in plain sight, transforming the site into a destination for fun-centric tourism that resembles an amusement park. The only significant difference is that this one is promoted by the central government.
That is how illusions work: through distraction. Traditional illusionists could make an elephant, or even a train, disappear before an audience’s eyes. The Modi-Shah duo appear to possess a similar talent. A visit to the world’s tallest statue, that of Patel, leaves visitors with little understanding of his life or work. This information is not hidden; museums and exhibitions exist. But because attractions and entertainment dominate the experience, tourists’ memories revolve around everything except Patel himself.
This is not merely a reflection of the Indian public’s supposed indifference to history. It appears to be part of a broader design: to conceal what matters in plain sight while cultivating, wherever possible, a personality cult around Modi.
A similar fate befell the decades-old Gandhi statue at Ahmedabad’s busy Income Tax crossroads. A flyover physically overshadowed the monument. Equally important, however, was the disappearance of the protests that once gave the site political life. For decades, small groups of demonstrators could be found there almost every day, advocating for one cause or another. The statue remains in place today, but it feels more hidden than prominent, overshadowed by the bustle of the junction. It comes to life only twice a year, when politicians across party lines arrive to perform the ritual of garlanding.
The redevelopment under way around Gandhi Ashram in Ahmedabad evokes a similar feeling. In the name of restoring the Ashram, what seems to be happening instead is the concealment of its most important spaces in plain sight.
How does one strip a place like Gandhi Ashram of its sanctity without touching its most revered sites or making visible alterations to locations such as Hriday Kunj, Vinoba and Mira’s huts, Magan Nivas, Nandini Guest House, or the prayer ground? The answer is simple and, by now, well tested: transform the surroundings and remodel the experience as a curated retreat offering “simple living” amid green, natural surroundings. In the process, the sanctity, simplicity, and historical character of the Ashram will be eroded in the name of preservation and restoration.
The restored complex will have two grand entrance gates, likely accompanied by plaques crediting the Prime Minister for “restoring the Ashram,” along with a host of museums, multimedia attractions, shows, and, inevitably, the distraction-in-chief: the food court.
The Ashram has undergone structural changes before, and objections were raised then too. Yet none of those earlier modifications altered the essential spirit of the place. The buildings and their surroundings retained an atmosphere that many visitors could feel, even if they could not fully explain it. The current redevelopment, however, appears to change the very nature of the Ashram experience. Even so, it is being widely celebrated in the media as a great service to Gandhi’s memory.
Tampering in plain sight
Perhaps the most striking example of this government’s ability to hide things in plain sight emerged when serious allegations and reports of electoral-roll manipulation began to surface. The alleged tampering was audacious precisely because the documents in question were publicly available and openly distributed, seemingly on the assumption that very few would examine them closely enough to detect anything unusual.
Indeed, when these allegations first surfaced, one common response was: the electoral rolls were shared with all political parties before the election, so why didn’t they check them? The answer may be simple. Few people could imagine that manipulation on such a scale was even possible, let alone that someone would have the confidence to attempt it.
Despite multiple reports alleging the tampering of electoral rolls, the government has yet to provide a substantive response, while the Election Commission has quietly reversed several of its more controversial decisions. The government, meanwhile, behaves as though nothing significant has occurred, remaining focused on what has increasingly become its signature political method: creating distractions while relying on its ability to hide things in plain sight.
Urvish Kothari is a Gujarat-based writer, editor, and satirist. He edited A Plain, Blunt Man: The Essential Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel (2023, Aleph).

title: Nvidia Reinstates Huang as AI Industry Faces Leadership Risks
description: Nvidia reinstates Jensen Huang as CEO after a boardroom reversal backed by Donald Trump, sending shares soaring and raising questions about corporate power.
author: Frontline News Desk
content:
Nvidia’s board reinstated Jensen Huang as president and chief executive officer of the world’s chipmaker by market value, marking a reversal in the history of the company and driving the stock to its biggest rally in decades. Fewer than two weeks after Huang departed Nvidia under the shadow of scandal, he is reclaiming both titles, the board stated in an announcement on November 23. US President Donald Trump had lobbied for the reinstatement, and the board cited input from the government of the United States when issuing the statement.
“Thank you all for the second chance. I am going to be a better CEO the second time around,” Huang told employees at Nvidia’s headquarters in Santa Clara, California. Chairman Harvey C. Jones said in the statement, "The board believes Jensen is the right person to lead Nvidia, and that his reinstatement is in the best interests of our stockholders, employees, partners and customers.”
Huang’s return follows weeks of turmoil at Nvidia, whose technology underpins the boom in artificial intelligence. The board had ousted him earlier this month after revelations that he had engaged in affairs outside his marriage—one with a subordinate and another with a woman whom the government of the US has investigated for espionage on behalf of China.
Supporters both within and outside the company, however, regarded the 63-year-old executive as irreplaceable. Huang had transformed Nvidia from a supplier of graphics chips into an enterprise valued at more than $5 trillion, while travelling the globe to champion AI as a revolution in industry.
News of his reinstatement sparked a rally for Nvidia. Shares surged 31 per cent to $165.05 in New York, marking the company’s highest gain in a single day since May 2003. Prior to the rebound, the stock had declined by roughly a third over the course of the year, erasing about $1.5 trillion in value on the market.
Nvidia’s board stated that its investigation into reports concerning Huang will continue, while the executive faces scrutiny from Congress over both his conduct and the export of technology to China. Huang is scheduled to sit for an interview with three committees of the House on December 1 and to testify before the Senate Banking Committee two days later at a hearing on export controls of the US. The company is still under scrutiny from investigators, including at the FBI and on Capitol Hill.
No consultation
People familiar with the deliberations said the board acted without consulting interim CEO Colette Kress or other executives, following an intervention by Trump, who pressed directors to make the move. Huang had appealed to the board for his return—a bid backed by some employees and prominent figures in Silicon Valley—after directors initially rejected his overture. The reversal echoed events at OpenAI in 2023, when Sam Altman was ousted as CEO and reinstated within a week amid backlash from investors and staff; like Huang, Altman is regarded as central to the development of AI.
Huang ranks as Nvidia’s fifth-largest shareholder with a stake of roughly 3.6 per cent, though he holds no shares with voting privileges of the kind that grant founders such as Mark Zuckerberg of Meta Platforms and Elon Musk of SpaceX control over their companies.
The executive relies on a style of management that involves intervening in problems at Nvidia and overseeing roughly 60 reports, nearly all in roles within engineering, including specialists in memory chips, networking, and graphics and processors.
“A lot of companies’ organisation charts, they all look the same. And it doesn’t make any sense to me. The architecture of the ‌company should reflect the environment in which it exists,” Huang said on a podcast in March. Huang has involved himself in the operations of startups backed by Nvidia, assisting them in securing customers and joining fundraising calls to attract investors, according to founders, venture capitalists, and a former Nvidia employee.
Huang’s return stumped many, and US lawmakers from both the Democratic and Republican parties strongly objected to his reinstatement. But it also reinforced the idea that some tech CEOs were considered irreplaceable, a big risk for ‌a company critical to the AI industry.
Speaking at a press conference in Brooklyn on November 23, New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani said: “I do not think that working people across the country signed up for their pensions being tied to the question of Jensen Huang’s fidelity to his marriage, and yet, for many days, that had a massive impact.”
He added, “We’re speaking about a divorce settlement that has been rumoured to be around $81 billion. That would be the cost of providing universal child care for every 3- and 4-year-old in the United States of America for an entire year. And a lot of this just brings to mind what Justice Brandeis said quite some time ago, which is, "We can have democracy; we can have great wealth concentrated in the hands of a few; we cannot have both.”
Nvidia leads the market in manufacturing accelerators for artificial intelligence—the chips used to train and run AI models—making the company a beneficiary of spending on infrastructure for data centres. The US government restricts sales of these chips to China, and Nvidia’s ties to the country, alongside its compliance with export controls, have drawn scrutiny.
Late last year, following lobbying from Huang, Trump loosened controls on chips and permitted Nvidia to sell its H200 processor—now generations behind its Vera Rubin line—to China. Last week, Kress, Nvidia’s chief financial officer, informed investors that the chipmaker would halt sales of licensed H200 products to the country.
The company will hire a new chief compliance officer, and the board recently formed a committee to oversee national security and export control matters, it said in a statement.
Tech firms soar
News of Huang’s return, released shortly after the opening bell on November 23, sparked a surge across equities, driving shares of Nvidia up by 31.5 per cent and adding more than $900 billion to the valuation of the company. Other firms on Wall Street also drew buying interest, lifting the Nasdaq by more than six per cent, the S&P 500 by 4.7 per cent, and the Dow by three percent.
Markets in Asia, which had opened the week with losses, followed that trajectory. Taipei led the region with a nine per cent gain as chipmakers TSMC and MediaTek each rose nearly 10 per cent. Seoul climbed more than six per cent on advances from SK Hynix and Samsung.
Tokyo closed nearly four per cent higher, propelled by jumps of 12.5 per cent in Advantest, 7.7 per cent in Tokyo Electron, and 10 per cent in Kioxia. Exchanges in Shanghai, Sydney, Singapore, Wellington, Bangkok, and Manila also posted gains, while Hong Kong slipped as technology firms in China lagged behind the rally.
China’s warning
Huang’s comeback—prompted by the intervention of Trump—drew caution from state media in China. Less than three hours after the board issued its announcement, the Global Times published a commentary urging China to “remain vigilant”.
The article said, “It is foreseeable that the malicious attempts to sow discord in China-US relations will not automatically disappear simply because Huang has been reinstated.” It added that the next round of “witch hunts” could include investigation letters, delays in export licences and congressional hearings.
(with inputs from agencies)

title: From IISER Pune’s CARE programme to IPSMF and George Soros: Who is Rohit Upadhyay and what lies behind the Germany visit of ‘independent journalists’ before CJP protest
description: Rohit Upadhyay, The Red Mike and Peek TV were actively involved in covering the CJP demonstration and peddling their agenda. | OpIndia News
author: Amit Kelkar
content:
An intriguing revelation has recently emerged in connection with the build-up to the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) protest. According to fact-checker Vijay Patel, Saurav Sharma of The Red Mike, along with Peek TV founders Priyanshi Sharma and Vedanta Agarwal, visited Germany with funding from the German government just a few months before the agitation.
However, they were also accompanied by another alleged journalist, Rohit Upadhyay, who has over 793K followers on Facebook, 162K followers on Instagram, and nearly 887K subscribers on YouTube.
Who is the person sitting behind The Red Mike’s Saurav Sharma, who visited Germany, funded by the German government, along with Peek TV founders, just a few months before the CJP protest? 1. This question leads me down a Rabbit hole! Read exclusive details in this thread👇 https://t.co/Au879buZVt
— Vijay Patel (@vijaygajera) November 25, 2026
The Red Mike, Peek TV and Upadhyay were all very active during this demonstration. OpIndia has previously reported that journalists posing as “neutral” voices were actively promoting the opposition’s agenda and readily agreed to do political propaganda for the Samajwadi Party ahead of the Uttar Pradesh elections in exchange for a few thousand rupees.
3. Interestingly, just like Peek TV and The Red Mike, Rohit Upadhyay was also hyperactive in the CJP protest. https://t.co/C7UpxBeFwo
— Vijay Patel (@vijaygajera) November 25, 2026
Upadhyay is a grantee of the International Centre for Journalists (ICFJ), which has tightly collaborated with Open Society Foundations (OSF) of George Soros. The two have teamed up alongside other groups on various OSF-backed projects. ICFJ has partnered with the Organised Crime and Corruption Reporting Project (OCCRP) on the Investigative Dashboard (ID) project, which obtained sponsorship from OSF.
He posted a photograph with anti-Hindu “comedian” Kunal Kamra and boasted about being “Dimagi Naxals.” Prime Minister Narendra Modi had used the term to describe those with the same ideology and seek to create unrest in the country.
Upadhyay has consistently disseminated propaganda on both national and international issues through his content. He has attacked Israel, glorified Hamas and praised the Islamist regime of Iran. He mocked India as an “artificial world leader” and even defamed Kanwariyas as violent while supporting Azam Khan‘s Jauhar University, which has been accused of being built on land snatched from farmers. He has even gone as far as defending the senior SP leader’s obscene remarks on Jaya Prada.
5. Now here is a shocking part of this rabbit hole. After the protest, the government institute IISER Pune has invited him to serve as a trainer for 40+ journalists under the Care Project. https://t.co/0GjtGkJvUB
— Vijay Patel (@vijaygajera) November 25, 2026
Upadhyay has collaborated with the Indian Institute of Science Education and Research (IISER), Pune, under its CARE (Communicating Action and Resilience for Environmental Health in India) venture. He served as part of its “VOICE Fellowship” and was later invited to conduct video journalism training for over 40 participants.
The CARE programme is chaired by Dr Shalini Sharma of the Department of Humanities and Social Sciences and mentored by self-proclaimed climate journalist Nidhi Jamwal. Upadhyay praised both in his post and remarked, “Keep an eye on these two beautiful minds, Shalini Sharma and Nidhi Jamwal. They have launched HEAL Magazine, and I am sure they will come up with many more interesting initiatives.”
Upadhyay further conveyed, “And when you have journalists like Hridayesh Joshi and Mayank Aggarwal in the room, you know the training is going to be special.” Aggarwal is a trustee of the controversial “The Reporters Collective,” which has a knack for misleading its audience with bogus reportage, while Joshi has a reputation for targeting developmental projects and accusing Hindu festivals such as Holi, Diwali and Chhath of polluting and damaging the environment. He is regularly featured on Newslaundry for this purpose.
7. Prof. Shalini Sharma is a fan of Marxist Neha and also feels ‘hope’ when Marxist CJP protesters were working for the ‘Regime Change’ https://t.co/aEz6HEWZfn
— Vijay Patel (@vijaygajera) November 25, 2026
Unpacking the nexus: A deeper dive down the rabbit hole
Sharma is a supporter of leftist anarchist Neha Bora and wanted her supposed hunger strike to also be credited with the resignation of former minister of education Dharmendra Pradhan. In another tweet, she asserted, “Brazil’s youth fought for the Amazon and democracy. Serbia’s students voted out a 14-year strongman. Young people are choosing democracy and the planet’s survival over business-as-usual. Our Gen Z is doing the same against the odds. I feel hope, not naivety.”
Sharma attempted to portray the politically motivated, violent protests as an organic youth movement against the Modi government, even as her ideological associates, Bora and Prashant Bhushan, had already acknowledged that it was, in fact, a regime-change operation along the lines of Bangladesh. The latter even came under fire for “drawing inspiration” from the bloody unrest in the neighbouring country and argued that her video had been doctored to save face.
The series of tweets shed light on the deeper political and ideological ties. Jamwal was seen with Rashtriya Janata Dal (RJD) Rajya Sabha MP Manoj Kumar Jha, whom she referred to as her “guru” for teaching her about “class and caste bias” during her master’s degree. She added that he “ignited their young minds and taught them to ask questions” while conveying her regards to him on Guru Purnima.
9. These two run this project at the government institute IISER and invite hardcore Marxists like Avinash Das to train young students and journalists. https://t.co/ZUdX29qEiw
— Vijay Patel (@vijaygajera) November 25, 2026
Moreover, the CARE program, run by Sharma and Jamwal, offers a platform to leftist figures such as director and fake-news peddler Avinash Das. He was arrested by the crime branch of the Gujarat police in 2022.
Sharma has used her position of authority to advance her ideological objectives by organising events to facilitate spaces for infamous leftist personalities, including Nikhil Dey and Nandini Oza.
Dey is a founding member of Mazdoor Kisan Shakti Sangathan (MKSS) & National Campaign for People’s Right to Information (NCPRI). He insisted that the centre has been deliberately weakening the RTI (Right to Information) Act through amendments during his speech at the 7th annual PM Mukhi Memorial Human Rights Lecture at IISER Pune
Dey, a known detractor of the Modi government, had earlier demanded an inquiry into sexual harassment charges against former Chief Justice of India (CJI) Ranjan Gogoi, which were deemed a potential “conspiracy because of his tough stands.” The matter was subsequently closed by the Supreme Court.
Similarly, Oza regularly maligns Hindutvavadis as “casteist and anti-minority,” attacks Hindu organisations, like the Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh (RSS) and invokes “feminism and secularism” to peddle Muslim victimhood and exploit caste lines. She used the institution to push an anti-Sardar Sarovar Dam narrative, which was propagated by the likes of Medha Patkar with her “Narmada Bachao Andolan” and backed by actor Aamir Khan, while Gujarat continued to face water scarcity for decades.
11. But who funds Shalini Sharma’s CARE project? It’s funded by Health Care Without Harm, Global. Health Care Without Harm is supported by PHFI, which is funded by Bill Gates. https://t.co/elWxTza887
— Vijay Patel (@vijaygajera) November 25, 2026
The CARE project has been discovered to be aided by the Public Health Foundation of India (PHFI), which has not only taken grants from the Gates Foundation but also works closely with Health Care Without Harm, likewise supported by this foundation.
Furthermore, adding yet another significant layer to this network, CJP co-convenor Ashutosh Ranka has also been employed by the Global Health Vision and the Global Alliance for Vaccines and Immunisation (GAVI), both funded by billionaire Bill Gates, who referred to India as “a laboratory to test new ideas.”
13. Interestingly, after returning from Germany, Peek TV and The Red Mike have secured funding from the IPSMF. In the monthly newsletter of the IPSMF, it has been mentioned that Peek TV was one of the three news outlets that were invited by the German government in Germany! https://t.co/rv7b8mMsT7
— Vijay Patel (@vijaygajera) November 25, 2026
On the other hand, Peek TV and The Red Mike secured financial assistance from the Independent and Public-Spirited Media Foundation (IPSMF) after returning from Germany. The IPSMF’s monthly newsletter mentioned Peek TV as one of the three news outlets invited to Germany by the government.
What is IPSMF
The alleged NGO (non-governmental organisation), set up by Azim Premji and Infosys co-founder Nandan Nilekani’s wife, Rohini Nilekani, in 2015, has aided the Islamist-leftist media cartel, including The Wire, The Caravan, Article 14, Mojo Story and Alt News, among others.
Swarajya was included in the list merely to create an impression of false balance and project an appearance of neutrality. IPSMF comprises at least 10 other wealthy Indians and was launched with an initial corpus of Rs 100 crore.
2. As many of you know that, the entire digital leftist propaganda media cartel including The Wire, The Caravan, Article 14, Mojo Story of Barkha Dutt, Alt News of Zubair and Pratik Sinha, and many more are funded by an NGO IPSMF. https://t.co/IC7kZteplX
— Vijay Patel (@vijaygajera) July 4, 2022
IPSMF continues to back “The Reporters Collective,” “Newslaundry,” “The Mooknayak,” and others, in addition to Peek TV and The Red Mike. OpIndia had already exposed IPSMF in 2017.
Ashish Dhawan, who co-founded Ashoka University and Ramachandra Guha were on its original board of trustees. The former also established The Convergence Foundation (TCF), where he currently serves as CEO. It too has strong associations with the Gates Foundation. The NGOs of other trustees, both former and current, shared similar ties to the foundation.
Meanwhile, Rohini Nilekani’s “EkStep Foundation” is linked to “Co-Impact,” a global partnership whose core members include the Gates Foundation and the Rockefeller Foundation. She expressed her admiration for George Soros, the Open Society Foundations (OSF), the Gates Foundation and the Ford Foundation in 2016. That same year, Lakshmi Chaudhry, IPSMF’s principal investment adviser at the time, wrote about a meeting involving the Gates Foundation that was hosted by the Omidyar Network.
It is also noteworthy that Azim Premji became the first Indian to sign “The Giving Pledge” campaign of Bill and Malinda gates in 2013. A few years later, The Bridgespan Group, a consulting firm for NGOs, entered India in 2015. It is supported by the Gates Foundation, the Ford Foundation, the Rockefeller Foundation, the Omidyar Network, and similar groups.
6. In 2015, an NGO The Bridgespan Group came to India. The Bridgespan Group is heavily funded by Bill Gates, Ford Foundation, Rockefeller Foundation, Omidyar Network, and many more American NGOs. This Group is working as a consulting agency for NGOs! https://t.co/YGIWr2yWzq
— Vijay Patel (@vijaygajera) July 4, 2022
The client list included familiar prominent names, including Azim Premji, the Gates Foundation, the Ford Foundation, the Omidyar Network, the Rockefeller Foundation and Tata Trusts.
Conclusion
This is a profoundly entrenched and intricate network involving both Indian and foreign elements spanning the media, academia and NGOs. All of them belong to the same ecosystem, working towards pursuing their agenda, which is cloaked in the guise of neutrality, humanitarian work and similar labels to shape public opinion and sentiment, while the notorious efforts continue behind the scenes.

title: Elon Musk Doubles SpaceX Gift, Every American Child To Get Two Shares
description: SpaceX chief executive Elon Musk on Thursday (26 November) said every child in the United States would get two shares of the company, one gifted by Sp
author: Arun Dhital
content:
News Brief
Arun Dhital
Nov 26, 2026 | Updated 05:05 PM GMT+5:30
Save & read from anywhere!
Bookmark stories for easy access on any device or the Swarajya app.
SpaceX chief executive Elon Musk on Thursday (26 November) said every child in the United States would get two shares of the company, one gifted by SpaceX and the other by him, widening a programme meant to give young Americans a stake in the firm and help them build wealth over time.
"Every child in America will receive two SpaceX shares, one from the company and one from me personally," Musk wrote on X.
SpaceX had earlier committed one newly issued Class A common share to each active Trump Account, a tax-advantaged investment account created to help American children save for the long term. Musk said he would personally match that contribution.
The company has not said whether Musk's shares will also be routed through Trump Accounts, or whether they will carry a lock-up period limiting their sale.
According to SpaceX, the scheme will let millions of children own a part of the company and benefit from its long-term growth. "Today, we are committing one SpaceX share to millions of American children to give the next generation a stake in building a more exciting future," it said in a social media post.
The company added that the move reflects its view that the next generation should have a role in building future infrastructure, as well as its goal of making life multiplanetary.
SpaceX stock ended Wednesday's session on Nasdaq at $127 per share.
Musk had first floated the idea last month. "Next ycn the future economy, directly to the people is the way," he added.

title: SP Bristles At Imran Masood's 'Taj Mahal On My Grave' Jibe, Questions Congress Silence
description: Congress MP Imran Masood's "goodbye" and "Taj Mahal on my grave" jibes on Wednesday evening have pushed the Samajwadi Party (SP) to take note of the m
author: Arun Dhital
content:
News Brief
Arun Dhital
Nov 26, 2026 | Updated 04:54 PM GMT+5:30
Save & read from anywhere!
Bookmark stories for easy access on any device or the Swarajya app.
Congress MP Imran Masood's "goodbye" and "Taj Mahal on my grave" jibes on Wednesday evening have pushed the Samajwadi Party (SP) to take note of the mounting criticism from its ally, after it had ignored his barbs through the day.
Some SP functionaries have also asked why the Congress leadership has stayed silent even as Masood's statements turn more aggressive each day.
In an interview with The Times of India on Wednesday, Masood said in Hindi, "I am unable to understand your battle … You want to fight the BJP or us. If you will want to stand on my neck and build a Taj Mahal on my grave, I will be suffocated. I will fight back."
Later, speaking to a news channel, Masood likened the Congress to a zero, which raises a number's value tenfold when added to it. "If you don't understand our importance, then OK, Goodbye, Thank You," he said.
Many in the SP feel Masood had the backing of a section, if not all, of the Congress leadership.
"Either the Congress brass has chosen to look the other way or they are unaware that such statements are being made by its party functionaries. In both the cases, such uncontrolled whataboutery is not a good sign," a senior SP functionary told TOI.
The functionary said Masood and AICC Uttar Pradesh in-charge Rajendra Pal Gautam had targeted the SP and its leadership over the alliance earlier as well. SP members, however, did not respond, as the party chief had strictly instructed them not to comment on the alliance.
"The issue is not that they attack SP, the problem is that there are no signs to suggest that their party leadership has objected to their unprovoked statements, which is strange," the SP functionary said.

title: Doval Pushes Deeper Indian Ocean Cooperation At Colombo Security Conclave In Male
description: National Security Adviser Ajit Doval has called for stronger cooperation among countries along the Indian Ocean, speaking at the eighth NSA-level meet
author: Arun Dhital
content:
News Brief
Arun Dhital
Nov 26, 2026 | Updated 04:24 PM GMT+5:30
Save & read from anywhere!
Bookmark stories for easy access on any device or the Swarajya app.
National Security Adviser Ajit Doval has called for stronger cooperation among countries along the Indian Ocean, speaking at the eighth NSA-level meeting of the Colombo Security Conclave (CSC) in Male on Wednesday (25 November).
Doval said India would work with member states to build their capacity to deal with emerging threats. Linking the grouping to two key Indian policies, he described the conclave as “the intersection between our neighbourhood's first approach and our Mahasagar vision.”
Mahasagar, India's expanded maritime doctrine centred on security, growth and sustainable development across the Global South, stands for “mutual and holistic advancement for security and growth across regions”. Prime Minister Narendra Modi unveiled it during a visit to Mauritius in March 2025, building on the Sagar (Security and Growth for All in the Region) initiative launched in 2015.
The CSC was formed in 2020 when India, Sri Lanka and the Maldives expanded their trilateral dialogue on maritime cooperation. Mauritius joined in March 2022, followed by Bangladesh in July 2024. On 30 August 2024, members signed the Charter and the Memorandum of Establishment for a secretariat in Colombo. Doval noted that the grouping now has its own secretariat and secretary-general.
The conclave works across five areas, namely maritime safety and security, countering terrorism and radicalisation, trafficking and transnational organised crime, cyber security and critical infrastructure protection, and humanitarian assistance and disaster relief.
National security advisers and delegations from India, the Maldives, Sri Lanka and Bangladesh took part in the three-day meeting, held from 24 to 26 November, with Australia and Malaysia attending as guests. Member countries signed a joint declaration setting out their common position in line with the agreed minutes.

title: दिल्ली: प्रदूषण से बिगड़ रही लोगों की सेहत, दो दिन में चेस्ट क्लीनिक पहुंचे 120 मरीज
description: Delhi’s worsening air pollution is taking a toll on public health. Around 120 patients visited chest clinics across the city in just two days, reporting respiratory problems.
author: आकांख्या राउत
content:
बुराड़ी की गीता को दिवाली के बाद से खांसी, सीने में दर्द और सांस लेने में परेशानी हो रही है.
बीते अगस्त, 2026 में स्वास्थ्य एवं परिवार कल्याण मंत्रालय ने एक नोटिस जारी किया. इसके तहत सितंबर से फरवरी के बीच देश के सभी जिला अस्पतालों और मेडिकल कॉलेजों में चेस्ट क्लीनिक शुरू किए जाने थे.
इसके बाद राष्ट्रीय रोग नियंत्रण केंद्र ने इन क्लीनिकों के लिए दिशानिर्देश भी जारी किए. इन निर्देशों के मुताबिक, क्लीनिक में मरीजों की जांच और इलाज के लिए जरूरी मेडिकल स्टाफ होना चाहिए. साथ ही, मरीजों को यह भी समझाया जाना चाहिए कि वायु प्रदूषण से होने वाली बीमारियों से कैसे बचें और कौन-सी सावधानियां बरतें. इसके बाद 6 नवंबर को दिल्ली के स्वास्थ्य विभाग ने हफ्तेभर के भीतर जिला अस्पतालों में ये चेस्ट क्लीनिक खोलने का निर्देश दिया.
न्यूज़लॉन्ड्री ने बुराड़ी, जहांगीरपुरी और जीटीबी नगर के अस्पताल का दौरा किया. गौरतलब है कि ये तीनों इलाके प्रदूषण से प्रभावित हैं. बुराड़ी और जहांगीरपुरी में सड़क की धूल प्रदूषण का एक बड़ा कारक है. इन इलाकों में बिना मास्क के सड़क पर खड़ा रहना भी मुश्किल हो जाता है.
बुराड़ी में हमारी मुलाकात गीता से हुई. गीता को दिवाली के बाद से खांसी, सीने में दर्द और सांस लेने में परेशानी हो रही थी.
देखिए हमारी यह खास रिपोर्ट.
भ्रामक सूचनाओं के दौर में आपको ऐसी खबरों की जरूरत है, जिन पर आप भरोसा कर सकें. न्यूज़लॉन्ड्री आपके लिए ऐसी ही खबरें लेकर आता है. हमारी पत्रकारिता को मजबूत करने के लिए सब्सक्राइब करें.

title: Myanmar vows to defy ‘inappropriate’ measures in Rohingya genocide ruling
description: Min Aung Hlaing dismisses the landmark ruling as a “one-sided accusation” and signals resistance to court-ordered reparations, safe Rohingya returns and prosecutions.
author: Associated Press
content:
Min Aung Hlaing dismisses the landmark ruling as a “one-sided accusation” and signals resistance to court-ordered reparations, safe Rohingya returns and prosecutions.
The leader of the Myanmar military-backed government said it will refuse to comply with some aspects of a landmark international court ruling that found the country responsible for genocide against the Rohingya minority.
President Min Aung Hlaing told a Cabinet meeting that his government would act accordingly but would reject measures it considered “inappropriate,” the state-run Global New Light of Myanmar newspaper reported on Thursday.
The president on Wednesday described the case as a “one-sided accusation” against the country, and said the use of the term “genocide” had seriously damaged Myanmar’s reputation.
The International Court of Justice, the United Nations’ top court, ruled last week that Myanmar committed genocide against the Rohingya in a brutal 2017 military operation. The court found that Myanmar’s security forces killed thousands of Rohingya civilians, perpetrated widespread acts of sexual violence and acts of extreme violence against children.
The court rejected Myanmar’s defense that the campaign was a legitimate operation against insurgents. Min Aung Hlaing, the former military leader, was in charge of the operation.
The report said that Min Aung Hlaing considered himself primarily responsible for all matters concerning Myanmar as the country’s leader, and would not accept actions that undermined the nation.
“Myanmar would take the actions appropriate for a responsible country but would not comply with requirements it considered inappropriate,” he said, without elaborating.
Myanmar’s government earlier described the International Court of Justice’s decision as unfair and a great disappointment, pointing out that six of the 15 judges had dissented.
The ruling was the first time the international court has ruled that a state committed genocide. It ordered Myanmar’s government to allow the Rohingya to return home safely, pay reparations and prosecute those suspected of having committed genocide.
The court’s rulings are final and legally binding, but it has no way to enforce them beyond reporting noncompliance to the U.N. Security Council. Myanmar is considered unlikely to fulfill any of the court’s demands.
The separate International Criminal Court, or ICC, also based in The Hague and considering legal action concerning Myanmar and the Rohingya, is under U.S. sanctions along with many of its judges and staff, so any action by the Security Council could face a U.S. veto. The council’s other permanent members, China and Russia, which maintain close relations with Min Aung Hlaing’s administration and have supported it internationally, could also block action.
ICC prosecutors requested an arrest warrant for Min Aung Hlaing in late 2024 over alleged crimes against humanity against the Rohingya, but judges have yet to publicly announce a decision.
Many Western governments and international organisations have pressed Myanmar to comply with the ICJ ruling. Human rights groups urged targeted sanctions against the military, its economic networks and arms supplies to enforce accountability.
The United Kingdom said Monday that it formally recognised the genocide against the Rohingya. It imposed sanctions on five senior Myanmar military officers, announced plans to restrict aviation fuel supplies to Myanmar and pledged 8 million pounds ($10.5 million) for humanitarian assistance and justice initiatives.
The Security Council is expected to meet privately on Dec. 7 at the request of the U.K., which expelled Myanmar’s defence attaché after the ruling.
Myanmar is now embroiled in a bloody civil war, with pro-democracy and other militias fighting against the military. Min Aung Hlaing seized power from Aung San Suu Kyi ‘s elected government in 2021 and became president earlier this year in an election critics said was neither free nor fair.
___
This version corrects paragraph 11 to state that the ICC, not the ICJ, is under U.S. sanctions.

title: Delhi’s chest clinics are filling up as toxic air takes its toll
description: Geeta, a resident of Burari, has been suffering from a cough, chest pain, and breathing difficulties since Diwali.
author: Akankhya Rout
content:
Geeta, a resident of Burari, has been suffering from a cough, chest pain, and breathing difficulties since Diwali.
In August 2026, the health ministry issued a notice directing all district hospitals and medical colleges to set up chest clinics, to be operational between September and February.
The National Centre for Disease Control (NCDC) then issued guidelines for these clinics. They are to be staffed with the medical personnel needed to examine and treat patients, who are also to be counselled on how to avoid pollution-related illnesses and what precautions to take. On November 6, the Delhi health department directed district hospitals to open these clinics within a week.
Newslaundry visited hospitals in Burari, Jahangirpuri, and GTB Nagar – areas badly affected by pollution. In Burari and Jahangirpuri, road dust is a major contributor; and it is hard to even stand on the street without a mask.
In Burari, we met Geeta, a local resident, who has had a cough, chest pain and breathing difficulties since Diwali.

title: Chennai couple donates Rs 208 crore gold, diamonds to Tirumala Balaji temple
description: Chennai-based couple Vardhaman Jain and Radhika Jain have made a historic donation of 121 kg of gold ornaments and diamonds, valued at Rs 208 crore, to the Tirumala Tirupati Devasthanams. This is considered the largest individual offering to Lord Venkateswara, with Andhra Pradesh Chief Minister N Chandrababu Naidu present at the event, who lauded the devotion and discussed TTD's future plans.
author: Saisuresh
content:
A Chennai-based couple made history with an unprecedented Rs 208 crore gold and diamond donation to the revered Tirumala Tirupati Devasthanams, marking the largest individual offering to Lord Venkateswara.
Key Points
- Chennai-based couple Vardhaman and Radhika Jain donated 121 kg of gold ornaments and diamonds worth Rs 208 crore to Tirumala Tirupati Devasthanams on Thursday.
- The donation, comprising 46 ornaments in nine sets and 238.2 carats of diamonds, is the largest offering ever made by an individual devotee to Lord Venkateswara.
- Andhra Pradesh Chief Minister N Chandrababu Naidu, present at the event, highlighted the historical devotion to the deity and TTD's transparent operations.
- The donation included 106 kg of gold for Srivaru and a 15-kg costume for Goddess Sri Padmavati Ammavaru.
- Naidu also announced plans to build 5,000 temples with TTD's help and expand 'anna prasadam' services.
Chennai-based devotee Vardhaman Jain and his wife Radhika Jain on Thursday donated 121 kg of gold ornaments and diamonds valued at around Rs 208 crore to Tirumala Tirupati Devasthanams in the presence of Chief Minister N Chandrababu Naidu here.
The donation comprises 46 ornaments in nine sets, which include a Srivaru crown, Padma Paadalu (ornaments for feet) and 238.2 carats of diamonds, among others.
"The Jain couple from Chennai donated 121 kg of gold ornaments to Srivaru in the presence of CM Chandrababu," an official press release said.
According to TTD sources, this would be the largest offering ever made by an individual devotee to Lord Venkateswara at Tirumala.
Details Of The Historic Donation
Out of the gems and jewellery donated, the golden ornaments donated to Srivaru weighed 106 kg, while Goddess Sri Padmavati Ammavaru received a 15-kg costume.
A golden tiger nail, myriad varieties of chains, crowns, gems and several other varieties of ornaments were part of the bountiful donation.
The CM thanked the Jains for their massive donation to the deity and observed that the glory of Srivaru is inexplicable.
An unprecedented development unfolded today in Tirumala, said Naidu, observing that the deity is adorned with 120 kg of gold ornaments every day.
Naidu said he was fortunate to have been part of this historic development, where valuable diamonds were also donated with the golden ornaments, valued at around Rs 206 crore in total.
CM Naidu On Devotion And TTD's Future
From the time of medieval king Sri Krishna Devaraya to the current Jains, devotion to the deity has continued and is also rising, said the CM.
According to the CM, Pallava, Chera, Chola and Pandya kings had developed the Tirupati temple while Mysuru and Maratha kings had donated several gifts and ornaments.
Naidu noted that Vijayanagara king Sri Krishna Devaraya had promoted the Hindu faith and also donated several ornaments to Lord Sri Venkateswara.
He underscored that the 'Ratna Kireetam' (a precious stones encrusted crown) and 'Peetambaram', ornaments donated by him, had a chequered history.
Though several temples were attacked in the past, nobody dared to undertake that adventure with Sri Venkateswara temple, said Naidu.
Observing that TTD is the most transparent organisation, the CM said the temple body was using all its resources towards devotees.
Naidu urged the temple body to save the sanctity of the deity and work for the protection of cows and added that the Tirupati temple should become a synonym for sacredness.
Naidu highlighted that 5,000 temples will be built with TTD's help and called for 'anna prasadam' (free food for devotees) wherever there is a temple.
He said temples should also be built overseas where Hindus are in large numbers.
Further, the CM appealed to devotees to cooperate with TTD and come forward in whichever way they could contribute.

title: Own a flat in Maharashtra? Get ready for a separate property card
description: The Maharashtra government has proposed a new system of 'Vertical Property Cards' to issue separate property cards for individual flats in buildings. This aims to enhance transparency in property transactions, reduce disputes, and record comprehensive details of ownership, area, rights, and liabilities for each unit. The draft rules, Maharashtra Land Revenue (Preparation and Maintenance of Records of Rights and Registers for Units in Buildings) Rules, 2026, will be published for public suggestions.
author: Senjo M R
content:
Maharashtra is set to revolutionise property ownership with its proposed "Vertical Property Card" system, aiming to bring unprecedented transparency and clarity to individual flat ownership and transactions across the state.
Key Points
- Maharashtra government proposes "Vertical Property Cards" for individual flats to enhance transparency and reduce disputes.
- Each flat will receive a unique property card detailing ownership, area, rights, mortgages, and other liabilities.
- The system will involve a main property record for the building and common areas, followed by separate records for each unit.
- Applications for these records will be open to landowners, developers, and flat owners, requiring sanctioned plans and registered documents.
- The draft rules will be published for 30 days to invite public objections and suggestions before finalisation and phased implementation.
The Maharashtra government has proposed issuing separate property cards for individual flats in buildings, recording details of ownership, area, associated rights, mortgages and other liabilities.
The move is aimed at bringing greater transparency to property transactions and reducing ownership disputes.
Talking to reporters, revenue minister Chandrashekhar Bawankule said the proposed system, called the Vertical Property Card, seeks to create an independent supplementary record of rights for every eligible residential or other unit, alongside the existing land records, under the Maharashtra Land Revenue Code, 1966.
The state government has proposed the Maharashtra Land Revenue (Preparation and Maintenance of Records of Rights and Registers for Units in Buildings) Rules, 2026, to provide a uniform mechanism for preparing and maintaining these records, he said.
Understanding The Vertical Property Card System
Under the proposed system, a main property record will first be prepared for the building and its common areas, followed by a separate record for each individual flat or unit. Every unit will be assigned a unique identification number.
The records will include the unit number, name of the holder, sanctioned area, associated rights and liabilities. Details of the building's sanctioned area, common spaces, open spaces and areas under roads will also be incorporated.
Different formats have been proposed for urban and rural areas. In urban land survey areas, formats D-1 and D-2 will be used for buildings and individual flats, respectively. In rural and other areas, formats I-A and I-B, corresponding to Village Forms 7-C and 7-D, have been proposed.
Application Process And Required Documents
Entries in the property cards will be based on sanctioned building plans, relevant certificates and registered documents. For new projects, the commencement certificate issued by the competent planning authority will form the basis, while existing buildings will require occupancy certificates and registered documents.
Landowners, promoters, developers, flat owners and authorised representatives of institutions will be eligible to apply for the records.
Depending on the nature of the project, applicants will have to submit the original property record, sanctioned building plan, relevant certificates, apartment deeds, transfer agreements or deemed conveyance documents and other registered papers, he said.
Comprehensive Details And Digital Integration
The proposed system will also incorporate details of bank loans, mortgages, property tax arrears, institutional dues, court-imposed restrictions and government liabilities, based on the applicable procedures and verified information, the minister said.
The entire process, from application and information collection to scrutiny, rectification, approval and distribution of digitally signed property cards, will be carried out through an integrated online system.
The government has also proposed linking the system with the departments of land records, cooperation, local self-government, planning authorities and registration to facilitate digital exchange of information.
In cases of demolition, redevelopment or reconstruction, existing records will be closed or updated in accordance with the rules, and fresh records will be prepared on the basis of newly sanctioned building plans.
Implementation And Expected Benefits
The proposed framework will also require amendments to relevant laws and rules governing cooperative societies, apartment ownership, municipal corporations and town planning. An interdepartmental committee and an empowered commissioner-level office have been proposed to ensure coordination, according to Bawankule.
The draft rules will be published for 30 days to invite objections and suggestions. After examining the responses, the government plans to finalise the rules, undertake pilot implementation and subsequently extend the system across the state in phases.
The initiative is expected to make ownership records more transparent, facilitate property purchases, sales and bank loans, improve disclosure of liabilities and encumbrances, reduce property-related disputes and fraud, and ensure that government records remain updated.

title: Key Hasina aide, two others held as Bangladesh braces for political unrest
description: Bangladesh's former deputy press secretary to ousted prime minister Sheikh Hasina, KM Shakhawat Moon, was arrested with two others in Dhaka on Thursday. The arrests come amidst heightened political tensions and increased security deployments across the country, ahead of Hasina's anticipated return next month. Incidents of violence have been reported, and the banned Awami League is promoting a lockdown, further escalating concerns.
author: Senjo M R
content:
Amidst escalating political tensions in Bangladesh, former deputy press secretary to ousted prime minister Sheikh Hasina, KM Shakhawat Moon, was arrested along with two others in Dhaka on Thursday, as the government beefs up security ahead of Hasina's anticipated return.
Key Points
- Former deputy press secretary to Sheikh Hasina, KM Shakhawat Moon, was arrested in Dhaka early Thursday.
- Two others, Mohammad Ilias Hossain and Sufi Mohammad Al Mamun, were also taken into custody.
- The arrests occurred amidst heightened political tensions in Bangladesh over Sheikh Hasina's planned return next month.
- Security has been beefed up across several districts, with border paramilitary forces deployed, especially in Hasina's home district Gopalganj.
- The Awami League, whose activities are banned, is promoting a lockdown for November 29 and 30, raising concerns about escalating tensions.
Bangladesh's ousted prime minister Sheikh Hasina's former deputy press secretary was arrested along with two others in the national capital early Thursday, official media reported.
KM Shakhawat Moon, Hasina's former deputy press secretary, and two others were taken into custody early Thursday from the Dhanmondi-27 area, the state-run BSS news agency reported.
The two others arrested along with Moon are former deputy commissioner Mohammad Ilias Hossain and income tax lawyer Sufi Mohammad Al Mamun, it added.
According to the Daily Star newspaper, Moon, Hossain and Mamun were taken into police custody after Jatiyatabadi Chhatra Dal (JCD) leaders and activists detained them in Dhaka's Dhanmondi area.
The JCD is the student wing of the ruling Bangladesh Nationalist Party.
Mohammadpur Police Station duty officer Sub-Inspector Masudur Rahman said police were preparing to produce the trio before a court.
Heightened Security Amidst Political Tensions
The BNP-led government has beefed up security across several districts, deploying 108 platoons of border paramilitary force, including 56 in Hasina's home district Gopalganj, as political tensions mount over her planned return next month.
There have been incidents of violence, including arson attacks targeting trains, buses and banks, across Bangladesh in recent weeks surrounding Hasina's possible return. Hasina has been staying in India since fleeing Dhaka in August 2024 following a student-led uprising that toppled her government.
Police blamed activists of the Awami League and its affiliated organisations for recent incidents of violence.
The heightened security comes amid fears that Hasina's supporters could intensify violence and sabotage in the coming days.
Government Stance And Future Outlook
Awami League, whose activities have been banned, is promoting a lockdown programme for November 29 and 30 through online platforms, adding to concerns over a possible escalation of tensions.
On Wednesday, Home Minister Salahuddin Ahmed said Awami League would never be allowed to do politics in Bangladesh.
Ahmed said Awami League is a "fascist and mafia force" responsible for the mass killings during the July 2024 uprising, BSS reported.

title: Maharashtra: ‘Work In Coordination To Ensure Effective Implementation Of Seva Doot Abhiyan,’ Says BJP
description: BJP Maharashtra President Ravindra Chavan urged party workers and office-bearers to coordinate for the nationwide ‘Seva Doot Abhiyan’, scheduled from December 1 to 25, 2026. At a Thane-Konkan divisional workshop in Panvel, leaders discussed planning and grassroots implementation to address public grievances and spread awareness of government welfare schemes.
author: Kalpesh Mhamunkar
content:
Mumbai, November 26, 2026: Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) State President Ravindra Chavan has urged party workers and office-bearers to work in close coordination to ensure the successful execution of the upcoming 'Seva Doot Abhiyan'.
He was addressing party members during a Thane-Konkan divisional workshop held in Panvel as part of the preparations for the nationwide campaign.
The BJP is scheduled to conduct the 'Seva Doot Abhiyan' across the country from December 1 to December 25, 2026. During the divisional workshop, party leaders held detailed discussions regarding the operational methodology, micro-planning and strategies for the effective implementation of the drive on the ground.
Campaign To Reach Every Section Of Society
Speaking at the event, Chavan emphasised that the primary objective of the campaign is to reach every section of society, understand their difficulties and grievances, and provide them with the necessary assistance.
He stated that the initiative also aims to spread awareness about various public welfare schemes launched by the Central and State governments right down to the grassroots level, appealing to all office-bearers and workers to collaborate seamlessly to make the campaign a success.
Also Watch:
Key Leaders Attend Divisional Workshop
The workshop saw a large turnout of key office-bearers and party workers from the Thane and Konkan divisions. Prominent leaders present at the event included State General Secretary MLA Madhavitaai Naik, Member of Parliament Dr. Hemant Savara, Member of Parliament Dhairyashil Patil, MLA Prashant Thakur, MLA Pramod Jathar, MLA Vikrant Patil, and BJP North Raigad District President Avinash Koli.

title: Maha Deputy CM Sunetra Pawar Directs Redistribution Of Unspent Sports Complex Funds, Seeks Immediate Cabinet
description: Maharashtra Deputy CM Sunetra Pawar directed officials to reclaim unspent funds from sports complex committees and redistribute them to facilities requiring urgent financial assistance. Chairing a meeting in Mumbai, she approved eligible sports infrastructure proposals and instructed officials to expedite cabinet approvals for projects exceeding the prescribed government grant limits.
author: Kalpesh Mhamunkar
content:
Mumbai: Deputy Chief Minister and Minister for Sports and Youth Welfare Sunetra Ajit Pawar has issued strict directives to reclaim long-unspent funds lying with various sports complex committees and redistribute them to other sports complexes in urgent need of financial assistance. Emphasising the need to accelerate the development of sports infrastructure across Maharashtra, she also instructed officials to ensure the immediate utilisation of remaining balances and to swiftly place proposals exceeding government grant limits before the state cabinet for approval.
Sports Infrastructure Development And Administrative Approvals
Pawar issued these key instructions while chairing a meeting of the State Sports Development Committee at the Sahyadri State Guest House on Thursday. The meeting was convened to review and grant administrative approvals to various divisional, district, and taluka-level sports complexes across the state, ensuring that the development of athletic facilities is not hampered by a shortage of funds and that existing allocations are utilised optimally.
During the session, multiple proposals for taluka, district, and divisional sports complexes were presented for consideration. Projects that fell within the prescribed government grant limits were granted administrative approval on the spot, while officials were directed to expedite the cabinet approval process for larger proposals requiring additional funding.
Also Watch:
Senior Officials Attend Committee Meeting
The meeting was attended by several top bureaucrats, including Principal Secretary of the Sports Department Ranjit Singh Deol, Secretary to the Deputy Chief Minister Dr Rajesh Deshmukh, Commissioner of Sports and Youth Services Deepak Singla, and Public Works Department Secretary Abasaheb Nagargoje, along with senior officials from the Finance, Planning, Urban Development-2, Revenue, and Sports departments.

title: Maharashtra Ranks Second In India Under AgriStack Scheme, Issues Digital Farmer IDs To 1.44 Crore
description: Maharashtra secured the second position nationally under the AgriStack scheme, issuing digital Farmer IDs to 1.44 crore farmers. Agriculture Minister Dattatray Bharne urged remaining farmers to register. The initiative simplifies access to crop insurance, compensation and government schemes by linking farmers' land records with Aadhaar.
author: Kalpesh Mhamunkar
content:
Mumbai: Maharashtra has secured the second position in the country under the AgriStack scheme, with 1.44 crore farmers in the state already issued a unique digital identity, known as a Farmer ID. Agriculture Minister Dattatray Bharne announced the milestone on Thursday and appealed to the remaining eligible farmers across the state to complete their registration at the earliest.
Digital Registration Under AgriStack Scheme
Implemented in accordance with Central Government guidelines, the AgriStack initiative aims to expand digital services in the agricultural sector and ensure the fast, transparent, and effective delivery of government schemes. The state government officially rolled out the scheme following a Government Resolution (GR) issued on October 18, 2024. According to the 2021 Agricultural Census, Maharashtra has 1.71 crore landholding farmers, of which 1.44 crore have been successfully registered so far, while enrolment for the rest is actively underway.
Farmer IDs Streamline Access To Schemes
Minister Bharne highlighted that the digital platform links farmers and their land records with Aadhaar, bringing transparency to beneficiary verification and eliminating the need for repeated document submissions to prove land ownership. This streamlined system facilitates easier access to crop insurance, disaster relief compensation, agricultural infrastructure funds, credit schemes, and expert farming advisories. Registration through Common Service Centres (CSCs) commenced on January 21, 2025, and holding a Farmer ID was made mandatory on April 15, 2025, to avail of agricultural government schemes. Reflecting the scheme's wide adoption, 84.60 lakh out of the 85.58 lakh beneficiaries of the recent 24th instalment of the PM Kisan Samman Nidhi Yojana in Maharashtra possess an AgriStack ID. Furthermore, farmers holding joint land records (7/12 extracts) are also being enrolled with a 'Joint' remark noted in their ownership details.
Digital Crop Surveys And Forest Landholders
Alongside farmer registration, the state has made significant strides in accurate agricultural data collection through digital crop surveys. Initiated on a pilot basis in Kharif 2023 and conducted via the central DCS app under the E-Pik Pahani drive, the survey successfully covered over 3.10 crore plots during the 2026 Kharif season.
To ensure inclusivity, the state is also integrating forest rights (Vanpatta) landholders into the AgriStack network. Out of nearly two lakh forest rights farmers in Maharashtra, the Tribal Development Department has provided data for 1.58 lakh individuals, and 78,000 of them have already completed their registration.
Registration For Exceptional Land Record Cases
Additionally, the government has opened a pathway for farmers facing exceptional or non-standard land record cases. Following recommendations from a committee headed by the Settlement Commissioner and Director of Land Records in Pune, the Revenue Department issued a GR on November 6, 2026. Under the procedural guidelines set in the September 18, 2026 GR, such applications will undergo inspection by the Village Revenue Officer, verification by the Circle Officer, and final approval by the Tehsildar. Once cleared, the data will be forwarded to the Central Project Management Unit, enabling these previously excluded farmers to obtain their Farmer IDs through CSCs just like regular applicants.
Also Watch:
Minister Urges Farmers To Complete Registration
Concluding his appeal, Minister Bharne urged unregistered farmers to visit their nearest 'Aaple Sarkar Seva Kendra' or register online directly via the official portal at https://mhfr.agristack.gov.in/farmer-registry-mh/#/. Farmers seeking further assistance or information have been advised to contact their local agriculture officers.
