title: India got nearly $31 billion in climate and sustainability funding—where did the money go?
description: India attracted nearly $31 billion in climate and sustainability equity funding since 2021, but more than 90% went to power and transport. The country needs an estimated $500 billion annually to meet its climate goals.
author: CNBCTV18.com
content:
India got nearly $31 billion in climate and sustainability funding—where did the money go?
- Published OnNov 26, 2026 | 20:40 IST
- Last Updated OnNov 26, 2026 | 20:40 IST
While green equity funding surged significantly, over ninety percent concentrated heavily in power and transport due to established business models and early policy support. Critical segments like agriculture, waste, and
India has attracted nearly $31 billion in climate and sustainability equity funding since 2021, but more than 90% of the money has gone into just two sectors — power and low-carbon fuels, and transport — highlighting how investment remains concentrated in areas with more established business models.
A report by the Indian Venture and Alternate Capital Association (IVCA) and Boston Consulting Group (BCG) found that power and low-carbon fuels attracted about $19 billion, while transport drew another $9.5 billion between 2021 and October 2026.
The report, titled India’s Climate & Sustainability Moment: Capital, Opportunity and the Road Ahead, analysed equity investments in companies with a significant presence in India. The data was compiled from deals tracked by Tracxn and Venture Intelligence, with duplicate transactions removed. Debt financing and initial public offerings were excluded.
Where did the money go?
Power and low-carbon fuels attracted the largest share, at about $19 billion. The category includes renewable energy and other technologies supporting India's shift towards cleaner power.
Transport received another $9.5 billion, taking the combined investment in the two sectors to about $28.5 billion. According to the report, both benefited from early policy support that helped make investments commercially viable.
Funding for other sectors was considerably smaller. Manufacturing and waste attracted about $1 billion each, while agriculture received roughly $1 billion. Other climate and sustainability segments together drew around $500 million.
Why did investors favour these sectors?
Capital largely flowed to areas where policy support, market demand and the prospect of commercial returns came together, the report said.
In power, long-term power purchase agreements, renewable-energy auctions and other policy measures helped give investors greater visibility on returns. Transport benefited from policies supporting electric vehicles, battery manufacturing and cleaner mobility.
Renewable power and electric mobility have increasingly become commercially viable, while areas such as energy storage, green hydrogen, bioenergy and recycling continue to face funding constraints and need policy support to scale up, the report said.
Despite attracting nearly $31 billion since 2021, India will need far more capital to meet its climate and sustainability commitments.
The report estimates that India could require $22 trillion-$24 trillion in investments between 2026 and 2070, or roughly $500 billion a year, against current annual climate investment of about $135 billion.

title: Solar Defence tests indigenous system designed to take down drone swarms
description: Solar Defence and Aerospace has completed trials of Bhargavastra, a vehicle-mounted system combining air defence rockets and guided micro-missiles to counter drone swarms.
author: CNBCTV18.com
content:
Solar Defence tests indigenous system designed to take down drone swarms
- Published OnNov 26, 2026 | 19:49 IST
- Last Updated OnNov 26, 2026 | 19:49 IST
Solar Defence and Aerospace has completed trials of Bhargavastra, a vehicle-mounted system combining air defence rockets and guided micro-missiles to counter drone swarms.
Solar Defence and Aerospace Limited (SDAL) has successfully completed the in-house development trials of Bhargavastra, an indigenous vehicle-mounted counter-swarm drone system, at the Pokaran field firing ranges in Rajasthan.
The trials were conducted between November 20 and November 24, 2026, following the successful design, development and integration of the system by the company.
According to SDAL, Bhargavastra is India's first indigenously designed and developed two-layer Vehicle-Mounted Counter Swarm Drone System (VMCSDS). It is designed to provide an integrated defence against the growing threat posed by enemy drone swarms.
The system combines air defence rockets and guided micro-missiles to create a two-layer defence mechanism, with the capability to engage multiple drones simultaneously.
Also read: Tamil Nadu breaks new ground with 15-day paternity leave for government employees
The development comes amid growing concerns over the use of unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) and coordinated drone swarms in modern warfare. Such systems pose an emerging challenge to conventional air defence infrastructure, increasing the need for specialised counter-drone capabilities.
With Bhargavastra, SDAL aims to offer an indigenous solution to address this evolving threat through a vehicle-mounted platform capable of countering multiple incoming drones.
The successful completion of the development trials marks a key milestone in the company's efforts to develop indigenous defence technologies.

title: मोगा की धरती से AAP का चुनावी शंखनाद: CM भगवंत मान ने पेश किया रिपोर्ट कार्ड, बोले- 'जब नीयत साफ हो तो भीड़ जुटानी नहीं पड़ती
description: पंजाब के मोगा में आयोजित 'खुशहाल पंजाब' महारैली में उमड़े दो लाख से अधिक लोगों के जनसैलाब ने राज्य की राजनीति में हलचल तेज कर दी है. इस रिकॉर्डतोड़ भीड़ के बीच मुख्यमंत्री भगवंत सिंह मान ने 2027 के विधानसभा चुनावों का बिगुल फूंकते हुए इसे अपनी सरकार की 'काम की राजनीति' पर जनता की ऐतिहासिक मुहर बताया.
author: भूपेंद्र राय
content:
पंजाब विधानसभा चुनाव 2027 की सरगर्मी तेज है. चुनाव से पहले मालवा के केंद्र मोगा को सत्ता के शक्ति प्रदर्शन का सबसे बड़ा अखाड़ा बनाया जा रहा है. आम आदमी पार्टी (AAP) के स्थापना दिवस के मौके पर गुरुवार को मोगा में 'खुशहाल पंजाब' महारैली आयोजित की गई. इस रैली के जरिए मुख्यमंत्री भगवंत सिंह मान ने चुनावी बिगुल फूंक दिया है. पार्टी के मुताबिक, इस रैली में उमड़े दो लाख लोगों के जनसैलाब के बीच सीएम मान ने अपनी सरकार के साढ़े चार साल के कामकाज का रिपोर्ट कार्ड पेश किया और इसे 'काम की राजनीति' पर जनता की ऐतिहासिक मुहर करार दिया.
मोगा में दो लाख लोगों के उमड़े जनसैलाब को मुख्यमंत्री भगवंत सिंह मान और आम आदमी पार्टी (आप) ने 'काम की राजनीति' पर एक ऐतिहासिक मुहर करार दिया है. मुख्यमंत्री ने कहा कि जब नीयत साफ हो और वादे ठोस नतीजों में बदलें, तो लोगों को खोखले नारों के जरिए जुटाने की जरूरत नहीं पड़ती. उन्होंने कहा कि जीरो बिजली बिल और बिना रिश्वत के मिली 77,000 से अधिक सरकारी नौकरियों से लेकर नहरों के अंतिम छोर (टेल) तक पहुंचे पानी, ₹10 लाख तक के मुफ्त इलाज और महिलाओं के लिए वित्तीय सहायता तक, सरकार के कार्यों ने लोगों को इस सोच से जुड़ने का ठोस कारण दिया है. मुख्यमंत्री मान ने कहा, 'यह विशाल जनसमूह एक स्पष्ट राजनीतिक संदेश देता है कि पंजाब पुराने खोखले वादों से आगे निकल चुका है और अब विकास, तरक्की और खुशहाली को चुन रहा है.'
मुख्यमंत्री भगवंत सिंह मान ने 'एक्स' (X) पर पोस्ट किया, जिसमें उन्होंने 'खुशहाल पंजाब' महारैली की झलकियां शेयर कीं और लिखा कि, 'आज मोगा की धरती पर लाखों पंजाबियों का उमड़ा यह विशाल जनसैलाब कोई साधारण भीड़ नहीं थी. यह काम की राजनीति पर लगी ऐतिहासिक मुहर थी. यह रिकॉर्डतोड़ ऐतिहासिक जनसमूह इस बात का सबूत है कि पंजाब अब पुराने खोखले वादों पर यकीन नहीं करता. यह तरक्की, विकास और खुशहाली को चुनता है. इस अथाह प्यार, विश्वास और समर्थन के लिए हर पंजाबी का तहे दिल से धन्यवाद.'
मुख्यमंत्री भगवंत सिंह मान ने महारैली को संबोधित करते हुए कहा, 'आज मैं पंजाब के लोगों से सीधे तौर पर अपने किए गए कामों और पूरे किए गए वादों के बारे में बात करना चाहता हूं. जिन लोगों ने दशकों तक इस राज्य पर राज किया, उन्हें भी जनता को बताना चाहिए कि उन्होंने पंजाब के लिए क्या किया. उनके पास सत्ता के कई साल थे, लेकिन राज्य लगातार समस्याओं से जूझता रहा. हमारी सरकार जनता के सामने अपना रिपोर्ट कार्ड पेश कर रही है क्योंकि हमारा मानना है कि सरकार जनता के प्रति जवाबदेह होनी चाहिए.'
शिरोमणि अकाली दल, कांग्रेस और भाजपा पर तीखा हमला बोलते हुए मुख्यमंत्री ने कहा, 'इन पार्टियों ने सालों तक पंजाब पर राज किया और बारी-बारी से सत्ता का आनंद लिया. इन्होंने एक-दूसरे पर आरोप लगाए, वादे किए और चुनाव के बाद जनता को भूल गए. अब ये सभी एकजुट हो रहे हैं क्योंकि ये आम आदमी पार्टी की सरकार द्वारा किए जा रहे कामों से घबराए हुए हैं. पंजाब के लोग इनका इतिहास जानते हैं और इनके नए राजनीतिक गठबंधनों से गुमराह नहीं होंगे.'
अकाली दल के नेतृत्व का हवाला देते हुए उन्होंने कहा, 'पंजाब के लोग जानते हैं कि अकाली दल को कौन चला रहा है और सत्ता में रहते हुए इस पार्टी ने क्या किया है. सुखबीर सिंह बादल, बिक्रम सिंह मजीठिया और अन्य अकाली नेताओं को जनता को जवाब देना होगा. पार्टी अपने नारे बदलकर या नए राजनीतिक समझौते करके जवाबदेही से भाग नहीं सकती.'
8 दिसंबर को मोगा के इसी मैदान में प्रधानमंत्री नरेंद्र मोदी की प्रस्तावित रैली का जिक्र करते हुए मुख्यमंत्री भगवंत सिंह मान ने कहा, 'जो लोग सालों तक एक-दूसरे की आलोचना करते रहे, वे अब एक ही मंच साझा करने की तैयारी कर रहे हैं. नरेंद्र मोदी, अमित शाह, रवनीत सिंह बिट्टू, सुनील जाखड़, केवल सिंह ढिल्लों, अश्विनी कुमार और तरुण चुघ उन नेताओं में शामिल हैं, जिनकी राजनीति को पंजाब के लोगों ने बहुत करीब से देखा है. उन्हें बताना चाहिए कि उन्होंने पंजाब के लिए क्या किया है.' उन्होंने कहा, 'चाहे वे अकाली दल, कांग्रेस या भाजपा से जुड़े हों, पंजाब के लोगों ने इन सभी की सरकारें देखी हैं. इनके पास राज्य के लिए काम करने के मौके थे. आज ये इसलिए हाथ नहीं मिला रहे हैं कि इनके मन में अचानक पंजाब के लिए प्यार जाग उठा है, बल्कि इसलिए एक साथ आ रहे हैं क्योंकि ये आम आदमी पार्टी की सरकार के कामों को रोकना चाहते हैं. जनता 2027 में इन्हें करारा जवाब देगी.'
सरकार के रोजगार रिकॉर्ड को रेखांकित करते हुए मुख्यमंत्री भगवंत सिंह मान ने कहा, 'हमने पंजाब के युवाओं को 77,182 सरकारी नौकरियां दी हैं. ये नौकरियां मेरिट के आधार पर और पारदर्शी प्रक्रिया के जरिए दी गई हैं.'
घरों को दी जा रही बिजली राहत के बारे में बोलते हुए मुख्यमंत्री भगवंत सिंह मान ने कहा, 'आज पंजाब के लगभग 90 प्रतिशत घरों के बिजली बिल जीरो आ रहे हैं. यह कोई नारा या कागजी वादा नहीं है, बल्कि यह एक ऐसी राहत है जो आम परिवारों तक पहुंच रही है.'
कृषि क्षेत्र को बिजली आपूर्ति के बारे में मुख्यमंत्री ने कहा, 'हमारे किसानों को अब दिन के समय बिजली मिल रही है. वे सुबह लगभग 9 बजे अपने खेतों में जा सकते हैं और शाम 5 बजे तक अपनी मोटरें बंद करके घर लौट सकते हैं.'
स्वास्थ्य बीमा योजना के बारे में बात करते हुए मुख्यमंत्री भगवंत सिंह मान ने कहा, 'हम एक ऐसी स्वास्थ्य बीमा योजना लेकर आए हैं, जिसके तहत पात्र परिवार ₹10 लाख तक का इलाज करवा सकते हैं. लगभग 65 लाख परिवार इस सुविधा के पात्र हैं और करीब 54 से 55 लाख स्वास्थ्य कार्ड जारी किए जा चुके हैं.'
तीन विवादित कृषि कानूनों के खिलाफ किसान आंदोलन का जिक्र करते हुए मुख्यमंत्री भगवंत सिंह मान ने कहा, 'किसान आंदोलन के दौरान लगभग 750 किसानों ने अपनी जान गंवाई. ये सिर्फ आंकड़े नहीं थे, बल्कि वे किसी के पिता, बेटे, भाई और परिवार के सदस्य थे. पंजाब उनकी कुर्बानियों को कभी नहीं भूलेगा. हमारी सरकार ने शहीद हुए किसानों के परिवारों को 5 लाख रुपये की वित्तीय सहायता और सरकारी नौकरियां दी हैं.'
पंजाब के अधिकारों और हितों से जुड़े मुद्दे उठाते हुए उन्होंने कहा, 'मैंने जगतार सिंह हवारा के संबंध में पत्र लिखा है. हमने ग्रामीण विकास कोष (आरडीएफ), बंदी सिखों की रिहाई और पंजाब को उसके वाजिब अधिकार देने का मुद्दा भी लगातार उठाया है. ये राज्य और इसके लोगों के लिए अहम मुद्दे हैं और हम इन्हें उठाते रहेंगे.'
'आप' नेता और पंजाब प्रभारी मनीष सिसोदिया ने कहा, 'बाबा साहेब आंबेडकर ने संविधान इसलिए बनाया था, ताकि सरकारें गरीब से गरीब व्यक्ति के लिए कल्याणकारी योजनाएं बनाएं. आज संविधान दिवस है और आज आम आदमी पार्टी का स्थापना दिवस भी है, जिसकी स्थापना राष्ट्रीय संयोजक अरविंद केजरीवाल ने देश को संविधान के दिखाए मार्ग पर आगे ले जाने के लिए की थी.' उन्होंने आगे कहा, 'मैं पिछले साढ़े चार साल के दौरान भगवंत मान सरकार की उपलब्धियों की सूची पेश नहीं करने जा रहा हूं. मैं एक "आम" पंजाबी परिवार की कहानी साझा करना चाहता हूं दो छोटे बच्चे, घर संभालने वाली एक मां, खेतों, दुकान या नौकरी पर कड़ी मेहनत करने वाला एक पिता, और अपनी उम्मीदों व सपनों वाले बुजुर्ग दादा-दादी. पिछले साढ़े चार सालों में भगवंत मान सरकार ने इस आम परिवार के हर सदस्य के सपनों को छुआ है.'
रैली के दौरान मुख्यमंत्री भगवंत सिंह मान ने तीन अनौपचारिक सर्वेक्षणों के जरिए जनसमूह से सीधा संवाद किया. इस दौरान उन्होंने 3 सवाल पूछे और उनका जवाब जाना.
सबसे पहले उन्होंने जीरो बिजली बिल के लाभ के बारे में लोगों से पूछते हुए कहा, 'आप में से कितने लोगों के बिजली बिल जीरो आ रहे हैं? हाथ खड़े करके बताइए.' मौजूद लोगों के बड़े बहुमत ने हाथ खड़े किए. लोगों की प्रतिक्रिया पर जवाब देते हुए मुख्यमंत्री भगवंत सिंह मान ने कहा, 'यह लाभ पूरे पंजाब के घरों तक पहुंच रहा है. लोग अपने मासिक खर्चों में आए अंतर को खुद महसूस कर सकते हैं. जब कोई सरकार आम परिवारों को राहत देने के लिए काम करती है तो ऐसा ही होता है.'
दूसरे सवाल में मुख्यमंत्री भगवंत सिंह मान ने जनसमूह से 10 लाख की स्वास्थ्य बीमा योजना के कार्ड के बारे में पूछा. उन्होंने कहा, 'आप में से कितने लोगों को 10 लाख की स्वास्थ्य बीमा योजना के तहत अपने स्वास्थ्य कार्ड मिल गए हैं?' लोगों की प्रतिक्रिया देखने के बाद उन्होंने कहा कि सरकार यह सुनिश्चित करने के लिए लगातार काम कर रही है कि सभी पात्र परिवारों को इसका लाभ मिले.
तीसरे सवाल में मुख्यमंत्री भगवंत सिंह मान ने लोगों से पूछा, 'क्या आप चाहते हैं कि 2027 में पंजाब में फिर से आम आदमी पार्टी की सरकार बने?' भीड़ ने जोरदार तालियों और नारों के साथ इसका समर्थन किया. लोगों के जोश पर प्रतिक्रिया देते हुए मुख्यमंत्री भगवंत सिंह मान ने कहा, 'मैं आपका जवाब सुन सकता हूं. पंजाब के लोगों ने अपना मन बना लिया है. विपक्षी दल पहले ही नतीजों को लेकर चिंतित हैं. उन्हें अभी से तैयारी कर लेनी चाहिए क्योंकि इस बार उनकी जमानत भी नहीं बचेगी.'

title: संसद के विशेष सत्र से पहले राजनीतिक हलचल तेज! मोदी कैबिनेट कल करेगी मंथन, कांग्रेस ने भी बुलाई मीटिंग
description: संसद के विशेष सत्र से पहले मोदी कैबिनेट और कांग्रेस ने 27 नवंबर को अहम बैठक बुलाई है. महिला आरक्षण और परिसीमन के मुद्दे पर सत्ता पक्ष और विपक्ष की रणनीति पर नजरें टिकी हैं.
author: ताहिर कामरान
content:
संसद के विशेष सत्र को लेकर दिल्ली में सियासी सरगर्मी तेज हो गई है. 30 नवंबर से शुरू होने वाली संसद की बैठक से पहले सत्ता पक्ष और विपक्ष, दोनों ने अपनी-अपनी रणनीति तैयार करनी शुरू कर दी है. एक तरफ प्रधानमंत्री नरेंद्र मोदी की अध्यक्षता में कैबिनेट की विशेष बैठक होने जा रही है, तो दूसरी तरफ कांग्रेस ने भी विपक्ष की रणनीति तय करने के लिए अहम बैठक बुलाई है. ऐसे में विशेष सत्र शुरू होने से पहले ही सियासी मुकाबले का मंच तैयार होता नजर आ रहा है.
देर रात मिली जानकारी के मुताबिक शुक्रवार यानी 27 नवंबर को मोदी कैबिनेट की एक अहम मीटिंग होने वाली है. इस बैठक में संसद के विशेष सत्र से जुड़े अहम मुद्दों पर चर्चा होने की उम्मीद है. हालांकि, होने वाली मीटिंग को लेकर कोई आधिकारिक एजेंडा अभी सामने नहीं आया है, लेकिन राजनीतिक दिग्गजों का कहना है कि सरकार इस सत्र में महिला आरक्षण और परिसीमन बिल जैसे बिलों पर चर्चा कर सकती है.
इससे पहले 25 नवंबर को दिल्ली में हुई कैबिनेट मीटिंग के दौरान सांसदों को विदेश दौरा ना करने की बात कही थी. पीएम मोदी ने संसद के आगामी सत्र को देखते हुए 15 दिसंबर तक विदेश यात्राओं से बचने की अपील की थी. मीडिया रिपोर्ट्स के मुताबिक, पीएम ने मंत्रियों को संसद से जुड़े कामकाज और तैयारियों को प्राथमिकता देने का निर्देश दिया था. अब 30 नवंबर से संसद का विशेष सत्र शुरू होने के ऐलान के बाद इस अपील को काफी अहम माना जा रहा है.
वहीं, कांग्रेस ने भी सरकार की तैयारियों के बीच अपनी रणनीति बनाने के लिए कमर कस ली है. कांग्रेस की पार्लियामेंट्री स्ट्रैटेजी ग्रुप की बैठक 27 नवंबर को शाम 4:30 बजे दिल्ली में होगी. इस बैठक में 30 नवंबर से शुरू होने वाली संसद की बैठक के दौरान पार्टी की रणनीति पर चर्चा की जाएगी. कांग्रेस नेतृत्व यह तय करेगा कि विशेष सत्र में किन मुद्दों को प्रमुखता से उठाना है और सरकार को किन सवालों पर घेरना है.
प्रधानमंत्री नरेंद्र मोदी ने संविधान दिवस के मौके पर कहा कि महिलाओं को न्याय मिलने से कोई नहीं रोक सकता. वहीं, विपक्ष की नजर इस बात पर है कि सरकार विशेष सत्र में महिला आरक्षण को लेकर क्या कदम उठाती है और परिसीमन के मुद्दे पर उसका क्या रुख रहता है. परिसीमन का मुद्दा इसलिए भी संवेदनशील है क्योंकि, इसका सीधा संबंध लोकसभा सीटों के पुनर्निर्धारण और राज्यों के राजनीतिक प्रतिनिधित्व से है. ऐसे में दक्षिण भारतीय राज्यों की चिंताओं और विपक्ष की आपत्तियों के बीच यह मुद्दा संसद में बड़े टकराव की वजह बन सकता है.

title: हरिवंश राय बच्चन की जिंदगी के वो किस्से, जो कम चर्चा में रहे
description: हरिवंश राय बच्चन का नाम आते ही सबसे पहले 'मधुशाला' याद आती है. लेकिन महात्मा गांधी के सामने मधुशाला का पाठ करने से लेकर तेजी सूरी से मुलाकात, जवाहरलाल नेहरू से जुड़ाव और परिवार का सरनेम 'बच्चन' बनने तक, उनके जीवन में कई ऐसे प्रसंग हैं जिनकी चर्चा कम होती है.
author: अमित सिंह
content:
दिसंबर 1933 की बात है. बनारस हिंदू विश्वविद्यालय के शिवाजी हॉल में एक कवि सम्मेलन चल रहा था. इलाहाबाद से आए 26 साल के एक युवा कवि ने अपनी रचना सुनानी शुरू की. कविता की हर चौथी पंक्ति के अंत में एक शब्द आता था. धीरे-धीरे श्रोता भी कवि के साथ उस शब्द को दोहराने लगे. वह शब्द था- मधुशाला.
उस कवि सम्मेलन की अध्यक्षता कर रहे अंग्रेजी के प्राध्यापक मनोरंजन प्रसाद सिन्हा ने बाद में अपने संस्मरण में लिखा कि सम्मेलन खत्म होने के बाद भी छात्रावासों में कविता की पंक्तियां गूंजती रहीं. जिन छात्रों ने कविता नहीं सुनी थी, उन्होंने दोबारा कवि सम्मेलन कराने की मांग की.
विश्वविद्यालय प्रशासन से अनुमति मिली और दूसरी बार जब कवि सम्मेलन हुआ तो हॉल में इतनी भीड़ जुटी कि दरवाजों के बाहर भी छात्र खड़े थे.
जिस रचना को सुनने के लिए विश्वविद्यालय के छात्र इतने बेचैन थे, वह उस समय तक किताब की शक्ल में प्रकाशित भी नहीं हुई थी. उसे छपने में करीब दो साल और लगे.
यह हरिवंश राय बच्चन की लोकप्रियता के शुरुआती दिनों का किस्सा है. 27 नवंबर 1907 को इलाहाबाद में जन्मे बच्चन की जिंदगी को समझने के लिए उस दौर के हिंदुस्तान को भी देखना होगा. उनकी निजी जिंदगी, साहित्य और देश के बदलते सामाजिक-राजनीतिक माहौल के बीच कई ऐसे रिश्ते और विरोधाभास थे, जो आज भी कम दिलचस्प नहीं हैं.
देश में उस समय स्वतंत्रता आंदोलन चल रहा था. महात्मा गांधी शराबबंदी के पक्षधर थे. कांग्रेस के कार्यक्रमों में खादी, स्वदेशी, संयम और सामाजिक सुधार की बातें होती थीं. इसी दौर में एक कवि मंचों से हाला, प्याला, साकी और मधुशाला की बातें कर रहा था.
1935 में मधुशाला प्रकाशित हुई तो साहित्य जगत में बहस छिड़ गई. साहित्यिक आलोचकों के एक वर्ग का मानना था कि बच्चन अपनी कविता के जरिए शराब पीने की संस्कृति को बढ़ावा दे रहे हैं. इंदौर में एक साहित्यिक आयोजन के दौरान महात्मा गांधी तक उनकी शिकायत पहुंचा दी गई.
बच्चन ने अपनी आत्मकथा में इस मुलाकात का जिक्र किया है. गांधीजी ने उन्हें रात में कार्यकारिणी की बैठक से पहले बुलाया था. बच्चन इस बात को लेकर परेशान थे कि अगर गांधीजी ने मधुशाला का पाठ करने से मना कर दिया या रचना को नष्ट करने के लिए कह दिया, तो वह क्या करेंगे?
गांधीजी के सामने बच्चन ने सोच-समझकर दो रुबाइयां चुनीं. इनमें से एक की आखिरी पंक्ति थी-
दूसरी रुबाई जीवन में अपना रास्ता चुनने और उस पर चलते रहने की बात करती थी. दोनों रुबाइयां सुनने के बाद गांधीजी को उनमें शराब का गुणगान नजर नहीं आया. बच्चन की आशंका दूर हो गई.
यहां एक और बात ध्यान देने वाली है. मधुशाला लिखने वाले बच्चन खुद मदिरापान से दूर रहते थे. दिसंबर 2014 में एक मीडिया कार्यक्रम के दौरान अमिताभ बच्चन ने भी अपने पिता के शराब न पीने की बात कही थी.
मधुशाला की प्रेरणा के तार करीब 900 साल पुराने फारस से जुड़ते हैं. वहां उमर खय्याम नाम के एक कवि हुए, जिनकी दिलचस्पी गणित, खगोल विज्ञान और दर्शन में भी थी. उनकी चार पंक्तियों वाली कविताओं यानी रुबाइयों को अंग्रेजी साहित्य में लोकप्रिय बनाने का श्रेय एडवर्ड फिट्जजेराल्ड को जाता है. 1859 में उनका अंग्रेजी अनुवाद प्रकाशित हुआ था.
अंग्रेजी साहित्य के विद्यार्थी हरिवंश राय बच्चन खय्याम की रुबाइयों से काफी प्रभावित थे. इसी प्रभाव में उन्होंने मधुशाला की रचना की. आगे चलकर उन्होंने खय्याम की रुबाइयों का हिंदी अनुवाद भी किया.
मधुशाला की लोकप्रियता में उसकी भाषा का भी बड़ा योगदान था. हिंदी के पाठकों को इसमें उर्दू और फारसी के शब्द सहजता से मिलते थे. चार पंक्तियों के छंद, उनकी लय और बच्चन के सुनाने के अंदाज ने इस रचना को किताबों से निकालकर आम लोगों के बीच पहुंचा दिया.
उनकी मंचीय लोकप्रियता का अंदाजा इसी बात से लगाया जा सकता है कि प्रेमचंद तक उनसे प्रभावित थे. हिन्दवी पर उपलब्ध बच्चन के जीवन परिचय के मुताबिक, प्रेमचंद ने एक बार कहा था कि मद्रास में भी अगर लोग किसी हिंदी कवि का नाम जानते हैं तो वह बच्चन का नाम है.
1935-36 का समय बच्चन की जिंदगी के सबसे मुश्किल वर्षों में गिना जा सकता है. एक तरफ मधुशाला ने उन्हें हिंदी साहित्य का चर्चित चेहरा बना दिया था, तो दूसरी तरफ उनकी पत्नी श्यामा क्षयरोग यानी टीबी से जूझ रही थीं.
दोनों की शादी बहुत कम उम्र में हुई थी. परिवार की आर्थिक स्थिति भी ऐसी नहीं थी कि श्यामा का बेहतर इलाज आसानी से कराया जा सके. आखिरकार 1936 में श्यामा का निधन हो गया.
उस वक्त टीबी के इलाज के लिए आज जैसी प्रभावी दवाएं उपलब्ध नहीं थीं.
श्यामा के निधन के बाद बच्चन की कविताओं का मिजाज बदलता दिखाई देता है. 1938 में 'निशा निमंत्रण' और 1939 में 'एकांत संगीत' प्रकाशित हुईं. इन रचनाओं में रात, अकेलापन, स्मृतियां और मृत्यु का एहसास बार-बार सामने आता है.
बच्चन के जीवन का यह दौर उनकी आत्मकथा में विस्तार से दर्ज है. उस समय उनकी उम्र 30 साल भी नहीं हुई थी.
31 दिसंबर की रात थी. बच्चन बरेली में अपने मित्र प्रोफेसर ज्योति प्रकाश के घर ठहरे हुए थे. तय हुआ कि नए साल की शुरुआत उनकी कविताओं के साथ होगी. वहां तेजी सूरी भी मौजूद थीं.
बच्चन से उनकी एक कविता सुनाने का आग्रह किया गया. कविता का शीर्षक था- 'क्या करूं संवेदना लेकर तुम्हारी?'
इस कविता में किसी दुखी इंसान के प्रति दिखाई जाने वाली संवेदना की सीमाओं की बात थी. बच्चन जब कविता सुनाते हुए उस हिस्से तक पहुंचे, जहां एक इंसान के आंसू दूसरे इंसान की आंखों से बहने की कल्पना की गई थी, तो तेजी रोने लगीं.
बच्चन ने अपनी आत्मकथा में लिखा है कि तेजी को रोता देखकर वह खुद भी भावुक हो गए. कमरे में मौजूद परिवार के लोग कब वहां से चले गए, दोनों को पता ही नहीं चला.
1942 में हरिवंश राय बच्चन और तेजी सूरी ने विवाह कर लिया. एक कायस्थ परिवार के युवक और सिख परिवार की युवती का यह विवाह उस दौर की सामाजिक परिस्थितियों के लिहाज से भी खास था.
17 अप्रैल 1949 को जवाहरलाल नेहरू ने एक लेख लिखा था, जो आज भी नेहरू अभिलेखागार में उपलब्ध है. यह लेख बच्चन की रचना के अंग्रेजी अनुवाद की भूमिका के तौर पर लिखा गया था.
नेहरू ने इसमें स्वीकार किया कि उन्हें बच्चन की मधुशाला पसंद है. उन्होंने आधुनिक हिंदी कविता के अंग्रेजी अनुवाद की जरूरत पर भी जोर दिया, ताकि दूसरे देशों के लोग भारतीय समाज की भावनाओं और विचारों को समझ सकें.
इसके कुछ साल बाद बच्चन कैम्ब्रिज विश्वविद्यालय पहुंचे. वहां उन्होंने आयरलैंड के नोबेल पुरस्कार विजेता कवि डब्ल्यू. बी. येट्स पर शोध किया. शोध के सिलसिले में वह आयरलैंड भी गए, जहां उनकी मुलाकात येट्स की पत्नी से हुई.
भारत लौटने के बाद उन्होंने आकाशवाणी और फिर विदेश मंत्रालय में काम किया. आजाद भारत में सरकारी कामकाज के लिए हिंदी शब्दावली तैयार करने की कोशिशों को भी उन्होंने करीब से देखा.
उनकी आत्मकथा में इससे जुड़ा एक दिलचस्प प्रसंग है. राष्ट्रकवि रामधारी सिंह दिनकर की अध्यक्षता वाली एक समिति में 'कस्टम्स हाउस ऑफिसर' का हिंदी अनुवाद 'सीमा शुल्क सदन अधिकारी' सुझाया गया. इसे सुनकर दिनकर को तुलसीदास की चौपाई याद आ गई.
सरकारी हिंदी को आम आदमी के लिए कितना सहज बनाया जाए, यह बहस आज भी जारी है. बच्चन ने अपने कामकाज के दौरान इस सवाल को करीब से देखा था.
हरिवंश राय जिस परिवार से आते थे, उसका उपनाम श्रीवास्तव था. बचपन में घर के लोग उन्हें प्यार से बच्चन बुलाते थे. आगे चलकर उन्होंने इसी नाम से कविताएं लिखनी शुरू कीं.
बच्चन की आत्मकथा का अंग्रेजी अनुवाद करने वाले हिंदी के विद्वान रूपर्ट स्नेल ने एक दिलचस्प जानकारी दी है. उनके मुताबिक, जब अमिताभ का स्कूल में दाखिला कराया गया, तब पहली बार बच्चन को परिवार के उपनाम के तौर पर इस्तेमाल किया गया.
जिस नाम से कभी घर में प्यार से पुकारा जाता था, आगे चलकर वही नाम हिंदी सिनेमा के सबसे चर्चित परिवारों में से एक की पहचान बन गया.
हरिवंश राय बच्चन की लोकप्रियता का एक दूसरा पहलू भी है. मधुशाला की जबरदस्त सफलता के चलते उनकी कई महत्वपूर्ण रचनाओं की चर्चा अपेक्षाकृत कम हुई.
1943 के बंगाल के अकाल पर उन्होंने 'बंगाल का काल' लिखा. गांधीजी की हत्या के बाद 'खादी के फूल' और 'सूत की माला' जैसी रचनाएं सामने आईं.
शेक्सपियर के 'मैकबेथ', 'ओथेलो', 'हैमलेट' और 'किंग लियर' का उन्होंने हिंदी में अनुवाद किया. भगवद्गीता को भी अलग-अलग काव्य रूपों में हिंदी पाठकों तक पहुंचाया.
1968 में उन्हें साहित्य अकादमी पुरस्कार मिला, लेकिन यह पुरस्कार मधुशाला के लिए नहीं, बल्कि 'दो चट्टानें' नाम के काव्य संग्रह के लिए था.
1969 से 1985 के बीच चार खंडों में प्रकाशित उनकी आत्मकथा भी कम महत्वपूर्ण नहीं है. इसमें अंग्रेजों के जमाने का इलाहाबाद, स्वतंत्रता आंदोलन, विश्वविद्यालयों की अंदरूनी राजनीति, नेहरू के दौर का सरकारी कामकाज और हिंदी सिनेमा में अमिताभ के उभार तक की कहानी दर्ज है.
18 जनवरी 2003 को बच्चन का निधन हो गया. आज सोशल मीडिया पर उनकी कविताओं की दो-चार पंक्तियां खूब साझा की जाती हैं, लेकिन उनके जीवन और दौर को समझने के लिए उनकी आत्मकथा के चारों खंड पढ़ना भी जरूरी है.
इन पन्नों में सिर्फ एक कवि की निजी जिंदगी नहीं है. यहां उस हिंदुस्तान की कहानी भी दर्ज है, जिसने अंग्रेजों की गुलामी देखी, आजादी का उत्साह महसूस किया और फिर एक नए राष्ट्र के निर्माण की चुनौतियों से जूझा.
बच्चन इस पूरे बदलाव के गवाह रहे. उन्होंने इसे सिर्फ देखा नहीं, अपनी लेखनी में दर्ज भी किया.

title: ‘I Got Shot, Fell Down, Lost Consciousness, Had 6 Surgeries’: 26/11 Survivor Devika Recalls Horror on 18th Anniversary
description: "I was nine years old at the time. As I tried to run with my dad, I got shot. I fell down and lost consciousness. I remained admitted for about 45 days. Six surgeries were performed on my leg,” Devika Rotawan, who testified against the lone surviving gunman Ajmal Kasab, recounted the trauma.
author: Ankita Paul
content:
‘I Got Shot, Fell Down, Lost Consciousness, Had 6 Surgeries’: 26/11 Survivor Devika Recalls Horror on 18th Anniversary
"I was nine years old at the time. As I tried to run with my dad, I got shot. I fell down and lost consciousness. I remained admitted for about 45 days. Six surgeries were performed on my leg,” Devika Rotawan, who testified against the lone surviving gunman Ajmal Kasab, recounted the trauma.
- India News
- 4 min read
Mumbai: Eighteen years after the 26/11 terror attacks, key eyewitness and survivor Devika Rotawan says the night still feels as raw as yesterday. The woman, who testified as a nine-year-old against the lone surviving gunman Ajmal Kasab, recounted the trauma she suffered at Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj Terminus (CST).
“It has been 18 years since 26/11 today, yet it still feels as though it happened just yesterday. I remember that night in the exact same way,” Rotawan said. She recalled travelling to Pune with her father and brother. “The three of us went from Bandra to CST. We went and sat in the main hall at CST in front of platforms 12 and 13. There was suddenly a loud bomb blast. After the blast, gunfire began. I saw people falling while running. There was blood from someone’s hand, someone’s leg and someone’s head. I was nine years old at the time. As I tried to run with my dad, I got shot. I fell down and lost consciousness. I remained admitted for about 45 days. Six surgeries were performed on my leg,” she said.
After her discharge, the family returned to their village in Rajasthan. Mumbai Crime Branch officers later contacted them, and on 10 June 2009 she and her father appeared in court and identified Kasab.
“Eighteen years have passed, sir, yet we still haven’t gotten complete justice. It brings great happiness that Kasab was hanged, but the main mastermind who is still sitting in Pakistan. I will appeal to the government to carry out more operations and eliminate the main mastermind,” she added.
Advertisement
The attacks, carried out by Pakistan-backed Lashkar-e-Taiba (LeT) terrorists on the night of 26 November 2008, left 166 people dead and around 300 injured over four days. Ten terrorists entered Mumbai by sea and struck carefully chosen targets including the Taj and Oberoi hotels, CST, the Jewish centre at Nariman House, Cama Hospital, Metro Cinema and Leopold Cafe. Nine of the attackers were killed; Kasab was arrested, sentenced to death in May 2010 and hanged in 2012 in a Pune prison.

title: ‘UCC in all BJP-ruled States Soon; Swami Vivekananda's Dream for Bharat Mata Will be Accomplished in 2047': Amit Shah
description: “Every single citizen in this country – irrespective of religion, whether Hindu, Sikh, Muslim, Christian, or Parsi – must get the right to live under one uniform law. Laws should not be framed on the basis of religion,” Union Home Minister Amit Shah said.
author: Ankita Paul
content:
‘UCC in all BJP-ruled States Soon; Swami Vivekananda's Dream for Bharat Mata Will be Accomplished in 2047': Amit Shah
“Every single citizen in this country – irrespective of religion, whether Hindu, Sikh, Muslim, Christian, or Parsi – must get the right to live under one uniform law. Laws should not be framed on the basis of religion,” Union Home Minister Amit Shah said.
- India News
- 6 min read
New Delhi: Union Home Minister Amit Shah on Thursday said the BJP would implement the Uniform Civil Code in every state under its rule in the coming days, while strongly defending the Constitution and criticising Congress leader Rahul Gandhi for allegedly mocking its institutions.
Addressing the ‘Samvidhan Gaurav Diwas’ seminar organised by the Delhi BJP, Shah said the Constitution’s framers had included the UCC in the Directive Principles of State Policy. “Every single citizen in this country – irrespective of religion, whether Hindu, Sikh, Muslim, Christian, or Parsi – must get the right to live under one uniform law. Laws should not be framed on the basis of religion,” he said, adding that this principle is rejected by Rahul Gandhi’s party.
“Today I have come to state with clarity that in the coming days, wherever there are BJP-ruled governments, we are going to implement the UCC,” Shah declared.
He linked the Constitution to India’s future, recalling a conversation with a Congress leader in Parliament who asked where Prime Minister Narendra Modi would be in 2047. “I replied, ‘Your focus is on individuals, whereas our focus is on Bharat Mata. India will certainly be there in 2047.’ So this resolve is a resolve to make India great, not a resolve to make any individual great,” Shah said. He expressed confidence that Swami Vivekananda’s dream for Bharat Mata would be fulfilled by the centenary of Independence, with the Constitution as the guiding path.
Advertisement
Shah accused Rahul Gandhi of talking about the Constitution while mocking it and its institutions. “He openly declares that we do not want a debate in Parliament, we want it on the streets… defaming the Election Commission, defaming revisions and the intensive revision of voter lists, and going abroad to defame India across the world,” the Home Minister said. He attributed this to continuous electoral defeats over 20 years, invoking the proverb “Naachna na aaye aangan tedha,” and reminded that the Congress had imposed the Emergency, locking the spirit of the Constitution “inside a dark dungeon for 18 months.”
On women’s reservation, Shah said the constitutional amendment providing 33 per cent seats for women in Parliament and state assemblies had been blocked by the Congress. “It is the resolve of the Bharatiya Janata Party and our leader Narendra Modi that the women of this country will definitely get 33 per cent reservation; you cannot stop us,” he asserted.
Advertisement
Highlighting the damage caused by Naxalism, Shah referred to elderly residents in Bastar still lacking basic facilities and said the Modi government’s political will had eradicated the menace, securing constitutionally guaranteed rights for 21 crore people.
He praised India’s peaceful transfers of power through the constitutional process and reiterated that the framers ensured power flows from the people and is exercised within constitutional limits. Every word of the Preamble, he said, was meant to build a great India.
Shah urged critics of Indian civilisation to examine the original copy of the Constitution, which opens with illustrations by Nandalal Bose depicting Lord Ram’s arrival in Ayodhya, Lord Buddha, Lord Mahavira, Guru Gobind Singh, Rani Lakshmibai, the Dandi March and Netaji Subhas Chandra Bose. “Please look at the original copy of the Constitution once… spare 15 minutes… and look at Nandalal Bose’s illustrations to understand the spirit of the Constitution,” he said.
Noting that the spirit of the Constitution had been neglected after Independence, Shah credited Prime Minister Modi with deciding in 2015 that November 26 would be observed every year as Constitution Pride Day to carry its highest values to every school, college and citizen.

title: Govt Moves to Reconvene Parliament from November 30 to December 3
description: Union Minister of Parliamentary Affairs Kiren Rijiju on Thursday said the Central government has requested the Lok Sabha Speaker and the Rajya Sabha Chairman to reconvene the Lower House on November 30 and the Upper House on December 2 to transact essential government business.
author: Asian News International
content:
Govt Moves to Reconvene Parliament from November 30 to December 3
Union Minister of Parliamentary Affairs Kiren Rijiju on Thursday said the Central government has requested the Lok Sabha Speaker and the Rajya Sabha Chairman to reconvene the Lower House on November 30 and the Upper House on December 2 to transact essential government business.
- India News
- 2 min read
New Delhi: Union Minister of Parliamentary Affairs Kiren Rijiju on Thursday said the Central government has requested the Lok Sabha Speaker and the Rajya Sabha Chairman to reconvene the Lower House on November 30 and the Upper House on December 2 to transact essential government business.
In a post on X, Rijiju added that the sittings of both Houses of Parliament are expected to conclude on December 3, subject to the exigencies of business.
"The Government has requested Hon’ble Speaker, Lok Sabha and Hon’ble Chairman, Rajya Sabha to reconvene Lok Sabha on Monday, 30th November, 2026 and Rajya Sabha on Wednesday, 2nd December, 2026 respectively to transact essential Government Business," Rijiju posted on X.
"Subject to exigencies of the Business, the sitting of both Houses may conclude on 3rd December, 2026," the Union Minister added.
Advertisement
The sittings of both Houses are scheduled to conclude on Thursday, December 3, 2026, subject to the exigencies of essential government business.
Speculation over the delimitation and women's reservation has intensified following Rijiju's announcement, as the announcement did not specify which bills would be taken up.
Advertisement
Meanwhile, a Congress Parliamentary Strategy Group meeting is to be held tomorrow in Delhi at 4.30 PM to discuss the strategy for the Parliament sitting to be held from November 30.
The decision to reconvene the Houses at short notice comes against the backdrop of an unprecedented procedural timeline following the previous parliamentary session.
Parliament last met during the Monsoon Session 2026, which concluded with both the Lok Sabha and Rajya Sabha being adjourned sine die (indefinitely) on August 13, 2026.
Neither House was prorogued following the August 13 adjournment. Crossing the 100-day mark in late November, this became the longest unprorogued gap between parliamentary sittings in India's constitutional history, surpassing the previous record of 87 days set in 2008.
Both Houses were only adjourned sine die on August 13, 2026, by their respective Presiding Officers. Formal prorogation by the President of India under Article 85(2)(a) was never issued.
Because the Monsoon Session was never prorogued, the government does not need the President to summon a brand-new session (which conventionally requires a 14-day notice).
Under the Rules of Procedure (such as Rule 15 in the Lok Sabha), the Speaker and Chairman can directly reconvene an unprorogued House at short notice to resume the existing session.
Keeping the Monsoon Session technically alive allowed the government to call Parliament back on short notice without issuing a fresh 14-day summons.

title: 18 years after 26/11: How Mumbai attacks changed India’s security architecture
description: Eighteen years ago, the Mumbai terrorist attacks triggered an overhaul of India's security architecture. As new threats emerge in the age of AI and encrypted communication channels, the post-26/11 security architecture continues to evolve.
author: Madhur Sharma
content:
18 years after 26/11: How Mumbai attacks changed India’s security architecture
Eighteen years ago, the Mumbai terrorist attacks triggered an overhaul of India's security architecture. As new threats emerge in the age of AI and encrypted communication channels, the post-26/11 security architecture continues to evolve.
Eighteen years ago, 10 Pakistani terrorists arrived in Mumbai by boat and unleashed a terror rampage.
They split into teams to attack carefully selected targets: Chhatrapati Shivaji Terminus to maximise casualties; the iconic Taj Mahal Palace and Oberoi Trident hotels to shock the nation and take as many hostages as possible; and Nariman House, a Chabad centre, to target Jews.
India's response was flawed from the outset. A breakdown in communications meant that a police team came under attack and never received reinforcements. National Security Guard (NSG) commandos, deployed from their base near Delhi, did not arrive until several hours later the following morning, and the initial response by the Indian Navy's Marcos commandos was hampered by the absence of detailed floor plans of the Taj.
Once the NSG killed the last terrorist, India began a yearslong overhaul of its national security and intelligence architecture — a process that continues to this day.
The results have been significant. India dismantled the urban bombing campaign that had terrorised the country throughout the 2000s, strengthened intelligence-sharing mechanisms, bolstered its legal framework for targeting terrorists and their financiers, and adopted a more muscular counterterrorism doctrine.
The government established the National Investigation Agency (NIA) after recognising that the country lacked a dedicated counterterrorism investigative body. Existing institutions such as the Multi-Agency Centre (Mac) were strengthened, while new organisations such as Natgrid were created to improve intelligence sharing and data retrieval. The NSG was also decentralised to reduce response times.
According to the South Asia Terrorism Portal, terrorism-related deaths have fallen by nearly 90 per cent since the 26/11 attacks.
These institutional reforms, combined with a policy of striking at the source of terrorism, as demonstrated most recently through Operation Sindoor, delivered nearly a decade in which there were no major terrorist attacks outside Kashmir and the Red Corridor, according to terrorism analyst Abhinav Pandya.
But Pandya stressed that terrorist groups are adapting their strategies and tactics, while the international political environment is becoming increasingly challenging. As a result, he argued, India must continue reforming its security and intelligence architecture to keep pace with evolving threats.
Intelligence reforms after the 26/11 attacks
One of the most damning findings to emerge after the attacks was that multiple warnings had been received before the terrorists arrived in Mumbai.
Investigative journalists Adrian Levy and Cathy Scott-Clark reported that the US Central Intelligence Agency (CIA) had shared 26 intelligence alerts with India before the attacks — some of them highly specific.
"Three warnings specifically mentioned the use of fidayeen, meaning guerrillas armed with grenades and AK-47s who fought to the death, inflicting heavy casualties before being overcome... Eleven warnings suggested the plan would involve multiple simultaneous attacks. Six warnings pointed to a sea-borne infiltration, which would be a first in India," Levy and Scott-Clark reported.
India concluded that the principal failure was not a lack of intelligence but shortcomings in the dissemination of available information, coordination among agencies, and the ability to act on intelligence inputs and analysis.
To address these weaknesses, the government strengthened the Multi-Agency Centre (Mac) and established Subsidiary Multi-Agency Centres (Smacs) across the states.
The Mac had originally been created after the Kargil War to improve intelligence-sharing on terrorism. But it was only after the 26/11 attacks that the institution acquired real authority and operational significance.
The Mac was made operational on a 24/7 basis. All participating agencies, including state police forces, were required to share intelligence, while the Mac was similarly mandated to disseminate intelligence received from one agency to all others. Regular inter-agency meetings were instituted, and a dedicated secure electronic network was established linking the Mac with participating organisations.
Natgrid was another major outcome of the post-26/11 reforms. Buts its implementation moved at a snail's pace. Conceptualised in 2009, it became operational only in 2020.
While the Mac focuses on intelligence dissemination, Natgrid functions as a database of databases. In simple terms, it is a platform that enables participating agencies to access relevant information from multiple databases through a single system. It is designed to help investigators identify links, track movements, trace financial transactions, and uncover criminal or terrorist networks.
NIA, counterterrorism laws, and expansion of the NSG
While the NIA was established as a dedicated counterterrorism investigative agency, the legal framework was also strengthened to target terrorists and their support networks.
The creation of the NIA addressed deficiencies in the investigative sphere, while the expansion and decentralisation of the NSG tackled shortcomings in operational response.
As the response to the Mumbai attacks was delayed by several hours, regional NSG hubs were established in Mumbai, Chennai, Hyderabad, and Kolkata to ensure that commandos could be deployed rapidly anywhere in the country.
Over the years, the NSG also expanded its strength and upgraded its equipment and capabilities.
The Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act (UAPA) was amended to allow individual terrorists to be designated as terrorists. Previously, only organisations could receive such a designation.
The NIA was also empowered to investigate terrorist acts affecting Indian citizens and Indian interests abroad, and to prosecute those accused of carrying them out.
India's muscular response targets the source of terrorism
Over the past decade, the most significant change has been doctrinal.
Rather than focusing solely on individual terrorists and their facilitators, India now maintains a stated policy of targeting the sources of terrorism.
Beginning with cross-border strikes in Myanmar and Pakistan-Occupied Jammu and Kashmir (PoJK), India has repeatedly demonstrated this approach. It struck a terrorist camp in Balakot following the Pulwama attack and later launched Operation Sindoor, targeting terrorist camps, launch pads, and headquarters across Pakistan and PoJK in the aftermath of the Pahalgam attack.
In line with India's stated policy of drawing no distinction between terrorists and those who support them, India also targeted Pakistani military assets after Pakistan responded to the anti-terror strikes. Between May 7 and May 10, 2025, India struck Pakistani airbases, air-defence sites, and other military facilities in response to Pakistani attacks carried out after India's initial strikes on terrorist targets on May 7.
Prime Minister Narendra Modi subsequently stated that any attack on Indian soil would be treated as an act of war and would invite an armed response.
As Firstpost previously reported, India controlled the escalation ladder throughout the conflict and called Pakistan's nuclear bluff. India did not allow Pakistan to regain the initiative and continued to raise the pressure until Islamabad sought peace on May 10.

title: Meet the experts at Network18’s Energy Edit sustainability summit
description: How does sustainability go hand-in-hand with development? With the help of experts and prominent voices, CNN-News18 & Firstpost Sustainability Conclave - The Energy Edit will examine the challenges of energy geopolitics to green growth and climate resilience
author: FP Studio
content:
Meet the experts at Network18’s Energy Edit sustainability summit
How does sustainability go hand-in-hand with development? With the help of experts and prominent voices, CNN-News18 & Firstpost Sustainability Conclave - The Energy Edit will examine the challenges of energy geopolitics to green growth and climate resilience
Sustainability is no longer synonymous with environmental protection; the conversation is fast changing. It sits at the centre of some of the biggest challenges facing governments and economies — from energy security and climate resilience to tech innovation, resource scarcity, and future growth.
As countries grapple with these challenges, informed perspectives across disciplines are needed. To understand this better, CNN-News18 & Firstpost Sustainability Conclave - The Energy Edit, presented by Bajaj group brings together experts from the fields of energy, engineering, economics, public policy, and sustainable growth to explore ideas and decisions that will help shape the next stage of sustainability.
The one-day conclave to be held on November 28 will feature leaders and experts who have worked closely on climate action, energy markets, public policy, and development.
Here’s the line-up of the distinguished voices.
Jeffrey Sachs, Director, Center for Sustainable Development
The world-renowned economics professor will be part of the session titled ‘Global South Moment: Can development and climate action go hand in hand?’ He’ll dig into one of the toughest questions in the sustainability debate: How do you pursue real economic growth while tackling the climate crisis at the same time?
John Swinney, First Minister of Scotland
Can climate goals be turned into an economic opportunity? Scotland’s First Minister, John Swinney, will answer this question in the session ‘Green Growth Playbook: Turning Climate Ambition into Economic Opportunity’. He will draw upon his own experience to discuss how sustainability can drive long-term economic growth rather than hold it back.
Dr Rosemary Barnes, a mechanical engineer
Holding a PhD, Dr Barnes will be part of two sessions: ‘Why Is Storing Renewable Energy So Difficult?’ and ‘The Energy Transition: Beyond the Hype’.
Drawing on her work on developing innovative solutions for a sustainable future, she will break down real-world engineering hurdles behind clean energy storage and the broader transition.
Dr Anas Alhajji, Managing Partner of Energy Outlook Advisors
An expert in energy markets, Dr Alhajji will participate in ‘The New Energy World Order’. He will discuss forces that are shaping the global energy landscape and the changing dynamics of energy, security, and geopolitics.
The summit will also feature other voices such as Arunabha Ghosh, a climate and energy expert, and Naina Lal Kidwai, a sustainability and women’s empowerment champion. The duo will participate in the session ‘Planet Under Pressure: From Climate Risk to Resilience’, which will focus on the importance of climate preparedness and resilience.
Dr Ewa Suwara, deputy head of the EU delegation to India, will be part of the ‘Beyond Borders: The Green Economy’ session that will focus on sustainable economic development.
Additionally, Kartik Verma, who works in climate education and rural communities, will feature in ‘Future is Ours: The Next Gen Environment Leaders’, highlighting the role of emerging voices in shaping environmental awareness and action.
Sustainability conversations that will matter
At the Sustainability Conclave, conversations will move way past big climate pledges to understand the challenges of energy transition. The sessions will dig into policies, technologies and choices that will define what comes next in sustainability.
The programme will address ambitions and practical challenges on issues such as the difficulty of storing renewable energy, the realities of moving beyond conventional energy systems, and the relationship between climate action and economic development.
The discussions will also delve into the role of international cooperation, the emergence of a green economy, and the changing relationship between energy and geopolitics.
The summit is scheduled to happen on 28 November 2026 in New Delhi. Visit https://www.firstpost.com/ms/sustainability-conclave-2026/ to learn more about the event.

title: Tamil Nadu introduces 15 days of paid paternity leave for government employees
description: New fathers can take 15 days of fully paid leave, either 15 days before the expected delivery date or within six months of childbirth
author: FP News Desk
content:
Tamil Nadu introduces 15 days of paid paternity leave for government employees
New fathers can take 15 days of fully paid leave, either 15 days before the expected delivery date or within six months of childbirth
Tamil Nadu has introduced 15 days of paid paternity leave for married male government employees, allowing new fathers to take time off to support their spouses during childbirth and care for their newborns.
The state government issued a Government Order (GO) announcing the new provision, which allows eligible employees to avail themselves of the leave either 15 days before the expected date of delivery or within six months of the child's birth.
According to a report by United News of India (UNI), the leave will be fully paid and will cover 15 calendar days. The provision will apply to married male employees working across Tamil Nadu government departments and administrative bodies.
The policy is aimed at encouraging shared parental responsibilities and giving fathers an opportunity to support their spouses during childbirth and the recovery period following delivery.
Under the new rules, employees can choose when to take the leave within the specified eligibility window. They can begin using it up to 15 days before the expected delivery date or take it at any point during the first six months after the child's birth.
The move also recognises the role fathers play in early childcare and newborn bonding, while giving families additional support during the initial months after childbirth.
The Government Order has come into immediate effect following its issuance.
Government employee associations in Tamil Nadu have welcomed the decision, describing it as a positive step towards more inclusive workplace policies and improved family welfare.

title: Women earn a third less than men in India's factories, shows ASI data
description: Women directly employed in factories earned ₹587 a day against ₹872 for men in FY25, with the wage gap widening to 60 per cent in the largest plants, according to ASI data
author: Himanshi Bhardwaj
content:
Women earn a third less than men in India's factories, shows ASI data
Women directly employed in factories earned ₹587 a day against ₹872 for men in FY25, with the wage gap widening to 60 per cent in the largest plants, according to ASI data
Listen to This Article
Women directly employed in India’s factories in 2024-25 (FY25) earned ₹ 587 a day, a third less than the ₹872 for men, according to the unit-level data from the Annual Survey of Industries (ASI) 2024-25. 
The gap does not close even when men and women work in the same factory. In factories that employ both men and women, women earned ₹592 a day against ₹925 for men — about 36 per cent less.
These factories employ 98 per cent of all women working directly in such places. Only 23 per cent of these factories paid women at least as much as men on a daily basis. In more than half of all such factories, women earned less than 95 per cent of men’s daily wage.
Women remain a small part of the factory workforce. In FY25 they made up 18 per cent of the 9.62 million workers employed directly by factories.
More than 70 per cent of the factories employed no women directly at all. Direct workers are those on the factory’s own payroll as distinct from the ones hired through a contractor.
Also Read
The gap widens sharply with the size of the factory. In factories with fewer than 50 people, women earned 19 per cent less than men. In plants with 1,000 to 4,999, the gap rose to 42 per cent. In the largest plants, with 5,000 or more people, women earned ₹616 a day against ₹1,531 for men, a difference of 60 per cent. The data further revealed that these large plants also employed women in the highest proportion. Women made up 30 per cent of the directly employed workers in the factories with 5,000 or more people, against 10 per cent in the smallest units.
Part of the gap in daily wages may come down to hours worked, said Tanu Goyal, senior fellow at the Indian Council for Research on International Economic Relations. Women tend to work fewer hours because most of the household work falls on them, she noted. “They’re not putting in enough hours of work. And that is because of a variety of reasons. Unpaid work like cooking is one of them.”
Mobility is another constraint, she said. Many women head home by three or four in the afternoon, and few work on the night shift. “They work in the morning and before sunset, they prefer to come back home, either because there’s no transportation or in general. Mobility is a challenge,” Goyal said.
“Men also tend to do overtime because they are okay with working at night. It is not so with women,” she reckoned. Across all 28 industry groups recorded by the ASI, the gap is widest in tobacco, where women make up 71 per cent of the direct workforce and earned ₹226 a day against ₹627 for men, a 64 per cent gap.
It was followed by chemicals, where women earned 48 per cent less. In tobacco, Goyal said, women are largely confined to the lowest-paid tasks like rolling bidis, and are often expected to accept lower pay.
“Women are generally working on the absolute shop floor where they are rolling the tobacco products. So it’s absolutely low-value work. As you go a little bit higher up the value, like packing, labelling, etc you employ more men,” she said.
Goyal also pointed to a general acceptance among women that they will work for lower wages. “I think it’s more of the acceptance that you are getting paid less and you will be paid less than men, and you don’t ask for more,” she said. At the other end, the gap is the narrowest in waste collection and treatment, where women earned 1.2 per cent less than men, and in refined petroleum, at 9.6 per cent. Notably, in repair and installation of machinery, women earned about 51 per cent more than men. All three employ very few women, however, with women making up less than 6 per cent of their direct workforce. Among states, the gap is widest in Jharkhand (54 per cent), followed by Andhra Pradesh (43 per cent), Kerala (42 per cent), Karnataka (39 per cent) and Maharashtra (39 per cent).
Three of them — Karnataka, Kerala and Andhra Pradesh — are among the four states where women form the largest share of direct factory workers. On the other hand, the gap is the narrowest in Punjab (13 per cent), Haryana (15 per cent) and Uttar Pradesh (15 per cent).

title: SC rules PMLA attachment orders must be confirmed by judicial member
description: The Supreme Court said a single-member bench can confirm attachment orders if its member is from the judicial field, while urging the Centre to consider restoring multiple adjudicating authorities.
author: Bhavini Mishra
content:
SC rules PMLA attachment orders must be confirmed by judicial member
The Supreme Court said a single-member bench can confirm attachment orders if its member is from the judicial field, while urging the Centre to consider restoring multiple adjudicating authorities.
Listen to This Article
The Supreme Court on Thursday ruled that an adjudicating authority under the Prevention of Money Laundering Act (PMLA) cannot confirm provisional attachment of properties by the Enforcement Directorate (ED) through a single-member bench unless the member is from the judicial field.
A Bench comprising Chief Justice of India Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana held that decisions confirming attachment under Section 8(3) of the PMLA, which can deprive individuals of the use and possession of their properties for a prolonged period, must involve a judicial member to ensure impartiality and legal objectivity.
The court clarified that it has not mandated a minimum two-member bench for such adjudication. A single-member bench can hear the matter, provided its member is a judicial member duly authorised to do so. The ruling came in Union of India versus Sekar, in which the court examined whether a single non-judicial member could exercise the adjudicatory powers under the PMLA.
The Bench also distinguished between the preliminary and final stages of the adjudication process. It said the issuance of a show-cause notice under Section 8(1) does not require a judicial member, as this stage involves examining the material submitted by the ED and initiating proceedings. However, the hearing and final determination under Sections 8(2) and 8(3) must include a judicial member.
The requirement will also apply to decisions concerning encumbrances and leasehold interests in attached properties under Section 9, and the retention of property and records under Sections 20(4) and 21(4) of the Act.
Also Read
The court directed the Chairperson of the Adjudicating Authority to issue an administrative circular to ensure compliance. It rejected the argument that the Chairperson of the authority must necessarily be a judicial member, holding that such a requirement was not envisaged under the statutory framework. The judgment will operate prospectively.
The court said it would not be in the interests of justice or expeditious adjudication to reopen orders already passed by benches comprising a single non-judicial member. Parties aggrieved by such orders can, however, challenge them on their merits through statutory appeals.
Caseload and multiple authorities
Separately, the court also urged the Centre to consider restoring the original framework of multiple adjudicating authorities, which was replaced by a single authority through a 2009 amendment to the PMLA. Taking note of the growing number of attachment proceedings, the Bench observed that the volume of cases, coupled with the statutory 180-day period for adjudication under Sections 8(2) and 8(3), was placing considerable pressure on the authority.
According to data furnished by the ED, provisional attachment orders increased from 158 in 2019-20 to 461 in 2024-25 and 712 in 2025-26.
The court recommended that the government consider repealing the 2009 amendment and reverting to the earlier arrangement of multiple adjudicating authorities. It said it could have invoked its powers under Article 142 of the Constitution to direct the setting up of regional authorities, but doing so would effectively negate the legislative change.
Background to the dispute
 The issue arose from a batch of petitions challenging the composition and functioning of the PMLA  Adjudicating Authority.
In January 2018, a Delhi High Court Division Bench of Justices S Muralidhar and IS Mehta held that single-member benches could comprise administrative members and need not necessarily include judicial members. It also directed disclosure of reasons underlying attachment proceedings and access to relevant material for affected parties. The Supreme Court stayed that judgment in July 2018.
In March 2023, a Telangana High Court single judge held that members performing quasi-judicial functions must possess legal qualifications. The decision was overturned by a Division Bench in February 2024 in a matter involving Karvy Realty.

title: SC gives HDFC Bank, ICICI Bank, two lenders a week to sanction prosecution
description: The direction comes in a case involving alleged collusion between lenders and developers under home loan subvention schemes, which has left several homebuyers facing financial distress
author: Bhavini Mishra
content:
SC gives HDFC Bank, ICICI Bank, two lenders a week to sanction prosecution
The direction comes in a case involving alleged collusion between lenders and developers under home loan subvention schemes, which has left several homebuyers facing financial distress
Listen to This Article
The Supreme Court (SC) on Thursday directed HDFC Bank, ICICI Bank, Sammaan Capital and PNB Housing Finance to grant unconditional sanction for the prosecution of their officials within a week in connection with an alleged builder-financier nexus that has left several homebuyers facing financial distress.
A Bench headed by Chief Justice of India (CJI) Surya Kant and comprising Justice Joymalya Bagchi and Justice V Mahadevan warned that the chairpersons and managing directors of the financial institutions would have to appear personally before it if they failed to comply with the direction.
The court was hearing a batch of petitions concerning home loan subvention schemes, under which developers had undertaken to pay the equated monthly instalments (EMIs) on behalf of homebuyers until they took possession of their flats or an agreed cut-off date.
“We direct all the banks or financial institutions referred to above to issue unconditional sanction for prosecution within one week, failing which the CMD and Chairman shall remain present in Court to show cause as to why appropriate action be not taken against them,” the court said.
The direction followed submissions by the Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) that it was facing difficulties in obtaining prosecution sanctions under Section 19 of the Prevention of Corruption Act, 1988, against officials of financial institutions allegedly found to be involved during investigations. The agency had also flagged conditional sanctions granted by HDFC Bank.
Also Read
In its sixth supplementary status report, the CBI informed the court that investigations had been completed in 25 of the 55 registered cases. It had filed 22 chargesheets, while closure reports had been submitted in three cases. The agency was at an advanced stage of investigation in another 20 cases, according to submissions made during the hearing.
Expressing displeasure over the delay in granting sanctions, CJI Kant said the court had already expressed strong suspicion about the relationship between banks and developers.
“Once we have passed the order … suspecting, strongly doubting you people hobnobbing with the builders… It is the bounden duty of the banking authorities to grant sanction. And if they will not grant, we are warning them, the next order will be against them,” he said.
The court directed the CBI to complete the remaining investigations expeditiously and asked the courts concerned to take cognisance of the chargesheets and frame charges without delay. The CJI also indicated that the SC would prescribe timelines for completing the trials and would not allow parties to adopt delaying tactics.
The matter will be taken up after seven to 10 days to review compliance with the directions.
How the dispute began
The proceedings originated from grievances raised by homebuyers who had invested in residential projects, primarily in Noida, Greater Noida and Gurugram, under subvention schemes launched between 2013 and 2015. Under these arrangements, banks and housing finance companies entered into tripartite agreements with buyers and developers. The lenders disbursed a substantial portion of the sanctioned home loans directly to developers, often upfront, while builders promised to service the EMIs until possession or an agreed date.
When several developers defaulted on these payments in 2018 and 2019, lenders began demanding instalments from homebuyers even though many projects remained incomplete and possession had not been handed over. Some buyers also alleged that banks had released 70-80 per cent of the loan amounts to developers without adequately linking disbursements to construction progress, in violation of regulatory requirements.
Aggrieved buyers initially approached the Delhi High Court, seeking, among other reliefs, directions to banks to recover the instalments from developers instead of from them. The High Court dismissed the petitions, citing the availability of alternative remedies before the Real Estate Regulatory Authority. The buyers subsequently approached the SC.
On March 4, 2025, the SC observed that the circumstances indicated a possible nexus between banks and developers. It noted that despite repeated directions to furnish information about loan disbursements, project completion and recovery proceedings, only nine financial institutions and five developers had filed compliance affidavits at that stage.
The court also restrained the execution of recovery certificates against homebuyers while allowing proceedings before debt recovery tribunals to continue.
On April 29, 2025, after considering a report submitted by amicus curiae Rajiv Jain, a former Intelligence Bureau director, the court found a prima facie nexus between banks and housing finance companies, on the one hand, and developers, on the other. It directed the CBI to initiate preliminary enquiries and investigate the alleged collusion, including possible violations of Reserve Bank of India and National Housing Bank guidelines governing loan disbursements.
The amicus report identified Supertech as a priority for investigation. It found that the developer had entered into subvention arrangements across 21 projects in six cities with 19 banks and housing finance companies, involving approximately 800 homebuyers.
Eight institutions figuring prominently in these projects were Indiabulls Housing Finance, PNB Housing Finance, Dewan Housing Finance, HDFC Housing Finance, ICICI Bank, India Infoline Housing Finance, L&T Housing Finance and Aditya Birla Housing Finance.
The report also highlighted separate lending exposures involving Corporation Bank, IDBI Bank, Punjab and Sind Bank, Indian Bank and Punjab National Bank. The court subsequently expanded the investigation to cover allegations concerning other developers and financial institutions.
The SC’s April 2025 intervention led to the registration of CBI cases to investigate the alleged criminality and identify the roles of officials of financial institutions and developers. The proceedings have since expanded to cover hundreds of petitions involving thousands of homebuyers across several states.

title: Large stressed firms yield better recoveries under IBC, but delays persist
description: Creditors recovered 31.1% of claims in large cases, marginally above the overall rate of 30.2%, as prolonged resolution timelines erode asset value.
author: Banikinkar Pattanayak
content:
New Delhi: Lenders have recovered a higher share of their claims from large stressed companies than from smaller firms under the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code (IBC), reflecting the stronger investor appeal of larger assets.
Creditors recovered 31.1% of their admitted claims from 218 large stressed companies, each with a default of at least ₹1,000 crore, that underwent resolution under the IBC until September. The recovery amounted to ₹3.91 trillion against admitted claims of ₹12.6 trillion, according to data released by the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Board of India (IBBI).
Across all 1,571 companies that saw resolution under the law since its adoption in late 2016, creditors recovered 30.2% of their admitted claims. The recovery amounted to ₹4.46 trillion against claims of ₹14.77 trillion, with the broader pool, which includes smaller companies, recording marginally lower realizations.
Recoveries from large cases were also higher relative to liquidation value, at 173.3%, compared with 167.4% across all resolved cases.
Larger companies typically have bigger asset bases, offering better prospects of recovery, and a wider geographical presence that can attract strategic investors. However, the size of the stressed asset is not necessarily the decisive factor. Experts point to the timing of insolvency proceedings as a more important influence: the longer a company remains distressed before resolution, the greater the erosion in asset value and the lower the eventual recovery.
The difference in recovery rates is modest, and realizations in a handful of large cases can skew the overall picture because of the substantial amounts involved.
While IBBI does not separately disclose resolution timelines for large and small companies, its data point to persistent delays across insolvency cases. As of September, resolution had taken more than 270 days in 72% of ongoing cases where the process was under way, the regulator's data showed.
In a September report, India Ratings and Research said the “expectations of a meaningful improvement in insolvency recoveries and resolution timelines are yet to be reflected in operating outcomes”.
While resolution activity under the IBC remains steady, creditor recoveries are broadly in line with historical trends, while timelines remain elevated, the rating agency said.
It added that “recovery timing remains a key constraint on recovery efficiency, particularly for stressed-asset portfolios where delayed resolutions can defer cash flows and erode underlying value”. “For security receipts backed by non-performing assets (SR) ratings where insolvency is the main resolution strategy, recovery timing is as important as the ultimate recovery value,” it added.
The average time taken to yield a resolution plan was 771 days as of September, excluding periods excluded by the adjudicating authority, according to IBBI's latest data. This was more than twice the 330-day outer limit stipulated under the law.

title: 26/11 Mumbai attack: Who were Ajmal Kasab’s lawyers? How much remuneration was to be paid to them, and on what basis?
description: Advocates Amin Solkar & Farhana Shah claim they are still awaiting fees for representing Ajmal Kasab in 2010 Bombay HC appeal. Despite official payment structure, Maharashtra State Legal Services Authority says they must submit detailed bills & attendance records before their dues can be cleared.
author: Garvit Bhirani
content:
Nearly 18 years after the 26/11 Mumbai attacks, advocates Amin Solkar and Farhana Shah, who were assigned to represent the sole captured attacker Ajmal Kasab, are yet to receive their fees for handling the case, according to PTI. The two lawyers appeared on Kasab's behalf before the Bombay High Court for nine months after the Maharashtra government appointed them in June 2010. The two lawyers were assigned to defend Kasab in his appeal against the death sentence awarded by a trial court. Despite completing their responsibilities more than 15 years ago, both claim their remuneration remains unsettled, raising questions over the delay in clearing payments to court-appointed legal representatives. According to the appointment notification issued on June 8, 2010, by the Maharashtra State Legal Services Authority (MSLSA), Solkar was entitled to remuneration equivalent to that of a special public prosecutor, while Shah was to receive fees on the scale applicable to an additional public prosecutor handling a death penalty confirmation case. Official sources estimated the applicable remuneration at approximately ₹1,500 to ₹2,000 per day. Amin Solkar and Farhana Shah were nominated by the Bombay High Court and subsequently appointed by the MSLSA to represent Kasab during the proceedings before the High Court. Solkar and Shah took up the defence after the court assigned them the responsibility of ensuring that Kasab had legal representation during his appeal against the capital punishment. Both advocates said the case required them to put their other professional commitments on hold to ensure that the proceedings continued without disruption. "We have still not received our fees for representing Kasab. I have been corresponding with the Maharashtra State Legal Services Authority time and again, but there seems to be no positive headway," Solkar told PTI. Shah also recalled the time and effort involved in handling the case, saying, "We gave our entire day for nine months to argue this case. We had to keep all our other cases on the backburner so that there was no hurdle caused to the proceedings." The June 8, 2010 notification specified the payment structure for both advocates by linking their remuneration to the rates applicable to government prosecutors. Under the arrangement, Solkar's fees were to match those of a special public prosecutor, while Shah was entitled to the remuneration of an additional public prosecutor handling a death penalty confirmation matter. Based on the applicable rates, official sources placed their daily remuneration at around ₹1,500- ₹2,000. Shah maintained that the notification also stipulated that their fees should be released after the High Court delivered its verdict. Solkar questioned why the government had not applied the same prescribed payment structure to settle their outstanding bills. "What is stopping the government from using the same pay scale and clearing our dues?" he questioned. The two advocates said their attempts to secure the pending remuneration have repeatedly run into requests from the MSLSA for detailed bills and attendance records specifying the dates and hours they appeared in court. They have questioned the demand, arguing that reconstructing such granular records more than a decade after the proceedings is difficult. Shah also pointed out that the appointment notification and the High Court order had already established the basis for their payment. However, an MSLSA official maintained that advocates must submit formal bills and appearance-related memorandums under the authority's standard procedure before their fees can be cleared. In contrast, Abbas Kazmi, who represented Kasab during the trial before special judge M L Tahaliyani, said his remuneration was paid without a similar prolonged delay. "My remuneration was cleared by the government soon after the completion of the trial," Kazmi said. The Bombay High Court began hearing Kasab's death sentence confirmation proceedings and appeal in June 2010. It upheld the death penalty in February 2011, a decision subsequently affirmed by the Supreme Court. Kasab, who had been held at Mumbai's Arthur Road prison following his capture, was executed at Yerwada Central Jail in Pune on November 21, 2012. The November 26, 2008 attacks involved 10 heavily armed Pakistani terrorists who targeted several locations in Mumbai over more than 60 hours. A total of 166 people, including six Americans, were killed. (With inputs from agency) Garvit Bhirani is a journalist based in Gurugram. With a total of six years of experience in journalism, he has previously worked with Vaco Binary Semantics for Google, taking on the role of news curation lead, and reported from the field on health, education, and agriculture stories for 101reporters and News9. He has also served as a content editor for entertainment and news media organisations.

Garvit holds bachelor’s and master’s degrees in journalism and mass communication from Guru Gobind Singh Indraprastha University and Gurugram University, respectively. During college days, he joined India’s only non-profit student journalism network, where he anchored daily news updates and produced his own weekly show called ‘Data Fix’.

He was selected for the YES Foundation Media for Social Change Fellowship in Delhi, the Talking Data to the Fourth Pillar residential workshop, and the VOICE Fellowship in Pune.

He holds certificates in COVID-19-verification reporting, data journalism, food & agriculture, tech policy, media literacy and countering misinformation, and tackling election disinformation courses from Thomson Foundation, IndiaSpend, The Dialogue, US Mission in India, and AFP.

title: Centre clears Rs 50,000 crore-plus urban projects across 16 states, UTs, including projects in Lucknow, Va
description: The Centre has approved several urban infrastructure projects totaling more than Rs 50,000 crore. This funding supports initiatives in states like Bihar, Uttar Pradesh, and Tamil Nadu, among others. Projects include city redevelopment, water management, and waste processing efforts. The Urban Challenge Fund encourages cities to adopt market-based financing instead of relying solely on government grants. These approvals aim to stimulate extensive infrastructure development across various regions.
author: ET Online
content:
The approvals were highlighted at a national workshop on unlocking market-based financing for UCF projects, organised by the Department of Urban Development, the Union Housing and Urban Affairs Ministry said.
The projects span urban redevelopment, city infrastructure, water management and waste processing, reflecting the fund's focus on mobilising private and market-linked financing for urban development, according to the ministry.
Among the projects cleared are creative redevelopment initiatives in Patna, Lucknow and Varanasi, along with a comprehensive development plan for Warangal.
A waste-to-energy project in Lucknow has also received approval.
Tamil Nadu has secured approvals for projects covering smart metering, water treatment and waste-to-energy. Under the fund's 'Cities as Growth Hubs' vertical, projects in the Sarusajai area of Guwahati and the Gangtok Gateway project in Sikkim have also been cleared, PTI reported, citing the ministry's statement.
The UCF marks a shift from the traditional grant-based model to a market-linked, reform-driven and outcome-oriented framework for financing urban infrastructure, the ministry said.
The Centre has provisioned Rs 1 lakh crore in assistance under the fund to catalyse investments of nearly Rs 4 lakh crore. Projects are classified under three verticals: Cities as Growth Hubs, Creative Redevelopment of Cities, and Water and Sanitation.

title: ‘Don't just wave constitution’: Amit Shah's swipe at Rahul Gandhi over 'pocket constitution'
description: Union Home Minister Amit Shah took a veiled swipe at Rahul Gandhi and the Opposition on Constitution Day, saying that carrying a copy of the Constitution and displaying it in public is not enough; political parties and individuals must also uphold its spirit. Referring to those who carry the Constitution in their pockets or wave it before the public, Shah urged them to spend 15 minutes reading the original document in Parliament's library and understanding its illustrations and historical significance. Shah highlighted the artwork in the original Constitution, including depictions of Lord Ram, Lord Buddha, Lord Mahavira and Rani Lakshmibai.
