title: Parliament to Reconvene on Nov 30; NDA Looks for Majority on Delimitation
description: National | Parliament reconvenes November 30 after 108 days as NDA seeks support for delimitation, 850 Lok Sabha seats and 33% women's reservation.
author: PratidinTime National Desk
content:
Parliament will meet again after a record gap, with the Lok Sabha resuming on Monday, November 30 and the Rajya Sabha on Wednesday, December 2. The BJP-led NDA is trying to assemble the two-thirds majority it lacked in April, when it could not carry its delimitation proposal through the Lok Sabha. Parliamentary Affairs Minister Kiren Rijiju announced the dates on Thursday.
"The Government has requested Hon'ble Speaker, Lok Sabha and Hon'ble Chairman, Rajya Sabha to reconvene Lok Sabha on Monday, 30th November, 2026 and Rajya Sabha on Wednesday, 2nd December, 2026 respectively to transact essential Government Business," Rijiju said in a post on social media.
He did not say what the business would be. The Union Cabinet is due to meet on Friday, and the delimitation bill is expected to be on its agenda, according to sources. The sittings may end on December 3, but in practice the Lok Sabha has four sittings and the Rajya Sabha two. The sittings continue the Monsoon Session, which was never prorogued and has been in suspension since August. By November 30, the gap since the last sitting will be 108 days, longer than the earlier record of 87 days set in 2008. A House whose session has not been prorogued can be recalled at less than a week's notice, whereas a fresh summons after prorogation needs two weeks.
The government's proposal would expand the Lok Sabha from 543 to 850 seats, with about 283 of them reserved for women by rotation. Seats would be redistributed among states on the basis of the 2011 census or any other census the Centre chooses, instead of waiting for Census 2027 to finish. The move is meant to clear the way for the 33 per cent women's quota that Parliament enacted in 2023. In April, Home Minister Amit Shah verbally promised that every state's seats would rise by a flat 50 per cent to preserve the existing balance, but that assurance was never written into the bill.
Because the proposal is a constitutional amendment, floor managers reckon the government needs around 360 votes in the Lok Sabha, depending on attendance. The NDA is believed to count 319 members as certain, 241 of them from the BJP. Including the 8 MPs of the NCP (Sharadchandra Pawar) would bring the tally to 327. The party's Supriya Sule has said it could back the bill if every state's seats rise by a flat 50 per cent, ensuring no regional bias, though she has ruled out a merger with the NCP faction already in the NDA. The DMK's 22 MPs would take the figure to nearly 350, still short by about 10, and the party has not stated its position on Shah's verbal assurance. The rest would have to come from the roughly 36 MPs who belong to neither bloc.
The Congress-led INDIA bloc has laid down four conditions: the Lok Sabha stays at 543 seats, each state keeps its present number, the 2023 women's reservation law is enforced immediately with 182 of the current seats set aside for women, and a constitutional amendment freezes this arrangement for 25 years. Sources said the Opposition would readily back the necessary bills if these were accepted, though that would amount to the government abandoning its redrawing plan altogether. The Opposition's argument is that the quota is already law and can be delinked from delimitation, and it has accused the government of using the women's quota as cover to redraw constituencies in its favour. Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge has repeatedly written to Prime Minister Narendra Modi seeking an all-party meeting.
The government, in turn, has accused the Congress of obstructing women's empowerment. Speaking earlier on Thursday at a Constitution Day event, Shah said, "I want to tell [Leader of Opposition] Rahul Gandhi: it is the resolve of the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) and our leader Narendra Modi that the women of this country will definitely get 33 per cent reservation; you cannot stop us." The Prime Minister spoke in a similar vein.
Time is also short. If the bills do not clear in this sitting, there may not be enough time to hold the 2029 Lok Sabha elections on redrawn boundaries.

title: India Emerges as Asia's Rising Power, Narrowing Gap with China in 2026 Index
description: India has further strengthened its position as a major power in Asia, with the gap between India and China narrowing to its lowest level, according to the 2026 edition of the Asia Power Index released by Australia’s Lowy Institute.
author: Sentinel Digital Desk
content:
NEW DELHI: India has further strengthened its position as a major power in Asia, with the gap between India and China narrowing to its lowest level, according to the 2026 edition of the Asia Power Index released by Australia’s Lowy Institute. India’s overall score rose to 40.5, making it the only country in Lowy’s Major Power tier, behind the two superpowers, the US and China, and ahead of Japan, Russia and Australia.
The 2026 Asia Power Index assesses 27 countries and territories across 131 indicators, examining economic and military capabilities, diplomatic influence, defence partnerships and cultural reach. Launched in 2018, the index tracks the distribution of power across Asia and changes in the regional balance of influence.
India's growing diplomatic influence, stronger long-term economic prospects and expanding regional security partnerships have contributed to its rising stature. India ranked fourth when the index was first launched in 2018 and retained that position in 2023. It moved to third place in 2024 after overtaking Japan and has maintained the position for the third consecutive edition. In 2025, India crossed the 40-point threshold, regaining its status in Lowy’s Major Power category. (PIB)

title: MHA Issues Alert on WhatsApp Web: Cyber Threats Linked to Pakistan-Based Operatives
description: The Union Home Ministry’s nodal cyber security agency I4C has cautioned government functionaries against sharing sensitive information through WhatsApp Web sessions, a move that follows detection of suspicious activities of ‘Pakistan-based intelligence operatives’.
author: Sentinel Digital Desk
content:
NEW DELHI: The Union Home Ministry’s nodal cyber security agency I4C has cautioned government functionaries against sharing sensitive information through WhatsApp Web sessions, a move that follows detection of suspicious activities of ‘Pakistan-based intelligence operatives’.
The cybersecurity advisory cautioning against using WhatsApp Web for official or sensitive work follows a probe that revealed Pakistan-based intelligence operatives infiltrated over 50 defence-related WhatsApp groups, said an official source on Monday.
Advising government officials to avoid staying logged in on computers and laptops, the National Cybercrime Threat Analytics Unit (NCTAU), Indian Cyber Crime Coordination Centre (I4C), warned that such sessions could be misused to take control of the account for fraud or phishing, said an official statement.
Sources said the Pakistan-based intelligence operatives used spoofed Indian numbers to join as ‘dead members’, monitoring chats in groups linked to the NSG, CRPF, commandos, and even DRDO without drawing attention. (IANS)

title: US, India enhance defence ties with Javelin Deal, Quad collaboration
description: India and the United States have significantly expanded their defence partnership in 2026 through a series of major military exercises, defence sales, co-production initiatives and enhanced cooperation under the Quad framework, reinforcing their shared commitment to regional security and a free and open Indo-Pacific.
author: Sentinel Digital Desk
content:
NEW DELHI: India and the United States have significantly expanded their defence partnership in 2026 through a series of major military exercises, defence sales, co-production initiatives and enhanced cooperation under the Quad framework, reinforcing their shared commitment to regional security and a free and open Indo-Pacific.
According to a fact sheet titled ‘US-India Major Defense Partnership’, the two countries continued to build on their Major Defence Partnership, which was strengthened by a new 10-year framework signed in 2025 to expand military cooperation and defence industrial collaboration.
“The United States and India share a strong and growing Major Defense Partnership built on trust, mutual respect, and shared security interests,” the fact sheet stated, highlighting the growing scope of bilateral military engagement.
The fact sheet noted that India conducts more military exercises with the United States than with any other country, reflecting the depth of their defence ties.
Among the major military engagements in 2026 was the 22nd edition of Exercise Yudh Abhyas, held from September 15 to 27 across Auli in Uttarakhand and the Mahajan Field Firing Range in Rajasthan. The exercise brought together approximately 500-600 military personnel from each country and focused on integrated combat operations, counterterrorism, drones, autonomous systems and live-fire training.
The United States also participated in the Indian Air Force’s multinational Exercise Tarang Shakti from September 26 to October 12 in Jodhpur, alongside six other foreign air forces. The exercise marked the first participation of American F-35 fifth-generation fighter aircraft in a military exercise on Indian soil, demonstrating growing cooperation between the two air forces.
Another significant engagement was the fifth edition of Exercise Tiger Triumph, conducted from October 31 to November 5 in Visakhapatnam. The bilateral tri-service exercise focused on humanitarian assistance and disaster relief (HADR), including joint amphibious operations, staff planning and coordination between the armed forces of both countries.
Maritime cooperation also remained a key pillar of the partnership, with the United States, India, Australia and Japan participating in Exercise Malabar 2026 from November 5 to 12 in Japan. Originally established as a bilateral US-India naval exercise in 1992, Malabar has evolved into a major multilateral maritime exercise involving all four Quad partners. On the defence industrial front, the two countries advanced cooperation through major agreements involving American military platforms and equipment. (ANI)

title: ‘Oil!’: 100 years ago, Upton Sinclair wrote the great American anti‑capitalist epic
description: Sinclair’s world was one in which writers could, and often did, hold corporations and governments publicly accountable.
author: Tamlyn Avery, The Conversation
content:
First serialised in the Communist Party publication The Daily Worker in 1926–7, Upton Sinclair’s Oil! is now known as the inspiration for Paul Thomas Anderson’s loose film adaptation There Will Be Blood (2007). But the novel is one of American literature’s most prescient anti-capitalist epics.
Set against the backdrop of California’s oil boom in the 1910s and the United States’ entry into World War I, Oil! is a family saga that identifies the dark shadow looming behind almost all of modernity’s uneven developments and pressing social issues. The oil industry is to Sinclair’s socialist worldview what whaling is to Herman Melville’s Moby-Dick. Whether spermaceti or crude, oil makes legible the entire incomprehensible sweep of the modern world as we know it.
Sinclair sets out to prove that oil is not an inert substance; it is the all-too-real lubricant that keeps the cogs of capitalism turning. Oil fuels progress, development and the growth of modern civilisation; it is the supreme metaphor of modernity itself.
The story of modernity is one of violent struggles and inequalities, and oil has left its unctuous residue across every aspect of economic, political, social and cultural life, often with disastrous consequences.
A radical career
Sinclair was born in 1878 – in the first decade that fossil fuels “provided more energy to societies than traditional photosynthesis”, as literary critic Michael Tondre has noted.
His childhood in Baltimore, Maryland, coincided with a period of increasing economic inequality and labour wars across the US. He likened his family life to “a series of Cinderella transformations” between scarcity and comfort, depending on whether his father, an alcoholic liquor salesman, “had the money for that week’s board”.
Lifting himself out of poverty by writing dime novels, Sinclair increasingly sought to educate himself about the labour struggles that were rumbling around the nation in the 1890s. He began contributing to various socialist magazines while undertaking postgraduate studies in New York, before turning in earnest to the political writing for which he would be remembered.
Sinclair produced an astonishing quantity of fiction and non-fiction. On several occasions, he ran (unsuccessfully) for public office on a socialist platform. His world was one in which writers could, and often did, hold corporations and governments publicly accountable. He recognised fiction was an especially powerful tool for activism and raising class consciousness.
“Great literature”, he reflected in his autobiography, had historically been “a product of the leisure classes and defends their position, whether consciously or by implication”. But literature, he claimed, was becoming “a weapon in the class struggle – of the master class to hold its servants down, and of the working class to break its bonds”.
The publication of The Jungle (1906) established Sinclair as a force to be reckoned with. A muckraking novel about the Chicago stockyards, The Jungle showed how the meatpacking industry’s unsanitary conditions and brutal exploitation of immigrant workers were enabled by corrupt capitalists with local politicians in their pockets.
The novel “aimed at the public’s heart”, Sinclair later quipped, but “by accident I hit it in the stomach”. The backlash prompted by his revelations forced President Theodore Roosevelt to endorse a Pure Food and Drug Act and Meat Inspection Act in 1906, to assure the public that adulterated or spoiled food was not being sold to consumers.
America’s rich and powerful learned to take seriously the threat posed by Sinclair’s pen. This earned him the esteem of many major left-wing intellectuals of the day, including Eugene Debs, Jack London and Albert Einstein.
Sinclair used his profits from The Jungle to establish a utopian commune, Helicon Home Colony, in New Jersey, which unfortunately burned down in 1907.
Human nature in the raw
Sinclair would go on to write King Coal (1917), which took up the cause of unionising coal miners, though it went largely unnoticed. It was Oil!, the third of his major industrial novels, in which he took up his most ambitious theme. In intricate detail, Sinclair set out to dramatise the supply chain through which crude oil is extracted from the earth, refined, stored, transported, produced and sold to the consumer as a commodity.
The novel was conceived in 1921, when Sinclair witnessed the Shell Oil corporation strike a 35-metre geyser near his wife’s property in Long Beach, California. Overnight, investors swarmed, trying to cash in on the liquid gold rush. “It was human nature in the raw,” Sinclair recalled, “and this was the first time I had seen it completely naked”:
“Cliques were formed, and tempers blazed – they never quite came to blows, but almost. And there sat a novelist, watching, listening, and storing away material for what he knew was going to be a great long novel. He listened to the lawyers and to the oilmen who came to make offers; they told their troubles. They wanted the lease as cheaply as possible, and they had no idea they were going to be in a novel with the title Oil! – including the exclamation point.”
The punctuation mark was necessary to avoid a copyright injunction, but it aptly symbolised the intoxicating process of abstraction that transformed crude oil into a magical substance fuelling our wildest desires and bitterest rivalries. Oil represented mobility, power and the potential to remake the world around our material wants and needs. But it obscured the volatile social processes, struggles and forces involved in its production.
Sinclair sought to extend the insights of radical journalistic exposés, including Mary Tarbell’s The History of Standard Oil Company (1904) about corruption in the oil industry. But he believed fiction had powerful advantages over journalism. It could humanise complex political and economic forces, making abstract issues feel comprehensible and relatable.
As a contribution to the fight against capitalism, he confided to a family member in 1925 that this “oil novel will be the best thing I have ever done”.
A radical education
Sinclair’s writing formula was simple and consistent. “Readers of my novels know that I have one favourite theme,” he claimed: “the contrast between the social classes”. There are “characters from both worlds” and plots “contrived to carry you from one to the other”.
Beginning in 1912, Oil! is a coming-of-age novel set around Los Angeles, or “Angel City” as it was called. Its young hero, James “Bunny” Ross Jr., is the son of a successful independent oil producer who is prospecting for new sites to drill.
Ross Sr. starts out as an independent entrepreneur who sees himself as one of the “little guys” standing up to the big oil companies, including Standard Oil and Shell, who use their money to buy land and political influence to squeeze out competitors.
As father and son speed across California, surveying land for suitable tracts to drill, they bribe everyone from highway policemen to local politicians. They seek to turn rocky passes into smooth highways for transporting oil and machinery.
Through Bunny’s perspective, Oil! demystifies the commodity’s production. The reader is drawn into the wondrous chemical and engineering feats through which an unrefined substance is blasted out of the earth’s core and refined, beginning a new life as energy for a waxing empire ruled not by any democratically elected government, but by an arbitrary handful of men at the helm of a small number of powerful corporations.
Bunny’s radical education intensifies when he strikes up a friendship with Paul Watkins, the son of an ignorant goatherd whom Ross Sr. swindles by purchasing his land cheaply and renting it back to him, before it is revealed that the fields are saturated with liquid gold.
This tract of land, ironically named Paradise, yields a “gusher” of crude right on the eve of World War I. The conflict causes the global demand for fuel to increase exponentially and Ross’ profits skyrocket, launching him into the big league of oil tsardom.
Bunny remains loyal to his father, who believes any means justifies the end, because “the world needs oil”. But his moral reservations deepen during a workers’ strike, when his father refuses to distance himself from the underhanded strike-breaking tactics of the corrupt Petroleum Employers’ Federation, including deploying private security firm Pinkertons to terrorise the workers into submission.
The strike leaves the idealistic Bunny with a growing sense reality may not stack up with the education he has received from his father – or from school and university, institutions which, he learns, receive funding from big oil donors, just like many contemporary universities.
The red millionaire
Paul represents Sinclair’s ideal “incarnation of the new, awakening working class”. He is knowledgeable, loyal, purposeful, courageous. He is, however, conscripted into the US Army and posted to Russia. After the armistice, he is forced, with his fellow servicemen to remain there to help crush the revolution. The reason, he discovers, is to prevent the Bolsheviks from socialising the nation’s oil resources and erasing the tsar’s debts to several major American banks.
Paul’s example teaches Bunny – and the reader – to see how oil gives limitless influence, control and wealth to the few, while it robs the vast majority of dignity and agency. For many workers, it denies life itself. For every inch of progress oil facilitates, thousands of lives are lost in the rush to build the industry, and in the wars fought to protect reserves and investments.
With an awe that is equal parts terror and admiration, Bunny begins to realise the magnitude of what oil represents. He feels obliged to play the role of oil prince. He drives sports cars and dates Hollywood actresses. But he increasingly feels alienated. The press dubs him a “red millionaire”.
Sinclair enters the capitalists’ world through this internalised class conflict. He shows how they control the circulation of knowledge in universities and newspapers, bribe politicians and lawmakers, pay film executives to produce propaganda demonising revolutionary workers’ movements, and fund religious groups to control their parishioners’ votes.
Sinclair’s understanding of many of these issues was based on his own observations and experiences. His discussion of Hollywood’s propaganda machine would prove to be prophetic. When Sinclair ran for governor of California in 1934 on a platform of ending poverty, Irving Thalberg, head of production at Metro-Goldwyn-Mayer, attacked him in newsreels that played before every feature film, sinking his campaign. Historian Greg Mitchell has argued the discrediting tactics used against Sinclair were the “birth of media politics”.
Bunny’s political conversion deepens amid a second larger strike, incorporating more industries this time. He expropriates his father’s profits to try and exonerate imprisoned strikers, including Paul, who has returned to California fully converted to communism.
With his comrades, Bunny establishes a radical newspaper to raise consciousness. He funds a night school for organising workers to learn about the class struggle, driving a wedge between him and his father’s world. Like Sinclair, Bunny remains adamant that factional disputes must not distract from the common enemy: capitalism, friend of the fascists, who were already on the march in 1927. This theme would be elaborated in Sinclair’s Pulitzer Prize-winning Lanny Budd series of the 1940s and 1950s.
Imagining a world without oil
Oil! is a campus novel, a family saga, a Bildungsroman, an engineering manual, a satire of sexual politics, a historical drama, and an anti-capitalist diatribe. It highlights the fact that oil touches every aspect of modernity. No aspect of modern society escapes the torrential flow of Sinclair’s imagination. The novel covers oil-related themes, such as the rise of the automobile industry, and less obviously connected themes, such as Prohibition, religious revivalism, the rise of Hollywood, spiritualism, and the birth-control movement.
The pleasure of a Sinclair potboiler is not its aesthetic polish, but immersing oneself in the immense ideas materialising on the page in a great “gush of words”, as Sinclair himself put it.
At 550 pages, Oil! is a slow-burner. But its rougher edges are offset by moments of sublime intensity, including this one early in the novel, when an accident causes the Paradise well to erupt in flames – a moment memorably captured in Anderson’s film:
“Mountains of smoke rose to the sky, and mountains of flame came seething down to the earth; every jet that struck the ground turned into a volcano, and rose again, higher than before; the whole mass, boiling and bursting, became a river of fire, a lava flood that went streaming down the valley, turning everything it touched into flame, then swallowing it up and hiding the flames in a cloud of smoke.”
This vitality plays an important part in training the reader to feel toward oil and those who manipulate it, moving from wonder and fear to disgust and hate.
As in all Sinclair novels, the narrator converts the protagonist’s moral lesson into a didactic message: we must recognise oil as the abstraction of “evil Power” that leads “nations to destruction by visions of unearned wealth, and the opportunity to enslave and exploit labor”. We must continue in our belief there will be utopia after capitalism, because everything is on the line and, in the words of Karl Marx and Friedrich Engels, which became Sinclair’s motto, “there is a world to win”.
There is no simple way to visualise what 100 million barrels of oil burning looks like, but this is approximately how much oil the world burns every 24 hours. Nor is it easy to comprehend the 42 billion tonnes of carbon dioxide emissions that enter our atmosphere in a single year.
It is no simpler to imagine what it will take to break free of fossil fuels. It must surely take the end of market-driven, profit-based mode of production. Yet, as philosopher Fredric Jameson once remarked, it “is easier to imagine the end of the world than to imagine the end of capitalism”. To his credit, Sinclair teaches us that we must always rise to that imaginative challenge.
Tamlyn Avery is a Lecturer in English Literature, Adelaide University.
This article first appeared on The Conversation.

title: On shrinking, shifting sandbars, migrants build lives amid floods and wandering elephants
description: Charlands are a refuge for migrants searching for land. For elephants, disruption due to agriculture and humans is causing them to search far and wide for food.
author: Arathi Menon
content:
Fifty-seven-year-old Budharu Muhammed recalls a time when bombs, shells and ammunition flowed down the Teesta towards Premganj char, a sandbar settlement around 15 km from Jalpaiguri town in West Bengal. It was 2023, when a massive glacial lake outburst flood from South Lhonak Lake in the Sikkim Himalayas caused a major surge in the Teesta, damaging infrastructure and affecting hydropower projects downstream.
Silt, sand and rubble were flushed downstream. According to Muhammed, some army camps were flooded, explaining the sudden appearance of military materiel in his village and the panic it triggered. “There were other toxic things flowing down from medical shops and factories, oil from vehicles and gas cylinders. The water was murky with a layer of oil on top,” he says. People complained of skin rashes and itching after coming into contact with the water, he recalls, describing a time of uncertainty and fear.
Located under Paharpur Gram Panchayat in the Sadar block of Jalpaiguri district, Premganj char, also known as Jaliapara, is identified as a highly vulnerable charland in the district’s disaster management plans.
Adding to the woes of residents facing constant flooding and erosion is another threat: the movement of maljurians, or groups of male elephants.
Maljurians comprise younger males and experienced adults that explore new landscapes, largely in search of food, explains Avijan Saha, a researcher with the wildlife conservation non-profit Airavat Trust who has studied the landscape for over a decade. “Other elephants can then follow the routes they have explored. These groups therefore play a role in helping elephants discover new feeding areas,” he says. A 2019 study of all-male elephant group formations in southern India found that such groupings can be an adaptive strategy in anthropogenically altered environments.
When maljurias visit in groups
Saha traces the beginning of elephant movement into Jaliapara to around 2018, when a group of 15-16 elephants from the nearby Baikunthapur forest began foraging on the charland. Although the area is not a traditional elephant corridor, the animals discovered its cultivated fields as a source of food, he says. Since then, more elephants have moved into the chars. Saha estimates that around 100 elephants enter Jaliapara seasonally each year, largely from nearby forests.
Baikunthapur forest and Mahananda Wildlife Sanctuary are important elephant habitats within the broader Eastern Dooars Elephant Reserve landscape. “The forests and protected areas are fragmented. Their ecological connections are important for elephants moving across North Bengal and adjoining areas,” Saha says.
According to Saha, the wider landscape, extending from the Mechi River near the India-Nepal border to the Sankosh River near the West Bengal-Assam border, supports more than 700 elephants. Saha, who has been closely observing elephant movements, estimates that around 300 use the landscape relevant to his research which includes Jaliapara, although the estimate remains largely anecdotal with no official records to substantiate it. He emphasises that elephant movements must be understood at the landscape scale rather than by examining individual chars in isolation.
Habitat fragmentation has been driven by tea cultivation, railway lines, settlements and tourism, which expanded particularly during the 1990s and 2000s. The Teesta-Mahananda Link Canal project, introduced around 1976 primarily for irrigation, also altered the landscape around Baikunthapur forest and the canal corridor, as per Saha’s observation. Subsequent agricultural expansion further changed land use.
Elephant movements are closely linked to cropping cycles. Haricharan Roy, 58, a resident, says the animals visit more frequently during the maize season, which runs from around March or April through June. “May and June are particularly important months for elephants,” Saha adds.
“The maize is then harvested, and the elephants begin dispersing. Paddy cultivation begins around September, and the elephants may return to feed,” Saha says, adding: “Maize fields are often concentrated in continuous stretches, whereas paddy fields are more dispersed. This means elephants may congregate in particular areas when maize is available but spread out when paddy is being cultivated.”
Learning to live with the jumbos
The residents of Jaliapara have developed their own ways to stay safe around elephants. “When they walk through water during heavy rain, we can hear the splashing sound, made by their heavy footsteps,” Roy says.
Residents climb a watchtower and use searchlights to spot elephants, beating drums and metal containers to drive them away. But little can be done when elephants arrive in large numbers, particularly bull elephants, the maljurians. “During the corn season, we can’t sleep out of fear. This year, they fully broke down two of our houses,” he adds.
Elephants move beyond the char through a wider landscape where cultivated fields, settlements and other human activities overlap with their routes. “For elephants, entering cultivated land is a high-risk, high-reward strategy. They face the risk of encountering people, but the food available can make the risk worthwhile,” Saha points out.
Despite crop damage and the destruction of homes, residents do not necessarily view elephants with hostility. “The local farmers encounter elephants routinely, yet there have not been any severe human retaliation against the animal,” Saha shares. “A few elephant fatalities in the past were due to accidental ingestion of pesticides used by farmers,” he adds.
Lives shaped by flooding and erosion
The number of officially recognised Teesta charlands remains unclear. The disaster management plan identifies several char settlements, including Premganj, Nathua, Mouamari, Doldolia and Jahajmari, but does not provide a comprehensive count of all Teesta chars.
Floods are not new to Jaliapara residents. Muhammed knows his birth year only because he was born during a major flood in 1968. The next big flood, in 2023, caused considerable damage to the livelihoods of farmers who also fish on the charland. “Many fish, small and large, died in huge numbers,” he says. Potato and pea crops also suffered severe damage. “The soil quality changed, turning into marsh. It is slowly improving. With more cultivation cycles, the soil gets better,” says Muhammed, drawing on decades of farming experience to remain optimistic about the charland’s future.
Teesta charlands are often temporary or semi-stable sand and silt formations created as the river deposits sediment carried from the Himalayas. Over time, some charlands become more stable and near-permanent. Changes in river flow, flooding, erosion and sediment loads continually reshape these landforms, causing some to expand, shift or disappear.
Monsoon patterns have also changed over the past 10 to 15 years, says researcher Saha. “When there is heavy rainfall, water is released from the dams, causing Teesta to rise suddenly,” he says.
During floods, residents move to a higher ground along the embankment or to parts of the char that remain above water. They return when the water recedes, Saha adds.
The river’s natural flow has changed over time due to multiple factors, including dams and barrages, says Eklabya Sharma, strategic advisor and distinguished fellow at ATREE, a non-profit organisation focused on environmental conservation and sustainable, socially just development. “In the past, charlands, formed under natural river flow conditions with the rivers following their own courses and changing routes according to the intensity of precipitation, were more sustainable,” he says.
Charlands have traditionally attracted agriculture and human settlements because of their fertile soils. However, changes in river flow and sediment movement have affected both the stability and fertility of these landforms, Sharma explains.
Muhammed began noticing riverbank erosion about a decade ago. “Earlier, Teesta was deeper,” he says. “The riverbed was low. Water flowed along its course without eroding the banks.” He attributes repeated flooding and erosion to the rising riverbed.
“Riverbeds are rising in places where sediment is accumulating,” Sharma explains. In addition to soil, large boulders and other material enter the river, while landslides can bring down trees and debris that obstruct water flow. He also points to the loss of natural forest cover, which previously helped reduce the amount of debris entering rivers.
A refuge for migrants looking for land
Despite frequent inundation, erosion and seasonal elephant visits, charlands support agriculture by providing cultivable land. Residents also depend on river-related livelihoods, including fishing, boat-making and collecting driftwood. Muhammed combines several occupations: he is a fisher, boatmaker, construction worker, farmer and farmland lessor.
Longtime residents of the char (also chaur in Bangla) like Muhammed lease portions of their land to farmers from other parts of West Bengal, many of whom have migrated from climate-vulnerable areas such as the Sundarbans and Cooch Behar.
“Some families who came from the Sundarbans have now settled permanently along the Teesta. People have also come from Burdwan, Cooch Behar and other parts of North Bengal,” says Saha.
Although these transient landforms do not legally belong to anyone, people occupy and cultivate them to sustain their livelihoods. Muhammed has 15 bighas of land on the char, equivalent to roughly five acres. “As long as the land remains, we cultivate and eat from it; if it washes away, it’s gone,” he says.
Muhammed lives with his wife, son, daughter-in-law and grandson in a kutcha house made largely of bamboo and mud, set within a large compound on a relatively safer side of the char.
Haricharan Roy has 10 bighas (3.3 acres) of land at Jaliapara. Originally from Basusuba village in Kranti block of Jalpaiguri district, Roy had no land of his own there. He moved to Mouamari village in Maynaguri block 25 years ago to pursue agriculture. After floods and erosion destroyed his cultivable land, he moved with his family of seven to Jaliapara three months ago.
“The biggest challenge for us here is the river in constant flux: when one bank erodes, another comes up,” Roy says.
When a sandbar emerges and has no recognised owner, someone may level it with a tractor and begin cultivation. Others then occupy portions of the land. “When migrants from other places come, we let them lease parcels of these lands from us to do cultivation,” Muhammed explains.
The arrangement is informal and resembles a syndicate, says Saha. Someone arriving from the Sundarbans, for instance, may approach a person living on higher ground and ask for land to cultivate. The amount charged depends on local demand and market conditions. “A seasonal lease might cost around Rs 5,000 to Rs 7,000 (for a bigha of land), although the amount varies. When the lease period ends, the cultivator may have to negotiate again for the next season.”
Potatoes, maize and sometimes paddy dominate cultivation. Farming is possible only while the land remains exposed and stable enough to support crops. Some migrants come for a single cultivation cycle before returning to their home areas for other seasons.
Life on these charlands is caught in a time warp, where a lessee who cannot pay in cash sometimes settles the dues with a share of the harvest.
“The local communities and political leaders know about these arrangements. The Irrigation Department and Agriculture Department are also aware of what is happening, but the system continues. As long as the arrangement remains relatively peaceful, there is little intervention,” Saha adds.
Bijoy Barman, 76, is a migrant from Sitalkuchi in Cooch Behar district. Around 15 such migrant families live in constant uncertainty. Barman recalls the floods earlier this year. “Our original house was over that side,” he says, pointing to the other end of the charland. “We stayed in waist-deep water for 15 days straight!” Rising river waters during the monsoon inundated the part of Jaliapara where his house stood.
The families now live in makeshift sheds with tarpaulin roofs stretched over four wooden posts. Their belongings are packed into bundles so they can flee to safety if the water suddenly surges or when maljurias come calling.
A precarious livelihood that goes unrecorded in state records can be lost at any time, either to the river or to the authorities. Such losses push families deeper into poverty. These migrants remain trapped in a cycle of transience, with no permanent home to return to.
“Teesta gives us and Teesta takes from us,” he says. “We invested Rs 22000 in farming paddy, did all the manual labor ourselves, hoping for a good harvest, but floods destroyed everything. It was a complete loss,” he says, his helplessness evident.
Migrants lead particularly precarious lives due to the lack of legal recognition of their occupation. “Despite living here all these years, my wife and I still don’t receive pension for seniors,” Barman says.
Their Aadhaar and voter ID cards carry the addresses and other details of their places of origin, not Jaliapara, leaving their lives on the charland unrecorded in official documents. Accessing healthcare is another challenge. During a medical emergency, residents must first cross the unpredictable river by canoe before travelling by road to the nearest government hospital. The journey can be difficult and time-consuming.
Understanding coexistence
For Saha, understanding the interactions between residents and elephants requires looking beyond immediate losses. Residents receive no compensation for crop losses, as they do not for flood damage, because their occupation of the chars is not formally recognised. “I do not want to approach the issue by immediately telling people that elephants are causing damage and that they must demand compensation,” he says.
“The problem is not simply that elephants are entering fields or that people are living on the chars,” Saha says. The chars shift with the river, residents adapt, and elephants respond to food availability and movement routes. Forest fragmentation, agricultural expansion and people’s dependence on these landscapes are interconnected.
Understanding coexistence, therefore, means looking beyond compensation to make sense of the relationships and changing landscapes that shape life on the chars.
“The charland belongs to Teesta. Nobody holds a grudge or has complaints against anyone else. We farm side by side, there are no conflicts. If Teesta erodes one spot, a new sandbar pops up elsewhere, so we go and claim a patch there,” Muhammed says.
Sumi Roy, 41, says residents have learnt to adapt to the Teesta’s changing moods. While many youngsters study in nearby towns, they return during the farming season to help their elders. Marriages and childbirth are celebrated on the char, with pregnant women taken to town hospitals in advance. “Isn’t God above us to look after us? Why would God let a human being die?” she asks.
Sumi also takes pride in the community’s solidarity. Recalling how a Muslim neighbour whose house was washed away stayed with her Hindu family until a new one was built for him, she says: “We don’t have any negative feelings towards each other. No jealousy, malice, quarrels, fights, brawls… everyone stands by each other. That is how it should be!”
This article was first published on Mongabay.

title: Special Parliament sitting proposed from Nov 30 amid talk of women's quota bill
description: The government has proposed special sittings of Parliament from November 30 for essential business, amid indications that the women's reservation bill may be reintroduced.
author: Onmanorama Staff
content:
Special Parliament sitting proposed from Nov 30 amid talk of women's quota bill
Mail This Article
The Government has proposed a special sitting of Parliament from November 30 to transact "essential" business, amid indications that the delimitation-linked women's reservation bill may be reintroduced.
"The Government has requested Hon'ble Speaker, Lok Sabha and Hon'ble Chairman, Rajya Sabha to reconvene Lok Sabha on Monday, 30th November, 2026 and Rajya Sabha on Wednesday, 2nd December, 2026 respectively to transact essential Government Business," Union Parliamentary Affairs Minister Kiren Rijiju said on Thursday.
Subject to the exigencies of business, the sittings of both Houses may conclude on December 3, 2026, Rijiju said in a post on X.
The development comes on a day Prime Minister Narendra Modi asserted that no force could stop the delivery of justice to women and blamed "one opposition party" for the defeat of the delimitation-linked Constitution amendment bill, which sought to provide 33 per cent reservation for women in legislative bodies.
In a signed article published in major newspapers on Thursday, Modi said, "The journey of our Constitution would be incomplete without recognising the remarkable women who helped shape it. But what happened earlier this year should fill our hearts with shame."
The Prime Minister said the legislation aimed at ensuring adequate representation for women in legislative bodies had been prevented from being passed by one opposition party, demonstrating its "disdain for constitutional values".
"I assure the 'Nari Shakti' of India that no force can prevent us from ensuring that justice is done to them," he said.

title: Parliament to reconvene from November 30 amid buzz over Delimitation, Women's Quota Bills
description: : Parliament will reconvene from November 30 amid speculation over the Modi government's delimitation plan, women's reservation Bill and efforts to secure a two-thirds majority.
author: DNA Web Team
content:
INDIA
: Parliament will reconvene from November 30 amid speculation over the Modi government's delimitation plan, women's reservation Bill and efforts to secure a two-thirds majority.
Parliament is set to reconvene next week, with the Lok Sabha scheduled to meet on November 30 and the Rajya Sabha on December 2, amid speculation that the Narendra Modi government may revive its proposed delimitation and women's reservation legislation.
Union Parliamentary Affairs Minister Kiren Rijiju said on Thursday that the government had requested the respective presiding officers to reconvene both Houses to transact "essential Government Business". The sittings may conclude on December 3, although the government has not officially specified the legislative agenda.
The development comes months after the government's attempt to push through constitutional amendments related to delimitation and women's reservation suffered a setback in the Lok Sabha in April.
The Monsoon Session was adjourned on August 13 without being formally prorogued. By November 30, the gap between sittings will have stretched to 108 days, surpassing the previous record of 87 days set in 2008.
The government is believed to be working towards securing the numbers required to revive its delimitation agenda after failing to secure a two-thirds majority for the constitutional amendment Bill in April.
Of the 528 members who voted on April 17, 298 supported the Bill while 230 opposed it. The legislation required 352 votes to pass.
The government's proposed legislation seeks to redraw parliamentary constituencies and increase the Lok Sabha's strength from the existing 543 seats to a maximum of 850.
The exercise is linked to the implementation of the 33 per cent reservation for women in the Lok Sabha and state assemblies, provided for under the Nari Shakti Vandan Adhiniyam, 2023.
The April legislation sought to allow delimitation without waiting for the completion of a fresh Census. It also proposed reserving approximately one-third of the expanded Lok Sabha seats for women.
However, the proposal triggered concerns, particularly among southern states, over a possible change in their representation in Parliament.
The government has indicated that it is considering a uniform 50 per cent increase in seats across states to maintain the existing balance. However, this assurance was not included in the original Bill's text.
The Congress-led Opposition has argued that women's reservation should be implemented without linking it to delimitation.
The Opposition has put forward four conditions: retaining the Lok Sabha's existing strength of 543 seats, maintaining the current number of seats allocated to each state, reserving 182 seats for women under the existing arrangement and freezing the proposed arrangement for 25 years through a constitutional amendment.
The Opposition has accused the government of using women's reservation as a justification to redraw electoral boundaries to its political advantage.
The government is believed to be exploring support beyond the NDA to secure the two-thirds majority required for constitutional amendments.
The NDA is estimated to have around 319 members, while support from the NCP (Sharadchandra Pawar) could take the tally to 327. The DMK's 22 MPs could potentially take the figure to 350, still short of the required numbers.
With the 2029 Lok Sabha elections approaching, the government faces a time constraint. Any delay in passing the legislation could complicate the implementation of delimitation and women's reservation before the next general election.

title: UP Election 2027: 25 lakh jobs, Rs 5,000 allowance for graduates; Akhilesh Yadav's key promises
description: Akhilesh Yadav unveils Samajwadi Party's 2027 UP election manifesto, promising 25 lakh government jobs, Rs 5,000 monthly allowance for unemployed graduates, free education and Rs 40,000 annual aid for women.
author: DNA Web Team
content:
INDIA
Akhilesh Yadav unveils Samajwadi Party's 2027 UP election manifesto, promising 25 lakh government jobs, Rs 5,000 monthly allowance for unemployed graduates, free education and Rs 40,000 annual aid for women.
The Samajwadi Party (SP), led by Akhilesh Yadav, has unveiled its manifesto for the 2027 Uttar Pradesh Assembly elections, placing employment, education, women's welfare and social justice at the centre of its proposed governance agenda. Released on Constitution Day in Lucknow on November 26, the document outlines a series of promises aimed at young people, women, farmers and marginalised communities.
Titled 'Jan-Man Ka Manifesto' and 'Sattais Ka Sankalp: PDA Ka Pran-Patra', the manifesto reflects the party's PDA (Pichhda, Dalit, Alpsankhyak) framework, representing backward classes, Dalits and minorities.
Employment is a central theme of the SP manifesto. Akhilesh Yadav has promised 25 lakh government jobs if the party comes to power in Uttar Pradesh. The party has also proposed a monthly unemployment allowance of Rs 5,000 for graduates who remain without jobs. The announcement seeks to address concerns around unemployment and economic opportunities among educated young people.
Yadav also referred to the aspirations of Gen Z and Gen Alpha, saying the party would focus on opportunities linked to artificial intelligence and digital platforms.
The manifesto promises free schooling and the reopening of primary schools that have been shut down. It also proposes permanent employment and better salaries for Shiksha Mitras, who currently work as contractual teachers in the state's education system.
The party has highlighted its earlier initiatives in the technology and education sectors, including the establishment of an IT City in Lucknow during its 2012-2017 tenure.
Women's welfare is another major component of the manifesto. Among the key proposals is annual financial assistance of Rs 40,000 for women.
The party is also preparing a separate manifesto for women, referred to as 'Aadhi Aabadi', which will focus on their welfare, security and economic empowerment.
The SP has promised free healthcare services and ambulance facilities, along with the restoration of the Old Pension Scheme (OPS).
Other proposals include AI-powered technology for policing, stronger measures for women's safety and faster delivery of justice through fast-track courts.
The party has also proposed developing new villages equipped with Wi-Fi connectivity, streetlights, electricity and paved roads.
The manifesto places the PDA alliance at the centre of the party's political and social justice agenda. Yadav said the framework would include anyone facing oppression or marginalisation.
The party is also preparing separate manifestos for districts and cities to address local development priorities.
By releasing its manifesto months ahead of the 2027 elections, the SP is seeking to present a broader policy roadmap covering employment, welfare, education and infrastructure. The party's promises will now form part of the political debate as Uttar Pradesh prepares for its next Assembly election.

title: Sharad Pawar hospitalised again in Mumbai, daughter Supriya Sule says suspected dehydration
description: NCP (SP) chief Sharad Pawar has been admitted to Mumbai's Breach Candy Hospital with suspected dehydration. Daughter Supriya Sule urges him to reduce travel.
author: DNA Web Team
content:
INDIA
NCP (SP) chief Sharad Pawar has been admitted to Mumbai's Breach Candy Hospital with suspected dehydration. Daughter Supriya Sule urges him to reduce travel.
Nationalist Congress Party (Sharadchandra Pawar) chief Sharad Pawar was admitted to Mumbai's Breach Candy Hospital on Thursday after reportedly suffering from dehydration, his daughter and party working president Supriya Sule confirmed.
In a post on X, Sule shared the health update and said the 85-year-old veteran politician needed to reduce his travel and slow down his hectic schedule.
"We are admitting Baba (Sharad Pawar) to Breach Candy Hospital. It appears to be dehydration. He needs to slow down and travel less, but Baba just doesn't listen. He loves his work far too much," Sule wrote.
She also thanked people for their concern and good wishes following news of her father's hospitalisation.
The latest admission comes weeks after Pawar underwent medical treatment at hospitals in Pune and Mumbai following complaints of cough and chest pain.
Earlier on November 2, Pawar was admitted to Pune's Ruby Hall Clinic after experiencing a bout of cough and pleuritic chest pain, a condition that can cause discomfort while breathing.
His daughter had then confirmed that he was undergoing medical investigations and that his health parameters were stable.
After receiving treatment in Pune, the NCP (SP) chief was admitted to Mumbai's Breach Candy Hospital on November 4 for further medical examinations. He was subsequently treated for a chest and respiratory infection.
During his earlier hospital stay, several political leaders visited the veteran politician to enquire about his health.
Shiv Sena (UBT) MP Sanjay Raut was among those who met Pawar at Breach Candy Hospital. Raut later shared an update on social media, describing his condition as stable and improving. He also presented Pawar with a copy of his recently published book, *Bodh Kirtan*.
NCP leader Praful Patel also visited the hospital and enquired about Pawar's health.
Sule's latest message has once again drawn attention to the demanding schedule of the senior politician. In her post, she indicated that Pawar's frequent work-related engagements and travel needed to be reduced.
The NCP (SP) chief, a former Maharashtra Chief Minister and Union minister, has remained actively involved in political and public engagements despite his recent medical concerns.
According to reports, Pawar has been admitted to Breach Candy Hospital for treatment and observation. His daughter has attributed the latest hospitalisation to suspected dehydration.
Further details regarding his treatment and discharge are awaited.

title: जिसके खिलाफ राहुल गांधी कर रहे सड़कों पर संग्राम, उसी के साथ फोटो खिंचाते दिखे पार्टी के वरिष्ठ नेता
description: अजय सिंह राहुल कांग्रेस के वरिष्ठ नेता हैं और मध्य प्रदेश के भूतपूर्व मुख्यमंत्री अर्जुन सिंह के बेटे हैं। वह राज्य के सबसे प्रभावशाली राजनीतिक परिवार से आते हैं। वे सीधी जिले के चुरहट से आते हैं, जो उनके परिवार का पारंपरिक गढ़ रहा है।
author: Pramod Praveen
content:
जिसके खिलाफ राहुल गांधी कर रहे सड़कों पर संग्राम, उसी के साथ फोटो खिंचाते दिखे पार्टी के वरिष्ठ नेता
अजय सिंह राहुल कांग्रेस के वरिष्ठ नेता हैं और मध्य प्रदेश के भूतपूर्व मुख्यमंत्री अर्जुन सिंह के बेटे हैं। वह राज्य के सबसे प्रभावशाली राजनीतिक परिवार से आते हैं। वे सीधी जिले के चुरहट से आते हैं, जो उनके परिवार का पारंपरिक गढ़ रहा है।
देश की मुख्य विपक्षी पार्टी कांग्रेस पिछले कुछ महीनों से SIR और मुख्य चुनाव आयुक्त (CEC) ज्ञानेश कुमार के खिलाफ सदन से लेकर सड़क तक संग्राम करती रही है, उसी ज्ञानेश कुमार के खिलाफ पार्टी के एक वरिष्ठ नेता फोटो खिंचवाते दिखे। अब उनका यह फोटो शूट सोशल मीडिया पर वायरल हो रहा है और कांग्रेस नेता की खिल्ली उड़ रही है। दरअसल, मध्य प्रदेश कांग्रेस के वरिष्ठ नेता अजय सिंह की CEC ज्ञानेश कुमार के साथ एक तस्वीर सामने आई है। ये तस्वीर भोपाल में एक निजी शादी समारोह की है।
बता दें कि कांग्रेस पार्टी ने बार-बार ज्ञानेश कुमार पर मतदाता सूची में हेरफेर करने और वोट चोरी करने आरोप लगाए हैं और चुनाव आयोग की मर्यादा को तार-तार करने के आरोप लगाए हैं। पार्टी नेता राहुल गांधी भी कई प्रेस कॉन्फ्रेन्स कर चुके हैं और वोट चोरी के मुद्दे पर राजधानी दिल्ली में आंदोलन कर चुके हैं। यहां तक कि सुप्रीम कोर्ट का दरवाजा भी खटखटा चुके हैं। एक दिन पहले ही सभी राज्यों की राजधानियों में भी कांग्रेस नेताओं ने SIR में कथित अनियमितता के खिलाफ और ज्ञानेश कुमार के इस्तीफे की मांग को लेकर अपना अभियान चलाया है।
कहां हुई मुलाकात?
बड़ी बात यह है कि अजय सिंह ने शादी समारोह की ये तस्वीर अपने सोशल मीडिया अकाउंट पर पोस्ट की थी, जिसमें वह ज्ञानेश कुमार और राज्य विधानसभा अध्यक्ष नरेंद्र सिंह तोमर के साथ नजर आ रहे हैं। दरअसल, यह मुलाकात वरिष्ठ पुलिस अधिकारी उपेंद्र जैन के बेटे की शादी के रिसेप्शन में हुई। अजय सिंह ने इंडियन एक्सप्रेस को बताया कि वे उपेंद्र जैन को करीब 40 वर्षों से जानते हैं और वे वहां एक मेहमान के तौर पर शामिल हुए थे। उन्हें पहले से इस बात की जानकारी नहीं थी कि वहां ज्ञानेश कुमार भी मौजूद होंगे। उपेंद्र जैन, ज्ञानेश कुमार के भतीजे हैं। अजय सिंह ने कहा कि ज्ञानेश कुमार से उनकी मुलाकात महज एक संयोग थी।
उनसे कोई बातचीत नहीं
अजय सिंह ने कहा, "मैं कार्यक्रम स्थल, 'पुलिस ऑफिसर्स मेस' में पहुंचा। वहां विधानसभा अध्यक्ष नरेंद्र सिंह तोमर जी खड़े थे। उपेंद्र जैन और उनकी पत्नी भी वहीं मौजूद थे, और उनके साथ कोई और भी था। उन्होंने मुझसे किसी का परिचय नहीं कराया। हम जाकर सोफे पर बैठ गए, क्योंकि दूल्हा-दुल्हन अभी तक मंच (डाइस) पर नहीं पहुंचे थे।" जब उनसे पूछा गया कि क्या उन्होंने ज्ञानेश कुमार से कोई बातचीत की, तो उन्होंने इससे इनकार किया। उन्होंने कहा, “अगर उस तस्वीर को देखकर यह चर्चा हो रही है कि हमारी ज्ञानेश कुमार से कोई बातचीत हुई है, तो मुझे यह स्पष्ट तौर पर रहना है कि उनसे हमारी कोई बातचीत नहीं हुई।”
कौन हैं अजय सिंह?
अजय सिंह राहुल कांग्रेस के वरिष्ठ नेता हैं और मध्य प्रदेश के भूतपूर्व मुख्यमंत्री अर्जुन सिंह के बेटे हैं। वह राज्य के सबसे प्रभावशाली राजनीतिक परिवार से आते हैं। वे सीधी जिले के चुरहट से आते हैं, जो उनके परिवार का पारंपरिक गढ़ रहा है। वह चुरहट विधानसभा सीट से सातवीं बार विधायक चुने गए हैं। वह मध्य प्रदेश विधानसभा में नेता प्रतिपक्ष भी रह चुके हैं।
होटल से एयरपोर्ट तक खाली हाथ भटके कार्यकर्ता
कांग्रेस नेताओं को जब बुधवार दोपहर लगभग 4 बजे CEC ज्ञानेश कुमार के भोपाल में होने की जानकारी मिली तो यूथ कांग्रेस और एनएसयूआई (NSUI) के कार्यकर्ता पुतला लेकर उस होटल की ओर दौड़े जहां उनके ठहरने की खबर थी। हालांकि, कार्यकर्ताओं के पहुंचने से पहले ही सीईसी एयरपोर्ट के लिए रवाना हो चुके थे। इसके बाद कार्यकर्ता एयरपोर्ट भी पहुंचे, लेकिन तब तक उनकी फ्लाइट उड़ान भर चुकी थी। यह प्रदर्शन आखिरकार प्रदेश कांग्रेस कमेटी (PCC) कार्यालय के बाहर सीईसी का पुतला फूंक कर समाप्त हुआ। इस दौरान प्रदेश कांग्रेस अध्यक्ष जीतू पटवारी भी प्रदर्शन से नदारद रहे। कांग्रेस प्रवक्ता मुकेश नायक ने स्वीकार किया कि पार्टी को सीईसी के आगमन की पूर्व सूचना नहीं थी। उन्होंने कहा कि यदि जानकारी पहले मिलती, तो हजारों कार्यकर्ता उन्हें भोपाल में प्रवेश नहीं करने देते।

title: 2030 तक बाल विवाह मुक्त भारत का संकल्प, दिल्ली में केंद्रीय मंत्री सावित्री ठाकुर के नेतृत्व में निकला मशाल जुलूस
description: जस्ट राइट्स फॉर चिल्ड्रेन (JRC) के संस्थापक भुवन ऋभु ने कहा कि 27 नवंबर को संयुक्त राष्ट्र द्वारा 'बाल, कम उम्र और जबरन विवाह के उन्मूलन के लिए अंतरराष्ट्रीय दिवस' घोषित किया जाना इस दिशा में एक ऐतिहासिक निर्णायक मोड़ है।
author: Shubham Sharma
content:
2030 तक बाल विवाह मुक्त भारत का संकल्प, दिल्ली में केंद्रीय मंत्री सावित्री ठाकुर के नेतृत्व में निकला मशाल जुलूस
जस्ट राइट्स फॉर चिल्ड्रेन (JRC) के संस्थापक भुवन ऋभु ने कहा कि 27 नवंबर को संयुक्त राष्ट्र द्वारा 'बाल, कम उम्र और जबरन विवाह के उन्मूलन के लिए अंतरराष्ट्रीय दिवस' घोषित किया जाना इस दिशा में एक ऐतिहासिक निर्णायक मोड़ है।
संविधान दिवस और 'बाल, कम उम्र एवं जबरन विवाह के उन्मूलन के लिए पहले अंतरराष्ट्रीय दिवस' की पूर्व संध्या पर केंद्रीय महिला एवं बाल विकास राज्य मंत्री सावित्री ठाकुर ने दिल्ली के कुसुमपुर पहाड़ी इलाके में एक जागरूकता मशाल जुलूस का नेतृत्व किया। बाल अधिकारों के संरक्षण के लिए काम करने वाले नागरिक समाज संगठनों के नेटवर्क जस्ट राइट्स फॉर चिल्ड्रेन (JRC) की ओर से आयोजित इस मार्च में लगभग 2,000 महिलाओं, बच्चों, बाल विवाह से बचाई गई बेटियों और स्थानीय निवासियों ने हिस्सा लिया।
कार्यक्रम के दौरान प्रतिभागियों ने दीप जलाकर बाल विवाह के खिलाफ अपनी प्रतिबद्धता जताई और साल 2030 तक भारत को बाल विवाह मुक्त बनाने का संकल्प लिया। केंद्रीय मंत्री सावित्री ठाकुर ने सभी को शपथ दिलाई कि वे न तो किसी बाल विवाह में शामिल होंगे, न ही इसे बढ़ावा देंगे और कहीं भी ऐसी सूचना मिलने पर तत्काल संबंधित अधिकारियों को सूचित करेंगे। इस अवसर पर JRC के संस्थापक भुवन ऋभु सहित कई नागरिक समाज संगठनों के प्रतिनिधि मौजूद रहे।
'बाल विवाह मुक्त भारत' अभियान के सकारात्मक परिणाम: सावित्री ठाकुर
इस मौके पर केंद्रीय राज्य मंत्री सावित्री ठाकुर ने कहा कि प्रधानमंत्री नरेंद्र मोदी के नेतृत्व में वर्ष 2024 में शुरू किए गए 'बाल विवाह मुक्त भारत' अभियान के सार्थक परिणाम सामने आ रहे हैं। उन्होंने सरकारी आंकड़ों और प्रयासों का विवरण देते हुए बताया:
बाल विवाह की दर में गिरावट: राष्ट्रीय परिवार स्वास्थ्य सर्वेक्षण (NFHS) के अनुसार, देश में बाल विवाह की दर 2005-06 में 47.4 प्रतिशत थी, जो 2023-24 में घटकर 20.1 प्रतिशत रह गई है।
जनजागरूकता और प्रशासनिक ढांचा: साल 2024 से अब तक सरकार 6.86 लाख से ज्यादा जागरूकता कार्यक्रम आयोजित कर चुकी है, जिनसे 12.5 करोड़ लोगों तक पहुंच बनी है। इसके अलावा, 'बाल विवाह मुक्त भारत' पोर्टल पर 72 हजार से अधिक बाल विवाह निषेध अधिकारियों का विवरण दर्ज है, जिनमें लगभग 60 हजार अधिकारी ग्राम पंचायत स्तर पर नियुक्त किए गए हैं।
कल्याणकारी योजनाओं का योगदान: केंद्रीय मंत्री ने कहा कि 'बेटी बचाओ, बेटी पढ़ाओ' (2015), मिशन वात्सल्य, मिशन शक्ति, सुकन्या समृद्धि योजना और समग्र शिक्षा जैसी पहलें बेटियों के बचपन को सुरक्षित बनाने में महत्वपूर्ण भूमिका निभा रही हैं। इस मुहिम को घर-घर पहुंचाने में नागरिक समाज संगठनों और जमीनी कार्यकर्ताओं की भूमिका बेहद अहम है।
27 नवंबर को 'अंतरराष्ट्रीय दिवस' की मान्यता ऐतिहासिक मोड़: भुवन ऋभु
जस्ट राइट्स फॉर चिल्ड्रेन (JRC) के संस्थापक भुवन ऋभु ने कहा कि 27 नवंबर को संयुक्त राष्ट्र द्वारा 'बाल, कम उम्र और जबरन विवाह के उन्मूलन के लिए अंतरराष्ट्रीय दिवस' घोषित किया जाना इस दिशा में एक ऐतिहासिक निर्णायक मोड़ है। उन्होंने कहा कि भारत ने 2026 तक बाल विवाह की दर में 10 प्रतिशत की कमी लाकर यह साबित किया है कि राजनीतिक इच्छाशक्ति, कानून के प्रभावी क्रियान्वयन और सामूहिक सामाजिक चेतना से बड़ा बदलाव संभव है। उन्होंने बाल विवाह को बच्चों के साथ होने वाला अपराध बताते हुए इसके पूर्ण उन्मूलन के लिए वैश्विक स्तर पर ठोस कार्रवाई का आह्वान किया।
कैसे हुई 27 नवंबर की वैश्विक घोषणा?
उल्लेखनीय है कि भुवन ऋभु ने बाल विवाह के उन्मूलन के लिए एक समर्पित अंतरराष्ट्रीय दिवस घोषित करने की वैश्विक पहल की शुरुआत की थी। मार्च 2026 में संयुक्त राष्ट्र में अपने संबोधन के दौरान उन्होंने अंतरराष्ट्रीय नेताओं के समक्ष यह मांग दोहराई थी, जिसके बाद भारत सहित 84 देशों ने इस प्रस्ताव का समर्थन किया। परिणामस्वरूप, 4 सितंबर 2026 को संयुक्त राष्ट्र महासभा ने सर्वसम्मति से प्रस्ताव पारित कर 27 नवंबर को 'बाल, कम उम्र और जबरन विवाह के उन्मूलन के लिए अंतरराष्ट्रीय दिवस' घोषित किया।
इस जागरूकता कार्यक्रम में एसोसिएशन फॉर वॉलंटरी एक्शन (AVA), इंडिया चाइल्ड प्रोटेक्शन (ICP), बाल विकास धारा, प्रयास जेएसी, कोसी लोक मंच, बेसिक फाउंडेशन और सहयोग केयर फॉर यू जैसे सहयोगी संगठनों ने भी सक्रिय भागीदारी निभाई।

title: ममता बनर्जी के भाई ने भतीजे अभिषेक के खिलाफ पुलिस में शिकायत दी, FIR दर्ज करने की मांग
description: कालीघाट पुलिस थाने पहुंचने के बाद उन्होंने संवाददाताओं को बताया कि तृणमूल के शासन के दौरान कई घटनाएं हुईं। यह सिलसिला 2024 से जारी है और आज भी बरकरार है।
author: Madan Tiwari
content:
ममता बनर्जी के भाई ने भतीजे अभिषेक के खिलाफ पुलिस में शिकायत दी, FIR दर्ज करने की मांग
कालीघाट पुलिस थाने पहुंचने के बाद उन्होंने संवाददाताओं को बताया कि तृणमूल के शासन के दौरान कई घटनाएं हुईं। यह सिलसिला 2024 से जारी है और आज भी बरकरार है।
पश्चिम बंगाल की पूर्व मुख्यमंत्री ममता बनर्जी के छोटे भाई स्वपन बनर्जी ने गुरुवार को पुलिस से संपर्क कर अपने भतीजे और ममता ऑल इंडिया तृणमूल कांग्रेस के राष्ट्रीय महासचिव अभिषेक बनर्जी के खिलाफ प्राथमिकी दर्ज (FIR) करने की मांग की। उन्होंने अभिषेक पर रक्तदान शिविर में बाधा डालने और धमकाने का आरोप लगाया। बाबुन के उपनाम से जाने जाने वाले स्वप्न बनर्जी ने दावा किया कि राज्य में तृणमूल के 15 साल के शासन के दौरान धमकाने और डराने की संस्कृति जड़ें जमा चुकी थी, जो इस साल मई में भाजपा के सत्ता में आने के बाद भी जारी रही। उन्होंने कहा कि वह 2024 से ऐसी घटनाओं के गवाह रहे हैं।
कालीघाट पुलिस थाने पहुंचने के बाद उन्होंने संवाददाताओं को बताया, "तृणमूल के शासन के दौरान कई घटनाएं हुईं। यह सिलसिला 2024 से जारी है और आज भी बरकरार है। सरकारी कामकाज में बाधा डालने, क्लबों पर जबरन कब्जा करने और धमकाने की घटनाएं हुई हैं। मैं कितना कुछ बताऊं? मैंने बहुत कुछ सहन किया है।" इन आरोपों पर अभिषेक बनर्जी की ओर से तत्काल कोई प्रतिक्रिया नहीं आई।
पुलिस में शिकायत की तात्कालिक वजह कथित तौर पर रक्तदान शिविर में बाधा डालने की घटना थी। हालांकि, घटना का विस्तृत ब्योरा और ममता तृणमूल के राष्ट्रीय महासचिव के खिलाफ लगाए गए विशिष्ट आरोपों की जानकारी तत्काल उपलब्ध नहीं हो सकी। इस ताजा घटनाक्रम से बाबुन और ममता बनर्जी के बीच लंबे समय से चले आ रहे मनमुटाव में एक नया मोड़ आ गया है। ममता बनर्जी ने एक समय सार्वजनिक रूप से अपने छोटे भाई से दूरी बना ली थी और यहां तक कहा था कि उन्होंने उनसे सभी संबंध तोड़ लिए हैं।
पश्चिम बंगाल विधानसभा चुनाव में भाजपा की जीत के बाद परिवार के भीतर का यह विवाद राजनीतिक रंग ले चुका है। भाजपा की जीत के साथ ही राज्य में तृणमूल का लगातार 15 साल से चला आ रहा शासन समाप्त हो गया। सत्ता परिवर्तन के बाद से बाबुन की भाजपा नेतृत्व के साथ नजदीकी नजर आ रही है। वह लगातार मुख्यमंत्री शुभेंदु अधिकारी की प्रशंसा भी करते रहे हैं।
हाल ही में उन्होंने अपने इलाके में आयोजित सामुदायिक दुर्गा पूजा के उद्घाटन के लिए शुभेंदु को आमंत्रित किया था। इस कार्यक्रम में वह सम्मान स्वरूप मुख्यमंत्री के पैर छूते हुए भी नजर आए थे। शुभेंदु के प्रति उनकी बार-बार सार्वजनिक रूप से प्रशंसा की अभिव्यक्तियों ने उनके राजनीतिक झुकाव और भाजपा की ओर संभावित रुख करने को लेकर अटकलों को हवा दी है। बाबुन ने हालांकि भाजपा में शामिल होने के किसी औपचारिक फैसले की सार्वजनिक रूप से घोषणा नहीं की है।

title: Rewa Crime: 74 की उम्र में बुजुर्ग देख रहा था शादी के सपने, लड़की ने खाली कर दिया अकाउंट
description: Matrimonial Site Marriage Scam: मेट्रिमोनियल एप पर बुजुर्ग ने बनाई प्रोफाइल, फोन कर युवती ने फंसाया, इलाज के बहाने ठगे 12.11 लाख रुपए।
author: Shailendra Sharma
content:
matrimonial site marriage scam elderly man 12 lakh fraud, एआई से बनाई गई प्रतीकात्मक तस्वीर (Source-Gemini)
Rewa Matrimonial Site Marriage Scam: मध्यप्रदेश के रीवा में मेट्रिमोनियल एप पर अपनी प्रोफाइल बनाना एक बुजुर्ग को महंगा पड़ गया। एप पर एक युवती ने उनकी प्रोफाइल देखी और फिर शादी के बहाने युवती ने उन्हें अपनी बातों के जाल में फंसा लिया। युवती ने पहले तो बुजुर्ग से मोबाइल पर मीठी-मीठी बातें की और फिर चोट लगने की झूठी सूचना देकर इलाज के नाम पर धीरे-धीरे 12.11 लाख रुपये ले लिए। करीब सात माह तक रुपए ऐंठने का सिलसिला चलता रहा। बाद में लड़की का मोबाइल बंद हो गया।
शादी का सपना पड़ा महंगा
74 वर्षीय बुजुर्ग ने मेट्रिमोनियल एप पर नवंबर 2025 में अपनी प्रोफाइल बनाई थी। कुछ दिन बाद ही उनको एक लड़की ने फोन कर अपनी पहचान सरस्वती उपाध्याय निवासी उज्जैन के रूप में दी। उसने शादी करने की इच्छा जाहिर की। लड़की लगातार उनसे मोबाइल पर बात करती रही। कुछ दिन बाद ही एक व्यक्ति ने फोन कर उनको सरस्वती के गिरने और सिर में चोट लगने की जानकारी दी। इसके बाद आरोपी ने दोबारा फोन कर इलाज के लिए रुपए मांगे। पीड़ित ने दिसंबर माह से लेकर सितंबर 2026 तक इलाज के लिए अलग-अलग किस्तों में 12.11 लाख रुपए दे दिए।
12.11 लाख रुपये ऐंठने के बाद शातिर लड़की व उसके साथी ने फोन करना बंद कर दिए और सारे नंबर बंद कर लिए। फोन नंबर बंद होने पर बुजुर्ग को अपने साथ हुए फ्रॉड की जानकारी हुई तो उन्होंने साइबर हेल्पलाइन नंबर में शिकायत दर्ज कराई। शून्य में मामला दर्ज होकर थाने पहुंचा है। पुलिस अब साइबर सेल की मदद से उन खातों की जानकारी मंगा रही है जिसमें उनसे रुपए जमा करवाए गए थे। थाना प्रभारी हितेन्द्रनाथ शर्मा ने बताया कि शून्य में एफआईआर थाने आई है जिस पर मामला दर्ज कर जांच की जा रही है।

title: Rajasthan: चलती ट्रेन में आर्मी जवान की हत्या मामला, आरोपी जुबेर मेमन की जमानत याचिका खारिज
description: चलती ट्रेन में सेना के जवान की हत्या के मामले में आरोपी जुबेर मेमन को दूसरी बार भी अदालत से राहत नहीं मिली। बचाव पक्ष ने बीमारी और परिवार की जिम्मेदारी का हवाला देकर जमानत मांगी थी, लेकिन अदालत ने अपराध की गंभीरता और महत्वपूर्ण गवाहों की गवाही बाकी होने को आधार बनाकर याचिका खारिज कर दी।
author: Kamal Mishra
content:
Bikaner Train Murder Case (photo-rail info)
बीकानेर। चलती ट्रेन में सेना के जवान जिगर कुमार की चाकू मारकर हत्या के मामले में आरोपी जुबेर मेमन को एक बार फिर अदालत से राहत नहीं मिली है। अपर सेशन न्यायाधीश मधु हिसारिया ने आरोपी की दूसरी जमानत याचिका भी खारिज कर दी। अदालत ने अपराध की गंभीरता, मामले की परिस्थितियों और अभियोजन पक्ष के महत्वपूर्ण गवाहों के बयान अभी बाकी होने को जमानत नहीं देने का आधार माना। इस फैसले के बाद आरोपी को फिलहाल जेल में ही रहना होगा।
यह मामला नवंबर 2025 में चलती ट्रेन में हुई उस वारदात से जुड़ा है, जिसने रेलवे और पुलिस महकमे में हड़कंप मचा दिया था। सेना का जवान जिगर कुमार छुट्टियां बिताने के लिए अपने गांव जा रहा था। इसी दौरान ट्रेन में विवाद के बाद उसकी हत्या कर दी गई थी।
प्रकरण के अनुसार, 3 नवंबर 2025 को देवकिशन पुत्र मघराज सारण ने जीआरपी थाने में रिपोर्ट दर्ज करवाई थी। रिपोर्ट के मुताबिक, 2 और 3 नवंबर की रात उनकी ड्यूटी ट्रेन संख्या 19224 में बठिंडा से बीकानेर तक थी। लूणकरनसर से ट्रेन रवाना होने के बाद पेंट्रीकार मैनेजर शिवकुमार ने एस-2 कोच में यात्री और अटेंडेंट के बीच झगड़ा होने की सूचना दी।
सूचना मिलने पर मौके पर पहुंचे तो एक यात्री लहूलुहान हालत में मिला। ट्रेन बीकानेर पहुंची तो घायल यात्री को चिकित्सकीय सहायता के लिए ले जाया गया, जहां चिकित्सक ने उसे मृत घोषित कर दिया। मृतक की पहचान सेना के जवान जिगर कुमार के रूप में हुई थी। प्रारंभिक जानकारी के अनुसार, ट्रेन में विवाद के दौरान जवान पर चाकू से हमला किया गया था। पुलिस ने मामले में भारतीय न्याय संहिता और आर्म्स एक्ट के तहत जांच पूरी कर आरोप पत्र पेश किया।
आरोपी जुबेर मेमन की ओर से अधिवक्ता रविकांत वर्मा ने जमानत के पक्ष में दलीलें पेश कीं। बचाव पक्ष ने कहा कि आरोपी 3 नवंबर 2025 से जेल में बंद है। मृतक के साथ उसकी कोई पुरानी रंजिश नहीं थी और दोनों अलग-अलग कोच में थे। यह भी दलील दी गई कि आरोपी के हाथ में चाकू नहीं था। इसके अलावा आरोपी की बीमारी का हवाला देते हुए बताया गया कि उसके पेट में गांठ है और वह मधुमेह से भी पीड़ित है। परिवार का एकमात्र कमाऊ सदस्य होने के आधार पर भी जमानत देने की मांग की गई।
अपर लोक अभियोजक शिवशंकर स्वामी और परिवादी की ओर से अधिवक्ता केशव व्यास ने जमानत याचिका का विरोध किया। अभियोजन पक्ष ने मामले की गंभीरता और जांच से जुड़े तथ्यों को देखते हुए आरोपी को जमानत नहीं देने की मांग की। दोनों पक्षों की दलीलें सुनने के बाद अदालत ने पाया कि अभियोजन पक्ष के 14 गवाहों के बयान दर्ज हो चुके हैं, लेकिन अनुसंधान अधिकारी सहित कई महत्वपूर्ण गवाहों की गवाही अभी बाकी है।
न्यायालय ने माना कि मामले की परिस्थितियों में ऐसा कोई महत्वपूर्ण बदलाव नहीं हुआ है, जिसके आधार पर आरोपी को दूसरी बार जमानत दी जा सके। अपर सेशन न्यायाधीश मधु हिसारिया ने अपराध की गंभीरता और शेष गवाहों की गवाही को ध्यान में रखते हुए जुबेर मेमन की दूसरी जमानत याचिका खारिज कर दी।

title: रतलाम का कुंडाल-कोटेश्वर डैम प्रशासन की कार्रवाई से सुर्खियों
description: कलेक्टर के निर्देश पर प्रशासन, बिजली कंपनी और जल संसाधन विभाग की संयुक्त टीम ने की कार्रवाई, पेयजल के लिए आरक्षित पानी पर सेंधमारी, प्रतिबंध के बावजूद बांध के डूब क्षेत्र में चोरी-छिपे सिंचाई, 12 पंपों की जब्ती
author: Gourishankar singh Jodha
content:
कलेक्टर के निर्देश पर प्रशासन, बिजली कंपनी और जल संसाधन विभाग की संयुक्त टीम ने की कार्रवाई, पेयजल के लिए आरक्षित पानी पर सेंधमारी, प्रतिबंध के बावजूद बांध के डूब क्षेत्र में चोरी-छिपे सिंचाई, 12 पंपों की जब्ती
रतलाम। जिले का कुंडाल-कोटेश्वर डैम फिर एक बार गुरुवार को कलेक्टर अजय कटेसरिया के निर्देश पर की गई कार्रवाई के बाद सुर्खियों में आ गया हैं। यहां डूब क्षेत्र में प्रशासन, बिजली कंपनी और जल संसाधन विभाग की संयुक्त टीम ने सिंचाई पर प्रतिबंध के बावजूद मोटर-पंप लगाकर पानी खींचने वालों पर सख्त कार्रवाई की है।
कलेक्टर अजय कटेसरिया के निर्देश पर पहुंची संयुक्त टीम ने मौके से 12 मोटर-पंप जब्त किए। इनमें 7 सबमर्सिबल और 5 ओपनवेल पंप शामिल हैं। बांध में जल उपलब्धता कम होने के कारण प्रशासन ने सिंचाई पर प्रतिबंध लागू किया है, ताकि पेयजल के लिए उपलब्ध पानी का संरक्षण और उचित प्रबंधन किया जा सके। इसके बावजूद डूब क्षेत्र में मोटर-पंप के जरिए सिंचाई किए जाने की जानकारी मिलने पर प्रशासन ने तत्काल कार्रवाई की।
कार्रवाई में तीन विभागों की संयुक्त टीम
तहसीलदार रतलाम ग्रामीण मनीष जैन ने बताया कि प्रतिबंध का उल्लंघन करने की सूचना पर प्रशासन, मध्यप्रदेश विद्युत मंडल और जल संसाधन विभाग की संयुक्त टीम मौके पर पहुंची। जांच के दौरान सिंचाई में उपयोग किए जा रहे 12 मोटर-पंप जब्त किए गए। मौके पर पंचनामा तैयार कर नियमानुसार जब्ती की कार्रवाई की गई। कार्रवाई में तहसीलदार मनीष जैन, बिजली कंपनी के कर्मचारी और जल संसाधन विभाग के उपयंत्री शामिल रहे। प्रशासन ने जल संरक्षण के लिए लागू प्रतिबंध का पालन सुनिश्चित करने की दिशा में यह कार्रवाई की।
जिले के 7 गांवों के 1803 हेक्टेयर क्षेत्र में होगी सिंचाई
कलेक्टर अजय कटेसरिया की अध्यक्षता में उद्यानिकी एवं खाद्य प्रसंस्करण विभाग की पर मोर क्रॉप योजना अंतर्गत प्रेशराइज्ड इरिगेशन परियोजना के संबंध में बैठक कलेक्टर कार्यालय सभागार में आयोजित की गई। बैठक में परियोजना की प्रगति एवं किसानों को लाभान्वित करने की प्रक्रिया की समीक्षा की गई। इस दौरान सीईओ जिला पंचायत वैशाली जैन सहित उद्यानिकी एवं कृषि विभाग के अधिकारी तथा किसान उपस्थित थे।
कुंडाल डैम से पानी की चोरी पर तत्काल कार्रवाई के निर्देश
बैठक के दौरान किसानों द्वारा कुंडाल डैम से पानी चोरी किए जाने की शिकायत पर कलेक्टर कटेसरिया ने संबंधित अधिकारियों को सख्त निर्देश दिए कि डैम से पानी चोरी करने के लिए उपयोग की जा रही अवैध मोटरों को तत्काल जब्त करने की कार्रवाई करें। उन्होंने जल संसाधन विभाग को स्पष्ट निर्देश दिए कि कहीं भी पानी की चोरी नहीं हो, इसकी निगरानी करें तथा शिकायत प्राप्त होने पर तत्काल कार्रवाई सुनिश्चित करें।
7 गांवों के 1803 हेक्टेयर क्षेत्र को मिलेगा सिंचाई का लाभ
प्रेशराइज्ड इरिगेशन परियोजना अंतर्गत रतलाम विकासखंड के सात गांव पिपलोदी, पिपलोदीखेड़ा, रावदिया, उमरन, बावड़ीखेड़ा, पिपलखूंटा एवं बिरमावल के किसानों को सिंचाई सुविधा का लाभ मिलेगा। परियोजना से कुल 1803 हेक्टेयर सिंचाई क्षेत्र लाभान्वित होगा। परियोजना अंतर्गत 766 किसानों को लाभान्वित करने का लक्ष्य रखा गया है। अब तक 374 आवेदन प्राप्त हो चुके हैं, जिनमें से 146 कार्यादेश स्वीकृत किए जा चुके हैं।
ड्रिप एवं स्प्रिंकलर से होगी सिंचाई
प्रेशराइज्ड इरिगेशन परियोजना के अंतर्गत किसानों को ड्रिप, मिनी स्प्रिंकलर एवं पोर्टेबल स्प्रिंकलर उपलब्ध कराए जाएंगे। इससे किसानों को सिंचाई के लिए आधुनिक तकनीक का लाभ मिलेगा तथा जल उपयोग की दक्षता बढ़ाने में मदद मिलेगी।
