title: Ex-terrorist fugitive’s 19-year run ends in arrest
description: JAMMU: A joint police team arrested a former terrorist wanted in a string of criminal cases from Tral in Awantipora district on Thursday, ending his
author: Sanjay Khajuria
content:
Mohd Mansha, a resident of Thuroo Lassoli, was arrested by Jammu and Kashmir Police
JAMMU: A joint police team arrested a former terrorist wanted in a string of criminal cases from Tral in Awantipora district on Thursday, ending his nearly two-decade-long run from the law.The fugitive, Mohammad Mansha, is a native of Lassoli in Reasi district’s Thuroo tehsil. An active terrorist from 2000 to 2007, he was wanted in at least 13 criminal cases involving serious offences such as murder, attempted murder, criminal conspiracy, waging war against govt and Arms Act violations.
He laid down arms in 2007, but managed to escape the law enforcement radar, continuing to evade arrest for the next 19 years, police said.Among the many cases in his name, Mansha was involved in the killing of a J&K Police SPO in 2000. He was charged under relevant sections of the RPC and the Arms Act, and declared an absconder after the chargesheet was submitted. A district and sessions court issued an arrest warrant against him in 2001.The joint operation involved sustained efforts, meticulous planning, and development of credible intelligence, a police spokesperson said. A special team from Mahore PS (Reasi) and the district absconder tracking unit was deputed to Tral. The team traced and arrested Mansha with assistance of Awantipora Police.

title: Sheshnag Lake row: Karan Singh questions need for wider road, PDP steps up heat
description: SRINAGAR: The controversy over the presence of heavy machinery near the ecologically fragile Sheshnag Lake along the Amarnath Yatra route shows no signs
author: Naseer Ganai
content:
Mehbooba demanded that the agreement be made public and asked why people were not being allowed to travel from Pahalgam to Chandanwari and beyond.
SRINAGAR: The controversy over the presence of heavy machinery near the ecologically fragile Sheshnag Lake along the Amarnath Yatra route shows no signs of dying down, with former Sadr-i-Riyasat (head of state) of Jammu & Kashmir, Karan Singh, saying every pilgrimage route need not be turned into a multi-lane road for the convenience of tourists. Mehbooba Mufti-led PDP has also stepped up its campaign, demanding that govt allow a joint team of politicians and environmentalists to visit the lake and make the site accessible for an independent assessment.Joining the voices opposing the move, Karan Singh, in a social media post, said: “We do not have to make every pilgrim route into a motorable road just for the convenience of tourists. Genuine pilgrims will not mind walking or riding towards this great shrine.”Mehbooba demanded transparency in the matter, saying if no work was taking place near the lake, as assured by forest minister Altaf Kaloo, there was no reason to prevent people from visiting the site.“How did JCBs reach Sheshnag? Who authorised their movement, and what action has been taken against those responsible?” she asked at a press conference.
Mehbooba said chief minister Omar Abdullah had signed a memorandum of understanding with the Border Roads Organisation (BRO) in Jan, assigning it the work of constructing a track in the area.
She demanded that the agreement be made public and asked why people were not being allowed to travel from Pahalgam to Chandanwari and beyond.J&K government on Wednesday dismissed allegations of construction near the high-altitude lake, with Kaloo saying the JCB machinery was operating 200-300 feet away and at a higher elevation.As an online petition demanding an immediate halt to excavation and road-widening work near the lake crossed over 16,000 signatures Thursday, environmental activist Raja Muzaffar Bhat said he received a “distressing SOS” last night from a young nature lover, Zarqua Banday, who was allegedly being harassed for starting the petition. Bhat said cyber police had called her family.

title: India-Germany submarine partnership can act as a catalyst for Indo-Pacific security: German envoy
description: With the India-Germany Project-75 India (P-75I) conventional submarine deal in CCS for final approval, Germany has reiterated its commitment to delivering
author: Sachin Parashar
content:
Wieck said the project will see extensive transfer of technology in the underwater domain, not just limited to the submarines, as he highlighted overarching policy frameworks established by Berlin to guarantee reliability.
With the India-Germany Project-75 India (P-75I) conventional submarine deal in CCS for final approval, Germany has reiterated its commitment to delivering comprehensive technology transfer under the long-term industrial partnership with India. German ambassador to India Jasper Wieck told TOI in an interview mutual trust regarding protection of sensitive technologies will be key to this partnership.Pegged at $ 8-9 billion, the proposed P-75I deal involving Germany’s TKMS and India’s Mazagon Dock Shipbuilders Limited (MDL) to build 6 submarines equipped with the vital Air-Independent Propulsion (AIP) technology—which allows vessels to remain submerged for weeks without surfacing—will be one of the largest-ever defence contracts signed by India.Wieck said the project will see extensive transfer of technology in the underwater domain, not just limited to the submarines, as he highlighted overarching policy frameworks established by Berlin to guarantee reliability."Germany has committed to becoming a reliable defence-industrial partner of India. The bilateral defense industrial cooperation roadmap, which was signed in April this year, explicitly includes defense technology transfer," said Wieck.
Asked about compartmentalisation and protection of sensitive submarine technology transferred to India, Wieck said technologies related to P-75I will only be shared with related Indian companies and government bodies. "Now, ultimately sharing technology with partners is always a question of trust and reliability, but here I can confirm India and Germany are definitely trusted partners in both directions," Wieck said.Speaking alongside Wieck about the technical execution of the project, TKMS global CEO Oliver Burkhard said P-75I is built around the transfer of the design of the submarine which will belong to the Indian Navy."You can't run a submarine if you haven't understood it. A few core technologies are protected in every partnership but India will get full access to that what they need to run, maintain, sustain those boats over the next 40 years," said Burkhard.Addressing India's concerns regarding TKMS' historical submarine contracts with Turkey, Burkhard clarified that each international program is strictly isolated and governed by German sovereign oversight."India does not have to worry because every program is ring-fenced. The technology, data, and intellectual property stay in that country and is protected by agreements between the two governments. The design India will receive is a highly advanced, unique-to-India boat and that has nothing to do with Turkey anymore," Burkhard said.Ambassador Wieck highlighted how the submarine agreement fits into Germany’s broader Indo-Pacific strategy, considering particularly regional security challenges and efforts to maintain rules-based maritime order."India plays a central role in the Indo-Pacific and India and Germany have a shared interest in upholding and defending the rules-based international order. And in the Indo-Pacific, that means the freedom of navigation and the security of lifelines of communication across the oceans. P75I is a long-term engagement with the potential of becoming a catalyst for deepening security and safety in the Indian Ocean," noted Wieck.Asked if India's ties with Russia might limit Germany's willingness to transfer sensitive naval technology, Wieck stressed mutual respect for sovereign choices."Each and every country around the world has its own network of partners and friends across the globe...instead of dwelling on India's partnerships with other countries, I'd rather focus on broadening and deepening the Indo-German partnership. Mutual trust, also regarding the protection of sensitive defense technology, is of course the key to that partnership," said Wieck.According to Burkhard, the submarine partnership might offer an opportunity for turning India a hub for Southeast Asian nations or others who want to join the submarine programme. "Submarines of the future can be built for other nations with, for example, a German design on one side, and on the other Indian competencies when it comes to assembly and manufacturing. A number of countries are approaching us. We are the global leaders in conventional submarines...so, if you can offer, for example, a country which is interested and it goes along with the political interests of India and Germany also to be part of a submarine building programme...it can be steered from a new hub in Asia, which will then be India for us," he said.
On the need to adhere to strict delivery schedules, Burkhard emphasised TKMS’ delivery track record - citing four submarines and one frigate delivered this year - and noted that execution is a shared responsibility with MDL, with indigenous content reaching 70% on the final boat. While acknowledging past delays, he stressed confidence in meeting timelines, stating, "we are also in a delivery mode which shows hopefully some confidence that, of course, we will meet the timelines".Addressing concerns over integrating the AIP system into a new design for India’s P75I submarines, Burkhard called AIP a proven technology operated by the German Navy for over 20 years and across more than 50 submarines in service or under contract. He noted that India will own the design for P75I, making future modifications easier without having to depend on the foreign original equipment manufacturer.

title: Karnataka Industries Minister holds talks with four Japanese companies
description: Karnataka Industries Minister discusses expansion plans and operations with four Japanese firms, including Seiren, Enomoto, Secom/Toyota Tsusho, and Makino.
author: The Hindu Bureau
content:
Large and Medium Industries Minister M.B. Patil held discussions with four Japanese companies on Thursday, the fourth day of his visit to Japan, focusing on their existing operations in Karnataka and expansion plans.
According to a release, during a meeting with Seiren Co. Ltd., a manufacturer of automotive interior materials, discussions focused on its manufacturing operations at the Kadakola Industrial Area in Mysuru and its plans to expand its presence in line with Toyota’s growing capacity in the State.
At a meeting with the leadership of Enomoto Co. Ltd., a Japanese manufacturer of precision connector components and semiconductor lead frames, discussions centred on potential expansion locations, including the Tumakuru Machine Tool Park and the Chennai-Bengaluru Industrial Corridor.
In a meeting with representatives of Secom and Toyota Tsusho Corporation, the Minister discussed the growth plans of Sakra World Hospital. Discussions were also held with Makino, a leading manufacturer of high-precision machine tools, the release said.

title: Amended Delimitation Bill likely to be tabled in special Parliament sitting from November 30
description: Parliament reconvenes from Nov 30 to Dec 3, 2026 to transact essential government business, per Rijiju.
author: Sobhana K. Nair
content:
The government has called for a special sitting of Parliament beginning Monday (November 30, 2026), where it is likely to table an amended Delimitation Bill.
The two Houses will meet on separate dates, Union Parliamentary Affairs Minister Kiren Rijiju announced on Thursday (November 26, 2026), which is the 104th day since the Monsoon Session adjourned indefinitely on August 13.
Lok Sabha sittings will begin on November 30 and Rajya Sabha sittings on December 2. Both Houses will conclude on December 3. The last record of a session of Parliament continuing unprorogued was in 2008, when it went on for 87 days.
The Union Cabinet will meet on Friday (November 27, 2026) to clear the amended legislation. According to sources, three crucial changes are being introduced: a uniform 50% increase in the share of Lok Sabha seats; extending the freeze for 25 years on using the 1971 Census as the basis to determine the proportional strength of each State in the Lok Sabha; and third, using the 2011 Census for redrawing constituencies within each State. This replicates the formula brought by the Atal Bihari Vajpayee government in the Constitution (Eighty-fourth Amendment) Act, 2001.
Reacting to the announcement, Congress general secretary (communication) Jairam Ramesh said the Narendra Modi government announced the session “after 105 days of operation lotus” in the hope of getting a “super-tainted” two-thirds majority to get the Bill passed. “Can there be a great insult to and assault on the Constitution,” he asked in a post on X, noting that the announcement came on Constitution Day.
Congress general secretary (organisation) K.C. Venugopal took to X to describe the attempt to pass the Delimitation Bill as “sansad chori”.
“To orchestrate this murder of the Constitution on Constitution Day shows how badly they want to mock our precious democratic system. We will not allow this to pass,” Mr. Venugopal said.
Changed numbers
Since April, when the legislative package, including the Delimitation Bill, was defeated by a united Opposition in the Lok Sabha, the seat arithmetic in the House has changed. Twenty TMC MPs broke away and merged with the Nationalist Citizens Party of India (NCPI), pledging support to the NDA. TMC challenged the split, which is currently under Lok Sabha Speaker Om Birla’s review. The NCPI faction, on Tuesday (November 24, 2026), 84 days after TMC’s challenge, submitted replies to Mr. Birla, defending its decision and asserting that the move did not violate any parliamentary or constitutional provisions.
Six Shiv Sena (UBT) MPs joined the Eknath Shinde-led Shiv Sena. Following the recent alliance between the BJP and the Shiromani Akali Dal (SAD), the lone SAD MP is also expected to vote with the government. It is also learnt that the YSR Congress, which has four MPs in the Lok Sabha, will extend support to the government on the Bill.
‘For the nation’s good’
In this evolving situation, all eyes are on the DMK, with 22 Lok Sabha MPs, and the NCP (Sharadchandra Pawar), with eight.
Senior NCP (SP) leader Supriya Sule, on Thursday (November 26, 2026), told reporters that pre-emptively opposing the law before its draft was made public was not a good move.
“First let the bill come. Let the entire bill come into our hands. When the bill is in our hands, then we will all talk about it, and if the bill is good for the nation, we might support it,” she said. She further added that there have been instances in the past when the Opposition has supported the government on matters of national importance and key reforms.
DMK’s dilemma
The DMK, meanwhile, has not made any public remarks on the issue. Though, as per sources, the government has reached out to the party informally. A dominant section of the DMK is leaning towards the argument that not supporting the present constitutional amendment could mean further reduced representation for Tamil Nadu.
“The freeze under Articles 81 and 82, which prevents the readjustment of seats allotted to each State in the Lok Sabha, has an inbuilt sunset clause. It provides that the freeze shall cease to operate once the relevant figures of the first Census undertaken after 2026 are published. If a constitutional amendment is not brought, the freeze will automatically lapse,” Swapnil Tripathi, who leads Charkha, Centre for Constitutional Law at the Vidhi Centre for Legal Policy, explained.
If the post-2026 Census figures are taken into consideration, a top DMK leader argued, the State could end up losing as many as 12 seats in the Lok Sabha. “We are for a fair delimitation,” a top DMK leader said.
Political arithmetic
A senior NDA leader said the government is confident of the support of at least 358 MPs, just two short of the required strength if all 540 MPs are present and voting. In April, during the Bill’s previous outing, 528 members were present and voted, with 298 voting in favour and 230 against. In the Rajya Sabha, the NDA has 152 MPs and is within striking distance of the two-thirds majority, which stands at 164 if the entire house is present and voting.

title: India must realise...: Nahid Islam on BJP minister's 'take over' Bangladesh threat
description: Nahid Islam demanded Arjun Singh039s removal and an apology over his threat concerning Bangladesh The exchange could intensify strained India-Bangladesh ties amid tensions over Sheikh Hasina039s extradition
author: India Today News Desk
content:
India must realise...: Nahid Islam on BJP minister's 'take over' Bangladesh threat
Nahid Islam demanded Arjun Singh's removal and an apology over his threat concerning Bangladesh. The exchange could intensify strained India-Bangladesh ties amid tensions over Sheikh Hasina's extradition.
Bangladeshi opposition leader and National Citizen Party (NCP) convener Nahid Islam has hit back at West Bengal Transport Minister Arjun Singh over his controversial threat to "take over" Dhaka, accusing the Indian leader of directly challenging the country's sovereignty. In a statement on X, Islam demanded removal of the BJP minister from the West Bengal cabinet and called for an unconditional apology over the remarks.
"By threatening to occupy Bangladesh, the Transport Minister of the West Bengal state government has directly targeted our independence and sovereignty. Such remarks regarding our beloved homeland achieved through the blood of millions of martyrs are an extreme affront to the self-respect of 180 million people," Islam said.
The remarks threaten to further deepen the fault lines in an already fragile India-Bangladesh relationship, with the latest confrontation unfolding amid growing friction over New Delhi's continued sheltering of ousted Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina.
NAHID ISLAM DEMANDS ACTION FROM DELHI AND DHAKA
Islam argued that the controversy was not merely about a statement by a state-level Indian politician, but about how both New Delhi and Dhaka respond to remarks that appear to challenge Bangladesh's territorial sovereignty.
"We strongly condemn and protest this statement and demand his immediate removal from the cabinet. At the same time, Arjun Singh must promptly withdraw these insolent remarks and offer an unconditional apology to the people of Bangladesh." He also criticised what he described as silence from the Indian government, saying more than 48 hours had passed without visible action against Singh.
"Delhi's silence only deepens our doubts about its respect for Bangladesh's independence and sovereignty," Islam said.
He was equally critical of Bangladesh's own government, accusing it of failing to respond strongly enough to the remarks.
"Equally troubling is the lack of any visible diplomatic response from the Bangladesh government in the wake of Arjun Singh's absurd, anti-sovereignty rhetoric. Such passivity is deeply disappointing for an independent, dignified, and assertive foreign policy."
WHAT DID ARJUN SINGH SAY?
The controversy began after Singh made a provocative statement linking Bangladesh's internal violence against Hindus to a possible Indian response.
"By December 16, we will take over Bangladesh. Enough is enough, there is no excuse for Bangladesh any more. The way Hindus have been killed in Bangladesh, we will definitely avenge that; there is no doubt about it," he said.
December 16 carries particular significance in Bangladesh as Victory Day, marking the country's victory in the 1971 Liberation War.
Islam rejected the claims that Bangladesh could be treated as a country whose sovereignty was open to challenge, framing Singh's remarks as an affront to the country's independence and the sacrifices associated with its creation.
INDIA-BANGLADESH TENSIONS RUN DEEPER
The latest confrontation comes as relations between New Delhi and Dhaka remain sensitive following the fall of Hasina's government in August 2024. Hasina fled to India after a student-led uprising brought down her government following weeks of escalating protests. She has remained in India since then, while Bangladesh has sought her extradition.
Dhaka's International Crimes Tribunal later sentenced Hasina to death in absentia in a case involving crimes against humanity linked to the crackdown on protesters. Hasina has denied the allegations.
Her proposed return to Bangladesh has become another major point of tension. Hasina has said she wants to return to Dhaka, while the Bangladeshi government has maintained that any return would have to take place through extradition.
Bangladesh's State Minister for Foreign Affairs Humayun Kobir recently called Hasina a "terrorist" and said she would not be allowed to return except through extradition.
Her spokesperson Syed Mozammel Ali, meanwhile, has said Hasina wants to travel from Delhi to Dhaka on Biman Bangladesh Airlines, arguing that she was taken to India on a Bangladeshi aircraft when she left the country on August 5, 2024. The demand has been rejected by Bangladesh's International Crimes Tribunal chief prosecutor Md Aminul Islam, who reportedly dismissed the idea of arranging a state aircraft for Hasina's return.
NAHID'S 'INDIAN HEGEMONY' CHARGE
Islam's latest attack also fits into his broader criticism of New Delhi. After meeting Bangladesh Prime Minister Tarique Rahman earlier this week, Islam accused India of giving shelter to a "murderer" and allowing its territory to be used against Bangladesh. He called for political unity to confront what he described as "Indian hegemony".
He has also accused India of attempting to destabilise Bangladesh and urged Dhaka to take a firmer position on bilateral issues, including Hasina's extradition and the renewal of the Ganga water-sharing treaty.
With Hasina's proposed return to Bangladesh on December 16 looming over an already tense circumsatnces, Nahid's remarks can add to the friction between Dhaka and New Delhi.

title: Delimitation, women's quota buzz puts NDA's majority arithmetic to test
description: The NDA is 40 MPs short of a two-thirds majority for the delimitation-linked women039s reservation Bill Here039s how regional parties could change the numbers
author: Himanshu Mishra
content:
Delimitation, women's quota buzz puts NDA's majority arithmetic to test
The NDA is 40 MPs short of a two-thirds majority for the delimitation-linked women's reservation Bill. Here's how regional parties could change the numbers.
The BJP-led NDA faces a fresh numbers challenge as speculation grows over the government's plan to revive the delimitation-linked women's reservation Bill during the proposed special sitting of Parliament. While the ruling alliance has an estimated 320 MPs in the Lok Sabha, its ability to secure the required two-thirds majority could depend on the positions of the DMK, NCP (Sharadchandra Pawar) and YSR Congress Party.
The Lok Sabha has a sanctioned strength of 543 members, with three vacancies leaving its current strength at 540. If all 540 members vote, the government would need 360 votes to pass the Constitution Amendment Bill.
The NDA currently has 320 MPs, leaving it 40 short of the required number. However, the voting threshold could change depending on how many MPs are present and vote.
Three possible scenarios illustrate the numbers challenge facing the government.
NDA'S STRENGTH: 320 MPs
The BJP, with 241 MPs, is the largest constituent of the ruling alliance. The remaining 79 MPs come from its allies.
The NDA's numbers include:
- BJP: 241
- National Citizens Party of India (NCPI): 20
- Telugu Desam Party (TDP): 16
- Shiv Sena: 13
- Janata Dal (United): 12
- Lok Janshakti Party (Ram Vilas): 5
- Rashtriya Lok Dal (RLD): 2
- Janata Samajwadi Party (JSP): 2
- Janata Dal (Secular): 2
- NCP, Shiromani Akali Dal, AGP, AJSU, Apna Dal (S), HAM and SKM: 1 each
- Total NDA strength: 320
SCENARIO 1: DMK, NCP (SP) AND YSRCP SUPPORT THE BILL
If all three parties back the legislation, their combined strength of 34 MPs would take the NDA's tally to 354.
- NDA: 320
- DMK: 22
- NCP (Sharadchandra Pawar): 8
- YSR Congress Party: 4
Total: 354
Even with the support of all three parties, the government would remain six votes short of the 360 required if all 540 members vote.
SCENARIO 2: DMK STAYS AWAY, NCP (SP) AND YSRCP SUPPORT THE BILL
If the DMK's 22 MPs remain absent while the NCP (SP) and YSRCP back the legislation, the government could secure 332 votes, including the support of the two regional parties.
With 22 DMK MPs absent, the number of members voting could fall to 518. The two-thirds threshold would then be 346 votes if all remaining members vote.
The government would still need 14 additional votes.
SCENARIO 3: DMK AND NCP (SP) STAY AWAY
If both the DMK and NCP (SP) abstain, while the YSRCP supports the Bill, the NDA's tally would rise to 324.
With 30 MPs from the DMK and NCP (SP) staying away, the number of members voting could fall to 510. The two-thirds requirement would then be 340 votes.
The NDA would remain 16 votes short.
WHY REGIONAL PARTIES MATTER
The three scenarios underline the importance of regional parties in the government's attempt to secure the numbers for the constitutional amendment.
The DMK has 22 Lok Sabha MPs, while the NCP (Sharadchandra Pawar) has eight and the YSRCP has four. Their support or absence could influence the voting threshold and the government's chances of passing the legislation.
The proposed amendment seeks to link the implementation of the 33 per cent reservation for women in the Lok Sabha and state assemblies to delimitation and an expansion of the Lower House.
The government is expected to take up the issue ahead of the proposed special sitting of Parliament, with the Lok Sabha scheduled to reconvene on November 30 and the Rajya Sabha on December 2.
The central question is whether the NDA can secure enough support, either through additional votes or a lower voting threshold resulting from opposition abstentions, to pass the constitutional amendment.
WHAT HAPPENED DURING THE APRIL VOTE?
The numbers challenge comes after the Constitution (131st Amendment) Bill was defeated in the Lok Sabha on April 17.
Of the 528 MPs who voted, 298 supported the Bill, and 230 opposed it. The government needed 352 votes to secure a two-thirds majority but fell short by 54 votes.
The April legislative package sought to expand the Lok Sabha and implement 33 per cent reservation for women in the Lower House and state assemblies through a fresh delimitation exercise.
Parliament passed the women's reservation law in 2023, linking its implementation to delimitation after the publication of figures from the first Census conducted after the law came into force.
PARLIAMENT TO RECONVENE FROM NOVEMBER 30
The numbers have returned to focus after Parliamentary Affairs Minister Kiren Rijiju announced on Thursday that the government had requested the Lok Sabha to reconvene on November 30 and the Rajya Sabha on December 2 to transact essential government business.
The sittings could conclude on December 3, depending on the business before the Houses, he said.
The proposed sittings will be an extension of the Monsoon Session. Parliament was adjourned sine die on August 13 but has not been prorogued.
The agenda for the proposed sitting has not been announced, but speculation over a fresh attempt to pass the delimitation-linked women's reservation legislation has intensified.

title: Stop heavy machinery near Sheshnag Lake, urges former J&K ruler Karan Singh
description: Karan Singh039s remarks come amid a growing controversy over construction activity near Sheshnag Lake after a video showing excavators and heavy machinery operating along its banks went viral
author: Mir Fareed
content:
Stop heavy machinery near Sheshnag Lake, urges former J&K ruler Karan Singh
Karan Singh's remarks come amid a growing controversy over construction activity near Sheshnag Lake, after a video showing excavators and heavy machinery operating along its banks went viral.
Former Jammu and Kashmir Sadar-i-Riyasat (Constitutional Head) Karan Singh has expressed shock over the use of heavy earth-moving machinery to widen the Amarnath pilgrimage route, particularly near the ecologically fragile Sheshnag Lake.
Supporting those protesting the construction activity, the erstwhile titular Maharaja has urged the authorities to halt the deployment of heavy equipment in the area.
In a statement, Karan Singh highlighted the ecological fragility of the Himalayas and cautioned against large-scale construction activity along sensitive pilgrimage routes. He recalled his longstanding concerns over avoidable road widening in Uttarakhand, pointing to the extensive use of dynamite in the region and the disasters associated with disturbing fragile mountain terrain, including the Kedarnath tragedy.
"I join my voice with those who are protesting about this, and would urge those concerned not to use heavy equipment on this route. We do not have to make every pilgrim route into a motorable road just for the convenience of tourists. Genuine pilgrims will not mind walking or riding towards this great shrine," he said.
Questioning the push to make every pilgrimage route motorable for the convenience of tourists, he said existing two-lane roads were sufficient. He added that genuine pilgrims would not mind walking or riding to the shrine rather than having every stretch of the route widened for vehicular access.
"In the name of tourists, an unnecessary programme of road widening is underway which involves extensive use of dynamite which severely damages the comparatively young Himalayas. In fact, several disasters have already occurred, including the one at Kedarnath some years ago," he further added.
His remarks come amid a growing controversy over construction activity near Sheshnag Lake, after a video showing excavators and heavy machinery operating along its banks went viral. The footage showed excavated soil being dumped near the lake's shoreline, triggering concerns among environmentalists and political leaders over the potential damage to the fragile Himalayan ecosystem.
Located at an altitude of around 11,780 feet in Anantnag district, Sheshnag is a glacier-fed alpine lake and one of the 14 officially identified high-risk glacial lakes in Jammu and Kashmir with the potential for glacial lake outburst floods (GLOFs). Such floods occur when water from a glacial lake is suddenly released downstream, posing a serious threat to settlements and infrastructure.
The controversy has also acquired a religious dimension, with Sheshnag regarded as a sacred site in Hinduism and an important halt for pilgrims travelling to the Amarnath cave shrine. According to Hindu belief, Lord Shiva left behind the serpents adorning his body at the lake before proceeding to the cave to narrate the Amar Katha to Goddess Parvati.
The Border Roads Organisation (BRO), which is responsible for the work, has said the activity is part of post-Amarnath Yatra maintenance and is being carried out with environmental safeguards. It maintained that the work was confined to existing tracks and aimed at stabilising vulnerable stretches, widening the paths to ease congestion and ensuring safer passage for pilgrims.
The BRO's clarification has, however, failed to quell the outrage, with political leaders and environmental concerns keeping the spotlight on the construction activity and its possible impact on the sensitive glacial ecosystem.

title: Centre authorises states, UTs to exercise powers under UAPA against Zakir Naik’s IRF
description: Centre authorises states, UTs to exercise powers under UAPA against Zakir Naik’s IRF | India News
author: PTI
content:
Centre authorises states, UTs to exercise powers under UAPA against Zakir Naik’s IRF
New Delhi, The Centre has authorised states and Union territories to exercise powers related to funds and premises under the stringent Unlawful Activities Act, 1967, in relation to fugitive preacher Zakir Naik's Islamic Research Foundation , which was declared an unlawful association earlier this month.
In a gazette notification issued on Thursday, the Ministry of Home Affairs invoked powers under Section 42 of the anti-terror law to issue the directive to state governments and Union territory administrators.
The ministry had extended the ban on the IRF as an unlawful association through a notification dated November 13 under sections 3 and 3 of the Act.
"The Central government declared the Islamic Research Foundation an unlawful association vide notification number S.O. 6182 dated November 13, 2026, published in the Gazette of India; in exercise of the powers conferred by Section 42 of the Unlawful Activities Act, 1967, the Central government hereby directs that all powers exercisable by it under sections 7 and 8 of the said Act shall also be exercised by the state governments and the Union territory administrations in relation to the above said unlawful association," the notification said.
Section 7 of the UA pertains to the powers of the government to prohibit the use or transfer of funds, securities and other financial assets suspected of being used or intended for the purposes of an unlawful association.
It also allows authorised officers to investigate such financial dealings, whereas Section 8 empowers the government to notify premises, including houses and buildings, suspected of being used for the activities of an unlawful association.
Following the notification, the authorities can regulate access to a premises and restrict the use of movable properties found there.
On November 13, the Centre extended the ban on fugitive preacher Zakir Naik's IRF for another five years under the stringent UA. The ban was to expire on November 14.
Naik, a resident of Maharashtra, was on a trip abroad when the government banned his organisation in 2016. Since then, he has been living in Malaysia. In 2017, his passport was also revoked at the request of the National Investigation Agency , which registered a case against him.
India has been pursuing legal and diplomatic measures against Naik since November 17, 2016, when the Central government declared his organisation an unlawful association citing allegations of promoting enmity and hatred between religious communities.
In May 2017, India approached INTERPOL for a Red Corner Notice against Naik, providing subsequent clarifications in August and October.
However, during its 102nd session in late December 2017, the Interpol Commission deemed the request premature because a charge-sheet had not been filed at the time of the initial application.
Based on a fresh court warrant issued on November 24, 2017, the Indian agencies submitted a renewed RCN request to INTERPOL on January 3, 2018, a response to which remains awaited.
India had also formally transmitted a provisional arrest and extradition request to Malaysia's Ministry of Foreign Affairs on January 19, 2018, after it was confirmed that Naik had been granted permanent residency status.
This article was generated from an automated news agency feed without modifications to text.

title: Judicial member must for ED attachment cases: Supreme Court
description: The court held that such consequential decisions cannot be left to a member without a legal background. | India News
author: Utkarsh Anand
content:
Utkarsh Anand is the National Legal Editor at Hindustan Times, where he leads the newspaper's coverage of the Supreme Court, constitutional law, the judiciary and the Union law ministry. He joined Hindustan Times in 2020 after stints at Press Trust of India (PTI), The Indian Express and CNN-News18, and has over two decades of experience reporting on law, governance and public policy. His work has focussed on some of India's most consequential constitutional and legal developments, including the Supreme Court's judgments on Article 370, marriage equality, decriminalisation of homosexuality, the Babri Masjid dispute, electoral reforms and judicial appointments. He specialises in making complex legal proceedings and judgments accessible to readers while examining their wider social and political impact. Beyond daily reportage, Utkarsh has led investigative projects and enterprise reporting that have shaped public debate and prompted institutional responses. His work has received several journalism awards, including the Ramnath Goenka Excellence in Journalism Award. As National Legal Editor, he has also played a key role in expanding Hindustan Times' legal journalism footprint, mentoring reporters and strengthening coverage across platforms. A Chevening South Asia Journalism Programme Fellow, Utkarsh regularly writes analyses on the judiciary and constitutional issues, and his reporting is widely followed by lawyers, judges, policymakers, academics and readers seeking clarity on India's evolving legal landscape.
Judicial member must for ED attachment cases: Supreme Court
The court held that such consequential decisions cannot be left to a member without a legal background.
The Supreme Court on Thursday ruled that the adjudicating authority (AA) under the Prevention of Money Laundering Act (PMLA) must include a judicial member while deciding whether to confirm the Enforcement Directorate’s (ED) provisional attachment of properties, holding that such consequential decisions cannot be left to a member without a legal background.
A bench, comprising Chief Justice of India (CJI) Surya Kant and justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana, clarified that while a single-member bench can undertake adjudication under the law, it must necessarily comprise the judicial member of the AA. The requirement, the court said, flows from the need to ensure legal objectivity when determining whether properties are involved in money laundering, a finding that can have serious consequences for the rights of individuals.
The ruling settles an important legal question that had divided high courts, with the Delhi, Calcutta and Telangana high courts having declined to insist on the presence of a judicial member in every bench of the AA. The Supreme Court has now drawn a clear distinction between the authority’s administrative and adjudicatory functions, holding that the former can be performed without a judicial member but the latter cannot.
“The AA is, however, plainly more than a custodian of records. As its very name indicates, its principal task is ‘adjudication’ under Section 8 of the PMLA,” noted the bench, distinguishing between the authority acting as the “keeper of the sealed cover” and when “it holds the scales”.
The court explained that when the ED provisionally attaches a property, it forwards the order, along with the material relied upon, to the AA, which preserves these records. This custodial function does not involve substantive decision-making or the appreciation of competing submissions and can, therefore, be discharged without a judicial member.
However, the position changes when the AA hears the affected person and the ED, examines the evidence and determines whether the property is involved in money laundering. Such an exercise requires the application of legal principles, interpretation of statutory provisions and appreciation of evidence, it said.
“The application of an independent judicial mind is...adequately ensured by the presence of a Judicial Member in the Bench undertaking adjudication under Sections 8(2) and 8(3) of PMLA,” it held.
The bench also rejected the Centre’s argument that the availability of an appeal before the appellate tribunal and subsequently the high court was sufficient safeguard against any erroneous decision by the AA.
“An appellate forum may correct the errors in a decision; it cannot supply what the original forum lacked,” said the court, adding that a defect in proceedings before the AA on account of the absence of a judicial member cannot be cured merely because an appeal lies to a judicial forum.
It further clarified that a judicial member need not necessarily be appointed as the chairperson of the AA. The chairperson’s role, it said, was essentially administrative, involving the constitution of benches and allocation of cases, and did not require the same application of legal mind as the adjudicatory process.
It accordingly directed the chairperson to issue the necessary administrative circular to ensure that every bench passing an order under Section 8(3) of the PMLA includes a judicial member. The court also extended the requirement to certain consequential determinations under other provisions of the PMLA, which are intrinsically linked to the adjudication of attachment, freezing or retention of property and records.
Notably, the judgment did not invalidate the issuance of show-cause notices under Section 8(1) by a bench without a judicial member, nor did it mandate that every adjudication must be conducted by a bench of two or more members. A single-member bench remains permissible, provided the member is drawn from the field of law.
The bench also clarified that its ruling would not automatically reopen orders already passed by a single, non-judicial member before Thursday. Persons aggrieved by such orders would, however, remain free to challenge them on their merits through the statutory appellate remedy.
SC flags need for multiple adjudicating authorities
Separately, the bench nudged the Centre to reconsider the 2009 amendment to the PMLA that restricted the number of adjudicating authorities to one, recommending that the government examine the desirability of restoring the original framework of multiple AAs, including regional authorities.
Pointing to the steep rise in provisional attachment orders (PAOs), the court said the existing arrangement was placing enormous pressure on the authority, particularly when it was required to complete adjudication within the statutory period of 180 days.
According to figures furnished by the ED, a total of 3,639 PAOs had been issued since July 2005. While 321 such orders were issued in 2023-24, the number rose to 461 in 2024-25 and further jumped to 712 in 2025-26. Another 138 PAOs were issued up to August 31, 2026.
The bench noted that the expansion of offences under the PMLA schedule and the consequent widening of proceedings under the law would only add to the workload, including applications for retention of seized properties and records.
“This juxtaposition of the increasing cases and the time-bound nature of adjudication, to our mind, puts an enormous pressure on the Members of the AA, especially those involved in the process of adjudication,” it said.
The court observed that the 2009 amendment, which replaced the original provision allowing the Centre to appoint one or more adjudicating authorities with a framework providing for only one, appeared to have created “an undesirable, if not unsolvable, lock-jam of cases at the level of the AA”. It cautioned that such circumstances could induce hurried and hasty decisions, adversely affecting stakeholders’ ability to access justice.
The bench said it would ordinarily have exercised its powers under Article 142 of the Constitution to direct the Centre to notify additional adjudicating authorities, which would also enable the creation of regional AAs. However, since the 2009 amendment itself was not under challenge, it refrained from issuing such a direction.
Instead, it recommended that the Union government “appropriately consider the suitability and desirability of repealing the 2009 Amendment and reverting to the original framework of multiple Adjudicating Authorities and take necessary steps for the same”.
In its concluding observations, the bench described the PMLA as a law of “exceptional rigour”, stressing that its stringent provisions must be accompanied by safeguards at the stage when an affected person gets the opportunity to contest the attachment of property.
“Independence of position is, however, only one half of that assurance. Where the authority is called upon to weigh evidence, apply statutory presumptions and construe the law, the assurance is fully honoured only when the person who decides is trained in the discipline of the law,” it said.

title: ASI hands over 12th-century bronze idol, 2 other repatriated antiquities to Tamil Nadu Police
description: ASI DG Yadubir Singh Rawat handed Somaskanda, Saint Sundarar with Paravai Nachiyar and Saint Kannappa Nayanar to the Idol Wing CID at Dharohar Bhawan | India News
author: PTI
content:
ASI hands over 12th-century bronze idol, 2 other repatriated antiquities to Tamil Nadu Police
ASI DG Yadubir Singh Rawat handed Somaskanda, Saint Sundarar with Paravai Nachiyar and Saint Kannappa Nayanar to the Idol Wing CID at Dharohar Bhawan
Three repatriated antiquities, including a 12th-century Chola-period bronze idol, were on Thursday handed over by the Archaeological Survey of India (ASI) to the Tamil Nadu Police at a function held at the ASI headquarters here, marking a "significant step" towards the recovery and restitution of India's cultural heritage, officials said.
The antiquities comprise two bronze idols repatriated from the Smithsonian Museum in the US and one from The Hague in the Netherlands. They were formally handed over to the respective police officers, the ASI said.
Also read: BJP office-bearer chants ‘kamal khila de’ at Taj Mahal, Archaeological Survey of India files plaint
The antiquities include Somaskanda (Lord Shiva and Uma), a 12th-century Chola-period bronze idol photographed in 1959 at the Siva Temple, Sri Visvanatha in Alattur, Mannargudi Taluk, Thanjavur district of Tamil Nadu. It was repatriated from the Smithsonian Museum, the ministry said.
Another antiquity, Saint Sundarar with Paravai Nachiyar, is a 16th-century bronze idol belonging to the Vijayanagara period. It was photographed in 1956 at the Shiva Temple, Sri Narisvara in Viracholapuram, Kallakurichi Taluk, Tamil Nadu, and was also repatriated from the Smithsonian Museum, it said in a statement.
The third antiquity, Saint Kannappa Nayanar, is a Chola-period bronze idol from Arulmigu Agneeswarasamy Temple in Thirupugalur, Nagapattinam district in Tamil Nadu.
It depicts the Shaivite saint in a 'tribhanga' standing posture, with his right hand raised towards his eye. The idol was repatriated from The Hague, the ASI said.
"In a significant step towards the recovery and restitution of India's cultural heritage, the Archaeological Survey of India today handed over the three repatriated antiquities to the Idol Wing CID, Tamil Nadu Police, at Dharohar Bhawan, New Delhi," it said.
Also read: ‘Total callousness’: SC slams Delhi civic body, ASI over neglected heritage sites
The formal handover was undertaken by ASI Director General Yadubir Singh Rawat, along with other representatives of the organisation.
The restitution of the antiquities marks an important milestone in India's ongoing efforts to bring its cultural treasures back to their rightful home, officials said.
The ASI continues to work towards identifying, recovering and repatriating India's lost heritage in coordination with national and international agencies, they added.

title: SBI Customers To Face UPI, ATM, Internet Banking Disruptions For Hours Today | Check Timings
description: State Bank of India announced temporary disruptions in UPI, ATM, internet banking, and fund transfer services during scheduled maintenance on Friday, November 27.
author: Yimkumla Longkumer, News Desk
content:
SBI Customers To Face UPI, ATM, Internet Banking Disruptions For Hours Today | Check Timings
State Bank of India announced temporary disruptions in UPI, ATM, internet banking, and fund transfer services during scheduled maintenance on Friday, November 27.
State Bank of India (SBI) customers will face temporary disruptions in several banking services, including UPI payments, ATM withdrawals, internet banking and fund transfers, during the early hours of Friday, November 27, due to scheduled maintenance.
The bank announced the service interruptions in two separate posts on social media platform X on Thursday, advising customers to plan their transactions accordingly.
“Due to scheduled maintenance activity, our following services will be temporarily unavailable on 27.11.2026," SBI said.
SBI Banking Services: Check Timings
According to the bank, different services will remain unavailable during the following time slots:
- Internet banking, YONO, YONO Lite and IMPS: 1:15 am to 1:45 am (30 minutes).
- NEFT: 1:55 am to 2:40 am (45 minutes).
- RTGS: 12:45 am to 1:30 am (45 minutes).
- ATM services: 1:45 am to 2:45 am (one hour).
- UPI services: 1:15 am to 2:00 am (45 minutes).
The scheduled maintenance will affect services at different intervals between 12:45 am and 2:45 am on Friday.
UPI Lite To Remain Available
In a separate announcement, SBI said its UPI services would be unavailable for 45 minutes, from 1:15 am to 2:00 am.
“Due to scheduled maintenance activity, SBI UPI services will be temporarily unavailable from 01:15 hrs to 02:00 hrs (IST) on 27.11.2026. The activity may, however, be completed early. Customers may continue to use UPI Lite Services for uninterrupted service," the bank said.
However, customers can continue to make payments through UPI Lite during this period.
UPI Lite allows users to make small-value digital payments using their available balance without entering a UPI PIN for every transaction.
SBI has advised customers to complete important payments and fund transfers before the scheduled maintenance windows. Those requiring cash during the affected hours are also advised to withdraw it in advance.
(With inputs from ANI)
Quick Answers
Internet banking, YONO, YONO Lite, and IMPS will be unavailable from 1:15 am to 1:45 am, while regular UPI services will be down from 1:15 am to 2:00 am on November 27, 2026, due to scheduled maintenance.

title: Bangladesh Leader Slams Bengal Minister's 'Take Over' Remark, Says India's Sovereignty Tied To Dhaka
description: Nahid Islam demanded Singh's immediate removal from the West Bengal Cabinet and called on him to withdraw his remarks and offer an unconditional apology.
author: Yimkumla Longkumer
content:
Bangladesh Leader Slams Bengal Minister's 'Take Over' Remark, Says India's Sovereignty Tied To Dhaka
Nahid Islam demanded Singh's immediate removal from the West Bengal Cabinet and called on him to withdraw his remarks and offer an unconditional apology.
Bangladesh’s National Citizen Party convenor Nahid Islam has strongly condemned West Bengal Transport Minister Arjun Singh’s remark about taking over Bangladesh, saying India’s own sovereignty and territorial integrity are closely linked to its neighbouring country.
In a lengthy post on X on Thursday, Islam demanded Singh’s immediate removal from the West Bengal Cabinet and called on him to withdraw his remarks and offer an unconditional apology to the people of Bangladesh.
“By threatening to occupy Bangladesh, the Transport Minister of the West Bengal state government has directly targeted our independence and sovereignty," Islam wrote.
By threatening to occupy Bangladesh, the Transport Minister of the West Bengal state government has directly targeted our independence and sovereignty. Such remarks regarding our beloved homeland achieved through the blood of millions of martyrs are an extreme affront to the self-respect of 180 million people.We strongly condemn and protest this statement and demand his immediate removal from the cabinet. At the same time, Arjun Singh must promptly withdraw these insolent remarks and offer an unconditional apology to the people of Bangladesh.
More than 48 hours have passed since a public official made such derogatory comments, yet the Indian government has taken no action against him. Delhi’s silence only deepens our doubts about its respect for Bangladesh’s independence and sovereignty.
Equally troubling is the lack of any visible diplomatic response from the Bangladesh government in the wake of Arjun Singh’s absurd, anti-sovereignty rhetoric. Such passivity is deeply disappointing for an independent, dignified, and assertive foreign policy.
Figures like Arjun Singh fail to grasp the glorious history of our people’s resilience and struggle. The era in which India reaped unilateral advantages during the past fascist regime by turning Bangladesh into a puppet state through the ousted autocrat Sheikh Hasina will never return. Today, 180 million Bangladeshis stand united like steel and resolute in defending their rightful claims, freedom, and sovereignty.
India must realize that its own sovereignty and territorial integrity are closely tied to Bangladesh. Undermining Bangladesh’s sovereignty or attempting to stoke internal instability through proxies can ultimately jeopardize India’s own territorial integrity. The people of Bangladesh remain vigilant and ready to thwart any anti-Bangladesh conspiracy by the Indian state.
— Nahid Islam (@NahidIslam_24) November 26, 2026
He called the comments as an “affront to the self-respect of 180 million Bangladeshis" and said the country would not tolerate any attempt to undermine its freedom.
“India must realize that its own sovereignty and territorial integrity are closely tied to Bangladesh," he added, warning that any attempt to undermine Bangladesh’s independence or create instability could also threaten India’s territorial integrity.
“The people of Bangladesh remain vigilant and ready to thwart any anti-Bangladesh conspiracy by the Indian state," he added.
What Did Arjun Singh Say?
Singh triggered a controversy on Wednesday after claiming that Bangladesh would be taken over by December 16 to avenge the alleged killings of Hindus in the neighbouring country.
“By December 16, we will take over Bangladesh. Enough is enough. There is no excuse for Bangladesh any more. The way Hindus have been killed in Bangladesh, we will definitely avenge that; there is no doubt about it," the BJP leader told reporters in Bhatpara.
December 16 holds special significance for Bangladesh as it celebrates Victory Day, marking the surrender of Pakistani forces in the 1971 Liberation War and the country’s emergence as an independent nation.
Nahid Islam Questions India’s Silence
Islam also questioned the Indian government’s response to Singh’s remarks, saying more than 48 hours had passed without any action against the minister.
“Delhi’s silence only deepens our doubts about its respect for Bangladesh’s independence and sovereignty," he wrote.
He also questioned the Bangladesh government’s silence over the remarks, expressing disappointment at the lack of an official diplomatic response.
“Equally troubling is the lack of any visible diplomatic response from the Bangladesh government in the wake of Arjun Singh’s absurd, anti-sovereignty rhetoric. Such passivity is deeply disappointing for an independent, dignified, and assertive foreign policy," he noted.
Referring to Bangladesh’s history, Islam said the country had achieved independence through the sacrifices of millions and that its people remained united in defending their sovereignty.
“The era in which India reaped unilateral advantages during the past fascist regime by turning Bangladesh into a puppet state through the ousted autocrat Sheikh Hasina will never return," he added.
(With inputs from PTI)
Quick Answers
Arjun Singh claimed that Bangladesh would be taken over by December 16 to avenge the alleged killings of Hindus in the neighbouring country.

title: Massive backlog of pending cases remains significant challenge for justice delivery system: President Droupadi
description: Asserting that making justice accessible based on equal opportunity by providing free legal aid is a directive of the Constitution, she stressed ensuring quality and reliability of legal representation for people belonging to the poor and deprived sections.
author: PTI
content:
Massive backlog of pending cases remains significant challenge for justice delivery system: President Droupadi Murmu
- Published OnNov 26, 2026 | 23:29 IST
- Last Updated OnNov 26, 2026 | 23:29 IST
Asserting that making justice accessible based on equal opportunity by providing free legal aid is a directive of the Constitution, she stressed ensuring quality and reliability of legal representation for people belonging to the poor and deprived sections.
President Droupadi Murmu on Thursday said the massive backlog of pending cases remains a significant challenge for the country's justice delivery system and stressed the timely delivery of justice.
Asserting that making justice accessible based on equal opportunity by providing free legal aid is a directive of the Constitution, she stressed ensuring quality and reliability of legal representation for people belonging to the poor and deprived sections.
"Not everyone possesses the resources required to access the high courts or the Supreme Court," the president said.
She said the Constitution mandates the provision of justice on the basis of equal opportunity, which includes the facilitation of free legal aid.
The objective of this mandate is to ensure that no citizen is denied the opportunity to seek justice due to economic constraints or any other form of hardship, President Murmu said.
She said that timely delivery of justice is an essential component of the very concept of justice.
To ensure that justice is accessible in a timely manner, the judiciary is undertaking various initiatives such as simplifying procedures, leveraging technology and establishing special courts, the president said.
She said that despite these efforts, the massive backlog of pending cases remains a significant challenge for our justice delivery system.
President Murmu expressed confidence that this challenge will be addressed through the concerted efforts being made at every level of the judiciary.
She said it is also crucial to focus on the quality and reliability of legal representation available to the poor and marginalised sections of society.
In this context, the district, state and national legal services authorities must intensify their efforts to ensure that justice reaches these vulnerable and disadvantaged groups, President Murmu said.
"A large number of criminal cases are pending in some districts of the country. I am pleased to know that the central government has taken an initiative to collaborate with national law universities to address this challenge in those districts.
"Students, researchers and pro bono clubs of national law universities are being involved in this effort. Such initiatives will instil sensitivity in the students and familiarise them with grassroots legal processes," she said.
President Murmu said that "justice for all" should not be just said but it is to be done, and asserted providing accessible justice to all.
She emphasised that true progress of a nation lies in ensuring that every citizen has an equal opportunity to thrive and succeed.
The president underscored the importance of providing every child with equal access to quality education.
"It is said that children are the future of the country... The key to development is education.
"That is why the Chief Justice (of India) is sitting here (on the dais)," the president said, addressing the Constitution Day celebrations organised by the Supreme Court here.
A person who is poor today cannot become rich tomorrow, but a child born into a poor family today can progress through education, she said.
"Should we not provide them with an opportunity? Can we not work in this direction?" the president asked.
"Indianness should be reflected in all aspects of the work culture of our institutions. Under the Constitution, it is also the duty of all citizens to understand the importance of the glorious traditions of our culture and preserve them," the president said.
She thanked the government for ensuring "adult franchise" for all and making the country Naxal-free.
All should get a chance to vote, President Murmu said.
"I want to thank the government. Today the entire country has become free from Naxals.
"When the Naxals were surrendering, I was looking at their faces. Is he really a Naxal (sic)?... Why were those people made Naxals? Why were we not made Naxals? We need to work on this 'why'," she added.
The president said that empathy and ethics should be given as much importance as the study of laws in legal education in our country.
She urged the leading lights in the lawyers' community to present inspiring examples for young lawyers.
The president said that larger and more active participation of women in the Bench and Bar will help make our society more fair, just, equitable and inclusive.
She highlighted that a woman's perspective can add to inclusion, diversity and balance to judicial decision-making.
President Murmu underlined the need to encourage greater participation by women as judges and lawyers. "Greater emphasis on inclusivity and merit will further strengthen our judiciary," she added.
The president noted that the Supreme Court has taken steps to promote access to justice by prioritising cases relating to specially abled persons, acid attack victims, senior citizens aged above 80 years and persons below the poverty line.
She appreciated the steps taken for more effective case management and listing, promoting digital transformation and encouraging amicable resolution of disputes.
President Murmu said that the Supreme Court, high courts and the district and lower courts have made an invaluable contribution to the glorious journey of our republic.
"Over the past decades, there have been unimaginable changes across many spheres of life. In particular, the influence of technology and media has become increasingly pervasive and profound.
"While adapting its role to changing circumstances and expectations, the judiciary has upheld and strengthened the fundamental ideals of justice," she said.
From time to time, the Indian judiciary has placed special emphasis on judicial accountability, thereby bringing to execution the ideals envisioned by the framers of the Constitution, the president said, adding that "the synergy between judicial independence and judicial accountability lends strength to the role of the judiciary".

title: Indian Youth Congress denies meeting Meta officials, demands disclosure of takedown orders
description: The Indian Youth Congress denied meeting Meta officials and demanded transparency on takedown orders, the revocation of account restrictions, and an apology for alleged political bias.
author: Ankit Kumar
content:
Indian Youth Congress denies meeting Meta officials, demands disclosure of takedown orders
- Published OnNov 26, 2026 | 23:25 IST
- Last Updated OnNov 26, 2026 | 23:25 IST
The Indian Youth Congress has denied reports of a meeting with Meta officials and demanded disclosure of government takedown orders and removals by automated systems since January 2026. The demands come amid protests over alleged removal of social media posts critical of the BJP.
The Indian Youth Congress (IYC) on Thursday, November 26, denied reports claiming that its leaders had met officials of Meta to discuss content moderation and restrictions on social media platforms. The Congress's youth wing also demanded that the company disclose government-issued takedown orders and details of content removals carried out by its automated systems since January 2026.
In a post on X, the IYC rejected reports of a meeting with Meta representatives, stating that no such meeting had taken place with its leadership and that it was not aware of any proposal or communication from the company.
The IYC also called on Meta to disclose the total number of government-issued takedown orders and removals carried out through its automated systems from January 2026 onwards.
What are Indian Youth Congress's demands from Meta?
The Congress's youth wing has demanded that Meta revoke what it described as pan-India restrictions on citizens' Facebook and Instagram accounts and posts.
It has also sought details of how the company's automated systems allegedly moderate content critical of the BJP government. Additionally, the IYC demanded an apology to citizens, journalists and opposition voices whose accounts or posts were allegedly removed without due process.
The organisation said it would not hold any discussions with Meta until its demands were addressed.
Accusing the company of acting with political bias, the IYC called on Meta to operate as a neutral platform and uphold freedom of expression. It also said it would continue its campaign through democratic means and legal remedies.
Why is Indian Youth Congress protesting against Meta?
The latest statement comes amid protests by Youth Congress members outside Meta-affiliated offices in Hyderabad, Mumbai and Gurugram. The protests began on November 20 over allegations that social media posts critical of the ruling BJP were being removed.
The IYC's clarification also follows media reports claiming that Meta officials had met party representatives on Tuesday to discuss content moderation and restrictions on its social media platforms. The organisation has, however, denied that any such meeting took place.

title: 'Stopping Deepam hurts sentiments of millions of people,' says Ashwini Vaishnaw
description: Addressing a Constitution Day event held by the BJP, Vaishnaw questioned whether citizens would eventually be barred from visiting temples if such restrictions went unchallenged.
author: PTI
content:
'Stopping Deepam hurts sentiments of millions of people,' says Ashwini Vaishnaw
- Published OnNov 26, 2026 | 23:19 IST
- Last Updated OnNov 26, 2026 | 23:19 IST
Addressing a Constitution Day event held by the BJP, Vaishnaw questioned whether citizens would eventually be barred from visiting temples if such restrictions went unchallenged.
Union Minister of Railways Ashwini Vaishnaw on Thursday mounted a sharp cultural and political offensive against the TVK government, asserting that "stopping the lighting of a traditional deepam," hurts the sentiments of millions of people and warned against "attempts to erase the country's civilisational heritage and temple traditions."
Addressing a Constitution Day event held by the BJP, Vaishnaw questioned whether citizens would eventually be barred from visiting temples if such restrictions went unchallenged.
"Tamil Nadu is intact. Stopping one deepam, you have stopped, you have hurt, you have destroyed and disturbed the emotions of millions of people. What will happen? Today you have stopped one deepam, tomorrow you will say that nobody can go to a temple? They'll shut down the temples. Is that what they want?" he asked.
The minister claimed that "true respect for the Constitution means safeguarding religious freedom and taking pride in our culture, Lord Muruga, and our ancient heritage,"
Turning his appeal directly toward TVK from the stage for railway schemes, Vaishnaw challenged the party to take up the cause of land acquisition, assuring that the Centre would provide all necessary funds and complete every project without hassle to deliver justice to the Tamil people.
The minister claimed that out of approximately 4,800 hectares required for railway projects in Tamil Nadu, the state government has acquired only 1,253 hectares, a mere 24 per cent.
Questioning how the railways can build without land, he called for cooperative federalism—where two steps by the Centre were met with one step by the state—so both Tamil Nadu and its people can progress
Urging leaders not to shy away from their responsibilities, he remarked while opponents might succeed in stopping a single deepam (lamp) from being lit, they cannot halt the growth, development, or global standing of the Tamil people, whose pride remains intact.
Vaishnaw also accused the Congress of "rejecting" constitutional methods of conducting elections and spreading nationwide confusion.
Pointing to the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls, he noted that the process was successfully conducted in Tamil Nadu without any objection from the Congress.
"Congress wants to just blame SIR for their own failures. And they will keep failing like this. Because for them, it is not the Constitution, it is the family. That is the only thing which is important for them. They don't believe in Dr Ambedkar's philosophy", he said.
Extending this argument to Electronic Voting Machines (EVMs), he dismissed the Congress party's recurring complaints that EVMs lead to their losses.
He said, "EVM voting took place across Tamil Nadu, Andhra Pradesh, Telangana, Karnataka, Kerala, Himachal Pradesh, and West Bengal where the Congress won zero seats."
Further, he claimed that the Congress party "refuses to do grassroots hard work and continues to rely solely on a family name."

title: 543 से 850 सीटें... संसद का बदलेगा सियासी नक्शा! किस राज्य की बढ़ेगी ताकत, किसकी घटेगी हिस्सेदारी? 21 सवालों में समझिए परिसीमन की ABCD
description: परिसीमन से लोकसभा की सीटें 543 से बढ़कर 850 तक हो सकती हैं. जानिए जनगणना, उत्तर-दक्षिण विवाद, महिला आरक्षण, राज्यों की राजनीतिक हिस्सेदारी और आपके निर्वाचन क्षेत्र पर इसका संभावित असर.
author: ताहिर कामरान
content:
देश की सियासत में इन दिनों एक ऐसी प्रक्रिया चर्चा का विषय बनी हुई है, जो आने वाले वर्षों में देश की सियासत का पूरा गणित बदल सकती है. इसका नाम है परिसीमन यानी Delimitation. यह वह प्रक्रिया है, जिसका असर सिर्फ राजनीतिक दलों या सिर्फ नेताओं तक सीमित नहीं रहेगा, बल्कि आम जनता के राजनीतिक सीमाएं भी बदल जाएंगी. इस प्रक्रिया के बाद आपका सांसद बदल सकता है और संसद में आपके राज्य की राजनीतिक हिस्सेदारी भी प्रभावित हो सकती है. क्योंकि इसमें लोकसभा की सीटें 543 से बढ़ाकर 850 तक करने का प्रावधान है.
बात सिर्फ लोकसभा की सीटों पर खत्म नहीं होती. सवाल यह भी है कि अगर सीटें बढ़ीं तो किस राज्य की राजनीतिक ताकत बढ़ेगी और किसकी हिस्सेदारी में कटौती हो सकती है? इस खबर में हम परिसीमन से जुड़े आपके तमाम सवालों को जवाब देंगे. हम बताएंगे कि परिसीमन क्या है? इसकी जरूरत क्यों पड़ती है? भारत में अब तक कितनी बार परिसीमन हुआ है? उत्तर और दक्षिण भारत के बीच इसको लेकर विवाद क्यों है? और सबसे बड़ा सवाल, क्या परिसीमन के बाद संसद में राज्यों की ताकत का संतुलन बदल जाएगा?
जवाब: परिसीमन वह प्रक्रिया है, जिसके तहत लोकसभा और विधानसभा क्षेत्रों की सरहदें तय होती हैं. यानी यह तय करना कि कौन सा गांव, शहर या इलाका किस चुनाव क्षेत्र में आएगा और किस क्षेत्र से कितने प्रतिनिधि चुने जाएंगे. आपका क्षेत्र अभी जिस विधानसभा या लोकसभा में आता है, जरूरी नहीं है कि परिसीमन के बाद भी उसी क्षेत्र में बना रहे. इस दौरान सभी क्षेत्रों को आबादी के लिहाज से फिर से बांटा जाता है.
जवाब: परिसीमन के अलग से एक आयोग यानी कमीशन का गठन किया जाता है. इस आयोग का नेतृत्व सुप्रीम कोर्ट के किसी रिटायर्ड जज करते हैं. इसके अलावा इस आयोग में मुख्य चुनाव आयुक्त, उनके प्रतिनिधि और राज्यों के चुनाव आयुक्त भी शामिल होते हैं.
जवाब: परिसीमन बिल के जरिए लोकसभा में अधिकतम सदस्य संख्या बढ़ाना चाहती है. साथ ही राज्यों को प्रतिनिधित्व को फिर से तय करना चाहती है.
जवाब: अप्रैल 2026 में पेश संविधान (131वां संशोधन) विधेयक में लोकसभा की अधिकतम सदस्य संख्या 850 करने का प्रस्ताव था. यह मौजूदा 543 सीटों से काफी ज्यादा है, लेकिन 850 सीटों का प्रस्ताव कानून नहीं बना है.
जवाब: लोकसभा और विधानसभा के परिसीमन से राज्यसभा की सीटों का बंटवारा अपने आप नहीं बदलता. राज्यसभा में राज्यों को मिलने वाली सीटें अलग संवैधानिक व्यवस्था के तहत तय होती हैं.
जवाब: अगर वर्तमान संवैधानिक व्यवस्था को देखें, तो 2026 के बाद होने वाली पहली जनगणना के आंकड़े के आधार पर परिसीमन का रास्ता खुलेगा. हालांकि, अप्रैल 2026 में सरकार ने जो प्रस्ताव पेश किया था, उसमें 2011 में हुई जनगणना के आधार पर परिसीमन की बात थी.
जवाब: 2023 में संसद ने महिलाओं को लोकसभा और विधानसभा में 33 प्रतिशत आरक्षण देने का कानून बनाया था, लेकिन इसे लागू करने की प्रक्रिया जनगणना और परिसीमन से जुड़ी हुई है. यानी परिसीमन पूरा होने के बाद ही महिला आरक्षण लागू करने का रास्ता खुलेगा.
जवाब: परिसीमन को लेकर उत्तर और दक्षिण में विवाद की असली वजह आबादी है. उत्तर भारत के कई राज्यों की आबादी तेजी से बढ़ी है, जबकि दक्षिण भारत के राज्यों ने जनसंख्या नियंत्रण में बेहतर काम किया है. अब डर यह है कि अगर सीटों का बंटवारा आबादी के हिसाब से हुआ तो उत्तर भारत को ज्यादा सीटें मिल सकती हैं और दक्षिण भारत की संसद में हिस्सेदारी कम हो सकती है.
जवाब: यह जरूरी नहीं है कि परिसीमन के बाद हर राज्य की सीटों में इजाफा ही हो. यह इस बात पर निर्भर करेगा कि सीटों के बंटवारे का कौन सा फॉर्मूला अपनाया जाता है. कुछ राज्यों की सीटें ज्यादा बढ़ सकती हैं, कुछ की कम और कुछ राज्यों की कुल हिस्सेदारी कम भी हो सकती है.
जवाब: सरकार ने अप्रैल 2026 में संविधान संशोधन बिल पेश किया था, लेकिन लोकसभा में इसे जरूरी दो-तिहाई बहुमत नहीं मिला. इसलिए यह बिल पास नहीं हो सका. अब केंद्र सरकार इसको फिर से ला सकती है.
जवाब: आजादी के बाद से अब तक देश में चार बार परिसीमन आयोग बनाया गया है. पहला 1952 में, दूसरा 1963 में, तीसरा 1973 में और चौथा 2002 में बनाया गया था.
जवाब: भारत में आखिरी बार बड़ा परिसीमन 2002 में बने आयोग ने किया था. यह परिसीमन 2001 में हुई जनगणना के आधार पर किया गया था. इस आयोग के आदेश साल 2008 से देशभर में लागू हुए थे. इस परिसीमन के दौरान विधानसभा क्षेत्रों में बदलाव हुआ था. हालांकि, लोकसभा सीटों में कोई बदलाव नहीं हुआ था.
जवाब: 1976 में सरकार ने संविधान में बदलाव करके लोकसभा में राज्यों की सीटों का बंटवारा 1971 की जनगणना के आधार पर स्थिर कर दिया गया था. बाद में इसे बढ़ाकर यह तय किया गया कि 2026 के बाद होने वाली पहली जनगणना के आंकड़े सामने आने के बाद तक के लिए स्थिर कर दिया गया था. यही वजह है कि राज्यों के बीच सीटों के बंटवारे में अब तक 1971 के आंकड़े ही आधार बने हुए हैं.
जवाब: हां, परिसीमन आयोग बनाने और उसे अधिकार देने के लिए संसद कानून बनाती है. अगर संविधान में बदलाव करना जरूरी हो, तो उसके लिए संसद में एक खास बहुमत चाहिए होता है.
जवाब: नहीं, परिसीमन आयोग के आदेशों को अदालत में चैलेंज नहीं किया जा सकता. संविधान की धारा 329(a) में यह प्रावधान है. हालांकि, ऐसा भी नहीं है कि हर तरह के संवैधानिक विवाद पर अदालत का रास्ता पूरी तरह बंद नहीं हो जाता. कुछ विशेष परिस्थितियों में अदालत में भी चैलेंज किया जा सकता है.
जवाब: हां, अगर परिसीमन का आधार आबादी तय की जाती है, तो फिर इन राज्यों को निश्चित तौर पर फायदा मिलेगा. हालांकि, इस बारे में अभी कुछ भी कहना मुश्किल है, इसके लिए अंतिम फॉर्मूला और परिसीमन आयोग का फैसला जरूरी होगा.
जवाब: इन राज्यों की समस्या आबादी है, क्योंकि इन राज्यों ने जनसंख्या नियंत्रण पर अच्छा काम किया है. ऐसे में अगर परिसीमन आबादी को आधार बनाकर किया जाता है.
जवाब: अगर लोकसभा की सभी 850 सीटें भरी हुई हैं तो बहुमत के लिए कम से कम 426 सांसदों का समर्थन चाहिए होगा. अभी 543 सीटों वाली लोकसभा में बहुमत का आंकड़ा 272 है.
जवाब: किसी राज्य के पास ज्यादा सांसद होने से ज्यादा पैसा मिलने को सीधे तौर पर हां नहीं कहा जा सकता. लेकिन केंद्र से मिलने वाला पैसा केवल लोकसभा सीटों की संख्या के आधार पर तय नहीं होता. इसमें वित्त आयोग और दूसरी सरकारी योजनाओं के नियम भी लागू होते हैं.
महिला आरक्षण कानून के तहत लोकसभा और विधानसभा में करीब एक-तिहाई सीटें महिलाओं के लिए आरक्षित होंगी, लेकिन यह आरक्षण परिसीमन के बाद लागू होगा. किन सीटों को महिलाओं के लिए आरक्षित किया जाएगा, यह तय करने के लिए अलग प्रक्रिया होगी.
जवाब: यह इस बात पर निर्भर करेगा कि जनगणना के आंकड़े कब तक आते हैं और परिसीमन की प्रक्रिया कब पूरी होती है. अप्रैल 2026 में सरकार ने 2029 के चुनाव से पहले बदलाव की तैयारी के तहत प्रस्ताव पेश किया था, लेकिन विधेयक पास नहीं हो सका. इसलिए नए परिसीमन के आधार पर 2029 का चुनाव होना अभी तय नहीं है.

title: क्या सरकार ने साध लिया दो-तिहाई बहुमत का गणित? परिसीमन बिल पास करवाने में कौन-से विपक्षी दल आए साथ
description: क्या मोदी सरकार ने परिसीमन पर संविधान संशोधन बिल पास करवाने के लिए संसद में संख्याबल का जुगाड़ कर लिया है? जिस तरह से उसने अचानक एक दिन का संसद सत्र बुलाया है, वह इसी ओर इशारा कर रहा है.
author: देवेंद्र कुमार
content:
मोदी सरकार ने अगले संसद का एक दिन का स्पेशल सेशन बुलाया है. अचानक बुलाए गए इस सेशन से कई सवाल खड़े हो गए हैं. पहला सवाल ये है कि क्या अगले एक हफ्ते में परिसीमन बिल पास हो जाएगा. दूसरा सवाल ये है कि क्या महिलाओं को संसदीय चुनाव में आरक्षण का संवैधानिक अधिकार मिल जाएगा? क्या इसके लिए संविधान संशोधन आसानी से हो पाएगा.
असल में हमारे देश के संविधान में काल और परिस्थिति के हिसाब से संशोधन के विकल्प मौजूद हैं. अब तक संविधान में 106 बार संशोधन हो चुका है और अब 107वीं बार संशोधन करके उसमें नए प्रावधान जोड़ने की तैयारी है.
केंद्र सरकार ने दोनों सदनों के स्पीकर से लोकसभा और राज्यसभा की बैठक दोबारा बुलाने का अनुरोध किया है. पिछले 105 दिनों से संसद का मानसून सत्र स्थगित है. संसदीय कार्य मंत्री किरेन रिजिजू ने कहा कि उन्होंने लोकसभा अध्यक्ष और राज्यसभा के सभापति से संसद का मानसून सत्र की विशेष बैठक बुलाने का आग्रह किया है.
