जिस तरह कैबिनेट की बैठक में प्रधानमंत्री नरेंद्र मोदी ने अपने मंत्रिमंडल के सहयोगियों को निर्देश दिए थे, उसके बाद से ही चर्चा थी कि परिसीमन के लिए संविधान संशोधन विधेयक पास कराने के मकसद से सरकार संसद का सत्र बुला सकती है.
सवाल है, जब सरकार के पास दो-तिहाई बहुमत नहीं है और 25 दिन पहले ही दिल्ली में विपक्ष ने बाकायदा एकजुटता का सार्वजनिक प्रदर्शन भी किया था, तो ऐसी स्थिति में केंद्र सरकार दो-तिहाई बहुमत का आंकड़ा कैसे हासिल कर पाएगी? आज हम इसी सवाल को डिकोड करेंगे.
प्रसिद्ध अमेरिकी इतिहासकार और राजनीतिक विचारक हेनरी एडम्स का मानना था कि 'व्यावहारिक राजनीति में नफरत को अनदेखा करने की कला भी शामिल है..यहां सब कुछ केवल संख्याओं को जोड़ने और विरोधियों को घटाने का खेल है.' यही लोकतांत्रिक राजनीति की सच्चाई है.
इसी सच्चाई को आधार बनाकर इस बार संसद में सरकार परिसीमन और महिला आरक्षण को लेकर संविधान संशोधन बिल पास कराने की तैयारी में है. सूत्रों के मुताबिक संसद के मानसून सत्र की विशेष बैठक में संविधान संशोधन विधेयक पेश किया जा सकता है.
लोकसभा अध्यक्ष और राज्यसभा के सभापति को दिए प्रस्ताव में 3 तारीखों का जिक्र है. लोकसभा का सत्र 30 नवंबर को और राज्यसभा का सत्र 2 दिसंबर को बुलाया जाएगा और 3 दिसंबर को ये सत्र खत्म हो सकता है. किरेन रिजिजू का कहना है कि यह सत्र मुख्य रूप से आवश्यक सरकारी कामकाज को पूरा करने के लिए बुलाया जा रहा है. सूत्रों के मुताबिक इस विशेष सत्र में परिसिमन बिल पेश किया जाएगा.
मानसून सत्र की इस विशेष बैठक से पहले कल केंद्रीय मंत्रिमंडल की बैठक होगी. सूत्रों का कहना है कि इसमें परिसीमन बिल और महिला आरक्षण से जुड़े संविधान संशोधन विधेयक पर चर्चा होगी. इससे पहले, बुधवार को हुई कैबिनेट की बैठक में भी इसके संकेत दिए गए थे.
सूत्रों के मुताबिक, प्रधानमंत्री नरेंद्र मोदी ने अपने मंत्रिमंडल के सहयोगियों से कहा है कि वे संसद के अगले सत्र की तैयारियां 15 दिसंबर से पहले पूरी कर लें. उन्होंने मंत्रियों को सलाह दी है कि वे सत्र से पहले विदेश यात्रा करने से बचें और दिल्ली में मौजूद रहें.
इससे साफ संकेत मिल रहे हैं कि 30 नवंबर को बुलाए गए विशेष सत्र में परिसीमन विधेयक पेश किया जा सकता है. परिसीमन बिल पास होने के बाद ही संसदीय चुनावों में महिला आरक्षण लागू होने का रास्ता साफ होगा. सबसे पहले आपको यह जानना चाहिए कि महिला आरक्षण कानून लागू करने के लिहाज से ये विशेष सत्र क्यों महत्वपूर्ण है?
महिला आरक्षण कानून बनने के बावजूद यह लागू नहीं हो सका है क्योंकि इसके लिए लोकसभा की सीटें 543 से बढ़ाकर 850 तक करनी हैं. संविधान में लोकसभा की सीटें बढ़ाने और नई जनगणना से पहले परिसीमन करने पर रोक है, जिसे बदलने के लिए संविधान संशोधन जरूरी है.
महिला आरक्षण कानून में एक शर्त यह भी है कि अगली जनगणना के बाद परिसीमन होगा. संविधान संशोधन करके इस शर्त को हटाना है. संविधान संशोधन पास होने के बाद सरकार 'परिसीमन बिल' लाएगी, जिसमें यह प्रावधान होगा कि आयोग के गठन के समय उपलब्ध आखिरी प्रकाशित जनगणना यानी 2011 की जनगणना के आधार पर ही सीटों का बंटवारा कर दिया जाए.
बिल पास होते ही केंद्र सरकार सुप्रीम कोर्ट के एक जज की अध्यक्षता में 'परिसीमन आयोग' बनाएगी. यह आयोग अगले डेढ़ से दो साल में देश भर में 850 लोकसभा सीटों और राज्यों की विधानसभा सीटों की सीमाएं तय करेगा. उनमें से एक-तिहाई सीटें महिलाओं के लिए आरक्षित होंगी. इसलिए सरकार संविधान संशोधन, परिसीमन और केंद्रशासित प्रदेश संशोधन विधेयक एक साथ संसद के मानसून सत्र की बिशेष बैठक में पेश कर सकती है.
संविधान संशोधन विधेयक पास करवाने के लिए सरकार को दो-तिहाई बहुमत की आवश्यकता होगी. इस समय लोकसभा में 543 में से 540 सांसद हैं. तीन सीटें खाली हैं, क्योंकि दो सदस्यों का निधन हो चुका है और एक सदस्य ने इस्तीफा दे दिया है. इस तरह सरकार को मानसून सत्र की विशेष बैठक में संविधान संशोधन विधेयक पास कराने के लिए कम से कम 360 सदस्यों का समर्थन चाहिए.
लोकसभा में बीजेपी के 241 सांसद हैं. दूसरे नंबर पर NCPI है, जो तृणमूल कांग्रेस से टूटकर बनी है. उसके 20 सांसद हैं. टीडीपी के 16, शिवसेना के 13 और जेडीयू के 12 सदस्य हैं. इसके अलावा छोटी पार्टियों और दो दिन पहले एनडीए में शामिल हुए अकाली दल को मिलाकर सरकार के पक्ष में 320 सांसद होते हैं.
मतलब, सरकार को संविधान संशोधन विधेयक पास कराने के लिए कम से कम 40 और सदस्यों के समर्थन की जरूरत है. इसी साल बजट सत्र में सरकार ने संविधान संशोधन विधेयक पेश किया था लेकिन तब विधेयक के पक्ष में 298 वोट ही पड़े थे. हालांकि जगनमोहन रेड्डी की पार्टी YSR कांग्रेस के 4 सांसद हैं जो संविधान संशोधन विधेयक पर एनडीए के साथ हैं. तृणमूल कांग्रेस टूटकर बनी पार्टी के 20 सांसद एनडीए के साथ आ गए हैं. सात महीने में संसद का समीकरण बदल गया है.
अब सरकार संशोधन विधेयक पास कराने को लेकर आश्वस्त है. इसकी वजह यह है कि 324 सांसदों का समर्थन पहले से एनडीए के पास है. अब शरद पवार की पार्टी एनसीपी ने भी समर्थन के संकेत दिए हैं. प्रिया सुले ने कहा है कि राष्ट्रहित में होने पर एनसीपी सरकार के साथ खड़ी हो सकती है.
अगर शरद पवार की पार्टी संविधान संशोधन विधेयक पर सरकार के साथ आ गई, तो फिर 32 सांसदों के समर्थन की जरूरत होगी. सरकार की नजर डीएमके पर है क्योंकि डीएमके इंडिया गठबंधन से पूरी तरह अलग है.
डीएमके के 20 सांसद हैं. सरकार को विश्वास है कि उनका समर्थन मिल जाएगा. ऐसे में सरकार के पास यह आंकड़ा 352 तक पहुंच जाएगा. फिर भी 8 सदस्यों के समर्थन की आवश्यकता होगी. ऐसे में सरकार की नजर झारखंड मुक्ति मोर्चा के 3, आम आदमी पार्टी के 3 और नेशनल कॉन्फ्रेंस के 2 सांसदों पर है.
अगर झारखंड मुक्ति मोर्चा, आम आदमी पार्टी और नेशनल कॉन्फ्रेंस सरकार को समर्थन दे देती हैं, तो संशोधन विधेयक आसानी से पास हो जाएगा. अगर ये पार्टियां समर्थन देने के बजाय वोटिंग के समय अनुपस्थित रहती हैं, तो फिर 355 सदस्यों के समर्थन की जरूरत होगी. सरकार को विश्वास है कि वह यह आंकड़ा भी जुटा लेगी. इसलिए बीजेपी आश्वस्त है, लेकिन इंडिया गठबंधन के नेता अपने सहयोगियों से कह रहे हैं कि वे सरकार की साजिश का शिकार न हों.
संविधान संशोधन विधेयक को सिर्फ लोकसभा में ही नहीं, बल्कि राज्यसभा में भी पास करना होगा. वहां सरकार को 164 सांसदों का समर्थन चाहिए, जबकि एनडीए के पास 158 सदस्य हैं. ऐसे में 6 सांसदों की कमी रहेगी. सरकार इस कमी को या तो विपक्ष के 6 सांसदों के समर्थन से पूरा करेगी या फिर अगर वोटिंग के समय 12 सांसद अनुपस्थित रह जाते हैं, तो सरकार संविधान संशोधन विधेयक पास करा लेगी.
साफ है कि पूरा खेल नंबरों का है. सरकार ने जिस तरह से मानसून सत्र की विशेष बैठक बुलाई है, प्रधानमंत्री मोदी ने जिस तरह सांसदों को तैयार रहने के लिए कहा है उससे स्पष्ट है कि सरकार बहुमत के आंकड़े के करीब है.

title: उत्तर भारत में कड़ाके की ठंड ने दी दस्तक, गिरेगा पारा, दक्षिण में बारिश का जोर; जानें अगले 3 दिन कैसा रहेगा मौसम
description: उत्तर भारत में अगले तीन दिन जहां सुबह के समय ठंडी हवाएं महसूस होंगी. वहीं रात में काफी ठंड लगेगी. जबकि दक्षिण भारत में बारिश तेज होने जा रही है.
author: देवेंद्र कुमार
content:
दिल्ली-एनसीआर समेत पूरा उत्तर भारत जहां प्रदूषण और बढ़ती ठंड को झेल रहा है.हिमालय की ऊंची पहाड़ियों से चल रही ठंडी और सूखी उत्तर-पश्चिमी हवाओं के चलते मैदानी इलाकों में पारा लगातार गिर रहा है. उपग्रह से मिली तस्वीरों में पूरा उत्तर-पश्चिम भारत ज्यादातर साफ और बादलों से मुक्त नजर आ रहा है. वहीं दक्षिण भारत में बारिश के आसार बन रहे हैं.
उत्तर-पश्चिम भारत में फिलहाल किसी नए पश्चिमी विक्षोभ का असर नहीं दिख रहा है. हिमालय की ऊंची पहाड़ियों से चल रही ठंडी और सूखी उत्तर-पश्चिमी हवाओं के चलते मैदानी इलाकों में पारा लगातार गिर रहा है. उपग्रह से मिली तस्वीरों में पूरा उत्तर-पश्चिम भारत ज्यादातर साफ और बादलों से मुक्त नजर आ रहा है.
भारतीय मौसम विज्ञान विभाग के वैज्ञानिक डॉ. नरेश ने बताया कि दिल्ली और आसपास के इलाकों में अगले तीन दिन न्यूनतम तापमान 9 डिग्री सेल्सियस से 12 डिग्री सेल्सियस के बीच रह सकता है. इस दौरान अधिकतम तापमान 24 डिग्री सेल्सियस से 26 डिग्री सेल्सियस के आसपास रहने का अनुमान है. यह इस मौसम के सामान्य स्तर के करीब होगा. इस पूरे हफ्ते मौसम इसी तरह का बना रहने की उम्मीद है.
उन्होंने बताया कि दिन में आसमान साफ रहेगा, मगर सुबह के वक्त हल्के से मध्यम स्तर का कोहरा छा सकता है. कहीं पर यह कोहरा घना भी हो सकता है.
पंजाब, हरियाणा और पश्चिमी उत्तर प्रदेश के कुछ इलाकों में अगले दो से तीन दिन सुबह के समय घने कोहरे की स्थिति बन सकती है. इसे देखते हुए मौसम विभाग ने येलो अलर्ट जारी किया है. सुबह दृश्यता कम होने से वाहन चालकों को संभलकर चलने को कहा गया है.
वैज्ञानिक डॉ. नरेश ने बताया कि आने वाले दिनों में कोई वेस्टर्न डिस्टरबेंस नहीं है, जो नॉर्थ वेस्ट इंडिया पर प्रभाव डाले. फिलहाल हिमालय से आ रही हवाओं का रुख सामान्य है, जिससे दिल्ली-एनसीआर में तापमान 10 से 12 डिग्री के बीच रहेगा.
राजस्थान की बात करें तो वहां के कुछ हिस्सों में कोल्ड वेव कंडीशन जैसी स्थिति है. राज्य के कई हिस्सों में तापमान 10 डिग्री से कम है. पूर्वी राजस्थान के कुछ हिस्सों में अगले 48 से 72 घंटों तक शीत लहर चल सकती है. मौसम विभाग ने किसानों को फसलों को ठंड से बचाने के लिए हल्की सिंचाई करने की सलाह दी है.
उत्तर भारत में जहां सर्दी बढ़ रही है, वहीं पूर्वी हवाओं के असर से दक्षिण भारत में बारिश की गतिविधियां तेज हैं. तमिलनाडु, पुडुचेरी, कराईकल और केरल में अगले दो से तीन दिनों में कई जगह मध्यम से भारी बारिश होने के आसार जताए गए हैं.
मौसम वैज्ञानिकों का अनुमान है कि दक्षिण अंडमान सागर के ऊपर एक नया चक्रवातीय परिसंचरण बन सकता है. अगर ऐसा हुआ तो अंडमान और निकोबार द्वीप समूह में 29 नवंबर से बारिश और तेज हो सकती है.
(तान्या चुग का इनपुट)

title: Shraddha Walkar Murder Case: Delhi Court Reschedules Evidence Recording as Aaftab Poonawala Seeks Exam Leave
description: Delhi's Saket Court postpones evidence recording in the Shraddha Walkar murder case to December 1 after Aaftab Poonawala seeks time for his IGNOU examinations.
author: Asian News International
content:
Shraddha Walkar Murder Case: Delhi Court Reschedules Evidence Recording as Aaftab Poonawala Seeks Exam Leave
A Delhi court has rescheduled the recording of prosecution evidence in the Shraddha Walkar murder case to December 1 after accused Aaftab Amin Poonawala sought an adjournment to appear for his IGNOU examinations scheduled between November 26 and December 17.
- India News
- 3 min read
New Delhi: Saket District Court on Thursday rescheduled the date of recording of Prosecution evidence in the Shraddha Walkar murder case in view of the educational examination of accused Aaftab Amin Poonawala. He is pursuing a course of Indira Gandhi National Open University (IGNOU). He has to appear for an examination situated at Tihar Jail complex.
The accused appeared before the court through video conferencing before the scheduled time and prayed for cancellation of today's date.
Additional Sessions Judge (ASJ) Hargurvarinder Singh Jaggi, after hearing the request of the accused, adjourned the recording of evidence for December 1, 2026.
Accused Aaftab Amin Poonawala submitted that he learnt about his exams following his last hearing on November 19. The exams are scheduled from November 26 to December 17.
Advertisement
He further submitted that all the exam slots are in the evening slot, 02:00 P.M. to 05:00 P.M. He prayed that today's date may be adjourned to a convenient date as per the directions of the Court.
Special Public Prosecutor (SPP) Madhukar Pandey was informed about the early appearance of accused Aaftab Amin Poonawala. He was also briefed on the delay in transmitting Poonawala's November 19 request letter, which prison authorities forwarded on November 26 via a cover letter received at 12:18 pm.
Advertisement
Earlier, Tihar Jail authorities filed a status report on the safety and security of accused Aaftab Amin Poonawala, who is in judicial custody in connection with the case.
This report was called by the Saket District Court on November 6 after the accused informed the court that not all five inmates who threatened him had been shifted; three are still there in the same security cell. Thereafter, the report was called. The court had directed the Jail authorities to ensure the safety and security of Aaftab Amin Poonawala in Jail Number 4 in Central Jail Tihar.
Additional Sessions Judge (ASJ) Hargurvarinder Singh Jaggi took the report on record and listed the matter for hearing on further directions on the status report and safety of Aaftab Amin Poonawala on November 26. Accused Aftab Amin Poonawala was produced through video conference from Tihar Jail in police security.
On November 4, Aaftab Amin Poonawala had alleged death threats and threats of bodily harm by jail inmates in Tihar Jail.
In view of the allegations, the Saket District Court had directed the Jail Authorities to ensure his safety and security and to change his ward or cell if required. The court also called for a status report from the concerned jail superintendent.
During the hearing on November 2, the accused had submitted that presently he is lodged in Jail No. 4A, Tihar Jail, Delhi, which is a special cell, but it also happens to be the punishment ward. The accused further submitted that for the past 10 days, few of the inmates have repeatedly imparted death threats to cause bodily harm to him that they will slash his face with improvised weapons, sua.
The accused had expressed his concerns about his safety and security within the prison. He also gave the names of 5 inmates who are imparting death threats to him. The court redacted the names of those inmates for the safety of the accused, Aaftab.
After hearing the submissions, the court directed the concerned Jail Superintendent to take immediate steps to ensure the safety and security of the accused.

title: Kharge Takes a Dig at Imran Masood, Urges Congress Leaders to Focus on Action Amid SP Seat-Sharing Row Ahead of Polls
description: Mallikarjun Kharge tells Congress MP Imran Masood to focus on action, not words, amid the Congress-SP seat-sharing dispute ahead of the 2027 Uttar Pradesh Assembly elections.
author: Melvin Narayan
content:
Kharge Takes a Dig at Imran Masood, Urges Congress Leaders to Focus on Action Amid SP Seat-Sharing Row Ahead of Polls
Congress chief Mallikarjun Kharge took a dig at MP Imran Masood, urging him to focus on action rather than words amid tensions with the Samajwadi Party over seat-sharing for the 2027 UP Assembly elections. Kharge also called for party unity to take on the BJP in Uttar Pradesh.
- India News
- 4 min read
New Delhi: Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge on Thursday issued a pointed message to party MP Imran Masood amid the growing differences between the Congress and the Samajwadi Party (SP) over seat-sharing arrangements for the 2027 Uttar Pradesh Assembly elections. Urging Masood to focus on action rather than statements, Kharge stressed the importance of collective efforts and unity within the party.
Speaking at a party event in Lucknow, Kharge mentioned Masood by name while referring to his frequent television appearances and outspoken remarks.
"Imran Masood, whom I frequently hear on television, where he often speaks with great passion. However, we must focus on action rather than just words; the more we work together, the further we will progress," Kharge said.
The Congress chief also acknowledged Masood's work in Parliament, saying that the Saharanpur MP consistently raises issues on behalf of the party and works to ensure that its position is firmly represented.
Advertisement
In another part of his address, Kharge cautioned party leaders against arrogance and internal differences, emphasising that unity would be crucial to the party's electoral prospects in Uttar Pradesh.
"The target is to defeat Yogi and Modi, and for that we must stay united. We must strive forward. We must shed arrogance," he said.
Advertisement
Kharge also warned that internal discord could make electoral victory difficult, urging party workers to remain cautious about divisions within their own ranks.
What Triggered Kharge's Remarks?
Kharge's comments come amid an escalating disagreement between the Congress and the SP over seat-sharing negotiations ahead of the 2027 Uttar Pradesh Assembly elections.
The two parties, which are allies in the INDIA bloc, have yet to arrive at a mutually acceptable seat-sharing arrangement. The Congress is understood to have sought around 130 seats out of the 403 Assembly constituencies, while the SP has reportedly offered 26 constituencies as an initial arrangement.
Tensions intensified after the Akhilesh Yadav-led SP announced its first list of five candidates on Tuesday while discussions with the Congress were still underway.
The announcement particularly upset Masood as the SP named candidates for Behat and Saharanpur, two Assembly constituencies falling within his Saharanpur Lok Sabha constituency.
Reacting to the development, Masood questioned the SP's approach and said that an alliance could not function if one partner unilaterally announced candidates and subsequently decided which seats would be left for the other.
"What else should I say? You (SP) release the list. Then you leave the seats. Are we alliance partners or your servants? Did we ask you to leave these seats for us?" Masood said.
He further maintained that the Congress was not seeking seats as a favour and insisted that alliance partners should be treated equally.
Masood also recalled that the Congress had contested 107 Assembly seats when Akhilesh Yadav was the Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister, questioning the SP's current approach to negotiations.
Akhilesh Yadav Seeks To Ease Tensions
Meanwhile, SP chief Akhilesh Yadav has attempted to ease the growing friction between the two parties by asking the Congress to look beyond the 26 constituencies initially discussed and identify additional seats where it believes it has a strong chance of winning.
Yadav has maintained that the seat-sharing arrangement should focus on the winnability of candidates and mutual consensus rather than a rigid division of constituencies.
However, Masood's repeated criticism of the SP has brought the differences between the INDIA bloc allies into the spotlight, even as negotiations continue.
The latest remarks from Kharge are being seen as a message to Congress leaders to avoid public confrontations with alliance partners and concentrate on strengthening the party's organisational position ahead of the crucial Uttar Pradesh elections.

title: In a First, Vijay Govt Announces 15-Day Paternity Leave for Male Govt Employees in Tamil Nadu
description: Tamil Nadu Chief Minister C Joseph Vijay has announced 15 days of paternity leave for married male government employees for the first time in the state. Employees can avail the leave 15 days before the expected delivery date or within six months after the child's birth.
author: Melvin Narayan
content:
In a First, Vijay Govt Announces 15-Day Paternity Leave for Male Govt Employees in Tamil Nadu
Tamil Nadu Chief Minister C Joseph Vijay has announced 15 days of paternity leave for married male government employees for the first time in the state. Employees can avail the leave 15 days before the expected delivery date or within six months after the child's birth.
- India News
- 2 min read
New Delhi: Tamil Nadu Chief Minister C Joseph Vijay on Thursday announced 15 days of paternity leave for married male government employees, introducing the provision for the first time in the state.
Under the new provision, male employees working in the Tamil Nadu government will be entitled to 15 days of paternity leave during their wives' maternity period. The leave can be availed either 15 days before the expected date of childbirth or within six months from the date of the child's birth.
The state government's announcement aims to enable fathers to support their wives during childbirth and participate in the early care of their newborn children.
According to the government order, the decision was taken after representations were received from government employees seeking the introduction of paternity leave for male staff.
Advertisement
The government said the period surrounding childbirth is important for both the mother and the child. It emphasised that fathers have an essential role in providing physical and emotional support to mothers while also sharing responsibilities related to childcare.
The official statement noted that the state already provides 365 days of maternity leave to women government employees. Extending a similar provision to male employees, it said, would encourage shared family responsibilities and strengthen the father's involvement in bringing up a child.
Advertisement
The newly announced provision will apply to married male government employees, who can choose when to utilise the 15-day leave within the specified period.
With this decision, Tamil Nadu joins states that have introduced paternity leave provisions for their government employees. The move marks a change in the state's leave policy by formally recognising the role of fathers during childbirth and the initial months of a child's life.

title: 'Zero tolerance for terrorism': India pays tribute to 26/11 victims
description: On the 18th anniversary of the Mumbai terror attacks, India, France, the US and Argentina remember the 166 lives lost and reaffirm their commitment to fighting terrorism.
author: FP News Desk
content:
'Zero tolerance for terrorism': India pays tribute to 26/11 victims
On the 18th anniversary of the Mumbai terror attacks, India, France, the US and Argentina remember the 166 lives lost and reaffirm their commitment to fighting terrorism.
External Affairs Minister S Jaishankar on Thursday paid tribute to the victims of the 26/11 Mumbai terror attacks, remembering the innocent lives lost and saluting the security personnel who laid down their lives in the line of duty.
Marking 18 years since the devastating attacks, Jaishankar reiterated India's commitment to combating terrorism in all its forms and bringing those responsible to justice.
“Remember innocent lives lost and salute the brave security personnel who made the supreme sacrifice during 26/11 Mumbai terror attacks. Committed to combating terrorism in all its forms and manifestations and bringing those involved to justice. Zero tolerance for terrorism,” he said in a post on X.
France expresses solidarity
The Indian Embassy in France also paid homage to the victims, including two French citizens who lost their lives in the attacks.
Recalling French President Emmanuel Macron and First Lady Brigitte Macron's visit to India in February, the Embassy highlighted their visit to the 26/11 memorial at the Taj Mahal Palace Hotel in Mumbai.
In a post on X, France had reaffirmed its solidarity with India in the fight against terrorism.
“Today marks 18 years of the horrific 26/11 Mumbai Attacks. We remember its victims, which included two French citizens. President Emmanuel Macron honoured their memory on his India visit and reaffirmed France's solidarity. France and India stand united against terrorism,” the Embassy said.
US backs India's anti-terror fight
US Ambassador to India Sergio Gor also paid tribute to the victims, remembering the 166 people killed, including six American citizens, and honouring the courage of India's security forces.
Gor recalled his visit to the memorial at the Taj Mahal Palace Hotel earlier this year alongside US Secretary of State Marco Rubio.
Reaffirming Washington's support for New Delhi, he emphasised the importance of cooperation between the two countries' law enforcement agencies in ensuring that those responsible for terrorism are brought to justice.
“The United States stands with India in the fight against terrorism, and our law enforcement partnership remains vital to bringing terrorists to justice,” Gor said in his message.
Argentina stands with India
Argentina's Ambassador to India, Mariano Caucino, also expressed solidarity with the Indian government and people on the 18th anniversary of the attacks.
Paying tribute to those who lost their lives in the 26 November 2008 assault, Caucino reiterated Argentina's opposition to terrorism.
“On the 18th anniversary of the 26/11 Mumbai terror attacks on Nov 26, 2008, our thoughts are with the Indian Government and Indian people, honouring the innocent lives lost in that heinous atrocity,” he said.
Concluding his message, the Ambassador reaffirmed Argentina's support, stating: “Always with Life and Against Terror – Argentina stands with India.”
Meanwhile, the Mumbai Police also paid tribute to the security personnel who made the supreme sacrifice during the attacks.
“Their courage stood tall in the face of terror. Their valour became a part of Mumbai's history. We remember and pay our deepest respects to all the bravehearts who made the supreme sacrifice for our city,” the Mumbai Police said in a social media post.
The Taj Mahal Palace Hotel also commemorated the anniversary by sharing a video on Instagram, remembering the resilience, courage and unity displayed by the city in the aftermath of the attacks.
"There are moments that become part of who we are. They remind us of the courage found in the face of adversity, the kindness that brings us together, and the strength of a city that has always found its way forward.Today, we remember with gratitude, honour with humility, and carry forward the values that unite us," they said.
Four days of terror
The 26/11 attacks remain one of the darkest chapters in India's history. On the night of 26 November 2008, 10 terrorists belonging to the Pakistan-based Lashkar-e-Taiba (LeT) entered Mumbai by sea and launched a series of coordinated attacks across the city.
Over four days, the assault claimed 166 lives and left around 300 people injured, sending shockwaves across India and the world.
Among the prominent targets were the Taj Mahal Palace Hotel, the Oberoi-Trident Hotel, Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj Terminus (CSMT), Nariman House, Cama Hospital, Metro Cinema and Leopold Cafe. Several of these locations were frequented by foreign nationals and residents of Mumbai.
A memory that endures
Eighteen years on, the scars of the attacks remain visible across Mumbai. Bullet marks at Leopold Cafe and Nariman House continue to serve as reminders of the violence, while memorials honour those who lost their lives.
The sacrifice of Assistant Sub-Inspector Tukaram Omble, who was killed while helping capture the lone surviving terrorist, Mohammad Ajmal Amir Kasab, remains a defining example of courage and duty.
Nine of the 10 attackers were killed during the security operation, while Kasab was captured alive. He was sentenced to death in May 2010 and hanged at Yerawada Central Jail in Pune on 21 November 2012.

title: How safe is bottled water? How chemicals in Bisleri put the $4 billion industry in the spotlight
description: Bisleri is in hot water after a sample was found to contain carcinogenic chemicals, bromate and PAHs, above the prescribed limit, prompting India’s food safety regulator to sanction prosecution. The findings have also put the entire packaged water industry under scrutiny, with the FSSAI warning of more tests of all brands
author: FP Explainers
content:
How safe is bottled water? How chemicals in Bisleri put the $4 billion industry in the spotlight
Bisleri is in hot water after a sample was found to contain carcinogenic chemicals, bromate and PAHs, above the prescribed limit, prompting India’s food safety regulator to sanction prosecution. The findings have also put the entire packaged water industry under scrutiny, with the FSSAI warning of more tests of all brands
When one thinks Bisleri, one thinks of pure water.
However, that notion is facing a huge cloud of suspicion after the Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (FSSAI) sanctioned prosecution against the packaged drinking water brand over an ‘unsafe’ sample.
This finding isn’t just a problem for Bisleri International but also for the country’s $4 billion packaged drinking water industry. We explain why.
Why is Bisleri facing prosecution?
On Sunday (November 22), India’s food safety regulator sanctioned prosecution against packaged drinking water manufacturer Bisleri International Pvt Ltd after a sample collected from its premises was found unsafe.
According to the FSSAI, the sample of water was found to be non-compliant with prescribed bromate limits and was declared unsafe under the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006. After the company appealed, the sample was sent to a referral laboratory. FSSAI said the laboratory also declared it unsafe after detecting polynuclear aromatic hydrocarbons (PAHs).
For those who don’t know, bromate and PAHs are both carcinogens, meaning they can cause or increase the risk of cancer.
How did Bisleri respond to FSSAI’s findings?
As Bisleri found itself in hot water, the brand issued a statement on Monday (November 23), maintaining that its water is “safe for consumption”.
It explained that the matter pertained to a sample taken from a batch in September 2025 from its Goa plant, one among its 143. The company added that FSSAI drew six samples there on 30 September 2025. Five passed all checks, while the sixth showed bromate at 12 microgrammes per litre, above the permitted 10.
Bisleri said it appealed in November 2025, and FSSAI sent the sample to a referral laboratory. That lab found bromate within the limit but flagged polynuclear aromatic hydrocarbons (PAHs). The mismatch, Bisleri said, “raised questions that Bisleri believed warranted clarification.”
The company adds in its statement that it then had the same sample tested at an FSSAI-approved lab, which also found bromate within the limit. Bisleri sent those results to FSSAI’s Western Regional Office in February this year.
Bisleri adds that its submissions were met with silence and that they “received no further communication from FSSAI after that submission and understood the matter to be closed”.
“Drinking water safety is a priority for Bisleri. We maintain stringent quality controls of over 90 tests across our 10-step manufacturing process and will continue to cooperate with FSSAI to address the matter through the appropriate regulatory process. A trusted brand for years, Bisleri remains safe for consumption,” the company said.
Will the latest findings shake public’s trust in Bisleri?
The FSSAI’s finding of bromate and PAHs in the Bisleri sample has led many to question if Bisleri’s water is safe to drink.
One Pune resident was quoted by the Times of India as saying, “For years, during train journeys and other travel, I would check whether I’d been sold the real ‘Bisleri’ or a fake ‘Bislery’ or ‘Besleri.’ Now it seems the problem is with the original.”
Another user wrote on X, “Do bisleri bachi hui hain, khatam karu ya nahi #FSSAI.”
As questions began to grow about the safety of Bisleri, shopkeepers also noted a change in buying patterns. “Once people lose confidence, they will think twice before purchasing. We are already seeing people asking for other drinking water brands,” said Ramesh Gupta, a local grocery store owner in Pune, to Times of India.
Even brand experts noted that such FSSAI’s action could hurt the trust that Bisleri has built over the years. Ganapathy Viswanathan, an independent communication consultant and author, was quoted as saying, “A brand like Bisleri does not build its reputation overnight. It has taken years of advertising, distribution and consumer confidence to reach where it is today.”
He noted that even though people don’t understand PAHs and bromate, the fact that Bisleri’s safety is being questioned may force people to move to other brands.
Harish Bijoor, brand and business strategist, was also quoted telling Open, “A brand is a trust statement. And to that extent, when that trust is questioned or shaken, consumers tend to reassess their ability to want that exact brand. I do believe this is going to suffer the downside of this FSSAI issue, and rightly so.”
Why does the action against Bisleri matter to the industry?
The action against Bisleri is significant for the country’s packaged drinking water market.
That’s because Bisleri International is the most dominant brand in this space. It controls 36 per cent of the industry whereas competitors like Aquafina trail at 20 per cent, and Kinley at 15 per cent. The remaining 29 per cent of the industry is held by smaller names or unbranded packaged drinking water.
Following Sunday’s findings, the FSSAI announced that it plans to test more Bisleri samples from across the nation. The FSSAI also said it would initiate legal proceedings against Bisleri.
In fact, Goa’s Food and Drugs Administration (FDA) has already stepped up against packaged drinking water in the state. FDA Director Shweta S Dessai said she has instructed officials to collect samples of different packaged water brands manufactured and sold in Goa for testing.
In Gujarat, Minister of State for Health Praful Pansheriya also told IANS that his department would step up inspections of all those who produce packaged drinking water. “Three to four days ago, my department issued instructions that starting tomorrow, wherever there are plants in Gujarat and wherever local bottled water is produced, both cleanliness and norms need to be checked, and this campaign of ours will be carried out across Gujarat.”
And the scrutiny isn’t going to be limited to just Bisleri. The FSSAI plans to conduct inspections of other packaged drinking water companies. As a government source said, “The whole industry is under the scanner now.”
This, according to Ankur Bisen, a partner at consulting firm The Knowledge Company, will result in all companies ensuring that their products comply with FSSAI norms.
Only time will tell if packaged drinking water is indeed safe in India.
With inputs from agencies

title: Who is the man in the photograph PM Modi gifted to Nepal PM Balen Shah?
description: PM Modi's gift collection for Balen Shah included a framed photograph, Gangajal from Varanasi, a Banarasi brocade stole in a traditional Gujarati Sadeli box and a Kalamkari painting of the Ramayana. One of these gifts came with a story of its own
author: FP News Desk
content:
Who is the man in the photograph PM Modi gifted to Nepal PM Balen Shah?
PM Modi's gift collection for Balen Shah included a framed photograph, Gangajal from Varanasi, a Banarasi brocade stole in a traditional Gujarati Sadeli box and a Kalamkari painting of the Ramayana. One of these gifts came with a story of its own
Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi's gifts to Nepal's Prime Minister Balen Shah ranged from Gangajal (sacred ganges water) and a Banarasi brocade stole to a Kalamkari artwork depicting the Sampoorna Ramayana (the complete story of the Ramayana). One present, however, stood apart from the rest.
It was a framed photograph from Gujarat that took Balen Shah back to his late father's postgraduate years. The photograph was of Dr Ram Narayan Shah at Gujarat Ayurveda University in Jamnagar.
Dr Ram Narayan Shah was an Ayurvedic physician who spent much of his professional life in Nepal's public healthcare system. From his early years in Mahottari to his postgraduate education in India and his decades of service in Kathmandu, his journey was rooted in the practice and promotion of traditional medicine.
From Mahottari to Jamnagar: The making of an Ayurvedic physician
Born in 1948 in Ekdara, in Nepal's Mahottari district, Ram Narayan Shah was the son of Muni Lal Shah, a local landowner and influential figure in the community. He grew up in Nepal's Terai region, where his family had agricultural and social ties, as per a profile published on him by Al Jazeera.
Shah chose to pursue a career in Ayurveda, the traditional system of medicine practised across the Indian subcontinent. His search for advanced training took him to India, where he enrolled for postgraduate studies at Gujarat Ayurveda University in Jamnagar.
The institution, now known as the Institute of Teaching and Research in Ayurveda, is a prominent centre for Ayurvedic education and research. Shah's years in Jamnagar in the late 1970s became a significant chapter in his life.
A career in Nepal's public healthcare system
After completing his studies in India, Shah returned to Nepal in the early 1980s and moved to Kathmandu with his family. He joined the government as an Ayurvedic physician and was assigned to Singha Durbar Vaidhyakhana, one of Nepal's oldest state-run institutions dedicated to the preparation and distribution of Ayurvedic medicines.
The institution has a long history in Nepal's traditional medicine system. It was established to prepare medicines for the royal household and the wider public, and has continued to play a role in the country's public healthcare network.
Shah spent several decades working in the government healthcare system. His career eventually took him to the top of the institution. Between 2001 and 2005, he served as the managing director of Singha Durbar Vaidhyakhana, overseeing an organisation responsible for producing traditional medicines and making them available to the public.
His work placed him within Nepal's efforts to preserve and develop its Ayurvedic healthcare system, even as modern medicine became increasingly widespread.
His ties to his hometown
Despite spending much of his professional life in Kathmandu, Shah retained close links with his ancestral home in Ekdara, Mahottari. He continued visiting the area and remained involved in community initiatives.
Reports in The Rising Nepal have noted his contributions to his hometown, including donating land for a weekly community market, locally known as a hatiya, and supporting the upkeep of a local temple.
These contributions reflected a connection to the community where he had grown up. Beyond his career in public service, Shah was remembered for supporting local infrastructure and religious institutions in his native village.
A legacy carried forward by his family
Dr Ram Narayan Shah died on December 1, 2025, at the age of 77 at Civil Hospital in Kathmandu. He was survived by his wife, Dhurba Devi Shah, and their children, including his youngest son, Balen Shah.
His death came months before his son became Nepal's prime minister. Balen, who first rose to prominence as a rapper and later became the mayor of Kathmandu, went on to take the country's top political office.
What are the big takeaways from the Modi-Balen Shah talks?
The high-level talks between PM Modi and Balen Shah delivered a series of major announcements covering development assistance, connectivity, energy and bilateral cooperation.
India announced a development cooperation package worth 24,000 crore Nepalese rupees (approximately Rs 15,000 crore) to support Nepal's reconstruction and development, including in the aftermath of severe floods. The two sides also signed eight memorandums of understanding (MoUs) covering satellite communications, civil servant training, healthcare, Ayurveda, forensic sciences and livestock development.
Connectivity featured prominently in the discussions. The leaders launched the Saryu-Kamala Express, connecting Ayodhya in India with Janakpur Dham in Nepal. They also inaugurated the Dharchula-Darchula motorable bridge and dedicated Phase II of the Motihari-Amlekhgunj petroleum pipeline, aimed at strengthening cross-border transport and energy links.
The two countries also stepped up cooperation in the energy sector. The foundation stones were laid for the 669 MW Lower Arun Hydroelectric Project and an oil storage terminal in Jhapa.

title: Researchers turn discarded pharma proteins into hydrogel for wound care
description: The NIT Rourkela team has developed a hydrogel from inactive bone morphogenetic protein-2, with potential applications in wound healing, tissue repair and controlled drug delivery
author: Hemant Kumar Rout
content:
Researchers turn discarded pharma proteins into hydrogel for wound care
The NIT Rourkela team has developed a hydrogel from inactive bone morphogenetic protein-2, with potential applications in wound healing, tissue repair and controlled drug delivery
Listen to This Article
What pharmaceutical companies discard as unusable protein waste could potentially find a second life as a material for wound healing and tissue regeneration.
Researchers at the National Institute of Technology (NIT) Rourkela have developed a technology to convert proteins that lost their biological activity during drug manufacturing into hydrogels capable of supporting tissue repair and controlled drug delivery.
The innovation offers a new use for discarded pharmaceutical materials and opens up possibilities for developing value-added biomaterials from otherwise unusable resources.
The research team, comprising Harekrushna Sahoo, Monalisa Mishra and Devendra Verma, used inactive bone morphogenetic protein-2 (BMP-2), a protein associated with bone and tissue development, as the raw material for producing a functional hydrogel for biomedical applications.
Proteins are sensitive molecules whose structures can be altered by exposure to heat, chemicals and other processing conditions. Such changes cause them to unfold and aggregate into clumps, rendering them unsuitable for their intended pharmaceutical applications. These inactive proteins are generally discarded by manufacturers.
Also Read
The NIT Rourkela team demonstrated that such discarded proteins need not be treated merely as industrial waste and can instead serve as a raw material for developing functional biomaterials.
The BMP-2 was heated to around 85 degrees Celsius for 10 minutes, causing it to lose its original three-dimensional structure and aggregate. The researchers then used a combination of hydrogen peroxide and hyaluronic acid to transform the protein aggregates into a hydrogel.
Hyaluronic acid, a naturally occurring substance in the human body known for its ability to retain moisture, plays an important role in determining the properties of the resulting material. The combination produces a porous gel structure capable of absorbing and retaining water, holding therapeutic compounds and interacting with biological tissues.
Explaining the contribution of the two components, Sahoo, a professor in the Department of Chemistry at NIT Rourkela, said the synthesis and performance were associated with the synergistic contributions of BMP-2 protein and hyaluronic acid, particularly the latter's water-retention properties, which improved the hydrogel's molecular and antioxidant activities and sustained drug-release characteristics.
In laboratory experiments, the researchers loaded the hydrogel with the antibiotic ampicillin and examined its drug-release behaviour. "The results indicated that the material could release the drug in a sustained manner, suggesting its possible application in delivering medicines directly to affected tissues," he said.
The hydrogel also demonstrated the ability to support the growth of fibroblasts, cells that play a critical role in wound repair by producing collagen and other components required for tissue formation. This property is relevant to wound-care applications, where an appropriate environment for cell growth and tissue regeneration is essential.
The team also evaluated the material's wound-healing potential using Drosophila melanogaster (fruit fly) as an in vivo experimental model. The findings were encouraging, although the researchers emphasised that further studies are necessary to establish its safety and effectiveness in higher animal models before considering human clinical trials.
Mishra, an associate professor in the Department of Life Sciences, said the evaluation of the wound-healing efficacy of the newly designed and synthesised BMP-2–hyaluronic acid composite hydrogel was conducted using Drosophila melanogaster as the in vivo model.                                             The hydrogel experiment 
"Although we found that the hydrogel is quite promising with our model, its biocompatibility still has to be established and proved with higher animal models before clinical trials," she said.
The next phase of research will focus on assessing the hydrogel's biocompatibility, toxicity and therapeutic performance through more advanced biological models. Establishing that the material does not cause adverse reactions in the body will be crucial to determining its suitability for medical applications.
Verma, a professor in the Department of Biotechnology and Medical Engineering, said the initial cell-line results were encouraging and that the material could emerge as a candidate for clinical applications if its safety is established.
"The cell-line outcome is promising and could be an efficient candidate for clinical trials, provided it is biocompatible and non-toxic to higher animal models. It might take 10–12 months to prove the same with higher animal models, which could open the way for clinical trials," he said.
The research findings have been published in the Royal Society of Chemistry's Journal of Materials Chemistry B. The researchers have also secured an Indian patent for the technology.
If further animal studies establish its safety and efficacy, the technology could provide a new platform for wound-care products and controlled drug delivery, while adding value to materials that are currently considered pharmaceutical waste.

title: SC seeks census SOPs from Centre, Directorate of Census Operations
description: The Supreme Court on Thursday asked the Centre and the Directorate of Census Operations to place on record the standard operating procedures  governing the conduct of the census within a week. This would include the methodology and safeguards for recording and verifying caste-related information.
author: PTI
content:
SC seeks census SOPs from Centre, Directorate of Census Operations
The Supreme Court on Thursday asked the Centre and the Directorate of Census Operations to place on record the standard operating procedures governing the conduct of the census within a week
Listen to This Article
The Supreme Court on Thursday asked the Centre and the Directorate of Census Operations to place on record the standard operating procedures governing the conduct of the census within a week. This would include the methodology and safeguards for recording and verifying caste-related information.
A bench comprising Chief Justice Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana took note of the submission made by Additional Solicitor General Aishwarya Bhati, appearing for the Centre, that she would apprise the court of the relevant SOPs.
The bench asked the law officer to provide the details within a week.
In its order dated October 12, the bench had requested the solicitor general to place on record the census SOPs being followed. It also directed that a complete set of the paper book be provided to the advocate-on-record for the Centre and the office of the solicitor general.
A plea by Aakash Goel raised concerns over the methodology and safeguards for collecting and verifying caste-related information under a notification of August 14 concerning the census.
Also Read
"Issue an appropriate writ, order or direction directing the Respondents to disclose and place in the public domain the methodology and safeguards governing recording and verification under Item 10 of Notification S.0.4505(E) dated 14.08.2026, including the applicable Household Schedule and relevant instructions, while preserving confidentiality of individual information," it said.
The petition sought a transparent and workable mechanism to record identifying particulars of government-issued caste certificates, wherever available, and verify their authenticity through the competent authorities.
The plea asked for disclosure of the methodology, applicable household schedule and instructions governing the collection and verification of caste particulars, while ensuring the confidentiality of individual information.
Besides, it sought a direction that caste data collected during Census 2027 should not be treated as the sole basis for formulating or revising reservation policies or determining caste-based allocation of welfare resources unless a transparent and verifiable verification protocol is put in place.
It pressed for a direction to authorities to place an affidavit before the court detailing the proposed protocol and the steps taken to implement it.

title: Odisha clears 19 projects worth ₹3,810 crore, power and tourism lead
description: Seven hospitality projects to create 1,500 jobs; garment manufacturing unit in Khordha to generate 5,500 jobs, taking the total employment potential of the approved projects to 11,251
author: Hemant Kumar Rout
content:
Odisha clears 19 projects worth ₹3,810 crore, power and tourism lead
Seven hospitality projects to create 1,500 jobs; garment manufacturing unit in Khordha to generate 5,500 jobs, taking the total employment potential of the approved projects to 11,251
Listen to This Article
The Odisha government on Thursday approved 19 investment proposals worth Rs 3,810.25 crore, with an estimated employment potential of 11,251.
Tourism and hospitality emerged as significant investment destinations, attracting seven projects worth Rs 607 crore and offering job opportunities for 1,500 people, while power, textiles, metal downstream, healthcare, steel, green mobility and recycling secured fresh investments.
The investment proposals were cleared at the 152nd State Level Single Window Clearance Authority (SLSWCA) meeting chaired by Chief Secretary Anu Garg. The projects are spread across 10 districts — Balasore, Cuttack, Ganjam, Jagatsinghpur, Jharsuguda, Kendrapara, Keonjhar, Khordha, Koraput and Sundargarh.
The proposed tourism projects include luxury resorts, eco-tourism destinations, wellness centres, hotels and amusement infrastructure, reflecting growing investor interest in Odisha's potential as a leisure and nature-based tourism destination.
Koraput has emerged as a major beneficiary, with three hospitality projects involving a cumulative investment of Rs 297 crore. Sacheti Hospitality Pvt Ltd will set up a five-star resort with an investment of Rs 121 crore, and TVR Estates and Resorts Pvt Ltd will establish a four-star eco-resort with a wellness centre at an investment of Rs 104 crore. Niladri Hotels and Resorts Pvt Ltd will invest Rs 72 crore in a four-star wellness resort.
Also Read
The other tourism investments include a four-star hotel by Nikhil Associates in Cuttack at an investment of Rs 82 crore and a four-star resort by Altone Resources in Jharsuguda involving Rs 80 crore. In Balasore, Padmabati Amusement Park will expand its existing facility with an investment of Rs 78 crore, while Highland Hotels and Resorts Pvt Ltd will establish a four-star hotel at an investment of Rs 70 crore.
The largest employment-generating proposal in this round comes from the textiles and apparel sector. Bodycare Creations Ltd will establish a garment manufacturing unit in Khordha with an investment of Rs 225 crore. The facility will have an annual production capacity of 66 million pieces and is expected to generate 5,500 jobs.
The metal downstream sector has attracted three proposals involving a combined investment of Rs 525.11 crore. Ratnamani Metals and Tubes Ltd will establish a carbon steel longitudinal submerged arc welded (LSAW) pipe manufacturing facility in Sundargarh at an investment of Rs 250 crore.
Qalvion Systems Pvt Ltd will set up a structural steel and machinery fabrication unit in Ganjam with an investment of Rs 217.67 crore. Baid Engineers Pvt Ltd will establish a heavy steel fabrication and structural engineering unit in Sundargarh, with an annual capacity of 20,000 tonnes, investing Rs 57.44 crore.
Healthcare and pharmaceuticals have secured investments worth Rs 373.93 crore. Vedanta Aluminium Metal Ltd will establish a 200-bed multispeciality hospital in Jharsuguda at an investment of Rs 311.52 crore. Pentaone Lifecare Pvt Ltd will set up a healthcare products manufacturing facility in Khordha with an investment of Rs 62.41 crore.
In the green mobility segment, EV Innovegic India Pvt Ltd will establish a manufacturing facility for solar-powered electric boats in Kendrapara. The project involves an investment of Rs 52 crore, adding a new dimension to Odisha's efforts to develop renewable-energy-based mobility and marine equipment manufacturing.
The chemicals and petrochemicals category has attracted a Rs 116.49 crore proposal from Net Zero Renewables LLP to set up a recycling unit in Sundargarh. The facility is expected to add to the state's emerging resource recovery and circular economy ecosystem.
The power sector accounts for two projects involving a combined investment of Rs 1,395.7 crore. Shri Mahavir Ferro Alloys Pvt Ltd will establish a 135 megawatt (MW) coal-washery reject-based thermal power plant in Sundargarh under the independent power producer (IPP) model, with an investment of Rs 912.8 crore. Maadurga Thermal Power Company Ltd will invest Rs 482.9 crore to double the capacity of its existing thermal power plant in Cuttack from 60 MW to 120 MW.
In the steel and iron sector, Crackers India (Alloys) Ltd has received approval for an investment of Rs 450 crore in Keonjhar to expand its existing direct reduced iron (DRI) facility by setting up a 0.15 million tonne per annum integrated steel manufacturing plant.
The plastics sector has attracted an investment of Rs 65.02 crore from Energon Polymatic Pvt Ltd, which will establish a polypropylene woven sacks and bags manufacturing facility in Jagatsinghpur.
Garg emphasised the need to ensure that investment approvals translate into timely implementation, productive employment and stronger industrial ecosystems across the state.
"Odisha is committed to building a diversified and competitive industrial ecosystem that creates meaningful employment and expands economic opportunities across the state. Our focus is not only on attracting investments, but also on ensuring their timely implementation, strengthening local industries and developing sector-specific capabilities," she said.

title: Saurav Das passport issue: MEA explains why CJP co-convenor was stopped from flying to London; details here
description: The MEA said Saurav Das received a seven-day show-cause notice from the Chennai Regional Passport Office over discrepancies in his passport’s place-of-birth details. CJP Co-convenor says immigration officials stopped him from travelling to UK and has challenged the decision in the Delhi High Court.
author: Garvit Bhirani
content:
The Ministry of External Affairs (MEA) on Wednesday said Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) co-convener Saurav Das had received a show-cause notice over inconsistencies in the place of birth mentioned in his passport. The notice was issued following inputs from the relevant authorities, according to PTI. MEA spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal said the Regional Passport Office (RPO) in Chennai served the notice on Saurav Das on Monday, asking him to submit his explanation within seven days. The clarification came after Das alleged that immigration authorities had stopped him from travelling to the United Kingdom, where he was scheduled to attend an Oxford University event and speak on the "cockroach movement". Meanwhile, Das moved the Delhi High Court on Wednesday, challenging the authorities' decision to prevent him from travelling overseas. Jaiswal emphasised that applicants are required to provide accurate details while applying for passports. "Let me say that the passport application provides for declaration of correct information by the applicant," he said. Explaining the procedure followed when inconsistencies are detected, Jaiswal said, "If at any stage a discrepancy is noted or reported by authorities, which amounts to suppression of facts, then we issue a show cause notice to the applicant to explain his or her point of view," he said. He further clarified that the notice against Das followed inputs from law enforcement agencies. "Based on reports that we received from the relevant law enforcement authorities, a show-cause notice was issued by RPO Chennai to Saurav Das on November 23 seeking his clarification within seven days regarding his place of birth," he added. PTI citing sources indicated that the CJP leader had obtained his passport from the Chennai Regional Passport Office, where officials subsequently flagged inconsistencies concerning his place of birth. Jaiswal also said Das had been advised against using the passport until he submitted his response to the notice. Meanwhile, Das claimed that immigration officials stopped him at the Delhi airport while he was completing departure formalities for his London-bound flight. Representing Das before the Delhi High Court, his lawyer told the bench that immigration officials had prevented his client from travelling without providing any formal order or restriction notice. "I was stopped at immigration. No order was shown to me. No LOC, no prohibition by any authority from letting me travel. I am seeking listing of a fresh petition today. I can still make it to the United Kingdom on November 27, which is where my arrangements are," Das's counsel submitted in the High Court. The lawyer informed the court that Das's scheduled flight was on Thursday. Responding to the submission, the bench said, "Let it be (heard) tomorrow." Earlier, in a social media post on Monday night, Das accused the government of deliberately preventing his UK visit to stop him from speaking to students at universities abroad. "This coward government did not allow me to board my flight to London where I was invited by prestigious universities like Oxford, Cambridge, LSE, Edinburgh to deliver talks on the cockroach movement," he said. He further alleged that the authorities were apprehensive about his engagement with international academic institutions, adding, "Indian students put their heart and soul to organise the events but this anti-intellectual govt was scared of me going to these prestigious institutions!," he alleged. Das was due to depart for London on a flight scheduled for 1 am on Tuesday. Garvit Bhirani is a journalist based in Gurugram. title: Tamil Nadu CM Vijay announces 15 days paternity leave for male government employees — Here's when they can take it
description: Male government employees will be eligible for 15 days of paternity leave, which can be availed either 15 days before the expected delivery date or within six months after the birth of the child, according to an official release.
author: Ravi Hari
content:
Tamil Nadu Chief Minister C Joseph Vijay on Thursday (November 26) announced 15 days of paternity leave for male government employees, introducing a new benefit aimed at encouraging fathers to participate more actively in childcare and supporting families during the crucial period surrounding childbirth.
The government said the decision was taken after receiving representations from employees seeking paternity leave, which were considered favourably by the state administration.
The move is aimed at promoting shared parenting responsibilities and ensuring fathers have adequate time to support their spouses and care for newborns during the early stages of parenthood.
When can Tamil Nadu government employees take paternity leave?
According to the government announcement, eligible male employees can avail 15 days of paternity leave within a specified period around childbirth.
- Before childbirth: Up to 15 days before the delivery of the baby.
- After childbirth: Anytime within six months following the birth of the child.
The government said the period surrounding childbirth is particularly important for both the mother and the child, making the father's presence and involvement in childcare equally significant.
Why has Tamil Nadu introduced paternity leave?
The state government said the decision was aimed at promoting a more balanced approach to parenting and enabling couples to share family responsibilities more equitably.
The initial weeks and months after childbirth can be particularly demanding for families, with mothers recovering from delivery while parents adjust to caring for a newborn.
The introduction of paternity leave is expected to encourage greater paternal involvement in early childcare and help working families manage the transition into parenthood.
Tamil Nadu government employees get 365 days maternity leave
Tamil Nadu currently provides female government employees with 365 days of maternity leave, reflecting the state's policy emphasis on maternal health and child welfare.
In August, the state government announced an extension of the 365-day maternity leave benefit to women government employees for their third child, bringing the entitlement in line with the leave available for their first two children.

title: 26/11 Mumbai attack: Who is Sunil Kudyadi? Taj Hotel security official known for supporting rescue operations
description: Taj Mahal Palace security chief Sunil Kudyadi helped police and commandos navigate the hotel and rescue people during the 2008 Mumbai attacks. During a 2026 visit, US Secretary of State Marco Rubio met Kudyadi, heard his account of the siege and paid tribute to the victims.
author: Garvit Bhirani
content:
As India marks 18 years since the November 26, 2008 Mumbai terror attacks, Taj Mahal Palace Hotel security chief Sunil Kudyadi has drawn attention for his firsthand account of the siege and his role in assisting rescue operations. Kudyadi was inside the iconic Mumbai hotel when Pakistani terrorists launched the coordinated attacks, which claimed 166 lives and left hundreds injured. He recently came into the spotlight after US Secretary of State Marco Rubio met him during his visit to the Taj Hotel in Mumbai on October 20. External Affairs Minister S Jaishankar introduced Kudyadi to Rubio, who heard his account of the events that unfolded inside the hotel during the attacks. According to several reports, Kudyadi helped security personnel navigate the hotel's complex layout during the operation to rescue people trapped inside. His familiarity with the premises proved valuable to the police and security forces responding to the attack. Sunil Kudyadi is the Associate Vice President of Security and Safety and Head of Security at Mumbai's Taj Mahal Palace Hotel. He was present at the hotel on November 26, 2008, when terrorists stormed the property as part of the coordinated attacks across Mumbai. Kudyadi's role during the siege involved assisting security personnel with information about the hotel's layout and guiding them through its premises. According to India Today, he used his knowledge of the building to help police and commandos, including personnel from the Marine Commandos (MARCOS), navigate the property. The Maharashtra government's High-Level Enquiry Committee report, headed by former Union Home Secretary Ram Pradhan, also documented the assistance provided by Taj security personnel during the operation. It recorded that Deputy Commissioner of Police Vishwas Nangre Patil entered the hotel through its rear entrance with Kudyadi on the night of November 26, 2008. On October 20, Rubio visited the Taj Mahal Palace Hotel during his three-day India trip and laid a wreath at the 26/11 memorial to honour those killed in the attacks, including six American citizens. Jaishankar introduced Kudyadi to the US Secretary of State and informed him that the hotel security official had been present during the attacks. Kudyadi then shared details of the assault, including how the attackers entered the building and moved through its floors. According to India Today, Kudyadi told Rubio, "They came in the middle of the night. They went up to the sixth floor from the kitchen." Jaishankar also explained that several people had been killed in the kitchen during the attack. Following the visit, Rubio recalled the victims and the people who responded to the attacks in a post on X. "At the Taj Mahal Palace Hotel, I laid a wreath honouring the victims of the horrific November 26, 2008, terrorist attacks, including six American citizens. We remember those lost, honour the courage of those who responded, and reaffirm the enduring US-India partnership and our shared commitment to combating terrorism," he said. Kudyadi's familiarity with the Taj's sprawling premises helped police and commandos move through the building during the operation to locate attackers and rescue people trapped inside. Former Union Home Secretary Ram Pradhan, who led the panel examining the 26/11 attacks, described Kudyadi as an "unsung hero". The report highlighted the importance of Kudyadi's assistance, observing that his knowledge of the hotel's complex layout was crucial in helping security personnel navigate the premises during the rescue operation. Taj security staff also assisted the police and National Security Guard (NSG) during the operation.
