title: Drought’s bitter harvest of debt
description: Telangana drought cripples farms and livelihoods, driving debt, suicides, and calls for urgent water relief amid El Niño-driven crisis.
author: Abhinay Deshpande
content:
Trigger warning: the following article contains references to suicide; please avoid reading if you are disturbed by the subject.
Four days after her husband died by suicide, 38-year-old Neelagiri Laxmi has barely had time to grieve. With two children to raise, a debt of over ₹10 lakh hanging over the family and her own health failing, she must somehow find the strength to keep the household going.
Her husband, Neelagiri Ashanna, 43, was a tenant farmer in Thalamadugu village of Adilabad district. He had borrowed the money from a private moneylender in Adilabad town at a high rate of interest to cultivate cotton on 20 acres of leased land, hoping that a good harvest would help secure his family’s future. But the rains failed, the crop withered and his hopes unravelled.
On November 14, Ashanna stepped out of his house after dinner. “I thought he had gone out to relieve himself. But he never came back. About half an hour later, I started looking for him, and we found his body,” says his 19-year-old son Abhilash, a second-year undergraduate student.
“There was no rain. The crop failed. He must have feared he wouldn’t be able to repay the loan,” says Laxmi, who must now manage the debt and household on her wages, despite health complications.
Published - November 27, 2026 05:41 am IST

title: Special Parliament sitting revives buzz over delimitation, women's quota bills
description: The NDA could reach 353 Lok Sabha votes for the proposed delimitation amendment The projected support remains seven votes short of the required two-thirds majority
author: India Today News Desk
content:
Special Parliament sitting revives buzz over delimitation, women's quota bills
The NDA could reach 353 Lok Sabha votes for the proposed delimitation amendment. The projected support remains seven votes short of the required two-thirds majority.
Political discussions have gathered pace over the government's plans to revive the contentious Delimitation Bill and Women's Reservation Bill, with the focus firmly on the numbers required to secure their passage in Parliament. The Lok Sabha Speaker and the Rajya Sabha Chairman okayed the proposal as the government asked them to reconvene the Lower House on November 30 and the Upper House on December 2 for special sittings, which may conclude on December 3.
The move has triggered fresh political calculations over whether the BJP-led NDA can muster the two-thirds majority needed to pass the proposed constitutional amendment, even as Opposition parties have criticised the timing and the government's legislative approach.
NDA EXPLORES SUPPORT BEYOND ALLIES
The government faces the challenge of securing the constitutionally mandated majority in both Houses.
Under Article 368, a Constitution amendment requires a majority of the total membership of each House and the support of at least two-thirds of members present and voting.
In the Lok Sabha, which has a sanctioned strength of 543, three seats are vacant.
The NDA currently has around 298 MPs, including 240 from the BJP, 16 from the Telugu Desam Party, 13 from the Eknath Shinde-led Shiv Sena and 12 from the Janata Dal (United).
The government's potential tally could rise to 319 with the support of 20 rebel Trinamool Congress MPs, who have broken away from the party and pledged support to the NDA, along with Shiromani Akali Dal MP Harsimrat Kaur Badal.
The numbers could increase further if regional parties extend their support.
The DMK has 22 MPs, the NCP (Sharadchandra Pawar) eight and the YSR Congress Party four.
Their combined support could take the projected tally to 353. NCP (SP) leader Supriya Sule has indicated that her party could consider backing the legislation if it provides for a uniform 50 per cent increase in Lok Sabha seats for every state.
With 353 votes, the government could meet the two-thirds requirement if 529 or fewer members vote.
If all 539 MPs other than the Speaker participate, 360 votes would be required. Abstentions among Opposition members could therefore prove significant.
WHY THE BILLS MATTER
The proposed constitutional amendment seeks to increase the maximum strength of the Lok Sabha from 543 to 850 through delimitation, paving the way for implementing 33 per cent reservation for women in the Lok Sabha and state legislative assemblies.
Parliament passed the Women's Reservation Act in 2023, but its implementation was linked to a delimitation exercise following the publication of figures from the first Census conducted after the law came into force.
The government is seeking to expedite the process so that the quota can be implemented before the 2029 Lok Sabha elections.
However, the proposed expansion has raised concerns among southern states over the possibility of changes in their relative representation in Parliament.
The government is understood to be considering a 50 per cent increase in seats for every state or retaining the existing proportion of representation based on the 1971 Census. No final decision has been announced.
APRIL DEFEAT CASTS SHADOW
The government's renewed efforts come after the Constitution (131st Amendment) Bill, 2026, was defeated in the Lok Sabha on April 17.
Of the 528 MPs who voted, 298 supported the Bill and 230 opposed it. The government needed 352 votes to secure the required two-thirds majority, falling short by 54 votes.
Following the defeat, the government held back the related Delimitation Bill, 2026, and the Union Territories Laws (Amendment) Bill, 2026.
The political arithmetic has since changed, with 26 MPs moving out of the Opposition camp, strengthening the government's position.
OPPOSITION QUESTIONS SPECIAL SITTING
The announcement of the special sittings has drawn sharp criticism from Opposition parties, which have questioned the decision to reconvene Parliament for a brief period instead of holding a regular Winter Session.
Congress general secretary Jairam Ramesh accused the government of seeking a "super-tainted" two-thirds majority after what he described as "105 days of Operation Lotus".
He called the move an "insult to and assault on the Constitution".
Congress MP Manish Tewari said the government's request "mocks the institution of Parliament", arguing that a special sitting should not become a substitute for a regular Winter Session.
CPI(M) MP John Brittas alleged that political manoeuvres were being used to manufacture a majority for delimitation, warning that "Women's empowerment must never become a smokescreen for electoral engineering."
Congress MP Renuka Chowdhury also questioned the short-notice announcement, saying Parliament must provide adequate opportunities for legislative scrutiny, Question Hour, Zero Hour and discussions on matters of public importance.
CABINET MEET, OPPOSITION HUDDLE IN FOCUS
The Union Cabinet is scheduled to meet on Friday and is likely to discuss the proposed legislation.
The Congress Parliamentary Strategy Group, chaired by Sonia Gandhi, is also scheduled to meet to formulate the party's response ahead of the special sittings.
The government has maintained its push for women's reservation, with Prime Minister Narendra Modi blaming the Opposition for the earlier defeat of the constitutional amendment.
With the proposed sittings approaching, attention will now centre on the final provisions of the Bills, the positions taken by regional parties and the government's ability to secure the required numbers in both Houses.
The coming days are expected to see further political consultations as the Centre attempts to revive legislation that failed to clear Parliament earlier this year.

title: 2 more Siang activists released; at most, a case of mischief is made out, says court
description: While granting interim relief to Ebo Mili, the court stated that the activist was required to “refrain himself from participating in illegal organising, calling for, or supporting any illegal bandh call, unlawful assembly or gathering which may disturb public peace and tranquility”
author: Shinjini Ghosh
content:
Prominent Arunachal activists Otul Jerang and Ebo Mili walked out of jail after a month after the East Siang District and Sessions Judge granted them bail on Thursday in connection with the protests held at Pasighat on October 23 against the proposed Siang Upper Multipurpose Project (SUMP).
Soon after walking out of custody, Mili, who is a lawyer, told The Indian Express, “I am currently doing well but the entire period was not just an ordeal for me but my family as well. I have been arrested in the past as well, but this was the first time that I was in jail for over a month.”
Both Jerang and Mili had voluntarily surrendered at the Pasighat police station on October 27 following which they were arrested.
Speaking from his hometown Roing, which is nearly 100 kilometres from Pasighat, Mili said, “When it comes to my family, they had to take the most amount of pressure. They do not belong to a financially strong background, and this entire period made them very helpless as well.”
Referring to the FIR that alleged that an ambulance was damaged as a result of stone-pelting by a mob, Pasighat District and Sessions Judge K Tasso said, “…the FIR does not explain any specific allegation of grievous hurt having been caused to the driver or any occupant of the ambulance. At most, a case of mischief is made out which is bailable and in that case also, there is prima facie no material to suggest the involvement of the accused.”
While granting interim relief, the court stated that Mili was required to “refrain himself from participating in illegal organizing, calling for, or supporting any illegal bandh call, unlawful assembly or gathering which may disturb public peace and tranquility.”
Following a 12-hour bandh that was called to oppose the proposed SUMP, the October 23 protests had turned violent, and incidents of arson and vandalism were reported from Pasighat in the East Siang district.
A police station, an NHPC office and several police vehicles were reportedly set on fire and residences of some of the local political leaders were allegedly vandalised. While police used tear gas to disperse the crowd, there were also reports of personnel sustaining injuries due to stone-pelting.
Soon after, several protesters and activists were arrested and the Centre also deployed troops to contain the protests. Lawyers of several activists who were jailed had earlier stated that there were nearly 10 cases registered against each of them.
Last week, Tajong Talom, another prominent anti-dam activist, walked out of jail after being rearrested a few days earlier.
The government has maintained that the proposed 11,000 MW dam is essential for national security and to counter China’s proposed mega dam.
However, residents along the Siang river and the indigenous communities have argued that the proposed SUMP will be a threat to their livelihoods, cultural and historical existence.
While the project is in the Pre-Feasibility Survey stage, various indigenous groups have urged authorities to stall the process.
In his first remarks since the October 23 protests, Union Home Minister Amit Shah on November 21 urged locals and stakeholders to have consultations with both the state and central governments.
While speaking at an event in Itanagar, Shah said that the proposed SUMP was a “national project” and that the government intended to hold “positive and constructive discussions.”

title: Caught by J&K police after 27 years, ex-militant carried no mobile, Aadhaar
description: Absconding from Jammu's Reasi district since 2019, Mohammad Mansha was found in Kashmir's Tral where he had started a new life with his family at a poultry farm under an assumed name
author: Arun Sharma
content:
For the last seven years, this former militant from Jammu’s Reasi district has been evading police.
Even though he surrendered in 2007, he needed to face trial for the crimes he had committed before that. This included his alleged involvement in the killing of a police officer in 2000.
On Thursday, police finally located him in another part of the Union Territory, in Kashmir’s Tral, where he had started a new life with his family at a poultry farm under an assumed name.
Now brought back to Reasi, he is set to face trial in the 27-year-old case.
What made the police’s search for Mohammad Mansha particularly difficult was the fact that he had stopped using all digital devices, said an official. In fact, he did not possess even an Aadhaar card, he added.
Originally a resident of Thuroo Lassoli in Reasi district, the 42-year-old had been evading trial in a total of 13 criminal cases, including murder, attempt to murder, and other terror-related incidents that took place between 2000 and 2007, a police officer told The Indian Express.
“He was particularly wanted in connection with FIR No. 127/2000, registered at Police Station, Mahore, for murder, attempt to murder and criminal conspiracy and waging war against India, registered under the provisions of the Ranbir Penal Code (RPC), besides Arms Act,” Mahore Station House Officer Inspector Surjeet Bhagat said.
A Special Police Officer (SPO) of J&K Police had been killed in that case, he added.
After completion of investigation, a chargesheet was presented before the competent court under Section 512 of the Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC), following which the accused was declared an absconder.
Joined terror ranks at 16
Mansha had left studies in Class 10 and joined terror ranks at the age of 16 in 2000, a police officer said. After his surrender in 2007, he married and had four children, including two daughters. His eldest son was studying in Class 11, he added.
The Court of the Principal District and Sessions Judge, Reasi, had issued an arrest warrant against him in 2001.
After his 2007 surrender before the Army, when pressure increased on him to face the trial, Mansha went underground along with his family in 2019.
To track him down, police in Reasi district constituted a special team, comprising personnel from Mahore Police Station and the District Absconder Tracking Unit. But every time, their efforts used to hit a dead-end, especially because he neither owned a mobile phone nor an Aadhaar card.
Finding that it was virtually impossible to track him down through digital surveillance, the police focussed on human intelligence. After a seven-year-long continuous hunt, the personnel finally traced him to a poultry farm in Tral where he had found employment over the last few years.
His family was also staying with him in that poultry farm, an official confirmed, adding that the accused was finally arrested through effective inter-district coordination between police from Reasi and Awantipora.
Reasi Police attributed the arrest to sustained efforts, meticulous planning and professional investigation, reaffirming its commitment to tracking down absconders and bringing those wanted in serious criminal cases to justice.

title: Government removes NSD officiating chairman Bharat Gupt amid his feud with director
description: The move comes amid a protracted feud between Gupt and NSD director Chittranjan Tripathi over termination of two contractual employees, including Gupt’s private secretary.
author: Shyamlal Yadav
content:
Shyamlal Yadav is one of the pioneers of the effective use of RTI for investigative reporting. He is... Read More
- Tags:
- National School of Drama
The Centre on Thursday removed Bharat Gupt as the officiating chairman of the National School of Drama (NSD), hours after he issued orders overturning the director’s decision to terminate the services of two contractual employees, including Gupt’s private secretary.
“It is hereby conveyed that the Central Government has decided to withdraw the nomination of Shri Bharat Gupt as a member of the Society, on administrative grounds, with immediate effect,” the Ministry of Culture said in a communication late Thursday evening.
The post of NSD Chairman was vacant, and therefore Vice-Chairman Gupt was officiating as the chairman. His tenure was ending in mid-January 2027.
Gupt told The Indian Express, “I was communicated about the decision by the NSD director this late evening. I have no role in NSD now. I was waiting for the ministry’s reply to my letters and reminders, but they didn’t respond, and now I am removed.”
NSD Director Chittranjan Tripathi did not pick up calls, but a senior NSD official said, “The news is correct. Mr Gupt is removed by the Ministry of Culture. The director has no role in this decision.”
Gupt had issued two letters on Thursday, cancelling the November 9 office memorandum, issued by the NSD director, that terminated the services of the two contractual employees: Gupt’s private secretary Kanhaiya Jha and NSD advisor Pradeep Kumar.
“The Office Memorandum dated 09.11.2026 will have no effect, and no administrative, financial, or other step shall be taken or continued under it. This order is issued because no supporting records or valid administrative reasons have been provided to justify ending the engagement early, despite repeated requests,” Gupt wrote in his order.
A day after the two contractual staffers were sacked, Gupt wrote to Culture Minister Gajendra Singh Shekhawat, requesting the terminations be “reconsidered and withdrawn”.
In the letter, Gupt had said that while there are nearly 100 contractual staff hired by the NSD, only two of them have been terminated from service.
While Gupt had asked both staffers not to hand over the charge, sources said almost every day they were being asked by the Director’s office to hand over the charge.

title: India set to deploy fifth S-400 along Pakistan border by February
description: At present, three S-400 long-range systems to counter aerial threats are deployed in Punjab, Rajasthan and Gujarat, and a fourth is deployed in Assam. | India News
author: Shishir Gupta
content:
Shishir Gupta is Executive Editor at Hindustan Times and one of India's top journalists covering national security, strategic affairs, foreign policy and geopolitics. Over the past three decades, he has extensively reported on India's military, diplomatic and security landscape, covering every major conflict and national security challenge, from the 1999 Kargil War and the 2020 East Ladakh standoff to Operation Sindoor in 2025. He has also covered major terror attacks, including the IC-814 hijacking, the 26/11 Mumbai attacks and the 2025 Pahalgam terror strike, along with numerous Pakistan-backed terrorist incidents in the Kashmir Valley and across India. He has reported on national and state elections for more than three decades. A recognised authority on strategic affairs, Gupta has covered India's nuclear programme since the Pokhran-II (Shakti series) tests in May 1998 and has written extensively on global nuclear issues, Indian diplomacy and the country's expanding global outreach. He has also reported widely on international conflicts and terrorism, with a special focus on the Indian subcontinent. Gupta has interviewed Prime Minister Narendra Modi more than four times, including Modi's first interview with the print media after becoming Prime Minister in May 2014. His other interviews include three with the Dalai Lama, as well as conversations with Benjamin Netanyahu, Amit Shah, Yogi Adityanath, S. Jaishankar, Nirmala Sitharaman and Piyush Goyal. He is the author of Indian Mujahideen: The Enemy Within (Hachette, 2011) and Himalayan Face-off: Chinese Assertion and Indian Riposte (Hachette, 2014). He was awarded the Chevening-Wolfson Joint Scholarship at Wolfson College, University of Cambridge, UK, in 1998 and participated in the International Visitor Leadership Program (IVLP) of the US State Department in 2006. He received the Ben Gurion Prize from Israel in 2011 and the K. Subrahmanyam Prize for Strategic Studies in 2015 from the Manohar Parrikar Institute for Defence Studies and Analyses (MP-IDSA). Since 2024, he has hosted Point Blank, Hindustan Times' weekly YouTube show on global geopolitics.
India set to deploy fifth S-400 along Pakistan border by February
At present, three S-400 long-range systems to counter aerial threats are deployed in Punjab, Rajasthan and Gujarat, and a fourth is deployed in Assam.
With China and Turkey supplying hardware, the US giving more teeth to F-16 fighters, and Saudi Arabia providing capital for Pakistan’s military capabilities, India has decided to further strengthen its western border by deploying a fifth S-400 air defence system to guard the 740km Line of Control (LoC) in Jammu & Kashmir, according to two top officials aware of the matter.
At present, three S-400 long-range systems to counter aerial threats are deployed in Punjab, Rajasthan and Gujarat, and a fourth is deployed in Assam to protect the 1126km long Line of Actual Control in Arunachal Pradesh.
S-400 purchase from Russia
While the Union government remains tight-lipped on national security, the officials cited above told HT that an Indian Air Force (IAF) pre-dispatch inspection team will visit Russia next month, and a fifth S-400 system will be ready for deployment by February 2027.
The S-400 system, of which India is seeking to buy another five from Russia in the coming year, can counter ballistic missiles, aircraft, unmanned combat air systems, kamikaze drones, and loitering ammunition from a range of 40km to 400 km. The S-400 proved itself during Operation Sindoor, ensuring that no ballistic missile or rocket fired by Pakistan hit the Indian territory, apart from knocking down Pakistani fighters, AEW&C aircraft, and ELINT platforms from the skies till as far as west of the Indus.
India prepares against Chinese threat
In the backdrop of China planning to supply J-35 fifth-generation fighters to Rawalpindi in 2027, India has decided to manufacture and acquire long-range stand-off weapons and loitering ammunition to counter Chinese long-range air-to-air missiles such as the PL-15 E (Extended), and air defence systems such as the HQ 9BE. PAF used Chinese J-10 fighters in tandem with Swedish AWACS to fire 200km range twin-data link PL-15 E missiles during Op Sindoor.
“We know the future war will be without contact with stand-off weapons. “Whoever has a longer-range missile and better anti-missile capability will have an edge,” said a top military officer.
Also Read I Defence, space, trade: The 75-year-old ‘iron brotherhood’ of China and Pakistan
The second official cited above said that India is aware that Beijing and Ankara are bolstering Pakistan militarily, Washington is providing an F-16 upgradation package, and Riyadh is releasing capital as compensation for Mecca Alliance support against Iranian-backed Houthis. Though Pakistan is seeking IMF support and has low forex reserves, it is buying eight Yuan (Hangor)-class AIP diesel attack submarines from China (over $5 billion), with one already deployed by the Pakistan Navy in June 2026, he added. Meanwhile, Turkey is upgrading its Agosta 90 B submarines and supplying long-range kamikaze drones to Pakistan, and China has already supplied armed Wing Loong II missile firing drones to boost Pakistan’s military-aerial capability, the people said.
In light of the national security assessment emanating from these acquisitions, coupled with the cross-border terror threat from Pakistan, India is preparing to bolster not only on long-range air-to -air, air-to-ground and ground-to-ground stand-off weapons but also upgrade its border infrastructure on the LAC, the officials added.

title: In Bengal, voters await their fate as judicial tribunals’ functioning comes under scrutiny
description: On September 18, the ECINET portal introduced an OTP-based system to check the status of appeals against exclusion. | India News
author: Himanshi Dahiya
content:
In Bengal, voters await their fate as judicial tribunals’ functioning comes under scrutiny
On September 18, the ECINET portal introduced an OTP-based system to check the status of appeals against exclusion.
Hasana Bibi Molla had voted in four assembly elections when her name was first flagged in January 2026 for logical discrepancy during the West Bengal special intensive revision. Molla, an elector from the Magrahat Paschim assembly constituency, had a spelling mismatch — a common reason for people ending up in the logical discrepancy list, which was 6 million strong at the time. In March, she was cleared by a judicial officer. In the same month, her name was included in the final roll and she voted on April 29 in the assembly elections.
On April 17, she realised her inclusion was challenged by the state’s Chief Electoral Officer (CEO) in front of the judicial tribunal.
Worse, her family says she cannot track the progress of her case on the West Bengal adjudication dashboard on the Election Commission of India’s ECINET portal.
“Whenever we try to log in to the portal, the pop-up says, ‘mobile number not provided while filing the appeal.’ We could track the application before September 18,” Hasana’s nephew, Abdul Halim Molla, told HT.
There was no response from ECI or Bengal CEO.
Also Read: ECI asks states, UTs to rectify electoral rolls during SSR
Hasana has lived in the same locality since 2005 and could link her to the base 2002 SIR list. HT spoke to at least 10 voters across West Bengal who described the same problem. All had been included in the adjudication supplementary lists, and all say the appeals against them became untraceable on the portal after September 18. They are part of the 1.6 million appeals filed by the state CEO against inclusions in the voter list.
Before September 18, electors who had an appeal filed against them could enter their EPIC numbers on the adjudication dashboard on the ECINET portal and it would display their appeal ID and status. For Hasina, the portal showed a ‘pending’ status until September 17 when she last checked.
On September 18, the ECINET portal introduced an OTP-based system to check the status of appeals against exclusion. From then until November 18, the “Track Appeal for Individuals (Under Adjudication)” page on voters.eci.gov.in returned a “Something went wrong” error for voters facing an appeal against their inclusion, according to screen recordings by electors seen by HT.
On Thursday, November 19, the error message changed. When an elector tries to check the status of their appeal, the portal now says: “Mobile number not provided while filing the appeal.”
In an affidavit before the Supreme Court last month, ECI said that of 3.8 million appeals filed before the tribunals, 2.2 million were filed by voters whose names were deleted, and 1.6 million challenged the inclusion of voters. The poll panel told the court that officers of the state CEO’s office filed the 1.6 million appeals against inclusion.
Appeals against inclusion mostly carry 17-digit IDs, while appeals against exclusion carry 20-digit IDs. The 17-digit appeals return the error. The 20-digit ones require an additional OTP, sent to the mobile number the appellant provided during filing. This is separate from the OTP for general account login, as per an analysis by Civic Research Group, a Kolkata-based research collective.
HT reviewed a screen recording of the portal after September 18, in which a known appeal against an elector’s inclusion could not be retrieved. A screenshot from before that date shows the same elector’s appeal, filed on April 5, listed as “pending” and visible to him.
Hasana’s family now has no idea what lies ahead. They have not been summoned to any hearing, and the only local official they could turn to had no answers. “We contacted our BLO who said he has no clue about these appeals. We haven’t received a notice for hearing, yet. Now we can’t even track the appeal status. How will she get back on the roll?” her nephew Abdul asked.
SIR began in West Bengal in November 2025. The draft roll in December removed more than 5.8 million names, which officials attributed to deaths, absence, permanent shifting and duplicate entries.
Also Read: 2.58 crore eligible voters still off UP electoral rolls, says CEO
When the final roll came out on February 28, over 6.3 million, names were deleted, and another 6 million placed “under adjudication”, largely over logical discrepancies in their enumeration forms.
The 19 judicial tribunals’ functioning has come under scrutiny. According to ECI’s affidavit before the top court, only 126,194 appeals were decided by September 21, while 3.7 million were pending. On November 23, the top court asked ECI to set up more tribunals.
For Hasana, until the portal allows access, her family can only wait, with no notice and no way to know how she will stay on the roll.

title: FIR registered against CPI(M) leader T I Madhusoodanan in Kannur over 'inflammatory speech'
description: Kerala police booked CPI(M) leader T.I. Madhusoodanan over an alleged provocative speech at a DYFI meeting following the Dhanaraj murder case verdict. | India News
author: PTI
content:
FIR registered against CPI(M) leader T I Madhusoodanan in Kannur over 'inflammatory speech'
Kerala police booked CPI(M) leader T.I. Madhusoodanan over an alleged provocative speech at a DYFI meeting following the Dhanaraj murder case verdict.
Published on: Nov 27, 2026, 05:44:27 IST
PTI
Share via
Copy link
Kannur (Keralam), Nov 26: A case was on Thursday registered against CPI(M) district secretariat member T I Madhusoodanan on a complaint alleging that he made a provocative speech at a public meeting organised by the DYFI in Payyannur recently.
The FIR has been registered under sections 192 (wantonly giving provocation with intent to cause riot), 351 (criminal intimidation) and 352 (intentional insult with intent to provoke breach of peace) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita on a complaint by Kerala Students Union state vice president P Muhammed Shammas to the state police chief.
According to the complaint, Madhusoodanan at the DYFI event held in Payyannur as part of the Koothuparamba Martyrs' Day celebrations, allegedly made a speech which could disrupt the peace and incite the opposing party's members to a riot.
The complainant also submitted visuals of the speech as evidence.
Earlier in the day, state Home Minister Ramesh Chenithala had said the Home Department was taking the remarks seriously and that the police were collecting the full text of the speech for examination.
Madhusoodanan had made the allegedly inflammatory speech following the court verdict in the Dhanaraj murder case.
A court in Thaliparamba had on Wednesday acquitted 16 BJP-RSS workers and convicted three key accused in the 2016 murder of CPI(M) local leader C V Dhanaraj.

title: From Thane To Konkan, Maharashtra BJP Plans December Push To Strengthen Grassroots Connect
description: The campaign, titled ‘Seva Doot Abhiyan’, will run from December 1 to 25 across the country to mark 25 years of Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s public life
author: Pathikrit Sen Gupta, Mayuresh Ganapatye
content:
From Thane To Konkan, Maharashtra BJP Plans December Push To Strengthen Grassroots Connect
The campaign, titled ‘Seva Doot Abhiyan’, will run from December 1 to 25 across the country to mark 25 years of Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s public life
Got Question about the News?
The Maharashtra BJP is preparing to take its organisational network beyond party offices and into villages, neighbourhoods and assembly constituencies through a 25-day public outreach campaign beginning December 1st. State BJP president Ravindra Chavan has asked party workers across the Thane-Konkan region to work in close coordination and use the exercise to strengthen the party’s connect with people.
The campaign, titled ‘Seva Doot Abhiyan’, will run from December 1 to 25 across the country to mark 25 years of Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s public life. In Maharashtra, the BJP plans to focus on direct interaction with citizens, particularly beneficiaries of government welfare schemes, while taking information about Central and state government initiatives to the grassroots.
- Maharashtra BJP Chief Uses 2011, 2024 G20 Photos To Counter Rahul Gandhi’s Attack On PM Modi
- BJP To Launch 'Seva Doot Abhiyan' From December 1 To Mark PM Modi's 25 Years In Public Life
- WHO Congratulates India On 1 Crore HPV Vaccine Doses; 6 States Achieve 100% Target Coverage
- 2027 Elections, Poll Strategy, Organisation To Be In Focus At BJP's National Office-Bearers Meet From Tomorrow
As part of the preparations, Chavan attended a Thane-Konkan divisional workshop in Panvel, where party office-bearers and workers were briefed on the campaign’s structure, implementation and organisational planning. The meeting focused on how the programme should be carried out at the local level and the need for coordination between different party units.
Chavan said the campaign should reach every section of society, with party workers making an effort to understand people’s problems and needs and connect them with available assistance. He stressed that information about welfare schemes must reach the last person and should not remain confined to government publicity or party platforms.
He also called for better coordination among office-bearers and workers, making it clear that the effectiveness of the campaign would depend on its execution on the ground.
The Thane-Konkan belt holds organisational significance for the BJP, with a mix of urban, semi-urban and rural constituencies. The workshop was attended by state general secretary and MLA Madhavi Naik, MP Dr Hemant Savara, MP Dhairyasheel Patil, MLAs Prashant Thakur, Pramod Jathar and Vikrant Patil, and North Raigad district president Avinash Koli, along with other regional office-bearers and party workers.
During the campaign, BJP leaders and workers will visit assembly constituencies and villages, interact with residents and explain government schemes and initiatives.
The Maharashtra BJP is launching a 25-day public outreach campaign named 'Seva Doot Abhiyan' starting December 1.
The nationwide campaign marks 25 years of Prime Minister Narendra Modi's public life.
State BJP president Ravindra Chavan led a Thane-Konkan divisional workshop in Panvel to brief party workers on campaign implementation.
The campaign aims to directly interact with citizens, focus on welfare scheme beneficiaries, and take government initiatives to the grassroots.
For the Maharashtra BJP, the December exercise is more than a nationwide organisational programme. It offers an opportunity to take its welfare agenda directly to voters and keep its grassroots machinery active. Whether these visits translate into meaningful public engagement, rather than one-way political messaging, will be the real test of the campaign.
Quick Answers
The Seva Doot Abhiyan is a 25-day public outreach campaign running from December 1 to 25 to mark 25 years of Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s public life. Led by state BJP president Ravindra Chavan, the initiative focuses on direct citizen interactions, promoting government welfare schemes, and strengthening the party's grassroots connect from Thane to Konkan.

title: Vijay's TVK Claims DMK Planning To Join BJP Amid Delimitation Buzz: 'What Use Is A Beard On A Goat'
description: The ruling TVK has claimed that the DMK is preparing to join hands with the BJP in Tamil Nadu, as the Centre plans to revive the delimitation-linked women's reservation Bill
author: Meemansa Shekhawat, Meemansa Shekhawat
content:
Vijay's TVK Claims DMK Planning To Join BJP Amid Delimitation Buzz: 'What Use Is A Beard On A Goat'
The ruling TVK has claimed that the DMK is preparing to join hands with the BJP in Tamil Nadu, as the Centre plans to revive the delimitation-linked women's reservation Bill
The ruling Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam (TVK) has claimed that the Dravida Munnetra Kazhagam (DMK) is preparing to join hands with the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) in Tamil Nadu, as the Centre plans to revive the delimitation-linked women’s reservation Bill during the proposed special sitting of Parliament.
The Central government has proposed a special parliamentary sitting from November 30 to December 3, 2026, with the Lok Sabha reconvening on November 30 and the Rajya Sabha on December 2.
- Karthigai Deepam Row: Annamalai Calls TVK’s Move ‘Historic Blunder’, Vijay's Party Cites 'Social Justice'
- Kallakurichi MLA Row Explodes: Udhayanidhi Stalin Meets Governor, Demands CBI Probe | BREAKING
- Udhayanidhi Meets Tamil Nadu Governor, Demands CBI Probe Into TVK MLA Arul Vignesh Case | News18
- 'Backstabbed Countless Devotees': BJP Fumes At Vijay's TVK Over Karthigai Deepam Row
Accusing the DMK of abandoning its ideological position, Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay’s TVK invoked former CM CN Annadurai’s famous question, “What is the use of a beard for a goat and a Governor for a country?"
The attack followed Leader of the Opposition Udhayanidhi Stalin’s meeting with Governor Rajendra Vishwanath Arlekar, which the TVK has described as an indicator of DMK’s inclination towards the BJP.
In a strongly-worded remark posted on X, it said, “The clay-idol dynasty, which swallowed up the DMK of the great scholar Anna, who asked, ‘What use is a beard on a goat or a governor for a state?’ and turned it into a family party, is proving through today’s meeting with the governor that all its loud claims from one stage to the next about being ideological stalwarts are nothing but empty bluster."
“ஆட்டுக்குத் தாடியும் நாட்டுக்கு ஆளுநரும் எதற்கு?" என்று கேட்ட பேரறிஞர் அண்ணாவின் திமுகவை கபளீகரம் செய்து, குடும்பக் கட்சியாக மாற்றிய மண்ணாங்கட்டிப் பரம்பரை, தாங்கள் கொள்கைக் குன்றுகள் என்று மேடைக்கு மேடை முழங்குவதெல்லாம் வெறும் வாய்ச்சவடால் என்பதை இன்றைய ஆளுநர் சந்திப்பின் மூலம் நிரூபிக்கிறது.ஆட்சியில் இருந்தவரை ஆளுநரைப் பேசவிடாமல் செய்துவிட்டோம் என்று கொக்கரித்துவிட்டு, இப்போது “ஆபத்பாந்தவனே" என்று ஆளுநரின் காலில் விழவும் தயாராகிவிட்டனர்.
“கலைஞரின் ஆசி பெற்ற சின்னம் தாமரை" என்ற வரலாறு மீண்டும் அரங்கேறப் போகிறது. அதற்கான அறிகுறிதான், சுமார் 14 ஆண்டுகளுக்குப் பிறகு உதயநிதி தலைமை நிர்வாகியாக இருக்கும் முரசொலியில் பாஜகவின் மாநிலத் தலைவரின் நேர்காணல் இடம்பெற்றிருப்பது.
பாசிசப் பாயாசம் பருகக் கொத்தடிமைகள் தயாராக இருக்கையில், மண்ணாங்கட்டிப் பரம்பரைக்கு கொள்கையாவது, கொய்யாக்காயாவது என்ற மனநிலைதான் !
அன்று போலவே பாஜகவைத் தமிழ்நாட்டில் வளர்க்கும் பணியை திமுக தலைமையேற்று நடத்தவிருக்கிறது.
திமுக ஒரு தீயசக்தி என்பதை மீண்டும் மீண்டும் நிரூபிக்கும் மண்ணாங்கட்டிப் பரம்பரைக்கு வாழ்த்துகள் !
— TVK IT Wing Official (@TVKHQITWingOffl) November 26, 2026
“After crowing that they had kept the governor from speaking for as long as they were in power, they are now ready to fall at the governor’s feet and call him ‘our savior in times of trouble'", said the TVK.
CM Vijay’s party also cited a report on BJP state president Nainar Nagenthran carried by the DMK mouthpiece, Murasoli.
“The history of ‘the lotus, the symbol blessed by Kalaignar’ is about to repeat itself. The sign of that is the interview with the BJP’s state president appearing in Murasoli, where Udhayanidhi is the chief executive, after nearly 14 years", it said.
The TVK alleged that the DMK was planning to “take the lead in nurturing the BJP" in Tamil Nadu.
“With the slaves ready to lap up fascist gruel, the clay-idol dynasty is in a state of mind that says, ‘At least some ideology, or even a guava leaf!’ Just as it did back then, the DMK is about to take the lead in nurturing the BJP in Tamil Nadu. Congratulations to the clay-idol dynasty, which will keep proving over and over that the DMK is an evil force!" it said.
There was no official reaction from the DMK at the time of filing this report.
The DMK, led by former CM MK Stalin, has opposed the delimitation bill in the past, arguing that the exercise would lead to a reduction in Tamil Nadu’s share of Parliamentary seats.
However, any move to back the proposed bill in the Parliament would be seen as the DMK’s response to its former ally, the Congress. Former CM MK Stalin’s party had fallen out with the Congress after it joined hands with the TVK following the Tamil Nadu Assembly elections 2026.
Quick Answers
The TVK claimed the DMK is preparing to align with the BJP as the Centre plans to revive the delimitation-linked women's reservation Bill and following a meeting between Leader of the Opposition Udhayanidhi Stalin and Governor Rajendra Vishwanath Arlekar.

title: Delimitation Dilemma: Is Rahul Gandhi Ready For The Sonia Gandhi Test?
description: The larger question is whether the government has regained its mojo while the Opposition has lost the momentum it had briefly managed to generate
author: Pathikrit Sen Gupta, Pallavi Ghosh
content:
Delimitation Dilemma: Is Rahul Gandhi Ready For The Sonia Gandhi Test?
The larger question is whether the government has regained its mojo while the Opposition has lost the momentum it had briefly managed to generate
Got Question about the News?
With the government recommending a special session of Parliament to push the Delimitation Bill, the spotlight is once again on Rahul Gandhi. After leading an aggressive Opposition campaign on the streets just days ago, his conspicuous absence raises questions about the Congress’s political strategy.
Given the high-decibel protests demanding the resignation of Election Commissioner of India Gyanesh Kumar, one would have expected Rahul Gandhi to lead the charge, particularly on Constitution Day. Instead, he was missing in action.
- 'Just A Side Player': Rahul Gandhi Says India 'Looking' As Pakistan Negotiates US-Iran War
- Rahul Gandhi Targets BJP-RSS Over Hindu Traditions, Says They Spread Fear And Hatred | News18
- Rahul Gandhi Shares Riteish Deshmukh-Genelia's Photo Amid 'Lap Remark' Row
- 1962 War To 'Hindu Rate Of Growth': Kiren Rijiju's 4 Questions To Congress After Rahul Gandhi's PM Jibe
The larger question is whether the government has regained its mojo while the Opposition has lost the momentum it had briefly managed to generate.
The Congress may have underestimated the possibility of its allies breaking ranks over the Delimitation Bill. The first setback came when Supriya Sule indicated that her party could consider supporting the legislation, citing its past backing of the government on issues such as GST and Operation Sindoor.
The DMK’s position has also raised questions, while AAP is expected to oppose the Bill. The Trinamool Congress could potentially see some MPs abstaining. But the biggest test may come from the Samajwadi Party. Although the SP has opposed the Bill, any abstentions or cross-voting could leave the Congress increasingly isolated.
THE ALLIES’ TEST
Rahul Gandhi had sought to turn street protests into a showcase of Opposition unity. But the real litmus test is now inside Parliament. The government appears confident of its numbers, but Rahul Gandhi’s credibility as the leader of a broader Opposition alliance is at stake.
The Congress has increasingly projected him as the face of the Opposition for the next Lok Sabha elections. But can he hold together disparate allies and play the role Sonia Gandhi did in 2004, when she became the glue that held the UPA together?
There are already questions within the Congress about the political positions of allies such as the DMK and the Pawar-led NCP. More importantly, the episode could expose a deeper problem: whether the Congress is still seen as an indispensable political force and a credible alternative to the BJP.
While Rahul Gandhi has raised issues such as vote chori and the economy, the Opposition’s street mobilisation at home appears to have lost steam. Constitution Day offered an opportunity to revive that momentum, but his absence was conspicuous.
Meanwhile, factionalism in Kerala and Punjab adds to the Congress’s challenges, even as the party struggles to manage its allies.
Ultimately, the question is whether Rahul Gandhi can emerge as an effective counterweight to the Prime Minister and hold together a fragmented Opposition. Did the Congress declare victory too early when it sensed a change in the political tide? And has that momentum already begun to slip away?
Quick Answers
Opposition parties face deep divisions over the Delimitation Bill, threatening alliance unity. Supriya Sule indicated her party might support the legislation, while the DMK's position has raised questions, AAP is expected to oppose it, and the Samajwadi Party's stance remains a critical test.

title: Tamil Nadu, Kerala face heavy rain; Delhi, north India under fog watch
description: The IMD forecasts heavy rainfall, thunderstorms, and gusty winds in Tamil Nadu, Puducherry, Karaikal, Kerala, Mahe, and Andhra Pradesh, while dense fog is expected in northern and northeastern regions
author: CNBCTV18.com
content:
Tamil Nadu, Kerala face heavy rain; Delhi, north India under fog watch
- Edited byTenzin Norzom
- Published OnNov 27, 2026 | 06:07 IST
- Last Updated OnNov 27, 2026 | 06:07 IST
The IMD forecasts heavy rainfall, thunderstorms, and gusty winds in Tamil Nadu, Puducherry, Karaikal, Kerala, Mahe, and Andhra Pradesh, while dense fog is expected in northern and northeastern regions
Several parts of south India are likely to remain wet on Friday, with the India Meteorological Department forecasting isolated heavy rainfall over Tamil Nadu, Puducherry and Karaikal as well as Kerala and Mahe.
The weather department has also warned of thunderstorms accompanied by lightning and gusty winds over parts of the southern peninsula, while dense fog is likely to affect parts of north and northeast India.
Tamil Nadu, Kerala to see heavy rain
Isolated heavy rainfall is very likely over Tamil Nadu, Puducherry and Karaikal and Kerala and Mahe on Friday, according to the IMD.
Thunderstorms with lightning and gusty winds of 30-40 kmph are also likely at isolated places over Tamil Nadu, Puducherry and Karaikal, Kerala and Mahe, Lakshadweep and Andhra Pradesh.
Andhra Pradesh is also likely to experience strong surface winds at isolated places.
The IMD said a trough in the easterlies extending from the Comorian area to South Interior Karnataka is influencing weather over the southern peninsula. An upper-air cyclonic circulation over the northwest Bay of Bengal and adjoining Odisha-West Bengal coast is also present.
The weather department expects fairly widespread to widespread rainfall over Kerala and Mahe and Lakshadweep through November 28, while rainfall is likely to remain scattered over several other parts of south India.
Dense fog in Delhi, Punjab and other northern areas
Dense fog is very likely at isolated places over Haryana, Chandigarh and Delhi and Punjab on Friday. Similar conditions are expected over parts of Uttar Pradesh, Himachal Pradesh and the northeastern states, including Assam and Meghalaya, Nagaland, Manipur, Mizoram and Tripura.
The IMD has warned that dense fog could affect airports, highways and railway routes, leading to slower travel and difficult driving conditions.
Delhi is expected to remain mainly clear apart from mist or shallow fog at isolated places in the morning. The maximum temperature is likely to stay between 25°C and 27°C, while the minimum could fall to 8°C-10°C.
Cold wave warning for East Rajasthan
Cold wave conditions are very likely at isolated places over East Rajasthan through November 28. The IMD has advised people to take precautions against prolonged exposure to cold.
The weather department has also indicated that an upper-air cyclonic circulation is likely to emerge over the South Andaman Sea around November 29. A low-pressure area could subsequently form over the South Andaman Sea and adjoining Andaman & Nicobar Islands and southeast Bay of Bengal around November 30.

title: Special Parliament session from Nov 30 may take up delimitation-linked Women's Reservation Bill
description: Parliamentary Affairs Minister Kiren Rijiju announced that Parliament will reconvene for a special sitting to transact essential government business, with Lok Sabha meeting on November 30 and Rajya Sa
author: Srabastee Biswas
content:
Special Parliament session from Nov 30 may take up delimitation-linked Women's Reservation Bill
- Edited byAjay Vaishnav
- Published OnNov 26, 2026 | 19:41 IST
- Last Updated OnNov 26, 2026 | 22:33 IST
Parliamentary Affairs Minister Kiren Rijiju announced that Parliament will reconvene for a special sitting to transact essential government business, with Lok Sabha meeting on November 30 and Rajya Sa
The government has called for a special sitting of Parliament from November 30 to transact "essential government business", with a PTI report saying that the delimitation-linked women's reservation Constitution amendment bill could be among the key items on the agenda.
Parliamentary Affairs Minister Kiren Rijiju said on Thursday that the government had requested the presiding officers of both Houses to reconvene Parliament next week.
"The Government has requested Hon'ble Speaker, Lok Sabha and Hon'ble Chairman, Rajya Sabha to reconvene Lok Sabha on Monday, 30th November, 2026 and Rajya Sabha on Wednesday, 2nd December, 2026 respectively to transact essential Government Business," Rijiju said in a post on X.
He added that, subject to business requirements, the sittings of both Houses may conclude on December 3.
The proposed sitting would be a continuation of the Monsoon Session, which was adjourned sine die on August 13 but has not yet been formally prorogued.
The announcement comes ahead of a Union Cabinet meeting scheduled for Friday.
PTI reported that the Cabinet is likely to discuss the Constitution amendment bill that seeks to provide 33% reservation for women in Parliament and state legislatures and is linked to a proposed delimitation exercise.
Prime Minister Narendra Modi, in a signed article published on Thursday, referred to the proposed legislation and said the government remained committed to ensuring greater representation for women in legislatures. He also criticised the defeat of the Bill in Parliament earlier this year.
The proposed amendment seeks to facilitate the implementation of women's reservation through a delimitation exercise that would increase the strength of the Lok Sabha from the current 543 seats to a maximum of 850 seats.
The government had earlier attempted to secure passage of the Bill in April, but it failed to obtain the required two-thirds majority in the Lok Sabha. In the current effective strength of 540 members, the threshold for passage is 361 votes.
The NDA currently has around 320 members in the Lok Sabha and would require support from other parties to secure the numbers needed for passage.
Since April, the composition of the House has changed following shifts by several MPs between political formations. These changes have improved the ruling alliance's position, although additional support would still be required if the legislation is brought back.
The special sitting is also expected to take place amid continuing political disputes over issues including the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls and opposition demands concerning Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar, raising the possibility of a contentious session if the proposed legislation is taken up for debate.
In a separate development, ANI reported that the Congress Parliamentary Strategy Group will meet in Delhi on Friday, November 27, at 4:30 pm to discuss the party’s strategy for the upcoming Winter Session of Parliament, which is scheduled to begin on November 30.

author: भूपेंद्र राय
content:
गुरु नानक देव जी का प्रकाश पर्व मनाने पाकिस्तान गए सिख श्रद्धालुओं के जत्थे से 3 लोग लापता हो गए हैं. लापता हुए तीनों श्रद्धालु पंजाब के रहने वाले हैं. बताया गया है कि इस बार भारत से कुल 2,339 सिख श्रद्धालुओं का जत्था पाकिस्तान गया था. यह जत्था 22 नवंबर को ननकाना साहिब पहुंचा था. 23 और 24 नवंबर को सभी श्रद्धालु ननकाना साहिब में ही रुके थे, लेकिन 25 नवंबर की सुबह जब जत्था अगले पड़ाव 'पंजा साहिब' के लिए रवाना होने को तैयार हुआ, तो ये तीनों श्रद्धालु वहां मौजूद नहीं थे.
जैसे ही खबर फैली कि तीन श्रद्धालु लापता हैं तो सब हैरान रह गए और उनकी तलाश शुरू की गई. काफी तलाश के बाद भी उनका कोई सुराग नहीं लग पाया है. बताया जा रहा है कि पाकिस्तान पुलिस तीनों की तलाश में जुटी है.
इस मामले में बीजेपी नेता और दिल्ली सिख गुरुद्वारा प्रबंधक कमेटी (DSGMC) के अध्यक्ष हरमीत सिंह कालका का बयान भी सामने आया है. उनका कहना है कि 'मुझे इस घटना की जानकारी मिली है कि SGPC की तरफ से जो जत्था गया था, उसमें से तीन लोग लापता हैं. अब यह देखना होगा कि जो यात्री वहां से गए हैं, क्या वे अपनी मर्जी से गए हैं? पहली नजर में लगता है कि वे अपनी मर्जी से ही गए हैं, लेकिन अगर लोग ऐसी हरकतें करते हैं तो यह बिल्कुल सही नहीं है और बेहद अफसोसजनक बात है.'
ਪਰਮਜੀਤ ਸਿੰਘ ਸਰਨਾ ਵੱਲੋਂ ਲਗਾਏ ਗਏ ਦੋਸ਼ਾਂ ਦਾ ਤਿੱਖਾ ਜਵਾਬ । #StrongResponse #FactBasedReply #PoliticalDebate #DSGMC #SikhLeadership https://t.co/DaPu0wIvcw
— Harmeet Singh Kalka (@hskalka) November 26, 2026
कालका ने आगे कहा कि पाकिस्तान सरकार को इस मामले की गंभीरता से जांच करनी चाहिए. उन्होंने नसीहत देते हुए कहा कि पहले जो हालात रहे हैं, उसे देखते हुए लोगों को सोचना चाहिए कि ऐसी हरकतों से न केवल आपका, बल्कि पूरी सिख कौम का सिर शर्म से झुकता है.
ननकाना साहिब सिख धर्म का प्रमुख तीर्थस्थल है, जो पाकिस्तान के पंजाब प्रांत में आता है. यह एक ऐतिहासिक शहर है और यहीं सिखों के पहले गुरु, गुरु नानक देव जी का जन्म हुआ था. यह जगह लाहौर से करीब 80 किलोमीटर दक्षिण-पश्चिम की तरफ पड़ती है. भारत और पाकिस्तान के बीच 1974 में हुए धार्मिक स्थलों के प्रोटोकॉल (एग्रीमेंट) के तहत, खास मौकों जैसे प्रकाश पर्व पर हर साल भारतीय श्रद्धालुओं के जत्थे यहां दर्शन के लिए जाते हैं.

title: अचानक संसद सत्र का बुलावा! 30 नवंबर को लोकसभा और 2 दिसंबर को राज्यसभा बैठक, किस बड़े बिल की तैयारी?
description: मोदी सरकार एक बार फिर देश को चौंकाने की तैयारी में है. सरकार ने लोकसभा अध्यक्ष और राज्यसभा सभापति से एक-एक दिन के लिए सदन की बैठक बुलाने का अनुरोध किया है. इन बैठकों का कार्य एजेंडा अभी स्पष्ट नहीं है. यह अनुरोध केंद्रीय संसदीय कार्य मंत्री किरेन रिजिजू ने भेजा है.
author: देवेंद्र कुमार
content:
मोदी सरकार एक बार फिर देश को चौंकाने की तैयारी में है. सरकार ने लोकसभा अध्यक्ष और राज्यसभा सभापति से एक-एक दिन के लिए सदन की बैठक बुलाने का अनुरोध किया है. इन बैठकों का कार्य एजेंडा अभी स्पष्ट नहीं है. यह अनुरोध केंद्रीय संसदीय कार्य मंत्री किरेन रिजिजू ने भेजा है.
किरेन रिजिजू ने सोशल मीडिया प्लेटफार्म एक्स पर पोस्ट करके लिखा, 'संसद के दोनों सदनों के स्पीकर्स से अनुरोध किया है कि वे 30 नवंबर 2026 को लोकसभा और 2 दिसंबर 2026 को राज्यसभा की बैठकें फिर से बुलाएं, ताकि आवश्यक सरकारी कामकाज निपटाया जा सके. कामकाज की जरूरतों को देखते हुए, दोनों सदनों की कार्यवाही 3 दिसंबर 2026 को समाप्त हो सकती है.'
(यह ब्रेकिंग खबर है. अपडेट हो रही है)

title: जब भारत के पास आकाश और S-400 है, तो 'भार्गवास्त्र' क्यों बनाया? चाहकर भी हवाई सीमा नहीं लांघ पाएगा दुश्मन
description: स्वार्म ड्रोन अटैक के बढ़ते खतरों को देखते हुए भारत अपनी क्षमताओं में लगातार विकास कर रहा है. ऐसे खतरों को ध्वस्त करने के लिए भारत ने एक अनोखे सिस्टम का विकास किया है, जो आसमान में मंडराते सैकड़ों ड्रोनों को भी तबाह कर सकता है.
author: देवेंद्र कुमार
content:
चीन और पाकिस्तान की ओर से बढ़ते ड्रोन हमलों के खतरों को देखते हुए भारत तेजी से अपनी एंटी-ड्रोन किलिंग क्षमताओं को विकसित कर रहा है. इसके लिए भारत ने 'भार्गवास्त्र' नाम का अनोखा सिस्टम विकसित किया है. इस सिस्टम में रॉकेट और छोटे आकार की मिसाइलें लगी होती हैं, जो दुश्मन का ड्रोन देखते ही उसे उड़ाकर हवा में ही खाक कर देती हैं.
इस एंटी ड्रोन सिस्टम का विकास सोलर डिफेंस एंड एयरोस्पेस लिमिटेड यानी SDAL ने किया है. 'भार्गवास्त्र' असल में एक 'व्हीकल-माउंटेड काउंटर स्वार्म ड्रोन सिस्टम' (VMCSDS) है. राजस्थान के पोखरण फायरिंग रेंज में 20 से 24 नवंबर 2026 के बीच इसके इन-हाउस ट्रायल किए गए. जिसमें वह आसमान से आ रहे सभी दुश्मनों को सटीकता से तबाह करने में कामयाब रहा.
डिफेंस एक्सपर्टों के मुताबिक, भारत ने यह सिस्टम दुश्मन के ड्रोन झुंडों से निपटने के लिए तैयार किया है. इस सिस्टम में रॉकेट और छोटी मिसाइलें, दोनों लगे होते हैं. जिससे यह आसमान में मंडराते किसी भी खतरे को खत्म कर सकता है. इस सिस्टम में एक साथ कई ड्रोनों को निशाना बनाने की क्षमता है.
'भार्गवास्त्र' में एयर डिफेंस रॉकेट और गाइडेड माइक्रो-मिसाइलों को एक वाहन पर जोड़ा गया है. यह लंबी और कम, दोनों दूरियों से आने वाले खतरों से निपट सकता है. यह सिस्टम दो चरणों में काम करता है. पहले चरण में आसमान में दिख रहे ड्रोन के झुंड को बिखेरने या खत्म करने के लिए रॉकेट दागे जाते हैं.
Solar Defence and Aerospace Limited (SDAL) has successfully designed, developed and integrated Bhargavastra, a Vehicle-Mounted Counter Swarm Drone System (VMCSDS), and completed its in-house development trials at Pokaran field firing ranges from 20th to 24th November 2026. The system offers an effective, two-layer defence against enemy drone swarms, with the capability to engage multiple drones simultaneously. Bhargavastra is India's first indigenously designed and developed two-layer vehiclemounted counter-swarm drone system, combining air defence rockets and guided micro-missiles to provide an integrated solution against this emerging threat. (Pics Source: Solar Defence and Aerospace Limited (SDAL)
— ANI (@ANI) November 26, 2026
इसके बाद भी अगर ड्रोन आगे बढ़ते हैं तो वाहन में लगी गाइडेड माइक्रो-मिसाइलें दागकर उन्हें गिरा दिया जाता है. चूंकि यह पूरा सिस्टम एक मिलिट्री ट्रक पर लोड है, इसलिए इसे रेगिस्तान, कठिन इलाकों या अन्य मोर्चों पर ले जाकर आसानी से तैनात किया जा सकता है.
इस सिस्टम के अगले हिस्से में एक कंट्रोल रूम में बना हुआ है. जबकि, ट्रक के ऊपर सेंसर, रडार और इलेक्ट्रो-ऑप्टिकल सिस्टम लगे हैं. ये सभी सिस्टम मिलकर आसमान में आ रहे ड्रोन, मिसाइलों, प्लेन की निगरानी करते हैं. जैसे ही रडार की ओर से दुश्मन के ड्रोन के आने का पता चलता है, तुरंत ही ऑटोमेटिक तरीके से रॉकेट और मिसाइलें एक्टिवेट हो जाती हैं और दुश्मन के ड्रोनों का बेड़ा आसमान में ही जलकर खत्म हो जाता है.
भारत की ओर से इस तरह की एंटी-ड्रोन क्षमता विकसित करने की सबसे बड़ी वजह उसके दुश्मन चीन और पाकिस्तान हैं. चीनी सेना बड़े ड्रोन झुंड की तकनीक पर काम कर रही है. उसने लद्दाख, उत्तराखंड और अरुणाचल प्रदेश से लगती एलएसी के पास ड्रोन बेस, हैंगर और सिग्नल जैमिंग सिस्टम भी लगाए हैं. इसकी वजह से ऊंचाई वाले इलाकों में भारत की सैन्य चौकियों और छावनियों के लिए ड्रोन हमले का खतरा काफी बढ़ गया है.
वहीं, पाकिस्तान अपनी आतंकी गतिविधियों को आगे बढ़ाने के लिए ड्रोन का इस्तेमाल कर रहा है. इसके सात ही, वह पंजाब, राजस्थान और जम्मू-कश्मीर की सीमा पर हथियार, विस्फोटक, नशीले पदार्थ और नकली नोट भी ड्रोनों के जरिए भेज रहा है. भारत पर हमले के लिए वह अपने सैन्य बेड़े में चीन और तुर्किये से विंग लूंग व बायराकटार जैसे ड्रोन जमा कर रहा है.
देश की दोनों सरहदों पर बढ़ते ड्रोन खतरे को देखते हुए भारत के लिए इस तरह की क्षमता विकसित करना अनिवार्य बना दिया है. वैसे भी, पारंपरिक सतह से हवा में मार करने वाली मिसाइलें महंगी होती हैं और बड़े लक्ष्यों के लिए बनाई जाती हैं. जबकि, छोटे ड्रोनों के झुंड पर महंगी मिसाइलें चलाना खर्चीला होता है और इससे मिसाइल भंडार भी जल्दी खत्म हो सकता है.
यहीं पर 'भार्गवास्त्र' सिस्टम की क्षमता काम आती है. आकाशतीर, पृथ्वी और बराक जैसी एयर डिफेंस में यूज होने वाली मिसाइलों की तुलना में 'भार्गवास्त्र' बहुत सस्ता है. इसका प्रतिक्रिया समय बहुत तेज है और एक साथ ड्रोन के पूरे झुंड को खत्म कर सकता है. ट्रक पर लोड होने की वजह से इसे हमले के बाद छिपाने और फुर्ती के साथ कहीं भी तैनात किया जा सकता है.
कुल मिलाकर, पड़ोस के दोनों दुश्मनों से बढ़ रहे खतरों को देखते हुए भारत पूरी तरह सचेत है. वे जिस तरह के हथियार अपने बेड़े में शामिल कर रहे हैं, भारत उन हथियारों का तोड़ अपने भंडार में जोड़ रहा है. जिससे अगर उन्होंने कभी भी हमले का दुस्साहस किया तो भारत की तीनों सेनाएं उन्हें कबाड़ का ढेर बनाने में देर न करें. 'भार्गवास्त्र' ठीक यही काम करने जा रहा है.

title: Fire Breaks Out at Cloth Godown on Kolkata’s AJC Bose Road; 10 Families Rescued
description: West Bengal Minister of State for Fire and Emergency Services Koushik Chowdhury said the situation is currently under control.
author: Asian News International
content:
Fire Breaks Out at Cloth Godown on Kolkata’s AJC Bose Road; 10 Families Rescued
West Bengal Minister of State for Fire and Emergency Services Koushik Chowdhury said the situation is currently under control.
- India News
- 2 min read
Kolkata, West Bengal: A fire broke out at a cloth godown in a multi-storey building on AJC Bose Road in the Mullickbazar area on Wednesday.
Multiple fire tenders were rushed to the spot, and firefighting operations are underway. No casualties have been reported so far.
Fire officer Shyam Chandra Mondal said the fire is on the ground floor and operations are still underway.
"It seems to be under control for now; we'll see how things progress. Ten fire tenders have arrived. We have also set up a fire pump at an open water source, which we are using to draw water for firefighting," he told ANI.
Advertisement
West Bengal Minister of State for Fire and Emergency Services Koushik Chowdhury said the situation is currently under control.
"There isn't a major fire, perhaps a small amount inside, but mostly, it is just smoke. Our fire brigade officers, including all the Assistant Fire Officers (AFOs), are doing an excellent job; they arrived promptly after receiving the alert. The local residents have also been very helpful, assisting right from the very beginning. Ten families were living here, and we have successfully rescued all of them; everyone else is safe," he told ANI.
Advertisement
On reaching the site, TMC MLA Sovandeb Chattopadhyay said the fire appears to be still burning with a great deal of smoke rising.
"It seems the fire originated in a godown located beneath the site, and subsequently spread to the entire area. It is likely that there will be significant damage, but the government will surely assist. Since the fire was not caused intentionally, but rather by an accident, it is expected that the government will extend some form of support," he told ANI.

title: India, China Held Talks in Eastern Sector Recently: MEA
description: "A meeting of the senior-most military commanders was held in the eastern sector recently; discussions between the two sides focused on improving border management and addressing outstanding issues along the LAC," Ministry of External Affairs (MEA) official spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal said.
author: Asian News International
content:
India, China Held Talks in Eastern Sector Recently: MEA
"A meeting of the senior-most military commanders was held in the eastern sector recently; discussions between the two sides focused on improving border management and addressing outstanding issues along the LAC," Ministry of External Affairs (MEA) official spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal said.
- India News
- 2 min read
New Delhi: India and China recently held a meeting of their senior-most military commanders in the eastern sector, with discussions centred on border management and addressing outstanding issues along the Line of Actual Control (LAC), the Ministry of External Affairs (MEA) announced on Wednesday.
Speaking at the weekly media briefing in New Delhi, MEA official spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal noted that New Delhi and Beijing maintain regular engagement through diplomatic and military mechanisms.
"India and China engage regularly through diplomatic and military mechanisms. A meeting of the senior-most military commanders was held in the eastern sector recently; discussions between the two sides focused on improving border management and addressing outstanding issues along the LAC. Such interactions are aimed at maintaining peace and tranquillity in the border areas and preventing any escalations," Jaiswal said.
Previously, on October 23, the MEA stated that both nations continue to rely on existing diplomatic and military mechanisms to settle outstanding issues and "avoid misunderstanding and miscalculation along the Line of Actual Control", while underlining that calm in the India-China border areas gets disturbed when Chinese troops depart from established patrolling patterns.
Advertisement
"As we have noted in the past, the situation in the India-China border areas gets disturbed from time to time when Chinese forces diverge from established patrolling patterns. Both sides continue to use existing diplomatic and military mechanisms to resolve outstanding issues and avoid misunderstanding and miscalculation along the Line of Actual Control," Jaiswal had remarked at that briefing.
He had further noted that both sides agreed to examine ways to improve understanding of the LAC in relevant areas to achieve better border management.
Advertisement
"I would also like to emphasise that the maintenance of peace and tranquillity in the border areas is essential for the overall development of bilateral relations," he had stated.
Earlier, on September 8, the MEA reported that the first senior-most military commander-level flag meeting took place along the LAC at Wacha on the Indian side in Arunachal Pradesh on September 6 and at Damai on the Chinese side on September 7.

title: Delhi High Court Allows Taj Mahal Photographers To Work Beyond 65, Strikes Down ASI's Age-Based Retirement Rule
description: The Delhi High Court has struck down the ASI's 65-year retirement limit for licensed Taj Mahal photographers, allowing them to continue working subject to medical fitness requirements and other conditions.
author: Asian News International
content:
Delhi High Court Allows Taj Mahal Photographers To Work Beyond 65, Strikes Down ASI's Age-Based Retirement Rule
The Delhi High Court has struck down the ASI's 65-year retirement limit for licensed Taj Mahal photographers, allowing them to continue working subject to medical fitness requirements and other conditions.
- India News
- 4 min read
New Delhi: The Delhi High Court has quashed the Archaeological Survey of India’s (ASI) policy fixing 65 years as the retirement age for licensed photographers working at the Taj Mahal, holding that the restriction is discriminatory and adversely affects their right to livelihood.
A division bench of Justice Prathiba M Singh and Justice Dinesh Bhatt observed that the photographers are independent professionals and not employees of the ASI. They should be allowed to continue their profession as long as their physical and mental faculties permit them to perform their duties.
The court observed that when the Supreme Court had struck down a similar age restriction for tourist guides, there was even less justification for imposing such a restriction on photographers, whose work involves considerably less physical exertion.
“These are self-employed persons, who ought to be permitted to work as long as their physical and mental faculties permit,” the bench observed.
Advertisement
The court was hearing two petitions filed by photographers challenging Clauses 9 and 9.3 of the ASI’s policy dated May 24, 2017, which prescribed medical fitness requirements after the age of 60 and fixed 65 years as the retirement age for licensed photographers working at centrally protected monuments.
The petitioners submitted that photography at the Taj Mahal was their sole source of livelihood and that several of them had been providing services at the monument for the last 30 to 40 years. They argued that the age restriction would deprive them and their families of their only source of income.
Advertisement
Opposing the petitions, the ASI argued that fixing an upper age limit was necessary to provide opportunities to younger photographers. It submitted that around 500 photographers were currently licensed to work at the Taj Mahal and that allowing older photographers to continue could restrict opportunities for younger professionals.
The authorities also raised concerns that some licensed photographers were sending nominees to the monument to provide photography services instead of performing the work themselves. They further submitted that some older photographers might not be sufficiently familiar with technological advancements in photography.
The High Court relied on the Supreme Court’s judgment in B.P. Sharma v. Union of India, in which a similar age restriction imposed on tourist guides had been struck down.
The bench noted that under Rule 8(d) of the Ancient Monuments and Archaeological Sites and Remains Rules, 1959, both photographers and tourist guides are required to obtain licences from the ASI to provide services within protected monuments.
It observed that tourist guides are required to accompany visitors and move around monuments, which may involve considerable physical exertion. Photographers, however, generally remain stationed at particular locations within the monument and provide their services there.
“The reasoning adopted by the Supreme Court in B.P. Sharma would, therefore, apply with greater force to the case of the Petitioners,” the court observed.
The bench further noted that with increasing life expectancy, professionals above the age of 65 can remain physically and mentally capable of performing their work. It also observed that the experience gained by photographers from working at the monument for several decades could be an advantage for tourists and visitors.
The court clarified that the ASI was entitled to require photographers to undergo medical fitness tests and furnish certificates from registered medical practitioners.
It held that the ASI could not curtail their livelihood merely on the ground that they had crossed the age of 65, subject to their meeting the prescribed fitness requirements.
While quashing the age restriction, the High Court also addressed the ASI’s concerns regarding licensed photographers allowing nominees to work in their place.
The court directed that no licensed photographer would be permitted to allow another person to use their licence or sub-license it in any manner. If any photographer was found doing so, the licence would be liable to be withdrawn with immediate effect.
The bench further directed that photographers would be required to undertake refresher courses conducted by the ASI to upgrade their skills and ensure quality services to tourists.
If the ASI conducts any test for photographers, the petitioners would also be required to appear in and qualify the same.
The court clarified that nominees already permitted under earlier court orders could continue only in cases involving licence holders with disabilities. No such permission would be granted to nominees of licence holders without disabilities.
The ASI was also permitted to conduct physical fitness tests or medical examinations of photographers after they attain the age of 65.
Subject to these conditions, the bench quashed Clause 9.3 of the 2017 policy prescribing 65 years as the retirement age for photographers.
It directed that the licences of the petitioners, which were stated to have been renewed to date, would be renewed for the remainder of the current year and thereafter on an annual basis.
