author: Anurag Animesh
content:
Hindi News / National News / उत्तर भारत में बढ़ेगी ठंड, 5 राज्यों में 2 से 4 डिग्री तक गिरेगा पारा, दिल्ली समेत कई राज्यों में कोहरे का अलर्ट
उत्तर भारत में बढ़ेगी ठंड, 5 राज्यों में 2 से 4 डिग्री तक गिरेगा पारा, दिल्ली समेत कई राज्यों में कोहरे का अलर्ट
उत्तर भारत में सर्दी का असर बढ़ने वाला है। मध्य प्रदेश, राजस्थान, छत्तीसगढ़, यूपी और बिहार में तापमान 2 से 4 डिग्री तक गिर सकता है। दिल्ली समेत कई राज्यों में घने कोहरे और दक्षिण भारत में बारिश का अलर्ट जारी है।
IMD Weather Forecast: उत्तर भारत के पहाड़ी और मैदानी इलाकों में सर्दी का असर लगातार बढ़ रहा है। कई राज्यों में तापमान में गिरावट दर्ज की जा रही है। इस बीच कुछ इलाकों में बारिश का दौर भी जारी है। भारतीय मौसम विभाग (IMD) के अनुसार, आने वाले दिनों में उत्तर भारत के कई हिस्सों में ठंड और बढ़ सकती है। मध्य प्रदेश, राजस्थान, छत्तीसगढ़, उत्तर प्रदेश और बिहार में न्यूनतम तापमान में 2 से 4 डिग्री सेल्सियस तक की गिरावट आने की संभावना है। इन राज्यों के कई स्थानों पर न्यूनतम तापमान पहले ही 10 डिग्री सेल्सियस से नीचे पहुंच चुका है।
इसके अलावा राष्ट्रीय राजधानी दिल्ली समेत उत्तर भारत के कई राज्यों में अगले तीन दिनों तक घने कोहरे की चेतावनी जारी की गई है। इससे सुबह और रात के समय दृश्यता प्रभावित हो सकती है।
अगले दो दिनों में कैसा रहेगा मौसम?
- पांच राज्यों में और गिरेगा तापमान
मौसम विभाग के मुताबिक, मध्य प्रदेश, राजस्थान, छत्तीसगढ़, उत्तर प्रदेश और बिहार में अगले दिनों के दौरान न्यूनतम तापमान 2 से 4 डिग्री सेल्सियस तक गिर सकता है। इससे इन राज्यों में ठंड का असर और बढ़ने की संभावना है। वहीं, पूर्वी राजस्थान के कुछ इलाकों में शीतलहर चल सकती है।
- दिल्ली समेत कई राज्यों में घने कोहरे की चेतावनी
दिल्ली, पंजाब, हरियाणा, हिमाचल प्रदेश और उत्तर प्रदेश के कुछ इलाकों में घना कोहरा छाने का अनुमान है। अगले तीन दिनों तक कोहरे का असर बने रहने की संभावना जताई गई है।
- दक्षिण भारत में बारिश और तेज हवाओं के आसार
उत्तर भारत में जहां ठंड बढ़ रही है, वहीं दक्षिण भारत के कुछ राज्यों में मौसम अलग रहने वाला है। आंध्र प्रदेश और केरल में तेज हवाएं चल सकती हैं। इसके अलावा तमिलनाडु और पुडुचेरी में 27 नवंबर को भारी बारिश होने की संभावना है।
जानें डिटेल्स
इस तरह आने वाले दिनों में देश के अलग-अलग हिस्सों में मौसम के कई रूप देखने को मिल सकते हैं। उत्तर भारत में ठंड और कोहरे का असर बढ़ेगा, जबकि दक्षिण भारत के कुछ क्षेत्रों में बारिश और तेज हवाएं परेशानी बढ़ा सकती हैं।

title: भारत में खाद्यान्न उत्पादन कैसे बढ़ा रहा है देश की कृषि ताकत? चावल, गेहूं से लेकर दलहन-तिलहन तक जानिए पूरी तस्वीर
description: भारत में खाद्यान्न उत्पादन लगातार बढ़ रहा है। जानिए चावल, गेहूं, मक्का, दलहन और तिलहन का उत्पादन कितना है, किन फसलों में भारत दुनिया में पहले स्थान पर है और सरकार का आत्मनिर्भरता पर क्या जोर है।
author: Anurag Animesh
content:
Hindi News / National News / भारत में खाद्यान्न उत्पादन कैसे बढ़ा रहा है देश की कृषि ताकत? चावल, गेहूं से लेकर दलहन-तिलहन तक जानिए पूरी तस्वीर
भारत में खाद्यान्न उत्पादन कैसे बढ़ा रहा है देश की कृषि ताकत? चावल, गेहूं से लेकर दलहन-तिलहन तक जानिए पूरी तस्वीर
भारत में खाद्यान्न उत्पादन लगातार बढ़ रहा है। जानिए चावल, गेहूं, मक्का, दलहन और तिलहन का उत्पादन कितना है, किन फसलों में भारत दुनिया में पहले स्थान पर है और सरकार का आत्मनिर्भरता पर क्या जोर है।
India Foodgrain Production: देश में खाद्यान्न उत्पादन ने नया रेकॉर्ड बनाया है। वर्ष 2025-26 में कुल खाद्यान्न उत्पादन 3785.38 लाख टन रहा, जो पिछले वर्ष के मुकाबले 208.06 लाख टन अधिक है। वहीं, अल नीनो और मानसून की देरी जैसी चुनौतियों के बावजूद खरीफ 2026-27 में 1671.43 लाख टन खाद्यान्न उत्पादन का अनुमान है। यह पिछले पांच साल के औसत से 97.67 लाख टन ज्यादा है। केंद्रीय कृषि मंत्री शिवराज सिंह चौहान ने बुधवार को दोनों वर्षों के उत्पादन अनुमान जारी किए।
जानें डिटेल्स
शिवराज ने पत्रकारों को बताया कि भारत चावल, दलहन, जूट, मोटे अनाज और मसालों के उत्पादन में दुनिया में पहले स्थान पर है। गेहूं, कपास, मूंगफली और फल-सब्जियों में दूसरे तथा गन्ना उत्पादन में ब्राजील के बाद दूसरे स्थान पर है। भारतीय चावल के निर्यात में भी पांच फीसदी की वृद्धि हुई है। अमेरिका, कनाडा और मध्य पूर्व सहित कई देशों में इसकी मांग बढ़ रही है। शिवराज ने कहा कि गेहूं-चावल में पर्याप्त भंडार के बाद अब दलहन और खाद्य तेलों में आत्मनिर्भरता सरकार की प्राथमिकता है। इसके लिए राष्ट्रीय दलहन और तिलहन मिशन चलाए जा रहे हैं।
गेहूं-चावल के बाद दलहन-तिलहन पर जोर
वर्ष 2025-26 में चावल उत्पादन 1551.54 लाख टन और गेहूं 1220.64 लाख टन रहा। मक्का उत्पादन 550.25 लाख टन, कुल मोटे अनाज 740.80 लाख टन और श्री अन्न 172.09 लाख टन दर्ज किया गया। दलहन उत्पादन 272.40 लाख टन रहा। इसमें चना 125.13, मूंग 43.96 और अरहर 35.99 लाख टन शामिल हैं।
तिलहन उत्पादन 432.55 लाख टन के रिकॉर्ड स्तर पर पहुंचा। मूंगफली 131.71 और सरसों 137.66 लाख टन रही, जबकि सोयाबीन उत्पादन 126.36 लाख टन दर्ज किया गया। गन्ना उत्पादन 5037.29 लाख टन, कपास 280.06 लाख गांठ और जूट-मेस्ता 94.28 लाख गांठ रहा।

title: पॅकेटबंद खाद्यपदार्थांवर साखर, मीठ, फॅटची माहिती देणे अनिवार्य
description: Special parliament session news: महिला आरक्षणासह मतदारसंघ फेररचना घटनादुरुस्ती विधेयक पुन्हा मांडण्याची शक्यता; बहुमतासाठी जुळवाजुळव सुरू.
author: पीटीआय
content:
नवी दिल्ली : पॅकेटबंद खाद्यपदार्थांवर छापण्यात येणार्‍या पोषणविषयक माहितीमध्ये अधिक स्पष्टता यावी यादृष्टीने सर्वोच्च न्यायालयाने गुरुवारी महत्त्वाचे निर्देश दिले. पोषणविषयक माहितीच्या तक्त्यात (फ्रंट-ऑफ-पॅकेज न्युट्रिशन लेबलिंग) केवळ ‘अतिरिक्त साखर’ आणि ‘अतिरिक्त फॅट’ अशी माहिती न देता ‘एकूण साखर’, ‘सॅच्युरेटेड फॅट’, तसेच मीठाचीही माहिती द्यावी, असे सर्वोच्च न्यायालयाने भारतीय अन्न सुरक्षा व मानक प्राधिकरणाला (एफएसएसएआय) सांगितले. उच्च प्रमाणात फॅट, साखर आणि मीठ असलेल्या पदार्थांसाठी स्वतंत्र धोक्याचे चिन्ह वापरण्याचे निर्देशही सर्वोच्च न्यायालयाने दिले.
‘एफओपीएनएल’ नियमांची चार महिन्यांच्या कालावधीत अंमलबजावणी सुरू करावी आणि नियमांचे काटेकोरपणे पालन होण्याची खबरदारी घेण्यासाठी प्रतिबंधात्मक उपायांसह सर्व खबरदारीची पावले उचलावीत, असे निर्देश न्या. जे.बी. पारडीवाला आणि न्या. के. विनोद चंद्रन यांच्या खंडपीठाने ‘एफएसएसएआय’ला दिले. ‘एफओपीएनएल’च्या प्रत्येक षटकोनात संबंधित खाद्यपदार्थातील घटक पदार्थांचे प्रमाणित चित्रात्मक सादरीकरण केलेले असेल, त्यामध्ये ‘हाय फॅट’, ‘हाय शुगर’ किंवा ‘हाय सॉल्ट’ याप्रमाणे शब्द वापरले जावेत, याची खबरदारी घेण्यासही न्यायालयाने ‘एफएसएसएआय’ला सांगितले. यासाठी ‘एफएसएसएआय’ने त्यांच्या भारतीय लोकांसाठी आहारविषयक मार्गदर्शक तत्त्वे (डीजीआय), २०२४पूर्वीच्या नियमांचा संदर्भ घ्यावा, असेही न्यायालयाने सुचवले.
पोषणविषयक साक्षरता ही देशाचे आरोग्य आणि उत्पादकतेसाठी केलेली गुंतवणूक आहे, असे निरीक्षण न्यायालयाने नोंदवले. ‘एफएसएसएआय’ने २०२०च्या अन्न सुरक्षा आणि मानक (शालेय मुलांसाठी सुरक्षित अन्न आणि संतुलित आहार) नियमांचे काटेकोरपणे पालन करावे अशी सूचनाही न्यायालयाने केली.
‘एफओपीएनएल’ म्हणजे काय?
पॅकेटबंद अन्नपदार्थ विकत घेताना ग्राहकांना माहितीपूर्ण निर्णय घेता यावा आणि अधिक सकस खाद्यपदार्थांची निवड करता यावी यासाठी त्यामध्ये कोणते घटक पदार्थ आहेत याची माहिती मिळावी यासाठी ‘फ्रंट-ऑफ-पॅकेज न्युट्रिशन लेबलिंग’ (एफओपीएनएल) हा तक्ता छापलेला असतो. भारतामध्ये यासंबंधी नियमांचे नियमन ‘एफएसएसएआय’कडून केले जाते.
केंद्र सरकारने शालेय अभ्यासक्रमात बदल करण्याबरोबरच संवादात्मक कार्यशाळा, अतिरिक्त आणि सह-अभ्यासक्रम उपक्रम यांसारख्या अतिरिक्त उपक्रमांच्या माध्यमातून मुलांना पोषणविषक साक्षरता शिकण्याची संधी द्यावी. – सर्वोच्च न्यायालय

title: संसदेचे विशेष अधिवेशन; मतदारसंघ फेररचनेचे घटनादुरुस्ती विधेयक नव्याने मांडणार?
description: Special parliament session news: महिला आरक्षणासह मतदारसंघ फेररचना घटनादुरुस्ती विधेयक पुन्हा मांडण्याची शक्यता; बहुमतासाठी जुळवाजुळव सुरू.
author: लोकसत्ता टीम
content:
नवी दिल्ली : महिला आरक्षणासह मतदारसंघ फेररचना घटनादुरुस्ती विधेयकावर लोकसभेत पराभव पत्कारावा लागल्यानंतर आठ महिन्यांतच केंद्र सरकारने संसदेचे विशेष अधिवेशन बोलावण्याचा निर्णय घेतला आहे. लोकसभेतचे कामकाज ३० नोव्हेंबरला तर, राज्यसभेचे कामकाज २ डिसेंबरला सुरू होईल. या अधिवेशनात कोणते विशिष्ट कामकाज वा विधेयके मांडली जातील हे अजून स्पष्ट झालेले नसले तरी महिला आरक्षणाशी जोडलेले लोकसभा मतदारसंघांच्या फेररचनेचे घटनादुरुस्ती विधेयक पुन्हा मांडले जाण्याची दाट शक्यता आहे.
केंद्र सरकारने अधिवेशन संस्थगित होऊन शंभराहून जास्त दिवस झाले तरी पावसाळी अधिवेशनाची समाप्ती केली नसल्याने ‘विशेष अधिवेशन’ बोलावले जाऊ शकते, असा कयास गेल्या दोन आठवड्यापासून केला जात होता. शिवाय, घटनादुरुस्ती विधेयकासाठी ‘विशेष अधिवेशन’ घेतले जाईल, असे केंद्र सरकारमधील सूत्रांची सूचित केले होते. केंद्रीय संसदीय कामकाजमंत्री किरेन रिजिजू यांनी गुरुवारी ‘एक्स’वर सरकारी कामकाज पूर्ण करण्यासाठी हे अधिवेशन बोलावले जात आहे, अशी घोषणा केली.
संसदेचे पावसाळी अधिवेशन १३ ऑगस्ट रोजी संस्थगित करण्यात आले होते. मात्र या अधिवेशनाच्या राष्ट्रपती द्रौपदी मुर्मू यांनी समाप्तीची घोषणा केली नव्हती. त्यामुळे पुढील आठवड्यात सोमवारी सुरू होणारे चार दिवसांच्या कालावधीचे अधिवेशन पावसाळी अधिवेशनाचा भाग असेल. वास्तविक, नोव्हेंबरच्या शेवटच्या आठवड्यामध्ये हिवाळी अधिवेशनाची सुरुवात होते. मात्र यावेळी पावसाळी अधिवेशनच पुनस्र्थापित करण्यात आले आहे.
घटनादुरुस्ती विधेयकामध्ये प्रत्येक राज्यात लोकसभेच्या ५० टक्के जागा वाढवण्याची हमी केंद्र सरकारने द्यावी, अशी मागणी विरोधकांनी केली होती.
ही मागणी मान्य करून नव्या विधेयकात तरतूद केली तर विधेयक मंजुरीचा मार्ग अधिक सुकर होऊ शकतो. लोकसभेमध्ये विधेयक मंजुरीसाठी ३६० सदस्यांच्या पाठिंब्याची गरज आहे. राष्ट्रवादी काँग्रेस शरदचंद्र पवार, द्रमुक, अकाली दल, वायएसआर काँग्रेस आदी पक्षांनी पाठिंबा दिला तर केंद्र सरकारकडे ३५४चे संख्याबळ असेल. आणखी ६ सदस्यांची पाठिंब्याची गरज भासत असली तरी विरोधी पक्षांच्या सहमतीने हे विधेयक संमत करण्याचा केंद्र सरकारचा प्रयत्न आहे. या विधेयकाविरोधातील काँग्रेसची भूमिका अजूनही कायम आहे.
संख्याबळासाठी जुळवाजुळव
* गेल्या तीन महिन्यांमध्ये केंद्र सरकारकडून घटनादुरुस्ती विधेयकासाठी दोन तृतीयांश संख्याबळाची जमवाजमव करण्याचा जोरदार प्रयत्न सुरू आहेत.
* विरोधकांच्या ‘इंडिया’ आघाडीतील घटक पक्षांची मनधरणी केली जात होती. ‘इंडिया’ आघाडीतील राष्ट्रवादी काँग्रेस शरदचंद्र पवार पक्ष व द्रमुक या दोन्ही पक्षांच्या नेत्यांशी संपर्क साधण्यात आला होता. या दोन्ही पक्षांनी दुरुस्तीसह आणल्या जाऊ शकणार्‍या विधेयकला विरोध दर्शवलेला नाही.
* याशिवाय आप, राष्ट्रीय जनता दल आदी विरोधी पक्षानी मतदानात सहभागी न होण्याचा निर्णय घेतला तर केंद्र सरकारकडे घटनादुरुस्ती विधेयक मंजूर करण्यासाठी पुरेसे संख्याबळ जमवता येऊ शकते, असे मानले जात आहे.
द्रमुक अनुकूल?
तमिळनाडूमध्ये सध्या सत्तेबाहेर असलेल्या द्रमुक पक्षाला प्रत्येक मुद्द्यावर भाजपला तीव्र विरोध करण्याची गरज नाही. जर तमिळनाडूचा लोकसभेतील सध्याचा सुमारे ७.२ टक्के जागांचा वाटा कायम राखला जाणार असेल, तर पक्ष विधेयकाचे समर्थन करेल, असे पक्षाच्या दोन वरिष्ठ नेत्यांनी सांगितले. तामिळनाडूचा सध्याचा प्रतिनिधित्वाचा वाटा अबाधित राहिल्यास, लोकसभेच्या जागा वाढवण्यास अनुकूल भूमिका असल्याचे या नेत्यांनी सांगितले.

title: कराराला उशीर नको! अमेरिकेशी व्यापाराच्या मुद्द्यावर निर्यातदारांचे सरकारला आवाहन
description: India US trade deal urgency grows as exporters back 17% tariff. अमेरिकेशी व्यापार करार, आयातशुल्क आणि निर्यातावरील परिणामाची सविस्तर माहिती.
author: लोकसत्ता टीम
content:
पीटीआय, नवी दिल्ली
‘भारताने अमेरिकेबरोबर व्यापार करार लवकरात लवकर करावा,’ असे आवाहन भारतातील निर्यातदारांनी सरकारला केले आहे. करार झाला, तर अमेरिकेकडून १७ टक्के आयातशुल्क आकारले गेले, तर ते भारतासाठी फायद्याचे ठरेल, अशी भूमिका निर्यातदारांनी मांडली.
‘फेडरेशन ऑफ इंडियन एक्स्पोर्ट ऑर्गनायजेशन’चे (एफआयईओ) अध्यक्ष एस. सी. रल्हन म्हणाले, ‘भारताने लवकरात लवकर अमेरिकेबरोबर करार करावा. अमेरिकेकडून मागण्यांमध्ये वाढ झाली आहे. अशा वेळी बाजार आणखी खुले झाले, तर निर्यातीत वाढ होईल. करार न झाल्यास स्थानिक निर्यातदारांचे नुकसान आहे. निर्यातीमध्ये भारताची स्पर्धा ज्या देशांशी आहे, त्यांचा यामुळे फायदा होत आहे. त्यांच्यावरील आयातशुल्क कमी आहे.’
प्रस्तावित आयातशुल्काला चीन, जपानचा विरोध
अतिरिक्त उत्पादनाची क्षमता असल्याचा आरोप करून अमेरिकेने प्रस्तावित केलेल्या आयातशुल्काला चीन, जपान आणि अमेरिकेच्या इतर मित्रदेशांनी विरोध केला आहे.
नव्या आयातशुल्काची अंमलबजावणी नव्या वर्षापासून लागू होण्याची शक्यता आहे. अमेरिकेचे व्यापार प्रतिनिधी जेमीसन ग्रीर यांनी सांगितले, की जगातील १४ देशांची अतिरिक्त उत्पादनाची क्षमता आणि होणारे अतिरिक्त उत्पादन अमेरिकेच्या व्यापारावर बोजा टाकणारे आहे. अमेरिकेचा सर्वांत मोठा भागीदार देश चीनवर २० टक्के आयातशुल्क लावले आहे. चीनने अमेरिकेच्या अतिरिक्त उत्पादनाच्या आरोपाचे खंडन केले आहे. आयातशुल्काचा वापर राजकीय डावपेचांसाठी वापरण्यास विरोध असल्याचे चीनच्या परराष्ट्र मंत्रालयाचे प्रवक्ते गुओ जिआकुन यांनी म्हटले आहे. करयुद्ध कुणाच्याही हिताचे नसल्याचे ते म्हणाले. जपानवर अमेरिकेने १५ टक्के आयातशुल्क लावले आहे.
जपाननेही अमेरिकेने केलेल्या आरोपांचे खंडन केले. ‘जपानची कुठलीही अतिरिक्त उत्पादनांची क्षमता नाही आणि बाजारबाह्य धोरणे नाहीत,’ अशी प्रतिक्रिया जपानचे मुख्य कॅबिनेट सचिव मिनोरू किहारा यांनी दिली. सिंगापूर, मलेशियानेही यास विरोध केला आहे.
रत्ने, दागिन्यांच्या निर्यातीचे नुकसान?
दरम्यान, आयातशुल्क वाढ, ग्राहकांपर्यंत पोहोचण्याच्या संधींबद्दल अनिश्चितता यामुळे भारतीय रत्ने आणि दागिन्यांच्या निर्यातीचे नुकसान होईल, अशी भीती रत्न आणि दागिने निर्यात संवर्धन परिषदेने (जीजेईपीसी) व्यक्त केली आहे. भारताकडून अमेरिकेला होणार्‍या रत्ने आणि दागिन्यांच्या निर्यातीत जवळपास १५ टक्के वाढ होऊन ती एप्रिल ते ऑक्टोबर २०२६ यादरम्यान ३६०.७ कोटी डॉलर इतकी होती. त्यामुळे, परिस्थितीमध्ये सुधारणा होण्यास सुरुवात झाली असली तरी प्रस्तावित २५ टक्के आयातशुल्कामुळे या क्षेत्रावर विपरीत परिणाम होईल, असे ‘जीजेईपीसी’चे अध्यक्ष किरिट भन्साली यांनी सांगितले.
अमेरिकेचे १७ टक्के आयातशुल्क हे भारतासाठी चांगले ठरू शकते. करार झाला, तर आकारण्यात येणारे शुल्क स्पर्धात्मक देशांपेक्षा कमी असेल. बांगलादेश, व्हिएतनामच्या तुलनेत आपल्याला त्यामुळे अधिक फायदा होईल. – रमेश जुनेजा, अध्यक्ष, ‘कौन्सिल फॉर लेदर एक्स्पोर्ट’

title: 'High Fat, Sugar, Salt': SC Directs Centre To Introduce Red Warning Labels On Packaged Foods
description: The Supreme Court has directed the Centre and FSSAI to introduce separate red warning labels on packaged foods high in fat, sugar and salt, and called for nutrition education in schools.
author: Swastika Sruti
content:
'High Fat, Sugar, Salt': SC Directs Centre To Introduce Red Warning Labels On Packaged Foods
The Supreme Court has ordered the Centre and the Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (FSSAI) to fortify the warning labels on the packaged food items that have higher quantities of fat, sugar or salt. The Court has sought for the imposition of separate and distinct warning signs on the cover of the foods so that people can know which are harmful food items.
AI-generated summary, reviewed by editors
The Bench of Justices JB Pardiwala and KV Viswanathan has stated that such products above the required limit should be having red hexagon-shaped warning symbols showing that the product is high in fat, sugar or salt.
This step would ensure that people understand food labels rather than understanding nutritional content in the small print on the back of the packets.
Three Separate Red Warning Labels For Fat, Sugar And Salt
According to the Supreme Court, packages of food products need to be labelled with a distinct warning symbol in case they contain an excessive amount of fat, sugar, and salt.
All these warnings would need to be put inside a red hexagon, and the exact ingredient that exceeds the limit needs to be specified.
This implies that in case a product contains excessive amounts of all three ingredients, then there would be three separate warnings on its package. A joint warning on fat, sugar, and salt will not serve the purpose.
The aim behind the decision of the Supreme Court was to facilitate identification of such products by consumers.
FSSAI Asked To Set Limits For Total Sugar And Saturated Fat
The Supreme Court has also asked FSSAI to consider the total sugar and saturated fat content of packaged food products while deciding the limits for these warning labels.
The regulator has been asked to rely on scientific research and available evidence before finalising the thresholds.
The Bench cautioned that the limits must be carefully decided. If the thresholds are too low, a large number of packaged food products could carry warning labels, making it difficult for consumers to distinguish between them.
On the other hand, if the limits are set too high, products containing excessive amounts of these ingredients may escape the warning system.
The court stressed that a balanced, science-based approach is necessary to ensure that the labels serve their intended purpose.
How Big Should The Red Warning Symbols Be?
The court has also laid down directions regarding the visibility and size of the warning symbols. According to its directions, each red hexagonal warning should occupy around 4 to 5 per cent of the principal display area of the food packet.
The text inside the symbols must be large and clear enough to be read under normal lighting conditions.
The objective is to ensure that warnings do not get hidden among other product details, brand logos or marketing information.
The Centre has been directed to ensure proper implementation of the Food Safety and Standards (Labelling and Display) Regulations, 2020, along with the latest directions issued by the Supreme Court.
Supreme Court Wants Healthy Eating Awareness In Schools
Apart from changes to food packaging, the Supreme Court has highlighted the importance of teaching children about healthy eating habits.
The Bench said that schools should consider introducing necessary changes to their curricula so that students understand nutrition through practical learning rather than depending only on textbook lessons.
It suggested activities such as interactive sessions, workshops and awareness programmes to help children identify nutritious food and understand which products should be consumed in moderation.
The focus is to develop healthy eating habits at an early age and improve children's understanding of the nutritional value of different foods.
FSSAI Asked To Submit Progress Report Within 10 Weeks
The Supreme Court has also sought an update from FSSAI on the preparation of the draft revised rules for food labelling.
The authority will have to submit an affidavit before the next hearing, explaining the progress made towards framing the proposed changes.
The matter has been listed for further hearing after 10 weeks.

title: Abdul Will Make Chandrashekhar Azad UP CM': Owaisi's Big Message At Lucknow Rally
description: Asaduddin Owaisi targets Yogi Adityanath at a Lucknow rally, saying Muslim voters will help make Chandrashekhar Azad the next Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister ahead of the 2027 Assembly elections.
author: Swastika Sruti
content:
Abdul Will Make Chandrashekhar Azad UP CM': Owaisi's Big Message At Lucknow Rally
Asaduddin Owaisi, the head of AIMIM, and Chandrashekhar Azad, the leader of Azad Samaj Party (Kanshi Ram), were seen together on stage at a common rally organized in Lucknow in the build-up to the 2027 UP Legislative Assembly elections.
AI-generated summary, reviewed by editors
At the rally held at Ramabai Ambedkar Maidan, Owaisi called for a political movement under the Samajik Parivartan Morcha, which would be aimed at taking on the government led by Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath. The alliance will try to unite Muslims, Dalits, and other oppressed sections and create an alternate political leadership in the state.
One of the most important statements made in his address was that he made in relation to the Muslim voters. According to him, they must come out of their vote-bank status and participate in political leadership making process.
"Now Abdul will no longer spread the carpet. Abdul will sit on the chair," he said, adding that voters would use their political strength to make Chandrashekhar Azad the chief minister.
Owaisi Attacks Yogi Adityanath Government Over Bulldozer Action And Encounters
While addressing the audience, Owaisi took on the government of Yogi Adityanath regarding the way they have dealt with law and order situations. According to him, justice could not be done through the bulldozing way of doing things and by carrying out police encounters.
In his direct attack on the chief minister of Uttar Pradesh, he declared that "the days of Baba are numbered".
Owaisi also accused the BJP and the Sangh Parivar of opposing the constitution. For him, it was very important to protect the constitution especially for Muslims, Dalits, and economically weaker sections of society.
'Swaraj Does Not Mean Thakur Or Yadav Rule': Owaisi
Owaisi also questioned the existing political power structure in Uttar Pradesh. He said that true self-rule should mean equal participation for all communities rather than the dominance of a particular caste or political family.
"Swaraj does not mean the rule of a Hindu nation. Rule of the people does not mean Thakur rule, Yadav rule, or rule by any one family," he said.
He further argued that political power in the state had often remained concentrated among particular social groups.
"Sometimes it's Thakur rule, sometimes Yadav rule. We won't accept either," he said, calling for equal representation and opportunities for disadvantaged communities.
Owaisi Takes A Dig At PM Modi And Yogi Adityanath
The AIMIM chief also targeted Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath during the rally.
In a sharp attack, Owaisi described the two leaders as "stand-up comedians" and blamed them for what he called the spread of hatred and division in the country and Uttar Pradesh.
He said the Samajik Parivartan Morcha would continue its political campaign until poor, weak and marginalised people received justice.
Referring to past attacks on himself and Chandrashekhar Azad, Owaisi said both leaders would not remain silent in the face of oppression.

title: Meerut Hotel Case: Accused Salman Who Dragged Woman On Road Arrested After Encounter; Watch Video
description: Meerut hotel case accused Salman, 29, has been arrested after an encounter. A video shows him crying and pleading with police, saying, 'I made a mistake.'
author: Swastika Sruti
content:
Meerut Hotel Case: Accused Salman Who Dragged Woman On Road Arrested After Encounter; Watch Video
The primary accused in the Meerut hotel case, Salman, has been arrested by Uttar Pradesh Police while staying absconded. A video uploaded after the arrest of the accused on Wednesday showed the accused crying and requesting the police to forgive him repeatedly.
AI-generated summary, reviewed by editors
"Sir, I made a mistake, please forgive me. I won't make it again," Salman can be heard saying in the video as he is being taken away by the police.
Salman, 29, was accused of kidnapping a woman and attempting to rape her before making an effort to force her to get married to him. In addition, the accused had allegedly assaulted and kidnapped the victim, who managed to escape from the attack.
The details of the case allegedly emerged from CCTV camera footage which caught parts of the alleged assault and kidnapping. According to the police, Salman sustained injuries while trying to escape from his arrest.
 #WATCH | Meerut, Uttar Pradesh: SSP B.B.G.T.S. Murthy says, "A complaint was received at the Sadar Bazar Police Station alleging that a Dalit woman had been held captive and sexually assaulted by an individual named Salman. A case has been registered under the relevant legal sections, and necessary legal action is being initiated. Today, on November 25, 2026, we received specific information that the accused was hiding near an underpass under construction, located close to Nahar Narhera village within the jurisdiction of the Lohia Nagar Police Station. Teams from both the Lohia Nagar and Sadar Bazar police stations immediately reached the spot and surrounded the area. Realising he was cornered, the accused opened fire on the police party. As the police attempted to apprehend him—while taking precautions to ensure their own safety—the accused tried to flee by climbing onto a nearby bridge. He subsequently slipped and fell from the bridge, sustaining injuries to his right and left arms. He has been promptly sent to a hospital for medical treatment, and further necessary legal action is being taken."(Source: Police)
— ANI (@ANI) November 25, 2026
How Meerut Police Arrested Salman
As per the statement issued by the police press note, Salman, who was a wanted accused in the case registered at Sadar Bazaar police station, was apprehended from Lohiya Nagar by the police.
He was reportedly surrounded by the police near the under-construction underpass adjacent to Narheda village. As soon as the police surrounded him, he fired upon them to kill them.
When the police tried to arrest him, he reportedly jumped into a bridge in order to run away but fell down and injured himself in his right leg and left hand.
He was then apprehended by the police and taken to PL Sharma District Hospital.
Illegal Pistol And Ammunition Recovered
During the arrest, police recovered an illegal .315-bore pistol, one live cartridge and one spent cartridge from Salman's possession.
Officials said Salman is a resident of the Rohta area and has several criminal cases registered against him at police stations in Meerut and Ghaziabad.
Police are now collecting evidence related to the case and have initiated further legal proceedings.
What Is The Meerut Hotel Case?
Salman is accused of holding a Hindu woman hostage inside a hotel in Meerut and attempting to rape her. He allegedly pressured her to marry him.
The woman reportedly managed to escape from the hotel, but the accused allegedly caught up with her, assaulted her on the road and abducted her. CCTV footage of the incident reportedly captured the sequence of events and became an important part of the case.
With Salman's arrest, police are continuing their investigation into the allegations and examining the available evidence.

title: Bill buzz as Centre moves to reconvene LS session for 'essential government business'
description: The Move Triggered Speculation That The Government Was Preparing To Push Through The Contentious Constitutional Amendment Bill Linked To Women’s Reservation And Delimitation, Which Requires A Two-thirds Majority In Each House
author: J.P. Yadav
content:
The Lok Sabha secretariat has reconvened Parliament from Monday after the Centre asked it to do so to transact “essential government business”.
The secretariat said the “second part of the eighth session of the Eighteenth Lok Sabha” was likely to conclude on December 3.
The move triggered speculation that the Narendra Modi government was preparing to push through the contentious constitutional amendment bill linked to women’s reservation and delimitation, which requires a two-thirds majority in each House. The Opposition had thwarted such a bid in April.
Parliamentary affairs minister Kiren Rijiju posted on X on Thursday: “The Government has requested Hon’ble Speaker, Lok Sabha, and Hon’ble Chairman, Rajya Sabha, to reconvene Lok Sabha on Monday, 30th November, 2026, and Rajya Sabha on Wednesday, 2nd December, 2026, respectively to transact essential Government Business...”
An urgent cabinet meeting chaired by Prime Minister Narendra Modi is scheduled for Friday afternoon to prepare for the parliamentary sitting, sources said.
The government has not yet prorogued the monsoon session, which was adjourned sine die on August 13, meaning Parliament can be reconvened with a minimum two days’ notice.
The sources said the objective behind the upcoming session was to pass three bills, including the amendment to facilitate the implementation of women’s reservation and undertake delimitation.
“We have more than the required numbers to pass the constitutional amendment bill,” a senior minister said, claiming the BJP leadership had secured assurances of support from Sharad Pawar’s NCP(SP) and the DMK.
Both parties had joined the wider Opposition in defeating the legislation in April. The DMK has 22 MPs in the Lok Sabha.
The announcement comes at a time when differences have emerged within the INDIA bloc over the proposed legislation.
The government’s sudden move has prompted the Congress to convene a special strategy meeting on Friday.
The Constitution (131st Amendment) Bill, 2026, was moved earlier in the year as part of a package of three bills aimed at fast-tracking the implementation of the 2023 women’s reservation law before 2029.
It proposes to do this after increasing the Lok Sabha’s strength from 543 seats to a maximum of 850 seats through a delimitation based on the 2011 population census.
The Congress wants women’s reservation implemented right away without an increase in Lok Sabha seats. It believes any delimitation should be based on the 2027 population census.
The Opposition had defeated the bill in April, accusing the government of using women’s reservation as a pretext to engage in gerrymandering in the name of delimitation. The government secured 298 votes in favour with 230 against.
The setback had prompted government managers to work behind the scenes to secure the numbers needed to revive the legislation. The defections and splits in the Trinamool Congress, AAP and the Shiv Sena (UBT) were seen as part of the broader effort to increase the government’s votes in Parliament.
Despite these developments, the NDA remains short of the required twothirds majority. The effective strength of the current Lok Sabha is 540, putting the twothirds mark at 360. The NDA has 293 members. Adding the 20 defectors from Trinamool and the 6 from the Shiv Sena (UBT) takes the government’s strength only to 319.
However, the two-thirds requirement is calculated on the basis of the members present and voting. Government managers believe they could lower the threshold by ensuring that MPs from the smaller parties stay away from the vote.

title: Govt reminder to Netflix on Pak series over streaming of Pakistani content in India
description: Ministry Cites Its May 2025 Advisory After Film Workers’ Bodies Oppose The Release Of 'Jo Bachay Hain Sang Samait Lo', Prompting A Response From Pakistan’s Ahsan Iqbal
author: Our Special Correspondent
content:
Union ministry of information and broadcasting officials have reminded Netflix of a standing advisory against streaming content from Pakistan in India, after representations by film workers’ guilds against a Pakistani series set for release on December 4.
The government has pointed to the advisory that was issued on May 8 last year, a day after India began Operation Sindoor against targets in Pakistan in retaliation for the Pahalgam massacre.
In that advisory, the ministry had cited the Code of Ethics under the Information Technology Act mandating “caution and discretion” on content that affects the sovereignty and integrity of India and jeopardises the security of the State, in addition to laying down other conditions related to national security and public order.
The advisory also drew attention to Section 3(1)(b) of Part-II of the IT Rules, 2021, which says streaming platforms and intermediaries must try to prevent users from sharing content that “threatens the unity, integrity, defence, security or sovereignty of India, friendly relations with foreign States, or public order”.
The advisory says: “Several terrorist attacks in India have been established to have cross-border linkages with Pakistan-based State and non-State actors. Recently, on 22.04.2025, the terrorist attack in Pahalgam led to the killing of several Indians, one Nepali citizen, and injuries to a number of others.
“In the interest of national security, all OTT platforms, media streaming platforms and intermediaries operating in India are advised to discontinue the web-series, films, songs, podcasts and other streaming media content, whether made available on a subscription-based model or otherwise, having its origins in Pakistan with immediate effect.”
The All Indian Cine Workers Association (AICWA) and the Federation of Western India Cine Employees (FWICE) had objected to the release of Jo Bachay Hain Sang Samait Lo after the show appeared on Netflix’s India catalogue. The drama series adapts an eponymous 2013 bestseller by Pakistani novelist Farhat Ishtiaq and stars Fawad Khan, Mahira Khan and Sanam Saeed.
The AICWA demanded a law to criminalise the carrying of any Pakistan-origin content. The FWICE sought the Prime Minister’s intervention to stop the streaming of the series in India and warned that it would physically prevent shooting for Netflix projects in India.
New agency PTI reported from Pakistan on the country’s planning minister, Ahsan Iqbal, saying on X: “First weaponising sports, then water, and now art and culture. The All Indian Cine Workers Association is urging New Delhi to permanently ban Pakistani content. How insecure do you have to be to see a cricket match as a political threat and a television drama as a national security concern? India, grow up. Let athletes play, let waters flow, let artists create, and let audiences decide what they watch.”
Iqbal’s account is blocked in India.

title: No relief for Lalu in graft case after Delhi High Court upholds corruption charges
description: HC Rejects Pleas By Lalu Prasad, Rabri Devi And Tejashwi Yadav, Upholding The Trial Court's Order Framing Corruption Charges In The IRCTC Hotel Contracts Case
author: Our Bureau
content:
Delhi High Court on Thursday upheld an order framing corruption charges against RJD leader Lalu Prasad and others while dismissing their pleas challenging a trial court decision in a case involving IRCTC hotel contracts.
“All petitions are dismissed. The order on charge is upheld,” Justice Swarana Kanta Sharma said while pronouncing the decision and rejecting the pleas of the accused challenging the trial court order framing charges against them.
The trial court had on October 13 framed charges against Lalu Prasad, his wife Rabri Devi and son Tejashwi Yadav in the IRCTC irregularities case. They challenged the decision in Delhi High Court.
“This court finds no infirmity in the impugned order dated 13.10.2025 passed by the Special Court. The material on record, considered in its entirety, discloses sufficient grounds to proceed against the accused persons, i.e. petitioners (Lalu and others) herein, for the offences for which charges have been framed against each of them. The impugned order does not call for any interference by this Court in exercise of its revisional jurisdiction,” the high court said.

title: Race Course, Savda Ghevra: Historic Delhi mosque fights for its future
description: Authorities have razed hundreds of houses in a neighbourhood in central Delhi, saying they were built on government land.
author: Zoya Mateen
content:
'We grew up around this historic Delhi mosque - now we have been forced out'
- Published
In the heart of Delhi, a short distance from the Indian prime minister's residence, a small mosque stands amid piles of rubble. Its pale walls and pointed arches remain intact, its courtyard still lined with green-and-white tiles.
But the people who gave life to the place are gone.
Mohammad Wasim, 50, points across the rubble to the spot where his house once stood.
"My father was married there, and, decades later, so was my daughter," says Wasim, a driver.
Wasim and his family were among hundreds of people who lived around the mosque in a patchwork of modest homes tucked between military compounds, exclusive clubs and sprawling bungalows in Race Course, one of the Indian capital's wealthiest and most heavily guarded neighbourhoods. Many of them had lived here for generations, working as drivers, cleaners and gardeners in the wealthy houses around them.
On 7 October, the authorities demolished their houses across three settlements, saying they had been built illegally on government land. They also raised security concerns because of the houses' proximity to military installations. Some 717 families were relocated to Savda Ghevra, a colony nearly 31 miles away, on the city's outskirts.
Residents had challenged the evictions in the Delhi High Court, arguing that moving so far from their jobs, schools and communities would upend their lives. But in August, the court allowed the relocation, accepting the government's security concerns and noting that alternative housing had been provided.
Only the mosque and a nearby Hindu temple were left standing. But their water and electricity supplies were cut off that day, and access to the compound has since been restricted. Worshippers are generally turned away at the gates, though some are occasionally allowed through after pleading with guards.
The government says it owns the land on which the mosque stands, but mosque authorities say it was registered in 1977 as waqf property - land or buildings set aside under Islamic law for religious or charitable purposes - and is listed, external as a heritage structure. The Delhi Waqf Board says it is nearly 300 years old, though other estimates put its age at 125-150 years.
The board has written to the authorities seeking restoration of the mosque's water and electricity and raising concerns about its future. Separately, a worshipper has petitioned the high court over restrictions on prayers and fears that the mosque could be demolished.
1 of 5
On 29 October, the government told the court it would take no action against the mosque for four weeks while considering the board's objections. It opposed restoring access for prayers, citing safety concerns during demolition work, a position disputed by the worshippers' lawyer. The court declined to intervene and scheduled another hearing for 16 December.
While the mosque's future remains uncertain, for Hindus and Muslims who lived around it for generations, the question now is what can be salvaged of the lives they built there.
Wasim still returns to the mosque to pray when he can, though guards sometimes turn him away. On a recent afternoon, he was among just four or five worshippers inside. A generator chugged loudly outside, supplying electricity after the power had been cut off.
"Our hearts and entire lives are tied to this place," he says. "How can we let it go, when our childhood was spent playing here?"
Rekha, a widow, remembers the colony with longing. She washed dishes in nearby homes, raised her family and performed seva (voluntary service) at the local temple.
To her, the word rehabilitation seems painfully inadequate: "How can a life built over decades be uprooted and planted somewhere else?" she asks.
Since the move, she has lost the work she depended on. Her 19-year-old son is struggling to find a job. She has been allotted a third-floor apartment but climbing stairs is painful because of a metal rod in her leg after an operation.
"I may have a house but my home was snatched away."
Critics say these experiences are part of a longer history of displacement in Delhi, where working-class communities have repeatedly been pushed, external to the city's distant edges because they lack documents proving legal ownership of land they have lived on for decades.
"Relocation disconnects them from both jobs and networks, resulting in livelihood and income loss," urban researcher Mukta Naik told the BBC.
As families scatter in search of work, she says, the informal support systems they once relied on become harder to rebuild.
"This leaves families to fend for themselves," she says.
The Delhi government's housing agency, the local municipal council and the central government's land office did not respond to requests for comment.
Savda Ghevra was established in 2006 on farmland near Delhi's border with Haryana state, to house families displaced from elsewhere in the city.
The first arrivals found little more than bare plots, without roads, running water or electricity. Over time, they built homes, opened shops and fought for basic services. By the early 2020s, an estimated 50,000 people lived here, external, having made a neighbourhood out of a place they had little choice but to inhabit.
Now the families from Race Course have begun the same slow work.
They have traded the lush tree-lined avenues of central Delhi for rows of nearly identical concrete blocks, with open fields stretching beyond. Life is going on, but much of what sustained these families remains on the other side of the city.
Every day, Babloo leaves home at 5am to take his children by metro to their old school in central Delhi, changing trains three times along the way. He waits out the six hours until classes finish at a tea stall outside his former neighbourhood. When he has work his wife makes the journey.
Their new home is too far away, he says, to return between the school runs. By the time the family reaches Savda Ghevra, it is around 4pm.
Babloo once worked at a club in Race Course. He has now found work in Meerut, a town to the north-east of Delhi. Residents knew they might have to leave, he says, but they hoped they would be relocated somewhere close enough to continue their jobs and their children's schooling.
The government says suitable apartments were unavailable closer to Race Course. In court, it cited Savda Ghevra's schools, dispensaries and transport links as evidence that the area could accommodate the displaced families.
But the presence of these facilities offers little reassurance to Naeem Khan, 63. His two grandsons have hearing and speech disabilities and need specialised care and schooling that he says are unavailable in the area.
The move has also scattered Naeem's family. One son and a divorced daughter share his tiny one-room apartment, while his two other sons had to move elsewhere due to lack of space.
"We have been thrown 20 years backward," he says.
The distance has been especially costly for women. Naik says childcare responsibilities, transport costs and safety concerns make long commutes to work particularly difficult for them.
At Race Course, the wealth surrounding the settlements offered small but vital ways to earn money - dishes to wash, gardens to tend, discarded bottles to collect and sell.
Akhtari, an elderly widow, collected mineral-water bottles for about 100 rupees (about $1.05; £0.80) a day and dried leftover rotis, or flatbreads, to sell as cattle feed.
Now even these modest sources of income have disappeared.
"Everyone living here was evicted; everyone is poor, broken, and struggling themselves," Akhtari says. "Who will hire someone else for housework?"
At Race Course, when she had nothing, the mosque's imam or a neighbour might give her money for flour. Her neighbours checked on her. In the new apartment, she has a roof over her head, but few people to fall back on.
She has begun to worry about what will happen if she falls ill.
"If I collapse and die inside, no one will even know," she says. " Hopefully someone will break down the door and find me."

title: Ranbir Kapoor in Ramayana: India's costliest film retells a beloved Hindu epic - but divides critics
description: Easily the most anticipated Bollywood film of the year, Ramayana: Rise of a Legend is the first of two parts.
author: Zoya Mateen
content:
India's costliest film retells a beloved Hindu epic - but divides critics
- Published
India's most expensive film - a lavish retelling of the Hindu epic Ramayana, made in two parts for a reported $500m (£370m) - has opened in cinemas worldwide, sparking enormous expectations and mixed reviews.
Directed by Nitesh Tiwari, Ramayana: Rise of a Legend is the first of two planned films, a sprawling production that brings together some of India's biggest stars, Hollywood visual-effects expertise and two Oscar-winning composers in an attempt to take one of the country's most revered stories to a global audience.
One of Hinduism's foundational epics, the Ramayana has travelled across centuries and continents, finding expression in poetry, temple sculpture, shadow puppetry, folk theatre and stories passed down through generations. It has outlasted kingdoms and empires, inspired religious devotion and political movements, and found new life, again and again, on TV and in cinema.
Tiwari's version returns to the familiar story of love, duty, exile and war, set in a world of gods and demons, celestial weapons and mighty kingdoms.
Ranbir Kapoor plays Lord Ram, the virtuous prince of Ayodhya. Banished from his kingdom for 14 years, he retreats to the forest with his wife Sita (played by Sai Pallavi), who is kidnapped by Ravana, the 10-headed king of Lanka.
Played by Yash, one of southern India's biggest stars, Ravana is a powerful warrior whose pride leads him into an epic battle with Ram (which will be depicted in part 2, set to release next year).
The film's producer, Namit Malhotra, heads visual-effects company DNEG, which has worked on Hollywood blockbusters including Dune and Interstellar. The music is a collaboration between AR Rahman, the Oscar-winning Indian composer of Slumdog Millionaire, and Hans Zimmer, whose scores for Gladiator, The Dark Knight and Dune have helped define the sound of modern Hollywood.
The film opened days ahead of Diwali, the Hindu festival of lights which celebrates Ram's return to Ayodhya after his exile.
But the critical response so far has been mixed.
Saibal Chatterjee of NDTV channel gave it, external three out of five stars, saying its visual spectacle often overshadowed the story. Its enormous scale, he wrote, "remains, for the most part, the only thing that stands out", while the acting remains "wildly inconsistent".
Rishabh Suri of the Hindustan Times newspaper was more enthusiastic, awarding it four stars.
"I am happy to report, all that money shows on screen," he wrote, praising the performances and visual effects, though he found the first half sluggish and the music underwhelming.
Shubhra Gupta, external of The Indian Express, who gave the film three stars, confessed to initial misgivings about its extravagant scale but found herself gradually won over, calling it the "perfect epic".
There was "enough sorcery and thrills and adventure" to sustain the spectacle, she wrote, and the filmmakers had managed to tell a sprawling story without being swallowed by it.
Internationally, too, the film drew contrasting reactions.
Writing in The Guardian, Peter Bradshaw called it a "thoroughly engaging, rousing and spectacular Indian epic melodrama". He found echoes of Shakespeare in the royal intrigue that sends Rama into exile, and of Homer in his quest to rescue Sita. Its sweeping landscapes and fantastical imagery reminded him of The Lord of the Rings and The Lion King.
"It's a rather amazing adventure," he wrote, external, giving it four stars.
Others were less impressed. Siddhant Adlakha of IGN scored the film four out of 10, describing its action as "clunky" and its computer-generated imagery as an "eye-sore".
Giovanni Lago of Next Best Picture, who gave it, external five out of 10, praised Yash's magnetic Ravana and the score by Rahman and Zimmer. But he felt the film's vast narrative might have been better served by a Game of Thrones-style series.
The use of AI to adjust actors' lip movements for the English-language version also drew criticism. While Tiwari said it was intended to make the film more accessible to international audiences, Adlakha likened the result to "exaggerated mouth movements superimposed on still images for comedy sketches".
In India, the film has invited comparisons with earlier adaptations, particularly Ramanand Sagar's Ramayan, which captivated the country nearly four decades ago with simple sets and special effects that now seem quaint.
When the series first aired in 1987, Sunday mornings across India took on an almost devotional stillness.
Streets emptied, shops lowered their shutters and neighbours crowded around TV sets. Some viewers bathed, lit incense and garlanded their screens before the broadcast, preparing for the show much as they might for worship.
Arvind Rajagopal, a media scholar at New York University, told the BBC in 2019 that trains and buses would stop and passengers disembark to watch the show on roadside TVs.
Broadcast on the state-run Doordarshan network, some of the most popular parts of the 78-episode series drew an estimated 80-100 million viewers, astonishing numbers at a time when owning a TV was a luxury in India.
The actors, too, became objects of reverence. Arun Govil, who played Ram, has recalled people weeping at the sight of him and touching his feet. Now, in a casting choice brimming with nostalgia, Govil returns in Tiwari's film as Dasharatha, Ram's father.
Other adaptations found their own ways to reimagine the epic. The 1992 Indo-Japanese animated film Ramayana: The Legend of Prince Rama brought the tale to life through richly detailed, hand-drawn animation.
Tiwari's Ramayana arrives with technological resources its predecessors could barely have imagined - but also with the expectations of generations who have grown up with the story and its characters.
It also comes at a politically charged moment in India, where Ram has become a powerful symbol of Hindu identity - over the past decade and a half, even popular analyses or retellings of the epic have landed in controversy.
The 2023 film Adipurush, another big-budget retelling of Ramayana, sparked backlash on several fronts.
Hindu groups called for a ban, accusing it of disrespecting religious figures, while some critics questioned its depiction of Ravana, which they said drew on Mughal imagery and reinforced stereotypes about Muslims. The film was also criticised for its dialogue and visual effects.
For the actors portraying these characters in the latest film, that burden was deeply felt.
"I was filled with fear," Kapoor told the BBC Asian Network's Haroon Rashid. "I knew that maybe I'm too old for this. I won't be able to do justice to it."
He called the role "an opportunity of a lifetime", but said playing a figure worshipped by millions left little room for the creative freedom he had enjoyed in other films.
Sai Pallavi, who plays Sita, said the experience was as much spiritual as artistic. Raised in a religious household, she said she approached the part not just as a performance, but as an opportunity for personal growth.
How the film is being received will become clearer soon, as audiences head to cinemas.
But whatever the verdict, it marks a major cultural moment for India, bringing a story loved for generations to the big screen on an unprecedented scale.

title: Ranji Smile: The forgotten chef who opened America’s first Indian restaurant
description: Indian chef Ranji Smile opened America’s first Indian restaurant in 1901 - then became a fake prince.
author: Dinyar Patel
content:
The Indian chef who brought curry to America - then vanished
- Published
One hundred and twenty-five years ago, in 1901, an Indian chef opened what was almost certainly the first Indian restaurant in the US.
Ranji Smile was one of the most colourful and enigmatic figures to shape the American food scene.
In the summer of 1899, Smile sailed from London to New York. We know hardly anything about his origins and early life, not even his real name.
"Ranji" was probably a nod to the Indian cricketing sensation KS Ranjitsinhji, then a star attraction at Test matches in Britain. "Smile" could have been an anglicisation of "Ismail".
Whatever his origins, Smile possessed an uncommon knack for reinvention. Once through the portals of Ellis Island, he appended a new name to his identity, something more in keeping with America's egalitarian promise: Joe.
Joe Ranji Smile arrived in New York to work at Sherry's Restaurant, a glittering new establishment on Fifth Avenue.
In London, he had been a curry cook at the Cecil and Savoy hotels. Here, according to an 1899 profile in Harper's, he was noticed by Sherry's owner, Louis Sherry, who invited him to bring his culinary skills across the Atlantic. Late Victorian London already boasted an Indian dining scene: as early as 1810, Sake Dean Mohamed, a native of Patna, had opened his Hindostanee Coffee House near Portman Square, plying customers with both curry and hookah.
Manhattanite tastebuds lacked much exposure to masala. There was, however, growing curiosity about India and its culture. Swami Vivekananda, the spellbinding orator and exponent of Hindu philosophy, enthralled audiences during his visits to the city in the 1890s. At the same time, more Indian sailors, students and professionals trickled into New York. This was probably why Louis Sherry decided to add a curry cook to his kitchen staff.
At Sherry's Restaurant, Smile joined one of the great culinary institutions of the American Gilded Age. Positioning itself as a rival to Delmonico's, New York's byword for fine dining, Sherry's catered to city plutocrats like the Astors and was famed for over-the-top dining experiences. During one such soiree, patrons marched their horses into a ballroom, saddled up and ate on horseback.
Smile, a skilled showman, thrived in this environment.
Customers soon flocked to taste his preparations of Bombay duck, a glutinous lizardfish that is a delicacy along the western Indian coast, and novel creations like "Lettuce Ceylon".
Cooking and serving became a performance. Dressed in a satin coat and blue silk turban, Smile salaamed in front of customers before enquiring, "Will you have the curry hot or mild, sahib?" Pictures of Sherry's curry chef were soon splashed across newspapers and magazines. One headline said it all: "New York women go wild over him."
As his fame grew, Smile decided in 1901 to leave Sherry's and set up his own establishment, one exclusively devoted to Indian cuisine. For financial backing, he leaned on Roland R Conklin, a prominent financier, external and the inventor of an early version of the motorhome.
Omar Khayyam, Smile's Indian restaurant, opened in late 1901 at 325 Fifth Avenue. This was prime real estate, a block away from the original Waldorf-Astoria Hotel where, 29 years later, the Empire State Building would rise. Smile adorned the restaurant with Indian draperies and hanging lanterns.
As the New York Herald reported, a fleet of Indian waiters in "voluminous turbans" staffed the premises, as did a group of Indian musicians. Now quite the embodiment of the American immigrant success story, Smile eagerly awaited his customers and fans.
Alas, they never materialised. Within a year, Omar Khayyam shuttered. The New York Sun claimed that people had "tired" of Indian fare, dismissing it as a passing fad.
Smile's stardom, which had blazed so brightly in the Big Apple, also began to dim. Unfortunately, his showmanship and flair for theatrics shaded into deceit and criminal activity.
Smile began claiming that he was, after all, not an everyday Joe but rather a prince, the son of the emir of Baluchistan, a fictional title. And, before opening Omar Khayyam, he made a quick visit to Bombay, where he pronounced himself to be a guest at the upcoming coronation of King Edward VII in London and recruited a retinue of staff: valets, a dancing girl, and "mahouts to drive his herds of elephants".
All of this was reported in New York newspapers like the Times because, as a subsequent federal case against him alleged, Smile illegally trafficked this staff into the US to work at his restaurant. Instead of becoming a pioneer outpost of Indian gastronomy, Omar Khayyam nearly got Smile deported.
"Prince" Joe Ranji Smile evaded deportation (many in his retinue were not as lucky) and went on evolving his invented persona, all while wooing and marrying a series of impressionable young American women. He began claiming that Indian food was a secret elixir for female beauty. "The eye will grow lustrous, the complexion will be yet so lovely," Smile promised, displaying his wives as clinching proof.
Meanwhile, he honed his performing skills at Indian cooking demonstrations across the country.
In Washington DC, Smile prepared dishes, including a dubious-sounding dessert called "bungalow", while a juggler and dancing girl entertained him. On his way to Chicago, as one newspaper in remote Idaho reported, he declared himself to be no longer the son of the emir but the brother of an even more fanciful figure, the "great Beglerberg of Baluchistan". If Smile was guilty of being a conman, then his American interlocutors were equally guilty of wide-eyed gullibility.
While Smile's theatrics and good food kept people entertained for a while, the tall tales and outright fabrications soon caught up with him.
Smile retreated from the public gaze, hurt by further brushes with the law which ranged from forcible confinement of one of his dancing girls to refusing to pay a bill at an Italian restaurant in Manhattan. By the 1920s, he apparently abandoned cooking entirely, listing his occupation as a merchant.
The final shred of evidence about Smile dates from 1937, when his fourth or fifth American wife approached the New York Supreme Court and filed for an annulment of her marriage to her now-absconded husband. Ranji Smile's last act of reinvention was to simply disappear.
Despite this inglorious end, Smile and his Indian restaurant did pave the way for the popularisation of Indian cuisine in America. Other immigrants soon tested the waters.
In 1909, Saint Nihal Singh, a peripatetic journalist from Punjab, introduced readers of the Chicago Daily Tribune to recipes for bhajias, puris, halwa, and "Fried Chicken a la Hindoo".
Aware of the unfamiliarity of many Indian ingredients amongst Chicagoans, Singh urged readers to look for them in the city's Chinese grocery stores. On another occasion, which might make contemporary chefs blush, he suggested that hamburger meat was an adequate substitute for preparing gosht pilau (a meat pilaf).
Not long after Ranji Smile was hauled to court for trafficking immigrants, a young man from Ceylon named KY Kira arrived at Ellis Island.
Like Smile, he had a talent for reinvention. Kira joined a troupe of Sinhalese dancers which performed for American circuses like Barnum and Bailey and Ringling Brothers. In 1913, he opened an Indian restaurant in Harlem, eventually called the Ceylon India Inn. Unlike Omar Khayyam, the Ceylon India Inn was a hit.
New York now had a much larger immigrant Indian population and the restaurant attracted expatriate nationalists and revolutionaries. But it also benefited from a burgeoning American interest in Indian culture and food. By the 1920s, Kira's restaurant, now located off Times Square, catered to Broadway and Hollywood stars. The Ceylon India Inn remained in business until the late 1980s, touting itself as the first Indian restaurant in America.
That, of course, was not the case. Ranji Smile might be long forgotten, but 125 years after the brief existence of his Omar Khayyam restaurant, his legacy lives on in the thousands of Indian eateries flourishing across the US.
Dinyar Patel is associate professor of history at SPJIMR in Mumbai

title: Prohibitory orders, detentions as Vijay govt defies SC order. Karthigai Deepam not lit at Deepathoon
description: Vijay govt's decision triggered protests by Hindu activists, leading to scuffles with police near the Thiruparankundram temple, while BJP leaders were detained.
author: Shweta Tripathi
content:
Chennai: The Vijay-led TVK government Tuesday defied the Supreme Court order permitting a one-time lighting of the Karthigai Deepam at the Deepathoon, as the ceremonial lamp was lit at the traditional location near the Uchi Pillayar Temple atop the Thiruparankundram hill in Tamil Nadu’s Madurai.
No lamp was lit on the disputed stone pillar even after the Madras High Court directed the Madurai district administration to comply with the Supreme Court’s orders.
Expressing the TVK’s clear stance, Law Minister CTR Nirmal Kumar wrote on X, “The Karthigai Mahadeepam was lit in the Deepa Mandapam near the Uchchipillaiyar temple located directly above the head of the presiding deity at Thiruparankundram.”
The decision triggered protests by Hindu activists and members of organisations including the Hindu Munnani, leading to scuffles with police near the Thiruparankundram temple. Nearly 50 protesters were detained after a confrontation in which two policemen sustained minor injuries.
BJP leader Tamilisai Soundararajan criticised Kumar. “A law minister gleefully posts about violating the Supreme Court’s order. Who is the message you are posting now meant for? As law minister, opposing the Supreme Court’s interim action is condemnable. The Tamil Nadu law minister is losing the moral right to remain in office. This government must answer for its conduct in disregarding Hindu sentiments and the law…” she wrote on X.
The Madras High Court’s Madurai bench had earlier directed the district administration to comply with the Supreme Court’s 20 November ruling. That order—passed by a bench of Justices Aravind Kumar and Vipul M. Pancholi—had stayed key findings of the High Court’s January judgment that treated the lighting of the ceremonial lamp at the Deepathoon as an essential religious practice.
The apex court permitted a strictly limited, one-time lighting on Tuesday, the day of the Karthigai Deepam festival, by a small authorised team from the temple Devasthanam and government officials. Public access, processions and demonstrations were barred, and the court made it clear that the permission created no customary, religious or proprietary right and would not serve as a precedent.
The Tamil Nadu government filed a review petition specifically challenging the one-time permission portion of the 20 November order, arguing it contains an error apparent on the face of the record. In its petition in SC earlier to stay the Madras High Court order to allow lighting of the lamp at the Deepathoon, the State had cited historical records, including a 1996 High Court order confirming the traditional location, and argued that the HC had effectively sought to create a new practice through a writ petition.
Both the Vijay-led TVK government as well as the DMK before it have opposed the lighting of the lamp at the Deepathoon—which is located close to a dargah—arguing that it is not an established temple custom, that the ritual has been performed at the Deepa Mandapam for over 150 years, and that altering the long-standing practice risks law and order.
On Tuesday, the TVK’s alliance partner VCK lauded its decision. VCK chief Thirumavalavan congratulated the government and appreciated the district collector and officials of the Hindu Religious and Charitable Endowments Department for lighting the grand lamp at the Deepa Mandapam near the Ucchi Pillayar Temple, as is customary. He also thanked CM Vijay for “thwarting the Sangh Parivar’s conspiracy and safeguarding social harmony in Tamil Nadu”, he wrote on X.
Prohibitory orders, detentions
The Madurai District Collector imposed prohibitory orders under Section 163 of the BNSS, banning assemblies, agitations, processions, public meetings and any unauthorised climbing of the hill until 10 am on Wednesday. Over 5,600 police personnel were deployed, the area was declared a temporary Red Zone with a drone ban, and the Deepathoon was barricaded.
Tamil Nadu BJP president Nainar Nagenthran was detained while heading towards Madurai from Tirunelveli. Former Union Minister L. Murugan was stopped in Coimbatore district and placed under house arrest. The BJP alleged that around 750 of its leaders and Hindu Munnani functionaries across southern districts were confined or prevented from travelling. Hindu Munnani members were also arrested in other places while attempting to proceed to the hill with ritual items.
The Madras High Court later directed the release of those unlawfully detained under the prohibitory orders.
(Edited by Gitanjali Das)
Also Read: CM Vijay’s popularity is intact, but his government in Tamil Nadu is facing a political storm

title: 120 seats sought, 26 seats offered: Why Congress-SP alliance talks for UP polls hit roadblock in Round 2
description: The Congress currently has two MLAs in the 403-member Uttar Pradesh Assembly, while the SP has 111. UP goes to polls next year.
author: Prashant Srivastava
content:
Lucknow: Seat-sharing talks between the Samajwadi Party (SP) and Congress for the 2027 Uttar Pradesh assembly elections have hit a roadblock. While the Congress has sought 120 seats, the SP has offered only 26 in its initial proposal.
For the second round of talks Tuesday, SP leaders arrived with a list of 26 seats, which did not go down well with the Congress leaders in attendance. According to sources in the know, the Congress instead sought discussions on all 403 assembly constituencies, arguing that seat-sharing should be decided on the basis of political and electoral calculations.
Tuesday’s talks come a day after the first round that lasted all of 20 minutes. Both parties’ representatives had met at the Delhi residence of senior Congress leader and Rajya Sabha MP Pramod Tiwari. During the meeting, the Congress submitted a list of 120 constituencies where it wants to contest. In response, the SP shared its preferred list of 26 seats for the Congress Tuesday.
ThePrint has learnt that the SP leaders indicated that the number could be increased after consultations with the party’s central leadership, but made it clear that the final offer was unlikely to cross 50 seats. This did not go down well with the Congress representatives present at the meeting.
SP Rajya Sabha MP Ram Gopal Yadav, it is learnt, defended his party’s proposal, citing the Congress’s electoral performance in the 2022 assembly elections. “Two of these seats were won by the Congress, and it finished second in four others. The remaining 20 seats are those where we received 60,000 to 70,000 votes, while the Congress got only around 2,000 votes,” he is learnt to have said.
जीतनेवाली पहली ‘26 सीटों’ से हुई है शुरुआत
मिलजुलकर समझदारी से और आगे बढ़ेगी बात
— Akhilesh Yadav (@yadavakhilesh) November 24, 2026
The Congress currently has just two MLAs in Uttar Pradesh and secured less than three percent of the votes in the 2022 assembly elections. The SP won 111 seats in 2022, securing 32.06 percent of the total vote share.
Asked whether a final agreement could be reached soon, Yadav said seats would be allocated on the basis of the Congress’s strength and that constituencies where it had performed poorly would be difficult to offer.
A Congress leader who was present at the meeting, speaking on condition of anonymity, said the SP’s offer was far below the party’s expectations. “Until yesterday, the SP was calling our demand impractical. Now, its own offer is extremely modest. An alliance cannot work with just 26 or 40 seats. Uttar Pradesh has 80 Lok Sabha constituencies. Even if we get one assembly seat in each Lok Sabha constituency, that would mean 80 seats. Our demand is for 100 seats. The SP can remove 20 constituencies from our original list of 120, but it should offer us at least 100.”
The leader added that the Congress would place the SP’s proposal before its central leadership, which was also unlikely to accept it. The final decision on how to proceed would now rest with the party high command.
How SP arrived at its 26-seat proposal
According to a senior SP functionary, the party has divided the proposed 26 constituencies into three categories, primarily on the basis of the Congress’s performance in the 2022 assembly elections.
The list includes the two seats won by the Congress in 2022—Rampur Khas and Pharenda—and four constituencies where it finished second—Mathura, Kheragarh, Jagdishpur and Kidwai Nagar.
The remaining 20 seats are spread across different regions. In western Uttar Pradesh and the Braj region, these include Baghpat, Modinagar, Hapur, Jewar, Siyana, Khurja, Khair, Iglas, Mant, Agra North and Fatehpur Sikri. In Awadh and central Uttar Pradesh, the proposed seats are Bilgram-Mallanwan, Govind Nagar and Nanpara. In eastern UP, the list includes Gorakhpur City, Khajani, Padrauna, Fazilnagar, Pindra and Varanasi Cantt. Interestingly, only one seat from the Rae Bareli and Amethi districts is on the SP’s list.
Sources said the SP has also asked the Congress to share the names of its potential candidates, along with details of caste equations and electoral calculations, for constituencies beyond the 26 seats proposed by the party.
After the meeting, Ram Gopal Yadav described the discussions as positive. Responding to questions about the short duration of the meeting, he said complicated issues take time to resolve but expressed hope that an agreement would be reached within the next two to three days.
SP MP Rajeev Rai also said both parties were examining constituencies individually and that the candidates’ winnability would be the only criterion for ticket distribution.
2024 versus 2022
According to sources, the Congress is basing its demand for a larger share of seats on its performance in the 2024 Lok Sabha elections, when it contested 17 constituencies in alliance with the SP and won six. The party secured a vote share of 9.46 percent.
The Congress believes it can bring Dalit, Brahmin and Extremely Backward Caste voters into the alliance’s fold. It also wants representation in almost every district to strengthen its organisational presence ahead of the assembly elections.
The SP, however, is relying on the Congress’s assembly election record. In 2022, the Congress contested 399 seats independently but managed to win only two, securing a vote share of 2.33 percent. Its candidates forfeited their deposits in 387 constituencies.
Even in the 2017 assembly elections, when the Congress contested in alliance with the SP, it won only seven of the 114 seats it contested.
The SP’s argument is that the Congress’s improved performance in the 2024 Lok Sabha elections was a result of the combined strength of the alliance and should not be treated as an indication of its independent electoral strength.
Congress has also sought 8 out of 10 assembly constituencies in Amethi and Rae Bareli districts. However, in the 2022 assembly elections, the SP won six of these seats, while the BJP secured the remaining four. The Congress failed to win even one seat in the two districts.
The party, however, believes that changing political equations, including cross-voting by some SP MLAs during the 2024 Rajya Sabha elections, could give it room to stake a claim in these constituencies.
(Edited by Gitanjali Das)

title: Tamil Nadu District Collector files formal complaint against TVK MLA Vignesh, alleging sexual harassment
description: In her complaint, Collector says Arul Vignesh turned up at her house drunk and sent her obscene messages. Comes amid questions over govt's handling of allegations and claim that no complaint existed.
author: Shweta Tripathi
content:
TVK had earlier taken the position that no formal case existed and that the allegations were politically motivated. However, at an alliance meeting Monday, Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay told alliance MLAs that the party is looking into the issue.
Police have registered a case against the MLA under the Tamil Nadu Prohibition of Harassment of Women Act. The development came hours after the Tamil Nadu government told the Madras High Court that neither Chief Secretary M. Sai Kumar nor the police had received any complaint or representation from the Collector in the matter.
State Public Prosecutor R. John Sathyan made the submission before Justice V. Lakshminarayanan, while the court heard a criminal writ petition filed by advocate R. Thrishuli seeking directions for the registration of an FIR against the MLA. The petitioner alleged that Vignesh trespassed into the Collector’s bungalow in an inebriated state, threatened officials, and sent obscene messages. The judge directed the prosecutor to contact the Collector and report back.
The Collector in her complaint stated that the MLA commented on her attire, behaved inappropriately, and attempted to invade her personal space at public events.
The allegations first gained public attention in early November after opposition leader and DMK MP K. Kanimozhi asked for an inquiry.
The DMK MP has welcomed the Collector’s action and said, “What will those who questioned me, other political leaders and the DMK that day, and accused even those who spoke about women’s safety of playing politics, say today? I wholeheartedly commend the District Collector, who courageously filed a police complaint against a ruling-party MLA and is setting an example for all women enduring harassment in their workplaces.”
Kanimozhi asked, “If the chief minister, who has failed to take action against his party’s MLA even after all this time, will he finally act? Or will he continue to take the position that protecting his party member, who faces such vile allegations, is more important than women’s safety? Justice delayed is justice denied. Will action finally be taken now?” Kanimozhi told the media Tuesday.
Vignesh had denied the charges, describing them as politically motivated and aimed at tarnishing his and the party’s image. He maintained that no such messages were sent and questioned claims of entering her residence which had heavy security.
DMK spokesperson T. K. S. Elangovan said the government wants to protect their MLA. “The MLA had sent a WhatsApp message to the Collector, and he had also spoken to her directly in a drunken state. The Collector had sent the complaint and she had also sent a complaint to the DGP and Chief Secretary. But this government boldly says that no complaint was received. A bunch of criminals are in the TVK, and they are doing all kinds of criminal activities. TVK cadres are involved nowadays, and the last six months have been the worst period for Tamil Nadu,” he said.
The National Commission for Women had earlier taken suo motu cognisance of media reports and sought a report from the Director General of Police. Opposition parties including the BJP and AIADMK had also asked the police authorities to register a case and conduct an independent probe. The matter remains under investigation following the registration of the complaint.
(Edited by Viny Mishra)
