title: The Inheritance Trap
content:
We’re glad this article found its way to you. If you’re not a subscriber, we’d love for you to consider subscribing—your support helps make this journalism possible. Either way, we hope you enjoy the read. Click to subscribe: subscribing
There is a set process of what happens when someone inherits property. On paper, the process of gathering death certificates, establishing a will, applying for property mutation, updating housing security records and addressing taxes should take about one year. Without a will, this timeline stretches. When a man dies intestate, meaning without a valid will, or leaves a will that does not cover all his assets, succession law decides who inherits. For a Hindu man, his wisdom mother sons and daughters inherit together as first-class heirs, in equal shares. With no will and several heirs, this process can take two to three years. Those years matter. Each step is a point at which a name can be added or quietly left out, and the longer the process runs, the more tired and pressured a family becomes.
When an owner dies, the heirs apply for mutations (called dakhil kharij in many states), the entry that updates the revenue records. It sounds like a formality. The supreme court has said many times that it is not a transfer of ownership. In Suraj Bhan v. Financial Commissioner (2007), it held that an entry in the revenue records does not confer title on the person named. In Balwant Singh v. Daulat Singh (1997), it held that mutation neither creates nor extinguishes title, and that its purpose is to let a person pay land revenue. In Jitendra Singh v. State of Madhya Pradesh (2021), it said so again.
This should protect a daughter left off the form. A case from Jammu shows what it does in practice. After a man died, the revenue authorities mutated his land in the names of his two sons. His two daughters, Kuldip Kaur and Balbir Kaur challenged the entry, and argued they were also entitled. In Rajdir Singh v. State of Jammu and Kashmir (2008), the Supreme Court held that the tenancy authorities and the High Court should not have decided questions of ownership and inheritance at all. Revenue records, it said confer no title, and the daughters were left to go to a civil court to establish their rights.
This is the first daw of the trap. The law protects her title, but only if she sues for it. A wrong entry does not take her share away. It does make her the one who must go to court to prove it, against her own family.
On paper, the revenue record is a fiscal document. In daily life, it is the document that banks, buyers, officials and schemes consult. The name on the page is who is treated as the owner, who is recognised as the farmer, and who can be approached about a sale or a loan. A 2013 Oxfam India policy brief argued that without land titles, women are not recognised as farmers. The numbers suggest how often women are missing from that record. Women were 13.9 per cent of operational landholders in the 2015-16 Agricultural Census. Researchers at the NCAER caution that operational holdings measure who uses the land, not who owns it. But they note a broader finding, women rarely hold land titles on their own, usually appear on joint titles, and in those cases tend to hold smaller shares. A separate source of data, the National Family Health Survey, found that 41.6 per cent of women owned a house or land alone or jointly in the first phase of NFHS-5 (2019-20), a figure that includes houses and joint ownership and so is not directly comparable.
The starkest evidence on paperwork comes from a 2013 study by UN women and a research partner in Andhra Pradesh and Bihar, Only about 60 per cent of the plots surveyed had formal documentation, and women held the title in under 10 per cent of the households that did. More than 61 per cent of women had never visited the local revenue office for land-related work, and another 18 per cent had gone with only a male relative. A woman who has never been to the office where the record is kept is hardly placed to correct it.
Possession in property law means actual physical control of a property and the ongoing exercise and enjoyment of it. It is distinct from formal ownership. A person can own a property without possessing it, and similarly, possess a property without owning it. For a married daughter, the former is more common. The share is hers on paper, and someone else is in the house, on the land or collecting the rent. Ownership, then, is about who is on the land, who collects the rent and who deals with the tenant. A married daughter usually lives elsewhere A brother lives close, farms the plot, or runs the shop. And over years, his possession becomes indistinguishable from ownership, to the family and to everyone else.
Then, comes a dreaded stage: a paper that needs her signature. It rarely looks like pressure, it in fact looks like a courtesy. A brother, an uncle, or a family friend who “knows these things” calls to say that a document is ready, it’s only a formality, and that she only needs to sign at the pencil mark. It is usually drawn up weeks after a death, when no one has valued the property or consulted their own lawyer, and when saying no could be construed as an insult to the dead. This is the release deed, or relinquishment, a paper in which a co-heir gives up her share, almost always “for the sake of the family.”
The law did what it was asked to do. It gave daughters an equal share, by birth, and the Supreme Court has said so more than once. Yet, the truth begins after the law is done speaking. It begins in a revenue office, where a form is filled without her. It begins in a revenue office, where a form is filled in without her. It continues on land she does not farm, in a house she does not live in, with a tenant who pays someone else. It reaches its sharpest point at a table, days after a funeral, where a paper is placed in front of her and signing feels like the only decent thing to do. Nowhere in that sequence does anyone break the law. That is what makes it so hard to see, and so hard to name.
The trap has two jaws. The first is procedural: a wrong entry does not take her share away, but she is the one who must go to court to prove it. The second is emotional: the lawful route runs through her own family, and the price of taking it is her place among them. Most women weigh both and decide, reasonably, to stay silent. What closes the gap is rarely a judgment. It is a name on a record, a copy in her own hands, a rent paid into her own account, a delay of two weeks before she signs. These are small, administrative, almost dull acts, and they are the difference between a right and a possession. The question for families is whether they will let her take those steps without treating them as an accusation. The question for everyone else is why ownership, for so many women, still depends on being willing to ask.

title: What Happens to a Woman's Property After Marriage?
content:
We’re glad this article found its way to you. If you’re not a subscriber, we’d love for you to consider subscribing—your support helps make this journalism possible. Either way, we hope you enjoy the read. Click to subscribe: subscribing
The plot was always supposed to be hers. Her father bought it in Udaipur in the late 90s and when he died, Shreya, then twenty-nine, inherited it in a partition deed that her brother signed without argument. It was one of those rare moments that went exactly as the law says it ought to. But, this was the last time anything went exactly as the law said it should
Shreya got married that winter. By spring, the rent from a small shop built in the plot was being paid into an account that she did not hold. By March, the building plan had been approved on a letter signed by her husband, and within three years, a buyer made an offer, and she was told that it would be better if the whole family sat together to discuss it.
She was never told it wasn’t going to be hers, no one said that. They only ask who is going to manage it. Once a daughter’s inheritance crosses the threshold of her marital home, who actually owns it, and who actually controls it?
Like many things in the Indian family, inherited property does not have a linear journey after a woman marries. There are five checkpoints, and ownership and control can come apart at each point.
The Paper Trail
Under Section 14 of the Hindu Succession Act, 1956, property a Hindu woman possesses is her absolute property. It does not become joint property with her husband if she gets married, and it does not become the property of her in-laws. And, the Supreme Court has repeated this in unusually plain language. In Maya Gopinathan v. Anoop S.B. (April, 2024), the Supreme Court reaffirmed that a woman's stridhan is her absolute property, to dispose of at her own pleasure, and that the husband has no title or independent dominion over it as an owner. 
Stridhan is a specific legal category, centered on gifts to a woman before, at and after a marriage. It is not identical to inherited property. But the principle the Court draws on, that a woman;s property is her own, is the same principle that Section 14 extends to what she inherits from her parents.
The Crises of Management
A husband will be “more familiar with these things.” A father-in-law will know the local broker. A brother-in-law can “just handle it.” A power of attorney is signed, often early, “to avoid running around.” It rarely has an end date. An authority granted for convenience can easily become a habit of control. A power of attorney does not transfer ownership. But a woman who has signed one, and who has never met her own tenant, may find that the actual distance between her and her property has become very wide.
“I signed it on a Monday in June, while I made breakfast before leaving for work”, says Kavita, a thirty-eight year old working in Education in Pune. “Eight years later I realised I did not know anything about my own tenant.”
Following the Money
Rental income from a property a woman owns is, as a general rule, income that belongs to her, and income-tax law treats it that way. That means a woman is expected to report it, and pay tax on it, in her own name. Clubbing provisions, which add one spouse’s income to the other’s, apply mainly to assets a husband has transferred to his wife, and not to property she inherited from her own parents. 
In reality, things happen differently. The rent goes into a joint account, or the husband’s account, or a family account used for household costs. The tax return is filed by the husband’s accountant. If the woman has a job, her own income is declared, and the rent appears, if at all, as a line she barely sees. “My CA treated it as family income for years”, says Pooja, aged forty-one, an HR consultant in Gurgaon. “I had to ask multiple times for a statement that showed the rent from my own mother’s flat in my own name.”
Can She Sell it?
Legally, yes. A woman who owns a property absolutely can sell it without her husband’s consent. A buyer’s lawyer will want her signature, not his. Socially, the answer is more complicated, and lawyers describe this familiar scene 
“A woman wants to sell, let’s say, and suddenly there's a family meeting. The husband asks her if she’s sure, the in-laws ask who will invest the money, inevitably a suggestion for saving ‘for the children’ is thrown around. No one says no, they make a thousand excuses.” Sometimes a buyer, or a bank or a registrar asks for a spouse’s no objection signature. Although the law does not require it, the woman agrees to avoid delays. Over time, the exception becomes an expectation.
There is only one place where the law itself erodes a woman’s ownership, and it only becomes visible at death. Under Section 15 of the Hindu Succession Act, if a Hindu woman dies without a will and children, property she inherited will go back to her father’s heirs, and property she inherited from her husband goes back to his. The Supreme Court has described the aim as ensuring the property “goes back to the source.”
But if she dies leaving a husband or children, everything she owns, including what she inherited from her parents passes first to her husband and children. And for self-acquired property, Section 15(1)(b) places her husband’s heirs ahead of her own parents. In November, 2025 a Supreme Court bench of Justices B.V. Nagarathna and R Mahadevan heard a challenge to that provision. The court did not rule on its validity. It instead appealed to Hindu women of all ages to make wills, and directed that where a woman’s parents or their heirs claim her property after she dies without a will, the parties must try pre-litigation mediation first.
The journey of a married woman's property reveals a distinction that Indian law has largely settled and that Indian families have largely not; ownership is a legal status, control is a daily practice. Ownership is a name on a deed. Control is who answers the tenant’s phone calls, who knows the bank password, who is asked first when an offer arrives. A woman can hold the former and have none of the latter. The two tend to separate not through force, but through care. The husband who manages the rent is, in his own mind, being helpful. The father-in-law who knows a broker is saving time. Taken in confluence, they produce an owner that is not consulted. If a daughter’s education and income can be used as a reason to withhold her share of the family’s wealth, her marriage can be used as a reason to withhold control of the share she did receive. In both cases, what looks like protection can end up becoming exclusion.

title: Why Women's Legislative Reservation Remains Pending Despite Constitutional Approval
description: India's Women's Reservation Law is in force, but its implementation remains pending until the completion of the next census and delimitation exercise amid wider political debates
author: Pritha Vashisth
content:
- The Women's Reservation Law reserves one-third of Lok Sabha and state assembly seats for women.
- Implementation awaits the next census and delimitation, despite the law taking effect in 2026.
- Delimitation and caste census debates have delayed the rollout of the 33% quota
The Women's Reservation Bill, formally known as the Nari Shakti Vandan Adhiniyam or the Constitution (One Hundred and Sixth Amendment) Act, 2023, represents a historic step toward greater gender equality in Indian politics. Passed with overwhelming support in Parliament in September 2023, the law aims to reserve one-third of seats for women in the Lok Sabha, state legislative assemblies, and the Delhi Assembly.
However, despite the law being notified and brought into force through a gazette in April 2026, the actual 33% reservation has not yet translated into reserved seats for women candidates in elections. This delay stems from its explicit linkage to complex constitutional processes involving population data and electoral boundary redrawing, processes that have proven politically contentious.
The core provision of the law is straightforward yet transformative. It mandates that, as nearly as possible, one-third of the total seats in the Lok Sabha and state legislative assemblies be reserved for women. It extends to seats already set aside for Scheduled Castes (SCs) and Scheduled Tribes (STs), ensuring that one-third of those reserved seats are also allocated to women from those communities on a rotational basis.
The law applies similarly to the Delhi Legislative Assembly. Once implemented, the reserved seats will rotate after every delimitation exercise to ensure fairness over time. The reservation is intended to last for 15 years from the date of commencement, though Parliament retains the power to extend it further. This framework draws inspiration from the successful implementation of similar quotas in local panchayats and municipalities since the 73rd and 74th Constitutional Amendments in the early 1990s, where women's participation has risen significantly, often exceeding the mandated one-third.
Why Has The Quota Not Come Into Force Yet?
Although the Act received presidential assent in 2023 and was formally notified in April 2026, making it part of the Constitution, the operationalisation of the 33% quota remains pending. The primary reason is a built-in safeguard in the law itself: the reservation cannot be enforced until after the completion of the first census conducted following the Act's commencement and the subsequent delimitation of constituencies.
This condition was included to ensure that the allocation of reserved seats reflects updated population realities and fairly distributed electoral boundaries. India's last major delimitation exercise was based on the 1971 census, with subsequent adjustments frozen to avoid disadvantaging states that had successfully controlled population growth. As a result, carrying out a fresh delimitation involves significant logistical, legal, and political preparation, which cannot be rushed without risking accusations of bias or unfairness.
How Is Delimitation Linked To Implementation?
Delimitation, the process of redrawing parliamentary and assembly constituency boundaries and reallocating seats among states based on population changes, is inextricably tied to the women's reservation because the quota must apply to one-third of the total seats in the new configuration. The 2023 law specifically ties its enforcement to this exercise following the next census, ensuring that women's reserved seats are created within an updated electoral map that accounts for demographic shifts.
Without delimitation, it would be impossible to determine which specific constituencies would be set aside for women or to rotate them fairly in future cycles. In April 2026, the government introduced supporting bills, including proposals to expand the size of the Lok Sabha significantly and to base delimitation on the 2011 census data rather than waiting for newer figures. These measures were intended to allow the women's quota to kick in for the 2029 general elections by creating additional seats to accommodate the one-third reservation without displacing existing ones.
What Role Does The Caste Census Debate Play?
The debate over conducting a caste census has significantly complicated and politicised the path to implementing the women's quota. Many opposition parties have insisted that any new population census should include detailed caste enumeration to provide accurate data for crafting welfare policies and adjusting reservations for Other Backwards Classes and other groups.
Proponents argue that without such data, policies remain blunt instruments that fail to address ground realities of social justice. In contrast, efforts to fast-track women's reservation through delimitation based on older census figures were perceived by some as an attempt to bypass a comprehensive caste-inclusive census, which could reveal updated demographic and social compositions and potentially fuel demands for broader quota revisions.
This intersection of issues has turned what should be a unifying gender empowerment measure into a battleground for deeper federal and social equity concerns. Critics of the government's 2026 approach accused it of using the women's bill as a vehicle to advance delimitation without adequately addressing caste data needs, while the government maintained that the two could be handled separately to avoid unnecessary delays in empowering women. The resulting deadlock highlights how intertwined questions of representation, population dynamics, and historical inequities have become in India's democratic framework.

title: From Nehru’s Midnight Speech To Modi’s Delimitation Push: Five Special Sessions That Shaped Parliament
description: From the midnight sitting that marked Independence to the confrontation over the India-US nuclear deal, the launch of the Goods and Services Tax (GST) and the inauguration of the new Parliament building, these sessions have reflected the political priorities of their time
author: Outlook News Desk
content:
- The explainer examines five landmark parliamentary sittings: the 1947 Independence midnight session, the 1962 China war debate, the 2008 Manmohan Singh government’s confidence vote, the 2017 GST launch and the 2023 new Parliament and women’s reservation session.
- The sessions reflected Parliament’s changing role in marking national milestones.
- The Modi government’s reported plan to convene another special sitting to revive the delimitation package has renewed debate over women’s reservation.
The Narendra Modi government is reportedly considering convening another special sitting of Parliament to revive legislation linking delimitation with the implementation of 33 per cent reservation for women in the Lok Sabha and state Assemblies. The move follows the defeat of a Constitution amendment bill in April, exposing political and constitutional differences over the proposed redistribution of parliamentary seats.
Reports suggest the government is weighing a short session before the Winter Session to reconsider the Constitution (131st Amendment) Bill, 2026, alongside the Delimitation Bill and the Union Territories Laws (Amendment) Bill. No dates have been officially announced.
The proposal has revived questions about the political significance of special sessions. Governments have convened extraordinary sittings to mark national milestones, debate security crises, establish political legitimacy and push through major legislative changes.
From the midnight sitting that marked Independence to the confrontation over the India-US nuclear deal, the launch of the Goods and Services Tax (GST) and the inauguration of the new Parliament building, these sessions have reflected the political priorities of their time.
From Independence To The China War
August 14–15, 1947: The midnight session of Independence
The most consequential midnight sitting in India’s parliamentary history took place on the night of August 14–15, 1947. The Constituent Assembly met in the Central Hall as British rule ended and India became independent.
Jawaharlal Nehru delivered his celebrated ‘Tryst with Destiny’ speech, marking the beginning of a new chapter in the country’s history. The Assembly assumed the responsibilities of the legislature of independent India while continuing its work of framing the Constitution.
The sitting was not a special session of Parliament in the contemporary sense. The Constituent Assembly had the dual responsibility of drafting the Constitution and functioning as the legislature until the first general elections. Nevertheless, the midnight meeting established Parliament’s symbolic association with the birth of independent India.
November 8–9, 1962: The China war session
Fifteen years later, Parliament was summoned amid one of independent India’s gravest security crises. The 1962 war with China exposed weaknesses in military preparedness and triggered criticism of the government’s handling of the conflict.
The Winter Session was advanced following demands from Opposition leaders, including then Bharatiya Jana Sangh leader Atal Bihari Vajpayee, for Parliament to convene and discuss the Chinese aggression. MPs questioned the government over military reverses, defence preparedness and its failure to anticipate the offensive.
Unlike the celebratory sitting of 1947, the 1962 session demonstrated Parliament’s role in holding the executive accountable during a national crisis. It brought questions of intelligence failures, diplomatic assessments and military readiness into legislative scrutiny.
Political Survival, Economic Reform And Institutional Change
July 21–22, 2008: Manmohan Singh’s confidence vote
The special sitting of July 2008 was driven by the survival of the government itself. The Left parties withdrew support to the United Progressive Alliance (UPA) over the India-US civil nuclear agreement, leaving Prime Minister Manmohan Singh facing the prospect of losing his parliamentary majority.
The government sought a confidence vote, and the Lok Sabha convened on July 21 and 22. The UPA survived, securing 275 votes against 256. The support of the Samajwadi Party under Mulayam Singh ensured the result.
The proceedings were overshadowed by allegations of horse-trading. Three BJP MPs displayed bundles of cash in the Lok Sabha, claiming they had been offered money to abstain or support the government. The episode became known as the cash-for-votes scandal.
The vote was significant beyond the government’s immediate survival. It ensured that the nuclear agreement, a defining foreign policy initiative of the Manmohan Singh government, could proceed despite the withdrawal of Left support.
June 30, 2017: The midnight launch of GST
The next major midnight sitting came in 2017, when the Modi government convened Parliament to mark the introduction of the Goods and Services Tax on July 1.
GST replaced a complex system of central and state indirect taxes with a unified tax framework. Its implementation followed years of negotiations between the Centre and states, including under the previous UPA government. The Constitution (101st Amendment) Act, passed in 2016, had enabled the new tax regime.
President Pranab Mukherjee and Prime Minister Modi jointly inaugurated GST during the midnight sitting. The government presented it as a landmark economic reform, drawing comparisons with the 1947 Independence sitting.
Several Opposition parties, including the Congress and the Left, boycotted the ceremony, arguing that the rollout was being turned into a political spectacle. Former prime minister Manmohan Singh also stayed away.
September 18–22, 2023: The new Parliament and women’s reservation
The special session in September 2023 marked another institutional milestone. Proceedings began in the old Parliament building before shifting to the new building on September 19. The session also included a discussion on 75 years of India’s parliamentary journey.
Its most consequential legislative development was the passage of the Nari Shakti Vandan Adhiniyam, providing for 33 per cent reservation for women in the Lok Sabha and state Assemblies.
However, implementation was linked to a future census and delimitation exercise, meaning the reservation would not take effect immediately. The session thus combined institutional symbolism with a major constitutional change, while leaving questions about the timing and implementation of women’s reservation unresolved.
Delimitation And The Politics Of Parliamentary Numbers
The proposed special sitting in 2026 could prove equally consequential, with its significance extending beyond the immediate legislation to the distribution of political representation.
The Constitution (131st Amendment) Bill, introduced in April, sought to facilitate women’s reservation by enabling an expansion of the Lok Sabha from its present strength of 543 seats to a maximum of 850 through delimitation. It was introduced alongside the Delimitation Bill and legislation concerning Union Territories.
The constitutional amendment failed to secure the required special majority in the Lok Sabha on April 17, with 298 MPs voting in favour and 230 against. The defeat exposed opposition to the proposed exercise, particularly among parties from southern states.
Their central concern is that delimitation based on population could increase the parliamentary weight of northern states relative to southern states, which have made greater progress in population control. The government has reportedly considered safeguards to preserve existing inter-state seat ratios while increasing the number of seats. However, no final formula has been established.
The history of special sessions shows that their significance has rarely been confined to the agenda. The 1947 sitting marked the birth of independent India; the 1962 session brought wartime accountability into Parliament; the 2008 vote determined the survival of a government; the 2017 sitting became a showcase for economic reform; and the 2023 session combined institutional change with a major constitutional measure.
If the government convenes another special sitting to revive the delimitation package, Parliament will once again become the arena for a debate extending beyond the immediate legislation. At stake will be not only the implementation of women’s reservation, but also the distribution of political representation between states and the federal balance underpinning India’s parliamentary democracy.

title: Who Is Uzaid Qureshi? Meerut Man Arrested Over Pakistan-Linked Instagram Terror Network, WhatsApp Chats
description: Uzaid Qureshi, a 22-year-old Meerut resident, has been arrested over alleged links with Pakistani handlers and an online radicalisation network being investigated in connection with a terror case in Jammu and Kashmir
author: Rucha Pramanick
content:
- Security agencies arrested Meerut resident Uzaid Qureshi over alleged links with Pakistani handlers and a suspected conspiracy targeting a military airbase in Jammu and Kashmir.
- Investigators are examining WhatsApp conversations and four Instagram accounts allegedly linked to an online network spreading extremist propaganda.
- The Intelligence Bureau, UP ATS and Jammu and Kashmir Police are investigating Qureshi's alleged connections and the wider network.
Security agencies have arrested Uzaid Qureshi, a 22-year-old man from Meerut, Uttar Pradesh, over his alleged links with Pakistani handlers and suspected involvement in a conspiracy to target a military airbase in Jammu and Kashmir. Qureshi was detained from Meerut on Monday night after investigators traced his alleged connections to a terror-related case in Jammu and Kashmir.
Officials familiar with the investigation said suspicious WhatsApp conversations were recovered from his mobile phone, which are now being examined.
Qureshi, a resident of Baniyapada in Meerut's Kotwali area, allegedly came under the scanner after the arrest and interrogation of Mohammad Sajid, a suspected terrorist held in Jammu and Kashmir in November 2025. Investigators reportedly found links between the two through online conversations.
According to police, Qureshi was also allegedly in contact with Pakistani handler Shahzad Bhatti. The agencies are examining the digital evidence to establish the extent of his involvement in the alleged conspiracy.
What Is The Alleged Pakistan-Linked Terror Network?
A separate strand of the investigation concerns an online network allegedly used to circulate extremist propaganda and radicalise individuals. According to Meerut police, the investigation began with a terror-related case registered in Jammu and Kashmir on November 24, 2025. A suspect arrested in Reasi reportedly disclosed information that led investigators to several individuals, including Qureshi. The case was registered under Sections 113 and 3 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS), relating to terrorist activities.
Police said preliminary questioning revealed four Instagram accounts allegedly operating as part of a coordinated online group. These included an account operated by Qureshi, another associated with Kishtwar in Jammu and Kashmir, and two accounts that investigators linked to Pakistan. The accounts were allegedly used to connect individuals, circulate material and promote extremist ideology. Police also identified online groups named 'Tuition Forty Brigade' and 'Al Mujahid' as part of the network.
What Do Investigators Suspect?
According to Meerut Senior Superintendent of Police BBGTS Murthy, Qureshi had allegedly been influenced by extremist videos circulated on YouTube and other social media platforms. Police said he had expressed willingness to participate in such activities through an online comment, which reportedly brought him into contact with Sajid. Investigators are examining whether the online network was being used to recruit and radicalise more people.
After his arrest, Qureshi was questioned by the Intelligence Bureau, Uttar Pradesh Anti-Terrorism Squad and other agencies, according to reports. The Jammu and Kashmir Police have been informed of his detention, and a team was expected to reach Meerut for further action. Investigators are continuing to examine his alleged links, digital communications and the wider network.
Uzaid Case Follows Other Alleged Online Recruitment Operations
The arrest of Uzaid Qureshi comes amid a series of investigations into alleged online recruitment networks involving Pakistan-based handlers and Indian youths. In April 2026, the Uttar Pradesh Anti-Terrorism Squad arrested Tushar Chauhan alias Hizbullah Ali Khan and Sameer Khan, accusing them of being groomed by Pakistani operatives Shahzad Bhatti and Abid Jatt through Instagram. Investigators alleged that the two men were being prepared to carry out grenade attacks at selected locations in Delhi and Uttar Pradesh, with communication later shifting to encrypted channels.
Another investigation emerged after the January 10, 2026, explosion outside Baldev Nagar police station in Ambala. The National Investigation Agency (NIA) alleged that a 25-year-old man from Ghaziabad, identified as Satyam, had been recruited by Bhatti through Instagram, WhatsApp and Signal to transport a vehicle carrying explosives and LPG cylinders. The agency's investigation subsequently led to a chargesheet against eight accused, including Bhatti and Satyam.
The NIA registered a separate case in November to investigate the alleged online recruitment of Indian youths by Bhatti and other suspected Pakistani operatives. Investigators are examining claims that social media and messaging platforms were used to approach young people, offer financial incentives and recruit local operatives for activities that could threaten internal security. The agency's probe follows the UP ATS investigation into the alleged network, suggesting that the Meerut arrest is being examined against a wider set of cases involving digital recruitment and cross-border handlers.

title: Sam Dalrymple Wins NIF Book Prize
description: The Kamaladevi Chattopadhyay NIF Book Prize honours exceptional nonfiction writing on modern India and Mr Dalrymple’s book traces how the five partitions of British India shaped the borders, politics and identities of modern South Asiia
author: AA Correspondent
content:
Sam Dalrymple Wins NIF Book Prize
The Kamaladevi Chattopadhyay NIF Book Prize honours exceptional nonfiction writing on modern India and Mr Dalrymple’s book traces how the five partitions of British India shaped the borders, politics and identities of modern South Asiia
New Delhi: Historian Sam Dalrymple has won the prestigious Kamaladevi Chattopadhyay New India Foundation Book Prize 2026 for his book Shattered Lands: Five Partitions and the Making of Modern Asia published by HarperCollins Fourth Estate. Mr Dalrymple will be presented with the award, which will include the cash prize of INR 15 lakh along with a trophy and a citation, at the official ceremony at the 15th edition of the Bangalore Literature Festival on December 12.
The Kamaladevi Chattopadhyay NIF Book Prize honours exceptional nonfiction writing on modern India and Mr Dalrymple’s book traces how the five partitions of British India shaped the borders, politics and identities of modern South Asia.
The 2026 KCBP shortlist was selected by an eminent jury comprising chairman of Tata Sons and Tata Group N. Chandrasekaran, political scientist and chair of KCBP NIF jury Niraja Gopal Jayal, partner at Trilegal Rahul Matthan, historian of science Jahnavi Phalkey, historian Srinath Raghavan, former foreign secretary of India Nirupama Rao and entrepreneur Manish Sabharwal.
NIF’s work centres on three main initiatives: the NIF Book Fellowship, the Translation Fellowship, and the Kamaladevi Chattopadhyay NIF Book Prize. NIF also partners with the Ashoka Centre for Translation on Bhashavaad, an annual translation conference.

title: Nirad Mohapatra’s Landmark 1984-Odia Film Maya Miriga Returns to the Big Screen
description: Opened for the public for free, the screenings got a huge response from Odia movie lovers
author: akshaya kumar sahoo
content:
Nirad Mohapatra’s Landmark 1984-Odia Film Maya Miriga Returns to the Big Screen
Opened for the public for free, the screenings got a huge response from Odia movie lovers
Bhubaneswar: Film Heritage Foundation (FHF) has announced that it has successfully restored famous movie maker Nirad Mohapatra’s 1984 Odia classic ‘Maya Miriga’ the most feted film in the history. The movie returned to the big screen in cinema halls in Bhubaneswar on Wednesday. The film was screened at Keshari Talkies after a formal opening by Odisha Chief Minister Mohan Charan Majhi Chief Minister in the presence of legendary actress Waheeda Rehman.
Opened for the public for free, the screenings got a huge response from Odia movie lovers.
The release coincides with Film Heritage Foundation’s flagship annual international film preservation and restoration workshop – the 10 edition of the ‘Film Preservation & Restoration Workshop India 2025’ that is being held at the Kalabhoomi Odisha Crafts Museum in Bhubaneswar from November 12 – 19, 2025. Film Heritage Foundation took up the restoration of this forgotten gem as it was in poor condition and we were in danger of losing a precious part of our film heritage.
Nirad Mohapatra’s requiem to the joint family “Maya Miriga” propelled a lesser known regional cinema into national and international recognition at the time it was made. However, since that time both the film and the filmmaker faded away into oblivion.
Noted film critic Maithili Rao termed the vanishing of Nirad Mohapatra from the movie making scene after such an ‘exquisitely elegiac, immensely moving first film’ as one of Indian cinema’s greater unanswered questions.
Shivendra Singh Dungarpur, director, Film Heritage Foundation, said, “It gives us immense satisfaction to be able release the restored version of Nirad Mohapatra’s ‘Maya Miriga’ – the only feature film he made – in cinemas in Bhubaneswar for the public in Odisha, especially as the restoration of the movie was extremely challenging and took three years. We have literally raised the film from the grave having found the negative in a very poor condition abandoned in a warehouse.”
He added: “Through its unhurried gaze set to the haunting soundtrack composed by Bhaskar Chandavarkar and remarkably subtle performances by the nonprofessional cast, the many-layered film tells the moving story of the disintegration of a middle-class joint family in a quiet town that still has resonance in the India of today four decades since the film was made. Unfortunately, the preservation of Odisha’s film heritage has been neglected and much of it is lost. I hope that the restoration of ‘Maya Miriga’ will inspire a movement for the preservation of Odisha’s neglected film heritage.’
Film Heritage Foundation’s policy is to restore hidden gems of India’s regional and artistic cinema that are in danger of being lost to the world. “We have to our credit several world-class restorations of such films– Aravindan Govindan’s two Malayalam films “Kummatty” and “Thamp” , Aribam Syam Sharma’s Manipuri film “Ishanou” and Girish Kasaravalli’s Kannada film “Ghatashradda.” Hence “Maya Miriga” was almost an obvious choice – not just for its beauty and the fact that it was in danger of vanishing, but also because it was a very important film from Odisha whose restoration would serve to bring Odia film heritage back into the limelight,” Dungarpur observed.

title: Private Consumption Picks Up on Easing Inflation and Better Rural Wage Growth
description: Cooling Prices, Rising Wages Fuel Private Consumption Surge in Q4 FY25
author: manisha
content:
Private Consumption Picks Up on Easing Inflation and Better Rural Wage Growth
Cooling Prices, Rising Wages Fuel Private Consumption Surge in Q4 FY25
Chennai: Easing inflation and improved real rural wage growth has led to a pick-up in private consumption, while focus on fiscal consolidation has slackened government consumption.
Private consumption  is expected to have grown at 7.5 per cent in Q4 FY25 against 6.9  per cent in the year ago quarter. Easing inflation along with steady and  sustained real rural wage growth had lifted the consumption demand growth to  the highest level since 1QFY25. 
The retail inflation stood at 3.7 per cent in Q4, dipping below the 4 per  cent target for the first time after a gap of 21 quarters.
Ind-Ra expects the retail inflation  to have declined to 3.2 per cent in April 2025 which would be the lowest since  July 2019 due to sustained easing of food inflation.
Prices of  key food items such as tomato decreased 34.2 per cent, onion 5.7 per cent,  potato 11.3 per cent, pulses 5.2 per cent, and rice 4 per cent in April 2025. Ind-Ra  expects wholesale inflation to have declined to 1.4 per cent in April 2025 from  2 per cent in March 2025.
Meanwhile, rural demand continued to recover as indicated by  various FMCG companies in their quarterly results for Q4. The rural real wage  growth remained positive for the third straight quarter. It averaged 3.7 per  cent in January-February, which was the fastest pace of growth since Q2 FY20.
However, the government consumption expenditure is expected  to have slowed down to 5 per cent in Q4 FY25 from a five-quarter high of 8.3  per cent in Q3 FY25. As the government consumption had grown by 6.6 per cent in  Q4 FY24, the high base led to the slower growth in the last quarter. Further, the government  moving ahead towards fiscal consolidation targets also saw the expenditure  coming down.
Investment demand inched up to 6.5 per cent in Q4 FY25 against  6 per cent in the year-ago quarter and 5.7 per cent in the previous quarter. 
( Source : Asian Age )

title: Hyderabad Must Prioritise People Over Vehicles To Fix Mobility Crisis: Jayesh Ranjan, Penalosa
description: Penalosa proposed satellite-based vehicle tracking and congestion-based charges, with motorists paying more for using busy roads during peak hours.
author: DC Correspondent
content:
Hyderabad Must Prioritise People Over Vehicles To Fix Mobility Crisis: Jayesh Ranjan, Penalosa
Penalosa proposed satellite-based vehicle tracking and congestion-based charges, with motorists paying more for using busy roads during peak hours.
Hyderabad: The city must move beyond traffic management and address deeper urban planning and governance failures to tackle its growing mobility crisis, special chief secretary Jayesh Ranjan and former Bogota. Colombia, mayor Enrique Penalosa said during a panel discussion at Cyberabad Moves 2026 on Thursday.
Ranjan said the first step was to identify the problem rather than resort to isolated solutions such as common mobility cards or pedestrian crossings.
He called for an ambitious shift in commuting patterns through better utilisation of road space, technology and policy interventions.
He said, "9.3 million new vehicles have been registered in the city over the past year, while a peak-hour survey at Cyber Towers found 10,138 people travelling alone in cars and another 3,584 vehicles carrying just two occupants."
Identifying institutional fragmentation as a major challenge, Sashi Verma, chief technology officer, Transport for London, said, Responsibility for urban development and mobility was divided among several agencies.
If all the related agencies or wings are under th same old and falling under the same ministry and a minister o overlook the operations, the work flow would have been smokther."
Verma alsk called for an empowered mechanism to integrate decision-making, funding and accountability rather than relying on coordination bodies.
He also criticised planning regulations that leave large portions of privately owned land fenced off as inaccessible open spaces, calling for developers to make spaces around buildings and ground floors more welcoming and accessible to the public.
Penalosa said Hyderabad must first decide what kind of city it wanted to become.
He stressed, "Metro Rail and mass transport could improve mobility but would not necessarily resolve traffic congestion.
Delhi's extensive Metro Rail network needed to restrict the use of private vehicles, particularly during peak hours, rather than merely expanding transport infrastructure."
He proposed satellite-based vehicle tracking and congestion-based charges, with motorists paying more for using busy roads during peak hours.
He also identified motorcycles as a major challenge, calling for strict enforcement against riding and parking on footpaths.
On bus transport, Penalosa advocated dedicated BRT corridors on high-demand roads, with lanes in the centre of the road and strict enforcement against other vehicles entering them.
He said quality footpaths were equally important as every public transport journey began and ended with walking.
He urged Hyderabad to develop extensive cycling corridors and public parks as the city expands.
Transport adviser N.V.S. Reddy suggested integrating employee transport services with the Cyberabad Police's Hawk Eye app to strengthen the safety of women commuters throughout their journeys, including first- and last-mile connectivity.
He also stressed the need for improved footpaths and walkways.
Rekha Srinivasan of United Way of Hyderabad highlighted research-led and on-ground interventions for safer, more accessible and inclusive transport, while industry representatives called for sustained corporate participation, staggered working hours and measurable CSR outcomes.

title: Jagan Alleges Poll Code Violations, Demands Re-Polling
description: He demanded re-polling wherever voting has been compromised and sought action against TD leaders, police personnel and officials responsible for undermining voting.
author: DC Correspondent
content:
Jagan Alleges Poll Code Violations, Demands Re-Polling
He demanded re-polling wherever voting has been compromised and sought action against TD leaders, police personnel and officials responsible for undermining voting.
Vijayawada: YSRC president and former chief minister Y.S. Jagan Mohan Reddy has alleged several violations of the Model Code of Conduct, including threats to voters, assaults on polling agents, theft of ballot papers, and mass rigging, during the local body elections in the state on Thursday.
In a post on X, he said during the second phase of municipal elections and the first phase of gram panchayat polls, the ruling Telugu Desam had used police and government officials to intimidate YSRC leaders, candidates, and voters to influence the outcome.
The YSRC chief cited several incidents.
In Ahobilam, he said, a vehicle in the convoy of TD MLA Bhuma Akhila Priya allegedly hit YSRC supporters, injuring five people and leaving a woman in critical condition.
In Mangampeta, NDA supporters allegedly attacked polling agents and broke one agent’s arm.
In Prasannayanapalli, TD leaders allegedly threatened polling officials and stole ballot papers.
In Narasampalli, two men allegedly poured ink into ballot boxes, halting polling in two wards.
In Vellaturu, TD groups allegedly shut polling booth doors and brought in outsiders to cast bogus votes.
Jagan Mohan Reddy said similar incidents have occurred across the state.
He questioned Chief Minister N. Chandrababu Naidu role in these developments, saying every voter has the right to cast a ballot without fear.
The former CM said the government will have to answer every voter who has been threatened, every polling agent who has been assaulted and every ballot paper that has been stolen.
He demanded re-polling wherever voting has been compromised.
He sought action against TD leaders, police personnel and officials responsible for undermining voting.
Jagan Mohan Reddy warned that the YSRC would take the matter to the court.

title: 17% tariff offer puts India’s policy choices under scrutiny
description: Washington has tied a potential cut in proposed Section 301 tariffs on India from 25% to 17% to sweeping policy demands, putting industrial schemes like Make in India and PLI under scrutiny ahead of trade talks.
author: Mukesh Jagota, Shubham Rana
content:
Even though the United States has signalled its willingness to reduce the additional Section 301 duty on India from 25% proposed to 17% under the forthcoming trade deal, it has laid out conditions that New Delhi might find difficult to meet. The US Trade Representative (USTR) in the document released on Wednesday giving the findings of its “structural excess capacity” probe into 14 economies sought changes to India’s manufacturing-led growth strategy, labour laws, financial policies and market-access regime.
The USTR alleged Indian manufacturers increasingly rely on capital, intermediate goods and inputs from non-market economies, particularly China, to scale production and lower costs.
According to official sources and experts, these demands amount to laying out a negotiating agenda that goes well beyond conventional concessions under a Bilateral Trade Agreement (BTA).
The USTR flagged five broad areas it wants India to address, arguing that these policies distort market competition and contribute to excess manufacturing capacity. It has, however, not spelt out specific legislative changes or quantified commitments that India must make to qualify for the proposed 17% rate. The terms would be subject to negotiations, with USTR inviting comments on the tariff action and possible adjustments following a final agreement.
“Offering India a 17% deal rate (versus 25% without a pact) is a calculated bait designed to show a marginal 1%–3% tariff edge over rivals like Bangladesh, Vietnam, and China rather than an objective assessment of overcapacity,” founder of Global Trade Research Initiative (GTRI) Ajay Srivastava said. “With the threat of up to 100% Graham tariffs still looming, New Delhi must reject a one-sided trade deal and defend its industrial expansion sector by sector as serving legitimate domestic, export, and future demand,” he added..
Madan Sabnavis, chief economist, Bank of Baroda said, “Even if the 25% tariff stays, it is unlikely to lead to a policy change in India since these are national policies. It is up to the Indian commerce department to put their case forward that there is nothing extraordinary being done under the Indian schemes (like production-linked incentives) and then try to negotiate the best possible tariff rate for India.”
The framework of the interim BTA has already been agreed to and both sides are working on a formal agreement. The understanding on the framework reached in February had proposed to cut additional tariffs on India to 18% from 50% of which 25% were duties linked to buying Russian crude. The offer went into cold storage as the US Supreme Court invalidated reciprocal tariffs which were the basis of negotiations.
Madhavi Arora, chief economist, Emkay Global Financial Services, noted that Section 301 tariffs are on a more solid legal footing and harder to challenge in court or via Congress than the earlier reciprocal tariffs. She, however, added that theRepublicans’ resounding midterm loss may mean that there is some moderation in these tariffs, with public hearings scheduled for late January 2027. The ongoing negotiations on the India-US bilateral trade deal will be crucial to ensure a lower tariff rate of 17% and preferential access for Indian exports to the US market,” she said.
India on Wednesday reiterated its commitment to an early conclusion of the BTA with the US, maintaining that trade-related concerns should be addressed within the framework of ongoing negotiations.
At the heart of Washington’s objections is India’s state-led industrial policy, including programmes such as Make in India, Production Linked Incentive (PLI) schemes and Atmanirbhar Bharat, which the US alleges channel resources towards expanding manufacturing capacity and exports without a commensurate increase in domestic demand. The US has particularly identified sectors such as steel, solar, healthcare and information and communications technology (ICT), where it argues government incentives and other interventions sustain production beyond market-driven levels.
The tariff proposal also provides exemptions from the additional Section 301 duties for specified products already covered by Section 232 national-security tariffs, including steel, aluminium and copper products, vehicles and parts, heavy vehicles, wood products, patented pharmaceuticals and semiconductor articles.
Manoj Mishra, partner and tax controversy management leader, Grant Thornton Bharat said: “With India’s key industrial initiatives, including Make in India and PLI, coming under USTR scrutiny, the proposed measures could weaken India’s export competitiveness, put pressure on profit margins and dampen manufacturing investments.” He added that while the possibility of a lower tariff rate of 17% exists, India could also leverage its expanding FTA network, diversify export markets and global supply chains to reduce dependence on the US and mitigate the impact of evolving tariff measures.
USTR has also invited comments on a possible mechanism allowing a specified volume of textile and apparel imports to enter the US at a reduced Section 301 tariff rate, potentially opening up scope for preferential access for Indian exporters.

title: Industry seeks better BTA terms; no tariff impact seen this fiscal
description: Proposed US tariffs are unlikely to hit Indian exports hard this fiscal year before February, but FIEO, EEPC, and GJEPC question whether a 17% trade deal rate gives India a real edge over rivals.
author: FE Bureau
content:
The proposed higher US tariffs are unlikely to significantly impact Indian exporters in the current financial year, as the measures are not expected to take effect before February at the earliest and are likely to be followed by a transition period. However, industry representatives said the proposed tariff structure has heightened uncertainty and questioned whether a 17% tariff for India under the proposed Bilateral Trade Agreement (BTA) would offer a meaningful competitive advantage over rival suppliers.
Ajay Sahai, Director General and CEO of the Federation of Indian Export Organisations (FIEO), said there was concern in the trade and industry but no panic among exporters. He said the government should use the limited window available to negotiate better terms.
India has maintained that any trade agreement with the US must provide a comparative tariff advantage. However, Sahai questioned the benefit when Vietnam could also come down to 15% under a BTA, while Bangladesh, Indonesia and Thailand face tariffs of around 18%.
“What is your advantage? How much will you gain? I don’t think it makes any sense,” he said, flagging concerns that concessions offered by India could be permanent even as the US administration could change. He also pointed to legal challenges to the forced-labour provisions as an additional source of uncertainty.
Pankaj Chadha, chairman of EEPC India, said the proposed 17% reciprocal tariff under a trade deal could erode India’s competitive advantage over several competing manufacturing economies. While Bangladesh, Indonesia, Malaysia and Thailand face tariffs of around 18%, India would continue to be at a disadvantage against the European Union, Japan, South Korea, Taiwan and Switzerland.
The gem and jewellery sector has also sought an early agreement to restore price competitiveness in the US market. Kirit Bhansali, chairman of the Gem and Jewellery Export Promotion Council, said the proposed 25% tariff could weigh on the sector after exports to the US rose 14.87% to $3.607 billion during April-October 2026.
The industry is hopeful that the BTA will bring the tariff down to 17%. However, Bhansali said developing alternative markets would take two to three years, while the impact of higher tariffs could be felt within 45 days to two months.
FIEO has backed an early conclusion of a balanced and reciprocal BTA, while seeking clarity on how the proposed measures would interact with existing duties under Sections 301 and 232. It has also called for special attention to MSMEs, which have limited capacity to absorb higher duties and compliance costs.

title: Textile exporters unfazed, pin hopes on early trade deal
description: Indian textile exporters eye an early US trade deal to cut proposed tariffs and regain competitiveness; watch how talks shape pricing and orders.
author: Narayanan V
content:
India’s textile and apparel exporters are unfazed by the latest US tariff proposals, banking on an early conclusion of the bilateral trade agreement (BTA) to secure a lower rate and improve their competitiveness against rival Asian exporters. However, they have called for greater clarity and predictability in the tariff regime to help plan orders and pricing.
The US on Wednesday proposed an additional tariff of up to 25% on Indian goods under its Section 301 investigation into structural excess capacity in manufacturing. The rate could, however, come down to 17% if India and the US reach a reciprocal trade agreement. Industry executives said India’s relative tariff position against competing sourcing destinations would be critical to its competitiveness in the US market.
Madhu Sudhan Bhageria, chairman and managing director of polyester filament yarn manufacturer Filatex India, said the proposed rates should be viewed in the context of tariffs faced by competing countries rather than in isolation.
“The headline rate matters less than India’s rate against competing supply bases. At the proposed 25%, India sits below Vietnam at 35%. With an agreement, India’s 17% would sit below Bangladesh and the ASEAN exporters at 18%, and China and Vietnam at 20%,” he said.
Filatex’s exposure to the US market is largely indirect, through Indian garment and home-textile manufacturers that use its yarn. “Those customers are buying on a need basis until there is clarity, but they have not stepped away,” he said.
The Confederation of Indian Textile Industry (CITI) has called for a stable and predictable tariff framework, pointing out that frequent changes in trade policies create uncertainty for exporters and overseas buyers. The chances of such a scenario is seen to be remote.
“Frequent changes in tariff policies and regulations create considerable uncertainty for exporters and their overseas buyers,” said Chandrima Chatterjee, secretary general of CITI. She added that such changes were difficult to accommodate in commercial negotiations, pricing arrangements and buyer commitments, particularly in the textile and apparel sector, where orders are often negotiated and finalised well in advance of shipment.
The proposed 25% tariff, replacing the existing additional tariff of 10%, would represent a net increase of 15 percentage points over the present tariff component, over and above applicable most-favoured-nation (MFN) duties, subject to the final provisions and exemptions.
However, if the proposed 25% tariff coexists with the 10% forced labour tariff, along with MFN rates that are relatively higher for many textile tariff lines, the cumulative duty can potentially rise to 40% and beyond.
“A lower rate of 17%, if secured through a trade agreement, could put India in a relatively favourable position against competing Asian economies, where the corresponding rates are indicated at 18-20%” Chatterjee added.
India’s ready-made garment (RMG) exports during April-October 2026-27 stood at $8.6 billion, down 2.97% year-on-year. Meanwhile, US apparel imports declined 6.1% during January-September 2026, while imports from India fell 25.2% to $3.1 billion, partly due to tariff-related uncertainties.
“In the emerging tariff scenario, the key factor is India’s relative tariff competitiveness vis-à-vis competing countries. A favourable India-US trade deal can help us regain the lost market share and subsequently expand it,” said Prabhu Dhamodharan, convenor of the Indian Texpreneurs Federation.
The Apparel Export Promotion Council (AEPC) also expressed optimism, saying the government was negotiating with the US administration to secure India’s exemption from the proposed Section 301 measures.
A Sakthivel, chairman of AEPC, said the proposed tariffs on competing countries were up to 35% for Vietnam, potentially falling to 20% with an agreement, and up to 18% for Bangladesh, Cambodia, Indonesia, Malaysia and Thailand.
“We are hopeful of a positive outcome from the India-US negotiations and a mutually beneficial trade deal that provides greater certainty to the industry,” he said.
Sakthivel said expanding market access through trade agreements, including the India-UK trade agreement operationalised on July 15 and the India-EU free trade agreement expected in 2027, along with continued market diversification, would support export growth.

title: ममता बनर्जी के परिवार में तकरार, भाई बाबुन ने अभिषेक बनर्जी के खिलाफ पुलिस से की शिकायत
description: West Bengal News: पश्चिम बंगाल की पूर्व मुख्यमंत्री ममता बनर्जी के भाई बाबुन बनर्जी ने तृणमूल कांग्रेस (TMC) सांसद अभिषेक बनर्जी के खिलाफ कोलकाता के कालीघाट थाने में लिखित शिकायत दर्ज कराई है. उन्होंने अभिषेक पर आपराधिक धमकी, सरकारी अधिकारियों के काम में बाधा डालने, न्यायपालिका का अपमान करने और देश की संप्रभुता को खतरे में डालने जैसे गंभीर आरोप लगाए हैं. बाबुन ने पुलिस से शिकायत को सिर्फ जनरल डायरी (GD) में दर्ज करने के बजाय FIR दर्ज कर कानूनी कार्रवाई करने की मांग की है.
author: शंकर पंड‍ित
content:
ममता बनर्जी के परिवार में तकरार, भाई बाबुन ने अभिषेक बनर्जी के खिलाफ पुलिस से की शिकायत
Edited by:
Agency:आईएएनएस
Last Updated:
West Bengal News: पश्चिम बंगाल की पूर्व मुख्यमंत्री ममता बनर्जी के भाई बाबुन बनर्जी ने तृणमूल कांग्रेस (TMC) सांसद अभिषेक बनर्जी के खिलाफ कोलकाता के कालीघाट थाने में लिखित शिकायत दर्ज कराई है. उन्होंने अभिषेक पर आपराधिक धमकी, सरकारी अधिकारियों के काम में बाधा डालने, न्यायपालिका का अपमान करने और देश की संप्रभुता को खतरे में डालने जैसे गंभीर आरोप लगाए हैं. बाबुन ने पुलिस से शिकायत को सिर्फ जनरल डायरी (GD) में दर्ज करने के बजाय FIR दर्ज कर कानूनी कार्रवाई करने की मांग की है.
West Bengal News: पश्चिम बंगाल में एक अजीब घटना देखने को मिली है. बंगाल की पूर्व मुख्यमंत्री ममता बनर्जी के घर में खटपट हो गई है. उनके भतीजे अभिषेक बनर्जी की मुसीबत बढ़ने वाली है. जी हां, ममता बनर्जी की भाई बाबुन बनर्जी ने गुरुवार को तृणमूल कांग्रेस सांसद अभिषेक बनर्जी के खिलाफ दक्षिण कोलकाता के कालीघाट पुलिस स्टेशन में लिखित शिकायत दर्ज कराई, जिसमें उन्होंने उन पर कई गंभीर आरोप लगाए हैं.
बाबुन बनर्जी ने अभिषेक बनर्जी पर आपराधिक बल का प्रयोग करने, लोक सेवकों को उनके कर्तव्यों के पालन से रोकने की कोशिश करने, आपराधिक धमकी देने, न्यायिक कार्यवाही में बैठे लोक सेवकों का जानबूझकर अपमान करने और भारत की संप्रभुता को खतरे में डालने का आरोप लगाया है.
उन्होंने यह भी आरोप लगाया कि टीएमसी सांसद जनता को न्यायपालिका और संवैधानिक अधिकारियों के खिलाफ भड़का कर विध्वंसक गतिविधियों और आपराधिक साजिश को बढ़ावा देने की कोशिश कर रहे हैं. बाबुन बनर्जी ने पुलिस से आग्रह किया कि वे इस शिकायत को केवल एक सामान्य डायरी प्रविष्टि (जनरल डायरी एंट्री) मानने के बजाय एक एफआईआर के रूप में दर्ज करें और आवश्यक कानूनी कार्रवाई शुरू करें.
सूत्रों के अनुसार, बाबुन गुरुवार को शिकायत दर्ज कराने के लिए कालीघाट पुलिस स्टेशन पहुंचे. उन्होंने आरोप लगाया कि धमकियों और डराने-धमकाने का जो माहौल पिछली तृणमूल कांग्रेस सरकार के दौरान शुरू हुआ था, वह राज्य में अब भी कायम है। उन्होंने दावा किया कि सरकारी कामकाज में बाधा डालने, स्थानीय क्लबों पर जबरन कब्जा करने और विभिन्न क्षेत्रों के लोगों को डराने-धमकाने की घटनाएं हो रही हैं.
Advertisement
उन्होंने लंबे समय तक बहुत कुछ सहा है, लेकिन अब स्थिति इतनी बिगड़ गई है कि उनके पास पुलिस के पास जाने के अलावा कोई विकल्प नहीं बचा है. शिकायत में पुलिसकर्मियों और सरकारी कर्मचारियों के दैनिक कामकाज में हस्तक्षेप करने के आरोपों के साथ-साथ न्यायपालिका पर हमले जैसे गंभीर आरोप भी लगाए गए हैं.
पुलिस अधिकारियों ने पुष्टि की है कि उन्हें लिखित शिकायत मिल गई है और मामले की जांच चल रही है. कोलकाता पुलिस के एक वरिष्ठ अधिकारी ने बताया कि लगाए गए आरोपों के आधार पर जांच की जाएगी, हालांकि अभी तक यह स्पष्ट नहीं है कि कोई औपचारिक प्राथमिकी (एफआईआर) दर्ज की गई है या नहीं. पूर्व मुख्यमंत्री के परिवार के भीतर चल रहे मतभेदों के सार्वजनिक होने से पश्चिम बंगाल के राजनीतिक हलकों में काफी हलचल मच गई है.

content:

Written by:

Today Weather Live: 27 नवंबर को देश के मौसम में बड़ा अंतर देखने को मिलेगा. मौसम विभाग (IMD) के अनुसार दिल्ली और हरियाणा में सुबह घना कोहरा छाने की आशंका है. इससे सड़क यातायात और विजिबिलिटी प्रभावित हो सकती है. पूर्वी राजस्थान में शीतलहर का अलर्ट है. उत्तर प्रदेश, बिहार, झारखंड और मध्य प्रदेश में मौसम मुख्य रूप से शुष्क रहने का अनुमान है. पहाड़ी राज्यों में भी सुबह और रात की ठंड बढ़ेगी. दूसरी तरफ दक्षिण भारत में बारिश और तेज हवाएं परेशानी बढ़ा सकती हैं. तमिलनाडु, केरल, पुडुचेरी और कराईकल में भारी बारिश की चेतावनी जारी की गई है. आंध्र प्रदेश और लक्षद्वीप में गरज-चमक के साथ तेज हवाएं चल सकती हैं. पूर्वोत्तर के कुछ राज्यों में भी घना कोहरा छाने का अनुमान है.
Aaj Ka Mausam Live: नवंबर का आखिरी शुक्रवार देश के अलग-अलग हिस्सों में मौसम के कई रंग लेकर आया है. कहीं सुबह की शुरुआत घने कोहरे के साथ हो सकती है तो कहीं बारिश और तेज हवाएं लोगों की परेशानी बढ़ा सकती हैं. मौसम विभाग (IMD) ने 27 नवंबर को दिल्ली-एनसीआर समेत उत्तर भारत के कई राज्यों में घने कोहरे की चेतावनी जारी की है. दिल्ली और हरियाणा में सुबह के समय विजिबिलिटी कम रहने की आशंका है. पूर्वी राजस्थान में शीतलहर का असर महसूस हो सकता है. दूसरी तरफ दक्षिण भारत में मौसम ज्यादा सक्रिय रहने वाला है. तमिलनाडु और केरल में भारी बारिश का अलर्ट है. आंध्र प्रदेश और आसपास के इलाकों में गरज-चमक के साथ तेज हवाएं चल सकती हैं.
यानी आज उत्तर भारत के लोगों को सुबह घर से निकलते समय कोहरे का सामना करना पड़ सकता है. वहीं दक्षिण भारत के कुछ राज्यों में बारिश और आंधी के कारण जनजीवन प्रभावित होने की आशंका है. मौसम विभाग के पूर्वानुमान के मुताबिक तमिलनाडु, पुडुचेरी और कराईकल में 40 से 50 किलोमीटर प्रति घंटे की रफ्तार से तेज हवाएं चल सकती हैं. केरल और माहे में भी भारी बारिश की संभावना है. पूर्वोत्तर के असम और मेघालय समेत कुछ राज्यों में घना कोहरा छाने का अनुमान है. उत्तर प्रदेश, बिहार और झारखंड में फिलहाल मौसम के बड़े बदलाव का अलर्ट नहीं है. आइए जानते हैं दिल्ली से लेकर दक्षिण भारत और पूर्वोत्तर तक आज मौसम का हाल कैसा रहने वाला है.
लखनऊ में अधिकतम तापमान 27 डिग्री और न्यूनतम 12 डिग्री सेल्सियस रहने की संभावना है. (PTI)
दिल्ली-NCR में सुबह कोहरे की चादर, ठंड भी बढ़ेगी
दिल्ली और आसपास के इलाकों में शुक्रवार सुबह घना कोहरा परेशानी बढ़ा सकता है. IMD ने राजधानी के लिए कोहरे का अलर्ट जारी किया है. सुबह के समय सड़कों पर विजिबिलिटी कम होने से वाहन चालकों को दिक्कत हो सकती है. खासकर दफ्तर और स्कूल जाने वाले लोगों को अतिरिक्त सावधानी बरतने की जरूरत होगी. दिल्ली में बारिश की कोई प्रमुख संभावना नहीं है. मौसम शुष्क बना रहेगा. तापमान की बात करें तो अधिकतम 26 डिग्री और न्यूनतम 9 डिग्री सेल्सियस रहने का अनुमान है. नोएडा और गाजियाबाद में भी सुबह के समय ठंड और धुंध का असर महसूस हो सकता है.
यूपी में मौसम रहेगा शुष्क, सुबह-रात बढ़ेगी ठंड

उत्तर प्रदेश में 27 नवंबर को मौसम के शुष्क रहने का अनुमान है. मौसम विभाग ने प्रदेश के लिए भारी बारिश का कोई प्रमुख अलर्ट जारी नहीं किया है. हालांकि सुबह और रात के समय तापमान में गिरावट से ठंड का असर बढ़ सकता है. लखनऊ में अधिकतम तापमान 27 डिग्री और न्यूनतम 12 डिग्री सेल्सियस रहने की संभावना है. पश्चिमी उत्तर प्रदेश में दिल्ली और हरियाणा से सटे इलाकों में सुबह के समय धुंध देखने को मिल सकती है. ऐसे में शुरुआती घंटों में वाहन चलाते समय सावधानी जरूरी होगी.
27 नवंबर को बड़े शहरों का तापमान
बिहार में बारिश का अलर्ट नहीं, ठंड का असर रहेगा
बिहार में शुक्रवार को मौसम सामान्य रूप से शुष्क रहने की संभावना है. राज्य के लिए भारी बारिश या तेज हवाओं को लेकर कोई विशेष चेतावनी नहीं दी गई है. हालांकि सुबह और रात के समय ठंड महसूस होगी. दिन में धूप निकलने से मौसम अपेक्षाकृत सामान्य रह सकता है. पटना में अधिकतम तापमान 27 डिग्री और न्यूनतम 19 डिग्री सेल्सियस रहने का अनुमान है. नवंबर के आखिरी दिनों में रात के तापमान में गिरावट के साथ सुबह की ठंड और बढ़ सकती है.
झारखंड में फिलहाल मौसम रहेगा सामान्य
झारखंड में 27 नवंबर को मौसम में किसी बड़े बदलाव की संभावना नहीं है. राज्य में बारिश को लेकर कोई प्रमुख चेतावनी सामने नहीं आई है. रांची समेत ज्यादातर इलाकों में मौसम शुष्क रहने का अनुमान है. सुबह और रात के समय ठंड का असर बढ़ सकता है. रांची में अधिकतम तापमान 24 डिग्री और न्यूनतम 13 डिग्री सेल्सियस रहने की संभावना है. दिन में धूप निकलने से लोगों को कुछ राहत मिल सकती है.
राजस्थान में पूर्वी हिस्सों में शीतलहर की आशंका
राजस्थान में नवंबर के आखिरी सप्ताह के साथ ठंड का असर बढ़ने लगा है. मौसम विभाग ने पूर्वी राजस्थान में शीतलहर की स्थिति बनने की आशंका जताई है. इससे सुबह और रात के समय ठंड ज्यादा महसूस हो सकती है. प्रदेश के अन्य हिस्सों में मौसम शुष्क रहने का अनुमान है. फिलहाल बारिश या आंधी को लेकर कोई बड़ा अलर्ट नहीं है. जयपुर में अधिकतम तापमान 26 डिग्री और न्यूनतम 14 डिग्री सेल्सियस रह सकता है. पूर्वी राजस्थान के लोगों को सुबह और देर रात ठंड से बचाव की तैयारी रखनी चाहिए.
मध्य प्रदेश में मौसम शुष्क, रात के तापमान में गिरावट
मध्य प्रदेश में शुक्रवार को मौसम सामान्य रहने की संभावना है. राज्य के लिए बारिश या तेज हवाओं का कोई प्रमुख अलर्ट नहीं है. भोपाल समेत कई शहरों में दिन के समय धूप निकल सकती है. हालांकि रात के तापमान में गिरावट के कारण सुबह और देर शाम ठंड का अहसास बढ़ेगा. भोपाल में अधिकतम तापमान 27 डिग्री और न्यूनतम 9 डिग्री सेल्सियस रहने का अनुमान है. आने वाले दिनों में ठंड का असर और बढ़ सकता है.
पंजाब-हरियाणा में घना कोहरा बढ़ाएगा परेशानी
- पंजाब और हरियाणा में शुक्रवार सुबह घना कोहरा छाने की संभावना है. मौसम विभाग ने दोनों राज्यों के कुछ इलाकों के लिए चेतावनी जारी की है. इससे हाईवे और प्रमुख सड़कों पर विजिबिलिटी कम हो सकती है.
- हरियाणा के साथ चंडीगढ़ में भी कोहरे का असर देखने को मिल सकता है. दिन चढ़ने के साथ विजिबिलिटी में सुधार होने की उम्मीद है. फिलहाल इन राज्यों में बारिश को लेकर कोई प्रमुख अलर्ट नहीं है. ठंडी हवाओं के कारण सुबह और रात के समय ठंड का असर बना रहेगा.
तमिलनाडु, पुडुचेरी और कराईकल में कुछ स्थानों पर भारी बारिश हो सकती है. (IMD)
उत्तराखंड में मौसम शुष्क, हिमाचल में कोहरा, जम्मू-कश्मीर में ठंड का असर
- उत्तराखंड में 27 नवंबर को मौसम मुख्य रूप से शुष्क रहने का अनुमान है. राज्य के लिए बारिश या बर्फबारी की कोई बड़ी चेतावनी जारी नहीं की गई है. हालांकि ऊंचाई वाले इलाकों में तापमान कम रहने से सुबह और रात के समय ठंड ज्यादा महसूस होगी. नैनीताल में अधिकतम तापमान 19 डिग्री और न्यूनतम 9 डिग्री सेल्सियस रहने का अनुमान है.
- हिमाचल प्रदेश के कुछ हिस्सों में शुक्रवार सुबह घना कोहरा छाने की आशंका है. मौसम विभाग ने राज्य के लिए कम विजिबिलिटी को लेकर चेतावनी दी है. हालांकि 27 नवंबर को भारी बारिश या बर्फबारी का कोई प्रमुख अलर्ट नहीं है. शिमला में अधिकतम तापमान 19 डिग्री और न्यूनतम 8 डिग्री सेल्सियस रहने की संभावना है. ऊंचाई वाले इलाकों में रात का मौसम काफी ठंडा रह सकता है.
- जम्मू-कश्मीर में नवंबर के आखिरी दिनों में ठंड का असर लगातार बढ़ रहा है. घाटी और ऊंचाई वाले इलाकों में सुबह तथा रात के समय तापमान कम रहने से ठंड महसूस होगी. हालांकि स्थानीय मौसम में बदलाव संभव है.
दक्षिण भारत में भारी बारिश और 50 KM तक तेज हवाओं का अलर्ट
दक्षिण भारत के कई राज्यों में शुक्रवार को मौसम सक्रिय रहेगा. तमिलनाडु, पुडुचेरी और कराईकल में कुछ स्थानों पर भारी बारिश हो सकती है. यहां गरज-चमक और बिजली गिरने की भी आशंका है. इन इलाकों में 40 से 50 किलोमीटर प्रति घंटे की रफ्तार से तेज हवाएं चल सकती हैं. केरल और माहे में भी कुछ जगहों पर भारी बारिश का अनुमान है. यहां हवा की गति 30 से 40 किलोमीटर प्रति घंटे तक रह सकती है. आंध्र प्रदेश में गरज-चमक के साथ बिजली गिरने और तेज सतही हवाओं की चेतावनी है. लक्षद्वीप में भी कुछ स्थानों पर बारिश और तेज हवाएं चल सकती हैं. कर्नाटक के तटीय और दक्षिण आंतरिक हिस्सों में हल्की से मध्यम बारिश होने की संभावना है. दक्षिण भारत के इन इलाकों में रहने वाले लोगों को गरज-चमक के दौरान खुले स्थानों और पेड़ों के नीचे खड़े होने से बचना चाहिए.
पूर्वोत्तर में असम-मेघालय समेत कई राज्यों में घना कोहरा
पूर्वोत्तर भारत के कुछ राज्यों में भी सुबह के समय घना कोहरा छा सकता है. IMD ने असम और मेघालय के साथ मणिपुर तथा त्रिपुरा के कुछ इलाकों में कम विजिबिलिटी की आशंका जताई है. इससे सुबह के समय सड़क और दूसरे परिवहन साधनों से सफर करने वालों को परेशानी हो सकती है. लोगों को यात्रा से पहले मौसम की स्थिति की जानकारी लेने की सलाह दी जाती है. ओडिशा के लिए 27 नवंबर को घने कोहरे की कोई नई प्रमुख चेतावनी नहीं दी गई है.

जाकिर नाइक की बढ़ी मुसीबत, अब इस्लामिक रिसर्च फाउंडेशन की लगेगी लंका, केंद्र ने राज्यों को दिया सुपरपावर

Agency:पीटीआई
Last Updated:
Zakir Naik News: केंद्र सरकार ने जाकिर नाइक के प्रतिबंधित संगठन इस्लामिक रिसर्च फाउंडेशन (IRF) के खिलाफ यूएपीए (UAPA) के तहत कार्रवाई करने के लिए राज्यों और केंद्र शासित प्रदेशों को अधिकार दे दिए हैं. गृह मंत्रालय ने UAPA की धारा 42 के तहत अधिसूचना जारी कर राज्यों को धारा 7 और 8 की शक्तियां सौंपी हैं. अब राज्य सरकारें संगठन के फंड और वित्तीय संपत्तियों के इस्तेमाल या हस्तांतरण पर रोक लगाने के साथ ही संदिग्ध परिसरों को भी अपने नियंत्रण में ले सकेंगी. इससे पहले 13 नवंबर को केंद्र ने IRF पर प्रतिबंध को पांच साल के लिए बढ़ाया था. जाकिर नाइक 2016 से मलेशिया में रह रहे हैं.
Zakir Naik News: भगोड़े इस्लामिक उपदेशक जाकिर नाइक की मुसीबत बढ़ने वाली है. जाकिर नाइक की भारत में प्रतिबंधित संस्था इस्लामिक रिसर्च फाउंडेशन की अब और लंका लगने वाली है. जी हां, केंद्र सरकार ने जाकिर नाइक की संस्था पर हथौड़ा चलाया है. केंद्र सरकार ने भगोड़े उपदेशक जाकिर नाइक के इस्लामिक रिसर्च फाउंडेशन (IRF) के खिलाफ राज्यों और केंद्र शासित प्रदेशों को सख्त यूएपीए यानी गैरकानूनी गतिविधियां (रोकथाम) अधिनियम (UAPA) के तहत फंड और परिसरों से जुड़ी शक्तियों का इस्तेमाल करने की अनुमति दे दी है. इस महीने की शुरुआत में जाकिर नाइक के इस संगठन को गैरकानूनी संगठन घोषित किया गया था.
दरअसल, इस बाबत केंद्र सरकार ने गुरुवार को एक अधिसूचना जारी की. इस गजट अधिसूचना में गृह मंत्रालय ने आतंकवाद-रोधी कानून की धारा 42 के तहत मिली शक्तियों का इस्तेमाल करते हुए राज्य सरकारों और केंद्र शासित प्रदेशों के प्रशासकों को यह निर्देश जारी किया है. मंत्रालय ने 13 नवंबर को जारी एक अधिसूचना के जरिए इस कानून की धारा 3(1) और 3(3) के तहत इस्लामिक रिसर्च फाउंडेशन पर लगे प्रतिबंध को आगे बढ़ा दिया था.
केंद्र सरकार ने क्या आदेश दिया
अधिसूचना में कहा गया है, ‘केंद्र सरकार ने भारत के राजपत्र में 13 नवंबर 2026 को प्रकाशित अधिसूचना संख्या S.O. 6182(E) के जरिए ‘इस्लामिक रिसर्च फाउंडेशन’ को एक ‘गैरकानूनी संगठन’ घोषित किया था. ‘गैरकानूनी गतिविधियां (रोकथाम) अधिनियम, 1967’ की धारा 42 के तहत मिली शक्तियों का इस्तेमाल करते हुए केंद्र सरकार अब यह निर्देश देती है कि इस कानून की धारा 7 और 8 के तहत केंद्र सरकार को जो भी शक्तियां प्राप्त हैं, उनका इस्तेमाल राज्य सरकारें और केंद्र शासित प्रदेशों के प्रशासन भी इस ‘गैरकानूनी संगठन’ के संबंध में कर सकते हैं.’

क्या है यूएपीए
दरअसल, यूएपीए यानी गैरकानूनी गतिविधियां (रोकथाम) अधिनियम (UAPA) की धारा 7 सरकार को यह अधिकार देती है कि वह ऐसे फंड, सिक्योरिटीज और अन्य वित्तीय संपत्तियों के इस्तेमाल या हस्तांतरण पर रोक लगा सके, जिनके बारे में यह संदेह हो कि उनका इस्तेमाल किसी ‘गैरकानूनी संगठन’ के उद्देश्यों के लिए किया जा रहा है या किया जाने वाला है.
यह धारा अधिकृत अधिकारियों को ऐसे वित्तीय लेन-देन की जांच करने की अनुमति भी देती है. वहीं, धारा 8 सरकार को यह अधिकार देती है कि वह उन परिसरों (जैसे घर या इमारतें) को अधिसूचित कर सके, जिनके बारे में यह संदेह हो कि उनका इस्तेमाल किसी ‘गैरकानूनी संगठन’ की गतिविधियों के लिए किया जा रहा है.
इस अधिसूचना के बाद अधिकारी किसी परिसर में प्रवेश को नियंत्रित कर सकते हैं और वहां मौजूद चल संपत्तियों के इस्तेमाल पर रोक लगा सकते हैं. गौरतलब है कि 13 नवंबर को 2026 केंद्र सरकार ने सख्त UAPA कानून के तहत भगोड़े उपदेशक जाकिर नाइक के संगठन IRF पर लगे प्रतिबंध को और पांच साल के लिए बढ़ा दिया था. यह प्रतिबंध 14 नवंबर को खत्म होने वाला था.
महाराष्ट्र का रहने वाला है जाकिर नाइक
जाकिर नाइक महाराष्ट्र का रहने वाला है. वह 2016 में विदेश यात्रा पर गया था. यह वही वक्त था, जब सरकार ने उसके संगठन पर प्रतिबंध लगा दिया था. तब से वह भागा हुआ है. जाकिर नाइक तब से मलेशिया में रह रहा है. 2017 में एनआईए यानी राष्ट्रीय जांच एजेंसी (NIA) के अनुरोध पर उसका पासपोर्ट भी रद्द कर दिया गया था. एनआईए ने उसके खिलाफ एक मामला भी दर्ज किया है.
कब से भारत ले रहा जाकिर नाइक पर एक्शन
भारत 17 नवंबर 2016 से जाकिर नाइक के खिलाफ कानूनी और राजनयिक कदम उठा रहा है. उस समय केंद्र सरकार ने धार्मिक समुदायों के बीच दुश्मनी और नफरत फैलाने के आरोपों का हवाला देते हुए उनके संगठन को ‘गैर-कानूनी संगठन’ घोषित कर दिया था. मई 2017 में भारत ने जाकिर नाइक के खिलाफ ‘रेड कॉर्नर नोटिस’ (RCN) जारी करने के लिए इंटरपोल (INTERPOL) से संपर्क किया और बाद में अगस्त और अक्टूबर में इस संबंध में और स्पष्टीकरण भी दिए.
- हालांकि, दिसंबर 2017 के आखिर में अपने 102वें सत्र के दौरान इंटरपोल आयोग ने इस अनुरोध को ‘समय से पहले’ का माना, क्योंकि शुरुआती आवेदन के समय तक कोई चार्जशीट दाखिल नहीं की गई थी.
- 24 नवंबर 2017 को जारी एक नए अदालती वारंट के आधार पर भारतीय एजेंसियों ने 3 जनवरी, 2018 को इंटरपोल को ‘रेड कॉर्नर नोटिस’ के लिए एक नया अनुरोध भेजा, जिस पर अभी भी जवाब का इंतजार है.
- इसके अलावा जब यह पुष्टि हो गई कि नाइक को ‘स्थायी निवास’ का दर्जा मिल गया है, तो भारत ने 19 जनवरी, 2018 को मलेशिया के विदेश मंत्रालय को औपचारिक रूप से ‘अस्थायी गिरफ्तारी’ और ‘प्रत्यर्पण’ का अनुरोध भेजा था.

title: Watch Video: AC ट्रेन के अंदर दीया जलाकर पूजा, फिर गूंजा शंख! वायरल वीडियो देख रेलवे भी अलर्ट
description: Watch Video: सोशल मीडिया पर एक वीडियो सामने आया है, जिसने लोगों का ध्यान अपनी ओर खींचा है. वीडियो में एक व्यक्ति ट्रेन के एसी कोच में बैठकर दिया जलाकर और शंख बजाकर पूजा कर रहा है. इसको लेकर लोग सवाल उठा रहे हैं.
author: Deepika Pandey
content:
Watch Video: ट्रेन में सफर के दौरान लोग अक्सर अपनी सुविधा के हिसाब से समय बिताते हैं लेकिन क्या चलती ट्रेन के AC कोच में दीया जलाकर पूजा करना सुरक्षित है? सोशल मीडिया पर वायरल हो रहे एक वीडियो ने इसी सवाल को लेकर नई बहस छेड़ दी है. वीडियो में एक यात्री ट्रेन के अंदर दीया जलाते, पूजा-पाठ करते और शंख बजाते हुए दिखाई दे रहा है. इस नजारे ने दूसरे यात्रियों की सुरक्षा को लेकर चिंता बढ़ा दी है.
AC कोच में दीया जलाकर की पूजा
वायरल वीडियो में एक यात्री AC ट्रेन कोच के भीतर पूजा करता नजर आ रहा है. इस दौरान दीया और अगरबत्ती जलाए जाने के साथ शंख बजाने की बात भी सामने आई है. वीडियो सामने आने के बाद सोशल मीडिया यूजर्स इस गतिविधि पर सवाल उठा रहे हैं. लोगों का कहना है कि ट्रेन जैसे सार्वजनिक और सीमित स्थान पर इस तरह खुली आग जलाना खतरनाक साबित हो सकता है.

दूसरे यात्री ने समझाया आग का खतरा
बताया जा रहा है कि कोच में मौजूद एक अन्य यात्री ने इस गतिविधि पर आपत्ति जताई और पूजा कर रहे व्यक्ति को सुरक्षा के खतरे के बारे में समझाया. यात्री ने चेतावनी दी कि अगरबत्ती के धुएं से फायर अलार्म सक्रिय हो सकता है. वहीं दीये की खुली लौ से आग लगने का जोखिम बना रहता है. चलती ट्रेन में ऐसी स्थिति पैदा होने पर कई यात्रियों की जान खतरे में पड़ सकती है.
रेलवे ने वीडियो पर लिया संज्ञान
मामला सोशल मीडिया पर चर्चा में आने के बाद भारतीय रेलवे ने भी प्रतिक्रिया दी है. रेलवे ने घटना की जांच करने के लिए वीडियो साझा करने वालों से यात्रा की तारीख, ट्रेन नंबर और PNR की जानकारी मांगी है. इन जानकारियों के आधार पर संबंधित ट्रेन और घटना का पता लगाने में मदद मिल सकती है.
शिकायत के लिए क्या हैं विकल्प?
रेलवे ने यात्रियों से अपील की है कि ट्रेन के अंदर सुरक्षा के लिए खतरा पैदा करने वाली किसी भी गतिविधि की सूचना तुरंत दें. इसके लिए रेल मदद (RailMadad) पोर्टल या ऐप का इस्तेमाल किया जा सकता है. यात्री हेल्पलाइन नंबर 139 पर कॉल करके भी शिकायत दर्ज करा सकते हैं.
