ನಾವು ಕೇವಲ ಮೌಖಿಕ ಭರವಸೆಗಳಿಗೆ ಹೋರಾಟವನ್ನು ಕೈಬಿಡುವುದಿಲ್ಲ. ನಾವು ಯಾರನ್ನೋ ಬೆದರಿಸಲು ಹೋರಾಟ ಮಾಡುತ್ತಿಲ್ಲ. ನಮ್ಮ ನ್ಯಾಯಯುತ ಬೇಡಿಕೆಗಳಿಗಾಗಿ ಶಾಂತಿಯುತವಾಗಿ ನಾವು ಪ್ರತಿಭಟನೆಯನ್ನು ನಡೆಸುತ್ತಿದ್ದೇವೆ. ಲಿಖಿತ ಭರವಸೆ ಸಿಗೋವರೆಗೂ ನಾವು ಪ್ರತಿಭಟನೆಯನ್ನು ಮುಂದುವರಿಸುತ್ತೇವೆ. . ಈಗ ನಮ್ಮ ಹಕ್ಕುಗಳಿಗಾಗಿ ಹೋರಾಡುತ್ತಿದ್ದರೆ ನಮ್ಮ ಮೇಲಿನ ವಿಶ್ವಾಸವನ್ನೇ ಪ್ರಶ್ನಿಸುತ್ತಿದ್ದೀರಿ. ನಮ್ಮ ಮೇಲೆ ವಿಶ್ವಾಸವಿಲ್ಲದಿದ್ದರೆ ಇಷ್ಟು ವರ್ಷ ನಮ್ಮಿಂದ ಸೇವೆ ಮಾಡಿಸಿಕೊಂಡಿದ್ದೇಕೆ? - ಡಿ.ನಾಗಲಕ್ಷ್ಮಿ, ಪ್ರಧಾನ ಕಾರ್ಯದರ್ಶಿ, ಆಶಾ ಕಾರ್ಯಕರ್ತೆಯರ ಸಂಘ
ಬೆಂಗಳೂರು: ಸರ್ಕಾರಕ್ಕೆ ಸಮಯಾವಕಾಶ ನೀಡದೆ ಪ್ರತಿಭಟನೆ ಮುಂದುವರಿಸುವುದು ಸರಿಯಲ್ಲ. ಆಶಾ ಕಾರ್ಯಕರ್ತೆಯರ ಸೇವೆ ಅವಶ್ಯಕತೆ ಇಲ್ಲ ಎಂದು ಹೇಳುತ್ತಿಲ್ಲ, ಆದರೆ ಒಬ್ಬರಿಲ್ಲದಿದ್ದರೆ ಇನ್ನೊಬ್ಬರು ಸಿಗುತ್ತಾರೆ ಎನ್ನುವುದನ್ನು ಅರ್ಥ ಮಾಡಿಕೊಳ್ಳಬೇಕು ಎಂದು ವೇತನ ಹೆಚ್ಚಳಕ್ಕೆ ಆಗ್ರಹಿಸಿ ಪ್ರತಿಭಟನೆ ನಡೆಸುತ್ತಿರುವ ಆಶಾ ಕಾರ್ಯಕರ್ತೆಯರ ಕುರಿತು ಆರೋಗ್ಯ ಸಚಿವ ಯು.ಟಿ. ಖಾದರ್‌ ಅಸಮಾಧಾನ ವ್ಯಕ್ತಪಡಿಸಿದ್ದಾರೆ.
ಆಹಾರ ನಿಯಂತ್ರಣ ಮತ್ತು ಔಷಧ ಆಡಳಿತ ಕುರಿತ ರಾಷ್ಟ್ರೀಯ ಸಮ್ಮೇಳನ ಉದ್ಘಾಟಿಸಿದ ನಂತರ ಮಾಧ್ಯಮಗಳೊಂದಿಗೆ ಮಾತನಾಡಿ, ಆಶಾ ಕಾರ್ಯಕರ್ತೆಯರು ಮಾಸಿಕ 15 ಸಾವಿರ ರೂ. ಗೌರವಧನ ಕೇಳುವುದು ತಪ್ಪಲ್ಲ. ಆದರೆ ಈ ವಿಚಾರದಲ್ಲಿ ಸರ್ಕಾರ ನಿರ್ಧಾರ ಮಾಡುತ್ತದೆ. ಸರ್ಕಾರ 15 ದಿನಗಳ ಸಮಯ ಕೇಳಿದ್ದೇ ಅಪರಾಧವೇ? ಅಧಿವೇಶನದಲ್ಲಿ ಸಿಹಿ ಸುದ್ದಿ ಕೊಡುತ್ತೇವೆ ಎಂದು ಸ್ವತಃ ಸಿಎಂ ಹೇಳಿದಾಗ ಅದಕ್ಕೆ ಗೌರವ ಕೊಡಬೇಕಿತ್ತು. ಒಂದು ವೇಳೆ ಅಧಿವೇಶನದಲ್ಲಿ ಏನೂ ಮಾಡದಿದ್ದರೆ ಮತ್ತೆ ಪ್ರತಿಭಟನೆ ಮಾಡಬಹುದಿತ್ತು. ಸುಮ್ಮನೆ ಪ್ರತಿಭಟಿಸುತ್ತಾ ನಾವೇ ಏನೋ ಸಾಧನೆ ಮಾಡಿದೆವು ಎನ್ನುವುದು ಸರಿಯೇ? ಎಂದರು.
ಆರೋಗ್ಯ ಸಚಿವರು ಸಹನೆ ಕಳೆದುಕೊಂಡಿದ್ದಾರೆಯೇ ಎಂಬ ಪ್ರಶ್ನೆಗೆ ಉತ್ತರಿಸಿ, ನಾನು ಸಹನೆ ಕಳೆದುಕೊಂಡಿಲ್ಲ, ಆದರೆ ಈ ಬೆಳವಣಿಗೆಯಿಂದ ಬೇಸರವಿದೆ. ರಾಜ್ಯದಲ್ಲಿ ಕೇವಲ 4 ಸಾವಿರ ರೂ. ಪಡೆಯುತ್ತಿರುವ ಅಕ್ಷರ ದಾಸೋಹ ತಾಯಂದಿರು ಹಾಗೂ 10 ಸಾವಿರ ರೂ. ಪಡೆಯುತ್ತಿರುವ ಉಪನ್ಯಾಸಕರು ಇದ್ದಾರೆ. ಹೀಗೆ ಎಲ್ಲರೂ ಪಟ್ಟು ಹಿಡಿದರೆ ಸರ್ಕಾರ ಏನು ಮಾಡಬೇಕು? ಯಾವುದೇ ವ್ಯವಸ್ಥೆ ವಿಶ್ವಾಸದ ಮೇಲೆ ನಡೆಯುತ್ತದೆ. ನಾವೂ ಅವರ ಮೇಲೆ ವಿಶ್ವಾಸ ಇಡದೆ, ಅವರ ಕೆಲಸ ಸರಿಯಿಲ್ಲ, ಬಾಣಂತಿ ಮರಣ ಕಡಿಮೆಯಾಗಿಲ್ಲ, ಸೇವೆ ಸರಿಯಾಗಿ ಸಿಗುತ್ತಿಲ್ಲ ಎಂದು ನಾವೂ ಹೇಳಿಕೊಂಡು ಹೋದರೆ ಹೇಗಿರುತ್ತದೆ? ಪರಸ್ಪರ ವಿಶ್ವಾಸ ಬೇಕಲ್ಲವೇ? ಸರ್ಕಾರ ಹೇಳಿದಾಗ ಸ್ವಲ್ಪ ಸಮಯ ಕೊಟ್ಟರೆ ಏನಾಗುತ್ತಿತ್ತು? ಎಂದರು.
ಆಶಾ ಕಾರ್ಯಕರ್ತೆಯರು ಕೆಲಸ ಚೆನ್ನಾಗಿ ಮಾಡುತ್ತಿಲ್ಲ ಎಂದು ನಾನು ಹೇಳುವುದಿಲ್ಲ, ಅವರು ಚೆನ್ನಾಗಿಯೇ ಕೆಲಸ ಮಾಡುತ್ತಿದ್ದಾರೆ, ಅವರ ಬಗ್ಗೆ ಗೌರವವಿದೆ. ಅವರ ಸೇವೆ ಅವಶ್ಯಕತೆ ಇಲ್ಲ ಎಂದೂ ನಾನು ಹೇಳುತ್ತಿಲ್ಲ. ಆದರೆ ಒಬ್ಬರಿಲ್ಲದಿದ್ದರೆ ಇನ್ನೊಬ್ಬರು ಇರುತ್ತಾರೆ. ಎಎನ್‌ಎಂ, ಸಿಎಚ್‌ಒ, ಡಾಕ್ಟರ್‌ಗಳೆಲ್ಲ ಇದ್ದಾರೆ. ತಮಿಳುನಾಡಿನಲ್ಲಿ ಆಶಾ ಕಾರ್ಯಕರ್ತೆಯರೇ ಇಲ್ಲದಿದ್ದರೂ ಅಲ್ಲಿ ನವಜಾತ ಶಿಶು ಮರಣ (ಐಎಂಆರ್‌), ಬಾಣಂತಿ ಮರಣ ಪ್ರಮಾಣ (ಎಂಎಂಆರ್‌), ಆರೋಗ್ಯ ಸೂಚ್ಯಂಕಗಳು ಉತ್ತಮವಾಗಿವೆಯಲ್ಲ? 10 ದಿನಗಳಿಂದ ಕೆಲಸ ಬಿಟ್ಟು ಕುಳಿತಿದ್ದರೂ ಜನರು ಆರೋಗ್ಯವಾಗಿದ್ದಾರೆ, ಹೆರಿಗೆಗಳೂ ಸುಗಮವಾಗಿ ಆಗುತ್ತಿವೆಯಲ್ಲವೇ? ತಾವು ಇಲ್ಲದಿದ್ದರೂ ಕೆಲಸ ನಡೆಯುತ್ತದೆ ಎಂದು ಇವರೇ ತೋರಿಸಿಕೊಡುತ್ತಿದ್ದಾರೆ ಎಂದು ಹೇಳಿದರು.
ದಾವಣಗೆರೆ: ಕಣ್ಮರೆಯಾಗಿರುವ ದಾಸಶ್ರೇಷ್ಠ ಕನಕದಾಸರ ‘ನೃಸಿಂಹಸ್ತವ’ ಕೃತಿಯ ಹುಡುಕಾಟಕ್ಕೇ ಈಗ ನೂರು ವರ್ಷಗಳಾಗಿದ್ದು ಐತಿಹಾಸಿಕ ಮಹತ್ವದ ಕನಕರ ಕೃತಿಗಾಗಿ ವಿದ್ವಾಂಸರು, ಸಂಶೋಧಕರು ಇನ್ನೂ ಶೋಧ ಮುಂದುವರಿಸಿದ್ದಾರೆ.
ದಾಸ ಸಾಹಿತ್ಯದ ಮೇರು ಪರ್ವತ ಎನಿಸಿದ ಕನಕದಾಸರು ‘ಮೋಹನ ತರಂಗಿಣಿ’, ‘ರಾಮಧಾನ್ಯ ಚರಿತೆ’, ‘ಹರಿಭಕ್ತಸಾರ’ ಮತ್ತು ‘ನಳಚರಿತ್ರೆ’ ಎಂಬ 4 ಪ್ರಮುಖ ಕಾವ್ಯ ಹಾಗೂ ಕೀರ್ತನೆಗಳ ಮೂಲಕ ಕನ್ನಡ ಸಾಹಿತ್ಯ ಲೋಕವನ್ನು ಶ್ರೀಮಂತಗೊಳಿಸಿದ್ದಾರೆ. ಕನಕದಾಸರ ಪ್ರಮುಖ ಕಾವ್ಯಗಳ ಸಾಲಿಗೆ ಸೇರಬೇಕಿದ್ದ ‘ನೃಸಿಂಹಸ್ತವ’ ಕೃತಿ ಇಂದಿಗೂ ನಿಗೂಢವಾಗಿಯೇ ಉಳಿದಿದ್ದು ಈ ಅಮೂಲ್ಯ ಸಾಹಿತ್ಯಿಕ ನಿಧಿಯನ್ನು ಶತಮಾನದಿಂದ ಹುಡುಕುತ್ತಿದ್ದರೂ ಇನ್ನೂ ಪತ್ತೆಯಾಗಿಲ್ಲ.
ಕನಕಮಹಿಮಾದರ್ಶದಲ್ಲಿ ಉಲ್ಲೇಖ:
ಕನಕದಾಸರ ‘ನೃಸಿಂಹಸ್ತವ’ ಕೃತಿಯ ಈ ರೋಚಕ ಹುಡುಕಾಟಕ್ಕೆ ನಾಂದಿ ಹಾಡಿದ್ದು 1926 ರಲ್ಲಿ ಪ್ರಕಟವಾದ ಹಿರಿಯ ವಿದ್ವಾಂಸ ಭೀಮಾಚಾರ್ಯ ವಡವಿ ಅವರ ‘ಕನಕಮಹಿಮಾದರ್ಶ’ ಎಂಬ ಕೃತಿ. ಇದರಲ್ಲಿ ಕನಕದಾಸರು ‘ನೃಸಿಂಹಸ್ತವ’ ಎಂಬ ಕೃತಿಯನ್ನು ರಚಿಸಿದ್ದಾರೆ ಮತ್ತು ಅದು ಬರೋಬ್ಬರಿ 97 ಪದ್ಯಗಳನ್ನು ಒಳಗೊಂಡಿದೆ ಎಂಬ ನಿಖರ ಮಾಹಿತಿಯನ್ನು ದಾಖಲಿಸಿದ್ದರು. ವಡವಿಯವರು ಪದ್ಯಗಳ ಸಂಖ್ಯೆಯನ್ನೂ ಸ್ಪಷ್ಟವಾಗಿ ಬರೆದಿದ್ದಾರೆ ಎಂದರೆ, 20ನೇ ಶತಮಾನದ ಆರಂಭದವರೆಗೂ ಈ ಕೃತಿಯ ಪ್ರತಿ ಎಲ್ಲಿಯೋ ಅಸ್ತಿತ್ವದಲ್ಲಿತ್ತು ಎಂಬುದು ಖಚಿತವಾಗಿದೆ. ಅಂದಿನಿಂದ ಇಂದಿನವರೆಗೂ ಕೃತಿ ಪತ್ತೆಗಾಗಿ ಹುಡುಕಾಟ ನಡೆಯುತ್ತಲೇ ಇದೆ.
ವಿದ್ವಾಂಸ ಭೀಮಾಚಾರ್ಯ ವಡವಿ ಮಾತ್ರವಲ್ಲ ಇನ್ನೋರ್ವ ವಿದ್ವಾಂಸ ಆರ್‌. ನರಸಿಂಹಾಚಾರ್ಯ ಅವರ ‘ಕರ್ಣಾಟಕ ಕವಿಚರಿತೆ’ (ಸಂಪುಟ-2) ಗ್ರಂಥದಲ್ಲಿಯೂ ನರಸಿಂಹಸ್ತವ ಕೃತಿಯ ಉಲ್ಲೇಖವಿದೆ. ಕಾಗಿನೆಲೆಯಾದಿಕೇಶವನ ಪರಮಭಕ್ತರಾಗಿದ್ದ ಕನಕದಾಸರು, ನರಸಿಂಹ ಸ್ವಾಮಿಯ ಸ್ತುತಿಗಾಗಿ ಇಂತಹದ್ದೊಂದು ಬೃಹತ್‌ ಕಿರುಕಾವ್ಯ ರಚಿಸಿರುವ ಸಾಧ್ಯತೆ ದಟ್ಟವಾಗಿದೆ. ಆದರೆ, 1926ರಿಂದ 2026 ರವರೆಗೆ ಒಂದು ಶತಮಾನ ಉರುಳಿದರೂ, ಆ 97 ಪದ್ಯಗಳು ಇನ್ನೂ ಕಣ್ಣಿಗೆ ಬಿದ್ದಿಲ್ಲ.
ಕೃತಿ ಕಣ್ಮರೆಗೆ ನಾನಾ ಕಾರಣ:
ಒಂದು ಇಡೀ ಕಾವ್ಯ ಹೀಗೆ ಕಣ್ಮರೆಯಾಗಲು ಹಲವು ಐತಿಹಾಸಿಕ ಕಾರಣಗಳಿವೆ. 16ನೇ ಶತಮಾನದಲ್ಲಿ ಸಾಹಿತ್ಯವನ್ನು ತಾಳೆಗರಿಗಳಲ್ಲಿ ಬರೆಯಲಾಗುತ್ತಿದ್ದುದರಿಂದ, ಕಾಲಕ್ರಮೇಣ ತೇವಾಂಶ, ಗೆದ್ದಲು ಅಥವಾ ಅಗ್ನಿ ಅನಾಹುತಗಳಿಗೆ ಸಿಲುಕಿ ಮೂಲ ಹಸ್ತಪ್ರತಿಗಳು ನಾಶವಾಗಿರುವ ಸಾಧ್ಯತೆಯಿದೆ. ಜತೆಗೆ ಕನಕದಾಸರ ಕೀರ್ತನೆಗಳು ಹಾಡುಗಾರರ ಮೌಖಿಕ ಪರಂಪರೆಯಲ್ಲಿ ಜನಮಾನಸಕ್ಕೆ ತಲುಪಿದಷ್ಟು ವೇಗವಾಗಿ, ಛಂದೋಬದ್ಧ ಕಾವ್ಯವಾದ ‘ನೃಸಿಂಹಸ್ತವ’ ಜನಸಾಮಾನ್ಯರಲ್ಲಿ ಪ್ರಸಾರವಾಗದೆ ಸೀಮಿತ ವಲಯದಲ್ಲೇ ಉಳಿದು ಮರೆಯಾಗಿರಬಹುದು.
ಇನ್ನೊಂದೆಡೆ, ರಾಜ್ಯದ ವಿಶ್ವವಿದ್ಯಾಲಯಗಳಲ್ಲಿರುವ ಹಸ್ತಪ್ರತಿಗಳ ಅಧ್ಯಯನವಾದಷ್ಟು ವಿವಿಧ ಮಠ-ಮಾನ್ಯಗಳು, ಹಳೆಯ ದೇವಾಲಯಗಳ ಭಂಡಾರಗಳು ಹಾಗೂ ಸಂಪ್ರದಾಯಸ್ಥ ಕುಟುಂಬಗಳ ಖಾಸಗಿ ಸಂಗ್ರಹಗಳಲ್ಲಿರುವ ಲಕ್ಷಾಂತರ ತಾಳೆಗರಿ ಕಟ್ಟುಗಳ ಪರಿಶೀಲನೆ ಇನ್ನೂ ಪೂರ್ಣವಾಗಿ ಆಗಿಲ್ಲ. ನಕಲು ಮಾಡುವಾಗ ಶೀರ್ಷಿಕೆ ಬದಲಾಗಿ ‘ನರಸಿಂಹ ಸ್ತೋತ್ರ’ ದಂತಹ ಬೇರೆ ಹೆಸರಿನಲ್ಲಿಯೋ ಅಥವಾ ಆರಂಭ-ಅಂತ್ಯದ ಗರಿಗಳು ಹರಿದುಹೋದ ‘ಅಪೂರ್ಣ ಹಸ್ತಪ್ರತಿ’ ಯಾಗಿಯೋ ಅದು ಎಲ್ಲಿಯೋ ಅಡಗಿರುವ ಸಾಧ್ಯತೆಯನ್ನು ತಳ್ಳಿಹಾಕುವಂತಿಲ್ಲ ಎನ್ನುತ್ತಾರೆ ಸಂಶೋಧಕರು.
ಯಾರಿವರು ವಿದ್ವಾಂಸ ವಡವಿ?
ಭೀಮಾಚಾರ್ಯ ವಡವಿಯವರು 20ನೇ ಶತಮಾನದ ಆರಂಭದಲ್ಲಿ ಹರಿದಾಸ ಸಾಹಿತ್ಯ ಮತ್ತು ಹಳೆಯ ಕನ್ನಡ ಹಸ್ತಪ್ರತಿಗಳ ಸಂಗ್ರಹ ಹಾಗೂ ಪ್ರಕಟಣೆಯಲ್ಲಿ ಮಹತ್ವದ ಪಾತ್ರ ವಹಿಸಿದ ಹಿರಿಯ ವಿದ್ವಾಂಸರು. ಆಧುನಿಕ ಮುದ್ರಣ ತಂತ್ರಜ್ಞಾನ ಇನ್ನೂ ಅಂಬೆಗಾಲಿಡುತ್ತಿದ್ದ ಕಾಲಘಟ್ಟದಲ್ಲಿ, ತಾಳೆಗರಿ ಮತ್ತು ಕಡತಗಳಲ್ಲಿ ಅಡಗಿದ್ದ ದಾಸರ ಅಪರೂಪದ ಕೃತಿಗಳನ್ನು ಹುಡುಕಿ, ಸಂಪಾದಿಸಿ ಪುಸ್ತಕ ರೂಪದಲ್ಲಿ ಹೊರತರುವ ಸಾಹಸ ಮಾಡಿದವರಲ್ಲಿ ಇವರು ಪ್ರಮುಖರಾಗಿದ್ದಾರೆ.
ವಿದ್ವಾಂಸರಾದ ವಡವಿ, ಆರ್‌. ನರಸಿಂಹಾಚಾರ್ಯ, ನರಸಿಂಹ ಪ್ರಗಾತ ಅವರ ಕೃತಿಗಳಲ್ಲಿ ಕನಕದಾಸ ರಚಿತ ‘ನೃಸಿಂಹಸ್ತವ’ ಕೃತಿ ಬಗ್ಗೆ ಉಲ್ಲೇಖವಿದ್ದು ಈ ಕೃತಿಗಾಗಿ ಇಂದಿಗೂ ಹುಡುಕಾಟ ನಡೆದಿದೆ. ನಾನು ಕೃತಿ ಹುಡುಕಾಟ ನಡೆಸಿದಾಗಲೇ 200ಕ್ಕೂ ಅಧಿಕ ಕನಕದಾಸರ ಅಪ್ರಕಟಿತ ಕೀರ್ತನೆಗಳು ಲಭ್ಯವಾಗಿವೆ. ಈ ದಿಸೆಯಲ್ಲಿ ಸರ್ಕಾರ ಸಂಶೋಧಕರಿಗೆ ವಿಶೇಷ ಪ್ರೋತ್ಸಾಹ ನೀಡಬೇಕಿದೆ.- ಡಾ।ಜಗನ್ನಾಥ ಗೇನಣ್ಣನವರ್‌, ಸಂಶೋಧಕರು, ಕಾಗಿನೆಲೆ ಅಭಿವೃದ್ಧಿ ಪ್ರಾಧಿಕಾರ
‘ನೃಸಿಂಹಸ್ತವ’ ಕೃತಿ ಹುಡುಕಲು ಸರ್ಕಾರದಿಂದ ವಿಶೇಷ ಪ್ರಯತ್ನ ನಡೆಯಬೇಕು. ಕೃತಿ ಸಿಕ್ಕಿದರೆ ಅದು ಕನ್ನಡ ಸಾಹಿತ್ಯ ಚರಿತ್ರೆಯಲ್ಲೇ ಒಂದು ಐತಿಹಾಸಿಕ ಮೈಲಿಗಲ್ಲಾಗುವುದರಲ್ಲಿ ಸಂಶಯವಿಲ್ಲ. - ಪ್ರಮೋದ್‌ ನಲವಾಗಲ, ಇತಿಹಾಸ ಸಂಶೋಧಕರು
-ಎಚ್‌.ಕೆ. ನಟರಾಜ

title: ಕನಕದಾಸರು ರಚಿಸಿದ ‘ನೃಸಿಂಹಸ್ತವ’ ಕೃತಿ ಹುಡುಕಾಟಕ್ಕೆ 100 ವರ್ಷ!

ದಾಸ ಸಾಹಿತ್ಯದ ಮೇರು ಪರ್ವತ ಎನಿಸಿದ ಕನಕದಾಸರು ‘ಮೋಹನ ತರಂಗಿಣಿ’, ‘ರಾಮಧಾನ್ಯ ಚರಿತೆ’, ‘ಹರಿಭಕ್ತಸಾರ’ ಮತ್ತು ‘ನಳಚರಿತ್ರೆ’ ಎಂಬ 4 ಪ್ರಮುಖ ಕಾವ್ಯ ಹಾಗೂ ಕೀರ್ತನೆಗಳ ಮೂಲಕ ಕನ್ನಡ ಸಾಹಿತ್ಯ ಲೋಕವನ್ನು ಶ್ರೀಮಂತಗೊಳಿಸಿದ್ದಾರೆ. ಕನಕದಾಸರ ಪ್ರಮುಖ ಕಾವ್ಯಗಳ ಸಾಲಿಗೆ ಸೇರಬೇಕಿದ್ದ ‘ನೃಸಿಂಹಸ್ತವ’ ಕೃತಿ ಇಂದಿಗೂ ನಿಗೂಢವಾಗಿಯೇ ಉಳಿದಿದ್ದು ಈ ಅಮೂಲ್ಯ ಸಾಹಿತ್ಯಿಕ ನಿಧಿಯನ್ನು ಶತಮಾನದಿಂದ ಹುಡುಕುತ್ತಿದ್ದರೂ ಇನ್ನೂ ಪತ್ತೆಯಾಗಿಲ್ಲ.
ಕನಕಮಹಿಮಾದರ್ಶದಲ್ಲಿ ಉಲ್ಲೇಖ:
ಕನಕದಾಸರ ‘ನೃಸಿಂಹಸ್ತವ’ ಕೃತಿಯ ಈ ರೋಚಕ ಹುಡುಕಾಟಕ್ಕೆ ನಾಂದಿ ಹಾಡಿದ್ದು 1926 ರಲ್ಲಿ ಪ್ರಕಟವಾದ ಹಿರಿಯ ವಿದ್ವಾಂಸ ಭೀಮಾಚಾರ್ಯ ವಡವಿ ಅವರ ‘ಕನಕಮಹಿಮಾದರ್ಶ’ ಎಂಬ ಕೃತಿ. ಇದರಲ್ಲಿ ಕನಕದಾಸರು ‘ನೃಸಿಂಹಸ್ತವ’ ಎಂಬ ಕೃತಿಯನ್ನು ರಚಿಸಿದ್ದಾರೆ ಮತ್ತು ಅದು ಬರೋಬ್ಬರಿ 97 ಪದ್ಯಗಳನ್ನು ಒಳಗೊಂಡಿದೆ ಎಂಬ ನಿಖರ ಮಾಹಿತಿಯನ್ನು ದಾಖಲಿಸಿದ್ದರು. ವಡವಿಯವರು ಪದ್ಯಗಳ ಸಂಖ್ಯೆಯನ್ನೂ ಸ್ಪಷ್ಟವಾಗಿ ಬರೆದಿದ್ದಾರೆ ಎಂದರೆ, 20ನೇ ಶತಮಾನದ ಆರಂಭದವರೆಗೂ ಈ ಕೃತಿಯ ಪ್ರತಿ ಎಲ್ಲಿಯೋ ಅಸ್ತಿತ್ವದಲ್ಲಿತ್ತು ಎಂಬುದು ಖಚಿತವಾಗಿದೆ. ಅಂದಿನಿಂದ ಇಂದಿನವರೆಗೂ ಕೃತಿ ಪತ್ತೆಗಾಗಿ ಹುಡುಕಾಟ ನಡೆಯುತ್ತಲೇ ಇದೆ.
ವಿದ್ವಾಂಸ ಭೀಮಾಚಾರ್ಯ ವಡವಿ ಮಾತ್ರವಲ್ಲ ಇನ್ನೋರ್ವ ವಿದ್ವಾಂಸ ಆರ್‌. ನರಸಿಂಹಾಚಾರ್ಯ ಅವರ ‘ಕರ್ಣಾಟಕ ಕವಿಚರಿತೆ’ (ಸಂಪುಟ-2) ಗ್ರಂಥದಲ್ಲಿಯೂ ನರಸಿಂಹಸ್ತವ ಕೃತಿಯ ಉಲ್ಲೇಖವಿದೆ. ಕಾಗಿನೆಲೆಯಾದಿಕೇಶವನ ಪರಮಭಕ್ತರಾಗಿದ್ದ ಕನಕದಾಸರು, ನರಸಿಂಹ ಸ್ವಾಮಿಯ ಸ್ತುತಿಗಾಗಿ ಇಂತಹದ್ದೊಂದು ಬೃಹತ್‌ ಕಿರುಕಾವ್ಯ ರಚಿಸಿರುವ ಸಾಧ್ಯತೆ ದಟ್ಟವಾಗಿದೆ. ಆದರೆ, 1926ರಿಂದ 2026 ರವರೆಗೆ ಒಂದು ಶತಮಾನ ಉರುಳಿದರೂ, ಆ 97 ಪದ್ಯಗಳು ಇನ್ನೂ ಕಣ್ಣಿಗೆ ಬಿದ್ದಿಲ್ಲ.
ಕೃತಿ ಕಣ್ಮರೆಗೆ ನಾನಾ ಕಾರಣ:
ಒಂದು ಇಡೀ ಕಾವ್ಯ ಹೀಗೆ ಕಣ್ಮರೆಯಾಗಲು ಹಲವು ಐತಿಹಾಸಿಕ ಕಾರಣಗಳಿವೆ. 16ನೇ ಶತಮಾನದಲ್ಲಿ ಸಾಹಿತ್ಯವನ್ನು ತಾಳೆಗರಿಗಳಲ್ಲಿ ಬರೆಯಲಾಗುತ್ತಿದ್ದುದರಿಂದ, ಕಾಲಕ್ರಮೇಣ ತೇವಾಂಶ, ಗೆದ್ದಲು ಅಥವಾ ಅಗ್ನಿ ಅನಾಹುತಗಳಿಗೆ ಸಿಲುಕಿ ಮೂಲ ಹಸ್ತಪ್ರತಿಗಳು ನಾಶವಾಗಿರುವ ಸಾಧ್ಯತೆಯಿದೆ. ಜತೆಗೆ ಕನಕದಾಸರ ಕೀರ್ತನೆಗಳು ಹಾಡುಗಾರರ ಮೌಖಿಕ ಪರಂಪರೆಯಲ್ಲಿ ಜನಮಾನಸಕ್ಕೆ ತಲುಪಿದಷ್ಟು ವೇಗವಾಗಿ, ಛಂದೋಬದ್ಧ ಕಾವ್ಯವಾದ ‘ನೃಸಿಂಹಸ್ತವ’ ಜನಸಾಮಾನ್ಯರಲ್ಲಿ ಪ್ರಸಾರವಾಗದೆ ಸೀಮಿತ ವಲಯದಲ್ಲೇ ಉಳಿದು ಮರೆಯಾಗಿರಬಹುದು.

ಬೆಂಗಳೂರು: ಸರ್ಕಾರಕ್ಕೆ ಸಮಯಾವಕಾಶ ನೀಡದೆ ಪ್ರತಿಭಟನೆ ಮುಂದುವರಿಸುವುದು ಸರಿಯಲ್ಲ. ಆಶಾ ಕಾರ್ಯಕರ್ತೆಯರ ಸೇವೆ ಅವಶ್ಯಕತೆ ಇಲ್ಲ ಎಂದು ಹೇಳುತ್ತಿಲ್ಲ, ಆದರೆ ಒಬ್ಬರಿಲ್ಲದಿದ್ದರೆ ಇನ್ನೊಬ್ಬರು ಸಿಗುತ್ತಾರೆ ಎನ್ನುವುದನ್ನು ಅರ್ಥ ಮಾಡಿಕೊಳ್ಳಬೇಕು ಎಂದು ವೇತನ ಹೆಚ್ಚಳಕ್ಕೆ ಆಗ್ರಹಿಸಿ ಪ್ರತಿಭಟನೆ ನಡೆಸುತ್ತಿರುವ ಆಶಾ ಕಾರ್ಯಕರ್ತೆಯರ ಕುರಿತು ಆರೋಗ್ಯ ಸಚಿವ ಯು.ಟಿ. ಖಾದರ್‌ ಅಸಮಾಧಾನ ವ್ಯಕ್ತಪಡಿಸಿದ್ದಾರೆ.
ಆಹಾರ ನಿಯಂತ್ರಣ ಮತ್ತು ಔಷಧ ಆಡಳಿತ ಕುರಿತ ರಾಷ್ಟ್ರೀಯ ಸಮ್ಮೇಳನ ಉದ್ಘಾಟಿಸಿದ ನಂತರ ಮಾಧ್ಯಮಗಳೊಂದಿಗೆ ಮಾತನಾಡಿ, ಆಶಾ ಕಾರ್ಯಕರ್ತೆಯರು ಮಾಸಿಕ 15 ಸಾವಿರ ರೂ. ಗೌರವಧನ ಕೇಳುವುದು ತಪ್ಪಲ್ಲ. ಆದರೆ ಈ ವಿಚಾರದಲ್ಲಿ ಸರ್ಕಾರ ನಿರ್ಧಾರ ಮಾಡುತ್ತದೆ. ಸರ್ಕಾರ 15 ದಿನಗಳ ಸಮಯ ಕೇಳಿದ್ದೇ ಅಪರಾಧವೇ? ಅಧಿವೇಶನದಲ್ಲಿ ಸಿಹಿ ಸುದ್ದಿ ಕೊಡುತ್ತೇವೆ ಎಂದು ಸ್ವತಃ ಸಿಎಂ ಹೇಳಿದಾಗ ಅದಕ್ಕೆ ಗೌರವ ಕೊಡಬೇಕಿತ್ತು. ಒಂದು ವೇಳೆ ಅಧಿವೇಶನದಲ್ಲಿ ಏನೂ ಮಾಡದಿದ್ದರೆ ಮತ್ತೆ ಪ್ರತಿಭಟನೆ ಮಾಡಬಹುದಿತ್ತು. ಸುಮ್ಮನೆ ಪ್ರತಿಭಟಿಸುತ್ತಾ ನಾವೇ ಏನೋ ಸಾಧನೆ ಮಾಡಿದೆವು ಎನ್ನುವುದು ಸರಿಯೇ? ಎಂದರು.
ಆರೋಗ್ಯ ಸಚಿವರು ಸಹನೆ ಕಳೆದುಕೊಂಡಿದ್ದಾರೆಯೇ ಎಂಬ ಪ್ರಶ್ನೆಗೆ ಉತ್ತರಿಸಿ, ನಾನು ಸಹನೆ ಕಳೆದುಕೊಂಡಿಲ್ಲ, ಆದರೆ ಈ ಬೆಳವಣಿಗೆಯಿಂದ ಬೇಸರವಿದೆ. ರಾಜ್ಯದಲ್ಲಿ ಕೇವಲ 4 ಸಾವಿರ ರೂ. ಪಡೆಯುತ್ತಿರುವ ಅಕ್ಷರ ದಾಸೋಹ ತಾಯಂದಿರು ಹಾಗೂ 10 ಸಾವಿರ ರೂ. ಪಡೆಯುತ್ತಿರುವ ಉಪನ್ಯಾಸಕರು ಇದ್ದಾರೆ. ಹೀಗೆ ಎಲ್ಲರೂ ಪಟ್ಟು ಹಿಡಿದರೆ ಸರ್ಕಾರ ಏನು ಮಾಡಬೇಕು? ಯಾವುದೇ ವ್ಯವಸ್ಥೆ ವಿಶ್ವಾಸದ ಮೇಲೆ ನಡೆಯುತ್ತದೆ. ನಾವೂ ಅವರ ಮೇಲೆ ವಿಶ್ವಾಸ ಇಡದೆ, ಅವರ ಕೆಲಸ ಸರಿಯಿಲ್ಲ, ಬಾಣಂತಿ ಮರಣ ಕಡಿಮೆಯಾಗಿಲ್ಲ, ಸೇವೆ ಸರಿಯಾಗಿ ಸಿಗುತ್ತಿಲ್ಲ ಎಂದು ನಾವೂ ಹೇಳಿಕೊಂಡು ಹೋದರೆ ಹೇಗಿರುತ್ತದೆ? ಪರಸ್ಪರ ವಿಶ್ವಾಸ ಬೇಕಲ್ಲವೇ? ಸರ್ಕಾರ ಹೇಳಿದಾಗ ಸ್ವಲ್ಪ ಸಮಯ ಕೊಟ್ಟರೆ ಏನಾಗುತ್ತಿತ್ತು? ಎಂದರು.
ಆಶಾ ಕಾರ್ಯಕರ್ತೆಯರು ಕೆಲಸ ಚೆನ್ನಾಗಿ ಮಾಡುತ್ತಿಲ್ಲ ಎಂದು ನಾನು ಹೇಳುವುದಿಲ್ಲ, ಅವರು ಚೆನ್ನಾಗಿಯೇ ಕೆಲಸ ಮಾಡುತ್ತಿದ್ದಾರೆ, ಅವರ ಬಗ್ಗೆ ಗೌರವವಿದೆ. ಅವರ ಸೇವೆ ಅವಶ್ಯಕತೆ ಇಲ್ಲ ಎಂದೂ ನಾನು ಹೇಳುತ್ತಿಲ್ಲ. ಆದರೆ ಒಬ್ಬರಿಲ್ಲದಿದ್ದರೆ ಇನ್ನೊಬ್ಬರು ಇರುತ್ತಾರೆ. ಎಎನ್‌ಎಂ, ಸಿಎಚ್‌ಒ, ಡಾಕ್ಟರ್‌ಗಳೆಲ್ಲ ಇದ್ದಾರೆ. ತಮಿಳುನಾಡಿನಲ್ಲಿ ಆಶಾ ಕಾರ್ಯಕರ್ತೆಯರೇ ಇಲ್ಲದಿದ್ದರೂ ಅಲ್ಲಿ ನವಜಾತ ಶಿಶು ಮರಣ (ಐಎಂಆರ್‌), ಬಾಣಂತಿ ಮರಣ ಪ್ರಮಾಣ (ಎಂಎಂಆರ್‌), ಆರೋಗ್ಯ ಸೂಚ್ಯಂಕಗಳು ಉತ್ತಮವಾಗಿವೆಯಲ್ಲ? 10 ದಿನಗಳಿಂದ ಕೆಲಸ ಬಿಟ್ಟು ಕುಳಿತಿದ್ದರೂ ಜನರು ಆರೋಗ್ಯವಾಗಿದ್ದಾರೆ, ಹೆರಿಗೆಗಳೂ ಸುಗಮವಾಗಿ ಆಗುತ್ತಿವೆಯಲ್ಲವೇ? ತಾವು ಇಲ್ಲದಿದ್ದರೂ ಕೆಲಸ ನಡೆಯುತ್ತದೆ ಎಂದು ಇವರೇ ತೋರಿಸಿಕೊಡುತ್ತಿದ್ದಾರೆ ಎಂದು ಹೇಳಿದರು.
ಬೆಂಗಳೂರು: ಆಶಾ ಕಾರ್ಯಕರ್ತೆಯರ ಹೋರಾಟಕ್ಕೆ ತೆರೆ ಎಳೆಯುವ ನಿರೀಕ್ಷೆಯಲ್ಲಿದ್ದ ಮುಖ್ಯಮಂತ್ರಿ ಹಾಗೂ ಸಂಘದ ಪ್ರತಿನಿಧಿಗಳ ಸಭೆಯ ಅನಿಶ್ಚಿತತೆ ಮುಂದುವರಿದಿದೆ. ಆದರೆ ಮುಖ್ಯಮಂತ್ರಿ ಡಿ.ಕೆ.ಶಿವಕುಮಾರ್‌ ಅವರು ಸಮಸ್ಯೆಗೆ ಪರಿಹಾರ ಕಂಡು ಹಿಡಿಯುವ ನಿಟ್ಟಿನಲ್ಲಿ ಹಣಕಾಸು ಹಾಗೂ ಆರೋಗ್ಯ ಸೇರಿದಂತೆ ಪ್ರಮುಖ ಇಲಾಖೆಯ ಉನ್ನತ ಅಧಿಕಾರಿಗಳ ಜತೆ ಶುಕ್ರವಾರ ಸಭೆ ನಡೆಸುವ ಸಾಧ್ಯತೆಗಳಿವೆ.
ಪ್ರತಿಭಟನೆ ಕೈಬಿಡುವಂತೆ ಹಲವು ಬಾರಿ ಮನವಿ ಮಾಡಿದರೂ ಆಶಾ ಕಾರ್ಯಕರ್ತೆಯರು ಹಠಕ್ಕೆ ಬಿದ್ದು ಫ್ರೀಡಂಪಾರ್ಕ್‌ ನಿಂದ ಕದಲದ ಬಗ್ಗೆ ಮುಖ್ಯಮಂತ್ರಿ ಬೇಸರಗೊಂಡಿದ್ದು, ಪ್ರತಿಭಟನಾನಿರತರ ಜತೆ ಸಭೆ ಬದಲಿಗೆ ಅಧಿಕಾರಿಗಳ ಸಭೆ ನಡೆಸಿ ಆಶಾ ಕಾರ್ಯಕರ್ತೆಯರ ಬೇಡಿಕೆ ಈಡೇರಿಸುವ ಸಾಧ್ಯಾಸಾಧ್ಯತೆಗಳ ಬಗ್ಗೆ ಸಮಾಲೋಚನೆ ನಡೆಸಲಿದ್ದಾರೆ ಎಂದು ತಿಳಿದುಬಂದಿದೆ. ಒಂದು ವೇಳೆ ಅಗತ್ಯವಿದ್ದರೆ ಸಭೆಗೆ ಮುಖಂಡರನ್ನು ಆಹ್ವಾನಿಸಬಹುದು ಎಂದು ಹೇಳಲಾಗುತ್ತಿದೆ.
ಎಐಯುಟಿಯುಸಿಗೆ ಸಂಯೋಜಿತ ಕರ್ನಾಟಕ ರಾಜ್ಯ ಸಂಯುಕ್ತ ಆಶಾ ಕಾರ್ಯಕರ್ತೆಯರ ಸಂಘದ ನೇತೃತ್ವದಲ್ಲಿ ನಡೆಯುತ್ತಿರುವ ಅನಿರ್ದಿಷ್ಟಾವಧಿ ಹೋರಾಟ ಗುರುವಾರ 10ನೇ ದಿನ ಪೂರೈಸಿ ಶುಕ್ರವಾರ (ನ.27)11ನೇ ದಿನಕ್ಕೆ ಕಾಲಿಟ್ಟಿದೆ. ಹೋರಾಟದ ಹಿನ್ನೆಲೆಯಲ್ಲಿ ಗುರುವಾರ ಮುಖ್ಯಮಂತ್ರಿಗಳ ಪ್ರಧಾನ ಸಲಹೆಗಾರ ಜಿ.ಸಿ.ಚಂದ್ರಶೇಖರ್ ಅವರು ಸಂಘದ ಪದಾಧಿಕಾರಿಗಳೊಂದಿಗೆ ಸುದೀರ್ಘ ಮಾತುಕತೆ ನಡೆಸಿದರು.
ಆಶಾ ಕಾರ್ಯಕರ್ತೆಯರ ಬೇಡಿಕೆಗಳನ್ನು ಆಲಿಸಿ ಚರ್ಚಿಸುವಂತೆ ಮುಖ್ಯಮಂತ್ರಿ ತಮ್ಮ ಪ್ರಧಾನ ಸಲಹೆಗಾರರಿಗೆ ಸೂಚಿಸಿದ್ದರು. ಅದರಂತೆ ನಡೆದ ಸಭೆಯಲ್ಲಿ ಸಂಘದ ಪದಾಧಿಕಾರಿಗಳು ಪ್ರಮುಖ ಬೇಡಿಕೆಗಳನ್ನು ವಿವರಿಸಿ, ಅವುಗಳ ಈಡೇರಿಕೆಯ ಅಗತ್ಯವನ್ನು ಮನವರಿಕೆ ಮಾಡಿಕೊಟ್ಟರು. ಬೇಡಿಕೆಗಳನ್ನು ಆಲಿಸಿದ ಚಂದ್ರಶೇಖರ್ ಅವರು, ಈ ಕುರಿತು ಮುಖ್ಯಮಂತ್ರಿಗಳೊಂದಿಗೆ ಚರ್ಚಿಸಿ ಮಾಹಿತಿ ನೀಡುವುದಾಗಿ ಭರವಸೆ ನೀಡಿದರು.
ಮುಖ್ಯಮಂತ್ರಿಗಳೊಂದಿಗೆ ಸಭೆ ನಡೆಯುವ ಕುರಿತು ನಮಗೆ ಇನ್ನೂ ಅಧಿಕೃತ ಮಾಹಿತಿ ಬಂದಿಲ್ಲ. ಗುರುವಾರ ಸಲಹೆಗಾರರ ಕಚೇರಿಯಲ್ಲಿ ನಮ್ಮ ಬೇಡಿಕೆಗಳ ಕುರಿತು ಚರ್ಚೆ ನಡೆಯಿತು. ಅವರು ಎಲ್ಲ ವಿವರಗಳನ್ನು ಆಲಿಸಿ, ಮುಖ್ಯಮಂತ್ರಿಗಳೊಂದಿಗೆ ಮಾತನಾಡಿ ತಿಳಿಸುವುದಾಗಿ ಹೇಳಿದರು. ಮಧ್ಯಾಹ್ನ ಮಾಹಿತಿ ನೀಡುವುದಾಗಿ ತಿಳಿಸಿದ್ದರೂ, ಮುಖ್ಯಮಂತ್ರಿಗಳು ಸಿಗದ ಕಾರಣ ಯಾವುದೇ ನಿರ್ಧಾರ ತಿಳಿಸಿಲ್ಲ ಎಂದು ಸಂಘದ ಪ್ರಧಾನ ಕಾರ್ಯದರ್ಶಿ ಡಿ.ನಾಗಲಕ್ಷ್ಮಿ ತಿಳಿಸಿದರು.
ಶುಕ್ರವಾರ ಮುಖ್ಯಮಂತ್ರಿಗಳೊಂದಿಗೆ ಮಾತನಾಡಿ ಸಭೆ ಏರ್ಪಡಿಸುವ ಕುರಿತು ತಿಳಿಸುವುದಾಗಿ ಸಲಹೆಗಾರರು ಹೇಳಿದ್ದಾರೆ. ಮುಖ್ಯಮಂತ್ರಿಗಳು ಸಿಕ್ಕರೆ ನ.27ರಂದು ಸಭೆ ನಡೆಸಬಹುದು, ಇಲ್ಲದಿದ್ದರೆ ಮುಂದಿನ ಸಭೆಗೆ ವ್ಯವಸ್ಥೆ ಮಾಡಲಾಗುವುದು ಎಂದಿದ್ದಾರೆ. ಆದರೆ, ಸಂಘಕ್ಕೆ ಈವರೆಗೆ ಅಧಿಕೃತ ನೋಟಿಸ್ ಅಥವಾ ಮಾಹಿತಿ ಬಂದಿಲ್ಲ ಎಂದು ಅವರು ಸ್ಪಷ್ಟಪಡಿಸಿದರು.
ಮಾತುಕತೆಯಲ್ಲಿ ಸಂಘದ ಅಧ್ಯಕ್ಷ ಕೆ.ಸೋಮಶೇಖರ್ ಯಾದಗಿರಿ, ಪ್ರಧಾನ ಕಾರ್ಯದರ್ಶಿ ಡಿ.ನಾಗಲಕ್ಷ್ಮಿ, ರಾಜ್ಯ ಉಪಾಧ್ಯಕ್ಷ ಹನುಮೇಶ್ ಜಿ., ಎಐಯುಟಿಯುಸಿ ರಾಜ್ಯ ಉಪಾಧ್ಯಕ್ಷ ಚಂದ್ರಶೇಖರ ಮೇಟಿ ಸೇರಿದಂತೆ ಆಶಾ ಮುಖಂಡರು ಭಾಗವಹಿಸಿದ್ದರು.
ಬ್ಲ್ಯಾಕ್‌ಮೇಲ್ ಮಾಡಿ ಹೆದರಿಸಲಾಗದು
ಸರ್ಕಾರವನ್ನು ಬ್ಲಾಕ್‌ಮೇಲ್‌ ಮಾಡಿ ಹೆದರಿಸಲಾಗದು. ಲಿಖಿತವಾಗಿ ಏನೂ ಬರೆದುಕೊಡಲಿಕ್ಕೂ ಆಗಲ್ಲ. ಇದು ಒಪ್ಪಂದವೂ ಅಲ್ಲ. ರಾಜ್ಯದ ಮುಖ್ಯಮಂತ್ರಿ ಮಾತಿನ ಮೇಲೆಯೇ ನಂಬಿಕೆ ಇಲ್ಲವೆಂದಾದರೆ, ಏನೂ ಮಾಡೋಕ್ಕಾಗಲ್ಲ. ಆಶಾ ಕಾರ್ಯಕರ್ತೆಯರ ಬೇಡಿಕೆ ತಪ್ಪಲ್ಲ. ನಾವು ನಿಮ್ಮ ಪರವಾಗಿದ್ದೇವೆ. ಆದರೆ, ಸರ್ಕಾರವನ್ನು ಹೆದರಿಸಬೇಡಿ. ಮೊದಲು ಪ್ರತಿಷ್ಠೆ ಬಿಡಬೇಕು. ಇಡೀ ದೇಶ ನಡೆಯುತ್ತಿರುವುದು ನಂಬಿಕೆಯ ಮೇಲೆ. ಇಲ್ಲಿ ವಿಶ್ವಾಸ ಇರಬೇಕು. ಕೇಂದ್ರ ಸರ್ಕಾರದ ಮುಂದೆ ಲಿಖಿತ ಉತ್ತರ ಯಾಕೆ ಕೇಳುತ್ತಿಲ್ಲ? -ಡಿ.ಕೆ. ಶಿವಕುಮಾರ್‌, ಮುಖ್ಯಮಂತ್ರಿ
ಬೆದರಿಸಲು ನಾವು ಪ್ರತಿಭಟಿಸುತ್ತಿಲ್ಲ

title: Government Research And Development Body Opens Recruitment, 10th Pass To Graduates Can Apply
description: Candidates are advised to submit their applications well in advance and not wait until the last date. No request for an extension of the application deadline will be entertained.
author: Rahul Kumar
content:
CSIR Recruitment 2026: The Council of Scientific and Industrial Research (CSIR) has invited applications for various regular posts, offering opportunities to candidates with qualifications ranging from Class 10 pass to graduation. The vacancies include Multi-Tasking Staff (MTS), Driver, Junior Hindi Translator, Security Assistant, and Security Officer. The posts carry salaries ranging from Pay Level 1 to Pay Level 7. Interested and eligible candidates can apply online until December 21, 2026, through the official website, recruitment.csir.res.in. The recruitment drive aims to fill a total of 29 vacancies.
Candidates are advised to submit their applications well in advance and not wait until the last date. No request for an extension of the application deadline will be entertained.
Age Limit And Relaxation
Applicants must be at least 18 years old and must not be more than 28 years old as on the last date for submission of online applications. The closing date for submission of applications will be considered the crucial date for determining the age of candidates.
Application Fee
All candidates, except women, SC, ST, PwBD and Ex-Servicemen candidates who are exempted from payment of the fee, are required to pay an application fee of Rs 500 (Rupees Five Hundred only).
The fee can be paid online through SBI Collect.
Applications submitted without the prescribed fee, where fee exemption is not applicable, will be summarily rejected. No representation against such rejection will be entertained.
The fee once paid will not be refunded or adjusted against any other examination or recruitment process under any circumstances.
Security Assistant / Watch & Ward Assistant: Selection Process
The selection process for the post of Security Assistant / Watch & Ward Assistant will consist of two stages.
Stage 1: Candidates will have to appear for a skill, physical and personality assessment test.
Stage 2: Candidates who qualify in Stage 1 will be invited to appear for a competitive written examination.
Eligible candidates applying for the post will first be called for the skill, physical and personality assessment test. Those who qualify will subsequently be invited for the competitive written examination.
The final merit list will be prepared based on candidates' performance in the competitive written examination.
For more details regarding eligibility criteria, age limit, selection process, and other recruitment-related information, candidates are advised to refer to the official notification.

title: Seats To Manifesto: Why Is Akhilesh Yadav In Such A Hurry Ahead Of UP Polls?
description: Are Akhilesh Yadav's early moves a sign of renewed confidence? Or is the SP chief deliberately trying to ensure that the Congress does not hold up his electoral preparations?
author: Kanika Katiyar, Mohd Asim
content:
Uttar Pradesh's political contest looks set. The state appears headed to a triangular contest between the NDA, the INDIA bloc and a possible third front of smaller social and political forces. But even as political equations remain fluid, Samajwadi Party (SP) chief Akhilesh Yadav appears to have taken an early lead in setting the electoral agenda, stepping up preparations and putting his campaign machinery into motion.
What makes Akhilesh Yadav's approach particularly interesting is the pace at which he is moving. Seat-sharing negotiations between the SP and Congress are yet to reach a conclusion. There is no clarity on the number of seats candidates either party will field, or on the larger promises and campaign strategy the alliance will take to voters. Yet Akhilesh appears unwilling to wait for these negotiations to conclude before getting down to business.
His early moves have triggered considerable discussion in political circles. Is this a sign of renewed confidence? Or is the SP chief deliberately trying to ensure that the Congress does not hold up his electoral preparations?
According to political observers and sources, Akhilesh Yadav is approaching the 2027 election with a renewed confidence. He also appears to have drawn lessons from the 2022 Assembly elections, the 2024 Lok Sabha results and, more recently, the experience of INDIA bloc allies in Bihar.
Why Is Akhilesh Yadav In A Hurry? The Big Reasons are:
1. 2024 Lok Sabha Results Boost
The biggest factor behind Akhilesh Yadav's renewed confidence is arguably the 2024 Lok Sabha election. The SP won 37 seats in Uttar Pradesh, while the Congress secured six, delivering a significant setback to the BJP in the state.
The INDIA bloc's campaign, built partly around the argument that the Constitution was under threat, resonated with voters. The results also strengthened SP's political standing and reinforced Akhilesh Yadav's belief that the SP could take on the BJP effectively with the right social coalition and electoral strategy.
That confidence appears to have carried over into preparations for 2027.
2. Lessons From The 2022 Assembly Elections
Akhilesh Yadav also seems to have learnt that electoral preparations cannot be left until the final stages of an election.
In 2022, the SP chief had begun campaigning as early as October, while the party released its candidate lists by January 13. The SP and Congress eventually contested separately, with each having its own candidates, campaign and electoral strategy.
This time, however, the SP is preparing for a potential alliance with the Congress. The uncertainty surrounding seat-sharing makes early planning even more important.
Sources suggest Akhilesh wants to avoid a repeat of the confusion and delays that can accompany last-minute candidate selection and alliance negotiations.
3. The Bihar Experience And Pressure On The Congress
Another important factor appears to be the experience of the INDIA bloc in Bihar.
The delay in seat-sharing negotiations between the RJD and Congress, followed by the alliance's electoral performance, has reportedly reinforced Akhilesh's belief that prolonged negotiations can hurt a coalition's prospects.
The SP has repeatedly floated a proposal of 26 seats for the Congress, a move that is being seen as an attempt to put pressure on its ally and ensure that an agreement is reached well in advance.
Sources say Akhilesh Yadav wants to maintain momentum during the election build-up rather than allow the Congress's pace of decision-making to affect the SP's preparations.
There is also a larger political calculation at play. Akhilesh is widely seen as the INDIA bloc's chief ministerial face in Uttar Pradesh. He knows that any delay or miscalculation by an alliance partner could ultimately affect his own prospects of returning to power.
4. Five Candidates, Two Political Messages
The SP chief's decision to announce candidates for five seats even as seat-sharing discussions with the Congress remain unresolved is particularly significant.
The move appears to carry two messages.
The first is directed at his own party. By announcing candidates early, Akhilesh wants to activate the organisation, give prospective candidates a head start and ensure that party workers begin preparing for the electoral battle.
The second message is aimed at the Congress. The unilateral announcement signals that the SP is not willing to put its preparations on hold indefinitely while negotiations continue.
It could also strengthen Akhilesh's bargaining position in discussions over seat-sharing, particularly his insistence that the Congress should seek seats where it has a realistic chance of winning.
Sources also point to strains between Akhilesh Yadav and Congress leader Imran Masood as one of the factors contributing to the current unease.
The Manifesto Gambit: Why 'PDA Ka Pran Patra' Matters
Perhaps the clearest indication of Akhilesh's early election strategy is the release of the SP's first manifesto, titled PDA Ka Pran Patra.
The document seeks to reach out to three important voter groups: young people, women and senior citizens. By placing specific promises before voters well ahead of the election, Akhilesh appears keen to establish what a potential SP government would offer before the BJP gets into full-fledged campaign mode.
The timing is significant.
The BJP has not yet unveiled a major election manifesto or made comparable broad announcements. Akhilesh, meanwhile, has already stepped up his campaign and is holding a series of political programmes.
The SP chief appears keen to turn potential anti-incumbency against the BJP into an electoral advantage. The manifesto is part of that effort: to offer voters a sense of what an alternative government could deliver, rather than merely campaign against the ruling party.
It is also an attempt to give the PDA slogan a more concrete political and electoral meaning.
But the manifesto gambit raises another question: Is Akhilesh getting so far ahead of his alliance partner that the INDIA bloc risks appearing divided even before the campaign formally gathers pace?
Who Holds The Cards In UP?
The central contradiction in Akhilesh's early campaign is that while he is moving quickly on the electoral front, the alliance arrangement remains unsettled.
Political sources suggest that Akhilesh Yadav is acutely aware of the relative strengths of the two parties in Uttar Pradesh. The SP has a much larger organisational presence and a stronger electoral base in the state, while the Congress is looking to rebuild its political relevance.
The 2024 results have nevertheless demonstrated that the Congress can contribute to the alliance's broader social coalition and electoral appeal.
Akhilesh, however, appears determined to ensure that the Congress does not dictate the pace or terms of the alliance. His early announcements, candidate selection and manifesto release can all be read as attempts to establish the SP's leadership of the campaign before the seat-sharing formula is finalised.
For Akhilesh Yadav, the 2027 Uttar Pradesh Assembly election is about more than simply defeating the BJP. It is also about consolidating his position as the principal challenger to the ruling party and ensuring that the alliance in UP revolves around his political strategy.

title: 'Troubled By World': A 'Suicide Pact' Note In Student's Death At Faridabad Hotel
description: On Tuesday, the body of 19-year-old Aruna Singh was recovered from a hotel room in the Sarai Khwaja area, where she had supposedly checked in with her boyfriend Vipin Yadav a day before.
author: Press Trust Of India
content:
A note revealing a suicide pact has given a fresh impetus to the search for the supposed lover of a Delhi University student, who was found dead in a hotel here earlier in the week.
On Tuesday, the body of 19-year-old Aruna Singh was recovered from a hotel room in the Sarai Khwaja area, where she had supposedly checked in with her boyfriend Vipin Yadav a day before.
Police have recovered two notes from the room, one bearing a suicide pact between the two lovers, the other revealing some money transactions involving lakhs of rupees. Vipin, 24, is on the run.
According to one of the notes, signed by Vipin, police said, the two knew each other for eight years and were in a romantic relationship.
In the note, Vipin says they both were troubled by the world and had decided to end their lives together.
The man says he will jump into the Agra canal, but before he does that, he will send his location to Aruna's phone. A scrutiny of Aruna's phone, though, revealed no such message.
The other note contains names of several individuals and some financial transactions involving them. The amounts ranged between Rs 50,000 and Rs 3.5 lakh. The note also records a payment of Rs 1 lakh to an individual on the morning of the incident.
According to the police, Vipin lost both his parents during the COVID pandemic. He was 17 then. A neighbour, Shambhu, Aruna's father, took him in for shelter.
"Aruna's father not only provided him with meals and offered him a place to stay, he even bought him a motorcycle," a relative said.
As he frequented Aruna's house, Vipin developed a romantic relationship with Aruna, the person said.
An officer said Vipin's father was a transporter and owned about 12 trucks and several properties.
After his parents' death, Vipin sold off the trucks one by one, along with a plot of land and a Maruti Brezza car. He mortgaged his 150-square-yard house, fell into bad company, and incurred heavy debts, one of his neighbours said.
On Monday morning, Aruna left home for college, and her brother drove her to the metro station. From there, Vipin took her on a motorcycle to a hotel.
In the hotel room, Vipin allegedly made Aruna consume rat poison, locked the room, and went away.
Earlier, a case of murder was filed at Dhauj Police Station at Aruna's brother's complaint.
"Four police teams have been deployed to apprehend Vipin," Dhauj SHO Inspector Anil Kumar said.
(Except for the headline, this story has not been edited by NDTV staff and is published from a syndicated feed.)

title: Jagan Mohan Reddy's YSRCP to back NDA's Delimitation Bill push in Parliament but with a rider
description: NEW DELHI: The Jagan Mohan Reddy-led YSRCP will support the NDA government's push for the Delimitation Bill in Parliament, provided it ensures regional
author: Abhishek Mishra
content:
NEW DELHI: The Jagan Mohan Reddy-led YSRCP will support the NDA government's push for the Delimitation Bill in Parliament, provided it ensures regional balance, party sources told news agency ANI on Friday.The support from the YSRCP will strengthen the NDA's numbers as the Centre prepares to bring the legislation back to Parliament during a special sitting.Party sources told ANI that the YSRCP would support the Bill if it is introduced with provisions "ensuring regional balance."The development assumes significance as the government seeks to secure the two-thirds majority required to pass the legislation, which failed to clear the floor test during the Budget Session.Apart from the YSRCP, Sharad Pawar-led NCP (SP) has also adopted a softer stance on the proposed legislation. Party leader Supriya Sule recently indicated that there might be "something good" about the Bill, adding that the party would not "blindly" oppose it simply because it was in the opposition.
The Union government's latest move to reconvene Parliament has added to the political focus on the proposed legislation. Ending the suspense, the government on Thursday moved to convene a short session of Parliament from November 30, during which it is expected to bring back the delimitation Bills to implement the women's reservation law from 2029.
The proposed exercise is expected to increase the maximum strength of the Lok Sabha to 850 from 550, with the government seeking to ensure that the expansion addresses concerns over regional representation.Parliamentary affairs minister Kiren Rijiju announced on Thursday that the government had requested Lok Sabha Speaker Om Birla to reconvene the Lower House on November 30 and Rajya Sabha chairman C P Radhakrishnan to call a sitting of the Upper House on December 2 to transact "essential government business".
Abhishek Mishra is a Digital Content Producer at The Times of India, working with the news desk. He writes with a keen eye on foreign policy, defence developments, and the shifting currents of geopolitics-and yes, Indian politics always finds a way onto his radar too.

title: Watch: Putin hails PM Modi's 'Make in India' vision, praises 16-year-old Indian AI entrepreneur
description: Russian President Vladimir Putin on Thursday praised the work of 16-year-old Indian entrepreneur Raul John Aju, linking his efforts in artificial
author: Aadrita Halder
content:
Russian President Vladimir Putin on Thursday praised the work of 16-year-old Indian entrepreneur Raul John Aju, linking his efforts in artificial intelligence (AI) to Prime Minister Narendra Modi's 'Make in India' initiative during the AI Journey 2026 conference.Putin and Kazakh President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev interacted with young innovators at the conference, where Aju, the founder and chief technology officer (CTO) of AI Realm Technologies, was among those introduced to the Russian president.During the interaction, Putin acknowledged Aju's work and highlighted how young innovators developing their own technological solutions contribute to the objectives of the 'Make in India' initiative."Ultimately your work helps realize PM Modi's "Make in India" call right? Because it helps young people find their own solutions and implement these solutions," Putin told Aju.
Putin's remarks come days after the Office of the United States Trade Representative (USTR) criticised India's manufacturing and export policies, including the 'Make in India' initiative, in a report examining structural excess capacity and production in manufacturing sectors.
Putin's praise comes days after US trade body targets 'Make in India'In its Section 301 investigation report into India's acts, policies and practices relating to structural excess capacity and production in manufacturing sectors, the USTR alleged that India had adopted several measures that contributed to excess manufacturing capacity and production while failing to effectively address the resulting global concerns."India engages in a range of acts, policies, and practices that create, maintain, or contribute to the structural excess capacity and production evident in the indicia described above. Key among these are the umbrella efforts of Make in India, PLI, Atmanirbhar Bharat (Self-Reliant India), and IBEF, with a particular emphasis on efforts related to or under these efforts in the steel, solar, health, and ICT sectors," the USTR said.The report specifically identified the government's flagship 'Make in India' programme, Production-Linked Incentive (PLI) scheme, Atmanirbhar Bharat initiative and India Brand Equity Foundation (IBEF) among the measures it said contributed to structural excess capacity.Who is Raul John Aju, the 'AI Kid of India'?Popularly known online as 'Raul the Rockstar' and often described as the 'AI Kid of India', Aju is a teenager from Kerala who has pursued artificial intelligence despite coming from a Commerce background rather than a conventional engineering or computer science pathway.According to information shared on his LinkedIn profile, his interest in technology began when he was around nine years old. What started as independent learning and experimentation gradually developed into AI projects, educational initiatives and a growing online community.Aju studied Plus Two Commerce at North Edappally GHSS while simultaneously working on artificial intelligence projects. His LinkedIn profile identifies him as the founder and CTO of AIRealm Technologies, where he develops AI products and practical technology solutions.Projects associated with him include ThinkCraft, RESQ AI and MeBot, among other AI-based tools. He is also associated with ThinkCraft Academy, an AI learning platform that introduces students and professionals to emerging technologies.
Beyond developing software, Aju has conducted AI workshops and sessions for students, educators and professionals, with a focus on making the technology accessible to people without technical backgrounds."I build things with AI. I talk about them. Sometimes I break them. Then I build them again," he writes in his LinkedIn introduction.His profile also states that he has delivered eight TEDx talks and conducted sessions at IITs, universities, schools and other institutions. He has built an online following of more than 500,000 people, sharing content related to artificial intelligence and emerging technologies.

title: Whatever is scarce wins
description: Two young Indians raised around Antwerp now teach big companies how to sound human on the internet.
author: Abhinav Kejriwal
content:
Two young Indians raised around Antwerp now teach big companies how to sound human on the internet. Their families learned the same lesson over a century: what you are really selling is trust.In 2020, an 18-year-old in Antwerp was listening to a podcast in which one brother kept giving the other the same advice. The host was Ali Abdaal, a doctor turned YouTuber. His brother Taimur, a start-up founder, told him over several episodes that Twitter was where the founders were, and where the real conversation about technology and business was happening. Ali kept putting it off, though he came round in the end and now has some 350,000 followers there.The listener, Aadit Sheth, took the advice more seriously than the man it was meant for. On Twitter (I refuse to call it X), the feed was full of it. He found it freeing. Within six months he was boiling down two-hour interviews by Tim Ferriss and Joe Rogan into threads. There was no grand plan. Mostly, he told me, he wanted to make good use of his time.Six years on, Aadit has more than half a million followers on X and a company built on what he learned there.
He and his co-founder, Arnav Kothari, run The Narrative Company, which helps large technology firms find their voice on X. They call it an AI-native social media agency. It is a curious label for a business whose best idea is that in a feed filling up with machine-made content, a human being is about to become the rarest thing on offer.Arnav grew up inside the diamond trade around Antwerp. His family's diamond and jewellery business, KGK, is about 120 years old and one of the largest in the world. He left a software strategy job in Boston and moved to Indore to hire an engineering team for it. The aim was to move buying that happened over calls and WhatsApp onto a platform. Six months in, the beta users did not love it, so the team reworked the design and relaunched three months later. Within three years the channel grew from nothing to $60m in annual sales, and getting there meant travelling between offices in India, Dubai, Antwerp, and New York to make it work for the teams using it. He has done sales for both businesses, and the contrast taught him what a brand is worth. In the family firm, a new account goes roughly like this: Someone already knows the head of procurement, there is an introduction, a dinner, and then, a contract. That ease is earned. Behind each introduction sit generations of trust and years of care in keeping it, and working inside the firm taught him to respect both. Flying between offices, he also noticed how much of that care now happens online, between visits.That gap is the whole subject of their work: how to make narratives clearer. I think it is also one of the most useful things to focus on.Every business wants a moat, something a rival cannot easily cross. When there is no moat, Arnav says, the moat is what people are already comfortable with. AI is making software, copy and advertising cheaper to produce. Efficiency is becoming the price of entry. What stays scarce is the feeling that a customer knows you and would choose you again.Aadit gets there through stories. He has been reading Satya Nadella's Hit Refresh, and was struck by the chapter on the birth of Nadella's son Zain, born with severe disabilities, and how fatherhood taught Nadella an empathy he had not had before. Aadit's own brother has special needs. And so, two paragraphs of a father's feelings moved him in a way nothing else could. People find their own lives inside someone else's story, and that is as true of a company as of a person. When Ivan Zhao tells how Notion nearly ran out of money, let go of almost everyone and moved to Kyoto to rebuild the product from scratch, people warm to the company and to what it stands for.Narrative began with that feeling. The founders admired how young firms such as Notion, Ramp and Anthropic talk to their users online, with humour and a sense that someone real is on the other side. Then they looked at the world's largest companies and found accounts that sounded like press releases. The idea was to carry the start-ups' community playbook into those older giants. Their answer is a hybrid: software in the back, people in front. Their tool, Nia, works like a "For You" feed for engagement: it uses AI to find conversations a company could usefully join, such as a developer describing an AI deployment problem a client could help with. The team then decides whether and how to take part, and Arnav, who leads Nia's development, works with clients on how it fits their needs. People stay in front because large companies still want a human to talk to, and because selling is still a human game: for now, it is people, not agents, who have to be persuaded to buy. The part no software can copy is taste: Aadit has spent six years learning, as a creator, what makes an audience trust an account."Whatever is scarce wins," Aadit told me. If everyone else is selling five hundred AI-generated ads, the winning move is to go the other way. His favourite example is Hector Serrano, who ran paid ads for the start-up Wispr Flow. By the account of the tech writer Lenny Rachitsky, Serrano made every ad himself for a year and a half. A few videos about how he did it travelled so far that Austin Rief, a co-founder of Morning Brew, publicly asked for a podcast on how Serrano had built a personal brand so fast. The résumé, in Aadit's view, used to record what you have done. Increasingly it shows how you think, in public. His advice to friends is blunt: open-source your thinking on X.Indians find this advice hard to take, and I don't think it is because we are shy. An American teenager applying to college writes an essay about who they are. Most Indian students never have to make that case until much later. We grow up inside a meritocracy whose promise is simple: do the work and you will win. It leaves out that someone has to know the work exists. Aadit points to Kunal Shah, the founder of CRED, who has spent the better part of a decade thinking out loud on X. A philosophy graduate from NMIMS, he built CRED and was then hired by Mark Zuckerberg to run WhatsApp worldwide. Aadit does not think that leap happens without a decade of public thinking behind it.Arnav's advice is also surprising. Don't rush it, he says. Build real knowledge first, because posting pays off far more when you have something to say. It is like going to the gym without a trainer: you will build a habit, but maybe with the wrong form. He does not post much himself. For three years at KGK he took roughly a hundred flights a year and had no settled base. The firm was making it easier to do business across distance while he went without a community of his own. He is clear now that he wants to spend his life helping people connect, and the new company is where he is starting: working out how companies can build real relationships with their audiences. That is what he wants to write about first. Maybe you haven't found what you want to say yet, he tells anxious friends, and that is fine.Which leaves the question hanging over his business: where does a good story end and a convenient fiction begin? And what makes a company's voice genuine when a team and software are helping it show up? Arnav has no formula, only a reasonable test. At 16, he co-founded a non-profit, Khilti Pari. When he pitched it to his school as an elective, the principal laughed and asked whether they were even incorporated. They were. It became the school's first student-created elective, drawing 10 to 15 students a year, and its exhibitions of paintings sourced from artists on Instagram raised crores of rupees over the years, enough to fund two vocational centres for girls in Rajasthan.
On visits to the villages he spoke with the girls' families. Some fathers had been drinking and did not understand what the charity was trying to do. It made him doubt how much education alone could change while the girls stayed financially dependent, so the work moved towards jobs and independence, including training for government posts. One story is about bringing people together, the other about changing his mind after listening to the people he meant to help. Both still shape the problems he chooses, building communities among them. So before he tells a story about what he is building, he asks whether it still feels true. Can he sleep at night with it?The internet offers something fast and strange: You can now be known by people you will never meet, years before you need anything from them. And sometimes you do meet them. That is how the two founders met. Arnav messaged Aadit on LinkedIn to suggest coffee, and they spent most of it showing each other AI tools on their laptops. They became close friends, and then built the company together. Because who would have thought that when Arnav messaged Aadit on LinkedIn for a coffee and they spent most of the time showing each other little optimisations on their laptops, that eventually, they would build the Narrative Company together.

title: ‘Even Z-Plus cover won’t save you’: Mumbai jewellery store firing linked to ₹10cr extortion demand
description: Mumbai jeweller attacked amid ₹10 crore extortion threats; two masked shooters fled as police investigate.
author: PTI
content:
A firing incident targeting a jewellery store in Mumbai is suspected to be linked to a ₹10-crore extortion attempt after the shop owner received multiple threatening messages last month but chose to ignore them, police said, citing preliminary investigations.
One of the messages allegedly warned that even Z-Plus security cover won’t save the shop owner, police said on Thursday (November 26, 2026).
Also read | Police recover motorcycle allegedly used by accused in Mahim firing
Two motorcycle-borne individuals wearing helmets fired three rounds at the store of PC Jain Jewellers in Mahim on Wednesday (November 25) evening before fleeing towards Bandra. No one was hurt in the firing.
According to the police, the shop owner, Bharat Jain, had allegedly been receiving repeated threats through WhatsApp messages and phone calls over the past month. However, assuming the messages were spam, he ignored them and did not approach the police.
During the investigation, police found that Mr. Jain had received threatening communications on three separate occasions before the firing incident.
On October 18, Mr. Jain received a call from an unknown number. After he did not respond, a threatening message was sent to him in the evening, warning that he would be shot. On October 24, he received another message stating, “Ready rakhna, chamatkar hoga”.
The final threat, sent on October 31, reportedly included a direct demand for ₹10 crore along with a death threat, according to police.
The final message allegedly read: “Ramji, zyada dimaag mat chala, teri janam kundli hai. Z-Plus security bhi laga rakh, paisa tujhe dena hoga. Yamraj ji ko dekhna hai toh theek, nahi toh 10 crore dena hoga.”
The message warned Mr. Jain that even if he had Z-Plus security, one of the highest levels of protection provided to individuals facing severe or extreme threats, he would still have to pay the demanded amount or face fatal consequences.
Since the threats originated from unknown mobile numbers, the shop owner initially dismissed them as spam and did not lodge a police complaint.
Also read | Cylinder explosion at Sowcarpet jewellery unit leaves seven with burns
Investigators suspect the firing was intended to intimidate Jain and pressure him into paying the ₹10 crore extortion amount.
Police said they are scanning CCTV footage from surrounding areas for clues to crack the case. Technical surveillance is also being used to identify and trace the two assailants who fled after the attack, they added.
Published - November 27, 2026 10:00 am IST

title: J&K Congress leader Peerzada Mohammad Sayeed dies at 73
description: Veteran J&K Congress leader Peerzada Mohammad Sayeed dies at 73, former MLA and minister in PDP-CCC sessions.
author: The Hindu Bureau
content:
Senior Congress leader and sitting legislator from Anantnag, Peerzada Mohammad Sayeed, 73, passed away on Thursday (November 26, 2026) evening, according to the family.
Mr. Sayeed has been unwell recently. The last rites will be performed at his native place Damhal Achabal in south Kashmir’s Anantnag.
Mr. Sayeed won the 2024 Assembly elections on a Congress ticket from the Anantnag constituency by a thin margin of 1600 votes. He was elected for the first time from the Kokernag constituency in 1987 and managed to win the seat again in 2002 and 2008.
A law graduate, Mr. Sayeed also served as president of the Jammu and Kashmir Pradesh Congress Committee (JKPCC).
J&K CM Omar Abdullah condoles demise
Jammu and Kashmir Chief Minister Omar Abdullah on Friday (November 27, 2026) expressed grief over the death of veteran Congress leader and Anantnag MLA Peerzada Mohammad Sayeed.
“Chief Minister has expressed deep grief over the passing away of Peerzada Mohammad Syed, MLA Anantnag and former Minister,” said a post on X by the official handle of Office of Chief Minister, J&K.
Paying rich tributes to Sayeed, Mr. Abdullah recalled his long and distinguished career in public service and his invaluable contributions to the welfare of the people of Jammu and Kashmir, it said.
The Chief Minister also extended his heartfelt condolences to the bereaved family, friends and supporters. He prayed for strength and fortitude for his family to bear this irreparable loss, the post said.
(With PTI inputs)

title: Govt may delink delimitation from Census, uniformly increase state seats by 50%
description: The move is part of the government039s renewed push to advance the delimitation-linked women039s reservation legislation which failed to secure the required support in Parliament in April
author: Aishwarya Paliwal
content:
Govt may delink delimitation from Census, uniformly increase state seats by 50%
The move is part of the government's renewed push to advance the delimitation-linked women's reservation legislation, which failed to secure the required support in Parliament in April.
The government is likely to consider two key proposals linked to the delimitation exercise: a 50 per cent increase in Lok Sabha seats across all states and delinking the process from the Census, sources said.
The proposals could be announced after the Union Cabinet meeting scheduled for 1 pm on Friday.
The move is part of the government's renewed push to advance the delimitation-linked women's reservation legislation, which failed to secure the required support in Parliament in April.
The Cabinet meeting comes ahead of a special sitting of Parliament, convened from November 30 to December 3.
While the Lok Sabha will reconvene on November 30, the Rajya Sabha will meet from December 2. The two Houses had been adjourned sine die on August 13, but the Monsoon Session was not formally prorogued.
Just a day ago, Prime Minister Narendra Modi backed women's reservation in Parliament and accused the opposition of stalling the Constitution (131st Amendment) Bill, 2026, which sought to link the implementation of 33 per cent reservation for women in legislatures with delimitation.
The Bill had been defeated in April after the government failed to secure the two-thirds majority required for a constitutional amendment.
In the 543-member Lok Sabha, the legislation needed at least 361 votes. With three vacancies, the House currently has 540 members.
The ruling NDA, which has around 320 MPs, fell short of the required numbers and needed support from outside its alliance to get the legislation through.
The political arithmetic has since shifted.
Twenty rebel Trinamool Congress MPs broke away from the party and merged with the Nationalist Citizens Party of India (NCPI), pledging support to the NDA.
Six Shiv Sena (UBT) MPs also joined the Eknath Shinde-led Shiv Sena, taking the total number of MPs who moved out of the opposition camp to 26.
Despite these developments, the government would still require additional backing to meet the constitutional threshold.
The DMK, with 22 MPs, and the NCP (Sharadchandra Pawar), with eight MPs, could play a significant role in the numbers game.
The government is also expected to face resistance from opposition parties over the alleged Special Intensive Revision (SIR) irregularities and their demand for Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar's resignation.
These issues could trigger protests during the special sitting.
