title: Stars vs. warning labels: Inside packaged food dispute and what the SC ruling means
description: “We have issued some directions which we feel, if implemented, will lead to healthier children. If taken in the right spirit, it will take the country to healthier times,” the SC said | India News
author: Chetan Chauhan
content:
Chetan Chauhan is the National Affairs Editor looking into all aspects of news and features from across India. A Chevening scholar with over three decades of experience in reporting and news management, Chetan has extensively covered all important aspects of the social sector, political economy, environment and climate change nationally and internationally. He did a journalism course at the Reuters Institute of Journalism in Oxford and Digital Media training at Nanyang Technological University in Singapore. He started as a reporter with The Statesman in 1996 and joined the Hindustan Times in 2000 in the metro bureau covering environment, crime and Delhi politics. He covered hot local news, from the Jessica Lal murder case to the rebellion of Delhi Congress MLAs against then Chief Minister Sheila Dikshit, to the replacement of toxic vehicle fuel with cleaner compressed natural gas (CNG) in the national capital. Some of his stories on air pollution became part of the Supreme Court’s landmark MC Mehta versus Government of India case in the National Capital Region (NCR), forcing the government to take corrective measures. As part of the national political bureau since 2004, he covered important central sectors such as environment, education, social justice, labour, rural development, water resources, renewable energy, agriculture, broadcasting and the Planning Commission for more than a decade producing several exclusive and investigative breaking stories. His specialisation is the environment, having covered at least a dozen United Nations global conferences on climate change, biodiversity and wildlife including climate summits in Paris, Copenhagen and Bali. He also covered India’s two five-year plans ---11th and 12th and reported on drafting and execution of right based laws such as Right to Education, Right to Information and rural job guarantee law, MG-NREGA, now being introduced in new format as VG-RAM-G Act. He has in-depth knowledge of social sector issues. He was one of the first to report on tigers vanishing from Sariska and Panna wildlife reserves in 2004 and 2008, respectively, leading to the setting up of the National Tiger Conservation Authority (NTCA) and the introduction of stringent penal provisions for poaching. He has written extensively on the rising human-animal conflict in India and the degradation of India’s biodiversity hotspots because of mining and other activities. Since 2004, Chetan has covered Parliament comprehensively and participated in training on the nuanced coverage of Parliament proceedings. He has travelled extensively across India to cover national and provincial elections since 1998, especially in the Hindi heartland states, considered India’s road to power. He writes a regular column for Hindustan Times, Ecostani, on important national politics, economy, Himalayan ecology and environmental issues. His other responsibilities include providing inputs for edits and edit page articles for the publication, apart from managing news flow from across India.
Stars vs. warning labels: Inside packaged food dispute and what the SC ruling means
“We have issued some directions which we feel, if implemented, will lead to healthier children. If taken in the right spirit, it will take the country to healthier times,” the SC said
The Supreme Court on Thursday ordered the Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (FSSAI) to introduce prominent red warning labels on packaged foods high in sugar, saturated fat or salt across a sector estimated by the food ministry to be worth ₹2.24 lakh crore in 2023–24.
A bench of justices JB Pardiwala and K Vinod Chandran said the warnings must carry standardised pictorial representations alongside the words “high fat, “high sugar” or “high salt” in bold, rejecting the regulator’s proposal to place all three warnings within a single hexagon.
“We have issued some directions which we feel, if implemented, will lead to healthier children. If taken in the right spirit, it will take the country to healthier times,” justice Pardiwala said, reading out the operative part of the verdict.
Deep Dive
The ruling asked FSSAI to examine science-based warning labels used in countries such as Chile, Mexico, Singapore and across Europe to help curb consumption of high-sugar products. It also invoked people’s right to make an informed food choice as a constitutional right under Article 21 of the Constitution, and pulled up the regulator for delays in deciding on front-of-pack nutrition labelling (FoPNL) since 2022.
The context
According to the Indian Council of Medical Research, non-communicable diseases cause roughly six million deaths each year, accounting for about 63% of annual mortality and projected to reach nearly 75% by 2030.
An Indian Council of Medical Research–India Diabetes study estimated that in 2021, 101 million people had diabetes, 136 million were pre-diabetic, 315 million had hypertension, 254 million had generalised obesity, 351 million had abdominal obesity, 231 million had hypercholesterolemia and 185 million had elevated LDL cholesterol.
The top court cited an analysis of recent National Family Health Survey data, 2023-2024 (“NFHS-6”)4, which underlined that the situation had progressively worsened compared with the numbers recorded by NFHS-5 2019-2021. Obesity in women has increased from 24% to 30.7% and in men from 22.9% to 27.3%, respectively. Diabetes in women has increased from 13.5% to 17.8% and in men from 15.6% to 20.9%, respectively.
According to the World Health Organisation (WHO), the rise in NCDs is due to four major behavioural risk factors -- tobacco use, unhealthy diets including the consumption of foods high in saturated fat, sugar and/or Salt (“HFSS foods”), harmful use of alcohol and insufficient physical activity. “While smoking, imbibing spirits and eschewing exercise are essentially personal choices and a healthy diet comes only with heightened awareness, consumption of toxic shelf-foods is driven by visual appeal and product advertising,” the Supreme Court said, pointing out that any targeted action to prevent the NCD public health crisis had to focus on the consumption of HFSS foods and ultra-processed foods.
In India, the court said, the ultra-processed food (UPF) sector grew by 13.37% in retail sales between the years 2011 and 2021 despite the daily consumption share of UPFs being lower than that of home-cooked.
Star rating versus warning label
In 2022, the FSSAI published draft rules for FoPNL proposing a star-rating system, from five stars for the least harmful items to one star for the most, based on added fat, sugar and salt. By contrast, warning labels alert consumers directly when a product contains high levels of fat, sugar or salt, or a combination of them.
The Supreme Court order noted that FSSAI received close to 14,000 comments on the draft. The food industry favoured the star rating, while consumers opted for the warning labels. More than 7,000 industry submissions warned that FoPNL would hurt livelihoods.
The bench observed that feedback leaned toward warning labels and awareness campaigns, as ultra-processed foods displace traditional foods, noting a lack of consensus on the proposed Indian Nutrition Rating system. It cited evidence that warning labels such as those in Chile and Europe outperform star ratings in shifting consumer habits. The government told FSSAI to withdraw the draft notification after a meeting chaired by the cabinet secretary in October 2025.
While the FSSAI and the health ministry argued that star ratings would simplify nutritional data and encourage product reformulation, the court said the insistence of the petitioner and scientific data helped the cout decide on settling for the warning labels.
Constitutional right
The court underlined that while the Constitution did not explicitly provide for right to food but food consumption could be be covered under right to live with human dignity. “Article 47, which also speaks of the State’s primary duty to raise the ‘nutrition level’ of the people at large, would infuse the right to food guaranteed within Article 21 as well,” the 131-page verdict said.
The bench said the state must ensure both quantity and quality of food, noting that the right to health extends beyond clinical care to broader determinants of health and conditions congenial to good health. Ensuring access to safe and nutritious food requires regulation of the general food environment to a large extent, it said, underlining that the words “raising the level of nutrition” in Article 47 should mean that sufficient attention should be given to “ensure the right to quality food” for all.
Invoking the right to live with dignity, the court said it includes the right to make informed choices, and it was the State’s responsibility to ensure that an individual can make a free and informed choice for public health rather than being influenced by marketing, dense and unreadable information. “Therefore, the State in giving full respect for the individual right to free and informed choice must ensure a social and informational order in which consumer interests and public health is prioritised,” the court said.
The court said it was within its jurisdiction under Article 32 as the issue concerns fundamental rights of citizens and was trying to fill the legislative vacuum on important public health issue.
Arun Gupta, head of Nutrition Promotion Network of India, a petitioner in the case, said the court had done something remarkable. “It has reminded the State that public health is not a bargaining chip. Anchored front-of-pack labelling in Article 21—the right to health, food, and informed choice,” said Gupta.
Giving FSSAI clarity
On the threshold limits for nutrients of concern such as salt and sugar, the court said thresholds should be determined by science, not by implementation difficulties. The court also rejected the FSSAI proposal to base the label only on salt, added sugar, and added fat on two counts. First, measuring added nutrients of concern was not possible, and therefore, it would be difficult for FSSAI to take action against the food industry for wrong labelling, as a “warning criterion that cannot be tested cannot be enforced.” Second, the court said that the impact on human health is from total nutrients of concern, and not just the added ones.
The warning levels have to be dynamic. “The FSSAI must also earnestly work towards the progressive reduction of these threshold levels over time, in a phased manner, to ensure that the food environment is constantly improved upon,” the court said, directing the regulator to bring a comprehensive definition of High Fat Salt Sugar (HFSS) foods.
Gupta said FSSAI must now choose science-based thresholds used by countries such as Chile and Mexico, as well as WHO.
The 2022 draft notification set the threshold levels at 21g for total sugar, 5g for saturated fat, and 450 mg for sodium/salt (the values provided under the DGI, 2024) per 100 gram/litre of packaged food. In 2024, the health ministry found that 94.1% of products exceeded at least one threshold nutrient-of-concern level, while 85.3% exceeded two or more threshold nutrient-of-concern levels.
The top court told FSSAI to ensure that these numbers are neither set too low nor too high. “If they are set too low, then almost all packaged food products in the market would carry a warning label. The saturation of the labels in the market would quickly desensitise the consumers and induce ‘label fatigue‘... On the other hand, if it is set too high, then most products would escape regulatory scrutiny,” the bench said. The FSSAI has four months to decide the threshold limits and the hexagon pictorial warning label for each nutrient of concern.

title: TMC name, symbol, party funds at stake as rival factions present claims before ECI today
description: The ECI could award them to one TMC faction, or keep both frozen and let each continue under its interim identity | India News
author: Himanshi Dahiya
content:
TMC name, symbol, party funds at stake as rival factions present claims before ECI today
The ECI could award them to one TMC faction, or keep both frozen and let each continue under its interim identity
The rival factions of the Trinamool Congress (TMC) will present their claims before the Election Commission of India (ECI) in Delhi on Friday over the party’s name and its twin-flowers-on-grass symbol. The hearing is scheduled for 4pm at the ECI’s office.
“Both factions have been called for a hearing. The ECI will listen to their arguments, and due procedure will be followed,” an ECI official said.
Abhishek Banerjee, Derek O’Brien, Dola Sen, Kalyan Banerjee and Mahua Moitra will represent the Mamata Banerjee camp. West Bengal Leader of Opposition Ritabrata Banerjee and Arup Roy lead the rebel group.
What is at stake
The ECI’s final order will decide which group gets the party’s identity. That includes recognition in Parliament. The rebels have staked a claim to the party funds. The ECI could award the original name and symbol to one faction, or keep both frozen and let each continue under its interim identity.
The rupture in the party followed the TMC’s defeat in the 2026 West Bengal assembly elections. In June, about 60 of its 80 legislators backed Ritabrata Banerjee’s claim to the Leader of the Opposition’s post over the Mamata Banerjee camp’s nominee, Sovandeb Chattopadhyay. The rebels elected Arup Roy chairperson and announced a parallel organisational structure. In Parliament, 20 of the party’s 27 Lok Sabha members broke away.
The dispute has been before the ECI since July 2. The ECI met both camps separately on September 12, ahead of the October 6 by-polls to Nandigram and Rejinagar assembly seats.
On September 17, it found two groups each claiming to be the party, and barred both from using the name and symbol in the bypolls pending a full hearing. The Mamata Banerjee faction was then allotted the name Mamata All India Trinamool Congress and the football player symbol. The rebels got the name Democratic Trinamool Congress and the envelope symbol.
Mamata Banerjee challenged the freeze in the Supreme Court. On September 28, the court directed the ECI to settle the matter within three months.
What the camps say
After the September meeting, the Mamata Banerjee faction said the rebel legislators fought the polls on TMC tickets, using a symbol Mamata Banerjee signed. It called the rivals “a bunch of traitors”.
Abhishek Banerjee said last week that the name and symbol would stay with the Mamata Banerjee faction. “We will prove how manipulations were made in filing affidavits,” he said.
After the September hearing, Ritabrata Banerjee said, “The Election Commission is the apex body; we must have faith in it.”

title: ‘The fight is on’: Opposition targets govt over special Parliament sitting, calls it ‘assault’ on Constitution
description: The Lok Sabha and Rajya Sabha secretariats issued bulletins confirming a four-day sitting from November 30 to December 3.  | India News
author: Anita Goswami
content:
Anita Goswami is a Senior Content Producer at Hindustan Times, where she primarily covers Indian and international news. With four years of industry experience, she has led coverage of Indian General elections, Assembly elections, and national polls in the United States, Canada, Bangladesh, and Nepal. Her reporting covers global wars and major events, including Operation Sindoor, Sheikh Hasina's ouster and the Mahakumbh Mela. She verifies facts and uses clear sources to ensure accurate reporting. As former Chief Copy Editor at Storytailors, she managed teams to produce top-quality content for networks like NDTV, Profit, CNBC-TV18, Upstox and News18. Her work is featured in NDTV, Meaww, and Global Pulse. Throughout her tenure, Anita has collaborated with and been mentored by top industry experts. When not reading, Anita can be found outdoors or at a bakery. Fields of interest: Indian political history, international elections, historical policy analysis, global conflicts, cultural events, Formula 1, art, media ethics and reporting on socio-political change over time.
‘The fight is on’: Opposition targets govt over special Parliament sitting, calls it ‘assault’ on Constitution
The Lok Sabha and Rajya Sabha secretariats issued bulletins confirming a four-day sitting from November 30 to December 3.
Opposition parties have criticised the BJP-led NDA government's decision to reconvene Parliament from November 30, accusing it of violating constitutional principles.
On Thursday, the Lok Sabha and Rajya Sabha secretariats issued bulletins confirming a four-day sitting from November 30 to December 3, with the Lower House meeting first and the Upper House reconvening on December 2. This came after an earlier request by Union parliamentary affairs minister Kiren Rijiju to Speaker Om Birla and Chairman CP Radhakrishnan to reconvene the Houses.
Reacting to the development, Congress general secretary Jairam Ramesh on Thursday alleged that the government was preparing to reintroduce the Constitution amendment bill, which seeks to increase the strength of the Lok Sabha to 850 seats and facilitate the implementation of women's reservation.
Deep Dive
In a post shared on X, Ramesh said that the central government made the delimitation bills public on April 14, Ambedkar Jayanti, before the legislation failed to pass in Parliament on April 17. “Now on Constitution Day, after 105 days of Operation Lotus, the Modi government announces a special session, hoping that it will get its super-tainted two-thirds majority to pass a Constitution amendment bill,” he said.
“Can there be a greater insult to and assault on the Constitution?” Ramesh asked, adding, “The fight is on.”
Congress MP Shashi Tharoor backed Ramesh's remarks, saying the Opposition's fight was to protect democratic institutions.
"Absolutely. The fight is on -- a fight to save Indian democracy, to protect India's unity and to save our Parliament's integrity," Tharoor wrote on X.
Congress leader P Chidambaram on Friday questioned the need for a fresh women's reservation Bill, saying Parliament had already passed the Constitution (106th Amendment) Act in 2023 and that his party had supported it.
Chidambaram said the 2023 amendment had been passed by both Houses of Parliament on September 20 and 21, and that the Congress had supported its passage while demanding its immediate implementation.
"Why is the BJP government not implementing the Act? What is the need for a new Bill?" he asked.
In another post, Chidambaram said the 2023 amendment linked women's reservation to delimitation following the next Census through Article 334A. He argued that removing the article would allow the quota to be implemented immediately.
He said the Congress and other opposition parties had opposed the inclusion of Article 334A during the passage of the Bill, but the BJP had insisted on retaining it.
"All that the BJP has to do is propose to delete Article 334A. Once Article 334A is deleted, women's reservation can be implemented immediately," Chidambaram wrote on X.
Congress general secretary KC Venugopal also accused the government of attempting to undermine democratic institutions through the proposed legislation.
"They are Vote Chors. They are Seat Chors. There is no doubt that their Delimitation Bill will be nothing more than an exercise in Sansad Chori," he said.
"To orchestrate this murder of the Constitution on Constitution Day shows how badly they want to mock our precious democratic system. We will not allow this to pass. Bring it on," Venugopal added.
The BJP has rejected allegations of vote theft, maintaining that the Opposition was blaming the government and constitutional institutions for its electoral setbacks. There was no immediate reaction from the ruling party to the Opposition's fresh allegations.
Rashtriya Janata Dal (RJD) MP Manoj Kumar Jha also took a swipe at the BJP, suggesting that the ruling party may have secured the numbers required to pass the legislation.
"So, the numbers have been 'cooked' by the BJP, and apparently, they used the finest 'cookware' available!" Jha wrote on X.
BJD vice-president Prasanna Acharya said his party had expected Parliament to be reconvened, as the Monsoon Session had been adjourned without being formally prorogued.
Speaking in Bhubaneswar, Acharya said the government had not yet clarified the purpose of the upcoming sitting, but indicated that the delimitation Bill linked to women's reservation could be brought back.
"As speculated, most likely the government is going to bring the Delimitation Bill tagged with the Women's Reservation Bill again," he told ANI. Acharya added that the BJD hoped the government would address the objections raised by opposition parties. "We hope that the points which were objected to by the Opposition parties will be amicably settled and the government will change its stand," he said.
Congress MP Karti P Chidambaram, meanwhile, hinted at a possible change in the political positions of some non-NDA parties.
"Guess the BJP government has got its ducks in a row!" he wrote, tagging the official social media accounts of the BJP, DMK and NCP-SP.
The Communist Party of India (Marxist) also opposed the proposed exercise. CPI(M) MP John Brittas accused the government of using political manoeuvres to secure a majority for delimitation and warned against linking the exercise to women's reservation.
"Women's empowerment must never become a smokescreen for electoral engineering," Brittas said.
Questioning the timing of the announcement, he alleged that the proposed changes were aimed at manufacturing a parliamentary majority rather than reflecting the people's mandate.
"The essence of the Constitution is respect for the people's mandate. Govts must be formed by that mandate, legislate through it, and never subvert it," he wrote on X.
"What is being done in the name of delimitation-amalgamation, merger, acquisition, and buyout designed to manufacture a majority'is nothing short of an assault on the Constitution," he added.
Brittas further warned that the special sitting could become the "saddest chapter in the history of Indian democracy".
"A majority manufactured through political manipulation is not a mandate. It is a mockery of democracy," he said.
On X, Congress MP Tewari said the request “mocks the institution of Parliament”, while adding that it was time for the Winter Session to convene. The government had not prorogued the Monsoon Session, which concluded on August 13.
“A Special Session is a mechanism for convening during the inter-session period. It can and should not become a substitute for a regular winter session,” Tewari wrote. He added, “Why not just convene a regular winter session and the government can if the government chooses too, it can always regurgitate defeated legislation.”
Congress MP Renuka Chowdhury questioned the short duration of the upcoming sitting, saying the government had given the Rajya Sabha only two days after more than 90 days of uncertainty over Parliament's calendar.
In a post on X, she said she had written to Rajya Sabha Chairman CP Radhakrishnan on November 19 seeking clarity on the parliamentary schedule.
"Is this a substitute for the Winter Session? Parliament is not a clearance counter for the Executive. It exists to hold the Government accountable, not rubber-stamp its agenda," she wrote.
BJD leader Prasanna Acharya said the government had not clarified the agenda for the upcoming parliamentary sitting and expressed hope that it would reconsider its position on the delimitation legislation.
"We hope that the points which were objected to by the Opposition parties will be amicably settled and the government will change its stand," he told ANI.
What BJP says
Amit Shah on Thursday reiterated the government's commitment to providing 33% reservation to women, accusing the Congress of holding up its implementation.
"Women will definitely get 33% reservation; this is our resolve," Shah wrote on X.
"Congress has been blocking this. I want to tell Rahul Gandhi today that it is the resolve of the BJP and Prime Minister Narendra Modi that the women of this country will get 33% reservation," he said.
Why the Opposition is objecting
The proposed delimitation legislation seeks to increase the strength of the Lok Sabha from its current 543 elected seats to a maximum of 850. The government has linked the proposed expansion to the implementation of 33% reservation for women in the Lower House.
Parliament passed the Women's Reservation Bill in September 2023 through the Constitution (106th Amendment) Act, also known as the Nari Shakti Vandan Adhiniyam. The law provides for reserving one-third of seats for women in the Lok Sabha, state legislative assemblies and the Delhi legislative assembly, including seats reserved for women from Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes.
The reservation has not yet come into effect. Under the 2023 Act, its implementation is subject to a Census being conducted after the law's commencement and a subsequent delimitation exercise.
Earlier this year, the government introduced the Constitution (131st Amendment) Bill in the Lok Sabha. It proposed increasing the strength of the Lower House to a maximum of 850 seats and changing the existing framework to enable the implementation of women's reservation before the next Census-based delimitation.
The Bill was put to a vote the next day but failed to secure the required two-thirds majority of members present and voting.
The Opposition INDIA bloc has called for implementing the 33% reservation in the existing 543-member Lok Sabha without waiting for an expansion of seats. Opposition parties have also questioned the proposed delimitation exercise, including the use of the 2011 Census as its population reference and its potential impact on the representation of states.
The Opposition earlier also raised concerns that population-based delimitation could give northern states a larger share of Lok Sabha seats while reducing the southern states' relative representation. States such as Tamil Nadu and Kerala say they should not be disadvantaged for controlling population growth.
The government at the time rejected this concern. Amit Shah said the expansion would increase southern states' seats from 129 (out of 543) to 195 (out of 850), keeping their combined share of the Lok Sabha at around 24%. The Opposition, though, sought clarity on the formula for allocating seats.

title: Delimitation Dilemma: Can Modi Govt Deliver Women's Quota Without Triggering A North-South Battle?
description: By linking women's reservation and delimitation, the govt risks turning a reform with considerable public appeal into a constitutional confrontation over federal representation.
author: News18
content:
Delimitation Dilemma: Can Modi Govt Deliver Women's Quota Without Triggering A North-South Battle?
By linking women's reservation and delimitation, the govt risks turning a reform with considerable public appeal into a constitutional confrontation over federal representation.
Got Question about the News?
With Parliament set to reconvene from November 30, speculation is mounting that the government could revive its delimitation-linked legislation to fast-track the implementation of 33 per cent reservation for women in the Lok Sabha and state Assemblies. The official legislative agenda, however, is yet to be announced.
- ‘Power-Hungry Leadership’: PM Modi Targets Emergency-Era Govt, Recalls Article 370 On Constitution Day
- 'No Force Can Stop Women's Reservation': In Constitution Day Message, PM Modi Targets Oppn
- 'Addiction Shatters Family Dreams': PM Modi Calls For Drug-Free India
- 'An Ordinary Person Like Me...': PM Modi Says His Appeal To Buy Less Gold Helped Bring Prices Down
Read More: BJP’s Delimitation Push 2.0: DMK’s Possible Shift, Pawar’s Stand And The New Numbers Game
For the BJP, this is unfinished business. The Constitution (131st Amendment) Bill, which sought to advance women’s reservation alongside an expansion of the Lok Sabha, failed to secure the required two-thirds majority in April. Prime Minister Narendra Modi has since made it clear that his government intends to pursue the issue, accusing the Opposition of denying women their rightful representation. On the Constitution Day, in an Op-ed, he wrote, “It is imperative that the 2029 Lok Sabha elections and the Assembly elections to the various states in the coming times are conducted with women’s reservation in place."
But there is a political complication that the government cannot wish away. Women’s reservation enjoys broad political support. Delimitation does not. By linking the two, the government risks turning a reform with considerable public appeal into a constitutional confrontation over federal representation.
The anxieties in southern India are not imaginary. Tamil Nadu, Kerala, Karnataka, Andhra Pradesh and Telangana have long argued that states which successfully controlled population growth should not be penalised through a redistribution of parliamentary seats that disproportionately benefits states with higher population growth.
Former Tamil Nadu Chief Minister MK Stalin had posed a particularly pointed question during the earlier confrontation: “When the Union government urged us to control population growth, to have smaller families, and to follow family planning measures, we complied. Is this now the punishment for having done what was asked of us with discipline?"
It is a question that goes beyond party politics. It touches the basic compact of Indian federalism.
The government’s argument, meanwhile, is that expanding the strength of legislatures while maintaining states’ proportional representation can accommodate both women’s reservation and the concerns of different regions. PM Modi has also assured states that there will be no discrimination in the exercise.
But assurances are not a substitute for legislative clarity. How many additional seats will each state get? What population benchmark will be used? Will the formula protect the relative political weight of states that have controlled population growth? These are questions that require transparent answers before Parliament is asked to vote.
There is also a simpler way of looking at the impasse. The 2023 Women’s Reservation Act had already established the principle of 33 per cent reservation. Why should its implementation remain tied to a delimitation exercise that is generating such serious disagreements? Could the government and Opposition not find a way to implement the quota on the existing strength of legislatures while separately debating delimitation?
That would require political accommodation, something that has increasingly become scarce in Parliament.
For the BJP, the temptation to frame the issue as a contest between those who support women’s empowerment and those who oppose it may be considerable. But such a narrative risks obscuring the substantive disagreement. Opposition to the delimitation formula is not necessarily opposition to women’s reservation.
The government has an opportunity to demonstrate that its commitment to Nari Shakti is larger than a political confrontation. Equally, the Opposition must explain how it proposes to deliver the promised representation without indefinitely postponing implementation.
The question before Parliament is therefore not simply whether India should reserve more seats for women. That principle has already been accepted. It is whether the country can achieve that objective without unsettling the federal balance that holds its diverse regions together.
India needs more women in its legislatures. It does not need their empowerment to become another North-versus-South contest.
But sources in the NDA alliance partners suggest, should it come to this legislative business, which still remains unclear, the government will have the numbers to sail through unlike last time, without creating any north-south spat, suggesting “backchannel reaching out to southern parties", which has been in progress ever since.
Quick Answers
Southern states like Tamil Nadu, Kerala, Karnataka, Andhra Pradesh, and Telangana fear that a population-based redistribution of parliamentary seats will penalise them for successfully controlling population growth, disproportionately benefiting northern states.

title: A Southern Opening For BJP? YSRCP Backs Delimitation, DMK Weighs Support With Conditions
description: DMK and YSRCP may be approaching the proposed legislation from different political positions, but both have placed the question of regional balance at the centre of the debate
author: Apoorva Misra
content:
A Southern Opening For BJP? YSRCP Backs Delimitation, DMK Weighs Support With Conditions
DMK and YSRCP may be approaching the proposed legislation from different political positions, but both have placed the question of regional balance at the centre of the debate
Got Question about the News?
The Centre’s renewed push for delimitation drew a nuanced response from regional parties in the South on Friday. While the YSR Congress Party (YSRCP) has signalled its willingness to support the proposed legislation, the DMK, which has been among the most vocal opponents of a population-based exercise, is now indicating that it could reconsider its position if Tamil Nadu’s share of parliamentary representation is protected.
The emerging positions point to a common concern among southern parties: any expansion of the Lok Sabha must not come at the cost of their relative political representation. States such as Tamil Nadu and Kerala have argued that a delimitation exercise based on population figures could benefit states with higher population growth while disadvantaging those that have invested in population stabilisation.
- Six Decades, Two Break-Ups And A Reunion: The Evolution Of BJP-Akali Dal Alliance
- 67 Votes Short In April: How Modi Govt Plans To Turn The Tables On Delimitation-Women's Quota Bill In Parliament
- BJP, SAD Back Together After Six Years. Can The Old Allies Find Common Ground Again?
- Congress Boasts Of ‘Strong Alliance’ With Samajwadi Party After First Seat-Sharing Meeting Ends In 15 Minutes
DMK’s Conditions
The DMK’s possible change of position is significant given its earlier opposition to the exercise. Sources in the party told CNN-News18 that the leadership is willing to consider supporting the proposed Bill if the new draft clearly protects Tamil Nadu’s existing share of approximately 7.2 per cent of Lok Sabha seats. They also said the next delimitation exercise based on the latest Census should take place only after 25 years.
ALSO READ | Delimitation Dilemma: Is Rahul Gandhi Ready For The Sonia Gandhi Test?
“If the new delimitation draft bill ensures Tamil Nadu will continue to have the same percentage representation and the next delimitation based on the latest census will be carried out only after 25 years, it is a fair deal and will be beneficial for the state," the sources said.
The sources added that the DMK had opposed delimitation so far because Tamil Nadu’s representation “will be reduced when 2027 census is taken as the basis".
A Shift From DMK’s 2024 Stand
The party’s current position marks a departure from the resolution moved by then chief minister MK Stalin in the Tamil Nadu Assembly on February 14, 2024. The resolution had urged the Centre to drop the delimitation exercise planned on the basis of the first Census after 2026.
It had also called for the existing proportion of representation in Parliament and state assemblies to be retained, even if the total number of seats increased. The resolution sought to protect the ratio based on the 1971 Census.
The DMK’s willingness to consider the new proposal, therefore, appears to rest on whether the Centre is prepared to translate its assurances into safeguards in the legislation.
The Rahul Gandhi Factor
There is also a political dimension to the DMK’s possible rethink. The party is now out of power in Tamil Nadu, following the assembly elections, and its relationship with the Congress has come under strain after the latter ended its alliance with the DMK and joined the TVK-led government.
The DMK leadership, according to several media reports, is looking at maintaining an equal distance from both the BJP and the Congress, with decisions on individual issues guided by Tamil Nadu’s interests rather than automatic political alignment.
This does not amount to a move towards a BJP alliance. Instead, delimitation could become an issue on which the DMK negotiates directly with the Centre, while continuing to oppose what it sees as an erosion of states’ rights.
ALSO READ | BJP Looks To Make Inroads Into SP, NCP(SP) On Delimitation In Fresh Test For Opposition Unity
Thus, the DMK and YSRCP may be approaching the proposed legislation from different political positions, but both have placed the question of regional balance at the centre of the debate.
The government has proposed increasing the strength of the Lok Sabha from its current 543 seats to as many as 850. The exercise is also linked to the implementation of 33% reservation for women in Parliament and state assemblies, with the Centre seeking to bring it into effect before the 2029 Lok Sabha elections.
For southern states, however, the key question is not simply how many seats the Lok Sabha will have after delimitation, but how those seats will be distributed. Their concern is that states which have controlled population growth should not lose their relative political voice as a consequence.
Quick Answers
The DMK indicated it could support the proposed delimitation bill if it guarantees that Tamil Nadu retains its existing share of approximately 7.2 percent of Lok Sabha seats and ensures the next delimitation based on the latest census occurs only after 25 years.

title: All about Bhargavastra, a counter-swarm drone system tested at Pokhran by Solar Defence and Aerospace
description: Solar Defence and Aerospace Limited successfully tested Bhargavastra, India's first indigenous two-layer vehicle-mounted counter-swarm drone system, during trials at the Pokhran field firing ranges in
author: CNBCTV18.com
content:
All about Bhargavastra, a counter-swarm drone system tested at Pokhran by Solar Defence and Aerospace
- Published OnNov 27, 2026 | 08:58 IST
- Last Updated OnNov 27, 2026 | 08:59 IST
Solar Defence has successfully tested its indigenous vehicle-mounted counter-swarm drone system at Pokhran, featuring a dual-layer architecture combining air-defence rockets and autonomous micro-missiles to neutralize coordinated aerial threats. Discover how the AI-driven system integrates surveillance radar and infrared sensors to protect high-altitude terrain.
Solar Defence and Aerospace Limited (SDAL) has completed in-house development trials of Bhargavastra, an indigenous two-layer, vehicle-mounted counter-swarm drone system, at the Pokhran field firing ranges in Rajasthan.
The trials were conducted from November 20 to 24, with the system being tested against actual swarm-drone targets.
During the trials, the system detected and tracked the drones before firing rockets at them, with the rocket warheads hitting their designated points. Separate tests were also conducted to demonstrate the guidance and terminal-homing capabilities of Bhargavastra's micro-missiles.
SDAL describes Bhargavastra as India's first indigenously designed and developed two-layer vehicle-mounted counter-swarm drone system. It is designed to detect, track and engage multiple hostile drones, including coordinated drone swarms and other unmanned aerial threats.
The system uses a combination of air-defence rockets and guided micro-missiles. Its Version-I is equipped with a 64-tube launcher for unguided air-defence rockets, while Version-II uses a 64-micro-missile launcher with autonomous guidance and an infrared seeker for precision engagement. SDAL developed the guided-missile version independently beyond the original Army requirement.
Bhargavastra's detection and tracking architecture combines surveillance radars, passive radio-frequency (RF) detectors and electro-optical/infrared (EO/IR) sensors. An AI-enabled Command, Control, Communications, Computers and Intelligence (C4I) system integrates the sensor inputs, tracks targets and coordinates their engagement.
The system's radar has a reported detection range of up to 10 km, while its EO tracking system can operate at around 6 km. The vehicle-mounted platform is designed for deployment across different terrains, including high-altitude areas.
The latest Pokhran trials are a significant step in the system's development. SDAL said the system is now ready for a prototype demonstration in its deliverable configuration, with further optimisation and trials planned to improve its engagement performance and kill probability.
The programme originates from a Project Sanction Order issued by the Ministry of Defence on July 9, 2024, under the Indian Army's Make-II (Buy Indian-IDDM) category. The programme envisages one prototype set and 12 deliverable sets following a successful prototype demonstration, with a project completion date of March 31, 2027.
SDAL has said that Bhargavastra's software, rockets and guided micro-missiles were designed, developed and manufactured in India, with the company retaining the intellectual property rights for the system.
Why it matters
Drone swarms can overwhelm conventional air-defence systems by sending multiple low-cost aerial targets simultaneously. Bhargavastra's two-layer design is intended to provide a hard-kill response, using rockets to engage groups of drones and guided micro-missiles for more precise interception.
A previous statement by SDAL Chairman Satyanarayan Nuwal had described the system as being close to completing its internal trials. “This entire system is complete in itself,” Nuwal told ANI in July, adding that the company had already tested the micro-missile and other components. He had also said the radar could detect aerial threats up to 10 km and the EO system up to 6 km.

title: Delhi AQI improves to 220 but remains ‘poor’; DTU, North Campus among most polluted areas
description: DTU recorded the highest AQI at 304, putting it in the ‘very poor’ category. North Campus followed at 291, while Ghoga recorded 289, CRRI Mathura Road 288 and ITO 286. The latter four stations were in the ‘poor’ category.
author: CNBCTV18.com
content:
Delhi AQI improves to 220 but remains ‘poor’; DTU, North Campus among most polluted areas
- Edited byTenzin Norzom
- Published OnNov 27, 2026 | 07:40 IST
- Last Updated OnNov 27, 2026 | 07:40 IST
While Delhi's overall pollution levels eased slightly, educational hubs and industrial pockets continue to grapple with severe air quality as calm morning winds trap particulate matter. Check which emergency curbs remain active across the capital.
Delhi's air quality improved marginally on Friday morning but remained in the ‘poor’ category, with the overall Air Quality Index (AQI) at 220 as of 7 am.
The reading was six points lower than at the same hour on Thursday, when the AQI stood at 226. Of the city's 59 monitoring stations, 56 were reporting, with PM2.5 the leading pollutant at 44 stations.
DTU recorded the highest AQI at 304, putting it in the ‘very poor’ category. North Campus followed at 291, while Ghoga recorded 289, CRRI Mathura Road 288 and ITO 286. The latter four stations were in the ‘poor’ category.
Across the capital, 36 stations were in the ‘poor’ category, 19 in the ‘moderate’ category and one in the ‘very poor’ category, while three stations were not reporting.
The marginal improvement comes even as morning conditions remain unfavourable for the dispersion of pollutants. The Air Quality Early Warning System showed calm winds in Delhi early Friday, with wind speed at zero metres per second at 6 a.m.
The latest EWS readings also showed PM2.5 continuing to dominate at several monitoring locations, including North Campus, ITO, Pusa and JNU. The system currently classifies Delhi's air quality as ‘poor’ and lists GRAP Stage I as in force.
Despite the slight day-on-day improvement, Delhi's air remains a concern, with pollution levels at several stations still close to or above the threshold for the ‘very poor’ category.

title: Odisha Police directs 12 days' annual menstrual leave for women cops, eases duties for pregnant personnel
description: Odisha Police directed authorities to provide women personnel 12 days of annual menstrual leave, night shift exemptions for pregnant and lactating women, and dedicated well-being officers.
author: CNBCTV18.com
content:
Odisha Police directs 12 days' annual menstrual leave for women cops, eases duties for pregnant personnel
- Published OnNov 27, 2026 | 07:27 IST
- Last Updated OnNov 27, 2026 | 07:27 IST
District authorities must now ensure dedicated menstrual leave and lighter duties for pregnant personnel following recent welfare directives. The framework also introduces dedicated well-being officers and improved sanitation facilities across stations.
Odisha Police has directed district authorities to ensure women personnel receive 12 days of additional casual leave annually for menstrual discomfort, while also providing relief from night shifts and strenuous assignments for pregnant and lactating women.
The guidelines, issued by the Crime Against Women and Children (CAW & CW) Wing on November 25, have been circulated to district Superintendents of Police (SPs), Deputy Commissioners of Police (DCPs) in Bhubaneswar and Cuttack, and Railway SPs in Cuttack and Rourkela for implementation.
Under the directive, women government employees are entitled to one additional day of casual leave every month, amounting to 12 days annually, to manage menstrual discomfort. The police wing has flagged instances where women personnel in some districts were allegedly denied this benefit and asked authorities to ensure that eligible employees can avail themselves of the leave.
Women experiencing severe menstrual discomfort may also be assigned less physically demanding responsibilities, such as control room duties, wherever operational requirements permit.
The guidelines further seek to exempt pregnant and lactating women from strenuous physical assignments, prolonged standing and physically demanding law-and-order deployments. They are also to be provided reasonable nursing breaks and flexibility in duty timings to facilitate breastfeeding and childcare.
Women personnel with children below three years should, as far as practicable, be exempted from night duties, static guard assignments and duties involving prolonged travel or extended absence from headquarters.
Women Well-being Officers, better workplace facilities
As part of the grievance redressal mechanism, every district has been directed to appoint a woman officer of the rank of Deputy Superintendent of Police or Additional SP as a dedicated 'Well-being Officer' for women personnel.
A woman Sub-Inspector, Assistant Sub-Inspector or Havildar will also be attached to the Force Section in Reserve Offices to help address deployment-related concerns and communicate grievances to senior officers.
The directive also calls for separate and hygienic toilets, changing rooms and rest facilities for women personnel at police stations and other duty locations. Facilities originally meant for women but diverted for other purposes must be restored.
District police chiefs have additionally been asked to earmark at least 15 minutes during monthly 'Alochana Sabha' meetings for interactions with women personnel to discuss their concerns.
The guidelines also emphasise gender-sensitivity training for supervisory officers, timely action on sexual harassment complaints under the 2013 law, and access to professional counsellors and psychologists for personnel facing mental health challenges.
The measures come amid concerns over the working conditions and welfare of women police personnel, including demanding duty schedules, night deployments and difficulties in accessing leave and raising workplace grievances.
Odisha Police has said the measures are aimed at creating a more supportive and gender-responsive working environment for women in the force.

title: जब नितिन गडकरी ने शुभेंदु अधिकारी के साथ चखा झालमुड़ी का स्वाद, CM ने की थी व्यवस्था
description: नितिन गडकरी ने झालमुड़ी खाने का वीडियो शेयर करते हुए लिखा कि सीएम शुभेंदु अधिकारी की ओर से झालमुड़ी की व्यवस्था की गई थी. बता दें कि केंद्रीय मंत्री यहां अपने मंत्रालय से जुड़ी कई विकास परियोजनाओं का उद्घाटन-शिलान्यास करने पहुंचे थे.
author: राज मिश्रा
content:
पश्चिम बंगाल विधानसभा चुनाव के वक्त पीएम मोदी ने झालमुड़ी खाई थी. इसके बाद से बंगाल पहुंचने बीजेपी का हर बड़ा-छोटा नेता झालमुड़ी का स्वाद जरूर लेता है. इसी कड़ी में केंद्रीय सड़क परिवहन एवं राजमार्ग मंत्री नितिन गडकरी ने पूर्व मेदिनीपुर में मुख्यमंत्री सुवेंदु अधिकारी के साथ झालमुड़ी खाई. नितिन गडकरी ने खुद इससे जुड़ा वीडियो सोशल मीडिया प्लेटफॉर्म 'एक्स' पर शेयर किया है. वीडियो शेयर करते हुए केंद्रीय मंत्री ने लिखा कि पश्चिम बंगाल के कोलाघाट, पूर्व मेदिनीपुर में राष्ट्रीय राजमार्ग के कार्यक्रम के दौरान मुख्यमंत्री सुवेंदु अधिकारी ने झालमुड़ी की व्यवस्था की थी. उनके साथ झालमुड़ी का आनंद लिया. राष्ट्रीय राजमार्ग-19 पर पालसित से दानकुनी तक 63.83 किमी लंबाई के मार्ग का 6-लेन में विकास किया गया.
पश्चिम बंगाल के कोलाघाट, पूर्व मेदिनीपुर में राष्ट्रीय राजमार्ग के कार्यक्रम के दौरान मुख्यमंत्री श्री @SuvenduWB जी ने झालमुड़ी की व्यवस्था की थी। उनके साथ झालमुड़ी का आनंद लिया। #झालमुड़ी #WestBengal https://t.co/505aRIFvtU

फरक्का में एक ब्रिज का उद्घाटन किया
यह मार्ग हावड़ा, हुगली और बर्धमान क्षेत्रों के बीच संपर्क को बेहतर बनाने के साथ साथ माल वाहक परिवहन और व्यापारी गतिविधियों को गति प्रदान करेगा. यह कोलकाता को दुर्गापुर और पश्चिम बंगाल के औद्योगिक क्षेत्रों से जोड़ने वाले महत्वपूर्ण कॉरिडोर को सशक्त बनाएगा. वहीं, फरक्का में गंगा नदी पर बने नए 4-लेन पुल और उसके संपर्क मार्ग को भी राष्ट्र को समर्पित किया गया है. 521.20 करोड़ रुपए की लागत वाली यह परियोजना मुर्शिदाबाद और मालदा क्षेत्रों के बीच आवागमन को सुगम बनाने और क्षेत्रीय संपर्क को मजबूत करने में महत्वपूर्ण भूमिका निभाएगी. इससे गंगा के आर-पार यात्रा का समय घटेगा और उत्तर बंगाल की ओर संपर्क भी सुदृढ़ होगा.
कुल 20 परियोजनाओं का भूमिपूजन हुआ
इसके साथ ही पश्चिम बंगाल में सड़क और पुल बुनियादी ढांचे के विस्तार के लिए कुल 20 परियोजनाओं का भूमिपूजन किया गया. सड़क सुरक्षा योजना के तहत राष्ट्रीय राजमार्ग-12 एवं राष्ट्रीय राजमार्ग-19 पर 57 वीयूपी/एलवीयूपी के निर्माण से सुरक्षित एवं सुगम आवागमन सुनिश्चित होगा. राज्य मार्गों पर सुरक्षित सफर सुनिश्चित होगा. राष्ट्रीय राजमार्ग-116 बी पर रामनगर बाईपास के निर्माण से शहर के भीतर ट्रैफिक जाम से राहत मिलेगी. सड़क चौड़ीकरण और बाईपास के निर्माण से यात्रा के समय में कमी आएगी. ईंधन और समय की बचत होगी. सेतुबंधन योजना के अंतर्गत नोरघाट एवं द्वारकेश्वर नदी पर 2 बड़े पुलों के निर्माण से संपर्क आसान होगा. दीघा, मंदारमणि, ताजपुर एवं बक्खाली तक बेहतर संपर्क से पर्यटन और मत्स्य व्यापार में वृद्धि होगी. झारखंड सीमा (गोवाई नदी चेक पोस्ट) तक सुगम मार्ग से अंतर-राज्यीय माल ढुलाई आसान होगी और समय की बचत होगी.
75 हजार करोड़ से चमकेंगी राज्य की सड़कें
इन परियोजनाओं से यातायात दबाव घटेगा और कोलकाता, कृष्णनगर, बहरमपुर, मालदा और दुर्गापुर के बीच संपर्क बेहतर होगा. इन सभी परियोजनाओं के माध्यम से पश्चिम बंगाल में आधुनिक सड़क नेटवर्क, बेहतर पुल और सुरक्षित यातायात का विस्तार होगा. बेहतर सड़क संपर्क से उद्योगों, व्यापारिक केंद्रों, कृषि क्षेत्रों और नागरिकों को विकास के नए अवसर प्राप्त होंगे.
कार्यक्रम के दौरान 75 हजार करोड़ की नई राष्ट्रीय राजमार्ग परियोजनाओं की घोषणा की गई. इसमें 20 हजार करोड़ की लागत से दानकुनी से कोलाघाट 58 किमी 8-लेन मार्ग के निर्माण की घोषणा की. 12 हजार करोड़ की लागत से मोरेग्राम से किशनगंज 245 किमी 4-लेन हाई स्पीड कॉरिडोर के निर्माण की घोषणा की गई. सबसे महत्वपूर्ण कोलकाता के लिए 250 किमी लंबाई के और 14 हजार करोड़ रुपए की लागत वाले रिंग रोड की घोषणा की गई. इसके साथ मार्ग चौड़ीकरण परियोजनाओं का भी ऐलान किया गया.

title: तमिलनाडु में होगा खेला, DMK बदलने जा रही पाला! BJP से दोस्ती की बढ़ी अटकलें, TVK के आरोप से सियासी भूचाल
description: तमिलनाडु के सीएम जोसेफ विजय की पार्टी टीवीके ने डीएमके पर एक बड़ा आरोप लगाया है. टीवीके का दावा है कि इतिहास खुद को दोहराने जा रहा है और डीएमके बीजेपी का साथ देने जा रही है.
author: अभिनव त्रिपाठी
content:
केंद्र सरकार ने 30 नवंबर से संसद का विशेष सत्र बुलाया है. 30 नवंबर को लोकसभा की बैठक होगी और 2 दिसंबर को राज्यसभा की बैठक प्रस्तावित है. सरकार की ओर से बुलाए गए संसद से विशेष सत्र के बाद महिला आरक्षण और परिसीमन अध्यादेश को लेकर चर्चा तेज है. इस बीच तमिलनाडु के सीएम विजय की पार्टी ने ऐसा दावा किया है, जिसने नई सियासी चर्चा छेड़ दी है.
दरअसल, मुख्यमंत्री विजय की पार्टी TVK ने दावा किया कि तमिलनाडु में DMK, BJP के साथ हाथ मिलाने की तैयारी कर रही है. यह दावा ऐसे समय पर किया गया है, जब माना जा रहा है कि परिसीमन बिल को पास कराने के लिए सरकार ने जरूरी आंकड़े को पूरा कर लिया है. हालांकि, डीएमके की ओर से इन आरोपों को खारिज किया गया. सूत्र बताते हैं कि DMK नेता जल्द ही परिसीमन के मुद्दे पर चर्चा करने के लिए बैठक करेंगे.
हाल में ही विपक्ष के नेता उदयनिधि स्टालिन ने तमिलनाडु के राज्यपाल राजेंद्र विश्वनाथ अर्लेकर से मुलाकात की थी. इस मुलाकात को TVK ने कथित राजनीतिक बदलाव करार दिया. हालांकि, डीएमके ने इस मुलाकात का बचाव किया है. दरअसल, तमिलनाडु में यह राजनीतिक बयानबाजी उस वक्त शुरू हुई, जब DMK के मुखपत्र 'मुरासोली' में BJP के प्रदेश अध्यक्ष नैनार नागेंद्रन के बारे में एक रिपोर्ट छपी.
हालांकि, DMK के प्रवक्ता सैयद हफीजुल्लाह ने कहा कि डीएमके किसी भी स्थिति में BJP के साथ गठबंधन नहीं करेगी. इसके साथ ही उन्होंने 'मुरासोली' की रिपोर्ट को लेकर TVK के दावे को भी खारिज कर दिया. डीएमके प्रवक्ता की ओर से कहा गया कि इसमें नागेंद्रन का कोई विस्तृत साक्षात्कार नहीं छपा था. यह केवल BJP नेता की ओर से सत्ताधारी TVK पर लगाए गए आरोपों पर आधारित एक समाचार रिपोर्ट है.
इस बीच टीवीके के आईटी विंग ने सोशल मीडिया पर एक पोस्ट किया और पूर्व मुख्यमंत्री CN अन्नादुरई के एक मशहूर सवाल का जिक्र करते हुए कहा कि बकरी के लिए दाढ़ी और देश के लिए राज्यपाल का क्या काम? इसी पोस्ट में आरोप लगाया गया कि एक समय पर राज्यपाल को विधानसभा में संबोधन न करने देने पर गर्व करने वाली डीएमके अब उनके चरणों में झुकने को तैयार है.
सबसे खास है कि इस पोस्ट में 'मुरासोली' में छपी रिपोर्ट का भी जिक्र किया गया है, जिसमें कहा जा रहा है कि डीएमके अब बीजेपी की मदद के लिए काम कर रही है. टीवीके ने यहां तक कह दिया कि इतिहास खुद को दोहराने जा रहा है. एनडीटीवी की एक रिपोर्ट के अनुसार, उदयनिधि स्टालिन और राज्यपाल की मुलाकात पर डीएमके ने कहा कि वर्तमान व्यवस्था के तहत राज्य सरकार के खिलाफ शिकायत दर्ज कराने के लिए विपक्ष को राज्यपाल के पास जाना ही पड़ता है.
एक सवाल के जवाब में डीएमके प्रवक्ता ने कहा कि परिसीमन पर पार्टी का रुख साफ है. तमिलनाडु की मौजूदा 7.2 प्रतिशत सीटों की हिस्सेदारी किसी भी स्थिति में सुरक्षित रहनी चाहिए. वहीं, जब उनसे पूछा गया कि क्या संसद में प्रतिनिधित्व की मांग पूरी होने पर DMK, BJP का समर्थन करेगी, तो हफीजुल्लाह ने इस पर कोई स्पष्ट जवाब नहीं दिया. बता दें कि संसद में सीटों के बढ़ने की स्थिति में अपनी सीटों की हिस्सेदारी बचाए रखना दक्षिणी राज्यों की प्रमुख चिंता रही है.

title: 67 वोट से मात, अब पलटवार की बिसात! 224 दिन बाद फिर मचेगा परिसीमन पर घमासान, सियासी शतरंज पर कैसे निकलेगी विपक्षी दांव की काट?
description: नरेंद्र मोदी सरकार ने 30 नवंबर को लोकसभा और 2 दिसंबर को राज्यसभा का विशेष सत्र बुलाया है. माना जा रहा है कि जो संविधान संशोधन विधेयक अप्रैल के महीने में गिर गया था, अब उसे पास कराने की पूरी तैयारी सरकार ने कर ली है.
author: रचित कुमार
content:
30 नवंबर को लोकसभा और 2 दिसंबर को राज्यसभा की कार्यवाही शुरू होगी, जो 3 दिसंबर तक चलेगी. इस दौरान नरेंद्र मोदी सरकार के सामने 'फ्लोर-मैनेजमेंट' की एक बड़ी परीक्षा होगी, ताकि जो काम अप्रैल में पूरा नहीं हो पाया था, वो अब हो सके. 17 अप्रैल 2026 को, 'संविधान (131वां संशोधन) विधेयक' लोकसभा में गिर गया था. इस बिल का मकसद लोकसभा की अधिकतम सदस्य संख्या को 550 से बढ़ाकर 850 करना और 2029 के चुनावों से पहले महिलाओं के लिए 33 प्रतिशत आरक्षण लागू करना था.
उस समय, नेशनल डेमोक्रेटिक अलायंस (NDA) के पास 293 सांसद थे. सदन में मौजूद और मतदान करने वाले 528 सदस्यों में से 298 ने विधेयक के पक्ष में और 230 ने विरोध में वोट दिया. यह उस रात के 352 वोटों के लक्ष्य से 54 वोट कम था, और सदन की पूरी क्षमता के हिसाब से जरूरी संख्या से लगभग 67 वोट कम था.
केंद्रीय संसदीय कार्य मंत्री किरेन रिजिजू ने इस सत्र की घोषणा तो की, लेकिन इसके एजेंडे के बारे में कोई जानकारी नहीं दी. राष्ट्रपति द्रौपदी मुर्मू ने अभी तक संसद के मॉनसून सत्र को औपचारिक रूप से खत्म नहीं किया है, जबकि सत्र की बैठकें खत्म हुए 105 दिन बीत चुके हैं, जो एक रिकॉर्ड है. इसका मतलब यह है कि सरकार मौजूदा सत्र के भीतर ही कम से कम दो दिन के नोटिस पर एक विशेष बैठक बुला सकती है. वहीं, एक नया सत्र बुलाने के लिए कम से कम 14 दिन के नोटिस की जरूरत होती है.
संविधान के अनुच्छेद 368 के तहत, किसी भी संवैधानिक संशोधन विधेयक को दोनों सदनों में दो शर्तें पूरी करनी होती हैं: कुल सदस्य संख्या का साधारण बहुमत, और सदन में मौजूद व मतदान करने वाले सदस्यों का दो-तिहाई बहुमत. 540 से 543 सदस्यों वाली पूरी क्षमता की लोकसभा में, यह 'दो-तिहाई' का जादुई आंकड़ा लगभग 360 से 362 वोटों का होता है. इसका मतलब यह है कि जब भी विपक्ष पूरी ताकत के साथ सदन में मौजूद होता है, तो 293 सांसदों वाले NDA को लगभग 67 वोटों की कमी का सामना करना पड़ता है.
माना जा रहा है कि बीजेपी के नेतृत्व वाले एनडीए के पास पक्के तौर पर 319 सदस्य हैं, जिनमें से 241 बीजेपी से हैं. इस संख्या में तृणमूल कांग्रेस का 20 सदस्यों वाला एक अलग हुआ गुट भी शामिल है. इसके अलावा, इस हफ्ते पंजाब के शिरोमणि अकाली दल का एक सांसद भी इसमें शामिल हो गया है. इस दल ने राज्य में होने वाले चुनावों से पहले बीजेपी के साथ अपना गठबंधन फिर से बहाल कर लिया है. NCP(SP) के आठ सांसदों को मिलाकर कुल संख्या 328 हो जाएगी.
इसके बाद एंट्री होती है डीएमके की. इसके 22 सांसदों के साथ NDA की संख्या 351 तक पहुंच जाएगी, जो कि लक्ष्य से लगभग 10 कम है, लेकिन काफी करीब है. इस साल की शुरुआत में तमिलनाडु में कांग्रेस के विजय की पार्टी TVK के साथ गठबंधन करने के बाद, DMK ने 'इंडिया' (INDIA) गठबंधन छोड़ दिया था. पार्टी इस मुद्दे पर अपने सांसदों की एक बैठक बुलाने की योजना बना रही है; क्योंकि अगर सभी राज्यों में एक समान 50 प्रतिशत की बढ़ोतरी की जाती है, तो 'उत्तर-दक्षिण असंतुलन' वाली उनकी मुख्य चिंता का समाधान हो सकता है.
इसके उलट, राज्यसभा में यह चुनौती काफी छोटी है. 245 सदस्यों वाले उच्च सदन में NDA के पास लगभग 141 सीटें हैं, जबकि दो-तिहाई बहुमत के लिए लगभग 163 सीटों की जरूरत होती है. ऐसे में, NDA को केवल 22 और वोटों की जरूरत है, और अगर कुछ क्षेत्रीय दल वोटिंग प्रक्रिया से दूर रहते हैं, तो यह संख्या और भी कम हो सकती है. संसद से पास होने के बाद, इस संशोधन को भारत की कम से कम आधी राज्य विधानसभाओं से भी मंजूरी मिलनी चाहिए, जहां NDA के पास पहले से ही मजबूत बहुमत है.
लोकसभा में 67 वोटों के अंतर को पाटने के लिए, सरकार के रणनीतिकारों के पास दो रास्ते हैं. पहला रास्ता है 'क्रॉस-वोटिंग' का, जिसके लिए विपक्ष के लगभग 70 सांसदों को अपनी पार्टी के व्हिप (आदेश) के खिलाफ जाकर समर्थन में वोट देने के लिए मनाना होगा. दसवीं अनुसूची के तहत दलबदल विरोधी कड़े नियमों को देखते हुए, यह एक बहुत मुश्किल काम है.
दूसरा और कहीं ज्यादा व्यावहारिक रास्ता है यानी 'रणनीतिक रूप से वोटिंग से दूर रहना'. चूंकि, अनुच्छेद 368 के तहत दो-तिहाई बहुमत की शर्त केवल 'मौजूद और वोट देने वाले' सदस्यों पर लागू होती है, इसलिए विपक्ष के सदस्यों का सदन से बाहर चले जाना (वॉकआउट) जीत के लिए जरूरी संख्या को कम कर देता है. अगर वोटिंग शुरू होने से पहले विपक्ष के लगभग 100 सांसद सदन से बाहर चले जाते हैं या वोटिंग में हिस्सा नहीं लेते हैं, तो वोट देने वालों की कुल संख्या घटकर लगभग 440 रह जाएगी. ऐसे में, दो-तिहाई बहुमत के लिए जरूरी संख्या भी घटकर 293 हो जाएगी, जो कि ठीक NDA की अपनी मौजूदा ताकत के बराबर है.
सरकार के विधेयक के तहत लोकसभा में सीटों की संख्या बढ़कर 850 हो जाएगी, जिनमें से लगभग 283 सीटें महिलाओं के लिए रोटेशन के आधार पर आरक्षित होंगी. साथ ही, इस विधेयक में एक ऐसा आयोग गठित करने का प्रावधान भी है, जो चुनाव क्षेत्रों की सीमाओं का पुनर्निर्धारण करेगा.
इस आशंका के चलते कि सीमाओं के पुनर्निर्धारण से अधिक आबादी वाले उत्तर भारत को आनुपातिक रूप से ज्यादा सीटें मिल सकती हैं. अमित शाह ने अप्रैल में कहा था कि सरकार सभी राज्यों में समान रूप से 50 प्रतिशत सीटों की बढ़ोतरी पर सहमत हो सकती है. हालांकि, संबंधित विधेयक के मूल पाठ में यह बात शामिल नहीं थी. अब यह देखना बाकी है कि क्या इस बार इसे विधेयक में शामिल किया जाएगा या नहीं.
अप्रैल में, INDIA गठबंधन ने एकजुट होकर मांग की थी कि महिलाओं के लिए 33 फीसदी आरक्षण को मौजूदा 543 सीटों में ही तुरंत लागू किया जाए, और इसे जनसंख्या के आधार पर होने वाले परिसीमन (सीटों के पुनर्निर्धारण) से न जोड़ा जाए. हालांकि, 30 नवंबर से पहले विपक्षी खेमे में नए राजनीतिक मतभेद उभर कर सामने आए हैं.
जहां कांग्रेस, समाजवादी पार्टी, तृणमूल कांग्रेस और वामपंथी दल इस मांग पर कायम हैं कि सदन में सीटों की संख्या 543 ही रहे और राज्यों के कोटे में बदलाव किए बिना आरक्षण लागू किया जाए, वहीं RJD सांसद मनोज झा ने केंद्र सरकार पर आरोप लगाया है कि वह महिला आरक्षण का इस्तेमाल निर्वाचन क्षेत्रों के स्वरूप को बदलने के लिए एक बहाने के तौर पर कर रही है. इसी तरह, DMK ने भी सार्वजनिक रूप से मौजूदा सीट संख्या को बनाए रखने का समर्थन किया है.
हालांकि, राजनीतिक गलियारों में इस बात पर काफी चर्चा है कि क्या दक्षिणी और क्षेत्रीय दल (जैसे RJD और यहां तक कि AAP) अपना रुख बदल सकते हैं, अगर राज्यों के कोटे को सुरक्षित रखने के लिए लिखित गारंटी दी जाती है. सबसे खास बात यह है कि इस हफ्ते नेशनलिस्ट कांग्रेस पार्टी (SP) की सांसद सुप्रिया सुले ने विपक्ष की सख्त लकीर से हटकर एक अलग रुख अपनाया. उन्होंने सांसदों से अपील की कि वे इस बिल को पहले पेश होने दें, क्योंकि राष्ट्रीय हित सबसे ऊपर है. कांग्रेस प्रमुख हर्षवर्धन सपकाल ने इस पर प्रतिक्रिया देते हुए कहा,'यह परिसीमन राष्ट्र-विरोधी है, देश के खिलाफ है और देश के लिए विनाशकारी है... सिर्फ कांग्रेस ही नहीं, बल्कि पूरा 'इंडिया' गठबंधन इस विधेयक का विरोध कर रहा है.'
साथ ही, उन्होंने यह भी संकेत दिया कि अगर जनसंख्या के आधार पर सीटों के रीडिस्ट्रिब्यूशन के बजाय सभी राज्यों में एक समान 50 प्रतिशत सीटों की बढ़ोतरी की जाती है, तो वे इस पर विचार करने के लिए तैयार हैं. YSRCP जैसे किसी भी तटस्थ दल की ओर से अगर वोटिंग से दूर रहने या अपना रुख बदलने जैसा कोई कदम उठाया जाता है, तो सरकार को वह जरूरी गणित मिल सकता है, जो उसे अप्रैल में नहीं मिल पाया था.

title: New Delimitation Bill May Propose 50% Seat Increase For All States, Specify State-Wise Allocation: Sources
description: The proposed Delimitation Bill may provide for a uniform 50% increase in Lok Sabha seats across states, with state-wise allocations specified in the legislation, sources said.
author: Shruti Sneha
content:
New Delimitation Bill May Propose 50% Seat Increase For All States, Specify State-Wise Allocation: Sources
The proposed Delimitation Bill may provide for a uniform 50% increase in Lok Sabha seats across states, with state-wise allocations specified in the legislation, sources said.
- India News
- 1 min read
New Delhi: The Centre is likely to delink delimitation from the Census and increase the number of Lok Sabha seats in every state uniformly by 50%, sources said.
The proposed Delimitation Bill is expected to provide for a 50% pro-rata increase in seats for each state. It will also specify the revised number of seats allocated to every state, bringing greater clarity to the distribution.
The Bill is also expected to address concerns raised by states over transparency in the delimitation exercise.

title: Delhi AQI Remains 'Poor' At 220, Wazirpur Most Polluted; CAQM Sets 2027 Clean Air Targets
description: Delhi recorded an AQI of 220 on Friday, remaining in the 'Poor' category. Wazirpur topped the pollution chart at 273 as CAQM set a 15-20% pollution reduction target for 2027.
author: Asian News International
content:
Delhi AQI Remains 'Poor' At 220, Wazirpur Most Polluted; CAQM Sets 2027 Clean Air Targets
Delhi recorded an AQI of 220 on Friday, remaining in the 'Poor' category. Wazirpur topped the pollution chart at 273 as CAQM set a 15-20% pollution reduction target for 2027.
- India News
- 3 min read
New Delhi: Delhi's air quality remained in the ‘Poor’ category on Friday, with the overall Air Quality Index (AQI) recorded at 220 at 8 am, according to the Central Pollution Control Board (CPCB).
Among the listed monitoring stations, Wazirpur recorded the highest AQI at 273, falling in the ‘Poor’ category, followed by Bawana at 266, Punjabi Bagh at 260 and Chandni Chowk at 257. IGI Airport (T3) registered an AQI of 289, while ITO recorded 285, both in the ‘Poor’ category.
Other locations reporting ‘Poor’ air quality included IIT Delhi at 242, Anand Vihar and Narela at 239 each, Rohini at 233, Mundka at 231, Vivek Vihar at 222, Ashok Vihar at 221 and RK Puram at 220. Sonia Vihar recorded an AQI of 217, while Dwarka Sector 8 and Okhla Phase 2 registered 207 and 203, respectively.
In the ‘Moderate’ category, Uttam Nagar recorded an AQI of 193, followed by Vasundhara Enclave at 181. In contrast, Major Dhyan Chand National Stadium recorded an AQI of 125, the lowest among the listed monitoring stations.
Advertisement
According to the CPCB classification, an AQI between 0 and 50 is considered 'good', 51-100 'satisfactory', 101-200 'moderate', 201-300 'poor', 301-400 'very poor ', and 401-500 'severe'.
Meanwhile, the Supreme Court on Monday indicated that it may consider restricting vehicles operating in Delhi-National Capital Region (NCR) to those complying with Bharat Stage-VI (BS-VI) emission norms as part of measures to combat worsening air pollution in the region.
Advertisement
A Bench comprising Chief Justice of India Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana observed while hearing a matter concerning air pollution in the national capital.
"We are clear we will allow only BS-VI vehicles in Delhi, if not NCR," the Bench remarked.
The Bench also suggested an alternative arrangement for the supply of essential commodities, proposing the establishment of warehouses at Delhi's borders where goods could be unloaded and subsequently transported into the city using smaller battery-operated or other non-polluting vehicles.
Separately, the Commission for Air Quality Management (CAQM) has introduced district-level action plans, setting a mandatory minimum target of 15 per cent reduction, with the potential to reach 20 per cent, in annual average air pollution levels across Delhi-NCR for 2027. The Commission has written to the governments of Delhi and other NCR states, calling for comprehensive Annual Action Plans for 2027 at the State, District and Municipal Corporation levels.
The plans aim to shift the focus from listing pollution-control activities to achieving measurable outcomes through defined targets, timelines, monitoring parameters and ground-level accountability.
Earlier, CAQM began assessing and ranking Delhi and neighbouring states on their performance in implementing pollution-control measures. Its 2026 report card, covering progress up to October, highlighted gaps in several areas, including industrial inspections, waste management, public transport and pollution-monitoring infrastructure.
According to the report card, none of the four states and Delhi had established the targeted number of green crematoriums. Against a combined target of 421 across Delhi, Haryana, Rajasthan and Uttar Pradesh, the achievement stood at zero as of October 31.

title: Modi Govt's Big Numbers Game: Can Opposition Walkouts Help Pass Women's Quota, Delimitation Bill In Parliament?
description: As Parliament reconvenes on November 30, the Modi government faces a numbers test to revive its Constitution Amendment Bill on women's reservation and delimitation after its April defeat.
author: Shruti Sneha
content:
Modi Govt's Big Numbers Game: Can Opposition Walkouts Help Pass Women's Quota, Delimitation Bill In Parliament?
As Parliament reconvenes on November 30, the Modi government faces a numbers test to revive its Constitution Amendment Bill on women's reservation and delimitation after its April defeat.
- India News
- 5 min read
New Delhi: Can the Narendra Modi government succeed in passing a crucial Constitution Amendment Bill without winning over the Opposition? That is the big question ahead of Parliament's upcoming sitting, with the government facing a difficult numbers game after its proposed legislation on women's reservation and delimitation suffered a rare defeat in April.
Parliament will reconvene on November 30, with the Rajya Sabha scheduled to meet from December 2. The four-day sitting, which will continue until December 3, is expected to put the government's floor-management skills to the test as it looks to revive the Constitution (131st Amendment) Bill.
The legislation, which proposed increasing the maximum strength of the Lok Sabha from 550 to 850 seats and facilitating 33 per cent reservation for women ahead of the 2029 Lok Sabha elections, failed to secure the required majority on April 17, 2026.
Despite the NDA having 293 MPs, the Bill received 298 votes in favour and 230 against, with 528 members participating in the division. It fell 54 votes short of the 352 required among members present and voting that night. The government was also facing a gap of around 67 votes against a full-strength House.
Advertisement
Union Parliamentary Affairs Minister Kiren Rijiju announced the dates of the upcoming sitting but did not disclose the agenda.
Interestingly, the Monsoon Session has not yet been formally prorogued by President Droupadi Murmu, even though Parliament's sittings concluded 105 days ago. This allows the government to reconvene Parliament within the existing session by giving a minimum notice of two days. Calling an entirely new session would require at least 14 days' notice.
Advertisement
Can Opposition Walkouts Help The Government Cross The Majority Mark?
The government's biggest challenge is the special majority required to pass a constitutional amendment. Under Article 368, such a Bill must secure a majority of the total membership of each House as well as the support of at least two-thirds of members present and voting.
In a Lok Sabha with 540 to 543 members, the two-thirds requirement could range between 360 and 362 votes if the entire House participates in the division. With 293 MPs, the NDA remains considerably short of that figure.
However, the government may have another way to improve its chances: Opposition abstentions.
Unlike an ordinary majority, the two-thirds requirement under Article 368 is calculated on the basis of members present and voting, not the entire strength of the House. This means that if a significant number of Opposition MPs abstain or walk out before voting, the number of votes required to pass the Bill would come down.
For instance, if around 100 Opposition MPs stay away and the voting pool falls to approximately 440, the two-thirds mark would drop to 294 votes. The NDA's existing strength of 293 would leave it just one vote short, making even limited support from outside the alliance potentially significant.
The other option would be to secure direct support from Opposition MPs. But convincing nearly 70 lawmakers to vote against their parties' positions would be difficult, particularly given the anti-defection provisions under the Tenth Schedule.
The Rajya Sabha presents a relatively smaller numerical challenge. With the NDA holding around 141 seats in the 245-member Upper House, it would need approximately 22 additional votes to reach the two-thirds mark of 163 if the entire House participates. The number could fall if some regional parties choose not to participate.
The amendment would also need ratification by at least half of the state legislatures after being passed by Parliament. The NDA is considered to have a comfortable position in this stage of the process.
Will The INDI Bloc Remain United This Time?
The Opposition's position on the Bill remains an important factor in the government's calculations. During the April vote, INDI bloc parties largely stood together, opposing the proposed changes and demanding that the 33 per cent women's quota be implemented within the existing 543 Lok Sabha seats.
The Congress, Samajwadi Party, Trinamool Congress and Left parties have maintained their opposition to increasing the House's strength through a delimitation exercise that could alter the representation of states. The DMK has also backed retaining the existing seat cap.
RJD MP Manoj Jha has raised concerns about the government's approach, accusing the Centre of using women's reservation as a reason to change the character of constituencies.
However, the Opposition may not be as politically united ahead of the November sitting. NCP (SP) MP Supriya Sule has taken a different position, urging lawmakers to allow the Bill to be introduced before deciding their response. She has also indicated openness to a proposal under which every state receives a uniform 50 per cent increase in seats instead of population-based redistribution.
Her position could become significant if the government offers written safeguards to address concerns over the representation of states. Regional parties, including the YSRCP, could also influence the final arithmetic through their voting decisions.
With the NDA short of the numbers required for a constitutional amendment, the government faces two political challenges: securing additional support and preventing the Opposition from maintaining the same unity it displayed in April.
The November 30 sitting, therefore, could become more than another parliamentary session. It will test whether the government can find a way around the numbers that brought down its ambitious legislation just months ago.
