title: Infosys Prize: Where Does India Stand in Research?
description: The Infosys Prize archive shows a shift towards overseas institutions. Research funding, elite laboratories and unequal academic opportunities shape India's scientific landscape.
author: N.V. Geetha
content:
On November 12, the Infosys Science Foundation announced six winners of the Infosys Prize 2026, recognising research in constitutional law, quantum simulation, wireless networks, oxygen biology, climate change and business cycles, and probability theory. Its awards have honoured scholars such as Abhijit Banerjee, Esther Duflo, Manjul Bhargava, and Akshay Venkatesh before they went on to win the Nobel Prize or the Fields Medal.
The announcement offers an opportunity to examine the changing geography of the prize and the limits of what its laureate records can tell us about Indian research institutions.
Before 2024, the age ceiling was generally 50, subject to exceptions under the earlier rules. In May 2024, the foundation reduced it to 40, without specifying any age relaxation in the revised rules, shifting the prize from mid-career recognition to early-career achievement and potential. A separate category for economics has been introduced, and humanities has been merged with social sciences. The new rules also require winners from outside India to spend 30 days at an institution in India in the next calendar year, to connect with students and researchers there.
The archive contains 110 laureate entries for 2008-2026, classified by each winner’s institutional affiliation at the time of the award. After correcting historical affiliations, 65 of 92 winners (71 per cent) in 2008-2023 were affiliated with Indian institutions. In 2024-2026, the comparable count is 5 of 18 (28 per cent), classifying Gautam Bhatia under his award-time appointment at the University of New South Wales (UNSW). Counting his continuing Jindal Global Law School affiliation instead would make it 6 of 18. These figures describe where the winners worked, rather than their nationality or the quality of those institutions.
There is an added complication. A public laureate archive may list an appointment a scholar took up after receiving the award. Raghuram Rajan’s 2011 entry on the Infosys Science Foundation website displays his later appointment as Chief Economic Adviser to the government of India, which he took up in 2012. When he won the prize in 2011, he was a professor at the University of Chicago. Similarly, Kalyanmoy Deb’s entry lists Michigan State University, but his Infosys biography says he moved there in 2013, after winning his 2011 prize while at IIT Kanpur.
The Rajan and Deb corrections offset each other in the India-versus-overseas total. A third correction concerns Sriram Ramaswamy, who won in 2011 while a professor at the Indian Institute of Science (IISc). He became director of the Tata Institute of Fundamental Research (TIFR) Centre for Interdisciplinary Sciences in July 2012. Assigning his award to IISc reduces the TIFR network’s total by one without changing India’s overall count. The comparisons therefore use the institution at the time of each award.
Despite these caveats, most winners in the past three prize years are affiliated with institutions abroad. In both 2024 and 2025, only two of the six winners each year were affiliated with institutions in India. For 2026, the main classification records one India-affiliated winner among six. The Infosys Science Foundation identifies Bhatia as Green Fellow at UNSW, so he is counted under Australia, while his adjunct appointment at Jindal Global Law School in India is acknowledged as an alternative affiliation.
The disciplines are different
The geographical distribution of prize winners also differs considerably by discipline. Across 2008-2026, 17 of 18 life sciences winners were affiliated with Indian institutions, compared with 14 of 18 in physical sciences and 13 of 17 in engineering and computer science, after the historical corrections. In mathematical sciences, 9 of 19 winners were affiliated with Indian institutions. Of the 38 winners in the combined humanities, social sciences, and economics grouping, 17 were affiliated with Indian institutions after the Rajan correction and Bhatia’s UNSW classification.
Before 2024, 14 of 15 physical sciences winners and 13 of 14 engineering and computer science winners were India-affiliated; in 2024-2026, neither field had an India-affiliated winner among the 3. Humanities, social sciences, and economics went from 17 of 32 to none of 6, while mathematical sciences rose from 6 of 16 to 3 of 3. Life sciences fell from 15 of 15 to 2 of 3. These recent samples are small and coincide with changes in eligibility and categories, so the figures do not establish what caused the shift.
The proportion in life sciences is the highest among the disciplines. Eleven of the 17 winners affiliated with institutions in India came from two major research networks: TIFR, including the National Centre for Biological Sciences, and the Centre for Cellular and Molecular Biology. These institutions have developed specialised facilities and research programmes over several decades. Their prominence in the list suggests that sustained institutional support can enable internationally recognised research within India.
The concentration extends across disciplines. The TIFR network accounts for 17 laureates across the prize archive, while the IITs, IISc, Council of Scientific and Industrial Research institutions, and the Indian Statistical Institute also appear repeatedly. This concentration merits investigation into research funding and institutional conditions across the wider university system, using evidence beyond prize records.
The concentration also has a historical context. Itty Abraham traced the divide between research and teaching to post-Independence choices favouring well-funded specialised laboratories outside universities (“The Two Faces of India’s New Science and Tech Policy”, The Wire Science, May 17, 2021). Shiv Visvanathan criticised the bureaucratisation of Indian science and called for universities to be freed from narrow specialisation so they could pursue more fundamental questions (“What India needs to transform to outthink the West”, The New Indian Express, December 10, 2024). These arguments provide context for assessing research institutions, although the prize records themselves measure affiliations rather than funding, facilities, or career security.
India’s research profile
But the evidence goes beyond the prize to a more general picture. In the Nature Index covering July 1, 2025 to June 30, 2026, India ranked eighth overall by fractional research output across 178 selected publications, comprising 177 journals and one conference. The index expanded from 145 to 178 publications in June 2026, adding journals in applied and social sciences and one conference, while also revising its subject-classification methodology. The index divides credit for each paper among its authors and institutions, then sums each country’s contribution.
India ranked fifth in chemistry, sixth in the broader natural sciences category, eighth in physical sciences, 13th in biological sciences, and 16th in health sciences and social sciences. The subject-level differences place India’s life sciences performance in a broader context.
Indian students have a very visible presence in international academic mobility. A 2023 study by Prithwiraj Choudhury, Ina Ganguli, and Patrick Gaulé on general-category candidates who took the IIT Joint Entrance Examination in 2010 found that, by 2018, 36 per cent of the top 1,000 scorers and 62 per cent of the top 100 scorers had moved abroad for further study or work after graduation. Their analysis points to elite-college credentials and alumni networks as drivers of migration. The findings describe the migration patterns of this specific cohort of high-scoring students.
Maintaining research connections
A researcher joining a foreign university can continue to supervise Indian students, work with Indian colleagues, and contribute to local institutions. Return migration can also transfer research practices and international links. Assessing laboratories, recruitment, research careers, and public funding would require evidence beyond the laureates’ institutional locations.
The Infosys Prize archive shows a pronounced change in winners’ geographical affiliations after the 2024 eligibility reforms, with different patterns across disciplines. It establishes where recognised researchers worked when they received the prize, while a fuller assessment of Indian universities calls for separate evidence on funding, facilities, and academic careers. The foundation’s residency requirement may encourage collaboration with institutions in India, and its impact can be assessed as those connections develop.
N.V. Geetha is a former Senior Technical Director at the National Informatics Centre. She writes data-based stories.

title: ICJ Verdict on Rohingya Genocide and Its Global Impact
description: The ICJ holds Myanmar responsible for genocide against the Rohingya, raising questions about international accountability, refugee rights and India's laws.
author: V. Venkatesan
content:
On November 19, the International Court of Justice (ICJ) held Myanmar responsible for genocide against the Rohingya, a predominantly Muslim community subjected to a military campaign in 2017 that drove hundreds of thousands of people into Bangladesh. It is the first time the court has found a state responsible for committing genocide. Myanmar had defended the operations as a response to armed insurgency, while the case before the court concerned the intent behind the violence.
A nine-judge majority inferred an intent to destroy a substantial part of the Rohingya population from the conduct of the security forces in 2017. Six judges drew a different conclusion from the same record.
The ruling departs from the outcome of two earlier cases involving Serbia. In the Bosnia and Herzegovina case (2007), the court established that genocide occurred at Srebrenica and held Serbia responsible for failing to prevent and punish it. In the Croatia case (2015), it rejected genocide claims advanced by both Croatia and Serbia. Neither judgment attributed the commission of genocide to the respondent state.
Article II of the Genocide Convention couples particular acts with a purpose: the destruction, in whole or in part, of a protected national, ethnic, racial, or religious group. Proof of grave violence establishes only part of what the court must find. The question in the Myanmar case was whether the acts also showed an intent to destroy the Rohingya.
The case offered no direct written order laying out an extermination policy. Instead, the majority examined the choice of victims, the repeated methods of attack, the conditions preceding the operation, and the conduct of troops towards people already fleeing.
The legal test was familiar from the court’s earlier cases. Where intent is inferred from surrounding circumstances, it must be the “only reasonable inference” from the evidence considered together. The dispute was over its application to the facts in northern Rakhine.
Myanmar relied on attacks by the Arakan Rohingya Salvation Army to explain the operations and also raised punishment or forcible displacement as possible objectives. The majority tested each explanation against the pattern of conduct recorded in individual villages and along routes out of Myanmar.
According to the majority, Myanmar’s operations did not separate civilians from alleged insurgents. The judges also considered attacks on children, gang rapes, executions, burned villages, and attacks on people fleeing the military.
In paragraph 453, the majority held that these features were “not consistent with an intent to conduct counter-insurgency operations”.
A further problem arose with Myanmar’s explanation for the displacement. If the aim was simply to force people out, the judges asked, why were civilians assaulted or killed while attempting to leave? The court also considered blocked crossings and landmines near escape routes, recognising that forcible displacement and genocide can occur together (paragraphs 455 to 462).
The majority concluded that counter-insurgency, expulsion, and punishment failed to explain the full evidentiary record. The finding of genocidal intent followed from the cumulative force of the evidence, not from any isolated incident.
The court situated the 2017 operations within earlier policies governing Rohingya citizenship, movement, marriage, and family life. That history supplied context for judging whether the soldiers’ actions reflected a broader purpose.
The historical record influenced the reading of selective attacks. Rohingya settlements suffered destruction while neighbouring communities were treated differently. The court assessed that distinction alongside official hostility and the systematic character of the operations.
The court also looked at online hate speech connected to Myanmar’s military. The Independent Investigative Mechanism for Myanmar had uncovered a network of Facebook pages linked to military figures and organisations that spread anti-Rohingya content.
The sexual violence evidence had a bearing on more than the count of individual offences. In paragraph 370, the court considered at least 1,834 acts of rape together with restrictions on marriage, births, and birth registration when assessing measures directed at the group’s reproductive life. The full extent of the violence is hard to establish, the judges said, because many survivors were reluctant to come forward.
The majority considered the attacks and their consequences relevant to Article II(d), the provision concerning measures intended to prevent births. In assessing sexual violence, the court also drew on the 1998 Akayesu judgment of the International Criminal Tribunal for Rwanda, which acknowledged that rape and sexual violence could be acts of genocide when accompanied by the necessary intent.
The court considered evidence that sexual violence had compromised reproductive capacity, caused lasting trauma, and affected prospects of marriage and childbearing within the Rohingya community.
The targeting of children had a separate evidentiary role. It weakened the argument that the victims had been selected for their participation in insurgency and strengthened the majority’s reading of the campaign as an attack on the group itself.
The court’s finding of genocide rested on killings, serious bodily or mental harm, and measures intended to prevent births, under Article II(a), (b), and (d) of the convention.
Vice President Julia Sebutinde, judges Peter Tomka, Ronny Abraham, Xue Hanqin, and Georg Nolte, and Claus Kress, the judge ad hoc chosen by Myanmar, signed the joint dissent. All six questioned whether the evidence permitted the necessary inference of genocidal intent.
Under Article 31 of the ICJ Statute, a state without a judge of its nationality on the bench may appoint a judge ad hoc for that specific case. Myanmar chose Kress and The Gambia chose Navanethem Pillay.
The dissenters acknowledged the violence, displacement, and other serious abuses that the Rohingya had endured. They also agreed that the Rohingya were a protected ethnic group and that the targeted population in northern Rakhine State constituted a substantial part of that group.
The dissent warned that giving substantial evidentiary value to discrimination, forced displacement, and attacks on the foundations of communal life could blur the line between genocide and other international crimes.
The dissenters objected that forced displacement had not been properly excluded as an alternative explanation. In their view, the majority had to show why that possibility failed on the complete record, and not merely that atrocities had occurred.
The majority’s reasoning also indicates that an intention to expel may coexist with an intention to destroy. A government may have territorial or military goals while using methods intended to destroy a protected group.
Debate and consequences
In an analysis published by The Guardian (November 19), its London-based senior international correspondent Julian Borger argues that the judgment renews the Genocide Convention’s relevance by providing a clearer method for assessing intent. He quotes the international-law scholar William Schabas on its implications for proceedings involving Israel, but notes the factual differences between the two cases.
Writing in EJIL: Talk! (November 19), the international-law scholar Marko Milanovic notes the court’s unusual split. The six dissenting votes, and separate opinions or declarations from all 15 judges, show the difficulty of agreeing on how to apply the genocide standard.
A critical assessment comes from thinc. (The Hague Initiative for International Cooperation), a Netherlands-based non-profit think tank founded in 2017 with the assistance of Christians for Israel, whose work centres on the Israel-Palestine conflict. In an article on its website titled “A Divided ICJ Lowers the Standard for Proving Genocidal Intent” (November 19), Director General Andrew Tucker argues that the majority lowered the threshold for proving genocidal intent and in effect shifted the burden of proof onto the defending state. He contends that the court gave too little weight to forced displacement and collective punishment as alternative explanations, and he criticises its reliance on UN and other non-governmental material.
How the court evaluated the evidence matters because much of it was collected beyond Myanmar’s borders. The government denied investigators access to the relevant areas. Refugee accounts, medical material, satellite observations, and digital records made up much of the material before the court.
In examining UN investigators’ work, the judges looked closely at how accounts were gathered, cross-checked, and corroborated. The court treated the reports of the UN Independent International Fact-Finding Mission on Myanmar as reliable but weighed them with caution, since the mission applied a “reasonable grounds” standard of proof.
Paragraph 79 preserves the ordinary burden of proof on The Gambia. Paragraphs 128 to 131 explain that where a respondent controls potentially decisive evidence, flexibility in evaluating the available material may be justified without transferring the burden of proof.
For future human-rights litigation, the distinction matters. A state gains no automatic advantage by keeping investigators away from the sites of alleged abuses, yet judges must still examine the reliability of the independent material that reaches them.
The judgment also found that Myanmar breached its obligation, under the court’s January 2020 provisional-measures order, to preserve evidence. Destruction and obstruction can affect both victims’ prospects of justice and a court’s ability to establish what happened.
The Gambia’s standing reveals another possible route to accountability when the affected population lacks the means to litigate against its own government. Supported by the 57-member Organisation of Islamic Cooperation (OIC), The Gambia instituted the case in its own name. The court accepted that a state party could seek compliance with obligations under the Genocide Convention even though the atrocities had taken place far from its territory.
Myanmar challenged the case as an OIC-backed proxy claim. In July 2022, the court rejected the objection: support by other states or an international organisation did not alter which country had brought the proceedings.
The court also dealt with the duty to prevent genocide, including the duties of a state faced with a serious risk that individuals acting alongside its security forces may commit acts of genocide. It found that Myanmar had violated that duty and its duty to punish genocide. The convention obliges governments to act before genocide is completed, to pay attention to warning signs and to the means available to prevent destruction. The scope of those obligations will depend on the state’s knowledge of the risk and its ability to influence the situation.
The ICJ ruling also revives a longstanding question in Indian constitutional law: what protection do people facing persecution have against deportation? Writing on his Constitutional Law and Philosophy blog (November 19), the constitutional-law scholar Gautam Bhatia revisited the Supreme Court’s interim order in Mohammad Salimullah v. Union of India. On April 8, 2021, a bench comprising Chief Justice of India S.A. Bobde and Justices A.S. Bopanna and V. Ramasubramanian declined to stop the proposed deportation of Rohingya detainees in Jammu and directed that the prescribed procedure be followed. The judges distinguished the guarantees of equality and life under Articles 14 and 21, which extend to everyone, from the freedom to reside and settle in India under Article 19(1)(e), which the Constitution reserves for citizens. That distinction informed the Supreme Court’s refusal to grant interim protection against deportation.
The Supreme Court also said it “cannot comment upon something happening in another country” when the petitioners raised conditions in Myanmar. Bhatia criticises its refusal to examine the danger the detainees could face on return. That risk lies at the heart of non-refoulement, the principle against sending a person to a place where they face persecution, torture, or other serious harm. In Bhatia’s view, the ICJ’s finding strengthens that criticism, although the scope of India’s constitutional obligations remains for Indian courts to determine.
In Nandita Haksar v. State of Manipur (May 3, 2021), the Manipur High Court took a different approach. Chief Justice Sanjay Kumar and Justice Lanusungkum Jamir held that Article 21’s protection of life encompassed non-refoulement, and allowed seven Myanmar nationals, including journalists and family members who had fled the 2021 military coup, to travel to Delhi to seek protection from the UN refugee agency. On April 25, 2022, a Supreme Court bench of Justices A.M. Khanwilkar and Abhay S. Oka stayed the operation of that judgment, provided it had not already been acted upon. These orders leave an unresolved issue: how should the state’s power to regulate entry and deportation be reconciled with the constitutional protection of life when credible evidence points to danger on return?
Compliance remains uncertain in Myanmar’s current political and military circumstances. The court ordered Myanmar to provide restitution and compensation, to investigate and, where warranted, prosecute those responsible, and to give assurances against repetition.
For the Rohingya, the judgment is a legal recognition of the harm done to their community. For the international system, its longer-term test is whether the principles established in court can help avert future atrocities and secure effective remedies for survivors.
V. Venkatesan is a Contributing Editor at Supreme Court Observer.

title: Tata Projects Secures Major Contract For 1,600 MW Ultra-Supercritical Thermal Power Project In Central India
description: Tata Projects Limited has secured the complete balance of plant turnkey package for a 1,600 MW ultra-supercritical thermal power project in central In
author: Swarajya Staff
content:
Infrastructure
Swarajya Staff
Nov 27, 2026 | Updated 10:34 AM GMT+5:30
Save & read from anywhere!
Bookmark stories for easy access on any device or the Swarajya app.
Tata Projects Limited has secured the complete balance of plant turnkey package for a 1,600 MW ultra-supercritical thermal power project in central India, marking a significant addition to the country's expanding coal-based generation capacity.
The engineering, procurement and construction contract, awarded by a leading integrated power utility, comprises two 800 MW units using advanced ultra-supercritical technology.
Under the contract, Tata Projects will oversee the design, engineering, manufacture, supply, construction, erection, testing and commissioning of all balance of plant systems.
The scope encompasses coal and biomass handling infrastructure, fuel and ash management facilities, water intake and cooling systems, electrical infrastructure, power evacuation systems, environmental facilities including a 275-metre triple-flue chimney, and all associated civil and structural works.
The project reflects India's continuing investment in thermal power infrastructure alongside renewable energy expansion.
Government figures show that 47,545 MW of thermal capacity remains under construction across the country, including 4,845 MW of stressed projects, whilst an additional 16,000 MW has been awarded and awaits construction.
The Ministry of Power has identified a requirement for approximately 315,000 MW of thermal capacity by 2035-36, necessitating the addition of at least 105,000 MW of new coal and lignite-based generation.
Ultra-supercritical technology represents a substantial efficiency improvement over conventional thermal plants, with modern units achieving thermal efficiency levels of approximately 44 per cent compared to 38 per cent for sub-critical plants.
The company has previously delivered more than five gigawatts of balance of plant and EPC projects, alongside flue gas desulphurisation systems serving approximately nine gigawatts of thermal power capacity across India.
The inclusion of biomass handling infrastructure indicates co-firing capability within the coal station, aligning with India's environmental objectives whilst maintaining baseload generation capacity.

title: ICF's Design Consultant Delay Puts Bengaluru Suburban Rail Coach Deliveries At Risk
description: Trains for Bengaluru's 148-km suburban rail network could arrive late, as the Integral Coach Factory (ICF) in Chennai is still to appoint a consultant
author: Arun Dhital
content:
News Brief
Arun Dhital
Nov 27, 2026 | Updated 10:30 AM GMT+5:30
Save & read from anywhere!
Bookmark stories for easy access on any device or the Swarajya app.
Trains for Bengaluru's 148-km suburban rail network could arrive late, as the Integral Coach Factory (ICF) in Chennai is still to appoint a consultant to design the rolling stock, raising doubts over availability once sections are ready.
Rail Infrastructure Development Company (Karnataka) Ltd (K-RIDE) placed a Rs 1,513.75-crore order with ICF for 153 air-conditioned coaches in May 2026 and signed a memorandum of understanding in September.
According to Moneycontrol, ICF has issued only an expression of interest for design consultancy, with no tender yet.
"ICF is yet to select a design consultant for the project," a source said. Medha-EC Engg and Italy's BLUE Engineering, both associated with Vande Bharat sleeper trains, have responded and are negotiating terms.
The design must be ready before ICF can freeze specifications and invite bids for the propulsion system. Design alone could take at least a year, while production, testing and rollout may need two more, including at least six months of mainline trials. "If the design work begins by April 2027, passenger services can be expected only by June 2030," the source said.
K-RIDE, however, aims to open the 25-km Mallige Line between Benniganahalli and Chikkabanavara by December 2028. An official said no delays were anticipated, pointing to ICF's capacity and the project's priority. "All trains will have Metro-like features and air-conditioned coaches," the official said.
An ICF spokesperson confirmed the position. "The design consultant is not yet finalised. We will float the propulsion tender in early 2027," the spokesperson said.
The coaches were bought without competitive bidding under a state procurement law exemption, and K-RIDE had promised first deliveries by November 2027.
Approved in 2020 with an October 2026 deadline, the project is now due by March 2030. Prime Minister Narendra Modi voiced displeasure over the delays at a PRAGATI review.

title: The Road To 360 Votes: BJP's Renewed Push For Delimitation And Women's Reservation
description: Parliament will reconvene for a special sitting from 30 November amid indications that the BJP-led NDA government is preparing to revive legislation l
author: Swarajya Staff
content:
Politics
Swarajya Staff
Nov 27, 2026 | Updated 09:41 AM GMT+5:30
Save & read from anywhere!
Bookmark stories for easy access on any device or the Swarajya app.
Parliament will reconvene for a special sitting from 30 November amid indications that the BJP-led NDA government is preparing to revive legislation linking delimitation to the implementation of 33 per cent women's reservation ahead of the 2029 Lok Sabha elections.
Parliamentary Affairs Minister Kiren Rijiju announced yesterday (26 November) that the government had requested the Lok Sabha to reconvene on 30 November and the Rajya Sabha on 2 December to transact essential government business.
The announcement follows Prime Minister Narendra Modi's Constitution Day message on Thursday, in which he reaffirmed his government's commitment to women's political representation and criticised the Opposition over the defeat of the constitutional amendment Bill in April.
The BJP's renewed push for constitutional amendments linking women's reservation to delimitation rests on a complex electoral mathematics problem: securing 360 votes in the Lok Sabha if all 539 sitting MPs other than the Speaker vote, and securing a majority of the total membership and a two-thirds majority of members present and voting in both Houses of Parliament.
After the Constitution (131st Amendment) Bill failed in April 2026 with 298 votes in favour and 230 against—54 votes short of the required threshold—the party had intensified outreach to opposition parties.
The BJP-led NDA could secure 319 votes with backing from 20 Trinamool Congress rebels and the Shiromani Akali Dal in the Lok Sabha.
That tally could rise to 353 votes if the DMK's 22 MPs, NCP (Sharadchandra Pawar)'s eight MPs, and YSR Congress Party's four lawmakers vote in favour.
The DMK has signalled support if Tamil Nadu's existing 7.2 per cent share of Lok Sabha seats is assured, while NCP leader Supriya Sule has indicated her party could back the bill with guarantees of uniform 50 per cent seat increases for every state.
The delimitation package proposed in April sought to expand the Lok Sabha from 543 to a maximum of 850 seats, with an envisaged strength of 816 seats, and enable delimitation using 2011 Census data rather than awaiting post-2026 census results.
Union Home Minister Amit Shah had earlier said that southern states' representation would increase from 129 to 195 seats—an approximately 50 per cent rise—with their overall share remaining nearly stable at 23.90 per cent compared to the current 23.76 per cent.
Tamil Nadu would gain 20 additional seats, Karnataka 14, Telangana nine, Andhra Pradesh 13, and Kerala 10.
The package ties 33 per cent women's reservation -- passed in 2023 but pending implementation following a fresh census and subsequent delimitation -- to this seat expansion.
Under the BJP's proposal, approximately 272 seats would be reserved for women in an 816-member House.
Opposition parties, particularly Congress, support women's quota but oppose the delimitation linkage, demanding implementation on the existing 543 seats and sub-quotas for OBC women.
If reintroduced and cleared by the Lok Sabha, the bill is expected to move to the Rajya Sabha on 2 December, where the NDA requires support from 19 additional members to secure passage.

title: Thiruparankundram pillar a British-era survey marker, says report
description: A new TN government report identifies the disputed Thiruparankundram Deepam pillar as a British-era survey marker. Pooja Prasanna breaks down the report in Let Me Explain.
author: Pooja Prasanna
content:
A new TN government report identifies the disputed Thiruparankundram Deepam pillar as a British-era survey marker. Pooja Prasanna breaks down the report in Let Me Explain.
On November 24, the Karthigai Deepam lamp was lit at the disputed stone pillar atop Thiruparankundram hill in Madurai.
Tamil Nadu instead witnessed a tense situation between the police, BJP and Hindutva groups
The stone pillar on a hill in Madurai has been at the centre of a heated religious and political dispute for a while now.
The pillar stands 50 metres away from the Sikandar Badusha Dargah on Thiruparankundram hill. Hindutva groups have secured court judgments that allow a lamp to be lit here during the annual Karthigai Deepam festival.
But the Tamil Nadu government and temple administration have argued that the pillar is not a traditional lamp-lighting structure, but an old survey marker.
Now, a new report by the state government appears to offer evidence for that claim.
It identifies the disputed pillar as part of a massive 200-year-old British-era project to map the Indian subcontinent.
The report in fact documents hundreds of similar survey stations across Tamil Nadu, some of which have since become places of worship.
So, what exactly did the surveyors leave behind, and what has the government found at Thiruparankundram?
Let me explain.

title: Friendship Dispute Leads To Teen's Murder In Delhi
description: A 17-year-old boy, Naushad, was allegedly stabbed to death in northwest Delhi's Shakurpur following a dispute related to his sister's friendship with one of the accused. Police have apprehended three individuals, including a 21-year-old man and two juveniles, in connection with the murder.
author: Text Feed
content:
A 17-year-old boy was tragically stabbed to death in northwest Delhi's Shakurpur following a dispute concerning his sister's friendship, leading to the apprehension of three suspects.
Key Points
- A 17-year-old boy was allegedly stabbed to death in northwest Delhi's Shakurpur on Friday.
- The victim, Naushad, was attacked with a knife during an argument with the accused and his associates on Thursday.
- The dispute stemmed from the victim's sister's friendship with one of the accused.
- Naushad succumbed to his injuries at Bhagwan Mahavir Hospital during treatment.
- Police have apprehended three persons, including a 21-year-old man and two juveniles, in connection with the murder.
A 17-year-old boy was allegedly stabbed to death during a dispute over his sister's friendship with a man in northwest Delhi's Shakurpur, police said on Friday.
Details Of The Incident
The victim, Naushad, was attacked with a knife during the argument with the accused and his associates on Thursday, police said.
"The dispute stemmed from the friendship between one of the accused and the victim's sister, which had triggered tensions between the two sides," a senior police officer told PTI.
After the attack, Naushad was rushed to Bhagwan Mahavir Hospital, where he succumbed to his injuries during treatment, the officer said.
"We have apprehended three persons -- a 21-year-old man identified as Atikur Rahman and two juveniles -- in connection with the murder," the officer said.
Police said further investigation into the case is underway.

title: Why Azam Khan 'wished' Akhilesh spent 6 months in jail
description: Senior Samajwadi Party leader Azam Khan expressed a wish for party president Akhilesh Yadav to experience jail for six months to understand the hardships of incarceration. Khan recounted his own traumatic prison experience, including separation from his son. Yadav acknowledged Khan's pain and discussed improving prison infrastructure. The remarks were made at the SP manifesto launch, highlighting the complex relationship and political dynamics within the party.
author: Utkarsh Mishra
content:
Samajwadi Party leader Azam Khan also recounted the trauma of being separated from his son Abdullah during a prison transfer, saying he feared they might never meet again.
Key Points
- Senior SP leader Azam Khan said he sometimes 'wished' Akhilesh Yadav had spent six months in jail to understand incarceration hardships.
- Khan shared his personal trauma of imprisonment, including separation from his son Abdullah during a prison transfer.
- Akhilesh Yadav acknowledged Khan's pain and referred to improving prison infrastructure, noting the best jail in Etawah was built under SP rule.
- Khan, a 10-time MLA and former minister, was released from Ghaziabad's Dasna jail on November 18 after securing interim bail in a money laundering case.
- The remarks were made during the launch of the Samajwadi Party's manifesto for the 2027 Uttar Pradesh Assembly elections.
Senior Samajwadi Party leader Azam Khan on Thursday said he sometimes 'wished' Akhilesh Yadav had spent six months in jail to understand the hardships of incarceration, prompting the party president to say he had felt the veteran leader's pain from time to time.
Khan also recounted the trauma of being separated from his son Abdullah during a prison transfer, saying he feared they might never meet again.
Azam Khan's Candid Remarks On Incarceration
Speaking at the launch of the Samajwadi Party's manifesto for the 2027 Uttar Pradesh Assembly elections in Lukcnow, Khan said he would sometimes tell Abdullah and others in jail that he wished Yadav, too, could experience imprisonment for a brief while to understand the conditions and emotional trauma faced by inmates.
"My heart wished Akhilesh ji, too, could come to jail for six months, so he could know how the days and nights pass and what one goes through," Khan said in a rhetorical remark.
Akhilesh Yadav's Response And Party Dynamics
After the manifesto unveiling, when journalists asked for his reaction to Khan's account of his prison experience, Yadav said, "He is a member of our party and our family. I have felt his pain from time to time."
During his speech, Yadav also referred to Khan's remarks about prison conditions, saying he had spoken to the veteran leader.
He said the best jail in Etawah had been built during the Samajwadi Party government and that efforts would be made to improve prison infrastructure in the future.
Speaking at the event, Khan said the most painful part of his incarceration was having to see his young son remain in jail alongside him for years.
He also described the uncertainty over Abdullah's whereabouts after being separated from him during a prison transfer.
Earlier, referring to Khan's expectations from the manifesto, Yadav had assured the senior leader that whatever was required to fulfil its promises would be done.
Responding to a question on whether Khan could expect relief from cases registered against him if the SP comes to power, Yadav referred to what he described as hardships caused by false cases and alleged misuse of official machinery.
Khan, who was seated on the stage, gestured in disagreement when the reporter raised the question about him and briefly got up from his seat.
His response was inaudible.
Citing a recent accident in Gorakhpur in which a 14-year-old boy died, Yadav questioned the police action and said officials should be asked why a murder case was sought to be registered in the matter.
Khan's Political Stature And Legal Battles
Khan, a 10-time MLA from Rampur, served as a cabinet minister in the Akhilesh Yadav-led government from 2012 to 2017, holding important portfolios including parliamentary affairs and urban development.
He was released from Ghaziabad's Dasna jail on November 18 after the Allahabad High Court granted him interim bail in a money laundering case registered by the Enforcement Directorate related to the Maulana Mohammad Ali Jauhar University in Rampur.
The Enforcement Directorate had arrested him on October 31, shortly after his release from Rampur jail in another case. He had spent nearly 11 months in jail during that preceding stint.
After the programme, Yadav accompanied Khan to the airport, from where the senior SP leader apparently left for Delhi. Visuals from outside the airport showed the two leaders speaking cordially.
At the manifesto launch, Yadav had described Khan as an elder leader and a member of his family, a description he has also used in the past for the veteran leader, who was a longtime close associate of his father and SP founder, late Mulayam Singh Yadav.

title: Parliament reconvened amid buzz over delimitation, women's quota
description: India's Parliament, comprising the Lok Sabha and Rajya Sabha, has been reconvened for a special sitting starting November 30 and December 2, respectively. The primary agenda is expected to be a constitutional amendment linking women's reservation to delimitation. The sittings will conclude by December 3 and will not include Question Hour, Zero Hour, or Private Members' Business.
author: Utkarsh Mishra
content:
Parliament is set to reconvene for a special session from November 30, with both Lok Sabha and Rajya Sabha expected to address a crucial constitutional amendment concerning women's reservation linked to delimitation.
Key Points
- Lok Sabha will reconvene on Monday, November 30, and Rajya Sabha on Wednesday, December 2, for a special sitting.
- The special session is likely to discuss a constitutional amendment linking women's reservation to delimitation.
- The sittings are scheduled to conclude on Thursday, December 3, for both Houses.
- There will be no Question Hour, Zero Hour, or Private Members' Business during these special sittings.
- Union Parliamentary Affairs Minister Kiren Rijiju confirmed the government's request to reconvene Parliament for essential business on Thursday.
The Lok Sabha and Rajya Sabha were reconvened on November 30 and December 2, respectively, on Thursday, hours after the government proposed a special sitting, in all probability to discuss and roll out a constitutional amendment linking the rollout of women's reservation to delimitation.
The two Houses were reconvened following separate directives issued by Lok Sabha Speaker Om Birla and Rajya Sabha Chairman C P Radhakrishnan, official sources said.
Parliamentary Schedule And Agenda
'Members are informed that under Rule 15 of Rules of Procedure and Conduct of Business in Lok Sabha, the Speaker has directed that Lok Sabha, which was adjourned sine die on August 13, 2026, will now sit at 11 am on Monday, November 30. As at present arranged, sittings of Lok Sabha, subject to exigencies of government business, will conclude on Thursday, December 3,' a notification issued by the Lok Sabha Secretariat said.
There would be no Question Hour, Zero Hour or Private Members' Business during the sittings, it said.
A similar message was sent to the members of the Rajya Sabha.
'The Rajya Sabha, which was adjourned sine die on August 13, 2026, has been reconvened by the Hon'ble Chairman to meet at 11 am on Wednesday, December 2, to transact essential government business and subject to exigencies of the business, the session may conclude on Thursday, December 3,' the message sent by the Rajya Sabha Secretariat said.
The comminuques also conveyed that there would be no Question Hour, Zero Hour or Private Members' Business during the sittings.
Government's Rationale For Special Session
Earlier, the government proposed a special sitting of Parliament from November 30 to transact "essential" business, amid indications that the delimitation-linked women's reservation bill may be reintroduced.
'The government has requested the Hon'ble Speaker, Lok Sabha, and the Hon'ble Chairman, Rajya Sabha, to reconvene Lok Sabha on Monday, November 30, 2026, and Rajya Sabha on Wednesday, December 2, 2026, to transact essential government business,' Union Parliamentary Affairs Minister Kiren Rijiju said in an X post on Thursday.
Subject to exigencies of the business, the sitting of both Houses may conclude on December 3, 2026, he said.

title: Jharkhand Double Murder: 2 Brothers Kill Wives, Bury Bodies In Forest; Tell Police They Had Gone Missing
description: The accused allegedly used an ambulance to transport the bodies before burying them in a Simdega forest; police recovered the bodies after the brothers confessed during interrogation.
author: Aleesha Sam
content:
Two brothers from Jharkhand were arrested for allegedly murdering their wives and burying their bodies in a forest in neighbouring Simdega district. The accused allegedly transported the bodies in an ambulance before burying them in the forest in an attempt to conceal the crime.
The accused have been identified as Shiv Shankar Sahu, an ambulance driver, and his brother Navin Sahu. Their wives, Mini Priya (28) and Radhika Kumari (20), were allegedly killed on November 24.
According to a report by NDTV, the brothers were allegedly angered by a long-standing dispute between the two women. Although the sisters-in-law had reportedly reconciled just two days before the murders, the brothers allegedly went ahead with the killings.
Brothers Allegedly Kill Wives, Transport Bodies In Ambulance
According to the police, the murders took place in the Shamshera area. Following the killings, the accused allegedly loaded the bodies into Shiv Shankar's ambulance and drove to a forest in Simdega district, where they buried them.
Police subsequently recovered an axe allegedly used in the murders and seized the ambulance used to transport the bodies.
Brothers Initially Claimed Wives Had Gone Missing
The incident came to light after the brothers initially told the police that their wives had left home without informing them.
However, following sustained questioning, the two allegedly confessed to the murders and disclosed where they had buried the bodies.
Police then reached the forest, exhumed the bodies and sent them to Sadar Hospital in Gumla for post-mortem examinations.
According to a News18 report, family members had spoken to the two women around 9 am on Monday and said everything appeared normal at the time.
Police Probe Motive Behind Double Murder
Investigators are now probing the circumstances surrounding the murders, including the exact nature of the dispute between the two women and what prompted the brothers to allegedly kill them despite their recent reconciliation.
Both accused have been arrested, and further investigation into the case is underway.

title: Indore’s Iconic Poha Eyes Global Market With Ready-To-Eat Version, Attracts Buyers At International Trade
description: Indore’s iconic poha is attracting attention at the 45th India International Trade Fair in New Delhi through an innovative ready-to-eat version. Prepared within 10 minutes by adding hot water, the product combines traditional flavours with modern food-processing technology. Entrepreneurs are exploring business partnerships, distribution opportunities.
author: Staff Reporter
content:
Indore (Madhya Pradesh): The city's iconic 'poha' is seeking a place in national and international markets, with an innovative ready-to-eat version attracting attention at the 45th India International Trade Fair in New Delhi.
Combining Indore's traditional flavours with modern food-processing technology, the product can be prepared in just 10 minutes by adding hot water. The ready-to-eat 'poha' comes with a pre-mixed spice blend, allowing consumers to enjoy the city's popular breakfast delicacy without elaborate preparation.
Its convenient packaging and quick preparation make it suitable for consumers beyond Indore, while also opening possibilities in international markets. Visitors and traders at the fair have shown keen interest in the product.
The fair, which began on Nov 13, has allowed Madhya Pradesh-based entrepreneurs to showcase their products and connect with potential buyers, distributors and investors.
Through business-to-business (B2B) interactions, the Indore product is exploring new commercial partnerships and wider distribution opportunities, potentially taking the city's signature breakfast beyond its traditional markets.

title: Bhopal Potters Market Opens At Gauhar Mahal, Showcases Ceramic Artworks By Four Master Potters
description: A four-day Bhopal Potters Market opened at Gauhar Mahal on Thursday with an exhibition featuring four master ceramists from Delhi, Goa and Puducherry. Their artworks explore cultural heritage, nature and rapid urbanisation. The main market, featuring 45 ceramists from around 10 cities, will welcome visitors from Friday through Sunday, between 11 am and 8 pm.
author: Staff Reporter
content:
Bhopal (Madhya Pradesh): A four-day Bhopal Potters Market began with the opening of an exhibition featuring artworks by four master potters at Gauhar Mahal on Thursday. The participating master potters include Suvajit Mondal and Aniruddh Sagar from Delhi, Shalini Dam from Goa, and Indrani Singh Cassime from Puducherry.
Their artworks highlight local heritage and cultural narratives, reflecting how traditional pottery techniques can evolve while preserving cultural roots. Drawing creative inspiration from natural elements, landscapes and lunar energy, the artists have translated poetic ideas into tactile ceramic sculptures and vessels.
One of the standout exhibits, a tall vertical ceramic installation by Suvajit Mondal, depicts the shrinking space of nature amidst expanding concrete cities, offering a visual reflection on changing urban environments.
Besides, the main Potters Market will open for visitors from Friday through Sunday, where 45 ceramists from about 10 cities across the country will showcase their clay artworks from 11 am to 8 pm.

title: Pune News: तुम्ही ग्राहकांच्या सेवेत जाण्याआधी आम्ही तुमच्या सेवेत, बिल तयार आहे; पुण्यात हॉटेलच्या ओपनिंगआधीच महापालिकेचा दणका
description: Pune municipal corporation: महापौर नागपुरे यांच्या प्रभागात ड्रेनेज वाहिनीचे काम सुरू आहे. त्याबाबतचा फ्लेक्स तेथे लावण्यात आला होता. त्याची तक्रार नागरिकांनी ‘भाऊ फ्लेक्स काढा’ या पोर्टलवर फोटोसह केली. त्यानंतर महापालिकेने आपल्या हँडलवर हा फ्लेक्स पोस्ट करून ‘ड्रेनेजची तसदी समजू शकतो, फ्लेक्सची तसदी कशाबद्दल,’ असा प्रश्न उपस्थित केला. त्यानंतर "माझ्या प्रभागातील ठेकेदाराने संबंधित फ्लेक्स लावला होता. महापालिकेने माझ्याशी संबंधित फ्लेक्स पोस्ट करून प्रश्न विचारला यापेक्षा अधिक पारदर्शक काय असू शकते ? सत्ताधाऱ्यांना वेगळा न्याय नसतो, हेच समोर आले," अशी प्रतिक्रिया महापौर मंजुषा नागपुरे यांनी दिली आहे.
author: Akshay Shitole
content:
PMC News: "महापालिकेतील सर्व पदाधिकारी, सभासदांना ‘भाऊ फ्लेक्स काढा’ पोर्टलवर आलेल्या तक्रारी दाखविल्या. आमचा हेतू बदनामी करण्याचा नसल्याचे निदर्शनास आणून दिले. त्यांनीही सर्व अनधिकृत फ्लेक्स काढून टाकण्याची तयारी दर्शवली. त्यानंतर पीएमसी केअर हँडलवरील पोस्टही हटवण्यात आली," अशी माहिती अतिरिक्त आयुक्त प्राजित नायर यांनी दिली आहे.
म. टा. प्रतिनिधी, पुणे: अनधिकृत फ्लेक्सविरोधातील कारवाईचा फटका राजकीय पदाधिकाऱ्यांनाही बसला. प्रशासनाने अधिकृत ‘एक्स हँडल’वरून महापौर मंजूषा नागपुरे, विरोधी पक्षनेते ॲड. नीलेश निकम आणि काँग्रेसचे गटनेते ॲड. चंदू कदम यांच्याशी संबंधित अनधिकृत फ्लेक्स अस्सल पुणेरी शैलीतील मजकुरासह पोस्ट केले. सायंकाळी सर्व पदाधिकाऱ्यांनी आपापले फ्लेक्स उतरवून घेण्यास सुरुवात केल्यानंतर पालिकेनेही या पोस्ट डिलिट केल्या. दरम्यान, ‘भाऊ फ्लेक्स काढा’ पोर्टलवर बॅनर, फ्लेक्सच्या १८८२ तक्रारी नोंदविण्यात आल्या आहेत. महापौर नागपुरे यांच्या प्रभागात ड्रेनेज वाहिनीचे काम सुरू आहे. त्याबाबतचा फ्लेक्स तेथे लावण्यात आला होता. त्याची तक्रार नागरिकांनी ‘भाऊ फ्लेक्स काढा’ या पोर्टलवर फोटोसह केली. त्यानंतर महापालिकेने आपल्या हँडलवर हा फ्लेक्स पोस्ट करून ‘ड्रेनेजची तसदी समजू शकतो, फ्लेक्सची तसदी कशाबद्दल,’ असा प्रश्न उपस्थित केला. त्यानंतर "माझ्या प्रभागातील ठेकेदाराने संबंधित फ्लेक्स लावला होता. महापालिकेने माझ्याशी संबंधित फ्लेक्स पोस्ट करून प्रश्न विचारला यापेक्षा अधिक पारदर्शक काय असू शकते ? सत्ताधाऱ्यांना वेगळा न्याय नसतो, हेच समोर आले," अशी प्रतिक्रिया महापौर मंजुषा नागपुरे यांनी दिली आहे.
‘आम्ही नागरिकांच्या सोबत’ असा फ्लेक्स काँग्रेस गटनेते ॲड. चंदू कदम यांनी लावला होता. त्यावर ‘आम्हीही नागरिकांसोबत’ अशी पोस्ट महापालिकेने केली. विरोधी पक्षनेते ॲड. नीलेश निकम यांच्या प्रभागात त्यांनीच लावलेला गणेशोत्सवाच्या शुभेच्छांचा फलक पोस्ट करून महापालिकेने ‘गणेशोत्सव सप्टेंबरमध्ये झाला, आता नोव्हेंबर आहे,’ असा उपरोधिक सवाल केला. त्यानंतर निकम यांनी आपली चूक मान्य करून फ्लेक्स काढून घेत असल्याचे जाहीर केले. नगरसेवक सुनील पांडे यांचे नाव विद्रुपीकरणाच्या तक्रारीच्या यादीत तिसऱ्या क्रमांकावर होते. पुरस्कार जाहीर झाल्यानंतर त्यांनी फ्लेक्स काढून घेतले. त्याचे फोटो टाकून ‘फ्लेक्स लावायला कार्यकर्ते होते, काढायला मात्र भाऊ स्वत: आले. पांडे यांचे अभिनंदन, पुरस्कार परत घेतला आहे. ‘दादा’ आणि ‘साहेब’ यांची वाट पहात आहोत,’ असा मजकूर महापालिकेने पोस्ट केला. डायनिंग हॉलला उ‌द्घाटनाआधीच 'बिल' बावधन परिसरात डायनिंग हॉल सुरू होणार असल्याच्या अनधिकृत जाहिराती लावण्यात आल्या आहेत. त्याविरोधात तक्रारी आल्यानंतर पालिकेने २३ अनधिकृत फ्लेक्ससाठी प्रत्येकी दोन हजार रुपयांप्रमाणे ४६ हजार रुपये दंड ठोठावत असल्याची पोस्ट केली आहे. 'डायनिंग हॉल अजून सुरूर व्हायचा आहे; पण पहिले बिल तयार आहे. उधारी बंद, तीन दिवसांत बिल भरावे,' असा टोलाही पालिकेने लगावला.
लेखकाबद्दलअक्षय शितोळेअक्षय शितोळे हे २०१८ पासून डिजिटल मीडियात कार्यरत असून सध्या मटा ऑनलाइनमध्ये प्रिन्सिपल डिजिटल कंटेंट प्रोड्युसर म्हणून जबाबदारी सांभाळत आहेत. राज्यभरातील रिपोर्टर्ससोबत समन्वय साधत महाराष्ट्रातील गावगाड्यापासून मोठ्या शहरांमधील दैनंदिन घडामोडी मटा ऑनलाइनसाठी वेगवान आणि अचूक पद्धतीने मिळवण्याचा त्यांचा प्रयत्न असतो. राजकीय बातम्यांमध्ये विशेष रस, बातम्यांमागची बातमी अर्थात घडामोडींचा विश्लेषणात्मक आढावा घेण्याचा सातत्याने प्रयत्न असतो. शेती आणि ग्रामीण जीवन हे जिव्हाळ्याचे विषय आहेत.
पत्रकारितेतील अनुभव
अक्षय शितोळे यांनी २०१८ मध्ये आपल्या पत्रकारितेतील प्रवासाचा प्रारंभ केला. सुरुवातीला न्यूज १८ लोकमत या वेबसाईटसाठी काम करताना ट्रेनी, सब एडिटर असा त्यांचा प्रवास राहिला. या कार्यकाळात प्रामुख्याने राजकीय बातम्यांसह स्थानिक पातळीवरील विविध घडामोडी कव्हर करण्याचे काम त्यांनी केले. २०१९ च्या विधानसभा आणि लोकसभा निवडणुकीदरम्यान त्यांनी विविध राजकीय घडामोडींचा विश्लेषणात्मक आढावा घेतला. पुढे २०२१ मटा ऑनलाइनमध्ये डिजिटल कंटेट प्रोड्युसर म्हणून जॉइन झाले. यावेळी राजकीय बातम्यांसह विविध जिल्ह्यांतील प्रतिनिधींशी समन्वय ठेवत वेबसाईटसाठी वेगवान आणि अचूक बातम्या मिळवण्याचा त्यांचा प्रयत्न राहिला. तसंच मटा ऑनलाइनला २५ वर्षे पूर्ण झाल्याच्या पार्श्वभूमीवर त्यांनी महाराष्ट्राच्या दोन दशकांच्या सामाजिक वाटचालीचा आढावा घेणारा विशेष लेख लिहिला होता. "आरक्षणाचे लढे आणि तिढे, टोकदार जातीय अस्मिता ; २५ वर्षांत कसं ढवळून निघालं महाराष्ट्राचं समाजमन?" शीर्षकाखाली लिहिलेल्या या लेखाच्या माध्यमातून महाराष्ट्रात मागील २५ वर्षांत जी सामाजिक स्थित्यंतरे झाली, ज्या घटनांनी महाराष्ट्राच्या सामाजिक रचनेवर परिणाम केला, अशा घडामोडींचा सविस्तर आढावा घेतला होता. २०२३ मध्ये त्यांनी लोकमत ऑनलाइनसोबतही काम केले असून ते २०२५ पासून पुन्हा मटा ऑनलाइनमध्ये प्रिन्सिपल डिजिलट कंटेंट प्रोड्युसर म्हणून रुजू झाले. विविध जिल्ह्यांतील रिपोर्टर्ससोबत संवाद साधत स्थानिक घडामोडींसह राज्यभरात महत्त्वाच्या बातम्या कव्हर करण्याचा त्यांचा प्रयत्न असतो. तसंच विश्लेषणात्मक व्हिडिओच्या माध्यमातून राजकीय घटनांचे अन्वयार्थ प्रेक्षकांसमोर उलगडण्याचा त्यांचा प्रयत्न असतो. महाराष्ट्रात २०२५-२६ साली झालेल्या स्थानिक स्वराज्य संस्थांच्या निवडणुकीदरम्यान त्यांनी विविध विश्लेषणात्मक व्हिडिओंच्या माध्यमातून राजकीय घडामोडींचं सोप्या शब्दांत विश्लेषण केले. तसंच महानगरपालिका निवडणूक निकालानंतर राजकीय विश्लेषकांची मुलाखत घेत या निवडणूक निकालाचा वेध घेण्याचा प्रयत्न केला.

title: BMC, कोर्ट ते बिग बींच्या बंगल्याला खोट्या धमक्यांचे ईमेल; अमेरिकेत नोकरी करणारा भारतीय techie मास्टरमाईंड, मुंबई पोलिसांनी जाळं टाकताच अडकला
description: Crime News : ﻿अमेरिकेत नोकरी करणारा २८ वर्षीय सॉफ्टवेअर इंजिनिअर हाच मुंबई महापालिका कार्यालय, मेट्रो स्थानके, विविध न्यायालये, शाळा, अमिताभ बच्चन यांचा बंगला आणि इतर महत्त्वाच्या ठिकाणी हल्ल्यांच्या धमक्या देणाऱ्या अनेक ईमेलमागे असल्याचा संशय मुंबई पोलिसांना आहे.﻿
author: Anish Bendre
content:
मुंबई : अमेरिकेत नोकरी करणारा २८ वर्षीय सॉफ्टवेअर इंजिनिअर हाच मुंबई महापालिका कार्यालय, मेट्रो स्थानके, बॉम्बे स्टॉक एक्सचेंज (बीएसई), विविध न्यायालये, शाळा, बॉलिवूड स्टार अमिताभ बच्चन यांचा बंगला आणि इतर महत्त्वाच्या ठिकाणी हल्ल्यांच्या धमक्या देणाऱ्या अनेक ईमेलमागे असल्याचा संशय मुंबई पोलिसांना आहे.
१५०० धमकीचे खोटे ईमेल
तमिळनाडूच्या तिरुनेलवेली जिल्ह्यातील रहिवासी असलेल्या शरथ सुब्रमण्यन शंकर याचे जुलै महिन्यात चेन्नई विमानतळावर आगमन झाल्यावर, राज्याच्या दहशतवादविरोधी पथकाने (एटीएस) मुंबई पोलिसांनी दिलेल्या गुप्त माहितीच्या आधारे ताब्यात घेतले होते. सध्या तो तमिळनाडू पोलिसांच्या ताब्यात आहे. गेल्या दोन वर्षांत त्याने देशातील विविध संस्थांना १५०० खोटे धमकीचे ईमेल पाठवल्याचा संशय आहे.
मुंबई पोलिसांच्या एका वरिष्ठ अधिकाऱ्याने सांगितले की, "आरोपीचा ताबा मिळाल्यावर, त्याने या धमक्या का दिल्या, हे जाणून घेण्यासाठी आम्ही त्याची चौकशी करु"
ईमेलवरुन जाळ्यात अडकवलं
धमक्यांच्या तपासात सहभागी असलेल्या मुंबई पोलिसांच्या एका अधिकाऱ्याने, शंकरच्या एका ईमेलमधील माहितीच्या आधारे त्याच्याशी संवाद साधून त्याला जाळ्यात अडकवले. पोलिसांशी बोलत आहोत हे माहीत नसलेल्या शंकरने, एका प्रश्नाला उत्तर देताना स्वतःच्या वैयक्तिक ईमेल आयडीवरुन प्रतिसाद दिला. ही माहिती मुंबई पोलिसांना त्याच्याबद्दल अधिक तपशील मिळवण्यासाठी पुरेशी ठरली. ही माहिती तमिळनाडू पोलिसांशी शेअर करण्यात आली आणि अमेरिकेवरुन परतल्यावर शंकरला अटक करण्यात आली.
Pune News : चिमुरड्याची मृत्यूशी झुंज, नातेवाईक 25 हजाराचं इंजेक्शन बसमध्ये विसरले; PMP कर्मचाऱ्यांची माणूसकी, अर्ध्या रात्री कुटुंबाला दिलासा
सर्व धमक्या निघाल्या खोट्या
मुंबईत आलेल्या प्रत्येक धमकीच्या ईमेलनंतर, संबंधित ठिकाण रिकामे करणे आणि सुरक्षा व्यवस्था कडक करणे असे प्रोटोकॉल राबवले जात असत. यामध्ये बॉम्ब शोधक व नाशक पथके, श्वान पथके आणि स्थानिक तसेच गुन्हे शाखेच्या पोलिसांची नियुक्ती केली जात असे. काही प्रकरणांमध्ये सार्वजनिक सेवांवरही परिणाम झाला होता. मात्र, या सर्व धमक्या खोट्या असल्याचे निष्पन्न झाले.
शंकरच्या अटकेपूर्वी, १० जून रोजी बॉम्बे स्टॉक एक्सचेंजला काही धमकीचे ईमेल पाठवण्यात आले होते, ज्यामध्ये इमारतीत आरडीएक्स ठेवल्याचा दावा करण्यात आला होता. हे ईमेल विविध खात्यांवरुन, व्हीपीएन आणि इतर तंत्रज्ञानाचा वापर करून पाठवण्यात आले होते, जेणेकरून पाठवणाऱ्याची ओळख लपवता येईल आणि डिजिटल मागोवा घेणे अत्यंत कठीण होईल. सूत्रांच्या माहितीनुसार, यामुळे तपासात विलंब झाला.
Nagpur News : आजारपणात काळजीवाहू, आईच्या निधनाने मुलगा खचला, बाराव्याच्या विधीवेळी हार्ट अटॅक, माऊलीमागून लेकराचाही अखेरचा श्वास
बनावट ईमेल खाती विकणाराही अटकेत
याव्यतिरिक्त, उत्तर प्रदेश एटीएसद्वारे अटक करण्यात आलेल्या अंकित शंखवार (२४) नावाच्या आणखी एका संशयिताची भूमिकाही तपासाधीन आहे. बनावट ईमेल खाती तयार करुन ती पुरवण्याचे रॅकेट चालवल्याप्रकरणी त्याला अटक करण्यात आली आहे. उत्तर प्रदेश एटीएसच्या प्राथमिक तपासात असे समोर आले आहे की, त्याने तयार केलेल्या ईमेल आयडींचा वापर करून १२ नोव्हेंबर रोजी मुंबईतील अनेक महत्त्वाच्या ठिकाणी बॉम्बच्या खोट्या धमक्या देण्यात आल्या होत्या.
उत्तर प्रदेश एटीएसच्या म्हणण्यानुसार, आरोपीने हे ईमेल आयडी एका बांगलादेशी नागरिकाला विकले होते आणि नंतर या खात्यांचा वापर मुंबईतील विविध ठिकाणी धमकीचे ईमेल पाठवण्यासाठी करण्यात आला. एटीएसचा असा दावा आहे की, ही ईमेल खाती पुरवल्याबद्दल अंकितला तुर्की आणि इजिप्तसारख्या देशांतील स्रोतांकडून ५० हजार डॉलर्स (सुमारे ४७ लाख रुपये) मिळाले होते. मुंबई पोलीस अजूनही त्याच्या नेमक्या भूमिकेचा तपास करत आहेत.
Bengaluru Crime : आठ दिवसापूर्वी मुलीचा जन्म, बापाने जुन्या मित्रांशी संबंध तोडण्याचं ठरवलं, एका निर्णयामुळे आयुष्याला मुकलामुंबई गुन्हे शाखेचे 'क्रिमिनल इंटेलिजन्स युनिट' आणि स्थानिक पोलीस ठाणी स्वतंत्रपणे या प्रकरणाचा तपास करत आहेत. एका पोलीस अधिकाऱ्याने सांगितले की, आरोपींची चौकशी केल्यानंतर त्यांच्या मोडस ऑपरेंडी, त्यांचा उद्देश आणि यात इतर कोणी सामील आहे का, हे स्पष्ट होईल.

title: एअरटेलचा ग्राहकांना दिलासा! 589 आणि 609 च्या स्वस्त प्लॅनमध्ये 60GB पर्यंत बल्क डेटा, अनलिमिटेड कॉलिंग
description: देशातील आघाडीची टेलिकॉम कंपनी एअरटेलने प्रीपेड ग्राहकांसाठी ट्रायच्या नियमांनुसार 589 आणि 609 चे दोन किफायतशीर प्लॅन्स सादर केले आहेत. यामध्ये दररोजच्या डेटा मर्यादेऐवजी 30 दिवस आणि एक महिन्याच्या वैधतेसह अनुक्रमे 50GB व 60GB एकत्रित डेटा, अनलिमिटेड कॉलिंग, 300 SMS आणि मोफत अ‍ॅडोब एक्सप्रेस प्रीमियम सबस्क्रिप्शन दिले जात आहे, चला तर मग याविषयीची माहिती पुढे जाणून घेऊया.
author: शुभम कुलकर्णी
content:
तुम्ही एअरटेलचे युजर्स असाल तर ही बातमी आधी वाचा. एअरटेल ग्राहकांना दैनंदिन डेटा मर्यादेचे बंधन नको आहे, त्यांच्यासाठी कंपनीने 'TRAI-Mandated' विभागात 589 आणि 609 चे दोन उत्तम पर्याय आणले आहेत. केवळ वीस रुपयांच्या फरकाने ग्राहकांना जास्त डेटा, एक महिन्याची पूर्ण वैधता आणि सुमारे चार हजार रुपये किमतीचे अ‍ॅडोब एक्सप्रेस सबस्क्रिप्शन मोफत मिळवण्याची संधी उपलब्ध झाली आहे.
Bharti Airtel ने आपल्या प्रीपेड ग्राहकांसाठी 'TRAI-Mandated Packs' (ट्रायने अनिवार्य केलेले प्लॅन्स) या विशेष विभागाअंतर्गत 589 आणि 609 किमतीचे दोन फायदेशीर प्लॅन्स उपलब्ध करून दिले आहेत. ज्या ग्राहकांना दररोजच्या डेटा मर्यादेचे बंधन नको आहे आणि ज्यांना आपल्या सोयीनुसार इंटरनेट वापरायचे आहे, त्यांच्यासाठी हे 'बल्क डेटा' प्लॅन्स अत्यंत उपयुक्त ठरत आहेत.
अतिरिक्त फायदे
या दोन्ही प्लॅन्सची तुलना करताना यापूर्वी केवळ 609 च्या प्लॅनमध्येच Adobe Express Premium चा उल्लेख करण्यात आला होता. मात्र, TelecomTalk ने प्रसिद्ध केलेल्या नोव्हेंबर 2026 च्या नवीन रिपोर्टनुसार, 589 आणि 609 या दोन्ही प्लॅन्समध्ये ग्राहकांना समान अतिरिक्त फायदे दिले जातात. यामध्ये प्रामुख्याने सुमारे 4,000 किमतीचे 12 महिन्यांचे मोफत सबस्क्रिप्शन, स्पॅम कॉल्सपासून संरक्षणासाठी 'Airtel Safe' आणि दर 30 दिवसांनी एक मोफत 'Hellotunes' यांचा समावेश आहे.
दोन्ही प्लॅन्सचे फायदे
589 चा प्रीपेड प्लॅन: या पॅकमध्ये ग्राहकांना संपूर्ण 30 दिवसांची वैधता मिळते. या कालावधीत वापरण्यासाठी एकूण 50GB हाय-स्पीड डेटा एकत्र (Bulk) दिला जातो. तसेच, देशभरात कोणत्याही नेटवर्कवर अनलिमिटेड लोकल, STD आणि रोमिंग कॉलिंगसह एकूण 300 SMS (दररोज कमाल 100 SMS मर्यादेसह) मिळतात. हा डेटा संपल्यानंतर प्रति MB 50 पैसे दराने शुल्क आकारले जाते.
609 चा प्रीपेड प्लॅन: केवळ 20 अधिक मोजल्यास ग्राहकांना 1 महिन्याची (कॅलेंडर महिना) वैधता मिळते. म्हणजेच, जर तुम्ही महिन्याच्या 5 तारखेला रिचार्ज केले, तर पुढील रिचार्ज पुढच्या महिन्याच्या 5 तारखेला करावा लागतो. या प्लॅनमध्ये एकूण 60 GB बल्क डेटा, अनलिमिटेड कॉलिंग आणि 300 SMS मिळतात. 31 दिवसांच्या महिन्यात या प्लॅनमुळे ग्राहकांना 1 दिवसाची अतिरिक्त वैधता आणि 10 GB जादा डेटा मिळतो.
TRAI चा नियम आणि Adobe Express ऑफर
टेलिकॉम रेग्युलेटरी अथॉरिटी ऑफ इंडिया (TRAI) च्या निर्देशांनुसार, ग्राहकांना ठराविक वैधतेचे आणि पारदर्शक दर असलेले प्लॅन्स सहज शोधता यावेत यासाठी एअरटेलने त्यांच्या Airtel Thanks App आणि वेबसाइट वर हा स्वतंत्र विभाग सुरू केला आहे.
याशिवाय, Airtel च्या अधिकृत प्रेस रिलीज आणि Adobe Help Center च्या माहितीनुसार, एअरटेलचे ग्राहक 29 जानेवारी 2026 ते 28 जानेवारी 2027 या कालावधीत कोणत्याही क्रेडिट कार्डशिवाय 'एअरटेल थँक्स ॲप'द्वारे 1 वर्षासाठी मोफत Adobe Express Premium क्लेम करू शकतात. तसेच, Airtel Terms & Conditions नुसार, जर ग्राहकाने त्यांचा सध्याचा प्लॅन संपण्यापूर्वीच त्याच किमतीचा (उदा. 589 किंवा 609 चा) पुन्हा रिचार्ज केला, तर उरलेली वैधता नवीन रिचार्जमध्ये जोडली जाते (Accretive Validity).

title: डॉली को 26 साल की उम्र में पता चला कि वह किसी देश की नागरिक नहीं हैं, फिर क्या हुआ?
description: गुजरात की डॉली वडालिया का जन्म मोज़ाम्बिक में हुआ था. वह 25 दिन की उम्र से भारत में रह रही थीं. यहां पढ़ाई की, नौकरी की और शादी भी हुई. लेकिन जब पति के साथ कनाडा जाने के लिए पासपोर्ट बनवाया, तो पता चला कि वह किसी भी देश की नागरिक नहीं हैं.
author: गोपाल कटेशिया
content:
डॉली को 26 साल की उम्र में पता चला कि वह किसी देश की नागरिक नहीं हैं, फिर क्या हुआ?
  - Author, गोपाल कटेशिया
  - पदनाम, बीबीसी गुजराती
- प्रकाशित
- पढ़ने का समय: 9 मिनट
गुजरात के राजकोट के एक अस्पताल में डॉली बराई नाम की 26 वर्षीय महिला डायटीशियन के तौर पर काम करती थीं. उनकी शादी खिलन वडालिया नाम के एक युवक से हुई, जो कनाडा के कैलगरी शहर में नौकरी करते हैं.
शादी समारोह और अन्य रस्में पूरी होने के बाद वडालिया परिवार ने डॉली को भी उनके पति के साथ कनाडा भेजने का फ़ैसला किया. लेकिन उन्हें बड़ा झटका लगा.
उन्हें पता चला कि डॉली दुनिया के किसी भी देश की नागरिक नहीं हैं. इस वजह से डॉली के कनाडा जाने की योजना अधूरी रह गई.
उन्होंने राज्य और केंद्र सरकार के विभिन्न दफ़्तरों से संपर्क किया और अधिकारियों के सामने अपनी बात रखते हुए कहा कि वह 25 दिन की उम्र से राजकोट में ही रह रही हैं. उन्होंने राजकोट में ही पढ़ाई की है और वहीं काम करती हैं. इसलिए वह भारत की नागरिक हैं.
लेकिन अधिकारियों ने विभिन्न क़ानूनों का हवाला देते हुए डॉली वडालिया की दलीलें स्वीकार नहीं कीं. इसके बाद उन्होंने गुजरात हाई कोर्ट का दरवाज़ा खटखटाया. लेकिन वहां से भी उन्हें कोई राहत नहीं मिली.
परिवार तनाव में था. शादी के तीन साल बाद भी पत्नी राजकोट में और पति कनाडा में रह रहे थे. दोनों मजबूरी में दुनिया के दो अलग-अलग महाद्वीपों में रह रहे थे.
हालांकि, उनके मामले को लेकर स्थानीय नेताओं ने केंद्र सरकार के सामने बात रखी, जिसके बाद अब डॉली वडालिया को उम्मीद की एक किरण दिखाई दी है.
व्यापार करने गए बराई परिवार ने रातोंरात मोज़ाम्बिक क्यों छोड़ा?
डॉली वडालिया ने बीबीसी को बताया कि उनके पिता केतन बराई 1995 में व्यापार करने के लिए अफ़्रीकी महाद्वीप के पूर्वी हिस्से में स्थित देश मोज़ाम्बिक गए थे. उनके परिवार के कुछ सदस्य पहले से ही वहां रहते थे.

डॉली के पिता ने मोज़ाम्बिक के समुद्र तट पर स्थित शाई-शाई शहर में किराने की एक दुकान खोली.
इसके बाद उनकी पत्नी आरती बराई भी मोज़ाम्बिक चली गईं. फ़रवरी 2000 में वहां इस दंपती के घर एक बेटी पैदा हुई, जिसका नाम उन्होंने डॉली रखा.
डॉली के माता-पिता ने मोज़ाम्बिक सरकार से उनका जन्म प्रमाणपत्र भी बनवा लिया था.
डॉली वडालिया कहती हैं, "मेरे जन्म के कुछ दिन बाद ही मोज़ाम्बिक में एक तूफ़ान आया. इसकी वजह से शाई-शाई में बहुत बारिश हुई और भयानक बाढ़ आ गई. इसमें मेरे माता-पिता ने जो कुछ भी बनाया था, सब नष्ट हो गया."
"करीब 18 दिन बाद हमें बाढ़ प्रभावित इलाक़े से बचाया गया. मेरे माता-पिता बाढ़ में सब कुछ खो चुके थे, इसलिए वे मुझे लेकर राजकोट वापस आ गए."
डॉली के जन्म के कुछ ही दिनों बाद शाई-शाई में प्राकृतिक आपदा आने के कारण केतन और आरती उनके लिए न तो मोज़ाम्बिक सरकार और न ही भारत सरकार से पासपोर्ट बनवा सके.
परिवार का कहना है कि उस समय मोज़ाम्बिक में भारतीय कॉन्सुलेट की ओर से जारी एक इमरजेंसी सर्टिफ़िकेट के आधार पर दंपती को अपनी बेटी के साथ मोज़ाम्बिक छोड़ने और भारत आने की अनुमति मिली थी.
उस इमरजेंसी सर्टिफ़िकेट के आधार पर बराई दंपती अपनी नवजात बेटी डॉली को लेकर 14 मार्च 2000 को भारत लौट आए.
इसके बाद वे कभी मोज़ाम्बिक नहीं गए और राजकोट में ही बस गए.
डॉली को स्कूल में दाखिला कैसे मिल गया?
राजकोट लौटने के बाद जब डॉली बड़ी हुईं, तो उनके माता-पिता उन्हें शहर के एक स्कूल में दाख़िला दिलाने गए.
डॉली कहती हैं, "मोज़ाम्बिक सरकार की ओर से जारी मेरा जन्म प्रमाणपत्र पुर्तगाली भाषा में था. इसी के आधार पर मुझे स्कूल में दाख़िला मिल गया और मेरा नाम स्कूल के जनरल रजिस्टर में दर्ज कर लिया गया."
"स्कूल की पढ़ाई पूरी होने के बाद मुझे स्कूल की ओर से स्कूल लिविंग सर्टिफ़िकेट (स्कूल छोड़ने का प्रमाणपत्र) दिया गया."
"इसमें भी दर्ज था कि मेरा जन्म मोज़ाम्बिक में हुआ है. इस तरह मेरे पास स्कूल लिविंग सर्टिफ़िकेट के रूप में जन्म से जुड़ा एक और दस्तावेज़ आ गया."
डॉली बताती हैं कि जन्म प्रमाणपत्र और स्कूल लिविंग सर्टिफ़िकेट के आधार पर उन्हें कॉलेज में भी दाख़िला मिल गया.
उन्होंने विज्ञान विषय में स्नातक की डिग्री हासिल की. इसके बाद होम साइंस (फ़ूड एंड न्यूट्रिशन) में मास्टर डिग्री भी प्राप्त की.
भारत सरकार ने उन्हें आधार कार्ड, मतदाता पहचान पत्र और पैन कार्ड भी जारी किए.
डॉली कहती हैं कि दूसरी लड़कियों और युवतियों की तरह उनकी ज़िंदगी भी सामान्य रूप से चल रही थी. लेकिन शादी के बाद उनके जीवन में ख़ुशियां आने के बजाय मानो भूकंप आ गया.
शादी के बाद डॉली से कहा गया कि वह दुनिया के किसी भी देश की नागरिक नहीं हैं
डॉली कहती हैं कि वह इस मान्यता के साथ बड़ी हुई थीं कि वह भारत की नागरिक हैं.
जुलाई 2023 में उनकी शादी खिलन वडालिया से हुई. मूल रूप से राजकोट के रहने वाले खिलन के पास कनाडा का वर्क परमिट है और वह वहां के कैलगरी शहर में काम करते हैं. शादी के बाद परिवार ने डॉली को भी उनके पति के साथ रहने के लिए कनाडा भेजने का फ़ैसला किया.
वीज़ा के लिए आवेदन करने के लिए किसी देश का वैध पासपोर्ट होना ज़रूरी था.
इसलिए डॉली ने भारतीय पासपोर्ट बनवाने के लिए सितंबर 2023 में आवेदन किया और अहमदाबाद स्थित क्षेत्रीय पासपोर्ट कार्यालय से संपर्क किया.
डॉली के जेठ रोनक वडालिया ने बीबीसी गुजराती को बताया, "पासपोर्ट कार्यालय के अधिकारियों ने डॉली का जन्म प्रमाणपत्र मांगा. हमने मोज़ाम्बिक सरकार की ओर से जारी प्रमाणपत्र जमा किया."
"लेकिन पासपोर्ट कार्यालय के अधिकारियों ने उसे मान्य नहीं माना और हमारा आवेदन ख़ारिज कर दिया. उन्होंने हमसे कहा कि डॉली को यह साबित करना होगा कि वह भारतीय नागरिक हैं."
इसके बाद डॉली ने मोज़ाम्बिक में भारतीय कॉन्सुलेट के अधिकारियों से अपने जन्म प्रमाणपत्र को प्रमाणित करवाया. उन्होंने कुछ अतिरिक्त दस्तावेज़ों के साथ मार्च 2025 में एक बार फिर पासपोर्ट के लिए आवेदन किया. हालांकि, पासपोर्ट कार्यालय ने इस बार भी उनका आवेदन स्वीकार नहीं किया और कहा कि वह भारतीय नागरिकता साबित नहीं कर पाई हैं.
इसके बाद डॉली ने राजकोट लौटकर भारतीय नागरिकता का प्रमाणपत्र हासिल करने के लिए ज़िला कलेक्टर कार्यालय से संपर्क किया.
डॉली कहती हैं, "अधिकारियों ने मुझसे कहा कि भारतीय नागरिक बनने के लिए मुझे किसी दूसरे देश का पासपोर्ट जमा करना होगा. इसके बाद ही मुझे भारतीय नागरिकता मिल सकेगी."
"हमने दिल्ली में मोज़ाम्बिक के हाई कमीशन से संपर्क किया."
"लेकिन उन्होंने मुझे साफ़ बता दिया कि मैं मोज़ाम्बिक की नागरिक नहीं हूं. वैसे भी मेरे पास कभी मोज़ाम्बिक का पासपोर्ट था ही नहीं. ऐसे में मैं क्या जमा कराती? मैं तो स्टेटलेस (किसी भी देश की नागरिकता न रखने वाली व्यक्ति) हो गई. इससे मेरी चिंता और बढ़ गई."
हाई कोर्ट का दरवाज़ा खटखटाया, लेकिन राहत क्यों नहीं मिली?
रोनक वडालिया बताते हैं कि काग़ज़ों पर डॉली के स्टेटलेस यानी किसी भी देश की नागरिकता नहीं रखने वाली महिला बन जाने से वडालिया और बराई परिवार तनाव में आ गए.
रोनक वडालिया कहते हैं, "हम सभी बहुत परेशान थे. हमें समझ नहीं आ रहा था कि अब क्या करें, किससे मिलें और किन दस्तावेज़ों के लिए किसके पास आवेदन करें. नियम यह है कि अगर कोई भारतीय विदेश में रहता है और वहां उसके बच्चे का जन्म होता है, तो बच्चे के जन्म के एक साल के भीतर उस देश में स्थित भारतीय हाई कमीशन या कॉन्सुलेट में उसका रजिस्ट्रेशन कराना होता है. ऐसा करने पर बच्चे को विरासत में भारतीय नागरिकता मिल जाती है."
"लेकिन डॉली के माता-पिता बाढ़ में अपना सब कुछ खोने के बाद कभी मोज़ाम्बिक लौट ही नहीं सके. उस समय संचार के इतने साधन भी नहीं थे कि वे किसी दूसरे तरीके से कॉन्सुलेट को इसकी जानकारी दे पाते."
अगर कोई विदेशी नागरिक लगातार सात साल तक भारत में रहता है, तो वह भारतीय नागरिकता हासिल करने के लिए आवेदन कर सकता है. इसके लिए उसे कुछ निर्धारित शर्तें पूरी करनी होती हैं.
लेकिन डॉली के लिए यह रास्ता भी बंद था, क्योंकि उनके पास इस बात का पर्याप्त सबूत नहीं था कि वह मोज़ाम्बिक की नागरिक हैं.
इसलिए डॉली ने जुलाई 2025 में गुजरात हाई कोर्ट में याचिका दायर की. उन्होंने अदालत से मांग की कि पासपोर्ट कार्यालय और राजकोट कलेक्टर कार्यालय के अधिकारियों के फ़ैसलों को रद्द किया जाए और उन्हें भारतीय पासपोर्ट जारी किया जाए.
अप्रैल 2026 में हाई कोर्ट ने फ़ैसला सुनाते हुए डॉली की याचिका ख़ारिज कर दी. अदालत ने कहा कि भारतीय पासपोर्ट हासिल करने के लिए उन्हें भारतीय नागरिक होना साबित करना होगा.
अदालत ने यह भी कहा कि अगर किसी असाधारण परिस्थिति के कारण मोज़ाम्बिक स्थित भारतीय कॉन्सुलेट में जन्म का रजिस्ट्रेशन नहीं हो सका था, तो देरी से रजिस्ट्रेशन के लिए किए गए आवेदन को स्वीकार करने का अधिकार भारत सरकार के गृह मंत्रालय की ओर से संबंधित देश के लिए नियुक्त मुख्य अधिकारी के पास है.
लंबी लड़ाई के बाद डॉली को उम्मीद की किरण क्यों दिखाई दे रही है?
रोनक वडालिया बताते हैं कि भारत के अलग-अलग सरकारी दफ़्तरों और अदालत से राहत नहीं मिलने के बाद परिवार ने पोरबंदर लोकसभा सीट के पूर्व सांसद रमेश धडुक और राजकोट लोकसभा सीट के मौजूदा सांसद परषोत्तम रूपाला से मदद मांगी.
रोनक कहते हैं, "हम उनके पास गए, अपनी परेशानी बताई और उनका मार्गदर्शन मांगा. हमने राज्यसभा के पूर्व सांसद रामभाई मोकरीया से भी संपर्क किया. इन सांसदों ने हमारी बात सुनी और मामले को समझा. इसके बाद रमेशभाई और परषोत्तमभाई ने हमें सिफ़ारिशी पत्र लिखकर दिए और दिल्ली में केंद्रीय गृह मंत्रालय भेजा."
बीबीसी गुजराती से बातचीत में केंद्र सरकार में मंत्री रह चुके परषोत्तम रूपाला ने कहा, "वह महिला फ़िलहाल किसी भी देश की नागरिक नहीं हैं. मुझे उनका मामला बहुत सही लगा. इसलिए मैंने उनकी अर्ज़ी केंद्रीय गृह मंत्रालय तक पहुंचाई और सिफ़ारिश की कि उन्हें भारतीय नागरिकता दी जाए."
रोनक वडालिया बताते हैं कि सांसदों की सिफ़ारिश के बाद दिल्ली में अधिकारियों ने उन्हें सलाह दी कि वे भारत सरकार को एक आवेदन दें. इसमें मोज़ाम्बिक स्थित भारतीय कॉन्सुलेट से डॉली के जन्म का रजिस्ट्रेशन देरी के बावजूद करने का अनुरोध किया जाए.
इसके बाद डॉली ने अधिकारियों की सलाह के मुताबिक भारत सरकार को आवेदन दिया. आख़िरकार विदेश मंत्रालय ने मोज़ाम्बिक स्थित भारतीय कॉन्सुलेट को आदेश दिया कि देरी के बावजूद डॉली के जन्म का रजिस्ट्रेशन किया जाए.
रोनक वडालिया कहते हैं, "इस आदेश के बाद कॉन्सुलेट ने देरी को माफ़ करते हुए डॉली के जन्म का रजिस्ट्रेशन कर लिया और हमें उसका प्रमाणपत्र दे दिया. जब हमने यह प्रमाणपत्र पासपोर्ट कार्यालय के अधिकारियों को दिखाया, तो उन्होंने डॉली का पासपोर्ट आवेदन स्वीकार कर लिया."
इसके बाद दिवाली के दौरान डॉली के फ़ोन पर एसएमएस अलर्ट आया कि उनके पासपोर्ट का आवेदन स्वीकार कर लिया गया है.
डॉली कहती हैं, "मुझे मैसेज मिला कि 11 नवंबर को पोस्टमैन मेरे घर पासपोर्ट पहुंचा देगा. मैं 11 नवंबर को सुबह से ही उसका इंतज़ार करने लगी. मुझे बहुत तनाव था कि सच में पासपोर्ट आएगा या नहीं, क्योंकि मेरी कई कोशिशें पहले नाकाम हो चुकी थीं."
"तनाव की वजह से मैंने घरवालों से कहा कि वे मुझे बुलाएं नहीं. आख़िरकार पोस्टमैन हमारे घर आया और उसने मेरे हाथ में पीले रंग का एक लिफ़ाफ़ा दिया. उस पर मेरा पता लिखा हुआ था."
"जब मैंने उसे खोलकर देखा, तो उसमें सचमुच मेरे नाम का भारतीय पासपोर्ट था. मुझे यक़ीन ही नहीं हो रहा था कि यह वाकई मेरा पासपोर्ट है."
"इस पासपोर्ट ने मुझे स्टेटलेस व्यक्ति से भारतीय नागरिक बना दिया."
डॉली कहती हैं कि वह कनाडा में अपने पति के पास जाने का बेसब्री से इंतज़ार कर रही हैं.
वह कहती हैं, "अब पासपोर्ट मिल गया है, इसलिए हम कनाडा का वीज़ा हासिल करने की तैयारी कर रहे हैं. उम्मीद है कि मैं जल्द ही कनाडा में अपने पति के पास जा सकूंगी."
बीबीसी के लिए कलेक्टिव न्यूज़रूम की ओर से प्रकाशित.
