title: Supreme Court rejects plea to remove video of Italian politician’s ‘Vote Chor’ slogan at Bharat Summit 2026
description: SC rejects plea to remove video of Italian politician chanting “Vote Chor, Gaddi Chhod” at Bharat Summit 2026.
author: The Hindu Bureau
content:
Supreme Court on Friday (November 27, 2026) rejected a plea for removal of videos of Italian politician Giacomo Filibeck raising slogan ”Vote Chor, Gaddi Chhod” during the Bharat Summit 2026 in Hyderabad.
A Bench of Justices Vikram Nath and Aparesh Kumar Singh passed the order while hearing a plea seeking a direction to some social media platforms to remove the videos.
After the Bench said it was dismissing the petition, the petitioner’s counsel urged that the authorities be asked to treat the same as a representation.
Filibeck, Secretary-General of the Party of European Socialists (PES), triggered a political controversy with the purported slogan and praise for Congress leader Rahul Gandhi for his campaign for clean and transparent electoral rolls.
Earlier, in an oral mention, advocate Syed Rizwan Ahmed said Mr. Filibeck, who is the secretary-general of the Party of European Socialists, had partisanly interfered in India’s internal political issues and democratic system by bringing up an “abusive slogan” being used by Opposition leaders targeting the electoral process under Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s government.
The lawyer also narrated how the Italian politician made remarks about his own convictions that the “government here was corrupt, that it was not bona fide”. Mr. Ahmed said Mr. Filibeck had even promised to work with the Opposition in this country to “restore, save and safeguard the democratic process”.
(With PTI inputs)
Published - November 27, 2026 12:56 pm IST

title: For the second time this year, Guindy Children’s Park closed as birds die of suspected flu
description: Guindy Children’s Park in Chennai closes again for precautionary bird death probe amid avian influenza concerns; NIHSAD tests awaited.
author: Geetha Srimathi
content:
Guindy Children’s Park in Chennai will remain closed to the public until November 30 following the death of birds at the facility on Friday (November 27, 2026). The cause of the deaths is yet to be established, a press release issued by the Forest Department said on Friday.
Samples have been sent to the National Institute of High Security Animal Diseases (NIHSAD), Bhopal, for testing. The results are awaited. The closure is a precautionary measure, officials said.
The park will be closed from November 28 to 30, or until further orders. The Forest Department said preventive measures were being implemented in accordance with the Union government’s guidelines.
These include isolating the affected enclosure, disinfecting and sanitising the premises, and intensifying biosecurity measures. The health of other birds and animals in the park is also being closely monitored.
Avian influenza concerns
The latest incident comes amid avian influenza concerns at zoological facilities in Tamil Nadu. Wetland bird enclosures at Arignar Anna Zoological Park in Vandalur were also temporarily closed to visitors after the virus was detected among birds. They reopened on November 18 after two rounds of samples, collected 15 days apart from the affected bird group, tested negative for avian influenza at NIHSAD, Bhopal.
This is the second time this year that Guindy Children’s Park has been closed following bird deaths suspected to be linked to avian influenza. In March, nearly 40 birds died at the Vedanthangal Aviary inside the park. Samples sent to NIHSAD confirmed the presence of the H5N1 virus, prompting the closure of the park from March 20.
The March outbreak saw the death of 30 birds on the night of March 13, including 24 night herons and six pelicans.
Further deaths were reported over the following days, and the last on March 18. The park was reopened after precautionary measures and monitoring.
The Forest Department has appealed to the public to cooperate with the precautionary measures.
Published - November 27, 2026 02:09 pm IST

title: Andhra Pradesh tenant farmers’ body seeks restoration of free crop insurance
description: The AP Tenant Farmers' Association alleged the coalition government failed farmers, with only 28.88 lakh of 1.25 crore e-crop acres insured.
author: G.V.R. Subba Rao
content:
The Andhra Pradesh Tenant Farmers’ Association has accused the coalition government of failing to fulfil its election promises on farmers’ welfare, leaving thousands of farmers, particularly tenant cultivators, struggling with mounting debts following extensive crop losses.
In a statement on Thursday (November 26, 2026), association State general secretary P. Jamal Mallaiah said the government had replaced the free crop insurance scheme with a voluntary system, leaving a large number of farmers without adequate insurance protection.
Nearly 10 lakh acres remained uncultivated during the current kharif season due to drought, while crops across several lakh acres were damaged by deficient rainfall, heavy rains and cyclones Arnab and Murasu, he said.
The government estimated crop damage across 31.59 lakh acres and assessed the input subsidy payable at ₹2,743.78 crore. However, the amount was yet to be released, he said.
Questioning the insurance coverage, he said that against 1.25 crore acres recorded under e-crop, insurance protection was available for only 28.88 lakh acres. Of the 38 lakh acres under paddy cultivation, just 7.50 lakh acres had insurance coverage.
He also alleged that the government had failed to clear pending premium contributions, delaying compensation to eligible farmers. Tenant farmers were particularly vulnerable as they had to bear cultivation expenses and land rent, but faced difficulties obtaining cultivation rights cards and accessing government benefits, he said.
The association leader demanded the restoration of free crop insurance, immediate payment of pending premiums and input subsidy, and direct compensation to actual cultivators, irrespective of land ownership. He also sought higher compensation and transparent disclosure of crop damage assessments.
Published - November 27, 2026 02:22 pm IST

title: Jharkhand couple beats 14-year-old daughter to death over making reels, arrested
description: Police said Kanaklata a Class 8 student was beaten to death with a stick on November 10 Her parents then dumped her body in the quarry in the area
author: India Today News Desk
content:
Jharkhand couple beats 14-year-old daughter to death over making reels, arrested
Police said Kanaklata, a Class 8 student, was beaten to death with a stick on November 10. Her parents then dumped her body in the quarry in the area.
A tribal couple in Jharkhand has been arrested for beating their 14-year-old daughter to death because she spent time on her mobile phone and made reels, news agency Press Trust of India reported, citing a police officer.
Ravindra Murmu and his wife, Sumani, were arrested on Thursday, nearly a fortnight after their daughter Kanaklata Murmu's body was recovered from an abandoned quarry in East Singhbhum district.
Police said Kanaklata, a Class 8 student, was beaten to death with a stick on November 10. Her parents then dumped her body in the quarry in the area.
The couple tried to mislead villagers and the police by claiming that their daughter had gone missing. Her body was recovered on November 13.
Following the recovery, angry villagers blocked a road and demanded the arrest of those responsible and adequate compensation for the bereaved family. They staged another road blockade the next day in support of their demands.
The couple's conduct after the body was recovered raised suspicion, but investigators could not initially act against them because of a lack of concrete evidence, the officer told Press Trust of India.
“Police conducted a thorough investigation and gathered evidence. Technical assistance and human intelligence helped us obtain vital clues,” he said.
The couple were later detained for questioning and confessed to the crime during interrogation. Kamalpur police station Officer-in-Charge Dhananjay Paswan confirmed that they were arrested on Thursday.
Asked about the motive, the officer said the parents had objected to their daughter spending time on her mobile phone and making reels. They assaulted her with a stick, leading to her death.
Police are investigating whether anyone else was involved in the killing, which followed an argument over the teenager's mobile phone use.

title: Naga ancestors return home after 100 years in Oxford museum
description: The return of 39 Naga ancestral remains from the Pitt Rivers Museum of Oxford University in the UK is more than a homecoming After nearly a century away the remains many of them skulls are returning to Nagaland bringing attention to colonial-era collecting and the Naga community039s efforts to reclaim its past
author: India Today News Desk
content:
Naga ancestors return home after 100 years in Oxford museum
The return of 39 Naga ancestral remains from the Pitt Rivers Museum of Oxford University in the UK is more than a homecoming. After nearly a century away, the remains, many of them skulls, are returning to Nagaland, bringing attention to colonial-era collecting, and the Naga community's efforts to reclaim its past.
"Ancestors are like stars in the night sky. We can't always see them, but we know they're always there."
It is an anonymous quote used in remembrance of those who have passed away. Today, it resonates with the Naga people as they prepare to welcome their ancestors back to their homeland.
The 39 ancestral remains, held at Britain's Pitt Rivers Museum for nearly a century, which include those of two children, a woman and a village chief, were handed over to a Naga delegation earlier this month following years of discussions, and will reach Nagaland on Friday, according to Nagaland Today. Their arrival marks a significant moment for communities seeking to reclaim a part of their history taken away during British colonial rule.
The return is part of a larger effort to restore ancestral connections, recognise historical wrongs, and give communities the opportunity to decide how their forebears should be remembered and honoured.
The remains had been housed at the Pitt Rivers Museum, part of the University of Oxford, for decades. Many were collected by British administrators John Henry Hutton and James Philip Mills, who served in the Naga Hills during the colonial period between approximately 1910 and 1940.
The repatriation process gathered momentum in 2020, when Naga anthropologist Dolly Kikon approached the museum after learning that it was reviewing the ethics of displaying human remains. What followed was six years of discussions, historical research and consultations involving Naga representatives and the institution.
Kikon, a professor at the University of California, Santa Cruz, has described the development as the first repatriation of human remains to India of its kind.
HOW REMAINS OF NAGA ANCESTORS ENDED UP IN OXFORD
The Pitt Rivers Museum, established in 1884, grew into one of the world's prominent repositories of archaeological and anthropological material. Its collection, which now exceeds 600,000 objects, includes material gathered from different parts of the world during the colonial era.
A considerable portion of its holdings came through British administrators, travellers, missionaries and researchers who collected material during their time in territories under colonial control.
Among those who contributed to its Naga collection were Hutton and Mills. Both were members of the Indian Civil Service and served in administrative positions in the Naga Hills.
Hutton, who became Deputy Commissioner of the Naga Hills District in 1917, developed an interest in the region's communities and their traditions. His academic work included books on the Angami and Sema Nagas. Mills, who succeeded him as Deputy Commissioner in the 1930s, also undertook extensive ethnographic research and authored studies on the Lhota, Ao and Rengma Naga communities.
Their administrative positions gave them considerable access to the region and its people. However, the circumstances in which some of the material entered museum collections raise uncomfortable questions about the relationship between colonial authority and the acquisition of cultural and human remains.
One particularly revealing episode concerns Mills's 1936 expedition to Pangsha village. Travelling with an armed escort, he sought the return of human heads reportedly taken from a neighbouring community. His account of the expedition also referred to the museum receiving what he described as valuable specimens.
The episode illustrates how colonial officials could combine their administrative and military authority with their interest in ethnographic collections. What might have been presented as academic collecting was not always separate from the unequal power structures of the time.
WHY MANY OF THE REMAINS ARE SKULLS
An important aspect of the repatriation is that many of the remains are skulls, reflecting the historical practice of headhunting among several Naga communities.
The practice needs to be understood within its historical and cultural setting rather than viewed only through the lens of colonial descriptions. For certain Naga communities, headhunting was historically associated with ideas of warriorhood, courage, social standing and the protection of one's village. It was embedded in a complex system of traditional beliefs and community practices.
The taking of an enemy's head was not an isolated act of violence. It carried social and symbolic significance within the societies in which the practice existed. The skulls subsequently became part of the historical record of a period when warfare, inter-village rivalries and ideas of honour shaped aspects of community life.
This context, however, does not diminish the importance of how the remains were acquired or the need to return them to their communities of origin.
The larger Naga collection at the Pitt Rivers Museum also includes material connected with human remains. According to the museum's records cited in research on the collection, 219 items are classified as human-remains-related material. These comprise 39 ancestral human remains and 178 objects containing, or potentially containing, human hair.
The scale of the collection highlights that the return of the 39 individuals is an important beginning, rather than necessarily the end of discussions surrounding Naga ancestral material held abroad.
A RETURN FROM UK AFTER YEARS OF NEGOTIATIONS
The decision to reconsider the museum's display of human remains became an important turning point in the process.
During the Covid-19 pandemic in 2020, the Pitt Rivers Museum removed human remains, including shrunken heads, from public exhibition as part of a wider reassessment of its colonial collections. This opened up conversations about the future of material that had remained in the institution for generations.
The museum subsequently worked with the Forum for Naga Reconciliation and representatives from different Naga communities to determine how the remains should be returned.
In early November, the institution formally transferred custodianship of the 39 remains to a Naga delegation comprising community leaders and scholars.
The museum's director, Laura Van Broekhoven, acknowledged the lengthy nature of the process and expressed hope that the initiative would contribute towards reconciliation and healing.
For Nagaland, the immediate significance is more intimate. After spending close to a century and thousands of miles away, 39 ancestors are finally returning to their land.

title: Defeat to dominance? How non-NDA parties are boosting BJP's confidence on delimitation bill
description: The BJP-led NDA fell 54 votes short of the two-thirds majority needed to pass its delimitation and women039s reservation legislation in April 2026 Eight months on the BJP is confident of getting it passed This is how changing political equations have altered parliamentary maths in a few months
author: Avinash Kateel
content:
Defeat to dominance? How non-NDA parties are boosting BJP's confidence on delimitation bill
The BJP-led NDA fell 54 votes short of the two-thirds majority needed to pass its delimitation and women's reservation legislation in April 2026. Eight months on, the BJP is confident of getting it passed. This is how changing political equations have altered parliamentary maths in a few months.
Just eight months ago, the BJP-led NDA government fell short of the numbers needed to push through its delimitation and women's reservation legislation. It was the first time in 12 years of Prime Minister Narendra Modi's tenure that a major government bill had been defeated on the floor of Parliament. Now, the political arithmetic appears to have changed. With reports of back-channel conversations with opposition MPs, possible support from regional parties and fresh proposals to address concerns raised by southern states, the BJP-led government is preparing for another test of strength in Parliament on the delimitation bill.
The government, which suffered a legislative defeat in April 2026 when its Constitution (131st Amendment) Bill failed to secure the required two-thirds majority, is now counting on regional parties, including the DMK and the Sharad Pawar-led NCP (SP), to bridge the gap. Then there are the rebel Trinamool Congress MPs who have flocked to the obscure NCPI.
The question is whether these additional political equations can deliver the numbers that the NDA could not muster in April. The BJP seems to be confident. The government kept the monsoon session alive well into the winter months.
After more than 100 days since Parliament was prorogued following the Monsoon Session, the government has now announced fresh sittings of both Houses.
Union Parliamentary Affairs Minister Kiren Rijiju on Thursday (November 26) said the Centre had requested the Lok Sabha Speaker and the Rajya Sabha Chairman to reconvene the Lok Sabha on Monday, November 30, and the Rajya Sabha on Wednesday, December 2, to transact "essential government business". Subject to the exigencies of business, the sittings of both Houses may conclude on December 2, 2026, he said.
According to news reports, the government is expected to use the session to introduce a fresh delimitation bill, with the revised proposals likely to address some of the objections that led to the earlier legislation's defeat.
FROM 293 IN 2024 TO 298 VOTES IN APRIL: THE BJP'S 2/3RD CALCULATION
The 2024 Lok Sabha election results left the BJP with 240 seats, 32 short of the 272 majority mark. Its allies contributed another 53 seats, taking the NDA's tally to 293.
The Telugu Desam Party, with 16 MPs, and the JD(U), with 12, were the two biggest pillars of the alliance. The Shiv Sena led by Eknath Shinde contributed seven MPs, while the Lok Janshakti Party (Ram Vilas) won five seats. Other allies included the Janata Dal (Secular) of Karnataka, Andhra Pradesh's Jana Sena Party and the UP-based Rashtriya Lok Dal.
The BJP thus formed the government with a cushion of 21 seats above the majority mark, but its dependence on regional NDA allies was evident.
That arithmetic was put to a different test in April 2026.
On April 17, the Constitution (131st Amendment) Bill, which sought to facilitate delimitation, expand the Lok Sabha and advance 33% women's reservation, was defeated in the Lower House.
Of the 528 MPs present and voting, 298 supported the Bill while 230 opposed it. Eleven MPs were absent. The government needed 352 votes, or two-thirds of the members present and voting, but fell short by 54.
The 298 votes in favour were five more than the NDA's original 2024 election tally of 293.
The bill's defeat exposed the difficulty of passing a constitutional amendment without support from the ruling alliance.
WHAT HAS CHANGED IN BJP'S NUMBERS IN PARLIAMENT NOW?
This time, the BJP is attempting to widen its support base by reaching out to regional parties and breakaway factions of Opposition parties.
The NDA's current estimate of support is around 320 MPs. This figure includes 20 rebel Trinamool Congress MPs and one Shiromani Akali Dal MP. The possible backing of four YSR Congress Party (YSRCP) MPs could take the tally to 324.
The government is also looking to secure the support of the DMK's 22 Lok Sabha MPs and the NCP (SP)'s eight MPs. If both parties back the legislation, the number could rise to 354.
However, even this expanded tally would leave the government short of the numbers required. With three Lok Sabha seats vacant, the effective strength of the House is 540. If all members vote, a constitutional amendment would require at least 360 votes, leaving the government six short even after accounting for the possible support of the YSRCP, DMK and NCP (SP).
The BJP, however, is not banking solely on these regional parties. According to a report in The Indian Express, the ruling party's leaders have indicated that six MPs from smaller parties have assured support. Another account suggests that three MPs belonging to two parties have individually agreed to back the legislation.
According to India Today TV's sources, the BJP leadership is reportedly aiming for around 380 votes, well above the 360-mark requirement.
WHY THE DMK'S 22 AND NCP-SP'S 8 MPs MATTER TO THE BJP
One of the biggest changes in the BJP's parliamentary arithmetic is the possibility of support from the DMK, which had opposed delimitation under its former CM MK Stalin but is now indicating that it might not oppose every proposal brought by the BJP-led government.
Two senior DMK leaders have told The Indian Express newspaper that the party could support delimitation if Tamil Nadu's existing share of roughly 7.2% of Lok Sabha seats is protected. The party's concern is that southern states, which have successfully controlled population growth, should not lose political representation when constituencies are redrawn.
The Centre's reported proposal to increase Lok Sabha seats by 50% uniformly across all states could address some of these concerns. The government is also considering delinking delimitation from the Census, according to India Today TV's Aishwarya Paliwal.
The DMK's strained relationship with the Congress, which ended its alliance with the Dravidian giant after the 2026 Assembly elections and joined the Vijay-led TVK government, could also influence its decision. For the BJP, the DMK's 22 MPs offer an opportunity to secure support beyond the NDA.
The other important regional player is the Maharashtra-based NCP (SP), which has eight Lok Sabha MPs. Its parliamentary leader, Supriya Sule, has said the party will examine the bill before deciding its stand, leaving open the possibility of support if it considers the legislation to be in the national interest. This is significant because the NCP (SP) is part of the INDIA bloc.
Together, the DMK and NCP (SP) account for 30 Lok Sabha MPs. If both parties back the legislation, they could substantially alter the arithmetic that defeated the government in April. The reported government support base of 324 MPs, which includes possible backing from rebel TMC MPs, the YSRCP and the Eknath Shinde-led Shiv Sena faction, could rise to 354 with the addition of the DMK and NCP (SP). That would still leave the government six votes short of the 360 required if all 540 sitting members vote.
WHAT IS THE MODI GOVERNMENT OFFERING TO PARTIES?
The BJP's renewed outreach is taking place alongside a possible change in the proposed delimitation framework.
According to India Today TV, the Union Cabinet is considering two proposals: a uniform 50% increase in Lok Sabha seats across all states and delinking the delimitation exercise from the Census.
The earlier proposal sought to expand the Lok Sabha from 543 to a maximum of 850 seats. However, the April draft did not explicitly incorporate the assurance of a proportional 50% increase in seats for every state. This became a major point of disagreement with regional parties, particularly the DMK and the NCP (SP).
The government is now attempting to address that concern before the special sitting of Parliament, scheduled from November 30 to December 3.
The Cabinet meetings — which are underway at the time of the publication — consideration of a revised proposal could therefore be crucial in determining whether the regional parties translate their conditional support into votes.
The numbers show why the BJP is looking beyond the NDA and seems confident. In 2024, the alliance's 293 seats were sufficient to form the government. In April 2026, 298 votes were not sufficient to pass a constitutional amendment. This time, the government has the numbers that it is attempting to assemble a broader parliamentary support beyond the NDA.

title: Supreme Court dismisses plea against Italian leader’s ‘vote chor’ slogan at Telangana event
description: While dismissing the plea, the bench said, “Let the government regulate freedom of speech of citizens first and then regulate that of foreigners." | India News
author: Abraham Thomas
content:
Supreme Court dismisses plea against Italian leader’s ‘vote chor’ slogan at Telangana event
While dismissing the plea, the bench said, “Let the government regulate freedom of speech of citizens first and then regulate that of foreigners."
The Supreme Court on Friday dismissed a petition seeking action against an Italian political functionary for raising a “demeaning political slogan” at Bharat Summit 2026 in Telangana and to pull down social media posts carrying such derogatory content.
A bench of justices Vikram Nath and Aparesh Kumar Singh said, “Why have you filed a petition under Article 32 of the Constitution? You can file a complaint against the person,” as it refused to entertain the petition filed by a lawyer Zahid Ali.
The petition argued by advocate Syed Rizvan Ahmad said that the objectionable comments were made by Giacomo Filibeck, an Italian political representative and Secretary-General of the Party of European Socialists, at a public event in India and a mechanism should be put in place to regulate the speeches made by foreigners on Indian soil.
The controversial slogan
Filibeck, while participating at the event organised on November 13 and 14 by the Telangana government, had said, “vote chor, gaddi chhod” – the political slogan coined by the Congress amid controversy over the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls.
The bench said, “Let the government regulate freedom of speech of citizens first and then regulate that of foreigners,” while adding, “The petition is dismissed.”
‘Petition not politically motivated’
Ahmed said that the petition is not politically motivated as it has not mentioned Lok Sabha Leader of Opposition Rahul Gandhi, the Indian National Congress or the Telangana chief minister A Revanth Reddy who were present at the site when the comments were made.
“So according to you, they have freedom to say anything,” the bench remarked as Ahmed pointed out that a foreigner cannot make political slogans when the law does not permit him to do so. “The government must regulate the speeches made by foreigners. It can even take steps to pull down social media posts carrying these speeches,” Ahmed said.
The petition filed through advocate Pulkit Agarwal said, “The Italian political representative not only raised the vulgar, derogatory and demeaning political slogan but also translated the same for other foreign delegates. The aforesaid derogatory and disrespecting slogan was in bad taste and derogatory to India's democratic processes, and a slogan that has been prominently associated with the Indian National Congress and its political campaign.”
The plea sought a direction to the Centre to take action under the provisions of the Immigration and Foreigners Act, 2025, the applicable visa conditions and other relevant laws to ensure that foreign political representatives, delegates and dignitaries visiting India do not engage in political or anti- government activities.
Under section 7 of the Immigration and Foreigners Act, 2025, the Centre is empowered to regulate or restrict the presence and activities of foreign nationals in India through appropriate orders, directions and instructions. Further, section 23 provides consequences for violation of visa conditions and other specified statutory requirements.

title: Supreme Court grants bail to former AAP legislator Naresh Balyan
description: Former AAP legislator Naresh Balyan said the evidence against him is inadmissible and he was never named originally | India News
author: Abraham Thomas
content:
Supreme Court grants bail to former AAP legislator Naresh Balyan
Former AAP legislator Naresh Balyan said the evidence against him is inadmissible and he was never named originally
The Supreme Court on Friday granted bail to former Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) legislator Naresh Balyan in a Maharashtra Control of Organised Crime Act (MCOCA) case for alleged links with UK-based gangster Kapil Sangwan.
A bench of Justices Vikram Nath and Aparesh Kumar Singh directed Balyan to cooperate with the trial while granting him bail. The Delhi police opposed the bail, calling the charge of organised crime serious.
Balyan moved the Supreme Court after the Delhi high court denied him bail. In August, the Supreme Court issued notice to the police after Balyan argued that the high court failed to note that under MCOCA the statutory requirement is not fulfilled, as there should be a continuing lawful activity of the organised crime in which the individual is charge-sheeted in the preceding 10 years.
Senior advocate Vikas Singh, who appeared for Balyan along with advocate Vivek Jain, said that the main witnesses in the case rescinded their statements. He pointed out that he had complained to the police, alleging that the person with whom he is alleged to have links was threatening him. Police granted Balyan protection based on his complaint.
Balyan said the evidence against him is inadmissible and he was never named originally.
The trial court denied bail to Balyan, observing that the criminal nexus between a politician and a gangster is perhaps the “most perilous threat” confronting a nation and its citizens and must be addressed with severity.
In his petition, Balyan said that he has been incarcerated since December 2025 and the investigation against him is complete.
In May, Delhi police filed a charge sheet against Balyan, alleging that he used his political clout to financially support Sangwan’s syndicate and shield its members from arrest. Balyan allegedly used virtual private networks, an encrypted messaging app to communicate, and phones registered in the name of his family to communicate with Sangwan and to evade detection.
Balyan was arrested on December 4 last year on allegations of organised crime, shortly after he was granted bail in the extortion case.

title: Gujarat ATS foils JeM attack plot, arrests Assam man with AK-47 rifle targeting Vadodara Air Force Station
description: Gujarat ATS has arrested a suspected Jaish-e-Mohammed (JeM) terrorist with assault rifles and bullets in Vadodara district on Friday, officials said, | India News
author: HT News Desk
content:

Gujarat ATS foils JeM attack plot, arrests Assam man with AK-47 rifle targeting Vadodara Air Force Station
Gujarat ATS has arrested a suspected Jaish-e-Mohammed (JeM) terrorist with assault rifles and bullets in Vadodara district on Friday, officials said,
The Gujarat Anti-Terrorist Squad (ATS) on Friday arrested a 22-year-old man allegedly linked to Pakistan-based terror outfit Jaish-e-Mohammed (JeM) for plotting an attack on a security establishment in the Vadodara district.
An AK-47-type automatic assault rifle, two empty magazines, 23 live cartridges, a JeM flag, and approximately ₹20,000 in cash were recovered from his possession, officials added.
The accused, Mohammad Saharul Islam Kabiruddin, a resident of Assam, was arrested near Paldi bus stand in Vadodara on Friday after the ATS received intelligence that he was in contact with a JeM handler and planning an attack using an automatic assault rifle.
“ATS received information that an individual from another state, affiliated with Jaish-e-Mohammed, was planning to enter Gujarat within the coming days, armed with an automatic assault rifle, with the intent of attacking a security establishment,” Gujarat ATS DIG Sunil Joshi said during a briefing on Friday.
The ATS had received intelligence that the suspect was expected to reach Gujarat within two to three days to prepare for the attack. Deputy Superintendent of Police Harsh Upadhyay led a team that verified the information through technical surveillance and human intelligence before tracking the suspect to Vadodara.
The investigation led the ATS to Hotel Milan near Sayajigunj railway station, where the accused had stayed. He had left the hotel around 9 am without completing the checkout formalities. The ATS subsequently established that he was travelling from Dahod towards Vadodara after switching off his regular mobile phone.
“It was discovered that a suspicious individual, identified as Mohammad Islam Kabiruddin, a native of Assam, had arrived in Vadodara after switching off his regular phone and was staying at a hotel… Monitoring this number revealed that he was travelling back toward Vadodara from Dahod. Consequently, roadblocks were set up at various locations,” Joshi said.
The ATS set up roadblocks near Golden Chowkdi on the Halol-Vadodara road and apprehended him near Paldi bus stand, close to Hotel Darshan.
An examination of his mobile phones indicated contact with Jaish-e-Mohammed. Investigators said they found images of the gate of Air Force Station Vadodara and other important structures marked with red crosses, which the accused identified as target points. The phones also contained a reconnaissance video of the Air Force Station, Google Maps screenshots, web links, audio and video clips, links to WhatsApp channels and groups, and instructional videos on operating an AK-47-type rifle.
Joshi said the accused was in contact with a Pakistan-based JeM handler identified as Mufti Rafiq alias Ibn Abdullah.
During questioning, the accused disclosed that he had been provided ₹50,000 to purchase a new mobile phone and arrange logistical support for the planned operation.
“The accused intended to carry out this terrorist act and then migrate to Pakistan to join the ranks of Jaish-e-Mohammed, with the ultimate goal of attaining ‘martyrdom’,” Joshi said.
A case has been registered at the Gujarat ATS police station under Sections 18, 20, 23(1) and 38 of the Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act, Sections 61, 148 and 149 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, and Section 25(1-AA) of the Arms Act.

title: Beyond Cricket And Curry: How Australia Is Using G'Day Namaste To Deepen India Ties
description: G'Day Namaste, the Australian Government's flagship festival celebrating Australia in India, will run across New Delhi, Mumbai, Chennai, Bengaluru, Kolkata and Kohima from Dec 7-12
author: Apoorva Misra, Siddhant Mishra
content:
Beyond Cricket And Curry: How Australia Is Using G'Day Namaste To Deepen India Ties
G'Day Namaste, the Australian Government's flagship festival celebrating Australia in India, will run across New Delhi, Mumbai, Chennai, Bengaluru, Kolkata and Kohima from Dec 7-12
Got Question about the News?
For decades, the India-Australia relationship was summed up in a cliché: cricket, curry and the Commonwealth. This December, Canberra wants Indians to see a fuller picture.
G’Day Namaste, the Australian Government’s flagship festival celebrating Australia in India, will run across New Delhi, Mumbai, Chennai, Bengaluru, Kolkata and Kohima from December 7 to 12. Prime Minister Anthony Albanese had announced the festival during PM Narendra Modi’s visit to Australia in July this year and it is being delivered with the Centre for Australia-India Relations and Cricket Australia.
- Will Jacks Ruled Out Of England-Australia T20I Series After Nasty Injury
- Cricket Australia Sandpapergate Probe To Also Include 2017-2018 Ashes
- 1st Time In 94 Years! All Top-5 India Batters Score 50+ In Same Innings Of Away Test
- GTA VI Is Here. And After 20 Years, I'm Tempted to Pick Up a Controller Again.
Big Bash Makes History In Chennai
The headline event is cricket. On December 12, the Melbourne Renegades and Perth Scorchers will play the opening match of the men’s Big Bash League (BBL) season at Chennai’s MA Chidambaram Stadium. It will be the first BBL regular-season match played outside Australia, and the first foreign cricket league game ever staged in India.
“Australians and Indians speak a common language when it comes to cricket," said Australian High Commissioner Philip Green. He called the fixture a way to “use sport to grow the connections in many other fields of our thriving partnership".
Cricket Australia’s Alistair Dobson called Chennai “home to some of the most passionate cricket fans on the planet".
Beyond The Boundary
The programme also covers business, education, clean technology and culture. It includes:
• The AUSTCHAM India-Australia Business Summit in New Delhi
• A Business Council of Australia Investment Roundtable and a Sports Summit in Mumbai
• Education and clean-tech showcases in Chennai
• Australian film and music events across cities
Australia will also be an official partner country at Nagaland’s Hornbill Festival. Kohima’s place on the list stands out, since festivals like this usually stay in the big metros. The festival will also feature First Nations culture and the Indian diaspora’s role in modern Australia.
“Australia and India have never been closer," Green said. Ryan Neelam, CEO of the Centre for Australia-India Relations, said the relationship is “ultimately about people".
The Bigger Picture
The cultural push comes as defence and security ties deepen. During PM Modi’s July visit, the two leaders signed a Joint Declaration on Defence and Security Cooperation. They also agreed to a classified Joint Maritime Security Collaboration Roadmap; an Australia-India Partnership on Cyber, Critical Technologies and Supply Chains (PACTS) that included a defence pillar.
Analysts link this to similar concerns about China’s assertiveness in the Indo-Pacific and the prospect of more mercurial US policy. Both countries are also Quad members. With Washington harder to predict, middle powers are relying more on each other.
Economic ties are moving more slowly. Trade has grown since the Economic Cooperation and Trade Agreement (ECTA) came into force in 2022. But the Asialink analysis of PM Modi’s visit warns that economic relations lag strategic cooperation and that the two sides are yet to achieve their true trade potential. This is why business summits and investment roundtables sit next to the cricket in this festival.
The diaspora connects all of this. There are now one million people of Indian origin in Australia. That community has become a political force, and Indian students remain a major source of income for Australian universities. Visa rules and student caps have caused friction in the past, so Australia also wants to show Indian audiences that it is a welcoming place.
Seen this way, G’Day Namaste is more than a cultural calendar. Canberra is trying to make Indian public opinion match the closeness the two governments already have. A sold-out BBL game in Chennai could be its most effective diplomatic tool.
Quick Answers
G’Day Namaste is the Australian Government's flagship festival celebrating Australia in India, running across New Delhi, Mumbai, Chennai, Bengaluru, Kolkata, and Kohima from December 7 to 12, 2026. The festival aims to showcase business, education, clean technology, and culture to deepen bilateral ties beyond traditional cricket and curry clichés.

title: CISF Finds Hidden Knife In Passenger's Belt At Delhi Airport: What Flyers Can And Cannot Carry
description: A pocket-sized knife hidden in a belt buckle slipped past the appearance of an ordinary accessory - until an X-ray scan flagged it. What else could get stopped at airport security?
category: Auto, Cities, Explainers, India, New Delhi
author: Parishmita Saikia
content:
CISF Finds Hidden Knife In Passenger's Belt At Delhi Airport: What Flyers Can And Cannot Carry
A pocket-sized knife hidden in a belt buckle slipped past the appearance of an ordinary accessory - until an X-ray scan flagged it. What else could get stopped at airport security?
Got Question about the News?
Delhi News: A small knife concealed inside a belt buckle was detected by Central Industrial Security Force (CISF) personnel during security screening at Delhi’s Indira Gandhi International (IGI) Airport, officials said on Friday, November 27.
The passenger had arrived from Hong Kong and was scheduled to take a connecting flight to Raipur in Chhattisgarh when the item was detected. The CISF shared a video of the recovery on social media, showing a pocket-sized knife concealed inside a black metallic belt buckle.
- Streamline Your Workflow: Multi-Device Bluetooth Keyboards and Mice Under Rs 2,500
- Mid-Air Chaos As Man Tries To Open Flight Door, Pinned Down By Co-Passengers, Crew | Video
- Delhi To Kashmir Drug Racket Busted: How A Bus Check Led NCB To A Secret Warehouse
- ‘In Total Rs 20,000 A Day’: Bengaluru Man Left Stunned After Driver Reveals Earnings From Cab Driving And Car Rentals
According to the force, a CISF screener noticed an unusual metallic object in the baggage during X-ray screening. The bag was then referred for a physical examination, which revealed the concealed knife.
In a post on X, the CISF said the detection reflected the alertness and professional competence of its personnel. The force did not share further details about the passenger or the subsequent action taken in the case.
???????????????? ???????????????????????????? ???????????????????????????????????? ???????????????????? ???????? ???????????????? ???????????????????????? ???????? ???????????????????? ????????????????????????????!Demonstrating keen observation and professional vigilance, CISF personnel at Delhi Airport detected a concealed knife embedded in a passenger’s belt buckle during security screening.
The passenger had arrived from Hong Kong and was scheduled to travel onward to Raipur. During X-BIS image interpretation, the screener noticed an unusual metallic object and referred the baggage for physical examination, which led to the recovery of the concealed knife. The prohibited item was removed in accordance with prescribed security procedures.
The detection reflects CISF’s unwavering vigilance and commitment to maintaining robust aviation security through professional competence and alertness.
#CISF #AirportSecurity #PassengerSafety #AviationSecurity #Knife
@CISFHQrs @PIB_India @DelhiAirport
— APS – CISF (@CISFAirport) November 27, 2026
Why The Detection Matters
The incident is a reminder that airport security checks are not limited to obvious weapons. Items that appear to be ordinary personal accessories can also conceal objects that may pose a risk inside an aircraft.
A knife, even a small one, can be used as a weapon in the confined space of an aircraft cabin. This is why sharp objects are restricted in hand baggage, regardless of whether they are carried separately or concealed inside another object.
The detection also underlines the role of baggage-screening technology and physical checks. When an X-ray image shows an unusual or unclear object, security personnel may refer the bag for additional examination.
What Items Are Not Allowed In Cabin Baggage?
Passengers should check the rules before packing, as several everyday objects are prohibited in cabin baggage. The restrictions are intended to prevent items that could be used to injure passengers or crew, interfere with aircraft operations or create other safety risks.
Some commonly restricted items include:
- Knives And Sharp Objects: Pocket knives, utility knives, box cutters, razor blades, meat cleavers, pointed metal scissors, swords and similar sharp objects.
- Tools: Hammers, drills, screwdrivers, pliers, wrenches, saws, crowbars and other tools that could be used as weapons.
- Weapons And Replicas: Firearms, ammunition, air guns, realistic toy weapons, stun guns and other weapon-like objects.
- Self-Defence Items: Pepper spray, mace, tear gas, electroshock devices and similar incapacitating substances.
- Flammable And Explosive Materials: Fireworks, firecrackers, explosives, petrol, lighter fluid and several types of flammable substances.
- Certain Sporting Equipment: Cricket bats, golf clubs, hockey sticks, baseball bats, bows and arrows, and other equipment that could cause injury.
The exact restrictions can vary by item and airline. Some objects are prohibited in cabin baggage but may be carried in checked-in baggage if they are properly packed and meet applicable safety conditions.
Can Knives Be Carried In Checked-In Baggage?
In general, knives are not permitted in cabin baggage but may be carried in checked-in baggage, subject to the airline’s conditions. Air India’s published baggage guidelines, for instance, list knives of different lengths and types as prohibited in carry-on baggage but permitted in checked-in baggage.
Sharp objects placed in checked-in baggage should be securely wrapped or sheathed to prevent injuries to baggage handlers and security personnel. Passengers should also check the rules of the airline and destination country before travelling.
There are limited exceptions for certain blunt-edged items. Air India’s guidelines, for example, allow round-bladed knives, butter knives and plastic cutlery without a sharp edge in cabin baggage. These exceptions do not extend to a concealed knife such as the one detected at Delhi airport.
Are There Exceptions For Kirpans Or Other Special Items?
Some items have specific provisions. Air India’s published guidelines allow a kirpan subject to size restrictions – a blade no longer than 15.2 cm and a total length, including the handle, not exceeding 22.8 cm. However, the same guidelines state that kirpans are not allowed on international flights or on the domestic leg of an international flight.
Medical equipment and essential medicines may also be allowed under specified conditions. Passengers carrying items such as syringes, insulin supplies or other medical devices should follow airline requirements and carry supporting documentation where necessary.
These limited provisions do not create a general exemption for sharp objects. A knife hidden inside a belt buckle would not qualify as an ordinary belt accessory simply because it is small or concealed.
Other Important Baggage Rules Flyers Should Know
Sharp objects are not the only items subject to restrictions. Liquids, aerosols and gels in cabin baggage are generally subject to a 100 ml-per-container limit under the airline guidance cited below. Medicines, baby food and certain other essential items may be allowed as exceptions, subject to screening and applicable conditions.
Spare lithium batteries and power banks must generally be carried in cabin baggage rather than checked-in luggage, and they are subject to capacity and quantity limits. Air India’s guidelines, for example, permit no more than two spare batteries, including power banks, per person under the specified conditions.
Passengers should also remember that an item being allowed in checked-in baggage does not automatically mean it can be carried on board. The distinction between cabin and checked baggage is important, and security personnel may inspect or remove prohibited articles during screening.
Quick Answers
A CISF screener noticed an unusual metallic object in the baggage during X-ray screening, which led to a physical examination that revealed a pocket-sized knife concealed inside a black metallic belt buckle.

title: BMW M 1000 RR launched at ₹59.90 lakh with carbon-fibre winglets and slide control
description: BMW Motorrad has launched the updated M 1000 RR in India at ₹59.90 lakh. The superbike gets a 218hp engine, new carbon-fibre winglets and electronic rider assistance systems.
author: Vivek Dubey
content:
BMW M 1000 RR launched at ₹59.90 lakh with carbon-fibre winglets and slide control
- Published OnNov 27, 2026 | 14:22 IST
- Last Updated OnNov 27, 2026 | 14:22 IST
BMW Motorrad has brought its track-focused superbike to India, packing a higher-output engine, heavily revised carbon aerodynamics, and advanced slide-control electronics.
Engine produces 218hp
The updated M 1000 RR is powered by a revised 999cc, liquid-cooled, inline four-cylinder engine producing 218hp (160kW), an increase of 6hp over the previous model, according to BMW Motorrad. The engine also develops 113Nm of peak torque. The engine gets a revised cylinder head with new intake port design, a redesigned combustion chamber and updated titanium valves. BMW has also modified the titanium exhaust system, including the cylinder-head flanges, oval header inlets and pre-silencer.
The updated BMW M 1000 RR leans into a corner during a racetrack test.
Power is transmitted to the rear wheel through a six-speed gearbox. The motorcycle also gets a new M short-stroke throttle with a reduced rotation angle of 58 degrees, allowing riders to reach full throttle with less wrist movement.
Winglets generate 23.1kg downforce
The updated BMW M 1000 RR gets a redesigned front fairing and M Winglets 3.0 made from carbon fibre-reinforced plastic (CFRP). The new aerodynamic components are designed to generate greater downforce and improve front-end stability at high speeds.
The M Winglets Evolution 3.0 generate up to 23.1kg of downforce, a claimed 33% increase over the outgoing model. The motorcycle also gets revised front and side fairing panels and a taller windscreen.
BMW Motorrad has made changes to the chassis, including a new engine mount on the left side and revised flex characteristics around the steering head. The motorcycle has a claimed kerb weight of 194kg and comes with a 1.5kg M Motorsport frame as standard.
Gets new electronic aids
The updated M 1000 RR introduces Slide Control and Brake Slide Assist. The Dynamic Traction Control (DTC) system now uses steering-angle sensor technology to offer separate Slip Control and Slide Control functions.
Slide Control helps riders manage controlled slides during acceleration, while Brake Slide Assist works with BMW Race ABS Pro to support controlled slides under braking. The braking system also gets a new 'Slick' ABS Pro setting designed for racetrack use.
The motorcycle features a 6.5-inch TFT instrument display and seven riding modes, including Rain, Road, Dynamic, Race and three configurable Race Pro modes. Other electronic features include Launch Control, Pit Lane Limiter, Wheelie Control, Engine Drag Torque Control and Shift Assistant Pro for clutchless upshifts and downshifts.
It also gets M Brake Ducts, which direct cooling air towards the brake callipers to help reduce their operating temperatures during demanding track sessions.
M Competition Package standard
The M Competition Package is offered as standard on the India-spec BMW M 1000 RR. It includes M Carbon wheels, additional M Carbon components, an M footrest system that saves 220g, a DLC-coated M Endurance chain and a milled and anodised swingarm pivot point. The package also includes an activation code for the M GPS Laptrigger.
The updated BMW M 1000 RR comes with a three-year, unlimited-kilometre warranty, which can be extended to the fourth and fifth years. BMW Motorrad also provides 24x7 roadside assistance throughout the year.

title: Is there a budget that can fix Delhi’s notorious air? Some say ₹25,000 crore
description: A proposed clean-air roadmap by IIT Delhi alumni suggests spending up to ₹25,000 crore to tackle Delhi-NCR pollution and achieve good air quality by 2030.
author: CNBCTV18.com
content:
Is there a budget that can fix Delhi’s notorious air? Some say ₹25,000 crore
- Edited byTenzin Norzom
- Published OnNov 27, 2026 | 13:59 IST
- Last Updated OnNov 27, 2026 | 14:01 IST
Fixing Delhi's hazardous air demands a massive multi-year investment spanning freight overhauls, public transport, and cleaner power plants, coupled with cross-agency coordination. Beyond capital spending, the roadmap banks on a citizen-led movement to drive lasting behavioral change. Discover how the proposal plans to finance truck scrappage and rural stubble burning controls.
For years, Delhi’s toxic air has been treated as an inevitable part of life in the capital. Every winter, pollution levels rise, the air turns hazardous, restrictions are imposed and the political blame game begins.
Meanwhile, its residents have learned to check the Air Quality Index (AQI) before stepping outside almost on instinct. Hopes of respite from the pollution grow dimmer while the same cycle repeats year after year.
So what would it cost to actually fix Delhi’s air? About ₹20,000-25,000 crore over the first three years, according to a proposed clean-air roadmap prepared by an IIT Delhi alumni network last year.
The plan aims to put Delhi-NCR on a path toward an average AQI below 50, considered good air quality, by 2030.
Also Read: Delhi's pollution puzzle: How AQI is calculated and what official figures may be missing
Spending that money alone, however, will not mean a decisive end to the air pollution menace.
The group has proposed a citizen-led movement called PRAAN or People Reclaiming Air And Nature, bringing together residents, doctors, scientists, schools, resident welfare associations, businesses and local officials. The idea is to move citizens from being passive recipients of government action to what the group describes as “co-creators” of clean air.
The roadmap argues that Delhi-NCR already has much of what is needed to tackle its pollution: the technology, expertise, funding and policy frameworks. What is missing, it says, is coordinated action across agencies, governments and communities.
That is where the ₹25,000 crore question gets more complicated. The money would not go toward one silver-bullet solution. Instead, the proposal divides the spending across trucks and freight, public transport, thermal power plants, road dust, stubble burning, clean cooking and pollution monitoring.
Where would the ₹25,000 crore go?
A significant chunk would target trucks and freight, which the plan identifies as a high-leverage area.
It proposes using the Vahan Stack and automatic number-plate recognition systems at toll points to identify polluting trucks. It also suggests a green contribution of ₹2,500 for BS4 and older heavy goods vehicles and ₹1,500 for light goods vehicles entering NCR.
A proposed Naya Safar Yojana would target about 2.1 lakh trucks with interest subsidies, EMI support and scrappage incentives to help operators replace older vehicles with BS6, CNG or electric trucks. The estimated government support for the full program is ₹4,000 crore.
Public transport is another major component, with about ₹2,000 crore proposed for a bus transition program.
The proposal also sets aside ₹6,000 crore for flue-gas desulphurization systems at nine thermal power plants, ₹1,500 crore for road repairs and mechanical sweeping, and ₹1,000 crore over three years for tackling stubble burning.
For households, it proposes a clean-cooking program covering 8 lakh households, with about ₹280 crore in leveraged financing through carbon credits. On the technology side, it calls for about 3,000 low-cost pollution sensors across Delhi-NCR at an estimated cost of ₹40-50 crore.
The larger argument behind the plan is that Delhi's air cannot be fixed by Delhi alone. Pollution moves across state and city boundaries, while responsibility for transport, industry, roads, construction, waste and agriculture is divided among multiple agencies.
The proposal therefore calls for an airshed-wide approach and a stronger delivery role for the Commission for Air Quality Management, backed by public dashboards, measurable targets and regular monitoring.
And alongside that government machinery, the citizen movement is meant to keep the pressure on through ward-level groups, citizen reporting, school programs, public pledges and regular reviews.

title: Avore Electric localises 90% of electric motorcycle parts, develops rare-earth-free motors
description: Avore Electric has achieved 90% domestic sourcing for its electric motorcycles and developed rare-earth-free motors in-house, but is yet to begin customer deliveries after its August 2026 launch.
author: Vivek Dubey
content:
Avore Electric localises 90% of electric motorcycle parts, develops rare-earth-free motors
- Published OnNov 27, 2026 | 13:57 IST
- Last Updated OnNov 27, 2026 | 13:57 IST
Avore Electric is prioritising deep domestic sourcing and proprietary rare-earth-free motors to shield its motorcycle lineup from global supply chain risks, while delaying customer deliveries to complete rigorous quality validation. Find out how the company plans to scale its local vendor network.
Avore Electric, the electric motorcycle brand of Samarth E-Mobility, has localised 90% of its component sourcing in India and developed rare-earth-free motors in-house.
However, the company is yet to begin customer deliveries following its electric motorcycle launch in August 2026, as it continues to validate components and strengthen its domestic supplier network.
The company said its 90% localisation figure is calculated by total part count. The remaining 10% comprises specialised components, including battery cells, magnets and semiconductors, which are currently sourced from global suppliers.
Avore Electric is exploring opportunities to onboard Indian suppliers for these components as domestic manufacturing capabilities expand, with the aim of reducing import dependence and strengthening India's domestic electric motorcycle manufacturing ecosystem.
Motor technology
Avore Electric has developed a motor that eliminates the use of rare-earth minerals in its magnet technology. The motor also features an auto-tuning function that enables automatic tuning, an application the company says is among the first of its kind in India.
It has filed a patent for the technology, with the aim of strengthening indigenous EV engineering and reducing the risk of supply chain disruptions.
The company also manufactures motor controllers, digital instrument displays, battery packs, tank lights and position lamps in-house. It said the approach gives it greater control over component development, quality and integration.
Delivery timelines
Despite launching its electric motorcycle range in August 2026, Avore Electric has not started customer deliveries. The company said it is following a quality and validation process and will begin deliveries only after its products meet the required standards.
Avore Electric's EX2 electric motorcycle, featuring the company's in-house developed components and rare-earth-free motor technology.
Priyank Rakholiya, Co-founder of Samarth E-Mobility, said the company's efforts to develop a domestic supplier network may have extended its rollout timelines.
“For us, quality is non-negotiable, and we would rather delay deliveries than bring a product to market that falls short of our standards,” Rakholiya said.
Avore Electric has been working with micro, small and medium enterprises (MSMEs) to improve their manufacturing processes and meet automotive-grade requirements. Its engineering and quality teams have worked with vendors to improve production precision, consistency and process controls.
The company has also introduced Advanced Product Quality Planning (APQP) and Production Part Approval Process (PPAP) to validate component design, engineering and manufacturing tolerances before mass production.
Manufacturing and testing
Avore Electric's manufacturing facility in Chhatral, Gujarat, spans 150,000 sq. ft. and has an installed capacity of 15,000 electric two-wheelers per month. The company has not disclosed its current production volumes, as customer deliveries have not commenced.
The facility follows quality management practices aligned with ISO 9001 and IATF 16949 standards. Its processes include Failure Mode and Effects Analysis (FMEA) to identify potential product failures, Statistical Process Control (SPC) to monitor manufacturing variations and Poka-yoke systems to minimise assembly-line errors.
The company also maintains traceability of components, sub-assemblies and software versions, from raw material sourcing and production to after-sales service.
Its battery production line includes automated cell grading and sorting, laser marking, wire bonding and charge-discharge cycle testing. The motor production line uses controlled thermal processes, precision bearing assembly and dynamometer testing before the motors are integrated into the motorcycles.
Prices and warranty
Avore Electric's electric motorcycle range comprises three variants: EX1, EX2 and EX2S. Their introductory prices are ₹1,24,999, ₹1,49,999 and ₹1,69,999, respectively. The motorcycles have completed the required homologation process.
The company offers a standard battery warranty of three years, along with an additional two-year warranty as part of its initial customer offering, taking the total coverage to five years.
On the policy front, Avore Electric has submitted an application for incentives under the PM E-DRIVE scheme. The company said its domestic sourcing strategy helps reduce logistics and transportation costs by bringing suppliers closer to its manufacturing facility. It also improves coordination with vendors and reduces emissions associated with long-distance transportation.

title: 'अहम विधेयक लेकर आ रहे...', परिसीमन बिल की अटकलों के बीच रिजिजू का बड़ा बयान; विपक्ष को दी खास सलाह
description: संसद के विशेष सत्र और परिसीमन बिल को लेकर चल रही अटकलों के बीच केंद्रीय संसदीय कार्यमंत्री ने कहा कि सरकार इस सत्र के दौरान एक अहम विधेयक लेकर आ रही है, जिसपर सभी दलों के सांसदों को चर्चा करनी चाहिए. उन्होंने इस दौरान किसी विधेयक के नाम का जिक्र नहीं किया.
author: अभिनव त्रिपाठी
content:
केंद्र सरकार की ओर से संसद के विशेष सत्र बुलाए जाने के बाद परिसीमन बिल को लेकर काफी चर्चा की जाने लगी है. जहां एक ओर महिला आरक्षण और परिसीमन बिल को पेश किए जाने की बात कही जा रही है, तो वहीं एफसीआरए बिल को लेकर भी अटकलें लगाई जा रही हैं. इस बीच संसदीय कार्यमंत्री किरेन रिजिजू का अहम बयान सामने आया है. उन्होंने कहा कि सरकार इस विशेष सत्र के दौरान अहम विधेयक लाने जा रही हैं. हालांकि, उन्होंने इस संबंध में अधिक जानकारी नहीं दी.
दरअस, गुरुवार (26 नवंबर) को किरेन रिजिजू ने सोशल मीडिया प्लेटफॉर्म एक्स पर एक पोस्ट किया और कहा कि सरकार ने लोकसभा के अध्यक्ष और राज्य सभा के सभापति के सामने 30 नवंबर से संसद का विशेष सत्र बुलाने की अपील की है. इसके कुछ समय बाद ही लोकसभा सचिवालय ने एक आधिकारिक बयान जारी किया और बताया कि 18वीं लोकसभा के आठवें सत्र का दूसरा भाग सोमवार, 30 नवंबर से शुरू होने वाला है.
संसदीय कार्यमंत्री किरेन रिजिजू ने कहा कि इस विशेष सत्र के दौरान सरकार महत्वपूर्ण विधेयक लाने जा रही है. हालांकि, इस दौरान उन्होंने इसके बारे में अधिक जानकारी नहीं दी. रिजिजू ने सभी राजनीतिक दलों से अपील करते हुए कहा कि सभी को इस बात का ध्यान रखना होगा कि संसद का विशेष सत्र के दौरान सार्थक चर्चा हो और कार्रवाही सुचारू रूप से चल सके.
इसके अलावा उन्होंने कहा कि कोई भी सांसद हल्की या कोई गैर-जिम्मेदाराना बात न करे और कोई पार्टी सदन में हंगामा न करे. रिजिजू का कहना है कि सभी सांसदों को अपनी बात रखने का पूरा मौका किसी भी स्थिति में मिलना चाहिए.
#WATCH | Delhi: On Parliament’s Special Session, Union Parliamentary Affairs Minsiter Kiren Rijiju says, "The government has decided to convene a four-day parliamentary session. We have communicated this to the Speaker of the Lok Sabha and the Chairman of the Rajya Sabha. We intend to bring forward significant legislative business in the Lok Sabha on November 30 and December 1, followed by the same in the Rajya Sabha on December 2 and 3. I have reached out to all political parties and held discussions with the leaders of major parties. Some MPs have made statements—on social media and in the broader media—suggesting that the government does not follow established rules. Such frivolous remarks should be avoided; the government is fully empowered to convene a session whenever there is important legislative business to address—a practice that has long been the norm. I do not wish to dwell on the past, but there are historical precedents where sessions were convened without the formal prorogation of the preceding one. This is a parliamentary democracy; it is entirely standard for the government to summon Parliament when there is critical national business to conduct. When a 'special session' is called, it signifies that there is work of particular importance—vital bills or national business to be addressed. To dismiss such a session as unconstitutional or to claim that the winter session has been prematurely terminated is irresponsible—especially coming from Members of Parliament. How could the mere act of convening a session be 'unconstitutional'? I urge these MPs to refrain from making such trivial or baseless claims. You are Members of Parliament; this is the very forum for deliberation. Parliament exists precisely so that its members can discuss matters of national importance and voice their perspectives. Therefore, as we convene this special session, I request the leaders of all political parties and every Member of Parliament to engage wholeheartedly. Whatever bills or business the government introduces, let there be a thorough and meaningful debate within the House. Whether or not you agree with the proposals is an entirely separate matter. In a democracy, you are free to agree with the government or to voice your opposition to its actions. However, the parliamentary session must proceed. The nation is listening. People across the country will observe and remember how we present our views in Parliament. Therefore, it is the responsibility of all Members of Parliament to ensure that the proceedings run smoothly..."
— ANI (@ANI) November 27, 2026
समाचार एजेंसी एएनआई के अनुसार, किरेन रिजिजू ने बताया कि विशेष काम के लिए ही संसद का विशेष सत्र बुलाया जा रहा है. केंद्रीय मंत्री ने कहा कि 30 नवंबर और 1 दिसंबर को लोकसभा में चर्चा होगी. वहीं, 2 और 3 दिसंबर को बिल पर राज्यसभा में चर्चा की जाएगी. वहीं, रिजिजू ने विपक्षी नेताओं को उन बयानों पर नाराजगी जताई है, जिसमें संसद के विशेष सत्र को असंवैधानिक बताया गया था.
उन्होंने कहा कि जब विशेष सत्र बुलाया जाता है, तो उसका उद्देश्य किसी जरूरी विधेयक या राष्ट्रीय महत्व के मुद्दे पर चर्चा करना होता है. विशेष सत्र को बुलाने की प्रक्रिया को असंवैधानिक कहना गैर-जिम्मेदाराना है. संसद का मंच बहस और चर्चा के लिए है. सरकार की ओर से जो भी प्रस्ताव पेश किए जाएं, उसपर सभी दलों को गंभीरता से चर्चा करनी चाहिए. सहमत होना या न होना एक अलग विषय है. (इनपुट- एएनआई)

title: इलाज के बहाने 11 महीने तक यौन शोषण: दरिंदे प्रोफेसर-डॉक्टर ने छात्रा के साथ किया दुष्कर्म, बताने पर दी 5 साल तक फेल करने की धमकी
description: महाराष्ट्र में एक डॉक्टर और प्रोफेसर पर 22 साल की सेकेंड ईयर की छात्रा के साथ दुष्कर्म का आरोप लगा है. आरोपी डॉक्टर ने छात्रा को किसी को बताने पर फेल करने की धमकी भी दी. उसके खिलाफ पुलिस में मामला दर्ज किया गया.
author: श्रुति कौल
content:
Maharashtra Crime News: महाराष्ट्र में बीड शहर के एक होम्योपैथिक मेडिकल कॉलेज से बेहद चौंकाने वाला मामला सामने आया है. यहां एक प्रोफेसर पर अपनी ही एक छात्रा के साथ महीनों तक यौन उत्पीड़न का आरोप लगा है. छात्रा के मुताबिक, आरोपी इलाज के बहाने रोज उसके साथ दुर्व्यवहार करता था और किसी को बताने पर फेल करने की धमकी देता था. मामले को लेकर शिवाजीनगर पुलिस ने आरोपी डॉक्टर को गिरफ्तार कर लिया है. उसके खिलाफ आगे की जांच की जा रही है.
रिपोर्ट के मुताबिक, 22 साल की पीड़िता होम्योपैथिक मेडिकल कॉलेज में सेकेंड ईयर की छात्रा बताई जा रही है. वह PCOD की समस्या से जूझ रही थी, जिसकी जांच के लिए वह लगातार अस्पताल जाती रहती थी. जनवरी 2026 में जांच के बहाने कॉलेज में प्रोफेसर के तौर पर काम कर रहे डॉक्टर अनीस अहमद ने उसके साथ छेड़छाड़ करने की कोशिश की, उसे गलत तरीके से छुआ और उसे यौन उत्पीड़न का शिकार बनाया. छात्रा ने अपनी शिकायत में बताया कि जब वह मेडिकल जांच के लिए अस्पताल में थी, तब आरोपी प्रोफेसर ने जांच के बहाने उसके साथ दुर्व्यवहार किया. छात्रा के विरोध करने पर आरोपी प्रोफेसर उसे धमकी देने लगा.
पीड़ित छात्रा के मुताबिक, आरोपी प्रोफेसर ने उससे कहा,' अगर तुमने किसी को इस बारे में बताया, तो मैं तुम्हें परीक्षा में फेल कर दूंगा और अगले 5 साल तक इसी एकेडमिक ईयर में अटकाए रखूंगा. पीड़िता ने ये भी आरोप लगाया कि यह उसके साथ हुई कोई पहली घटना नहीं है. उसका दावा है कि जनवरी 2026 से प्रोफेसर ने बार-बार उसे मेडिकल इलाज या जांच के बहाने बुलाया और 11 महीने की अवधि में 3-4 बार इसी तरह लगातार उसका उत्पीड़न किया. आरोपी लगातार उसे चेकअप के बहाने बार-बार अस्पताल बुलाता था. छात्रा ने भी फेल होने के डर से ग्यारह महीने तक आरोपी के दुर्व्यवहार को सहन किया.
लगातार हो रहे उत्पीड़न और धमकियों से डरी हुई छात्रा ने आखिरकार हिम्मत जुटाई और शिवाजीनगर पुलिस स्टेशन में आरोपी के खिलाफ शिकायत दर्ज कराई. पुलिस ने शिकायत पर कार्रवाई करते हुए तुरंत मामला दर्ज किया और आरोपी डॉक्टर अनीस अहमद को गिरफ्तार कर लिया. इस घटना से मेडिकल और एजुकेशन इंडस्ट्री में भारी आक्रोश फैल गया है. पुलिस मामले की आगे जांच कर रही है.

title: हर मिनट करेगा 5000 राउंड गोलों की बौछार, दुश्मन होगा लाचार! भारत रूस से खरीदेगा डिफेंस और अटैक वाला 'जंगबाज'!
description: भारत और रूस के बीच कुल 52 पैंटसिर-S1M एयर डिफेंस सिस्टम खरीदने पर बातचीत चल रही है, जिनमें 13 रूस से आएंगे और 39 मुल्क में लाइसेंस के तहत बनाए जाएंगे.
author: रचित कुमार
content:
जल्द ही भारतीय सेना को एक ऐसा आसमानी रक्षक मिलने वाला है, जो हर मिनट 5000 राउंड गोले दाग सकता है.सॉलिड डिफेंस के साथ-साथ विस्फोटक अटैक कर सकता है, और आसमान में दुश्मन की हर साजिश को मटियामेट कर सकता है. हम बात कर रहे हैं पैंटसिर-S1M एयर डिफेंस मिसाइल सिस्टम की, जिसे लेकर भारत और रूस में बातचीत चल रही है.अगर ये डील फाइनल हुई,तो फिर ये रूसी जंगबाज हिंदुस्तान सरहदों की रखवाली करेगा.
रणभूमि में बारूदी तूफान लाने वाला एक जंगबाज, जल्द ही भारत की सरजमीं पर दस्तक देने वाला है. ये बैटल ग्राउंड का ऐसा शिकारी है, जो डिफेंस भी करता है और ताबड़तोड़ अटैक भी. नाम है पैंटसिर-S1M एयर डिफेंस मिसाइल सिस्टम. रूस के पैंटसिर-S1M एयर डिफेंस मिसाइल सिस्टम को लेकर बड़ी खबर सामने आई है. मीडिया रिपोर्ट्स में दावा किया जा रहा है कि भारत रूस से पैंटसिर-S1M एयर डिफेंस मिसाइल सिस्टम खरीद सकता है. रक्षा मंत्रालय 52 पैंटसिर-S1M सिस्टम को खरीदने की तैयारी में है, जिनमें से 13 पैंटसिर-S1M सिस्टम सीधे रूस से आयात किए जाएंगे, तो वहीं 39 सिस्टम भारत के रक्षा संयंत्रों में लाइसेंस के जरिए बनेंगे.
पैंटसिर-S1M को भारत के मल्टी-लेयर्ड एयर डिफेंस सिस्टम में शामिल किया जाएगा, जिसमें पहले से ही रूस का S-400 लॉन्ग-रेंज एयर डिफेंस मिसाइल सिस्टम मौजूद है. यानी जमीन से लेकर आसमान तक, रूसी जंगबाज ऐसा सुरक्षा चक्रव्यूह बनाएंगे,जिसे भेद पाना नामुमकिन होगा.
पैंटसिर-S1M की सबसे खास बात ये है कि जंग के मैदान में इसे दुश्मन के लड़ाकू विमान, हेलिकॉप्टर, क्रूज मिसाइल, गाइडेड बम और स्वार्म ड्रोन जैसे कम ऊंचाई पर उड़ने वाले खतरों को तहस-नहस करने के लिए डिजाइन किया गया है. पैंटसिर-S1M एयर डिफेंस सिस्टम को S-400 की तरह विध्वंसक माना जाता है. यूक्रेन युद्ध में भी रूसी डिफेंस ने इस जंगबाज का जबरदस्त तरीके से इस्तेमाल किया था.इतना ही नहीं, यूरोप और NATO देशों के साथ-साथ अमेरिका भी इस एयर डिफेंस सिस्टम से थर्राता है.
अब आप अंदाजा लगाइए कि अगर पैंटसिर-S1M एयर डिफेंस सिस्टम S-400 के साथ पाकिस्तान और चीन के बॉर्डर पर तैनात हुआ, तो दुश्मन मुल्क के पैरों तले जमीन खिसक जाएगी, क्योंकि अब आपको पैंटसिर-S1M से जुड़ी वो अहम जानकारियां बता रहे हैं, जो इसे जंग का सबसे दमदार लड़ाका बनाती है.
पैंटसिर-S1M एयर मिसाइल सिस्टम की सबसे खास बात ये है कि चलते हुए भी ये टारगेट पर निशाना लगा सकता है.वहीं इस जंगबाज में फेज्ड-ऐरे रडार इलेक्ट्रो-ऑप्टिकल सेंसर और फायर-कंट्रोल सिस्टम होते हैं, जो कई हवाई लक्ष्यों को एक साथ ट्रैक और इंगेज कर सकते हैं, और पलक झपकते ही उन्हें तबाह कर सकते हैं.

title: 'Very Significant Business': Kiren Rijiju Keeps Delimitation Bill Suspense Alive, Urges MPs To Be Constructive
description: Kiren Rijiju keeps the Delimitation Bill speculation alive ahead of Parliament's Special Session, saying the government has 'very significant business' lined up and urging MPs to participate constructively.
author: Asian News International
content:
'Very Significant Business': Kiren Rijiju Keeps Delimitation Bill Suspense Alive, Urges MPs To Be Constructive
Kiren Rijiju keeps the Delimitation Bill speculation alive ahead of Parliament's Special Session, saying the government has 'very significant business' lined up and urging MPs to participate constructively.
- India News
- 3 min read
New Delhi: Union Parliamentary Affairs Minister Kiren Rijiju on Friday said the government would bring forward "very significant business" during the upcoming Special Session of Parliament, while urging all Members of Parliament to participate constructively in the proceedings amid speculation over the proposed Delimitation Bill.
Responding to speculation about the Delimitation Bill, Rijiju said, "I will provide details later regarding the specific bills to be introduced during the session. For now, I can inform you that we are bringing forward very significant business, and all Members of Parliament should participate constructively. The world is watching--India is the largest democracy--and it is our duty to conduct these parliamentary sessions with a sense of responsibility."
Responding to Opposition leaders' remarks questioning the need for the Special Session, Rijiju said Parliament convenes for different sessions throughout the year and special sessions are called whenever necessary. He appealed to political leaders to avoid making comments that could affect the functioning of the House.
"I have already appealed against making such comments. Parliament convenes for various sessions--the Monsoon, Winter, and Budget sessions--and special sessions are also called when necessary. Members are free to express their views openly within Parliament, but it is everyone’s collective responsibility to ensure that the House functions effectively," he said.
Advertisement
Rijiju's remarks come amid speculation that the proposed Delimitation Bill could be taken up during the upcoming sittings. The government has not yet specified the Bills that will be introduced during the session.
The Lok Sabha Secretariat has announced that the Second Part of the Eighth Session of the Eighteenth Lok Sabha will commence on November 30 and is likely to conclude on December 3, subject to the exigencies of government business.
Advertisement
Rijiju had earlier said that the government had requested the Lok Sabha Speaker and the Rajya Sabha Chairman to reconvene the Lower House on November 30 and the Upper House on December 2, respectively, to transact essential government business.
The proposed Delimitation Bill has drawn criticism from several Opposition parties, with leaders raising concerns over linking the exercise with the implementation of women's reservation.
Nationalist Congress Party-Sharadchandra Pawar (NCP-SP) MP Supriya Sule on Friday kept cards close on delimitation, saying, "The session has been announced, but I don't have the agenda. I have not seen the bill yet. Until I see the bill, I cannot say anything."
Communist Party of India (CPI) MP P Sandosh Kumar reiterated his party's opposition to the Bill in its existing form, saying that linking women's reservation with delimitation was unacceptable.

title: Big Political Reunion In Punjab: Akali Dal Returns to NDA After 6 Years Ahead of 2027 Assembly Polls
description: The Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) and the Shiromani Akali Dal (SAD) have formally announced an alliance ahead of the Punjab Assembly elections, with leaders from both parties pledging to eradicate the drug menace from the state.
author: Namya Kapur
content:
Big Political Reunion In Punjab: Akali Dal Returns to NDA After 6 Years Ahead of 2027 Assembly Polls
The Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) and the Shiromani Akali Dal (SAD) have formally announced an alliance ahead of the Punjab Assembly elections, with leaders from both parties pledging to eradicate the drug menace from the state.
- India News
- 3 min read
New Delhi: In a major realignment in Punjab politics ahead of the 2027 Assembly elections, the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) and the Shiromani Akali Dal (SAD) formally revived their pre-poll alliance on Tuesday, ending a six-year separation.
According to reports, BJP national president Nitin Nabin and SAD president Sukhbir Singh Badal formalised the tie-up in the presence of Union Home Minister Amit Shah at the BJP headquarters in New Delhi.
Ahead of the formal announcement, which coincided with the auspicious occasion of Guru Nanak Jayanti, Nabin offered prayers at Gurdwara Rakab Ganj Sahib in the national capital, and senior BJP leaders felicitated Badal before addressing the press.
Senior leaders from both parties, including Punjab BJP president Kewal Singh Dhillon, former state chiefs Sunil Jakhar and Ashwani Sharma, and veteran Akali Dal leader Baldev Singh Bhunder, were present in Delhi to mark the reunion.
Advertisement
Ending a Six-Year Rift Over Farm Laws
The renewal of the partnership brings two of the National Democratic Alliance’s (NDA) oldest constituents back together after their decades-long association collapsed in September 2020.
At the time, the Akali Dal walked out of the NDA in protest against the Centre's three agricultural laws, with SAD MP Harsimrat Kaur Badal resigning from the Union Cabinet.
Advertisement
Although the central government subsequently repealed the farm laws, both parties contested the 2022 Punjab Assembly elections and the 2024 Lok Sabha polls independently.
Political observers noted that the reconciliation opens the door for the Akali Dal's formal return to the NDA at the Centre, including the possible induction of Harsimrat Kaur Badal back into the Union Cabinet.
The Electoral Arithmetic Behind the Reunion
Both parties have faced significant electoral headwinds in Punjab while contesting separately.
In the 2022 Assembly elections, the Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) swept to power by winning 92 of the state's 117 seats with roughly 42 per cent of the vote share, relegating both the Congress (22.98 per cent) and the traditional Akali-BJP combine to the margins.
In that election, the Akali Dal secured 18.38 per cent of the votes, while the BJP and its smaller allies garnered around 8 per cent. Seat-Sharing and Organisational Preparations
While the top leadership has sealed the alliance, negotiations over seat-sharing and candidate selection remain a critical next step.
Just a day before the alliance announcement, Punjab BJP president Kewal Singh Dhillon constituted a 16-member State Election Committee for the 2027 polls, comprising prominent leaders such as Manpreet Badal, Tarun Chugh, Sunil Jakhar, Preneet Kaur, and Ravneet Singh Bittu, tasked with shaping the party's campaign strategy and drafting a chargesheet against the state government.
The revival of the BJP-SAD alliance drew sharp criticism from rival political camps in the state. Meanwhile, both the Congress, which has launched its Punjab Mangda Insaaf campaign, and the ruling Aam Aadmi Party, led by Chief Minister Bhagwant Mann and national convener Arvind Kejriwal, have already stepped up their grassroots mobilisation and candidate announcements, setting the stage for a fiercely contested multi-cornered battle in 2027.
