title: 'If It Suits Us, We Will Accept It': DMK's TKS Elangovan On Revised Delimitation Bill Ahead Of Special Parliament Session
description: DMK spokesperson TKS Elangovan says the party will consider supporting the revised Delimitation Bill if its concerns and suggestions are addressed ahead of the special Parliament session.
author: Asian News International
content:
'If It Suits Us, We Will Accept It': DMK's TKS Elangovan On Revised Delimitation Bill Ahead Of Special Parliament Session
DMK spokesperson TKS Elangovan says the party will consider supporting the revised Delimitation Bill if its concerns and suggestions are addressed ahead of the special Parliament session.
- India News
- 4 min read
Chennai: Dravida Munnetra Kazhagam (DMK) spokesperson TKS Elangovan on Friday said the party would examine the Centre's proposed revised delimitation Bill before taking a final stand, asserting that the DMK would consider supporting the legislation if its concerns and suggestions had been incorporated.
Speaking to reporters, Elangovan said the party had opposed the earlier draft of the delimitation Bill over concerns about its potential impact on states and regional representation. However, he maintained that the DMK was open to examining the revised version once it was formally introduced.
He emphasised that the party's position would depend on the provisions of the fresh Bill and whether the concerns raised by states and regional parties had been addressed.
"The old bill (delimitation), we had opposed. If this (new) bill is acceptable, we will accept it. Let the bill come first, then we will see how they have reworked the bill. Let us see whether it will affect the states or not; the state or regional parties have to decide,” Elangovan told ANI.
Advertisement
He further said the DMK would assess the revised legislation before commenting on its provisions, adding that the party would consider accepting it if its suggestions had been taken into account.
“Let us see how the fresh delimitation, the fresh bill, how the fresh bill comes. After going through it, we can comment on it. If it suits us or if it has taken our views also, then we have to accept it. But let us see; let the bill come," he added.
Advertisement
Elangovan's remarks come amid an intensifying political debate over the proposed delimitation exercise and women's reservation ahead of the reconvened Parliament session.
On Friday, Tamil Nadu Congress Committee (TNCC) president Manickam Tagore criticised the DMK over its reported change of stand on the proposed Delimitation Bill, while accusing the BJP-led Centre of making a "desperate" attempt to secure the numbers required to pass the legislation in Parliament.
In a post on X, Tagore alleged that the Centre was attempting to garner the support of Opposition parties and secure the tacit backing of some parties to reach the required 360 votes for the proposed legislation during the upcoming parliamentary sittings.
The Congress leader also questioned the government's decision to convene a brief four-day parliamentary sitting from November 30 to December 3, alleging that the move was aimed at pushing through major legislative proposals without adequate discussion.
"The Union BJP government has shelved the monsoon session without properly concluding it, leaving it pending for over 100 days, and has hastily convened Parliament for just 4 days (November 30 to December 3) on Constitution Day, November 26. Normally, 15 days’ advance notice must be given before convening a new session, and MPs must be given 14 days to submit questions," he said.
Tagore further alleged that the government had cancelled Question Hour, Zero Hour and Private Members' Bills, claiming that the move deprived Members of Parliament of opportunities to raise public issues and exercise their parliamentary rights.
"But the Modi government, unable to answer the people’s questions, has cancelled Question Hour, Zero Hour and private members’ bills, stripping MPs of their constitutional rights. Rather than discussing the country’s major problems or the people’s livelihoods, the BJP is desperate to push through the 131st Constitution Amendment Bill to increase Lok Sabha constituencies from 550 to 850 and the delimitation bill by taking a shortcut," he said.
In an apparent reference to the DMK, Tagore aimed at parties that had earlier made strong statements about protecting Tamil Nadu's interests, alleging that they had now softened their position on the proposed legislation.
On Thursday, the Lok Sabha Secretariat announced that the Second Part of the Eighth Session of the Eighteenth Lok Sabha would commence on November 30 and was likely to conclude on December 3, subject to the exigencies of government business.
Union Minister of Parliamentary Affairs Kiren Rijiju said the government had requested the Lok Sabha Speaker and the Rajya Sabha Chairman to reconvene the Lower House on November 30 and the Upper House on December 2, respectively, to transact essential government business.
The announcement has intensified speculation over the possible introduction of the Delimitation Bill and the Women's Reservation Bill, although the government has not specified which Bills will be taken up during the sittings.
Parliament last met during the Monsoon Session 2026, which concluded on August 13, when both Houses were adjourned sine die. The proposed Delimitation Bill aims to increase the number of Lok Sabha seats to 850.

title: Passenger conceals knife in belt buckle and flies from Hong Kong to Delhi before CISF finds out | Watch
description: A CISF security personnel at Delhi Airport spotted a knife concealed inside a passenger’s belt buckle during X-ray screening. A video showed how the buckle opened to reveal the hidden blade
author: FP News Desk
content:
Passenger conceals knife in belt buckle and flies from Hong Kong to Delhi before CISF finds out | Watch
A CISF security personnel at Delhi Airport spotted a knife concealed inside a passenger’s belt buckle during X-ray screening. A video showed how the buckle opened to reveal the hidden blade
A knife disguised as a belt buckle was caught at Delhi Airport after a Central Industrial Security Force (CISF) personnel noticed something amiss while interpreting an X-ray image, the force said in a post on X.
The passenger had arrived from Hong Kong and was due to travel on to Raipur.
Flagged on the X-ray screen
During X-BIS image interpretation, the screener picked up an unusual metallic object. The item was referred for physical examination, which led to the discovery of the concealed knife.
The CISF described the find as an unusually designed prohibited item and said it reflected the screener's alertness, keen observation and professionalism in safeguarding aviation security.
A video accompanying the post shows a belt with an oval buckle. When the buckle is pressed, a component emerges and unfolds into a knife.
Watch the video here:
In a voice-over, the narrator says the belt aroused suspicion during the pre-screening process and was referred for a physical check. Subsequent examination showed that it contained a hidden knife. The narrator then closes the knife and fastens the belt back into its original form.

title: Bhargavastra: How India's indigenous anti-drone system could change air defence
description: India's indigenous Bhargavastra counter-drone system has successfully completed development trials at Rajasthan's Pokhran firing ranges. Developed by Solar Defence and Aerospace Limited, the vehicle-mounted system combines air defence rockets and guided micro-missiles to tackle hostile drone swarms
author: Anmol Singla
content:
Bhargavastra: How India's indigenous anti-drone system could change air defence
India's indigenous Bhargavastra counter-drone system has successfully completed development trials at Rajasthan's Pokhran firing ranges. Developed by Solar Defence and Aerospace Limited, the vehicle-mounted system combines air defence rockets and guided micro-missiles to tackle hostile drone swarms
India has taken another step in countering one of modern warfare's fastest-growing threats, the drone swarm.
Bhargavastra, billed as India's first indigenously designed and developed two-layer, vehicle-mounted counter-swarm drone system, completed its development trials at the Pokhran field firing ranges in Rajasthan.
The announcement came on Thursday, November 26. The system was built by Nagpur-based Solar Defence and Aerospace Limited (SDAL) and is now headed toward the next phase of Indian Army evaluation.
What happened at Pokhran
According to SDAL, the trials were in-house development trials, held from November 20 to 24, of an air defence system designed to engage multiple hostile drones at once. The company says the system fired both rockets and micro-missiles during the campaign.
Two sets of tests stand out. Rockets were fired at actual swarm-drone targets that Bhargavastra's own sensors and C4I network had detected and tracked, and SDAL says the warheads struck their designated points.
In a separate series, the micro-missiles' guidance and terminal homing against drones were tested, and the company described those demonstrations as successful.
The Army has not yet issued its own evaluation.
How Bhargavastra is built
The "two-layer" label refers to two weapon types working together. Version-I uses air defence rockets, while Version-II adds guided micro-missiles with autonomous guidance and infrared seekers for precision engagement.
The launcher is sized for volume. It carries 64 tubes for rockets in Version-I and 64 micro-missiles in Version-II. A swarm is dangerous because of numbers, and the system is designed to answer in kind.
The deployment footprint is compact. The complete system is spread across three Army-inducted vehicles, which carry the launchers along with the integrated sensors and command-and-control equipment.
Using vehicles the Army already operates simplifies logistics, which matters for any system meant to move with troops.
A counter-drone weapon is only as good as its ability to find small, low-flying, often quiet targets. Bhargavastra's detection and tracking network includes radio-frequency detectors and surveillance radars, with electro-optical systems supporting tracking by day and night.
An integrated C4I command system coordinates the sensors, the tracking and the weapon engagement.
The command-and-control centre reportedly includes a radar that can detect UAVs up to 10 km away, an EO/IR surveillance system and passive RF sensors. Together they provide layered detection, tracking and classification, and a combined air situation picture that lets operators engage single drones or coordinated swarms.
Passive RF sensors listen for the signals drones emit rather than transmitting themselves. Combined with radar and optics, the system can cross-check a contact before an operator or the software assigns a weapon to it.
What the army requires
Bhargavastra is tied to a formal military requirement. The Army's requirement for a vehicle-mounted counter-swarm drone system was issued through a Ministry of Defence (Defence Production) PSO on July 9, 2024, under the Make II (Buy Indian-IDDM) category.
The contract structure is specific. The programme called for a rocket-based Version-I system, with one prototype set and 12 further sets to be delivered after a successful prototype demonstration. The stipulated project completion date is March 31, 2027.
SDAL says it went further than required. The company says it independently developed Version-II with guided micro-missiles, developed the system and its software in India, and holds complete intellectual property rights over the rockets and micro-missiles.
The next milestones are clear. Further optimisation and trials are planned to improve engagement and kill probability, and the system is now ready for prototype demonstration in its deliverable configuration, a step toward the Army's planned prototype evaluation and subsequent deliveries.
From Gopalpur to Nagpur
The Pokhran announcement is the latest in a chain of public milestones. The system first drew wide attention after tests at the Seaward Firing Range in Gopalpur, Odisha.
Three trials of the rocket were conducted there on May 13, 2025, in the presence of senior Indian Army officials. Reports said the system executed single and salvo-mode launches and achieved all its target parameters.
The tests came soon after Operation Sindoor, which sharpened public interest in counter-drone capability.
An Indian Army team visited SDAL's Nagpur facility on July 24, 2026, for a status review against the Make-II requirement. The full system was demonstrated, with a command-and-control vehicle carrying radar, EO/IR and RF detectors linked to the C4I system, plus a launcher vehicle carrying all the launch tubes.
The demonstration followed a clear sequence. SDAL flew a drone swarm that the sensors detected, the C4I system displayed the situational picture and raised an attack alert, and the launcher was then assigned targets.
The full firing sequence was demonstrated, though no actual rocket was fired inside the plant for safety reasons.
At that event, SDAL chairman Satyanarayan Nuwal gave a timeline that the Pokhran campaign now appears to meet. He said internal trials would be finished within two to three months, and noted that micro-missiles had already been tested at Balasore and Pokhran.
The system completed its in-house development trials in November, roughly four months later.
Why Bhargavastra could be a game-changer
Cost economics
Drones are cheap, and the missiles used to stop them have often been expensive. The July demonstration noted that militaries are looking for economical alternatives to costly surface-to-air missiles, with an estimated 100,000 drones used annually in active combat.
A system built around rockets and micro-missiles aims to bring the cost of each intercept closer to the cost of the threat. SDAL describes it as low-cost, but no per-unit prices have been published yet.
Hard-kill against jamming-proof drones
Many counter-drone tools rely on jamming or spoofing. Bhargavastra is a hard-kill solution, which matters against autonomous drones that are immune to electronic countermeasures.
If a drone navigates on its own and does not depend on a radio link, jamming has little to attack. A physical interceptor still works.
Built for India's geography
India's borders run from the Thar desert to the Himalayas. The system is designed for deployment across deserts, plains and mountainous terrain up to 5,000 metres above mean sea level.
Whether it performs at those extremes will be a key test in formal trials.
Layered defence in one package
Instead of separate tools for detection, tracking and kill, Bhargavastra combines them.
It is designed to integrate with the existing C4I networks of the Indian Armed Forces, supporting future network-centric operations. Integration with existing command systems is often what separates a promising prototype from something forces can actually field.
Indigenous design and intellectual property
The development of the system, software, rockets and micro-missiles inside India, with the company retaining IP rights, fits the government's push for self-reliance in defence.
That reduces dependence on imports and foreign upgrade cycles.
A claim of global novelty
SDAL says that, going by open-source information, Bhargavastra is believed to be among the world's first fully integrated, vehicle-mounted, multi-layer counter-swarm systems using unguided rockets and micro-missiles with dedicated swarm-neutralisation capability.
How Bhargavastra fits into India's Sudarshan Chakra
Prime Minister Narendra Modi announced Mission Sudarshan Chakra as a decade-long initiative to strengthen national security. In his Independence Day address from the Red Fort in 2025, he said that by 2035 key public spaces such as railway platforms, hospitals and religious sites would come under a national security shield.
The mission is meant to integrate advanced surveillance, interception and counter-strike capabilities.
Nuwal has argued that Bhargavastra can be a building block. He said he was confident that, building on Bhargavastra, a Sudarshan Chakra with ranges of 2.5 km, 6 km and 25 km could be completed by 2030, whether through DRDO or other agencies.
The government's stated target is 2035.
What next
The immediate step is a prototype demonstration in deliverable configuration. After that, the Army's evaluation process decides whether the system moves toward induction.
The programme's stated completion date is March 31, 2027, so the next several months will show whether Bhargavastra holds up under the Army's own scrutiny.
For SDAL, the near-term work is refinement of kill probability. For the Army, the questions are reliability, ease of use and cost at scale.
For the wider defence sector, the project is a test case for whether a private Indian company can field a complete, integrated air defence subsystem under the Make-II route.

He has far too many disparate interests with a constant itch for travel. title: Election Commission fixes flaw in website that exposed sensitive data of some voters: Report
description: A flaw on the Election Commission of India's website that exposed voters' personal details and identity-document paths has been fixed after a news agency flagged it
author: FP News Desk
content:
Election Commission fixes flaw in website that exposed sensitive data of some voters: Report
A flaw on the Election Commission of India's website that exposed voters' personal details and identity-document paths has been fixed after a news agency flagged it
The Election Commission of India (ECI) has addressed a security vulnerability on its website that left some voters’ personal details and uploaded identity documents accessible, following an investigation that brought the flaw to the commission’s attention, Reuters reported.
Cybersecurity experts who examined the issue warned that the weakness could have been exploited relatively easily, potentially putting voters’ sensitive information at risk.
The development comes months before crucial assembly elections in several states, including Uttar Pradesh, India’s most populous state, placing the spotlight on the security of the country’s electoral data systems.
How the flaw worked
Over a review spanning more than a month, news agency Reuters found that a logged-in voter who asked the site to arrange a call with a local electoral officer could see the reference number of their enrolment or update form in the network tab of the browser's developer tools. The tab opens with a simple right click.
Booking the call with such a number caused the same network data to display the user's name, phone number, email address, date of birth and address. It also showed file paths to identity documents, including passports, that voters had uploaded. None of this appeared on the browser's main screen.
Indian security researchers Karan Saini and Ehraz Ahmed, who went through Reuters' findings step by step on the ECI site, said this pointed to a weakness in the website's code.
Their greater worry was that the reference numbers ran in a predictable sequence. That meant attackers could guess them and automate the downloading of data on a large scale. An ordinary user would be unlikely to stumble on these steps while requesting a call, the researchers said, but cybercriminals could replicate them and harvest data in bulk.
Documents within reach
Because of that predictability, the researchers said criminals could have fetched identity documents such as passports or national ID cards using freely available web tools that demand only basic coding skills.
A Reuters reporter was able to download a copy of his own national identity card by following the steps. The researchers said an attacker could go further and use the number pattern to retrieve other voters' documents.
Saini said a criminal armed with an understanding of how browsers request documents from servers, together with the exposed file paths, could have downloaded them. The server appeared to verify only that a user was logged in, he said, not whether that person was entitled to view a given document.
Commission's response
Reuters said it shared its findings with the ECI and its three commissioners on October 26 and sought comment.
On Thursday, an ECI spokesman said the commission's information technology division had been asked to examine the findings. A few hours later the vulnerability had been fixed, with sensitive fields, including personal details and file paths, now redacted, according to a Reuters review and the two researchers. The researchers confirmed the fix effectively prevents misuse of the data.
Political reaction
Pawan Khera, a spokesperson for the Indian National Congress, told Reuters on Thursday that the findings were "deeply alarming". He said that in an electoral setting, exposing voters' personal information could enable targeted intimidation, profiling, voter suppression and the manipulation of vulnerable communities.
Former election commissioner Ashok Lavasa, told of the findings, said the lapse seemed unintentional. Such information, he said, is not gathered to be placed in the public domain.

title: Over 500 cops deployed for Diljit's Mumbai concert after bomb threat
description: Bomb Detection and Disposal Squad (BDDS) teams have swept the venue, officials said, adding that entry checks will be carried out across all five gates instead of three
author: Press Trust of India
content:
Over 500 cops deployed for Diljit's Mumbai concert after bomb threat
Bomb Detection and Disposal Squad (BDDS) teams have swept the venue, officials said, adding that entry checks will be carried out across all five gates instead of three
Listen to This Article
More than 500 Mumbai police personnel will be deployed at Mahalaxmi Racecourse here for actor-singer Diljit Dosanjh's concert on Friday following a threat email warning of possible attacks on the venue and Metro stations, officials said.
Bomb Detection and Disposal Squad (BDDS) teams have swept the venue, they said, adding that entry checks will be carried out across all five gates instead of three.
Private security personnel have also been roped in to assist police, an official said.
An email threatening blasts, grenade attacks and planting of IEDs at the mayor's office, metro rail stations and Dosanjh's concert was received on Thursday, the anniversary of the devastating 26/11 terror attacks.
The email, sent by an individual identifying herself as Hannah Meler, contained references to Khalistan, the 1984 anti-Sikh riots as well as threats of violence linked to a programme involving Dosanjh and people associated with the event.
Also Read
In view of the threat, the Mumbai police has deployed around 200 constables, 150 women constables and 75 officers, besides plainclothes personnel stationed around the singer. Dog squads and an Anti-Narcotics Cell (ANC) team will also remain present at the venue, an official said.
He said that a no-car zone extending 500 to 700 metres around the racecourse will be enforced, and parking will not be permitted at the event, though no road diversions have been announced.
Organisers have been instructed not to disclose details of the singer's hotel or arrival time as part of the security protocol, sources said.
Meanwhile, organisers have prohibited posters, banners, signs and flags of any kind inside Mahalaxmi Racecourse for the concert, which is part of Dosanjh's RuPay AURA India Tour 2026.
(Only the headline and picture of this report may have been reworked by the Business Standard staff; the rest of the content is auto-generated from a syndicated feed.)

title: Tamil Nadu's share of Lok Sabha seats must remain intact: MK Stalin
description: Stalin has laid down two conditions for any expansion of the Lok Sabha, as the Centre prepares to revisit the delimitation-linked women's reservation legislation ahead of the 2029 elections
author: Akshita Singh
content:
Tamil Nadu's share of Lok Sabha seats must remain intact: MK Stalin
Stalin has laid down two conditions for any expansion of the Lok Sabha, as the Centre prepares to revisit the delimitation-linked women's reservation legislation ahead of the 2029 elections
Listen to This Article
Former Tamil Nadu chief minister and Dravida Munnetra Kazhagam (DKM) supremo MK Stalin on Friday maintained that the state’s existing 7.18 per cent share of Lok Sabha seats must not be reduced under any circumstances if the number of parliamentary constituencies is increased through delimitation. He also demanded that the existing proportion of parliamentary representation among states, based on the 1971 Census, remain unchanged for another 25 years.
His comments came ahead of a special sitting of Parliament, which the government has convened from November 30 to December 3 to transact “essential government business”.
In a post on X, Stalin said the DMK would not compromise on the two demands, which were part of resolutions passed by the Tamil Nadu Legislative Assembly and the Joint Action Committee on fair delimitation.
“If the number of parliamentary constituencies is increased, under no circumstances should Tamil Nadu’s existing 7.18 per cent share of seats in the lower house be reduced,” Stalin said.
He added that the existing proportion of parliamentary representation among states, determined on the basis of the 1971 Census and frozen earlier, must remain unchanged for another 25 years.
Also Read
“The DMK stands firm on these two demands and will continue to do so. There is no change in our position, and there is no question of any compromise,” he said.
Stalin also said the DMK was the first party in the country to raise concerns about the possible consequences of delimitation. He said Chennai hosted the first meeting that brought together national political leaders to demand a fair delimitation exercise.
Centre plans special Parliament sitting
The Lok Sabha will reconvene on November 30, while the Rajya Sabha will meet on December 2. The sittings will conclude on December 3, subject to the requirements of government business, according to official sources.
Parliamentary Affairs Minister Kiren Rijiju announced the decision on X on Thursday. The special sitting will be an extension of the Monsoon Session, which was adjourned sine die on August 13 but was not formally prorogued.
The Union Cabinet is also expected to discuss the delimitation-linked women's reservation proposal ahead of the special sitting, news agency PTI reported.
The development has renewed speculation about the government's plans to reintroduce the Constitution (131st Amendment) Bill, 2026, which was defeated in Parliament in April.
What does the proposed Delimitation Bill seek to change?
The proposed Constitution amendment seeks to increase the maximum strength of the Lok Sabha from the existing 550 to 850 members. This would include up to 815 members from states and 35 from Union Territories, according to the provisions outlined in the proposed legislation.
The Bill also seeks to change the framework governing the allocation of parliamentary seats among states and Union Territories, allowing Parliament to determine which Census figures will be used for delimitation.
The separate Delimitation Bill, 2026, provides for the constitution of a Delimitation Commission to readjust and reallocate seats in the Lok Sabha and state legislative assemblies.
It proposes using the latest published Census figures available when the commission is constituted. This could mean that the next delimitation exercise will use the 2011 Census, the latest published Census data currently available.
The proposed constitutional amendment also seeks to bring forward the implementation of 33 per cent reservation for women in the Lok Sabha and state legislative assemblies.
Under the Constitution (106th Amendment) Act, 2023, women's reservation was linked to the completion of a Census followed by delimitation. The proposed amendment seeks to remove the requirement of waiting for a fresh Census and enable the quota to take effect following delimitation based on the latest published Census figures.
The government aims to implement the reservation ahead of the 2029 Lok Sabha elections.
Previous attempt to pass the Bill failed
The government had introduced the Constitution (131st Amendment) Bill, 2026, alongside the Delimitation Bill, 2026, and the Union Territories Laws (Amendment) Bill during a special sitting of Parliament in April.
However, the Constitution amendment failed to secure the required two-thirds majority in the Lok Sabha on April 17. Of the 528 members who voted, 298 supported the Bill and 230 opposed it. The proposal fell short of the required 352 votes.
The defeat rendered the two related Bills infructuous, and they were not taken up for consideration.

title: Pak intruder shot dead by BSF troops along international border in Punjab
description: Officials said the man was shot dead around 2 am in the Pahadpur border post area along the Ujh River in Pathankot
author: Press Trust of India
content:

title: What is subvention scheme fraud? Why has SC directed HDFC Bank, ICICI Bank to sanction prosecution of officials
description: The Supreme Court has directed HDFC Bank, ICICI Bank and two other lenders to sanction prosecution of officials within a week in alleged subvention frauds, where homebuyers faced loan recovery after builders defaulted on EMI payments.
author: Livemint
content:
The Supreme Court has directed HDFC Bank, ICICI Bank, Sammaan Capital and PNB Housing Finance to grant unconditional sanction for the prosecution of their officials within a week in alleged subvention scheme frauds involving real estate developers and financial institutions, PTI reported.
A bench comprising Chief Justice Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana warned that the heads of these institutions would have to appear personally before the court if they failed to comply with the order.
"We direct all the banks or financial institutions referred to above to issue unconditional sanction for prosecution within one week, failing which the CMD and Chairman shall remain present in court to show cause as to why appropriate action be not taken against them," the bench said.
The order came while the apex court was hearing a batch of petitions concerning subvention schemes, under which homebuyers were allegedly subjected to loan recovery proceedings after developers failed to meet their financial commitments.
Under a subvention scheme, a bank or financial institution sanctions a home loan and disburses the amount directly into the builder's account. In return, the developer agrees to pay the equated monthly instalments (EMIs) on behalf of the buyer until possession of the flat is handed over.
The arrangement is generally governed by a tripartite agreement between the homebuyer, the developer and the lender.
The scheme is intended to reduce the immediate financial burden on homebuyers, who do not have to begin paying EMIs while waiting for their homes to be delivered.
However, problems arise when developers fail to honour their commitment to pay the EMIs. In such cases, banks can demand repayment from homebuyers, leaving them liable for loans even when they have not received possession of their properties.
The petitions before the Supreme Court concern allegations that banks and developers were involved in arrangements that left homebuyers facing loan recovery proceedings despite builders failing to meet their obligations under the tripartite agreements.
The court is examining cases involving alleged collusion between financial institutions and developers to dupe homebuyers, particularly in the National Capital Region (NCR).
During Thursday's hearing, Additional Solicitor General Aishwarya Bhati, appearing for the Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI), told the court that the agency was facing difficulties in obtaining prosecution sanctions under Section 19 of the Prevention of Corruption Act. This included cases where HDFC Bank had granted conditional sanctions.
Bhati also informed the bench that the CBI had filed its sixth supplementary status report. Investigations had been completed in 25 of the 55 registered cases, with 22 chargesheets filed and closure reports submitted in three cases.
The bench said granting prosecution sanction was the responsibility of the banking authorities and directed the CBI to complete the remaining investigations within two weeks.
The court also said it would prescribe timelines for completing the trials and would not permit delaying tactics.
In July last year, the Supreme Court had allowed the CBI to register 22 cases over what it described as an "unholy nexus" between banks and developers to dupe homebuyers in the NCR.

title: Delhi: Pollution may be worse in your kitchen than on your balcony; study finds 50% more fine particles in some houses
description: Researchers monitoring 24 homes in four south Delhi neighbourhoods found indoor PM2.5 averaged 45% higher than outdoor levels while PM10 was 46% higher.
author: Sounak Mukhopadhyay
content:
Fine particle pollution was roughly 50% higher inside poorly-ventilated south Delhi homes than outdoors. The study covered 24 homes across four neighbourhoods, PTI reported. Even homes with working kitchen exhaust systems recorded higher air pollution indoors than outside. But their indoor readings were lower than those in homes with poor ventilation. In poorly-ventilated homes, indoor PM2.5 averaged 119.17 micrograms per cubic metre. The outdoor average was 79.34 micrograms per cubic metre. In well-ventilated homes, indoor PM2.5 averaged 77.34, compared with 56.14 outdoors. This put indoor levels about 38% above outdoor readings in those homes. PM10 readings followed a similar pattern. Poorly-ventilated homes averaged 138.63 micrograms per cubic metre indoors and 91.19 micrograms per cubic metre outdoors. That put the indoor reading around 52% higher. Well-ventilated homes averaged 89.51 micrograms per cubic metre indoors and 64.81 micrograms per cubic metre outdoors, a difference of about 38%. Indoor PM2.5 was about 54% higher in poorly ventilated homes than in well-ventilated ones. For PM10, the gap was about 55%. Across all 24 homes, PM2.5 averaged 98.25 micrograms per cubic metre indoors and 67.74 micrograms per cubic metre outdoors. PM10 averaged 114.07 micrograms per cubic metre indoors and 78 micrograms per cubic metre outdoors. The indoor averages were about 45% higher for PM2.5 and 46% higher for PM10. Researchers monitored homes in Shaheen Bagh, Jasola Vihar, Batla House and Okhla Vihar. They collected readings from February to April 2023. They measured indoor pollution in kitchens and outdoor pollution on balconies. Each home was monitored for 8 hours each day over 3 consecutive days. The researchers skipped night-time monitoring because of privacy concerns. They classified homes according to whether working kitchen chimneys or exhaust fans operated during monitoring. The study linked better ventilation with lower indoor particle levels. Still, both groups recorded higher average particle levels inside kitchens than on balconies. The researchers linked higher indoor readings to household activities and poor ventilation. They also pointed to Delhi pollution entering homes from outside. Cooking, cleaning, smoking and burning incense can add particles to indoor air. Poor ventilation can allow indoor-generated particles to accumulate. The team did not measure how much each contributed to cooking, traffic, or dust. The team included researchers from Jamia Millia Islamia in New Delhi. Researchers from Jazan University in Saudi Arabia also took part. Others came from Baba Ghulam Shah Badshah University in Rajouri, Jammu and Kashmir. The journal Discover Environment published the study in 2025. The researchers said improving ventilation, maintaining exhaust systems and reducing indoor pollution sources could help. title: RK Family Trust dispute: Supreme Court ends mediation between Rani Kapur, Priya Sachdeva Kapoor; here’s why
description: The Supreme Court has ended mediation in the  ₹30,000-crore RK Family Trust dispute after 15 sittings failed to produce a settlement. The court questioned Rani Kapur's demands and advised her to take a practical view, as the inheritance battle heads back to litigation.
author: Swati Gandhi
content:
The Supreme Court on Thursday put an end to mediation in the high-stakes inheritance dispute surrounding the family of late industrialist Sunjay Kapur, who passed away in June last year. The apex court noted that efforts to broker a settlement had reached an impasse and asked the warring parties to prepare for the legal "battle" ahead. The court said it would now proceed to pass an order in the dispute concerning the RK Family Trust and Sunjay Kapur's estate. The development came after the top court took note of a second report submitted by court-appointed mediator and former Chief Justice of India DY Chandrachud, who was appointed to the role in May. The report confirmed that mediation between the parties had failed, ANI reported. A two-judge bench of Justices JB Pardiwala and K V Viswanathan was informed that the parties had held 15 sittings but failed to arrive at a settlement. The bench questioned why they had been unable to resolve the dispute through mediation. It also asked the parties to consider whether continuing with mediation would serve any purpose, given the mediator's assessment that the talks had reached a dead end. The bench added that it would urge the Delhi High Court to expedite consideration of an interim application seeking the protection and preservation of the family trust's assets. The request is expected to be made in an order to be issued shortly. The development marks a setback to the Supreme Court's attempt to prevent a bitter family feud over the vast assets associated with the Sona Group from escalating into prolonged litigation. During the previous hearing in August, the top court had expressed satisfaction with the progress of mediation led by DY Chandrachud. It observed that six sessions had been held by then, during which the parties had cooperated in exploring a "holistic settlement" of their claims. The court had subsequently extended the mediation process until November 2, hoping that the differences could be resolved amicably. However, Senior Advocate Mukul Rohatgi, representing Sunjay Kapur's wife, Priya Sachdeva Kapoor, told the apex court that the late industrialist's mother, Rani Kapur, had reportedly walked out of the mediation and was blaming Priya for the failure of the settlement process. Opposing this, Senior Advocate Siddharth Dave, appearing for the late businessman's mother, claimed that the money and assets held by the RK Family Trust were not being managed properly. He added that Priya Kapoor was effectively sitting on the trust's funds and assets. Announcing the closure of the mediation process, the court then turned to the nature of Rani Kapur's claim and asked what exactly she wanted from the trust — whether she was seeking a monetary settlement or the entire corpus. Dave responded that the late businessman's mother had been seeking both money and assets that constituted the trust's corpus. The court also sought clarity on the value of the assets involved. In response to a question about the trust's corpus, a figure of around ₹30,000 crore was cited. Counsel for Rani Kapur told the court that the octogenarian was seeking ₹6,000 crore, along with other assets from the trust's corpus. Addressing Rani Kapur, the court advised her to show flexibility and understanding, and to take a practical view of the dispute. It observed that prolonged litigation would be an endless exercise and could prove futile. The dispute stems from the constitution and control of the RK Family Trust and the assets transferred into it. Challenging the trust's constitution, Rani Kapur alleged that her late son, Sunjay, and his wife, Priya Kapoor, had transferred her assets into the trust without her consent. With mediation now closed, the dispute is set to return to the legal process. The Supreme Court is expected to pass an order in the matter, while the Delhi High Court may be urged to expedite the hearing of the interim application concerning the protection and preservation of the trust's assets. The failure of mediation means the parties may now have to pursue their claims through prolonged court proceedings. title: SC to consider plea to extend priority for voter appeals to 6 more civic bodies in WB SIR case
description: The Supreme Court has agreed to consider extending priority hearings for voter appeals arising from West Bengals electoral roll revision to six more municipal corporations beyond Kolkata, as civic polls approach. Petitioners said around two lakh appeals are pending across the seven corporations and urged quicker disposal, while the court stressed that tribunals must prioritise inclusion cases but also work within practical limits.
author: PTI
content:
New Delhi: The Supreme Court on Friday agreed to consider submissions seeking to extend priority hearing by appellate tribunals of voter appeals arising from West Bengal's Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls to six more poll-bound municipal corporations, besides the Kolkata Municipal Corporation (KMC).
On November 23, a bench comprising Chief Justice Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana had directed the Election Commission to increase the number of appellate tribunals hearing appeals arising from the SIR of electoral rolls in West Bengal.
The bench's direction had come after consultation with the chief justice of the Calcutta High Court.
The court ordered tribunals to prioritise appeals against deletions of voters, especially from assembly constituencies where civic body polls are scheduled.
In the Friday hearing, lawyer Prashant Bhushan and senior lawyer Gopal Sankaranarayanan represented some petitioners.
Bhushan said that the November 23 order named only the Kolkata Municipal Corporation (KMC), although a similar situation exists in six other municipal corporations.
He sought a minor modification so that the order covers the "Kolkata Municipal Corporation and such other municipal corporations where elections are due," seven in all.
Justice Bagchi agreed to consider the submissions, but said piling on urgent matters could make the exercise unrealistic.
"It is a difficult task for the tribunals," he said, adding that the bench would take a pragmatic approach.
"We understand the concern. You have made the application, we'll consider it," he said.
Asked about pendency, Bhushan said about 1.30 lakh appeals are pending in Kolkata and about 75,000 in the other six corporations combined, roughly two lakh in all.
Bhushan also suggested that if appeals remain pending when the civic polls are held, the deleted voters should be allowed to vote.
Sankaranarayanan told the bench that state police have been tasked with visiting the homes of appellants whose cases are pending and asking them to produce documents.
The senior lawyer said they have been told to finish the exercise by November 29 and handed a police checklist to the bench.
Justice Bagchi asked whether the documents were being formally collected and placed before the tribunals. Sankaranarayanan said the EC has told the petitioners it has nothing to do with the exercise and attributed it to the state.
Justice Bagchi noted that many people, at least in the KMC area, hold valid passports, and that tribunals need not take long to decide such cases.
He said the petitioners could approach the high court on the police action. Sankaranarayanan said they would.
The CJI added that the first concern is to ensure the appeals are decided.
Justice Bagchi said the court has already said that appeals seeking inclusion must be decided quickly.
In March, the EC set up 19 appellate tribunals at the apex court's direction.
About 700 judicial officers from West Bengal, Odisha, and Jharkhand were deployed to handle roughly 60 lakh claims and objections arising from the exercise.
On August 25, the apex court had directed the EC to furnish details of pending and disposed-of appeals, including a segregation of cases filed by voters challenging their exclusion or inclusion in the electoral rolls.
It also asked the poll panel to indicate how many additional tribunals would be required to ensure time-bound adjudication.

title: Delimitation Bill: DMK's MK Stalin says no compromise on Tamil Nadu's Lok Sabha seat share, sets two condi
description: MK Stalin has reaffirmed the DMK's demands regarding Tamil Nadu's representation in the Lok Sabha. He stated that the current 7.18 percent share of Lok Sabha seats should remain intact. The chief minister also insisted that the existing representation proportion based on the 1971 Census must not change for an additional 25 years. Stalin noted the importance of safeguards against unfavorable delimitation outcomes for the state.
author: ET Online
content:
In a post on X, Stalin said, “The DMK was the first in India to raise its voice against the dangers of delimitation! It was only in Chennai that political leaders from across the country came together for the first time to demand fair delimitation.”
Stalin further reiterated two demands concerning the allocation of Lok Sabha seats among states.
The first demand is that Tamil Nadu’s existing 7.18 per cent share of seats in the Lok Sabha should not be reduced, even if the total number of parliamentary constituencies is increased.
The second demand is that the existing proportion of parliamentary representation among states, determined based on the 1971 Census, should remain unchanged for another 25 years.
Why South Indian states are concerned?
The delimitation issue has remained a major concern for southern states, including Andhra Pradesh, Telangana, Tamil Nadu, Kerala and Karnataka. These states have expressed apprehension that a population-based redistribution of parliamentary seats could reduce their relative share of representation compared with states that have recorded higher population growth.
Under the existing constitutional framework, the allocation of Lok Sabha seats among states has been retained based on the 1971 Census, with the freeze extended until the publication of the first Census after 2026. The debate has consequently centred on balancing population-based representation with concerns of states that have pursued population stabilisation.
The issue has gained attention ahead of the reconvened Parliament session scheduled to begin on November 30. The Lok Sabha Secretariat has announced that the second part of the Eighth Session of the Eighteenth Lok Sabha will commence on November 30 and is likely to conclude on December 3, subject to the exigencies of government business.
Union Parliamentary Affairs Minister Kiren Rijiju said the government had requested the Lok Sabha Speaker and the Rajya Sabha Chairman to reconvene the Lower House on November 30 and the Upper House on December 2, respectively, to transact essential government business.
Although the government has not specified which Bills will be taken up during the sittings, the announcement has intensified speculation over the possible introduction of the Delimitation Bill and the implementation of women's reservation.
Parliament last met during the Monsoon Session 2026, which concluded on August 13, with both Houses adjourned sine die. The proposed Delimitation Bill aims to increase the strength of the Lok Sabha to 850 seats.

title: Explained | India-US trade pact and tariffs
description: The US has proposed a fresh set of tariffs on 14 economies, including India.
author: PTI
content:
Image for representational purposes.
Credit: iStock Photo
India and the US finalised the framework for the first phase of their bilateral trade agreement (BTA) in February this year, following negotiations that were launched in February 2025.
But changes in Washington's tariff structure have brought the two sides back to the negotiating table.
The US has proposed a fresh set of tariffs on 14 economies, including India.
Here is an explainer to understand the developments so far.
India is pursuing the agreement to safeguard the competitiveness of its exports amid high American tariffs and secure an edge over rival South and South East Asian manufacturing economies.
The US is using tariffs against its trading partners such as India to address trade deficits, shield domestic industries from foreign competition and press countries to negotiate trade agreements on terms favourable to Washington.
The US has alleged that trading partners like India and China impose steep import duties and restrictive regulations on American goods while enjoying low-tariff access to the US market.
It is a customs or import duty imposed by the importing country on goods entering its territory and paid by the importer. Tariffs increase the cost of imported goods and can make them more expensive than domestically produced products. They are used to protect domestic industries, generate government revenue and influence trade flows.
The US has been India's largest trading partner since 2021-22. Exports grew 0.92 pc to USD 87.3 billion during 2025-26, while imports increased 15.95 per cent to USD 52.9 billion. India's trade surplus with the US declined to USD 34.4 billion in 2025-26 from USD 40.89 billion in 2024-25.
The US is India's largest export destination for sectors such as textiles, pharmaceuticals, engineering goods, gems and jewellery, chemicals and electronics.
Any increase in tariffs could affect the price competitiveness of Indian products and exporters' ability to retain or expand their market share.
The US announced a 25 pc duty from August 7, 2025. An additional 25 pc tariff was imposed on Indian goods as a penalty for New Delhi's continued purchase of Russian oil. After this order, the total tariff on Indian goods, barring an exemption list, rose to 50 pc.
On February 2, 2026, India and the US agreed on a trade deal, under which Washington agreed to bring down the reciprocal tariff on Indian goods to 18 pc. On February 20, the US Supreme Court struck down the reciprocal tariff system.
The Donald Trump administration subsequently turned to Section 301 of the Trade Act of 1974, which allows the US to impose tariffs following investigations into alleged unfair trade practices. The probes into forced labour and excess manufacturing capacity are part of Washington's efforts to rebuild its tariff regime under an alternative legal provision.
On July 24, the US imposed a 10 and 12.5 pc tariff on 60 countries, including India (10 pc), under Section 301, citing concerns related to 'forced labour'.
The US Trade Representative (USTR) on November 25 announced the findings of its second Sec 301 investigations into structural excess manufacturing capacity in 14 economies, including India, and proposed additional tariffs on their goods.
For India, it proposed tariffs of up to 25 per cent, while indicating that the rate could be adjusted to 17 per cent if the two countries reach a trade agreement.
The USTR has alleged that India's industrial policies (such as the 'Make in India' initiative and PLI schemes), manufacturing expansion plans, labour protections, financial practices and market access barriers contribute to structural excess capacity and hurt American firms.
The report has identified sectors such as steel, solar, pharmaceuticals, medical devices and information and communications technology as areas of concern.
India has rejected the allegations, stating that it does not have structural excess capacity in any sector.
It emphasised that any trade-related concerns should be addressed within the framework of the trade pact negotiations.
It said India remains committed to working closely with the US towards the early conclusion of the India-US BTA in accordance with the Joint Statement issued on 7th February 2026.
The two countries announced that they have reached a framework for an interim agreement regarding reciprocal and mutually beneficial trade. The terms of that pact include:
- India will eliminate or reduce tariffs on all US industrial goods and a wide range of food and agri products.
- The US will apply a reciprocal tariff rate of 18 pc on Indian goods, subject to the successful conclusion of the interim agreement.
- Both will address non-tariff barriers that affect bilateral trade.
IMPORTANT: "In the event of any changes to the agreed-upon tariffs of either country, the US and India agree that the other country may modify its commitments."
- India intends to purchase USD 500 billion of US energy products, aircraft and aircraft parts, precious metals, technology products, and coking coal over the next 5 years.
India has stated on multiple occasions that the deal has been finalised and will be signed once the US tariff framework is in place and India gets a comparative advantage over its competitor nations.
Comparative advantage means securing lower US import tariffs and better market access than rival manufacturing countries, such as Bangladesh, Vietnam, Indonesia, Thailand, and China, so Indian exporters can price goods more competitively in the US market.
The latest USTR's report has proposed a 17 per cent tariff on India if the trade pact is finalised. It gives only one per cent edge over Bangladesh, Cambodia, Indonesia, Malaysia, and Thailand (18 per cent deal rate) and a 3 per cent edge over Vietnam and China (20 per cent deal rate). Without a pact, tariffs against India could go up to 25 pc.
However, according to experts, Indian exporters could face a tariff disadvantage against goods from several other countries in the US market, as Washington's latest Section 301 investigation into structural excess capacity covers only 14 trading partners, while the probe into forced-labour-related trade practices covers 60 countries.
This leaves a much larger group of economies (including Pakistan, Sri Lanka, the Philippines and Turkiye) potentially outside the additional tariff action, giving their exporters a relative cost advantage in the US market.
While exporters are urging the government to finalise the pact at the earliest, think tank GTRI said that with the threat of up to 100 pc Graham tariffs still looming, New Delhi must reject a one-sided trade deal and defend its industrial expansion sector by sector as serving legitimate domestic, export, and future demand.
The USTR has decided to schedule public hearings on its proposals on January 25 and has sought written comments from interested persons by January 5 as part of the final regulatory requirements before the tariffs come into effect.

title: Explained | Key changes likely in amended Delimitation Bill and why they matter
description: In the previous attempt to pass the bill on April 17, the NDA government fell short of the required two-third majority for a Constitution amendment.
author: DH Online
content:
AI-generated Photo
The Parliament is set to reconvene after over three months on November 30 and is likely to push the Constitution Amendment Bill linked to the delimitation exercise.
Experience a more refined e-paper today
The bill proposes to increase the number of Lok Sabha seats to 850 from the existing 543, factoring the population growth. If passed, it will also pave way for 33 per cent reservation for women in Parliament and state assemblies from the 2029 general elections.
In the previous attempt to pass the bill on April 17, the NDA government fell short of the required two-third majority for a Constitution amendment.
Currently, the bill requires 361 votes out of 543 to pass the in the Lok Sabha. With three vacancies, effective strength currently stands at 540. Further, considering the Speaker (who votes only in a tie) and suspended TMC MP Kalyan Banerjee, the government would need roughly 360 votes if all 539 members participate.
Following the blockage of the bill in the Lok Sabha, it was sent to a delimitation commission to make changes to the text.
According to reports, there are major changes that are likely to reflect in the text that will be discussed in the Houses next week.
The government is likely to guarantee a flat 50 per cent increase in seats by maintaining the existing proportion of seats in states (as per 1971 census) and freeze it for the next 25 years.
The proposal for new constituencies in each state may be de-markated on the basis of 2011 census, while also retaining the provision for 33% women's quota.
Earlier, the bill had proposed to increase Lok Sabha seats from 543 to a maximum of 850 seats with the 2011 Census as the base.
Home Minister Amit Shah said in Lok Sabha that the plan is to increase the seats to 816, which would translate to a 50 per cent rise across states.
However, opposition parties were not satisfied with Shah’s statement and wanted an explicit mention of 50 per cent pro rata rise in seats in the bill.
Providing an example at the time, Shah had said Karnataka has 28 seats, which is about 5.15 per cent of the total representation of 543 seats in the Lok Sabha. After delimitation, Shah said this would increase to 42 and the share would be 5.14 per cent.
Questions were also raised about choosing Census 2011 as the base year when the Census 2027 was to be published ahead of the next Lok Sabha elections.
The number game
DMK, a key opposition party, had said it would consider supporting the bill if a flat 50 per cent increase is a Constitutional guarantee. DMK has said that it stands for “fair” delimitation that maintains Tamil Nadu’s current proportion of 7.19 per cent representation in Lok Sabha as also a 25 year freeze on numbers.
In fact, in April, Shah had said that Tamil Nadu's seat share in the Lok Sabha increase from 39 to 59 and share will go up from 7.18 per cent to 7.23 per cent.
I.N.D.I.A. ally NCP (SP)’s Supriya Sule on Wednesday said that her party is willing to see the content of the bill before taking a stand, while also indicating her support in case of a 50 per cent flat increase in seats.
The passage depends on the support of the DMK and NCP (SP), which together have 30 MPs.
In April, the NDA managed to get 298 votes. The numbers have improved since then. The ruling alliance now has 320 members and needs 40 more votes to cross the threshold.
20 rebel Trinamool Congress MPs broke away and merged with the Nationalist Citizens Party of India (NCPI), extending support to the NDA earlier in the year, while Six Shiv Sena (UBT) MPs crossed over to the Eknath Shinde-led Shiv Sena.
With the Shiromani Akali Dal also returning to the alliance, the NDA’s strength has climbed to approximately 325.
The remaining gap could be closed through DMK and NCP (SP)'s combined 30 seats. Their support would take the tally to 355, which is still five short of the required mark.
NDA leaders are in talks with smaller parties and independents, including the YSRCP (4), JMM (3), VCK (2) and RLP (1), while hoping for abstentions from some I.N.D.I.A. bloc members.
(With DHNS inputs)

title: Government appeals to MPs to ensure smooth special sitting of Parliament
description: Parliamentary Affairs Minister Kiren Rijiju said it is a joint responsibility of all members to ensure that the world's largest parliamentary democracy, India, sets an example.
author: PTI
image_url: https://media.assettype.com/deccanherald/2025-03-28/t2q3a9qd/Members in the Lok Sabha during the Monsoon session of Parliament, in New Delhi,?w=1200&h=675&auto=format%2Ccompress&fit=max&enlarge=true
content:
Government appeals to MPs to ensure smooth special sitting of Parliament
Parliamentary Affairs Minister Kiren Rijiju said it is a joint responsibility of all members to ensure that the world's largest parliamentary democracy, India, sets an example.
Members in the Lok Sabha in the Parliament, in New Delhi.
Credit: PTI File Photo
New Delhi: The Union government on Friday appealed to all MPs to ensure a smooth special sitting of Parliament that will discuss "very important bills."
A day after a four-day sitting of Parliament was announced, Parliamentary Affairs Minister Kiren Rijiju said it is a joint responsibility of all members to ensure that the world's largest parliamentary democracy, India, sets an example.
"My appeal to the members of Parliament is to ensure that Parliament functions smoothly. We are proud of our democracy, and we must ensure that Parliament functions smoothly," he told reporters here.
Rijiju said the government has called for a four-day special sitting — November 30 and December 1 in Lok Sabha, and December 2 and 3 in Rajya Sabha.
"When the government calls a session or a special session, that means there are very important bills or business for the nation," he said.
The minister said the members of Parliament have a very special task, an onerous responsibility, in ensuring a smooth run of Parliament.
"Members have all the rights, all the freedom to agree or to disagree. But that has to be put in proper perspective through rules, through conventions on the floor of the House," he said.
The special sitting was announced on Thursday to transact "essential" business, amid indications that the government may reintroduce a constitutional amendment linking the rollout of women's reservation to delimitation.
The government has been keen to push through the Constitution amendment bill for a long time.
It seeks to expand the Lok Sabha's strength from the existing 543 seats to a maximum of 850 through delimitation. The treasury benches have said it will pave the way for the implementation of 33 per cent reservation for women in Parliament and State legislatures ahead of the 2029 general election.
The government's earlier move to pass the proposed legislation in Parliament was defeated in April due to a lack of numbers.
