title: UP PCS 2025: Allahabad High Court Cancels Prelims Result, Orders Fresh Merit List
description: UP PCS 2025 Prelims Result: Commission ordered to prepare a fresh merit list and result; Mains, interviews to be conducted again.
author: Rahul Kumar
content:
UP PCS 2025 Prelims Result: In a significant ruling, the Allahabad High Court on Friday ordered the Uttar Pradesh Public Service Commission (UPPSC) to cancel the result of the Uttar Pradesh Provincial Civil Services (Combined State/Upper Subordinate Services) (UP PCS) Preliminary Examination 2025. The commission will now have to prepare the merit list afresh and declare a new result. The Mains examination and interviews will subsequently be conducted again for the UPPCS 2025 recruitment cycle.
The Main examination had already been conducted, its result declared, and the interview process completed. The interview result was awaited.
The cancellation followed a petition filed before the High Court challenging the manner in which the preliminary examination result had been prepared.
The petition raised issues concerning the treatment of candidates in the open category. It argued that candidates who had not availed themselves of any reservation should be placed in the unreserved, or open, category.
The High Court, however, held that the open category is not restricted to candidates belonging to the unreserved category. Any meritorious candidate, irrespective of their category, can be considered under the open category if they qualify on merit.
The plea alleged that the reservation rules had not been properly followed while preparing the result. The single bench of the Allahabad High Court subsequently cancelled the UPPCS 2025 preliminary examination result.
In a separate development, the Uttar Pradesh government on Thursday appointed senior IPS officer Alok Singh as the chairman of the Uttar Pradesh Public Service Commission (UPPSC), Prayagraj, the state's principal recruiting body for government services.
On Wednesday, the High Court had quashed the preliminary examination result for the 2025 Assistant Prosecution Officer recruitment, holding that meritorious candidates from reserved categories cannot be excluded from the open category at any stage of the selection process.

title: Surplus Treasury Claims Meet Debt Reality As AAP Launches Punjab Campaign
description: Economists say freebies retain electoral pull because most voters experience them as immediate cash or free power, not as entries in the state budget.
author: Manjeet Sehgal
content:
Arvind Kejriwal told a Moga rally that the AAP government spent four years filling Punjab's "sarkari khajana". The fiscal record points the other way. Between March 2022 and March 2026, the state's net outstanding debt rose by approximately Rs 1.35 lakh crore, from Rs 2.73 lakh crore when AAP took office to roughly Rs 4.08 lakh crore by the end of FY 2025-26. Gross borrowings look larger still because budget documents include short-term Ways and Means Advances from the RBI and rollover repayments. The treasury was not filled. It was leveraged.
A ruling party that funds its doles with fresh loans and then presents the arrangement as a filled treasury is not merely campaigning. It is asking voters to treat borrowed money as earned surplus. On its foundation day, the AAP government chose this path: protect an inflated image of plenty, keep the monthly transfers flowing, and leave the rising interest burden for later. Whether that bargain produces a khushhaal Punjab or simply postpones a darker reckoning is no longer a question of accounting. It is a question the electorate will answer when it decides if the immediate gain is worth the deferred cost.
Economists say freebies retain electoral pull because most voters experience them as immediate cash or free power, not as entries in the state budget. Delayed salaries and unpaid arrears affect a limited set of government employees; the wider electorate sees the monthly transfer or the zero electricity bill. AAP's promise to continue these schemes therefore converts fiscal strain into a simple choice: keep the benefit or risk losing it. With interest payments already taking 17.2 per cent of expenditure and new women's cash transfers budgeted at Rs 9,300 crore, committed liabilities crowd out capital spending. The political calculation is that short-term household relief will outweigh long-term development shortfalls at the ballot box.
Welfare and subsidy bills explain much of the rise. The power subsidy stood at roughly Rs 19,657 crore in FY 2025-26 and is budgeted above Rs 20,000 crore for FY 2026-27. Over four years the cumulative power outlay reached Rs 76,000-Rs 78,000 crore. Free agricultural tubewell electricity accounted for about Rs 10,413 crore a year. The 300-unit free domestic power scheme, covering nearly 90 per cent of households, cost Rs 6,859-Rs 7,614 crore annually. Industrial concessions added another Rs 2,384 crore. Social security pensions for 33-35 lakh beneficiaries formed the second-largest recurring outflow at Rs 6,132 crore a year, or Rs 23,500-Rs 24,000 crore over four years. Subsidised ration and nutrition kits cost Rs 800-Rs 900 crore annually. Zero-ticket bus travel for women cost the exchequer Rs 2,042 crore across the term. Cashless healthcare top-ups and Aam Aadmi Clinics absorbed Rs 1,046 crore in FY 2025-26 and Rs 3,500-Rs 4,000 crore over four years, rising to Rs 2,000 crore in FY 2026-27. The Mukh Mantri Maavan Dheeyan Satkar Yojana, offering Rs 1,000 a month to women and Rs 1,500 to Scheduled Caste women, was budgeted at Rs 9,300 crore from FY 2026-27 after remaining unlaunched through the first four years.
AAP raised more loans in four years compared to SAD-BJP's 10-year rule
Comparisons with earlier governments sharpen the picture. AAP's four-year net addition of roughly Rs 1.35 lakh crore already exceeds the approximately Rs 1.31 lakh crore added across the full ten-year SAD-BJP term from 2007 to 2017. Stripping out the one-off UDAY power-bond takeover of about Rs 15,628 crore brings the SAD-BJP ten-year figure down to roughly Rs 87,000 crore. Against that adjusted total, AAP's four-year borrowing is higher by about Rs 48,000 crore. Projected forward to the FY 2026-27 Budget Estimate of Rs 4.47 lakh crore, AAP's five-year net addition reaches Rs 1.65-Rs 1.74 lakh crore. Congress added roughly Rs 91,000-Rs 1 lakh crore over its five years from 2017 to 2022. The annual pace under AAP averages about Rs 33,750 crore, compared with Rs 18,200-Rs 20,000 crore under Congress and Rs 13,100 crore under SAD-BJP (or Rs 8,700 crore excluding UDAY).
At the same Moga rally, Kejriwal framed existing schemes-women's cash transfers, free power, health cover, pilgrimage trips and free bus travel-as guarantees that would continue only under AAP. He warned that rivals would roll them back. Charanjit Singh Channi has indicated that welfare schemes would continue. Amrinder Singh Raja Warring has argued for ending free power for better-off households while keeping targeted support for the poor.
The split gives AAP an opening to warn beneficiaries of cutbacks. The fiscal habit itself is older. Targeted concessions under SAD-BJP became a political compulsion under Congress and expanded further under AAP through universal power relief and the new Rs 9,300 crore women's scheme. Public debt is projected to reach Rs 4,47,754 crore by the end of 2026-27. Interest payments alone will take Rs 28,755 crore, or 17.2 per cent of total expenditure. Competing on larger handouts leaves narrow room for long-term assets.
AAP's campaign pledges remain under scrutiny
AAP made eradication of the drug menace, a core 2022 poll plank. Enforcement drives, seizures and property demolitions have not ended arguments that narcotics availability and substance abuse continue. A legal or assured MSP guarantee across crops was a pre-poll flashpoint and remains unresolved friction between cultivators, the state and the Centre. Decisive accountability in the 2015 sacrilege and Behbal Kalan police-firing cases was central to AAP's moral pitch; slow or contested legal progress keeps the issue open. Aam Aadmi Clinics were rolled out, yet the total count has fallen well short of the 16,000-clinic benchmark associated with pre-poll trackers. The Rs 1,000-per-month cash assistance for women stayed deferred through much of the term before entering the budget frame in 2026, allowing rivals to ask why beneficiaries waited years. Beyond the headline figure of 77,182 government jobs, broader employment expectations and secondary manifesto items such as Rs 5 canteens and student laptops have given opposition parties material to accuse the administration of overpromising.
AAP formally opened its 2027 campaign on 26 November 2026 with the Khushhaal Punjab Maha Rally at Matwani village in Moga, timed to the party's 14th Foundation Day and Constitution Day. Kejriwal and Mann presented a five-year report card that included free electricity, Rs 10 lakh health coverage, school upgrades and financial support for women, while claiming the Centre had withheld funds. The rally also launched smart ration cards aimed at up to 10 lakh families, with nearly six lakh targeted in the first phase. Mann highlighted the induction of 77,182 youth into government posts on merit without bribery or political clout. AAP leaders contrasted their party with established political families and internal factionalism in Congress and SAD.
Days after the BJP and SAD revived their coalition, Mann accused both of political convenience and pressed the BJP over shared stages with Akali leader Bikram Singh Majithia despite past drug-related allegations. Claiming a turnout of more than two lakh people and 71 already-announced candidates, AAP used Moga to stake an early claim in Malwa ahead of Prime Minister Narendra Modi's scheduled 8 December visit for a joint alliance rally. The event drew a legal challenge. A public-interest petition in the Punjab and Haryana High Court alleged that over 2,500 state transport buses were pulled off regular routes, disrupting corridors such as Barnala-Moga and Mansa. The state government defended the deployment by citing a 12 November protocol order that classified the event as an official State-Level Function handled by the Food and Civil Supplies Department for smart ration card distribution. Opposition figures, including Leader of the Opposition Partap Singh Bajwa, Punjab Congress chief Pargat Singh and BJP leader Sunil Jakhar, accused the ruling party of using public resources and taxpayers' money for a partisan launch.
The Moga rally presented four years of welfare expansion as proof that the treasury had been filled. The debt numbers, the annual borrowing velocity and the unfinished pledges on drugs, MSP and sacrilege cases sit beside that claim. Whether voters weigh the cash transfers and free power more heavily than the rising interest burden and the still-open campaign promises will decide if the fear of rollback outweighs the fiscal record when polling begins.

title: Amritpal Singh, Breakaway Akalis In Alliance Talks In Punjab, Mayawati May Join Too
description: The proposed grouping is largely viewed internally as a "Panthic and regional alliance" aimed at mounting a strong challenge in the upcoming elections, sources said.
author: Reet Kaur Sahni
content:
Ahead of the 2027 Assembly elections in Punjab, political parties are working to solidify their blocs and reach out to voters. So far, three major fronts have emerged: the incumbent Aam Aadmi Party (AAP), the Congress, and the freshly revived Shiromani Akali Dal (SAD)-BJP alliance. Now, a fourth front--dubbed a "Panthic alliance"--appears to be taking shape.
According to sources, three factions--Waris Punjab De, Akali Dal (Punar Surjit), and Akali Dal (Amritsar)--are in talks to form a coalition ahead of the polls. People familiar with the matter said that the proposed grouping is largely viewed internally as a "Panthic and regional alliance" aimed at mounting a strong challenge in the upcoming elections.
READ | Jailed Hardliner Amritpal Singh Likely To Contest Against Bhagwant Mann In Punjab Assembly Polls
Sources said the pact between Waris Punjab De and Akali Dal (Punar Surjit) has been largely finalised, while negotiations with Simranjit Singh Mann's Akali Dal (Amritsar) are still underway. Meanwhile, Mayawati's Bahujan Samaj Party (BSP), which was earlier part of the discussions, has temporarily been put on hold. According to sources, the leadership wants to consolidate the Panthic factions first before bringing the BSP on board. The parties are engaged in active dialogue to formalise a seat-sharing arrangement ahead of the elections to Punjab's 117-member Assembly early next year.
Speaking exclusively to NDTV, Waris Punjab De leader Manpreet Singh Ayali confirmed the developments.
READ | "From Farm Laws to Chitta": Bhagwant Mann Questions SAD-BJP U-Turns
"Yes, there are talks going on between the parties. The alliance is more or less done. The seat-sharing arrangement has to be worked out at the earliest. We want to ensure the Panthic parties keep a united front. Once that is done, we will bring in the BSP," he said.
Sarabjeet Singh Khalsa, an MP from the same party, echoed the sentiment, adding that the arrangement aims to unite all three factions on core Panthic issues.
Sources also indicated that the broader plan is to eventually bring localised farm groups into the fold. For now, however, the primary focus remains finalising the seat-sharing formula and aligning the parties around a mutually agreeable agenda.

title: Tampering with vehicle number plates to attract five times the toll on national highways
description: NEW DELHI: The government on Friday said that commuters who deliberately mask their vehicle's number plates at multi-lane free flow toll plazas to evade
author: Rohitashwa Ranjan
content:
NEW DELHI: The government on Friday said that commuters who deliberately mask their vehicle's number plates at multi-lane free flow toll plazas to evade charges will have to pay a penalty of five times the user fee.The ministry of road transport and highways, in a statement, said that the penalty will be charged in addition to recovery of the user fee itself. It also added that the penalty amount will be passed on to the authority."The ministry of road transport & highways has decided to levy a penalty on vehicle users who deliberately mask, tamper with or conceal their vehicle registration numbers, or do not affix a FASTag, to avoid paying user fee under the Multi-Lane Free Flow (MLFF) tolling system," the statement read."It will apply only where the act is established to have been done with intent to evade user fee. It covers registration numbers on the front, the rear or both, in cases where the FASTag also could not be detected," it added.The ministry said that the vehicles involved will be identified through a robust, technology-driven process.
It added that tampering with, masking or concealing a number plate, or not affixing a FASTag, to avoid user fee is a deliberate act of evasion.
MLFF is a barrier-less electronic tolling system. Overhead gantry-mounted FASTag readers and Automatic Number Plate Recognition (ANPR) cameras identify vehicles and deduct the user fee automatically, so vehicles do not have to stop. It reduces waiting time, congestion, fuel use and emissions.The penalty is proposed to apply wherever MLFF is in use, and at each new location where it is introduced in future.
Rohitashwa Ranjan is a digital journalist with The Times of India, where he decodes Indian politics as a carefully staged production with scripts, subtext and everything behind. His stories track elections, party dynamics and the things that often are buried beneath the headlines. When not parsing vote shares or alliances, he is usually reading between the lines, where the real story tends to reside.

title: 'Asked about farmers' crisis': Rohit Pawar meets Sharad Pawar, says his health 'perfectly fine'
description: NEW DELHI: NCP(SP) MLA Rohit Pawar on Friday said party chief Sharad Pawar was doing well and was likely to be discharged from the hospital in a day or
author: Priyanka Jaiswal
content:
NEW DELHI: NCP(SP) MLA Rohit Pawar on Friday said party chief Sharad Pawar was doing well and was likely to be discharged from the hospital in a day or two. He also said that during their conversation, the senior leader enquired about the crisis affecting farmers and agricultural labourers in Maharashtra.NCP (SP) chief Sharad Pawar was admitted to Mumbai's Breach Candy Hospital on Thursday after suffering from dehydration, his daughter and party working president Supriya Sule confirmed.Speaking to reporters, Rohit Pawar said he had spoken to Sharad Pawar and also interacted with his grandmother, who was present with the NCP-SP chief.“Pawar Sahab’s health is perfectly fine... He will likely be discharged in a day or two. When I met him, he asked about the farmers and agricultural labourers in Maharashtra—specifically regarding the severe crisis currently affecting the state,” he said.
On the proposed special Parliament session and the reported 50% increase in the number of MPs, Rohit Pawar said the Cabinet had taken a decision, but the draft had not been released yet.“Once the draft is available, all our MPs will study it and determine an appropriate stance,” he said, adding that the party would articulate its position in Parliament.
Rohit Pawar also said a meeting of the INDIA alliance could take place on Saturday or Sunday, where constituent parties would present their respective positions.“When it happens, all the constituent parties will present their respective positions... Our party’s stance will be articulated in Parliament,” he added.
Priyanka Jaiswal has four years of experience in digital journalism, news agency reporting and video production. Currently with The Times of India, she covers public policy, politics and global affairs. She is particularly drawn to human-interest stories that put people at the heart of an issue, spark awareness , and contribute to meaningful conversations.

title: 'Alleged omissions specifically detailed': HC rejects CM Vijay's plea against petition challenging Perambur win
description: NEW DELHI: In a setback to Tamil Nadu chief minister C Joseph Vijay, the Madras high court on Friday dismissed his plea seeking rejection of an election
author: Karan Manral
content:
NEW DELHI: In a setback to Tamil Nadu chief minister C Joseph Vijay, the Madras high court on Friday dismissed his plea seeking rejection of an election petition challenging his victory from the Perambur assembly constituency.Justice V Lakshminarayanan ruled that the petition filed by S Dinesh, a voter from Perambur, disclosed a valid cause of action and was maintainable, Bar and Bench reported.The judge observed that the alleged omissions and discrepancies in Vijay's nomination affidavit had been specifically detailed in the petition, adding that their significance could only be determined during the trial.Dinesh alleged that the Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam (TVK) chief had concealed or misrepresented details of several property transactions in the affidavit submitted along with his nomination papers. He sought the annulment of Vijay's election.Dinesh alleged that Vijay had failed to disclose the purchase of three acres of land in Panruti for Rs 30 crore in January and the sale of a commercial property in Padi for Rs 35 crore the following month. He further claimed that a 50% share in a property in Kodaikanal, which the chief minister had declared as agricultural land, was classified as government land in revenue records.
The petitioner contended that the alleged omissions deprived voters of information they were entitled to know and amounted to undue influence, a corrupt practice under Section 123(2) of the Representation of the People Act, 1951.Vijay contested the allegations and sought dismissal of the petition at the threshold, arguing that it failed to establish the material facts necessary to sustain the case. His lawyers maintained that Vijay had declared assets worth more than Rs 600 crore and that the alleged discrepancies did not demonstrate how voters' choices had been influenced.
Vijay secured 1,20,365 votes in Perambur in the April assembly elections, defeating DMK candidate RD Shekar by a margin of 53,715 votes. He had also won from Tiruchirappalli East but vacated the seat to retain Perambur.Shekar and another Perambur voter, TN Lakshmi Narasimhan, had filed separate petitions challenging Vijay's election from the constituency.

title: Reading Books at Sea Shore: New initiative at Rushikonda Beach, Visakhapatnam
description: Discover ‘Reading Books at Sea Shore’, a new initiative by Andhra Pradesh Tourism and Visakhapatnam Public Library that brings a beachside reading experience to Rushikonda Beach in Visakhapatnam
author: Nivedita Ganguly
content:
The next time visitors to Rushikonda beach feel like taking a break from the sun and the sea, they can reach for a book instead of their phones. A new initiative, ‘Reading Books at Sea Shore’, is bringing the pleasure of reading outdoors by offering beachgoers a quiet corner to browse through books while listening to the waves.
Launched by Andhra Pradesh Tourism in collaboration with the Visakhapatnam Public Library, the initiative is designed to add a leisurely, literary dimension to the beach experience. Around 2,000 books have been donated by the Visakhapatnam Public Library for this initiative, a part of which have been arranged in racks at the Information Centre-cum-police outpost at Rushikonda. Visitors can choose a title, settle into one of the reclined wooden chairs placed along the beach and spend some time reading. The books can be returned after use, with no charges involved.
The collection spans several genres, including spirituality, children’s literature, fiction and non-fiction, catering to readers across age groups and interests. The idea is to make books easily accessible to anyone who wishes to pick one up, whether for a few minutes or a longer stretch of time.
The concept is the brainchild of J Madhavi, District Tourism Officer, Visakhapatnam, who felt that a beach visit could offer more than water-based recreation and sightseeing.
“We receive a considerable number of tourists from West Bengal, Chhattisgarh and Odisha, many of whom visit Rushikonda with their families. Not everyone is looking for an activity all the time. Some simply want to sit back, unwind and enjoy the surroundings. We thought reading would be a wonderful way to offer them that quiet time, with a book for company,” she says.
The arrangement is deliberately informal. Visitors can browse through the collection, pick a book and read at their own pace before returning it. The Tourism Department is also working on a register to maintain a record of the books displayed and those taken up for reading.
“A register will keep track of the titles available and those picked up by visitors. We also plan to replenish the collection every month so that readers have something new to look forward to,” says DS Varma, secretary, Visakhapatnam Public Library.
Two signboards, one in English and another in Telugu, have been installed on the beach to draw attention to the initiative and explain the facility to visitors. With the tourist season gathering pace, the department hopes the reading corner will encourage people to slow down and experience the beach differently.
For tourists visiting from other States, the idea also offers an opportunity to spend some unhurried time between outings. Suparna Sarkar, a Bengali tourist visiting Rushikonda with her family says, “We usually come to the beach to relax and spend time together. While the children are busy enjoying the beach, we can spend some quiet time reading. It is a refreshing concept and something one rarely comes across at a beach.”
P Vaishnavi, a management student, who stopped by to browse through the collection, feels the initiative could make the beach more inviting for families. “It is nice to have something different from the usual beach activities. You can sit comfortably, pick up a book and read without having to spend anything. I hope more people make use of it, especially youngsters,” she says.
The reading facility will be open every day from 10.30am to 6pm. Books can be borrowed for reading within the beach premises and returned without any fee.
The initiative adds to the range of recreational offerings at Rushikonda. Andhra Pradesh Tourism already facilitates speed boating, while private operators offer activities such as paragliding and parasailing. Food shacks have also been set up by the department, with plans to introduce a few more.

title: Anti-CEC protests: Supreme Court to examine if police must grant journalists ‘special privilege’ at protests
description: Supreme Court to decide if journalists deserve special privileges at protests, or custody-like treatment, amid debates on who qualifies as a journalist.
author: Krishnadas Rajagopal
content:
The Supreme Court on Thursday said it would test whether law enforcement agencies should grant journalists any “special privilege” at protest sites.
A three-judge Bench headed by Chief Justice of India Surya Kant said journalistic freedom must be balanced with the administration of public order.
“Whether a journalist has a special privilege in a situation of an assemblage, demonstration, or other exercise of democratic rights in relation to law enforcement agencies... Or is the law enforcement agencies’ purpose only the maintenance of law and order, and there cannot be any additional journalistic privilege…” observed Justice Joymalya Bagchi, laying out the debate.
Also Read | 43 journalists detained, several assaulted, while covering protests against CEC: CPJ
‘Allow us to do our work’
The court’s remarks came during the hearing of multiple petitions alleging the abuse and illegal removal of journalists — including women media professionals — from demonstration sites during the widespread protests demanding the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar in October.
The Kerala Union of Working Journalists, represented by senior advocate P.V. Dinesh, said journalists were not claiming any “privilege” whatsoever.
“We are only saying that we are just journalists. Allow us to do our work,” Mr. Dinesh clarified.
He referred to the specific cases of seven journalists who have alleged that they faced abuse at the hands of the police. The court directed the journalists’ body to approach its High-Powered Enquiry Committee (HPEC), which has been set up to hear individual grievances against the police using excessive force disproportionate to the maintenance of public order.
‘Superior treatment’
Justice Bagchi went on to voice a larger question bothering the court, that is, whether journalists require a “superior or a different species” of treatment at places of democratic processes like a protest, demonstration, or public assembly.
Mr. Dinesh said the rights of journalists were already crystallised by law and judicial precedents. He said the core issue here was whether “established journalists covering an event can be taken into custody”.
The court said journalists canvassing wrongful detention or alleging that they were stopped from performing their professional duties during the protests were free to demonstrate their cases before the HPEC. Justice Bagchi said the top court would focus on addressing or further clarifying the law.
Explained | Police ‘handling’ of women protesters: What law says about crowd control, use of force
What is ‘custody’?
One of the questions raised by Justice Bagchi, which he said the court would determine, was whether “picking up someone and removing them from a spot amounts to ‘custody’.”
“If so, what are the consequences if we hold it as ‘custody’? We could examine this,” the judge said.
Justice Bagchi, at one point, said a journalist’s status was not a “self-confirmed” one, noting that there was a realm of atomised individuals who self-identify as ‘journalists’.
The Delhi Police, in its affidavit in the case, had assured the court that it “respected the role of the press”. The police had denied removing or detaining anyone who had not hindered their work.
‘Reel-makers are not journalists’
However, the police claimed that the protests against the NEET-UG 2026 paper leak in July and against the CEC in October were swarmed by individuals masquerading as journalists by using a camera and a microphone. The affidavit blamed “reel-makers” and “content-creators” interfering with their operational space. The police said current laws, guidelines, and rules did not consider reel-makers and content-creators as ‘working journalists’.
The affidavit had urged the court to determine if “reel-makers can be elevated to the status of journalists or reporters”.
Justice Bagchi asked whether a person could be considered a professional journalist only if she was accredited or registered under the law or employed with an established print or electronic media house. The judge questioned whether a person, who seemed to be a spokesperson of the people, or a citizen journalist, could be recognised as engaged in the profession of journalism.
The petitioners said nomenclatures like ‘reel-makers’ and ‘content-creators’ used by the police in its affidavit seemed to be an afterthought, and cannot be applied to restrict, restrain, or remove the people covering protests.

title: Hiding number plates to dodge barrier-free tolls? Prepare to pay 6 times more
description: The road transport ministry will penalise motorists who deliberately evade MLFF tolls by masking number plates or removing FASTags The measure seeks to deter evasion and strengthen compliance with barrier-free electronic toll collection
author: Ashutosh Mishra
content:
Hiding number plates to dodge barrier-free tolls? Prepare to pay 6 times more
The road transport ministry will penalise motorists who deliberately evade MLFF tolls by masking number plates or removing FASTags. The measure seeks to deter evasion and strengthen compliance with barrier-free electronic toll collection.
Vehicle owners deliberately masking or tampering with number plates to evade toll payments under the Multi-Lane Free Flow (MLFF) system will have to pay a penalty five times the applicable toll fee, in addition to the original amount, taking the total payment to six times the normal toll.
The Ministry of Road Transport and Highways has decided to penalise motorists who conceal, tamper with or mask their vehicle registration numbers, or do not affix a FASTag, with the intention of avoiding toll payments under the barrier-free electronic toll collection system.
Under the proposed penalty framework, the additional charge will be five times the applicable user fee and will be passed on to the concerned Authority.
HOW MUCH WILL MOTORISTS HAVE TO PAY?
The five-time penalty will be charged over and above the original toll fee, meaning motorists caught deliberately evading toll payments will have to pay six times the normal amount.
For instance, if the applicable toll is Rs 100, the penalty will be Rs 500, taking the total amount payable to Rs 600. Similarly, for a toll fee of Rs 150, the additional penalty will be Rs 750, bringing the total to Rs 900.
The Ministry has clarified that the penalty will apply only when deliberate attempts to avoid paying the user fee are established. This includes concealing or tampering with the vehicle's registration number on the front number plate, rear number plate or both.
It will also cover instances where a FASTag cannot be detected because of deliberate attempts to evade toll payments.
HOW DOES THE MLFF TOLLING SYSTEM WORK?
The Multi-Lane Free Flow (MLFF) system is a barrier-free electronic toll collection mechanism that allows vehicles to pass through toll plazas without stopping.
Overhead gantries fitted with FASTag readers and Automatic Number Plate Recognition (ANPR) cameras identify vehicles and facilitate automatic deduction of the applicable toll fee.
The system is designed to eliminate stopping at toll plazas, thereby reducing waiting time, traffic congestion, fuel consumption and vehicle emissions.
HOW WILL TOLL EVADERS BE IDENTIFIED?
Vehicles violating the provisions will be identified through a technology-driven process using FASTag readers and ANPR cameras installed on overhead gantries.
The Ministry intends to implement the penalty at all locations where the MLFF system is currently operational, as well as at every new toll location where the system is introduced in the future.
WHAT MOTORISTS NEED TO ENSURE
The Ministry has advised vehicle owners to keep their registration number plates clearly visible and ensure FASTags are properly affixed to their vehicles.
Motorists have also been asked to pay the applicable user fee and refrain from attempting to bypass the electronic toll collection mechanism.
Deliberately masking, concealing or tampering with number plates, or not affixing a FASTag to evade toll payments, could result in a steep financial penalty, with the total amount payable reaching six times the normal toll fee.
The move is aimed at discouraging deliberate toll evasion and ensuring compliance with the MLFF electronic toll collection system.

title: Bengal announces voter roll Special Summary Revision dates, draft list on Dec 15
description: The draft electoral rolls in West Bengal is to be published on December 15 and special voter verification camps to be held from December 19 ahead of the final publication on February 8
author: India Today News Desk
content:
Bengal announces voter roll Special Summary Revision dates, draft list on Dec 15
The draft electoral rolls in West Bengal is to be published on December 15 and special voter verification camps to be held from December 19, ahead of the final publication on February 8.
The Election Commission has announced a revised schedule for the Special Summary Revision (SSR) of electoral rolls in West Bengal, with the draft electoral rolls set to be published on December 15 and special campaign days for voters to verify their details, enrolment and corrections scheduled from December 19, the Chief Electoral Officer (CEO) said on Friday.
The revision will be conducted with January 1 as the qualifying date, according to the CEO. The exercise will allow eligible citizens to register as voters, check their details and seek corrections if their information is incorrect or their names are missing from the electoral rolls.
Under the revised schedule, polling stations will be rationalised and rearranged by December 3. The draft electoral rolls will be published on December 15, after which voters can submit claims and objections until January 14.
The Election Commission has set February 1 as the deadline for disposing of claims and objections, with the final electoral rolls scheduled to be published on February 8.
Special Campaign Days will be organised on December 19, 20, 26 and 27 and January 2, 3, 9 and 10 at designated polling stations across the districts.
Booth Level Officers (BLOs) will remain present at the polling stations on these days to help voters verify their details, apply for enrolment, submit claims and objections, and seek corrections to their electoral particulars.
Booth Level Agents (BLAs) of registered political parties have also been requested to attend the campaign days.
The CEO's office has urged voters to use the camps to check whether their names and other details are correctly reflected in the electoral rolls and complete any necessary formalities.
The revision comes amid complaints of incorrect and erroneous entries in electoral rolls during the Special Intensive Revision (SIR). The Election Commission has directed officials to identify and rectify discrepancies during the ongoing SSR.
In a letter to chief electoral officers of states and Union territories, the poll body said existing electoral particulars of voters, including names, relationship details, dates of birth, mobile numbers and photographs, should be compared with the corresponding information collected during the SIR.
Any mismatch detected during the exercise should be flagged for verification and necessary corrective action, the Commission said.
BLOs have been directed to visit the electors concerned, verify their particulars and obtain duly filled-in and signed Form 8 applications wherever required.
Electoral Registration Officers (EROs) and Assistant Electoral Registration Officers (AEROs) have been asked to examine and dispose of such applications in accordance with the prescribed procedure.

title: Indian Navy gets BrahMos-armed Vindhyagiri, final ship of stealth frigate trio
description: GRSE delivered Vindhyagiri its third and final P17A frigate to the Indian Navy in Kolkata The handover completes the shipyard039s three-warship programme and strengthens indigenous naval shipbuilding
author: Shivani Sharma
content:
Indian Navy gets BrahMos-armed Vindhyagiri, final ship of stealth frigate trio
GRSE delivered Vindhyagiri, its third and final P17A frigate, to the Indian Navy in Kolkata. The handover completes the shipyard's three-warship programme and strengthens indigenous naval shipbuilding.
Garden Reach Shipbuilders & Engineers (GRSE) on Friday delivered Vindhyagiri, the third and final Advanced Guided-Missile Frigate of the P17A series built by the shipyard for the Indian Navy, completing its three-warship programme and strengthening the Navy's indigenous fleet.
The 149-metre-long, 6,670-tonne warship was formally accepted by Rear Admiral RS Dhaliwal at a ceremony in Kolkata. The delivery marks a significant milestone in India's efforts to bolster its maritime capabilities and achieve self-reliance in defence manufacturing.
The delivery of Vindhyagiri comes less than eight months after GRSE handed over Dunagiri, the second frigate in the series. The shipyard had delivered the first P17A frigate earlier.
BRAHMOS AND BARAK-8 MISSILES BOOST COMBAT CAPABILITIES
Equipped with BrahMos anti-ship and land-attack cruise missiles and Barak-8 surface-to-air missiles, Vindhyagiri has enhanced offensive and defensive capabilities. The frigate is designed to undertake anti-air, anti-surface and anti-submarine warfare operations.
Powered by a combination of diesel engines and gas turbines, the advanced warship features an Active Electronically Scanned Array (AESA) radar and modern combat systems. It also has aviation facilities to operate helicopters and can accommodate 225 personnel.
PRESIDENT MURMU LAUNCHED WARSHIP IN AUGUST 2023
Vindhyagiri was launched by President Droupadi Murmu on August 17, 2023. It is the 811th vessel delivered by GRSE and the 121st warship in the shipyard's history.
The P17A programme is also significant for its contribution to India's indigenous defence manufacturing ecosystem, generating opportunities for micro, small and medium enterprises (MSMEs), start-ups and original equipment manufacturers.
GRSE BUILDING 11 FRONTLINE NAVAL PLATFORMS
GRSE is currently constructing 11 frontline naval platforms, comprising two Anti-Submarine Warfare Shallow Water Crafts, four Next Generation Offshore Patrol Vessels and five Next Generation Corvettes.
The shipyard is also building 36 other vessels, including 13 export platforms, underlining its expanding shipbuilding activities.
The delivery of Vindhyagiri marks the completion of GRSE's P17A frigate programme while reflecting the growing capabilities of India's domestic shipbuilding industry and the Indian Navy's operational preparedness.

title: CDS General Subramani flags Pakistan’s space growth with China, Turkey’s help: ‘Must factor it into our calculus’
description: Emphasising the need to factor these developments into India's strategic planning, the CDS called for strengthening the country's own space capabilities. | India News
author: HT News Desk
content:
Follow the latest breaking news, major developments and agenda-setting stories from India and around the world with the newsdesk at Hindustan Times. Operating round the clock, the desk brings together experienced editors, reporters and correspondents to deliver fast, accurate and contextual reporting across subjects that influence public policy, governance, business, society and international affairs. The team also leads coverage of major breaking news events, policy announcements, court proceedings, natural disasters, public emergencies and significant international developments. Reports published by the newsdesk are based on information gathered from reporters on the ground, official statements, government agencies, court records, regulatory filings, recognised institutions and other authoritative sources. Stories undergo editorial scrutiny and verification processes to ensure accuracy, fairness and relevance, and are updated as events evolve and additional information becomes available. Whether covering a key political decision in New Delhi, an economic policy shift affecting millions, a landmark court ruling or a major global event, the HT News Desk aims to provide readers with reliable, fact-based journalism that delivers not only the latest developments but also the context and analysis needed to understand their wider implications.
CDS General Subramani flags Pakistan’s space growth with China, Turkey’s help: ‘Must factor it into our calculus’
Emphasising the need to factor these developments into India's strategic planning, the CDS called for strengthening the country's own space capabilities.
Chief of Defence Staff (CDS) General N S Raja Subramani on Friday flagged Pakistan's growing space capabilities, aided by support from China and Turkey. During an address on the 'Future of warfare and India's preparedness to conduct multi-domain operations', the CDS official noted that Islamabad's space programme was advancing with Chinese assistance and could receive further support from Turkey.
Further emphasising the need to factor these developments into India's strategic planning, the CDS called for strengthening the country's own space capabilities.
"Pakistan's space capability is improving with Chinese help. It will be aided by the Turkish too. We must factor it into our calculus. Need to look at enhancing our capability," the CDS said.
The official's remarks came days after Pakistani air force pilot Muhammad Zeeshan Ali became the first foreign astronaut to blast off China's Shenzhou-24 spacecraft to the Tiangong space station. “The friendship between China and Pakistan is as vast as outer space," Ali had told reporters, according to a Bloomberg report.
Also Read | Biggest threat to India lies in 'cognitive domain', says former CDS Gen Anil Chauhan
Distinction between war and peace ‘blurring’
Gen Raja Subramani highlighted that the distinction between war and peace is "blurring" today, according to news agency PTI.
During an address on the 'Future of warfare and India's preparedness to conduct multi-domain operations', he said, “We are being subjected to cognitive warfare by adversary in an insidious way." He also underlined the evolving nature of technology and warfare.
Also Read | ‘Million-dollar missile' vs '$3,000 drone’: CDS NS Raja Subramani says 3 shifts shaping modern warfare
On military preparedness, Gen Raja Subramani emphasised, “We need not look at a prescribed template. We need to have our own template.”
He also referred to 'Operation Sindoor', describing its second phase as a strong example of joint, integrated and multi-domain military operations.
He further asserted that India maintained control over the escalation matrix and escalation dominance, adding that the operation resulted in a "decisive victory" for the country.
He said multi-domain operations is not about combining all the capabilities; rather, it implies integrating different capabilities to “pose multiple dilemmas to an adversary,” the PTI report added. The official said an integrated command and control system is a prerequisite for conducting multi-domain operations.
Also Read | Armed forces need a balance of youth, experience: Chief of Defence Staff
The general officer said integration of military-space architecture and the ability to communicate effectively are key to carrying out such operations. He also added that cyber defence is an integral component of multi-domain operations.
(with inputs from PTI)

title: Sharad Pawar’s NCP announces support for delimitation bill before special Parliament sitting
description: The Centre has proposed the expansion of the Lok Sabha and delimitation of constituencies, a move opposed by the opposition INDIA bloc. | India News
author: Shailesh Gaikwad, Akanksha Verma
content:
Shailesh Gaikwad is political editor and heads the political bureau in Hindustan Times' Mumbai edition.In his career of over 20 years, he has covered Maharashtra politics, state government and urban governance issues.
Sharad Pawar’s NCP announces support for delimitation bill before special Parliament sitting
The Centre has proposed the expansion of the Lok Sabha and delimitation of constituencies, a move opposed by the opposition INDIA bloc.
The NCP(SP) on Friday announced its decision to support the Centre's delimitation bill in the special Parliament session, to be held from November 30 to December 3. The announcement was made by NCP(SP) leader Jitendra Awhad after a meeting with party chief Sharad Pawar.
Speaking outside the Breach Candy hospital in Mumbai, where Pawar is admitted, Awhad said, “Pawar saheb told me that as per constitutional provisions, delimitation has to be done. Supriya tai and the MPs have taken a decision. Our party will support the delimitation.”
The Centre has proposed the expansion of the Lok Sabha and delimitation of constituencies, a move opposed by the opposition INDIA bloc. Awhad's announcement came hours after the Union Cabinet decided on delimitation, which includes a 50 per cent increase in the Lok Sabha seats across the country.
Earlier in the day, NCP(SP) working president Supriya Sule said she would not attend the INDIA bloc meeting to be convened on Saturday to discuss the Opposition's floor strategy as her father was ailing. The party will send its MPs for the meeting.
NCP(SP)'s 3 conditions to back delimitation
Sule had earlier said that the party has set three conditions for its support to the bill: First, the women's reservation must be implemented. Second, there should be a 50 per cent increase in Lok Sabha seats across all the states and third, there should be adequate representation to the opposition parties in the delimitation commission that will redraw the boundaries.
NCP(SP) issues whip to MPs
The NCP(SP) on Friday issued a whip directing its Lok Sabha MPs to remain present in the House from November 30. The party has eight MPs in the Lok Sabha and one in the Rajya Sabha.

title: India, EU have compelling reasons to work more closely, says top EU official Olof Skoog
description: India and the European Union have strong reasons to deepen cooperation amid concerns over China and Russia, and US trade policies, EU official Olof Skoog says. | India News
author: Rezaul H Laskar
content:
Rezaul Hasan Laskar is Foreign Editor with the Hindustan Times, which he joined in 2015. He began as a journalist in his hometown of Shillong in northeast India and has worked in newspapers and wire services over the years. He moved to New Delhi in 1997 and initially focused on defence, national security, Jammu and Kashmir and the northeast, while also working of foreign policy and international relations. He has been part of the media delegation accompanying PMs on foreign visits and has reported from destinations ranging from Tibet to Ukraine. Between 2007 and 2013, he was the Press Trust of India correspondent in Pakistan, one of only two Indian journalists allowed to report from the country. He extensively covered Pakistan’s domestic politics and the life of the common people, as well as the fallout of the 2008 Mumbai attacks on India-Pakistan relations and the subsequent trial in Pakistan of the suspects involved in the attack. As part of his reportage in Pakistan, he travelled the breadth of the country, from the Swat Valley to Balochistan. Reza’s first gig in journalism was writing a weekly music column, and music – especially classic rock – remains a keen interest. He is also a movie buff and a keen photographer.
India, EU have compelling reasons to work more closely, says top EU official Olof Skoog
India and the European Union have strong reasons to deepen cooperation amid concerns over China and Russia, and US trade policies, EU official Olof Skoog says.
India and the European Union (EU), which believe in a rules-based order, freedom of navigation and respect for sovereignty, have compelling reasons to work more closely together against the backdrop of the actions of China and Russia or even the trade policies of the US, EU deputy secretary general for political affairs Olof Skoog said on Friday.
Skoog, who is in New Delhi for political consultations in the run-up to the signing of the India-EU free trade agreement (FTA) next month, welcomed India’s proposals for ending the hostilities but noted in an interview with HT that most such moves had been blocked by Russia. Following are edited excerpts of the interview:
India and the EU are in the final stages of concluding their FTA. How is the process proceeding and how important is it to have a bilateral investment agreement in place too?
The FTA is going well, meaning the 27 countries are looking at it and then there will be a signature on December 16. After that, we have the scrutiny by the European Parliament. Although the ratification comes after that, there could still be preliminary applications as of next year. But the agreement is the agreement, then it’s the implementation. There’s a lot that needs to be worked out. Both India and the EU have the task of enticing, informing and getting the private sector and others to start applying it and understand how to draw the benefits.
On the investment agreement — in order for this new relationship to release potential dividends on both sides, there needs to be predictability, safety and security for investments. There, I think there’s still work to be done. We can create conditions for the private sector to invest more, but for them to drink out of that hole, they need to know their investment is safe for the foreseeable future. That’s where the investment agreement comes in; that’s an integral part of releasing the full potential of the FTA.
How has the India-EU Security and Defence Partnership (SDP) changed cooperation in this sector? How is defence industrial collaboration progressing?
I think we’re already seeing the effects of the SDP in the sense that there’s much more intense consultations, but some of that is to really start working much more intensely and regularly together to understand our security policy environment here, in Europe and everything in between. It’s about starting and deepening that dialogue, and also cooperating more, to pass the same messages to our other partners in the world, those who are less inclined to trust international law and the multilateral system. It’s not very visible but you can already feel that the relationship has moved to a different quality. There’s much less of ‘We cannot discuss this, please don’t touch on that’ — all those sensitivities are gone and we’re in a trusted relationship that means a lot.
But more on tangible results — we are conceptually going from buyer-seller to cooperation on hard security. India and the EU find ourselves in a situation where we’re trying to break some dependencies of the past. That doesn’t mean we are closing in on ourselves — we do it with reliable, predictable partners, but also ones that bring technical added value to what we’re trying to do.
SDP partners have a privileged entry point into that kind of defence cooperation. The EU can provide conditions for that, including loans that we provide to member states, which they can use for big investments and for inviting partners that have SDP agreements, India being one. It opens up new areas of collaboration. Again, it will be up to the defence sector to gauge that added value, both on the Indian side and the European side.
Does India’s long-standing military relationship with Russia act as an impediment?
I don’t know, but certainly, the relationship with Russia is one that is very integral to our dialogue with India. Not just because we are monitoring Russia’s influence around the world, but because the qualitative deterioration of security in Europe isn’t just limited to Russian aggression against Ukraine; [it is] actually a very aggressive posture by Russia vis-a-vis EU countries. Anything that is seen to facilitate that posture of Russia, materially or politically, is very sensitive to Europe. That’s a conversation we’re certainly having but that’s as far as I can see the implications of it.
Do you see the EU working more closely with India on matters such as hybrid threats, disinformation or protection of critical infrastructure?
That’s definitely part of the area where we see a need for further cooperation. Both here and in Europe, we see that is a new threat coming in. For democracies such as India and European countries, the role of foreign interference and manipulation of information is one that will always be used to influence elections through misinformation and other means. The more we compare notes of what we’ve seen in Europe — not just in the EU but also in some neighbouring countries like Moldova and Armenia, where traditionally the Russian influence is quite big. I think there’s a playbook there that is advancing very quickly, very sophisticated — and the more we can compare notes and cooperate on that, it’s very important.
We also see that on maritime security, [and undersea cables], there’s been a lot of incidents in the Baltic Sea, and you can say that’s far away from the Indian Ocean, but in a way, it isn’t because it’s all connected. Given how dependent we are economically on this part of the world, it’s an enlightened self-interest to be very involved in maritime security in the Indian Ocean.
One of India’s main concerns in the Indo-Pacific is China’s assertive actions, such as the maritime disputes in the South China Sea. Do you see the EU and India working more closely together to make the Indo-Pacific more secure and more open in terms of trade?
Whether it’s China, Russia, or in some cases the US hitting us both with tariffs etc, based on this fundamental notion that we’re both better off if international law is respected, there’s predictability, there’s free trade, sovereignty and territorial integrity are respected, UNCLOS [United Nations Convention on the Law of the Sea] is allowed to function and [there is] freedom of navigation — I think we really see eye to eye on all these issues.
Whether it’s China, Russia, or in some cases the US, there’s a lot that speaks to us, to the added value of deeper cooperation between India and the EU. I very much see that happening.
That will also manifest itself in more concrete cooperation, military exercises, port calls by EU member states. It’s true we don’t have a standing navy or army, but we do have joint operations such as Atalanta and Aspides, and they interact in a very positive way with the Indian Navy in the northern Indian Ocean.
It doesn’t mean we go hand-in-hand as we approach China or the others, but we compare notes and share experiences, and then we have our bilateral efforts with China through dialogue for resolving some issues we have in both trade and security.
Just reflecting on the recent trilateral meeting of some global leaders in China, I don’t think the youth in India or in Europe feels this is the kind of leadership that will provide the best options for our future when it comes to climate change, respect for rules or governance of AI. There is a huge craving for a different kind of leadership, one that respects the rules that provide predictability, that stands up for democracy both internally and in the international sphere. That’s why I’m very stimulated by the fact that India and the EU are coming together, because we are really big players, and there are a lot of smaller countries who are looking for that kind of alternative leadership. If we can provide that, I really think it’s extremely encouraging to see this coming together. And my message is just for India to look at the EU as one of its, if not the most, important partners for the future.
How do you view the efforts to end the Russia-Ukraine war and what do you make of India’s proposals for ending attacks and creating grain corridors?
First of all, we welcome initiatives by India and others to complement some things we’re trying to do, on releasing grain and opening up the Black Sea to supplies for world food security. But I have to be very open with you and say that, so far, all those initiatives have been blocked by Russia.
Russia is expanding and escalating its attacks against Ukraine and the Ukrainian population because of the stalemate on the frontlines, although most recently, Ukraine has gained terrain. To compensate for that, Russia is taking the war to the cities and the civilian population.
The timetable of Russia, and we see that as they approach new rounds of talks in Abu Dhabi or wherever, is that they are just not engaging on anything that could [lead to a] ceasefire or stop the conflict in order to see what a just and sustainable peace could look like.
Unfortunately, the Russian timetable doesn’t coincide with the American one, which tries to achieve results on the negotiating table soon, nor does it coincide with [Europe’s], India’s or Ukraine’s timetable, which is to try to stop the onslaught and bloodshed now.

title: Setback To INDIA Bloc As Sharad Pawar's NCP Backs Delimitation Bill: 'Constitutional Requirement'
description: Jitendra Awhad announced that Sharad Pawar's NCP-SP would support delimitation, days after Supriya Sule outlined conditions for backing the proposed exercise
author: Anushka Vats
content:
Setback To INDIA Bloc As Sharad Pawar's NCP Backs Delimitation Bill: 'Constitutional Requirement'
Jitendra Awhad announced that Sharad Pawar's NCP-SP would support delimitation, days after Supriya Sule outlined conditions for backing the proposed exercise
The Sharad Pawar-led Nationalist Congress Party (Sharadchandra Pawar) will support the Centre’s proposed delimitation Bill, party leader Jitendra Awhad announced on Friday.
Speaking about it, Awhad informed that the party had agreed to back the exercise, citing its constitutional significance.
- Parliament's Special Session Triggers Delimitation Buzz; Supriya Sule Says Agenda Unknown | News18
- Sharad Pawar's NCP-SP Backs Delimitation Bill, BIG Political Twist Ahead Of Parliament Session
- Sharad Pawar's NCP Issues Whip: All MPs Ordered To Attend Special Parliament Session | News18
- Delimitation Numbers: When Every Vote Counts, These 16 Single-MP Parties May Be Key
“The discussion wasn’t about our party’s official stance. The general point being made was that the delimitation process is a constitutional requirement. A decision has been made to support the delimitation process, and we will indeed support it. We will support the delimitation," Awhad said, according to a message shared after his interaction with the media.
The announcement comes days after NCP-SP working president and MP Supriya Sule cited the conditions under which her party could consider supporting the proposed exercise.
What Did Supriya Sule Say Earlier?
Sule had earlier said that her party was open to supporting delimitation if certain conditions were included in the proposed legislation.
She had put forward three demands: implementation of women’s reservation alongside delimitation, a uniform 50 per cent increase in Lok Sabha seats across all states, and adequate representation for Opposition parties in the proposed Delimitation Commission.
Sule had argued that increasing the number of seats was necessary as the growing electorate had made it difficult for MPs to serve large constituencies effectively.
However, on Friday, she maintained that the party would take a formal position only after examining the actual legislation. She said the party had not yet received the Bill and questioned how it could announce a final stand without reviewing its provisions.
Which Other Parties Are Supporting Delimitation?
The NCP-SP’s announcement comes as several regional parties have indicated that they could support the proposed exercise, subject to safeguards.
DMK: The Tamil Nadu ruling party has indicated that it could consider supporting the revised proposal if the state’s existing share of Lok Sabha seats is protected. It has also sought safeguards against frequent delimitation exercises.
YSR Congress Party (YSRCP): The party led by YS Jagan Mohan Reddy has signalled support, provided the revised arrangement protects regional balance and ensures a proportionate increase in seats for southern states.
NCP-SP: The Sharad Pawar-led party has now announced its support, with Sule having earlier called for a uniform 50 per cent increase in seats across states and implementation of women’s reservation.
The Congress, meanwhile, has opposed the bill, arguing that the 33 per cent women’s reservation should be implemented without linking it to a fresh delimitation exercise. The Samajwadi Party has also raised concerns over the need for a Census before delimitation and representation for OBCs and minority women.
Quick Answers
Party leader Jitendra Awhad announced that the NCP (Sharadchandra Pawar) agreed to back the exercise because they consider the delimitation process to be a constitutional requirement.

title: News This Week (Nov 23-27): Centre's Delimitation Bill Push, Jensen Huang's Return, Sooryavanshi's 200 & Mo
description: From Parliament's delimitation push and Jensen Huang's Nvidia comeback to Vaibhav Sooryavanshi's record-breaking 200 and fresh US tariffs, here's what made headlines this week.
author: Saurabh Verma
content:
News This Week (Nov 23-27): Centre's Delimitation Bill Push, Jensen Huang's Return, Sooryavanshi's 200 & More
From Parliament's delimitation push and Jensen Huang's Nvidia comeback to Vaibhav Sooryavanshi's record-breaking 200 and fresh US tariffs, here's what made headlines this week.
News This Week (November 23-27): From the corridors of Parliament to the cricket field, this week was packed with developments that made headlines across politics, business, sports and entertainment. The government’s fresh push for the delimitation and women’s reservation legislation, Jensen Huang’s return to Nvidia, and 15-year-old Vaibhav Sooryavanshi’s record-breaking double century grabbed attention. Meanwhile, a proposed US tariff move targeting Indian imports and Sooraj Barjatya’s latest film, Yeh Prem Mol Liya, also kept the news cycle buzzing. Here’s a look at the biggest stories that shaped the week.
Delimitation Bill In Parliament
- Jensen Huang Returns To Nvidia HQ, Promises To Be A 'Better CEO' As Staff Cheer | Video
- 'I'd Rather Torture You Into Greatness': Nvidia's Jensen Huang Accused Of Humiliating Employees
- Jensen Huang To Face US Senators In Public Hearing On Nvidia, China Chip Sales
- Spy Links, China Chips & More: The Questions Still Haunting Jensen Huang As He Returns To Nvidia
The government has convened a special session of Parliament to introduce crucial legislation linked to delimitation and the implementation of the women’s reservation law. The proposed delimitation bill was defeated in the Lok Sabha in April this year after the government failed to secure the required support. However, the government now appears confident of getting the legislation passed.
The proposed exercise seeks to increase the strength of the Lok Sabha from the existing 543 seats to a maximum of 850. The government maintains that the move will pave the way for implementing 33 per cent reservation for women in Parliament and state legislatures ahead of the 2029 general elections.
Jensen Huang Returns As Nvidia CEO
Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang returned to the helm of the artificial intelligence giant after the company’s board reinstated him following his brief exit. His departure had triggered a sharp decline in Nvidia shares and stocks of companies closely linked to the AI industry.
The company said it decided to reinstate Huang after receiving information from the US government indicating that he did not pose a national security risk. His return sparked a rally in Nvidia shares, which had come under pressure during his absence.
Vaibhav Sooryavanshi Smashes Record-Breaking Double Century
The young batter smashed 28 sixes and seven fours to power India to a seven-wicket victory on Tuesday. He reached his century in just 28 balls, breaking the previous List A record of a 29-ball hundred held by Australia’s Jake Fraser-McGurk.
Sooryavanshi also became the fastest batter to score a double century in List A cricket, reaching the milestone in just 52 balls.
Yeh Prem Mol Liya: Release And Storyline
What happens when love challenges long-standing societal norms? Sooraj Barjatya’s Yeh Prem Mol Liya, starring Ayushmann Khurrana and Sharvari, explores this question through an unconventional love story.
The film follows Prem, a music composer looking for his big break, who finds inspiration in Purva, a journalist. What begins as a one-sided attraction gradually develops into friendship, but a family emergency changes their relationship.
Purva has the responsibility of looking after her all-women family and cannot leave her home after marriage. Prem must therefore confront traditional expectations and challenge societal stereotypes to make their relationship work.
Fresh US Tariff Proposal For India
The United States has proposed imposing tariffs of up to 25 per cent on imports from India, with a provision to bring the rate down to 17 per cent if the two countries reach a bilateral trade agreement.
The proposal follows investigations initiated by the US Trade Representative (USTR) into 16 economies over concerns related to structural excess capacity and production in manufacturing sectors.
The jurisdictions under investigation include China, the European Union, Singapore, Switzerland, Indonesia, Malaysia, Cambodia, Thailand, South Korea, Vietnam, Taiwan, Bangladesh, Japan, Norway, Mexico and India.
From major political decisions and global trade developments to sporting milestones and big-screen releases, this week offered plenty to keep readers engaged. That’s a wrap on this week’s biggest stories. We’ll be back with another roundup of the developments making news across India and the world.
Quick Answers
The proposed delimitation exercise seeks to increase the Lok Sabha strength from 543 seats to a maximum of 850 seats. The government maintains this move will pave the way for implementing a 33 percent reservation for women in Parliament and state legislatures ahead of the 2029 general elections.

title: LOCs Against CJP's Abhijeet Dipke, Ashutosh Ranka And Saurav Das: What Is It And Why Was It Issued?
description: A Look Out Circular (LOC) is an alert issued by authorities through Bureau of Immigration to airports and border exit points to monitor or stop a named person from leaving country
author: News18
content:
LOCs Against CJP's Abhijeet Dipke, Ashutosh Ranka And Saurav Das: What Is It And Why Was It Issued?
A Look Out Circular (LOC) is an alert issued by authorities through Bureau of Immigration to airports and border exit points to monitor or stop a named person from leaving country
Got Question about the News?
The Mumbai Police recently issued Look Out Circulars (LOC) against Cockroach Janata Party (CJP) leaders Abhijeet Dipke, Ashutosh Ranka and Saurav Das in connection with a First Information Report (FIR) registered on October 3 over an unpermitted protest at Dadar’s Shivaji Park in Mumbai on October 2.
A Look Out Circular (LOC) is an alert issued by authorities through the Bureau of Immigration to airports and border exit points to monitor or stop a named person from leaving the country.
- After Saurav Das, Lookout Circulars Against CJP Founder Abhijeet Dipke, Ashutosh Ranka
- 'Look Out Notice Issued Against CJP's Saurav Das': Centre Tells Delhi HC, Cites Passport Discrepancies
- CJP's Saurav Das Was Stopped At Delhi Airport Over RPO Notice: What Is It?
- Saurav Das Passport Row | Abhijit Dipke Questions Discrepancies | Oxford Trip Blocked | CJP News
THE CASE
The October 3 FIR at Shivaji Park police station followed a Gandhi Jayanti protest where demonstrators demanded the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar. Police invoked provisions including Sections 189 (unlawful assembly) and 223 (disobedience of a public servant’s lawful order) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS), along with Sections 37 and 135 of the Maharashtra Police Act.
Police stated the circulars were issued out of apprehension that the leaders might leave India while the investigation was underway.
DAS STOPPED, DIPKE’S DARE
Immigration officials stopped Saurav Das at Delhi’s Indira Gandhi International Airport on November 23, 2026, as he tried to fly to the UK. After Das petitioned the Delhi High Court, the central government disclosed on November 26, 2026, that the LOC had been requested by Mumbai Police, and officials also cited scrutiny over alleged passport discrepancies.
On November 26, 2026, at a CJP rally at Samvidhan Chowk in Nagpur, Dipke publicly challenged Mumbai Police to arrest him over the LOC, while Ranka dismissed claims that leaders had fled the venue and pledged to expand party outreach.
WHAT IS AN LOC?
In India, a Look Out Circular (LOC) is an administrative alert issued to immigration authorities at international airports, seaports, and land borders to track, stop, or detain a specific individual trying to enter or leave the country.
For the general public, an LOC is not common—you will not have one issued against you during routine travel. However, among law enforcement, financial investigators, and courts, it is a frequently used tool when someone is suspected of trying to flee the country to evade legal action or large financial defaults.
HOW AN LOC WORKS
While investigative agencies request the circular, it is formally opened and enforced by the Bureau of Immigration (BoI) under the Ministry of Home Affairs (MHA).
When an individual flagged by an LOC reaches an immigration counter, officials follow one of three standardized instructions:
- Prevent departure and inform the agency that requested the LOC.
- Detain the individual and hand them over to the requesting agency or local police.
- Monitor and notify (simply log their arrival or departure without stopping them
- Under updated MHA rules, an LOC does not expire automatically after one year; it remains active until the originating agency or a court formally requests its deletion.
WHO CAN REQUEST AN LOC AND WHY?
Under Ministry of Home Affairs guidelines, LOCs cannot be issued arbitrarily—they require a formal request from designated authorities:
Law Enforcement & Investigating Agencies: Police (Superintendent of Police rank and above), CBI, Enforcement Directorate (ED), National Investigation Agency (NIA), Income Tax, and Customs departments—typically when an accused person is evading arrest or trial in a cognizable offense.
Public Sector Banks: Chairmen, Managing Directors, or CEOs of public sector banks are authorized to request LOCs against major “willful defaulters" to prevent them from fleeing India with unpaid loans. (Note: High Courts have placed strict scrutiny on bank-issued LOCs to ensure they do not violate a citizen’s fundamental right to travel.)
Courts of Law: Criminal and civil courts can directly order the BoI to open an LOC during ongoing judicial proceedings.
Statutory bodies like the National Commission for Women or the National Company Law Tribunal cannot directly open an LOC; they must route requests through a police or criminal investigation agency.
HOW COMMON ARE THEY?
Rare for ordinary citizens: Unless you are named in a serious criminal FIR, facing an investigation by agencies like the ED/CBI, involved in a major court dispute, or flagged as a willful loan defaulter, an LOC will not affect you.
Routinely used in investigations: Because LOCs are confidential, the government does not publish a live public database. However, parliamentary disclosures and Right to Information (RTI) data show tens of thousands are issued over multi-year periods—for example, over 40,700 LOCs were issued against foreign nationals alone between 2018 and 2020, and six public sector banks alone issued over 1,070 LOCs against loan defaulters across a five-year span.
Quick Answers
Mumbai Police issued Look Out Circulars against the Cockroach Janata Party leaders in connection with an FIR registered on October 3 over an unpermitted protest at Dadar’s Shivaji Park on Gandhi Jayanti, demanding the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar.

title: NCP (SP) backs delimitation process after Sharad Pawar talks; Supriya Sule to skip INDIA alliance meet
description: NCP SP leader Jitendra Awhad stated the party will support the delimitation process, while Maharashtra minister Uday Samant said the Centre would welcome Sharad Pawar's support.
author: Srabastee Biswas
content:
NCP (SP) backs delimitation process after Sharad Pawar talks; Supriya Sule to skip INDIA alliance meet
- Edited byAjay
- Published OnNov 27, 2026 | 18:36 IST
- Last Updated OnNov 27, 2026 | 18:44 IST
A looming political alignment is drawing attention as the ruling coalition welcomes potential opposition backing for an upcoming constitutional overhaul. Discover how internal party divisions and leadership health are shaping the opposition floor strategy.
NCP (SP) leader Jitendra Awhad on Friday said the party would support the delimitation process, while Maharashtra minister Uday Samant said the BJP-led central government would welcome Sharad Pawar's support for the proposed bill, ANI reported. The statements came amid speculation over the NCP (SP)'s position on the legislation ahead of the special session of Parliament.
Speaking to reporters in Mumbai, Awhad said his discussion with Sharad Pawar was not about the party's official position but focused on delimitation as a constitutional requirement.
"The discussion wasn't about our party's official stance. The general point being made was that the delimitation process is a constitutional requirement... A decision has been made to support the delimitation process, and we will indeed support it. We will support the delimitation," Awhad said, according to ANI.
Samant, meanwhile, said the Centre would welcome Pawar joining the National Democratic Alliance (NDA) or extending support to the delimitation bill.
Speaking to reporters outside Nanded airport before leaving for Hingoli, the Maharashtra Industries Minister said the final decision on the legislation would be taken by Parliament.
"Members of Parliament will decide the delimitation and it will take place in the Lok Sabha and Rajya Sabha. Instead of talking today about who supports whom, we will see in the upcoming session. If Sharad Pawar is coming with the NDA or supports this (delimitation) bill, the central government will welcome it," Samant said.
The remarks came after the NCP (SP) issued a whip on Friday directing its Lok Sabha MPs to remain present in the House from November 30. The move came amid speculation that the party could support the BJP-led government on the proposed delimitation legislation.
Supriya Sule says NCP-SP yet to take a final position on bill
NCP (SP) MP Supriya Sule said she had not seen the proposed legislation and could not comment on the party's position without examining its provisions.
Speaking to reporters in Mumbai about the special Parliament session and the delimitation bill, Sule said she was not aware of the details or the session's agenda. She added that the party would follow its established procedure for issuing a whip.
"I am not aware of the details. The session has been announced, but I do not have the agenda. Our party is a very disciplined party, and the whip is issued by our senior leader Amol Kolhe when the dates are announced. I have not seen the bill yet, so how can I state the party's position on it? I do not know anything about this matter...We are not a faction; we are a party," Sule said.
She also said she would not attend the INDIA bloc meeting scheduled for Saturday to discuss the Opposition's floor strategy for the special Parliament session, as her father, Sharad Pawar, was hospitalised. Pawar was admitted to a hospital in south Mumbai on Thursday due to dehydration.
Samant dismisses 'Operation Tiger' speculation
Separately, Samant dismissed speculation surrounding 'Operation Tiger', a purported attempt to bring leaders from the Uddhav Thackeray-led Shiv Sena (UBT) into the Shiv Sena headed by Deputy Chief Minister Eknath Shinde.
The minister said his party was not looking to induct new leaders and that the government's immediate focus was on drought relief and industrial development in Maharashtra.
"Operation Tiger or someone joining the (Shiv Sena) party is not in my sight now. There is drought in Maharashtra and we are trying to help farmers from every department. As part of this, I am going to Hingoli for a district investment summit," Samant said.
He also said Maharashtra was targeting investment commitments worth ₹1.5 lakh crore. The state had earlier secured memorandums of understanding (MoUs) worth ₹90,000 crore, which increased to ₹1 lakh crore last year, he added.

title: SC seeks Centre's view on caste certificates for children based on mother's identity
description: A bench comprising Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana said that the issue assumes significance especially in cases where the mother has custody of the child.
author: PTI
content:
SC seeks Centre's view on caste certificates for children based on mother's identity
- Published OnNov 27, 2026 | 17:46 IST
- Last Updated OnNov 27, 2026 | 17:46 IST
The apex court wants the government to explore uniform guidelines for issuing caste certificates through maternal identity amid single motherhood and adoption cases, while preserving established constitutional reservation principles. How will the Centre balance legal precedents with evolving family structures?
The Supreme Court on Friday asked the Centre to examine the possibility of framing guidelines for issuing caste certificates to children based on their mother’s caste identity in cases involving divorce, abandonment, adoption and single motherhood.
A bench comprising Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana said that the issue assumes significance especially in cases where the mother has custody of the child.
The bench also deliberated on whether an exception could be carved out to the established principle of determining a child’s caste with reference to the father’s caste, without disturbing the principles laid down in Constitution Bench judgments dealing with caste-based reservations and migration.
It asked the Centre, represented by Attorney General R Venkataramani, to examine the issue.
The bench asked the attorney general to assist it in addressing the legal and constitutional questions involved.
It declined to segregate cases involving parents belonging to the same caste from those arising out of inter-caste marriages, saying that the issues would be considered together.
The pleas were adjourned for further consideration.
