title: Maharashtra makes check dams mandatory alongside every new bridge to boost water storage
description: Maharashtra has also planned small lakes on grazing land and extended the Gaalmukt Dharan scheme until June 30 to help improve water storage and support farmers.
author: CNBCTV18.com
content:
Maharashtra makes check dams mandatory alongside every new bridge to boost water storage
- Edited bySudarsanan M
- Published OnNov 27, 2026 | 17:35 IST
- Last Updated OnNov 27, 2026 | 17:38 IST
To combat severe drought, Maharashtra is mandating check dams alongside all new state and central bridges to retain crucial river water. Officials are also launching local lake excavation projects and extending free silt removal initiatives to support farming communities. Find out how these multi-agency water policies will impact upcoming infrastructure budgets.
The Maharashtra government has decided to use new bridges as a way to save rainwater and improve water supply. Under the new rule, every new bridge built over a river or stream will also have to include a check dam. The rule will cover projects funded by both the state and Central governments.
The decision comes at a time when Maharashtra is facing drought and water shortages. The government wants to make better use of available water and increase the amount of water stored in rivers and streams.
The decision was taken at a meeting of the Cabinet Sub-Committee on Drought Mitigation on Wednesday. Revenue Minister Chandrashekhar Bawankule chaired the meeting, which was attended by Water Resources Minister Girish Mahajan and senior government officials.
Bawankule said the government wants to ensure that at least one metre of water is stored below every bridge. Check dams are small barriers built across rivers and streams. They slow down the flow of water and help collect it at one place.
The new rule will apply to bridges built by the Public Works Department, Maharashtra State Road Development Corporation (MSRDC), Mumbai Metropolitan Region Development Authority (MMRDA), City and Industrial Development Corporation (CIDCO) and Navi Mumbai Airport Influence Notified Area (NAINA).
It will also cover bridges built under the Chief Minister's Gram Sadak Yojana. The government is planning to include bridge-cum-check dams in the proposed Shaktipeeth Expressway project as well.
The state government is also considering proposals from gram panchayats to build small lakes on grazing land. Each lake will cover an area of two to three acres. The plan is aimed at increasing water storage and improving water availability in the coming years.
The government has extended the deadline of the Gaalmukt Dharan scheme until June 30. Under this scheme, silt is removed from tanks managed by gram panchayats, Zilla Parishads and Malgujari authorities. The removed silt is then given to farmers free of cost for use on their farms.
The government has fixed the rate for removing silt at ₹32 per cubic metre. The transportation cost has been set at ₹37 per cubic metre. The maximum subsidy available under the scheme is ₹37,500.

title: दुबई से पंजाब तक निवेश की बयार: इन्वेस्टर्स को मिलेगी बिजली शुल्क और टैक्स में 100% छूट, मंत्री अमन अरोड़ा का बड़ा ऐलान
description: पंजाब की आम आदमी पार्टी सरकार ने राज्य में निवेश बढ़ाने के लिए बड़ी पहल की है. सरकार ने प्रदेश में निवेश करने वाले उद्यमियों को बिजली और टैक्स में 100 फीसदी छूट देने का एलान किया है.
author: देवेंद्र कुमार
content:
भारत के सबसे तेजी से उभरते औद्योगिक राज्यों में अपनी पैठ मजबूत करते हुए, पंजाब के उद्योग एवं वाणिज्य मंत्री अमन अरोड़ा ने संयुक्त अरब अमीरात (UAE) के निवेशकों और वैश्विक कारोबारियों को पंजाब की धरती पर कारोबार करने के लिए खुला निमंत्रण दिया है. दुबई में आयोजित वार्षिक निवेश बैठक (AIM) के दौरान उन्होंने स्पष्ट किया कि मान सरकार निवेशकों को लुभाने के लिए पूरी तरह तैयार है और राज्य की नई औद्योगिक एवं व्यापार विकास नीति-2026 के तहत कई बेहतरीन सौगातें दी जा रही हैं.
इस दौरान मंत्री ने निवेशकों को भरोसा दिलाया कि 'इन्वेस्ट पंजाब' सिंगल-विंडो प्लेटफॉर्म के जरिए उन्हें हर चरण पर पूरा सहयोग मिलेगा, ताकि वे बिना किसी प्रशासनिक उलझन के आसानी से अपना बिजनेस स्थापित कर सकें.
फूड प्रोसेसिंग से लेकर हरित ऊर्जा तक: इन क्षेत्रों में निवेश का सबसे बड़ा न्योता
पंजाब सरकार चाहती है कि यूएई के निवेशक राज्य को सिर्फ एक बड़े बाजार के रूप में न देखें, बल्कि विनिर्माण, लॉजिस्टिक्स और वैश्विक स्तर के कारोबार के लिए एक मजबूत रणनीतिक साझेदार के रूप में अपनाएं. बैठक में विशेष रूप से निम्नलिखित क्षेत्रों पर जोर दिया गया:
अमन अरोड़ा ने बताया कि राज्य का मुख्य उद्देश्य कारोबार करने में आसानी (Ease of Doing Business), त्वरित मंजूरियों और पूरी नीतिगत पारदर्शिता के साथ निवेशकों को अधिकतम सहायता प्रदान करना है.
नई औद्योगिक नीति-2026: 100% से 125% तक वित्तीय प्रोत्साहन और आकर्षक पैकेज
पंजाब की नई औद्योगिक एवं व्यापार विकास नीति निवेशकों के लिए बेहद फायदेमंद साबित हो रही है. मंत्री ने इसके खास प्रावधानों की जानकारी देते हुए बताया कि किस तरह यह नीति नई इकाइयों के साथ-साथ पुरानी इकाइयों के विस्तार में भी मददगार है:
शानदार वित्तीय रिटर्न: पात्र विनिर्माण इकाइयों को स्थिर फिक्स्ड कैपिटल इन्वेस्टमेंट (FCI) का 100 प्रतिशत तक वित्तीय प्रोत्साहन मिल सकता है. वहीं, प्राथमिकता वाले क्षेत्रों, सीमावर्ती जिलों और कंडी इलाकों की इकाइयों के लिए यह दायरा बढ़कर 125 प्रतिशत तक हो जाता है (यह लाभ कुल 500 करोड़ रुपये की सीमा के अधीन है).
पूंजी और टैक्स में छूट: पात्र FCI का 20 प्रतिशत तक कैपिटल सब्सिडी (अधिकतम 10 करोड़ रुपये तक), शुद्ध SGST की 75 प्रतिशत तक प्रतिपूर्ति और बिजली शुल्क पर 100 प्रतिशत की पूरी छूट शामिल है.
रोजगार से जुड़ा लाभ: यह नीति नई नौकरियों के सृजन और आधुनिक तकनीकों को अपनाने पर अतिरिक्त प्रोत्साहन भी देती है.
राजपुरा का 1,100 एकड़ का एकीकृत विनिर्माण क्लस्टर: निवेशकों के लिए ड्रीम प्रोजेक्ट
यूएई के निवेशकों को आकर्षित करने के लिए पंजाब सरकार ने अमृतसर-कोलकाता औद्योगिक कॉरिडोर (AKIC) के तहत राजपुरा में एक विशाल 1,100 एकड़ का एकीकृत विनिर्माण क्लस्टर तैयार किया है. अमन अरोड़ा ने इसे विनिर्माण और सहायक उद्योगों से जुड़े कारोबारियों के लिए एक स्वर्णिम अवसर बताया. यह क्लस्टर न केवल बड़े पैमाने पर निवेश खींचेगा, बल्कि स्थानीय युवाओं के लिए रोजगार के नए द्वार भी खोलेगा.
'इन्वेस्ट पंजाब' पोर्टल: घर बैठे डिजिटल रूप से जुड़ने की सुविधा
विदेशी निवेशकों की आसानी के लिए 'इन्वेस्ट पंजाब' को एक बेहद उन्नत और पारदर्शी डिजिटल प्लेटफॉर्म बनाया गया है. अब दुबई या दुनिया के किसी भी कोने में बैठा निवेशक इस पोर्टल के माध्यम से सीधे आवेदन कर सकता है, मंजूरियों की स्थिति ट्रैक कर सकता है और विभाग के चक्कर काटने की झंझट से पूरी तरह मुक्त हो सकता है.
'इन्वेस्ट पंजाब' की टीम निवेशकों को सही जमीन चुनने से लेकर लाइसेंस, सरकारी मंजूरियों और बाद की हर संभव सहायता (आफ्टर-केयर) के लिए पूरी तरह प्रतिबद्ध है. मुख्यमंत्री भगवंत मान के नेतृत्व में पंजाब सरकार यूएई के वैश्विक नेटवर्क और पंजाब की मजबूत मानव संसाधन क्षमताओं को मिलाकर एक दीर्घकालिक और ऐतिहासिक साझेदारी लिखने के लिए पूरी तरह तैयार है.

title: पश्चिम बंगाल विधानसभा में बड़ा उलटफेर: कलकत्ता हाई कोर्ट ने रद्द की बागी TMC नेता ऋतब्रत बनर्जी की LoP नियुक्ति, चीफ व्हिप का फैसला भी खारिज
description: कलकत्ता हाई कोर्ट ने पश्चिम बंगाल विधानसभा में हुई दो बड़ी नियुक्तियों को सिरे से खारिज कर दिया है. कोर्ट ने स्पीकर के उस आदेश को पलट दिया, जिसके तहत TMC के बागी नेता ऋतब्रत बनर्जी को LoP और अखरुज्जमां को चीफ व्हिप बनाया गया था.
author: भूपेंद्र राय
content:
पश्चिम बंगाल से बड़ी खबर है. कलकत्ता हाई कोर्ट ने विधानसभा स्पीकर के फैसले को बड़ा झटका दिया है. कोर्ट ने TMC के बागी नेता ऋतब्रत बनर्जी को नेता प्रतिपक्ष (LoP) बनाने का आदेश रद्द कर दिया है. इसके साथ ही अखरुज्जमां की चीफ व्हिप पद पर नियुक्ति भी खारिज कर दी है. मामले की सुनावई करते हुए जस्टिस कृष्णा राव की बेंच ने साफ कहा कि यह नियुक्ति कानून के तहत टिकने योग्य नहीं है. कोर्ट ने स्पीकर को 10 दिनों के भीतर इस फैसले पर दोबारा विचार करने का निर्देश दिया है.
हाई कोर्ट का यह डिसीजन TMC के ममता बनर्जी गुट के नेता सोभनदेब चट्टोपाध्याय की याचिका पर पर सुनवाई के बाद आया है. उन्होंने ऋतब्रत बनर्जी को नेता प्रतिपक्ष (LoP) बनाए जाने के स्पीकर के फैसले को कोर्ट में चैलेंज किया था.
#WATCH | Kolkata, West Bengal: Lawyer of TMC MLA Sovandeb Chattopadhyay, Srisarnno Bannerjee says, "Today, the court has set aside the order of the speaker in which he had engaged Ritabrata Banerjee as the Leader of Opposition and Akhruzzaman as the Chief Whip and has directed the speaker to take a decision within 10 days as to who shall be the Leader of Opposition. Therefore, the petition filed by Sovandeb Chattopadhyay, who was originally chosen by the All India Trinamool Congress as leader of opposition has been allowed by the court... I hope Ritabrata Banerjee now takes good advice from his advocate friend, Akhruzzaman, whose name I have not seen in a single legal journal so far...."
— ANI (@ANI) November 27, 2026
दरअसल, हाल में प्रदेश में हुए विधानसभा चुनावों के बाद ममता बनर्जी की पार्टी तृणमूल कांग्रेस (TMC) राज्य की सबसे बड़ी विपक्षी पार्टी बनकर उभरी थी. नियम के अनुसार, नेता प्रतिपक्ष का पद उसी पार्टी को मिलता है. इसलिए TMC ने बाकायदा एक चिट्ठी लिखकर विधानसभा स्पीकर को बताया था कि उन्होंने अपने सीनियर विधायक सोभनदेब चट्टोपाध्याय को इस पद के लिए चुना है. लेकिन बवाल तब हुआ जब TMC के ही कुछ विधायकों ने पार्टी से बगावत कर दी.
The Calcutta High Court single bench of Justice Krishna Rao has set aside and quashed the Speaker’s June 3 order appointing Ritabrata Banerjee as Leader of the Opposition and Akhruzzaman as Chief Whip, finding the order unsustainable. The Speaker has been directed to reconsider the appointments of the Leader of the Opposition and Chief Whip in accordance with law within 10 days of receiving the order
— IANS (@ians_india) November 27, 2026
ऋतब्रत बनर्जी की अगुवाई वाले बागी गुट ने भी नेता प्रतिपक्ष की कुर्सी पर अपना दावा ठोक दिया. हैरानी की बात यह रही कि विधानसभा स्पीकर ने मुख्य पार्टी (TMC) के फैसले को नजरअंदाज किया और बागी गुट की बात मानते हुए 3 जून को ऋतब्रत बनर्जी को ही नेता प्रतिपक्ष घोषित कर दिया.
लाइव लॉ की रिपोर्ट के अनुसार, तृणमूल कांग्रेस (TMC) के वरिष्ठ विधायक सोभनदेब चट्टोपाध्याय ने याचिका में स्पीकर के उस फैसले को चुनौती दी थी, जिसमें पार्टी के आधिकारिक उम्मीदवार यानी खुद सोभनदेब को नजरअंदाज कर दिया गया था. स्पीकर ने उनकी जगह TMC के एक बागी गुट के नेता ऋतब्रत बनर्जी को नेता प्रतिपक्ष बना दिया था. इससे पहले सुप्रीम कोर्ट ने भी हाई कोर्ट को इस विवाद को जल्द सुलझाने का निर्देश दिया था.
A hearing was scheduled today at the Calcutta High Court regarding the position of the Leader of the Opposition in the West Bengal Legislative Assembly. This legal dispute concerns who should hold the position of Leader of the Opposition in the West Bengal Legislative Assembly—Sovandeb Chattopadhyay or Ritabrata Banerjee. Today, Justice Krishna Rao of the Calcutta High Court announced that the Speaker’s previous decision has been set aside. The decision taken by the Speaker regarding the Leader of the Opposition has been quashed. The Speaker must reach a fresh decision within 10 days.
— ANI (@ANI) November 27, 2026
लाइव लॉ की रिपोर्ट के अनुसार, स्पीकर के इस फैसले के खिलाफ शोभनदेव चट्टोपाध्याय ने कलकत्ता हाई कोर्ट में याचिका दायर कर दी. उनकी दलील थी कि स्पीकर ने राजनीतिक दल के आधिकारिक फैसले की अनदेखी की है. यह मामला पहले सिंगल बेंच और फिर डिवीजन बेंच के पास गया. अगस्त में डिवीजन बेंच ने एक अंतरिम व्यवस्था के तहत ऋतब्रत बनर्जी को दो महीने तक पद पर बने रहने की इजाजत दी थी और सिंगल बेंच को इस मुख्य विवाद पर अंतिम फैसला लेने को कहा था. सिंगल बेंच ने सभी पक्षों की दलीलें सुनने के बाद 21 नवंबर को अपना फैसला सुरक्षित रख लिया था. अब हाई कोर्ट ने ऋतब्रत की नियुक्ति को रद्द करते हुए गेंद वापस स्पीकर के पाले में डाल दी है.

title: तमिलनाडु में पहाड़ी पर नहीं जला दीप तो भड़का सुप्रीम कोर्ट! DGP से लेकर DM तक कई अफसरों को नोटिस, छीना मंदिर का कंट्रोल
description: आदेश के बाद भी मदुरै के दीप स्तंभ पर देव दीपावली को दीपक न जलाना तमिलनाडु की जोसेफ विजय सरकार को भारी पड़ गया है. सुप्रीम कोर्ट ने इस पर गहरी नाराजगी जाहिर करते हुए राज्य सरकार के तमाम अधिकारियों को नोटिस जारी किया है.
author: देवेंद्र कुमार
content:
सुप्रीम कोर्ट के आदेश के बावजूद मदुरै के पास पहाड़ी की चोटी पर बने दीप स्तम्भ पर जोसेफ विजय सरकार ने दीप नहीं जलाया. इससे सुप्रीम कोर्ट भड़क गया है. अदालत ने शुक्रवार को मामले की सुनवाई करते हुए तमिलनाडु के चीफ सेक्रेटरी, डीजीपी. मदुरै के डीएम, पुलिस कमिश्नर, एसपी, तमिलनाडु मंदिर संस्थापन बोर्ड के कमिश्नर व डिप्टी कमिश्नर और मंदिर के कार्यकारी अधिकारी को अवमानना का नोटिस जारी किया है.
मामले की सुनवाई करते हुए जस्टिस अरविंद कुमार और जस्टिस विपुल पंचोली की खंडपीठ ने ये सख्त टिप्पणियां कीं. कोर्ट ने उन सभी को आदेश की अवहेलना पर अपना पक्ष रखने को कहा है. इसके साथ ही, सुप्रीम कोर्ट ने मंदिर बोर्ड को अंतरिम तौर पर मंदिर के काम काज से हटा दिया है. मंदिर के सामान्य कामकाज के संचालन के लिए अदालत 2 रिटायर्ड जजों को फिलहाल रिसीवर नियुक्त किया है.
सुप्रीम कोर्ट ने कहा कि प्रथम दृष्टया यह हरकत जानबूझ कर अदालत के आदेश की अवहेलना दिखती है. जोसेफ विजय सरकार को फटकार लगाते हुए अदालत ने कहा, 'हम डीएम की प्रारंभिक रिपोर्ट और माफीनामा से संतुष्ट नहीं हैं. यह माफीनामा सिर्फ घड़ियाली आंसू हैं. सबको अगली तारीख पर कोर्ट में व्यक्तिगत रूप से पेश होकर इस अवहेलना का जवाब देना होगा.'
अदालत ने मंदिर बोर्ड के ट्रस्टी को भी नोटिस जारी कर जवाब दाखिल करने को कहा है. इसके साथ ही कोर्ट ने मंदिर बोर्ड को अंतरिम तौर पर मंदिर के काम काज से हटा दिया है. साथ ही, अंतरिम व्यवस्था के लिए 2 रिटायर्ड जजों को मंदिर का रिसीवर नियुक्त किया गया है. अदालत ने कहा कि ये दोनों रिसीवर 28 नवंबर को दीपा थून पर पहाड़ी की चोटी पर दीपक जलाना सुनिश्चित करेंगे.
सुप्रीम कोर्ट ने मदुरै में तैनात CRPF कमांडेंट को मंदिर और दरगाह की सुरक्षा अपने नियंत्रण में लेने का आदेश दिया. यह भी हुक्म दिया कि पहाड़ी की चोटी पर दीपक जलाते समय सीआरपीएफ के जवान दोनों रिसीवर की सुरक्षा सुनिश्चित करेंगे. साथ ही, वहां पर कानून-व्यवस्था की स्थिति को भी संभालेंगे.
तिरुप्परनकुंद्रम पहाड़ी पर दीपथून में दीप न जलने को सुप्रीम कोर्ट ने अक्षम्य चूक बताया. अदालत ने कहा कि इस मामले में मंदिर प्रबंधन के स्तर पर ट्रस्टियों की भारी चूक हुई है. लिहाजा, अब मंदिर की व्यवस्था कोर्ट रिसीवर को सौंप दी गई है. ये रिसीवर स्थानीय परंपरा और पूजा-पद्धति के हिसाब से मंदिर का कामकाज संभालेंगे. वहीं, राज्य सरकार को उन्हें पूरा सहयोग देना होगा.
अदालत ने दो टूक कहा कि उसके आदेश कोई मोलभाव या चर्चा का विषय नहीं हैं, बल्कि हर अधिकारी को इनका पालन करना ही होगा. बेंच ने आगाह किया कि आदेशों की अनदेखी करने वालों से सख्ती से निपटने का वक्त आ गया है, वरना संवैधानिक अराजकता के हालात बन सकते हैं. कोर्ट ने कड़े शब्दों में कहा कि चाहे कोई कितने भी बड़े पद पर क्यों न हो, लेकिन न्याय की प्रक्रिया को कमजोर करने की हरकत बर्दाश्त नहीं की जाएगी.
संविधान के अनुच्छेद 144 का जिक्र करते हुए अदालत ने याद दिलाया कि सभी अधिकारियों की जिम्मेदारी है कि वे सुप्रीम कोर्ट के आदेशों को लागू करने में मदद करें. इसमें किसी भी तरह की कोताही नहीं होनी चाहिए. उल्लंघन होने पर कोर्ट चुप नहीं बैठ सकता और अवमानना कानून का इस्तेमाल करने से भी नहीं हिचकेगा. कोर्ट ने तमिलनाडु के चीफ सेक्रेटरी, डीजीपी समेत 13 अफसरों को अवमानना नोटिस जारी कर पूछा है कि 20 नवंबर के आदेश की अवहेलना पर उनके खिलाफ कार्रवाई क्यों न की जाए.
सुनवाई के दौरान याचिकाकर्ताओं की ओर से वरिष्ठ वकील गुरु कृष्णकुमार और जे. साई दीपक ने पैरवी की. एएसआई की तरफ से पेश सॉलिसिटर जनरल ने भी उनकी मांग का समर्थन करते हुए दीप स्तंभ पर दीप जलाने को उचित बताया. दूसरी तरफ, तमिलनाडु सरकार और अधिकारियों के वकीलों ने दावा किया कि मदुरै कलेक्टर ने कोर्ट के आदेश के पालन में जरूरी कदम उठाए थे और उनकी अंतिम रिपोर्ट का इंतजार किया जाना चाहिए.
मंदिर के कार्यकारी अधिकारी के वकील ने कहा कि दीप जलाने के स्थान का फैसला ट्रस्ट बोर्ड ने बैठक में लिया था, जिसे बदलने का अधिकार उनके पास नहीं था. उन्होंने कहा कि क्षेत्र में कानून-व्यवस्था बनाए रखने के लिए 5,797 जवान तैनात थे और कहीं कोई उल्लंघन नहीं हुआ.

title: Delhi's Kusumpur Pahadi Says No More to Child Marriage: Can India Meet the 2030 Target?
description: Around 2,000 people join a campaign in Delhi's Kusumpur Pahadi against child marriage as India works towards its 2030 elimination target.
author: Harsh Trivedi
content:
Delhi's Kusumpur Pahadi Says No More to Child Marriage: Can India Meet the 2030 Target?
Around 2,000 people gathered in Delhi's Kusumpur Pahadi on Constitution Day to pledge action against child marriage. With prevalence declining to 20.1% in 2023-24, the campaign highlights India's challenge of eliminating the practice by 2030.
- India News
- 3 min read
New Delhi: A neighbourhood better known for its crowded lanes became the centre of a campaign against child marriage on Thursday evening, as around 2,000 women, children, survivors and local residents gathered in Delhi's Kusumpur Pahadi to take a stand against the practice.
Marking Constitution Day, the gathering saw residents light diyas and participate in an awareness march led by Union Minister of State for Women and Child Development Savitri Thakur. Organised by Just Rights for Children (JRC), the initiative brought together community members and survivors to underline the need for collective action against child marriage.
For JRC founder Bhuwan Ribhu, the gathering was part of a much larger fight that must extend beyond awareness events and government campaigns. Speaking at the programme, Ribhu described the international recognition of November 27 as the International Day for the Elimination of Child, Early and Forced Marriage as a "historic tipping point".
He also highlighted the 2030 deadline to end child marriage, pointing out that five years is a short window to eliminate a practice that has continued for centuries. The challenge, he indicated, is to turn growing international recognition and national commitments into action at the grassroots.
Advertisement
Survivor's Story From the Neighbourhood
The gathering also brought forward the experience of a child marriage survivor from Kusumpur Pahadi, who shared how she managed to stop her own marriage by contacting a helpline.
Now studying in Class 11, she spoke about how reaching out for help changed the course of her life. Her account highlighted the importance of awareness, accessible support systems and timely intervention in preventing child marriages.
Advertisement
The story also brought the focus back to the role of local communities, where neighbours and residents can often be the first to know about an impending underage marriage.
Numbers Behind the Campaign
Addressing the gathering, Thakur cited National Family Health Survey figures showing that child marriage prevalence declined from 47.4 per cent in 2005-06 to 20.1 per cent in 2023-24.
She also highlighted the Bal Vivah Mukt Bharat campaign, launched in 2024, which has conducted over 6.86 lakh awareness programmes, reaching approximately 12.5 crore people.
While the decline marks progress, one in five girls continuing to be affected underlines the distance still to be covered.
A Neighbourhood's Pledge, a National Challenge
As part of the programme, Thakur administered an oath in which participants pledged not to be involved in child marriages and to report such cases to the authorities.
The message from Kusumpur Pahadi was that preventing child marriage cannot remain the responsibility of government agencies alone. Families, neighbourhoods, community leaders and local authorities all have a role to play.
With November 27 marking the first International Day for the Elimination of Child, Early and Forced Marriage, the gathering also sought to connect a local campaign with a wider global effort.
For Ribhu and the organisation, the 2030 target remains the larger objective. For the residents of Delhi's Kusumpur Pahadi, the message on Thursday was more immediate: no girl should have to give up her childhood because of an early marriage.

title: 'Light Deepam at Deepathoon Tomorrow': SC Orders Ritual, Suspends Temple Trustees, Directs CRPF Security Amid Row
description: The Supreme Court ordered Karthigai Deepam lighting at Tamil Nadu's Deepathoon on November 28, suspended temple trustees and handed hill security to the CRPF.
author: Melvin Narayan
content:
'Light Deepam at Deepathoon Tomorrow': SC Orders Ritual, Suspends Temple Trustees, Directs CRPF Security Amid Row
The Supreme Court has ordered the Karthigai Deepam lamp to be lit at Thiruparankundram's Deepathoon on November 28. The bench also suspended the temple trustees, appointed two retired judges as receivers and directed the CRPF to oversee security amid the ongoing row.
- India News
- 5 min read
New Delhi: The Supreme Court on Friday directed that the traditional Karthigai Deepam lamp be lit at the disputed Deepathoon pillar atop Thiruparankundram hill in Tamil Nadu's Madurai district on Saturday, November 28, amid an escalating legal row over the implementation of its earlier order.
The court also suspended the temple's Board of Trustees, appointed two retired judges as receivers and directed the Central Reserve Police Force (CRPF) to take charge of security at the temple and the hill.
A bench of Justices Aravind Kumar and Vipul M Pancholi issued the directions while hearing contempt petitions alleging wilful disobedience of its November 20 order, which had permitted the lighting of the ceremonial lamp at Deepathoon on November 24 as a one-time arrangement.
Contempt Notice to TN Officials
The Supreme Court also issued contempt notices to Tamil Nadu Chief Secretary, Director General of Police (DGP), Madurai District Collector and other senior officials, seeking their explanation over the alleged failure to implement its directions.
Advertisement
The notices extend to the Secretary and Commissioner of the Hindu Religious and Charitable Endowments (HR&CE) Department, Madurai Police Commissioner, Superintendent of Police and temple authorities, among others. The Chief Secretary has been directed to ensure that the notices are personally served on the officials within three days and submit an affidavit confirming compliance.
The bench directed the newly appointed receivers to ensure that the lamp is lit at the Deepathoon on Saturday, November 28, considering the religious significance of the Karthigai Deepam festival. The court also permitted devotees to light the lamp at the pillar, subject to the condition that the ritual be conducted at least 50 metres away from the Sikandar Dargah situated on the hill.
Advertisement
The court further directed that the lamp be lit using the flame from the ceremonial lamp at the Uchipillaiyar Mandapam. The CRPF has been tasked with ensuring security arrangements and protecting both the temple and the dargah so that devotees can perform their respective religious rituals peacefully.
SC Pulls Up Tamil Nadu Government
During the hearing, the Supreme Court strongly criticised the Tamil Nadu government and authorities over their failure to implement the November 20 order. The bench observed that the failure to light the lamp at Deepathoon, when viewed alongside the temple board's resolution, prima facie indicated wilful and flagrant disobedience of the court's directions.
The court reportedly remarked that the time had come to deal with the situation with an iron hand, warning that such conduct could lead to constitutional chaos. It also observed that an order passed by the Supreme Court was not an invitation for negotiations until the court itself modified it.
The bench took note of the failure of the state police and administration to ensure compliance with its earlier directions and subsequently transferred security arrangements for the entire hill to the CRPF.
How the Deepathoon Controversy Escalated
The controversy centres on the location of the traditional Karthigai Deepam lamp at Thiruparankundram hill in Madurai. The dispute concerns the lighting of the ceremonial lamp at Deepathoon, a stone pillar located near the Sikandar Dargah, instead of the customary Deepa Mandapam near the Uchipillaiyar Temple.
On November 20, the Supreme Court had permitted the lighting of the lamp at Deepathoon on November 24 as a one-time arrangement. The order specified that the ritual should be performed between 6 pm and 6.30 pm by a team authorised by the Arulmigu Subramaniaswamy Temple Devasthanam, with the district administration responsible for coordinating the arrangements.
However, the lamp was not lit at the designated pillar on November 24. Instead, the ceremonial lamp was lit at the traditional Deepa Mandapam near the Uchipillaiyar Temple.
Following the development, Madurai District Collector Nishant Krishna submitted a preliminary status report before the Supreme Court, apologising for the failure to implement the directions. He attributed the situation to the temple's Board of Trustees, stating that it had not authorised the team that was supposed to carry out the ritual at Deepathoon.
The temple board maintained that the lamp should be lit at the customary location, citing longstanding religious traditions, customs and Agama rules. The issue subsequently triggered contempt petitions alleging deliberate non-compliance with the Supreme Court's order.
The Supreme Court's latest directions mark a significant development in the ongoing dispute, with the lamp now ordered to be lit at Deepathoon on November 28 under the supervision of the court-appointed receivers and security arrangements by the CRPF.

title: Big Boost for NDA: Sharad Pawar's NCP-SP With 8 Lok Sabha MPs to Back Delimitation Bill
description: Sharad Pawar-led NCP-SP has decided to support the Centre's proposed Delimitation Bill, MLA Jitendra Awhad confirmed after meeting the party chief. The party's eight Lok Sabha MPs could provide support to the NDA as the legislation heads for a crucial parliamentary session.
author: Melvin Narayan
content:
Big Boost for NDA: Sharad Pawar's NCP-SP With 8 Lok Sabha MPs to Back Delimitation Bill
Sharad Pawar-led NCP-SP has decided to support the Centre's proposed Delimitation Bill, MLA Jitendra Awhad confirmed after meeting the party chief. The party's eight Lok Sabha MPs could provide support to the NDA as the legislation heads for a crucial parliamentary session.
- India News
- 3 min read
Mumbai: In a significant political development ahead of the special Parliament session, the Sharad Pawar-led Nationalist Congress Party (NCP-SP) has decided to support the Centre's proposed Delimitation Bill, with party MLA Jitendra Awhad confirming the decision after meeting NCP-SP chief Sharad Pawar on Friday.
The party, which has eight members in the Lok Sabha, is expected to extend its support to the proposed legislation, potentially providing a boost to the BJP-led NDA government's efforts to secure the numbers required to pass the Bill.
Awhad confirmed the party's position after meeting Sharad Pawar in Mumbai. The development comes amid growing speculation over the NCP-SP's stand on the proposed delimitation exercise and its implications for Opposition unity.
The announcement is significant as the NCP-SP had earlier indicated that it was open to supporting the proposed legislation, subject to certain conditions, including a uniform 50 per cent increase in Lok Sabha seats across all states.
Advertisement
Party working president and Baramati MP Supriya Sule had previously maintained that the party would examine the provisions of the proposed Bill before taking a final position. She had also argued that women's reservation should be implemented alongside delimitation and that no state should be disadvantaged in the redistribution of parliamentary representation.
The Union Cabinet on Friday cleared amendments to the Delimitation and Women's Reservation Bills, proposing a 50 per cent increase in Lok Sabha seats. The proposed changes could increase the strength of the Lower House from the existing 543 elected seats to as many as 850.
Advertisement
The legislation is aimed at facilitating the implementation of 33 per cent reservation for women in the Lok Sabha and state legislative assemblies through the delimitation exercise.
The development could also have political implications for the INDIA bloc, of which the NCP-SP is a constituent. The Congress has opposed linking the implementation of women's reservation with delimitation, raising concerns that the proposed exercise could alter the balance of political representation between states.
Congress leaders have reportedly been attempting to persuade Sharad Pawar and Supriya Sule against supporting the legislation, with concerns that such a move could weaken Opposition unity ahead of the 2029 Lok Sabha elections.
The NCP-SP's eight Lok Sabha MPs could prove important in the parliamentary arithmetic surrounding the proposed constitutional amendments, which require a special majority for passage.
The special sitting of Parliament is scheduled to begin in the Lok Sabha on November 30 and will continue until December 4. The Rajya Sabha is scheduled to reconvene on December 2.
The NCP-SP's decision to support the proposed Bill marks a significant development ahead of the special session, particularly as several Opposition parties continue to question the Centre's approach to delimitation and its proposed link with women's reservation.

title: Post-Sindoor information strategy gathers pace: India hosts second group of foreign defence journalists
description: Thirty-three journalists from 32 countries get access to Army, Navy, and Air Force establishments, defence companies, and military formations as New Delhi steps up international outreach.
author: Snehesh Alex Philip
content:
Post-Sindoor information strategy gathers pace: India hosts second group of foreign defence journalists
Thirty-three journalists from 32 countries get access to Army, Navy, and Air Force establishments, defence companies, and military formations as New Delhi steps up international outreach.
India is hosting a group of 33 defence journalists from 32 countries, including the United States, Armenia, Vietnam, and Sri Lanka, giving them access to military establishments of the Army, Navy and Air Force, as well as visits to defence companies and shipyards.
This is the second such visit organised by the Ministry of External Affairs (MEA) this year as part of India's broader international outreach following Operation Sindoor. The first visit, held in February, saw participation of journalists from 28 countries.
The initiative, unprecedented in its scale and access, marks a shift in India's engagement with the foreign media following Operation Sindoor. More such curated visits are in the pipeline, sources said, adding that the aim is to instutionalise it.
The initiative was conceived and driven by the Ministry of External Affairs, particularly its External Publicity Division, in coordination with the spokespersons of the three armed services.
Sources explained that the first visit was a success with over 400 pages of reports being filed by them all together. They said that many journalists have also put in visa requests for follow-up on their own since they wanted to visit India to pursue more stories.
The two-week programme began on November 16, with the journalists visiting India’s leading shipyard Mazagon Dock Shipbuilders Limited, that specialises in submarine manufacturing.
They were subsequently taken to the Air Force's Maintenance Command in Nashik, where they were briefed on how the IAF maintains and services its diverse fleet of aircraft.
At Bharat Forge in Nagpur, the group was briefed on the company's artillery programmes and other defence initiatives, including armoured vehicles. Interestingly, Armenia has deployed artillery guns manufactured by the Indian company.
The journalists also visited Sulur Air Force Station, where they were briefed on the Tejas fighter aircraft.
Besides interacting with senior officers from the Army, Navy, and Air Force, journalists are scheduled to spend two days with the Army's 12 Corps. The programme will include live demonstrations of military manoeuvres and Special Forces tactics.
External Affairs Minister S Jaishankar also met visiting journalists.
The latest initiative builds on India's efforts to provide foreign defence correspondents with greater access to its military establishments and defence infrastructure.
Last year, following Operation Sindoor, the MEA and other government agencies facilitated a visit by Shashank Joshi, Defence Editor of The Economist, to the northern front, with a focus on infrastructure development along India's border with China.
The visit was notable for the level of access provided by the Army, without the usual curated interactions and tightly controlled media briefings.
Sources said more visits are being planned for specialist journalists based overseas as well as foreign correspondents posted in India. The concerned departments, including the MEA, have also been asked to establish protocols for foreign journalists seeking access to military establishments and information, and to take a more proactive approach to such requests.
The government has also stepped up the role of a multi-agency information warfare group through which several outreach and communication initiatives are being planned and executed.
Over the past three years, the MEA has engaged journalists and influencers from over 143 countries, with the intensity of these interactions increasing in recent months.
The latest visit is part of a wider effort to familiarise international media with India's military capabilities, defence manufacturing ecosystem, and security priorities while also ensuring that the country's perspective reaches a wider global audience.

title: 50% more Lok Sabha seats, 33% women’s quota and 2051 freeze: Can BJP pass the Delimitation Bill?
description: The BJP is stepping up efforts to secure the numbers needed to pass the Delimitation Bill in Parliament. The YSR Congress Party (YSRCP) has signalled support for the proposed legislation, while the DMK, one of its strongest critics, appears open to reconsidering its position. The four-day Parliament sitting beginning November 30 will be crucial for the Centre's numbers game
author: FP Explainers
content:
50% more Lok Sabha seats, 33% women’s quota and 2051 freeze: Can BJP pass the Delimitation Bill?
The BJP is stepping up efforts to secure the numbers needed to pass the Delimitation Bill in Parliament. The YSR Congress Party (YSRCP) has signalled support for the proposed legislation, while the DMK, one of its strongest critics, appears open to reconsidering its position. The four-day Parliament sitting beginning November 30 will be crucial for the Centre's numbers game
The Centre has renewed its push for the delimitation bill, and now it's getting support from the southern part of the country as well. YSR Congress Party (YSRCP) has signalled its willingness to support the proposed legislation. Meanwhile, the DMK, which was one of the most vocal opponents of a population-based exercise, is now indicating that it could reconsider its position.
The bill is likely to be taken up in the coming four-day Parliament sitting from November 30.
Let's look into it more closely.
What is the government's proposal
The Union Cabinet has cleared a fresh delimitation-linked Constitution Amendment Bill aimed at increasing the strength of the Lok Sabha and facilitating the implementation of 33 per cent reservation for women.
The government has introduced two key changes to its earlier proposal: a uniform 50 per cent increase in Lok Sabha seats across states and an extension of the freeze on state-wise seat allocation based on the 1971 Census until 2051.
The Union Cabinet has approved a Constitution Amendment Bill providing for women’s reservation through delimitation. The proposal provides for an equal proportionate increase of 50 per cent in seats across all states, while maintaining their existing relative shares until 2051.
The government’s earlier legislative package, introduced in April, included the Constitution (131st Amendment) Bill, the Delimitation Bill and the Union Territories Laws (Amendment) Bill. The constitutional amendment proposed raising the maximum strength of the Lok Sabha from 550 to 850, including up to 815 members from states and 35 from Union Territories.
The accompanying Delimitation Bill proposed setting up a delimitation commission to readjust seats and redraw constituencies.
Under the earlier proposal, the delimitation commission would be headed by a sitting or retired Supreme Court judge. It would undertake the exercise of readjusting the number of seats allocated to states and redrawing constituency boundaries using the latest available Census figures when the commission is constituted.
How the 50% increase works
The government has proposed increasing Lok Sabha seats by 50 per cent for every state, rather than distributing the additional seats solely on the basis of population figures. This would allow states to gain additional parliamentary constituencies while maintaining their existing proportion of representation in the Lok Sabha.
Union Law Minister Arjun Ram Meghwal had explained the government’s earlier proposal in Parliament by saying that every state would receive 50 per cent more seats.
He said: “The total Lok Sabha seats would be 815, and 272 will be reserved for women.”
Prime Minister Narendra Modi had assured Parliament that there would be “no change in those ratios”, referring to the existing proportion of representation among states.
Union Home Minister Amit Shah had also presented figures to argue that the share of the five southern states would increase under the proposed arrangement.
The fresh proposal retains the uniform 50 per cent increase in Lok Sabha seats across states.
The government has incorporated this provision to address concerns that states which have successfully controlled population growth could lose their relative parliamentary representation under a population-based redistribution.
Why the Centre wants to freeze state-wise seat shares
The Centre has proposed extending the existing freeze on using the 1971 Census as the basis for determining the proportional strength of states in the Lok Sabha by another 25 years, taking it up to 2051.
This means the relative share of parliamentary seats allocated to states would remain protected during this period.
State-wise Lok Sabha seat allocation has been based on the 1971 Census since 1976. A constitutional amendment that year froze the allocation until the first Census conducted after 2000. A subsequent amendment extended the freeze until the first Census after 2026. The stated objective behind the earlier extensions was to encourage states to continue population-control measures.
The government is seeking to balance population-based representation with the concerns of states that have pursued population stabilisation.
Southern states, including Andhra Pradesh, Telangana, Tamil Nadu, Kerala and Karnataka, have expressed concerns that a fresh redistribution based on population could reduce their relative representation compared with states that have recorded higher population growth.
The government’s position has been that no state would lose its existing share of representation during the exercise.
The proposed uniform increase in seats is intended to allow states to gain additional constituencies without altering their relative proportions in the Lok Sabha.
How the Centre plans to implement 33% reservation
Parliament passed the Nari Shakti Vandan Adhiniyam in 2023, providing for approximately one-third reservation for women in the Lok Sabha and state legislative assemblies.
But the legislation linked the implementation of the quota to a delimitation exercise following the first Census conducted after the law came into force.
The reservation is designed to operate through constituencies. This means constituencies must first be identified and their boundaries determined before seats can be earmarked for women. The law also provides for the rotation of reserved constituencies after each subsequent delimitation exercise.
The Centre’s proposed constitutional changes seek to advance the implementation of women’s reservation before the 2029 general elections.
The government’s argument is that expanding the Lok Sabha would create additional constituencies, allowing seats to be reserved for women without reducing the existing number of constituencies available to other representatives.
Under the government’s earlier April proposal, the delimitation exercise would use the latest available Census figures at the time the commission was constituted.
Since the new Census was still under way, this would effectively mean using the 2011 Census figures. The government had argued that this approach would enable women’s reservation to be implemented in time for the 2029 Lok Sabha elections.
The government’s earlier proposal envisaged 272 seats reserved for women in a Lok Sabha with 815 members.
With input from agencies

title: Inside Kejriwal’s ‘Sheesh Mahal’: Rs 11.56 lakh chandelier, Rs 2 cr bed, and more
description: Delhi’s former chief minister Arvind Kejriwal’s official residence, dubbed ‘Sheesh Mahal’ by the BJP, has been opened to the media, offering a glimpse of its lavish interiors. From a Rs 11.56 lakh chandelier and Rs 6.79 lakh centre table to a Rs 41 lakh baithak and a nearly Rs 2 crore bed, price tags were displayed across the bungalow. The Delhi government plans to open it to the public through a ticketing system
author: FP Explainers
content:
Inside Kejriwal’s ‘Sheesh Mahal’: Rs 11.56 lakh chandelier, Rs 2 cr bed, and more
Delhi’s former chief minister Arvind Kejriwal’s official residence, dubbed ‘Sheesh Mahal’ by the BJP, has been opened to the media, offering a glimpse of its lavish interiors. From a Rs 11.56 lakh chandelier and Rs 6.79 lakh centre table to a Rs 41 lakh baithak and a nearly Rs 2 crore bed, price tags were displayed across the bungalow. The Delhi government plans to open it to the public through a ticketing system
The Delhi government on November 27 opened former chief minister Arvind Kejriwal’s official residence, popularly known as ‘Sheesh Mahal’, to the media, offering a glimpse of its expensive interiors, furnishings and amenities.
The BJP-led government has alleged that public money was spent lavishly on renovating the bungalow, which served as Kejriwal’s residence during his tenure as chief minister.
Located at 6, Flagstaff Road in north Delhi, the bungalow was opened for a media tour on Friday. The government plans to allow public visits through a ticketing system, with the entry fee expected to be around Rs 20. Senior citizens and college students may be allowed to enter free of charge, according to Moneycontrol.
The property, maintained by the Public Works Department (PWD), was displayed with price tags on several household items.
These included a chandelier worth Rs 11.56 lakh, a two-seater sofa priced at Rs 5.47 lakh, a TV unit costing Rs 30 lakh and a double bed valued at nearly Rs 2 crore, according to videos shared by news agencies.
Other items on display included a mandir worth Rs 6.71 lakh, curtains costing Rs 5.69 lakh, chairs priced at Rs 5.58 lakh and a central table valued at Rs 6.79 lakh.
The New Indian Express also reported other expensive sections of the bungalow. These included a baithak costing Rs 41.16 lakh, a powder room valued at Rs 5.80 lakh, a lobby area worth Rs 7.58 lakh and a kitchen dumbwaiter priced at Rs 7 lakh.
What does Kejriwal’s former residence look like?
The bungalow has eight bedrooms and 12 toilets, along with a jacuzzi bath, a spa, expensive carpets and five OLED televisions. It also reportedly has automated doors and windows, more than 50 air conditioners and a kitchen set-up worth Rs 95 lakh.
During the media tour, Delhi minister Parvesh Verma, who heads the PWD, defended the decision to open the property. According to NDTV, he said the government wanted people to see how public money had been spent.
"...The purpose of opening Sheesh Mahal today is to show the public where their money has been spent. Public awareness of how taxpayers' money is used is important. The person who once claimed that he would not take a car or bungalow and wanted the government to find him a small two-room house had an initial project budget of ₹8 crore, which eventually exceeded ₹58 crore...", he said, according to Moneycontrol.
What did the BJP ministers allege?
Delhi minister Kapil Mishra also accused the former AAP government of spending public money on the residence while the city was battling the Covid-19 pandemic.
Speaking to ANI during the media tour, Mishra alleged that the renovation and furnishings reflected corruption and misuse of taxpayers' money.
"It has been opened to the media today, and through your cameras, the entire nation will witness the sordid game of corruption and plunder that Kejriwal played—at a time when Delhi was gasping for oxygen during the COVID-19 pandemic. The very man who once claimed he would live in a single-room house has engaged in massive corruption using public funds," Mishra said.
He also alleged that several materials and furnishings had been sourced from abroad. Mishra cited marble imported from Vietnam, along with crockery and tables procured from other countries.
The bungalow also contains a room that Verma described as the place where Kejriwal used to conduct Facebook Live sessions to project a simple lifestyle.
The minister showed a wooden chair with a torn seat in the room. "In this room, everything was very simple," he said.
"He (Kejriwal) used to do Facebook Live from here to show the public how he lived a simple life," Verma alleged.
What does the CAG report say about the renovation?
The controversy surrounding the bungalow's renovation had also featured in a report by the Comptroller and Auditor General (CAG), which was tabled in the Delhi Assembly.
According to NDTV, the CAG found that renovation work at Kejriwal's then official residence was completed at Rs 33.66 crore, around 342 per cent above the estimated cost.
Of this amount, Rs 18.88 crore was spent on what the report described as "superior specifications, artistic, antique and ornamental" items.
The report also pointed to alleged irregularities in the provision of additional accommodation at the bungalow, as well as additions and alterations to the camp office and staff block by the PWD.
What has AAP said about opening Sheesh Mahal?
The Aam Aadmi Party has criticised the Delhi government's decision to open the bungalow for public viewing, calling it an attempt to divert attention from the pollution of the Yamuna.
AAP Delhi unit president Saurabh Bharadwaj questioned the government over the condition of the river and the deaths of thousands of fish.
"He can talk about anything else he wants, but Verma cannot escape questions about the Yamuna. We will not allow him to divert attention from this issue. We will keep bringing him back to the condition of the river and demanding answers," Bharadwaj said, according to NDTV.
He also asked the minister to explain "why thousands of fish died". "He cannot simply run away from these questions," Bharadwaj said.
When will the public be allowed inside?
The Delhi government first plans to organise media visits before opening the premises to the public through a ticketing system. Public Works Department minister Parvesh Verma announced the media tour on November 26, saying that the public would subsequently be able to book visits.
"The doors of Sheesh Mahal will open from tomorrow. We will show it to the media," Verma said in a post on X on November 26.
He also said the decision to allow public visits was being taken in response to public demand.
The government is expected to introduce an online booking system, with officials indicating that tickets could cost around Rs 20. Senior citizens and college students may be exempt from the fee.
However, public viewing could be temporary. A senior government official told The Times of India that the government was considering handing the property over to a private hospitality company after the viewing period.
"The public viewing will be for a limited period of time. After that, the plan to hand it over to a private hospitality company is in the works. It will be finalised soon," the official said.
The company could manage the property for official conferences, lunches and meetings.
Kejriwal lived at the Flagstaff Road bungalow with his family from 2015 until October 2024, when he vacated it after stepping down as chief minister. The BJP coined the term 'Sheesh Mahal' during its campaign for the February 2025 Delhi Assembly elections, accusing the former chief minister of spending excessively on the renovation.

title: Collegium favours a 'particular section' over merit, diversity: Ex-CJI
description: Former CJI BR Gavai has questioned the Collegium's approach to judicial appointments and transfers, alleging that merit and diversity have taken a back seat in the selection of judges to higher courts
author: Akshita Singh
content:
Collegium favours a 'particular section' over merit, diversity: Ex-CJI
Former CJI BR Gavai has questioned the Collegium's approach to judicial appointments and transfers, alleging that merit and diversity have taken a back seat in the selection of judges to higher courts
Listen to This Article
Former Chief Justice of India BR Gavai on Friday wrote to President Droupadi Murmu seeking her intervention in judicial appointments and transfers. He alleged that recent Collegium recommendations favour candidates from "one particular section of the society", at the expense of merit, diversity and inclusivity.
In a three-page letter, Gavai alleged that candidates from one section of society were being favoured for elevation to the higher judiciary, while Scheduled Castes (SCs), Scheduled Tribes (STs), Other Backward Classes (OBCs), minorities, women and other communities were being excluded.
"I am constrained to voice my dissent and disappointment," Gavai wrote, alleging that recent appointments and transfers were being made in disregard of diversity, inclusion and merit.
The letter was addressed to President Murmu and marked to Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Union Law Minister Arjun Ram Meghwal.
Gavai questions representation in higher judiciary
Gavai said a community accounting for less than 5 per cent of India's population had secured more than 40 per cent representation in the Supreme Court in the recent past.
Also Read
He also referred to data presented by Union Law Minister Arjun Ram Meghwal in the Rajya Sabha in March 2025.
According to the data, of the 715 high court judges appointed since 2018, 22 belonged to the Scheduled Castes (SCs), 16 to the Scheduled Tribes (STs), 89 to the Other Backward Classes (OBCs) and 37 to minority communities. Together, these four categories accounted for 164 appointments, or around 23 per cent of the total.
Gavai said the representation of different sections of society had been considered during his tenure in the Collegium.
In the letter, he wrote: "When I was a part of the collegium and was Chief Justice of India, I always followed the principles of diversity and inclusion."
He added that adequate representation was ensured for SCs, STs, OBCs, minorities and women while considering candidates for elevation to the high courts and the Supreme Court.
However, he alleged that recent recommendations ignored these principles. "In the recent past disturbing events have unfolded, showing complete disregard for the principles of merit and inclusivity," he wrote.
Gavai questions recent transfers and appointments
The former CJI also raised concerns over the transfer of high court judges and subsequent recommendations for their elevation.
He referred to an instance in which a chief justice was transferred from one high court to a smaller high court and was subsequently recommended for appointment as the chief justice of a prominent high court.
Gavai alleged that another meritorious and hardworking chief justice was transferred to a smaller high court to accommodate the appointment.
He said he had been part of the Collegium that recommended the first chief justice's transfer and later headed the Collegium when the subsequent transfer recommendation was made.
"I am aware of the factors that prevailed at the relevant time with the collegium for recommending such an appointment/transfer. However, on account of propriety and judicial disciple I refrain from divulging these reasons," he wrote.
Citing another instance, Gavai alleged that a judge who had been transferred from his parent high court to another high court on punitive considerations was subsequently appointed chief justice of a large and prominent high court.
"In another instance, a judge was transferred from his parent high court to another high court on punitive consideration and was subsequently rewarded by appointment as chief justice of a large and a prominent high court," the letter read.
Gavai urges President to intervene
Gavai also questioned whether the Collegium's primacy in judicial appointments could place it beyond accountability.
Referring to Article 124(2) of the Constitution, which provides for the appointment of Supreme Court judges by the President, he argued that the President's constitutional responsibilities remained relevant to the process.
He said the Collegium's recommendations being treated as decisive under judicial convention did not make the body unaccountable or absolve the President of her constitutional duties.
Gavai also said the executive and Parliament were stakeholders in judicial appointments and transfers. He referred to instances in which the government and legislature had requested the Collegium and high courts to consider suitable candidates from marginalised communities to improve representation.
He urged President Murmu to intervene, as she deemed appropriate, and remind all stakeholders of their constitutional responsibilities towards ensuring equal representation in the higher judiciary.

title: Karthigai Deepam row: SC issues contempt notice to Tamil Nadu officials
description: "The wilful non-compliance of orders of the Court, especially by the executive authorities, cannot go unnoticed and it has to be dealt with an iron hand," the bench said
author: Press Trust of India
content:
Karthigai Deepam row: SC issues contempt notice to Tamil Nadu officials
"The wilful non-compliance of orders of the Court, especially by the executive authorities, cannot go unnoticed and it has to be dealt with an iron hand," the bench said
Listen to This Article
Observing that the executive authorities in Tamil Nadu acted on the diktat of their political bosses, the Supreme Court on Friday issued a contempt notice to the Tamil Nadu chief secretary, DGP, Madurai collector and others over the violation of its November 20 Karthigai Deepam order.
The top court suspended the board of trustees of Arulmigu Subramaniaswamy temple and ordered lighting of lamp at Thiruparankundram Deepathoon on Saturday using the flame lit at Uchaipillaiyar mandapam.
Asking the Tamil Nadu chief secretary to appear personally, a bench of Justices Aravind Kumar and Vipul M Pancholi directed him to file an affidavit detailing emails, calls exchanged and messages exchanged between officials.
"The wilful non-compliance of orders of the Court, especially by the executive authorities, cannot go unnoticed and it has to be dealt with an iron hand," the bench said.
The top court also handed over the security of Tamil Nadu's Arulmigu Subramaniaswamy temple and Thiruparankundram hill to CRPF, citing the failure of the Tamil Nadu Police to implement its orders.
Also Read
The apex court said it cannot sit in a silo if its order is not complied with and added that its order is not an invitation to negotiate as it binds the State, its officers and every religious institution.
It said any attempt to pollute stream of justice by any person, howsoever high he may be, will not be tolerated.
The top court said the conduct of officers prima facie reveals a state of administrative chaos in Tamil Nadu.
"The conduct alleged, as borne out by the record, would prima facie disclose a brazen and wilful disobedience of this Court's order, a flagrant disregard of the undertaking given before the High Court and a calculated affront to the authority of both constitutional courts," the bench said.
On Wednesday, the Tamil Nadu government apologised to the top court over the non-lighting of the ceremonial lamp at Deepathoon and blamed the Arulmigu Subramaniaswamy temple authorities for it.
Despite the apex court's permission, the Karthigai Deepam was lit only at its customary Uchipillayar mandapam at Thirupparankundram on November 24 and not at Deepathoon.

title: SC refuses urgent listing of plea against Ranbir Kapoor-starrer Ramayana
description: The petition alleges that the makers distorted mythological facts in their depiction of the epic
author: Press Trust of India
content:
SC refuses urgent listing of plea against Ranbir Kapoor-starrer Ramayana
The petition alleges that the makers distorted mythological facts in their depiction of the epic
Listen to This Article
The Supreme Court on Friday declined to list for urgent hearing a petition challenging the release of the Ranbir Kapoor-starrer Ramayana: Rise of a Legend, saying anyone with a different view of the epic is free to make a film of their own.
A bench of Chief Justice Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana observed that the film is already running in theatres and that those who wanted to watch it have already done so.
The petitioner's counsel told the court that the plea had been registered on November 23 and was yet to be listed for hearing.
"The movie has already been released. Those who wanted to watch it have already seen it," the CJI said. When the counsel argued that "many facts have been distorted" in the film, Justice Bagchi said, "They made a movie as they understand, you make a movie as you understand. Don't waste the time of the court. If you have a counter view about the epic, make a movie based on that." As the lawyer pressed for an early hearing, the bench said the matter would be listed in due course.
The petition alleges that the makers distorted mythological facts in their depiction of the epic.
Also Read
Ramayana: Rise of a Legend, also referred to as Ramayana: Part 1, is directed by Nitesh Tiwari and produced by Namit Malhotra.
It brings the epic to the big screen with Ranbir Kapoor as Lord Rama, Sai Pallavi as Sita, and Yash as Ravana.
The ensemble cast includes Sunny Deol, Ravie Dubey, Lara Dutta, Arun Govil, Kajal Aggarwal, Rakul Preet Singh and Vivek Oberoi. The film was released in theatres on November 5, 2026.

title: Delimitation row: Centre approves bill for 50% more Lok Sabha seats for every state, freeze on representation till 2051
description: The Union Cabinet has approved a bill proposing a roughly 50 per cent increase in Lok Sabha seats for all states, using the 2011 Census and freezing seat numbers until 2051.
author: Sayak Basu
content:
The Union Cabinet on Friday has cleared a new women's reservation bill linked to delimitation which proposes a 50 per cent increase in Lok Sabha seats in all states.
This bill is likely to be brought before the special sitting of the Parliament which is set to begin next week.
The Union Cabinet gave its nod to the new bill with amendments in order to ensure no state loses its share of representation in the Lok Sabha in proportion to others after the delimitation exercise is carried out, PTI reported citing sources.
Quick answers to key questions
It proposes increasing Lok Sabha strength from 543 seats to a maximum of 850 through delimitation. The Cabinet-approved proposal also says every state would receive a similar increase in seats.
The proposal is reported to use the 2011 Census to redraw the increased number of seats.
The proposed freeze is intended to keep state representation from changing again until 2051. The government says the uniform increase is meant to address concerns about states losing their relative share of Lok Sabha seats.
Southern states have recorded slower population growth than several northern states, raising concern that population-based delimitation could reduce their relative representation. The proposed uniform increase is intended to address those concerns.
The government says increasing the number of seats would help implement the 33% women's reservation in Parliament and state assemblies ahead of the 2029 Lok Sabha election.
The bill also proposes a freeze on the number of seats till 2051, with the sources telling PTI that the uniform 51 per cent increase has been mandated in order to address the concerns southern states have expressed earlier.
The new bill is reportedly using the 2011 Census in order to redraw the increased seats.
If this proposed amendment passes, India will see an increase in the number of Lok Sabha seats from 543 to a maximum of 850 through delimitation.
The government's opinion is that this move will allow for the implementation of the 33 per cent quota for women in the Parliament as well as state assemblies ahead of the 2029 Lok Sabha elections.
The government has called for a four-day special sitting -- November 30 and December 1 in Lok Sabha, and December 2 and 3 in Rajya Sabha.
"When the government calls a session or a special session, that means there are very important bills or business for the nation," Parliamentary Affairs Minister Kiren Rijiju said, as per PTI.
The opposition INDIA bloc is against the legislation and will be meeting on Saturday to discuss its strategy.
Non-INDIA bloc parties like the DMK, AAP, and the BJD have also been invited for the meeting, PTI reported citing sources.
Speaking with reporters, Congress general secretary in-charge organisation K C Venugopal said, "PM (Narendra) Modi and (Home Minister) Amit Shah want to set a big trap against the people of India. That is the design of this entire episode."
Notably, Supriya Sule of the NCP(SP) has said that she will not be attending the meeting since her father, party patriarch Sharad Pawar, is unwell. This comes amid buzz that the NCP(SP) might decide to side with the BJP on the delimitation issue.
MK Stalin has warned that under no circumstances should the 7.18 per cent seat share of Tamil Nadu in the Lok Sabha should be reduced.
"No change in position, no compromise, the DMK will never compromise on Tamil Nadu's interests; nor will it depart from its principles," Stalin said in a statement.
Jharkhand Mukti Morcha (JMM) Rajya Sabha MP Mahua Majhi questioned how the government could proceed with the bill without any update data, accusing the ruling party of renewed attempts of political poaching.
"If they don’t even have the necessary data, how can they carry out a delimitation exercise? This suggests that the politics of poaching has begun once again. We have several apprehensions regarding this: a session was called for just a single day,” Majhi told ANI.
Shiv Sena (UBT) MP Sanjay Raut slammed the proposed bill on Friday, calling it “anti-national and anti-democratic”
“Realising they are set to lose in 2029, they have devised a new ploy: they intend to bring in 860 MPs and carry out a delimitation exercise. This bill is anti-national and anti-democratic; it must be opposed. Those who vote in favour of this bill will be traitors to the nation. Their names will be recorded in history as traitors,” Raut was quoted as saying by ANI.

title: West Bengal consumer commission directs momo outlet to pay  ₹50,000 for charging  ₹10 extra for packaging
description: The customer bought two plates of chicken momos, each priced at  ₹109, from the outlet on October 29, 2024. The customer was charged an additional  ₹10 on the bill.
author: Kanishka Singharia
content:
The District Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission, West Bengal, held a Kolkata food outlet liable for deficiency in service and unfair trade practices for charging ₹10 extra for packaging, according to a report by The Indian Express. The bench comprising President Manoj Kumar Rai and member Gopal Chandra Roy directed the food outlet to pay ₹50,000. “OP no. 1 has failed to prove that the complainant requested him to provide packaging and agreed to provide cost for the same. So, deficiency in service on the part of OP no 1 is proved,” the order read. The customer had bought two plates of chicken momos, each priced at ₹109, from the outlet on October 29, 2024. The customer was charged an additional Rs. 10 on the bill, leading to an altercation between the two. The customer demanded that the extra amount be refunded; however, the outlet outright refused. Triggered by the incident, the consumer moved the consumer court, seeking a refund and compensation. The food outlet rejected the allegations, claiming that the customer had requested extra packaging to ensure the food remained safe and hygienic and did not spill while he travelled on a motorcycle. It further maintained that the packaging fee had been disclosed to the customer before the order was placed and that he had agreed to pay it. However, the commission found that the outlet had not submitted any evidence showing that the customer had asked for the momos to be packed separately. Referring to Section 36(5) of the Sale of Goods Act, 1930, the commission said that the seller is responsible for bearing the expenses involved in making goods ready for delivery, unless there is a different agreement between the parties. “Section 36 (5) of the Sale of Goods’ Act, 1930 provides that unless otherwise agreed, the expenses of and incidental to putting the goods into a deliverable state shall be borne by the seller. Therefore, in view of the aforesaid provision, it is duty of the OP No. 1 as seller, to provide packaging of the goods sold by them for taking it away and the OP No. 1 shall have to bear the cost of such packaging,” the order read, according to The Indian Express report. The commission also pointed out that the food outlet had failed to establish that the customer had been informed about the additional ₹10 packaging fee before placing the order. Concluding that the outlet was guilty of deficiency in service, the commission directed it to return the ₹10 packaging charge to the customer. It also ordered the company to pay ₹100 as compensation and ₹2,000 towards litigation expenses. In addition, the food outlet has been directed to deposit ₹50,000 into the Consumer Legal Aid Account of the Commission. title: Voter data at risk? Election Commission website flaw—now fixed—left personal details and IDs exposed, probe finds
description: The Election Commission of India has fixed a website security flaw that exposed voters' personal details, including phone numbers, addresses, and file paths to identity documents.
author: Pragya Singha Roy
content:
The Election Commission of India (ECI) has fixed a security vulnerability in its website that exposed sensitive personal information and identity documents of registered voters. The flaw was discovered by Reuters during a month-long investigation and reported to the poll body on October 26, 2026. The weakness meant that information such as voters' names, phone numbers, email addresses, date of birth, residential addresses and file paths to uploaded voter identification documents could be accessed via the developer tool of a browser.
The security gap was fixed on Thursday, November 26, after Reuters repeatedly sought a response from the Election Commission. This development comes one month before assembly polls in pivotal states such as Uttar Pradesh, and at a time when the ECI is facing intense questioning on its voter list verification drive. The vulnerability could've been used to harvest voters' personal data in large numbers, security researchers said.
The flaw was connected to the website's call-booking system, which was unveiled in June 2025, according to Reuters. Voters logged in to their accounts and asked for a call from their electorate officer; the browser network tab on the website showed a reference number from their voter registration or information update form.
Using these reference numbers to book calls, Reuters found that the website exposed additional personal details that were not displayed on the main webpage. These comprised personal details, home addresses and file paths to voter-registered ID documents.
The security flaw has been verified by Indian security researchers Karan Saini and Ehraz Ahmed, who studied the report. They said the reference numbers were in a predictable sequence that could enable an attack to guess the numbers and automate the process of gathering sensitive information.
The researchers said cybercriminals could have used publicly available web tools and basic coding knowledge to download identity documents, including passports and national identity cards.
Reuters said that one of its reporters was able to follow the steps to download a copy of his national identity document. It seems the server was trying to check if someone was logged in but failed to verify whether they were allowed to access a certain document, Saini said.
However, Reuters said it could not establish whether anyone had exploited the vulnerability, how long it had existed or how many voters may have been affected.
Reuters first contacted the Election Commission and its three commissioners on October 26, seeking comments on the findings. The institution did not respond to repeated requests.
On Thursday, November 26, an ECI spokesperson told Reuters that the commission's IT division had been asked to examine the issue. Hours later, a review by Reuters and the researchers confirmed that the vulnerability had been addressed. The same approach was no longer available to access sensitive information or document file paths.
Congress spokesman Pawan Khera said the revelations were "deeply alarming" and warned that such exposure could allow for voter information to be targeted for intimidation, profiling and voter suppression.
Former election commissioner Ashok Lavasa told Reuters that the exposure was accidental. The ECI's website privacy statement also notes that no system is 100% secure.
The incident follows a similar security concern reported in 2019, when researcher Karan Saini found that the commission's online voter search portal was exposing personal information through the browser's network tab.

title: Gurugram to prepare 'Annual Action Plan 2027' to tackle air pollution
description: The proposed plan will prioritise end-to-end paving of roads, footpaths and other public spaces, along with increasing greenery and planting grass in suitable areas. Measures to control dust, including the deployment of mechanical road sweepers and anti-smog guns, will be regularly monitored, an official said following a meeting at the Municipal Corporation office.
author: ET Online
content:
The proposed plan will prioritise end-to-end paving of roads, footpaths and other public spaces, along with increasing greenery and planting grass in suitable areas. Measures to control dust, including the deployment of mechanical road sweepers and anti-smog guns, will be regularly monitored, an official said following a meeting at the Municipal Corporation office.
The commissioner also directed officials to step up night patrolling, prevent waste burning and crack down on the illegal dumping of construction and demolition (C&D) waste. Instructions were also issued to set up C&D waste collection centres in Pataudi, Farrukhnagar and Sohna.
According to an official statement, Pankaj stressed that roads, footpaths, central verges and green belts should have no exposed soil patches. He called for comprehensive paving, along with the development of green spaces and grass cover wherever feasible.
All concerned departments have also been directed to ensure that roads under their jurisdiction are constructed and maintained in accordance with the guidelines of the Commission for Air Quality Management (CAQM).
The commissioner has set specific targets for various departments and asked them to complete the assigned tasks within the stipulated timelines.
Other measures outlined in the action plan include installing air quality monitoring stations, expanding parking facilities, setting up electric vehicle (EV) charging and battery-swapping stations, easing road congestion and introducing smart traffic signals.
Pankaj also directed officials to review the progress of these initiatives regularly and ensure timely implementation. The measures are aimed at reducing traffic congestion and vehicular emissions while improving urban infrastructure and civic amenities for residents.

title: Attacks on maritime shipping and seafarers 'simply unacceptable': S Jaishankar
description: S Jaishankar highlighted the importance of joint efforts among Indian Ocean states for enhancing maritime security and trade. He condemned recent attacks on maritime shipping, labeling them as unacceptable and requiring global action. Addressing the IORA ministerial conclave, he advocated for robust cooperation with dialogue partners to tackle regional challenges. Jaishankar also emphasized Indias vision for enhancing collective voice and engaging meaningfully with member states.
author: PTI
content:
New Delhi: The Indian Ocean is central to global trade, energy security and connectivity and all littoral states in the region must jointly work towards its safety, External Affairs Minister S Jaishankar said on Friday as he described increasing attacks on maritime shipping and seafarers as "simply unacceptable".
In an address at a ministerial conclave of the Indian Ocean Rim Association (IORA), Jaishankar also called for respecting maritime laws, especially UNCLOS (the UN Convention on the Law of the Sea) -- remarks that came amid growing contestation in the global maritime sphere, including China's military muscle-flexing in the South China Sea.
India hosted the conclave in New Delhi in its capacity as the current chair of the IORA that comprises 23 nations including Australia, Indonesia, South Africa, Kenya, Tanzania, Mozambique, Somalia, Oman, Yemen, Bangladesh, Malaysia and Thailand. The US, the European Union and several other dialogue partners of the IORA also joined the gathering.
Also read: Special Parliament session: Congress issues whip, asks MPs to be present for House proceedings
In his remarks, Jaishankar delved into what he called the "volatile aspects of a transforming global order" and highlighted the adverse impacts of conflicts, frictions and disruptions.
"The Indian Ocean is particularly poised to address its challenges. Recognising the criticality of maritime trade to global growth, we must deliver on its safety and security. International Law, particularly UNCLOS, must be respected," he said.
The external affairs minister said attacks on maritime shipping and seafarers are "simply unacceptable" and that they call for a global response.
Jaishankar's comments came against the backdrop of mounting global concerns over attacks on merchant shipping in West Asia as well as in the Black Sea in which several Indian sailors were killed.
"Whether it is to counter terrorism, narcotics trade or illegal, unreported, and unregulated fishing, or indeed response to climate events and disaster situations, we have to become more self-reliant as well as more enthusiastic about cooperating with partners," he said.
Jaishankar said the Indian Ocean is central to global trade, energy security and connectivity and all littoral states in the region must jointly work towards "meaningful collaboration" in ensuring a better future for its people.
The grouping must enhance its collective voice and reinforce its role as a regional platform at a time of significant "geopolitical changes", he said.
"The Indian Ocean is central to global trade, energy security, connectivity and economic prosperity. It is also a region of immense diversity, opportunity and shared challenges," Jaishankar said in his opening remarks at the meeting.
He said India's approach to IORA and India's chairship of the bloc is guided by vision MAHASAGAR.
Prime Minister Narendra Modi announced the vision MAHASAGAR or "Mutual and Holistic Advancement for Security and Growth Across Regions" for India's engagement with the Global South during his visit to Mauritius in March last year.
Jaishankar said India's theme for the IORA -- Innovation, Openness, Resilience and Adaptability in the Indian Ocean Region -- reflects its conviction that the grouping must remain responsive and adaptive to the changing regional and global environment, while delivering tangible benefits to its member states.
"At a time of significant geopolitical changes, IORA must enhance its collective voice and reinforce its role as a regional platform," he said.
"Achieving these requires greater coordination among member states, meaningful collaboration with dialogue partners and a stronger focus on practical cooperation," he said.
Jaishankar said India is working to strengthen cooperation across IORA's priority areas and cross-cutting issues such as deepening engagement with the grouping's dialogue partners and promoting practical regional initiatives.
"A stronger institutional foundation is essential for IORA to fulfil its larger role in the region. In this context, the theme of today's meeting, 'A Stronger Regional Voice: Positioning IORA in a Changing Global Order' is particularly relevant," Jaishankar said.
The IORA has been focusing on boosting the blue economy through a common vision for balanced economic development in the Indian Ocean region besides working on maritime security.
The IORA's foundation charter sets the guiding principles for it to facilitate economic cooperation, in a spirit of multilateralism, and expand understanding and mutually beneficial cooperation through a consensus-based, evolutionary and non-intrusive approach.
US Ambassador Sergio Gor also spoke at the conclave.
"I reaffirmed America's commitment to freedom of navigation and cooperation on maritime security, energy, infrastructure, and critical minerals. Open sea lanes are essential to global trade and prosperity," he said on social media.
