title: 'Privileged strategic partnership': Russian FM Lavrov hails ties with India
description: Russian Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov has described India's ties with Moscow as a \"privileged strategic partnership\", highlighting the country's
author: Trisha Mahajan
content:
Europe preparing for war with Russia, demanding truce in Ukraine: Russian FM Lavrov says US displaying more "political maturity"
Russian Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov has described India's ties with Moscow as a "privileged strategic partnership", highlighting the country's importance alongside China and Iran as Russia looks to strengthen its international partnerships amid a shift towards a multipolar world order.Speaking at a meeting with participants of the Alexander Gorchakov Public Diplomacy Fund's Dialogue for the Future programme in Moscow on Thursday, Lavrov said Russia continued to have strong partners despite deteriorating relations with Western countries."Our relations with India are officially described as a privileged strategic partnership. We also enjoy an especially advanced strategic partnership with the Islamic Republic of Iran, formalised in a treaty signed a year and a half ago," he said, as quoted by ANI.Referring to ties with Beijing, Lavrov said the Russia-China partnership had demonstrated its effectiveness at the recently concluded Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) summit in Shenzhen, including through the first-ever trilateral summit involving Russia, China and the United States.He also pointed to Russia's wider network of partnerships through groupings such as BRICS, the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO), the Eurasian Economic Union (EAEU), the Commonwealth of Independent States (CIS) and the Collective Security Treaty Organisation (CSTO).
"We have no shortage of partners with whom to work," Lavrov said, describing BRICS as a "broad-based association of truly global reach".His remarks come amid continued diplomatic engagement between India and Russia over bilateral ties as well as the Ukraine conflict. Earlier this month, External Affairs Minister S Jaishankar said India had held discussions with Russia, Ukraine and European countries on three key issues arising from the war: protecting civilian shipping and seafarers, restoring grain exports through the Black Sea and preventing attacks on energy infrastructure.Speaking on the sidelines of the G20 foreign ministers' meeting in Atlanta, Jaishankar said India was attempting to bring the concerned parties together to find common ground on these issues.He stressed that civilian vessels and seafarers should not be targeted and called for restoring grain shipments from both Russia and Ukraine, warning that exports through the Black Sea had declined sharply.On energy infrastructure, Jaishankar said reaching an understanding would be particularly complicated because countries had different interpretations of what needed protection, ranging from refineries and electricity grids to ships carrying fuel.Meanwhile, Lavrov also talked about Moscow's strategic relationship with Tehran. Russia and Iran signed a Comprehensive Strategic Partnership Treaty in January 2025, covering cooperation in areas including trade, energy, science, technology and defence. The agreement entered into force in October that year.Making a broader assessment of global power dynamics, Lavrov said the traditional Western-dominated world order was giving way to new centres of economic and political influence."It is obvious to everyone that the issue concerns the tectonic shifts that are underway on the international stage, where the old world order, which was maintained for 500 years, first by Europeans and subsequently by the 'collective West,' is being replaced with new growth centres," he said.
Describing multipolarity as an inevitable historical process, Lavrov argued that countries attempting to delay the transition would eventually have to engage with emerging centres of influence."Those who are trying to slow down this process can possibly hinder the rise of the new multipolar world order, but this will eventually take place anyway, and they will have to find common ground," he said.Taking aim at Western countries, he added that the United States, Europe and their allies could no longer dictate how other nations should conduct their international relations or decide whom they should cooperate with.Lavrov said Russia would continue to work through multilateral platforms, including the United Nations and the Organisation for Security and Cooperation in Europe (OSCE), while implementing decisions reached collectively.
Trisha Mahajan is a journalist with The Times of India digital, with keen interest in covering business and corporate affairs. She also reports on key national and world developments and global news trends. A keen reader with a strong interest in storytelling that adds context, clarity, and depth to complex issues.

title: Maximum assembly seats capped at 650, rotaional reserved seats for women: What's in new delimitation bill
description: NEW DELHI: The Centre has proposed increasing the number of Lok Sabha seats by 50% for every state and Union territory, along with a similar increase in
author: Rohitashwa Ranjan
content:
NEW DELHI: The Centre has proposed increasing the number of Lok Sabha seats by 50% for every state and Union territory, along with a similar increase in the strength of their legislative assemblies, to implement one-third reservation for women.This is the Centre's second attempt to push the legislation after its earlier proposal was defeated in the Lok Sabha in April this year.The earlier three Bills were introduced to facilitate the setting up of a Delimitation Commission to readjust the allocation of seats in the Lok Sabha and state and Union territory assemblies, besides redrawing constituency boundaries.
The fresh Bill, set to be introduced in the Lok Sabha on Monday, makes substantial changes to the original legislation, particularly in the constitution of the Delimitation Commission, the use of Census figures, the allocation of seats reserved for women and the expansion of legislative representation."The objective of the present Bill is to give immediate effect to one-third reservation for women, including women belonging to Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes, in the House of the People and the Legislative Assemblies of the states and the Union territories, through a delimitation exercise," the Bill's Statement of Objects and Reasons says.
What is in the new Bill
- The Constitution (132nd Amendment) Bill, 2026, proposes to increase the maximum strength of the Lok Sabha to 850, with up to 815 members from states and 35 from Union territories.
- It also proposes to raise the maximum strength of a state legislative assembly from 500 to 650.
- It further proposes a 50% increase in the number of seats in the Lok Sabha and state and Union territory assemblies over their existing strength before the delimitation exercise.
- The Bill provides that the women's quota will remain in force for 15 years from the commencement of the 2023 amendment, with Parliament empowered to extend it through legislation.
- Parliament will also decide the authority and manner in which seats reserved for women will be rotated.
- Another key change is that the Centre will have to constitute the Delimitation Commission as soon as possible after the proposed legislation comes into force. The original Bill provided for setting up the commission "from time to time".
- The fresh Bill seeks to enable the rollout of the women's quota after the first delimitation exercise under the proposed amendment. The exercise will use the latest Census figures published by the time the law comes into force.
- This means the 2011 Census data will be used if no newer figures are published by then. The Delimitation Commission will use these figures to readjust seat allocations and redraw territorial constituencies.”
Rohitashwa Ranjan is a digital journalist with The Times of India, where he decodes Indian politics as a carefully staged production with scripts, subtext and everything behind. His stories track elections, party dynamics and the things that often are buried beneath the headlines. When not parsing vote shares or alliances, he is usually reading between the lines, where the real story tends to reside.

title: 'Brought disgrace to Tamil Nadu': Stalin targets TVK govt after Supreme Court's Deepam rebuke
description: NEW DELHI: DMK chief MK Stalin on Friday accused the TVK-led Tamil Nadu government of bringing \"disgrace\" to the state by failing to present a strong
author: Karan Manral
content:
NEW DELHI: DMK chief MK Stalin on Friday accused the TVK-led Tamil Nadu government of bringing "disgrace" to the state by failing to present a strong defence before the Supreme Court in the Deepam case.His remarks came hours after the Supreme Court came down heavily on the Tamil Nadu government for defying its order in the case, observing that it was prima facie in contempt of court."The incompetent TVK government has brought unprecedented peril to Tamil Nadu’s history—threatening our traditions, religious harmony, and state rights! The Supreme Court verdict in the Thiruparankundram matter is a blatant defeat for the TVK government!" Stalin wrote in Tamil on X.
Stalin X post
"The Supreme Court has ordered that a lamp be lit tomorrow on a pillar atop the Tirupparankundram hill. The incompetent Vijay administration has brought disgrace to Tamil Nadu by failing to present strong arguments in court," the former chief minister added.Stalin termed the Supreme Court's directives, including handing over security of the Thiruparankundram temple and hill to the CRPF, suspending its board of trustees, appointing two former judges to oversee its management and summoning senior officials, a "shock."He also likened the TVK government's handling of the issue to a monkey mishandling a delicate flower garland and accused it of using the temple's board of trustees as a shield.
"The Dravidian movement—through sixty years of struggle, bloodshed, and the sacrifice of many lives—had secured and safeguarded state rights, which were once in the hands of fraudulent groups—under the control of democratic governance. Now, through a single legal case, all of this has been surrendered to the Union government," Stalin said.
The DMK supremo cited chief minister C Joseph Vijay's lack of political experience, given his background as a Tamil film superstar before entering politics, but maintained that the real problem was his "reluctance" to allow experienced and knowledgeable people to get close to him.Stalin described Vijay's silence on the issue as a "historic betrayal" of Tamil Nadu.The Supreme Court's order followed the authorities' failure to allow the ceremonial lighting of the Karthigai Deepam lamp atop the Deepathoon in Madurai, despite the court's one-time directive issued on November 20. Instead, the lamp was lit at its customary spot at the Deepa Mandapam near the Ucchi Pillayar temple.
Karan Manral is a journalist at the Times of India. He covers politics, social issues, and international affairs, exploring stories that affect people’s everyday lives. He also writes explainers to make these stories easier for readers to follow.

title: Electoral awareness contest winners receive certificates
description: Visakhapatnam students win certificates in electoral awareness essay and quiz contests across three phases, with winners honored by the DRO.
author: The Hindu Bureau
content:
District Revenue Officer (DRO) S.D. Anita distributed certificates to students who won essay-writing and quiz competitions organised as part of the electoral awareness programme in Visakhapatnam.
Presenting the certificates at a programme held at the Collectorate conference hall on Thursday. Ms. Anita congratulated the winners.
The competitions were conducted in three phases from November 2 to 20, in accordance with the directions of the Election Commission of India (ECI), for students of government, aided and private schools and colleges in the Visakhapatnam Assembly constituency.
Essay competitions focused on topics— importance of a clean electoral roll and the significance of the right to vote. The quiz competitions covered electronic voting machines (EVMs), voter verifiable paper audit trail (VVPAT), polling and the counting of votes.
Winners were selected through competitions held initially at the institutional level, followed by constituency and district-level rounds.
District Education Officer Prem Kumar, headmasters, teachers, students, parents and election department staff attended the programme.

title: Sunny Joseph meets Kharge as factional feud continues to convulse Congress in Keralam
description: KPCC chief Sunny Joseph meets Kharge as Kerala Congress factional feuding prompts talks on restructuring and extended KPCC meeting plans.
author: The Hindu Bureau
content:
Kerala Pradesh Congress Committee (KPCC) president Sunny Joseph met All India Congress Committee (AICC) president Mallikarjun Kharge in New Delhi on Friday, even as factional feuding continues to convulse the party in Keralam. Mr. Joseph, who left for New Delhi on Thursday with an “overflowing in-tray of unsettled organisational affairs,” as per a senior Congress leader, signalled that his “relatively brief meeting” with Mr. Kharge has set the ball rolling on organisational restructuring.
“Not all matters about Keralam were on the table. I have sought an appointment with Leader of the Opposition Rahul Gandhi on Saturday,” he told The Hindu.
Mr. Joseph hinted that the AICC would engage the KPCC’s top leadership on a range of Keralam-specific organisational and political matters in the coming days. Another party insider said Mr. Joseph might seek AICC approval for an extended KPCC meeting to discuss organisational issues, including what he termed “dysfunction” plaguing the party due to the lack of a full-time State president.
‘Organisational void’
He surmised that the “organisational void” had spawned the current bout of hyper-partisanship and prevented the party from curtailing it at the outset. “The Congress could ill-afford a gridlocked party apparatus beset by factional feuding. Rapid restructuring from the grassroots level upwards is the sole panacea for the organisational torpor,” he added. The KPCC extended meeting will likely include members of the party’s Political Affairs Committee (PAC), KPCC executive, and District Congress Committee (DCC). “The meeting might also deliberate on forming a high-powered panel to decide political appointments to boards and corporations through consensus, lest arbitrary decisions spark factional schisms,” he added.
Notably, Mr. Joseph’s meeting with Mr. Kharge comes close on the heels of veteran Congress leader K.C. Joseph and Benny Behanan, MP, both influential “A-group” leaders owing allegiance to the late Chief Minister Oommen Chandy, and KPCC working president Shafi Parambil’s meeting with Mr. Kharge last week.
Mr. K.C. Joseph told The Hindu on Friday that the national leadership’s immediate priority seemed to be the winter session of the Parliament. “Mr. Kharge had promised to address KPCC’s concerns once Mr. Gandhi returned from the US. Even though Mr. Gandhi is back, the nomination of the new KPCC president and reorganisation process may have to wait for now,” he said.

title: Three armed men rob jewellery shop of 20 sovereigns in Palakkad
description: Three armed men robbed about 20 sovereigns of gold from Ishan Gold in Palakkad, firing a shot and fleeing as police investigate.
author: PTI
content:
Three men allegedly robbed around 20 sovereigns of gold ornaments from a jewellery shop at Peringottukurissi here on Friday (November 27) after threatening employees with a gun and a knife, the police said.
The incident took place at ‘Ishan Gold’ jewellery, where the accused arrived in a vehicle pretending to be customers interested in purchasing ornaments, the police said.
While a salesperson was attending to them, the men aroused suspicion, prompting the employee to call the manager.
When the manager arrived, one of the accused took out a pistol while another threatened the staff with a knife, the police said.
The gang allegedly grabbed gold rings kept on the display shelves and attempted to flee. However, employees resisted the robbery and raised an alarm, the police said.
The shop owner said the assailants fired one shot during the robbery.
Preliminary estimates put the quantity of gold stolen at around 20 sovereigns, the police said.
Police suspect that the accused are youths from outside the State.
The Kottayi police have registered a case and launched an investigation.
The police teams are pursuing the suspects and taking steps to prevent them from escaping from the State, as the jewellery is located close to the Keralam-Tamil Nadu border.
CCTV footage of the incident has been circulated among police stations to help identify and trace the accused, the police said.
Published - November 27, 2026 08:45 pm IST

title: 50% seat hike, women's quota after delimitation: What the new Bill proposes
description: The Bill proposes a 50 per cent increase in Lok Sabha and Assembly seats redrawing constituencies using the latest available census figures and implementing one-third women039s reservation through delimitation with the revised seat allocation remaining in place until 2051
author: India Today News Desk
content:
50% seat hike, women's quota after delimitation: What the new Bill proposes
The Bill proposes a 50 per cent increase in Lok Sabha and Assembly seats, redrawing constituencies using the latest available census figures, and implementing one-third women's reservation through delimitation, with the revised seat allocation remaining in place until 2051.
The Centre has proposed a major overhaul of electoral representation, increasing Lok Sabha and state Assembly seats by 50 per cent across states and Union territories to facilitate the implementation of one-third reservation for women. The proposed delimitation exercise would also redraw constituency boundaries, with the revised seat allocations and boundaries remaining in place until 2051.
The Constitution (132nd Amendment) Bill, 2026, popularly referred to as Delimitation Bill, slated for introduction in the Lok Sabha on Monday, seeks to raise the maximum strength of the Lower House to 850, comprising up to 815 members from states and 35 from Union territories. It also proposes to increase the maximum strength of state Assemblies from 500 to 650, according to the details of the Bill accessed by India Today.
"The objective of the present Bill is to give immediate effect to one-third reservation for women, including women belonging to Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes, in the House of the People and the Legislative Assemblies of the states and the Union territories, through a delimitation exercise," the Bill's Statement of Objects and Reasons says.
The Bill stipulates that the delimitation exercise "shall provide for an increase of 50 per cent in the number of seats in the House of the People and the Legislative Assemblies of the states and Union territories, over and above the number of seats existing immediately before such delimitation".
WHY CENTRE PROPOSING 50% INCREASE IN SEATS?
The primary objective of the proposed constitutional amendment is to facilitate the implementation of one-third reservation for women in the Lok Sabha and state and Union territory Assemblies through a delimitation exercise. It proposes a 50 per cent increase in the number of Lok Sabha seats allocated to every state and Union territory, with the strength of their respective legislative Assemblies also rising by the same proportion.
The Bill explicitly provides that the delimitation exercise "shall provide for an increase of fifty per cent in the number of seats in the House of the People and the Legislative Assemblies of the States and Union territories, over and above the number of seats existing immediately before such delimitation".
It further links the implementation of women's reservation to "the constitutional scheme of readjustment in the allocation of seats in the House of the People and the Legislative Assemblies and re-drawing boundaries of territorial constituencies by the Delimitation Commission".
In effect, the proposed expansion would create additional constituencies while redrawing existing boundaries, paving the way for the implementation of the women's quota.
LOK SABHA STRENGTH TO RISE TO 850
The Bill proposes to amend Article 81 of the Constitution to increase the maximum strength of the Lok Sabha from 550 to 850 members.
Under the proposed amendment, the House would have up to 815 members elected from states, compared with the existing ceiling of 530 and up to 35 members representing Union territories, against the current limit of 20. This would take the Lok Sabha's maximum strength to 850.
The amendment seeks to replace the existing limits under Article 81(1)(a) and Article 81(1)(b), which cap the number of members elected from states and Union territories at 530 and 20, respectively.
However, the Bill does not specify the final number of seats each state or Union territory would get. Instead, it provides for a 50 per cent increase in their existing seat allocation as part of the delimitation exercise.
STATE ASSEMBLIES TO HAVE A MAXIMUM STRENGTH OF 650
The Bill also proposes to increase the maximum strength of state Legislative Assemblies from 500 to 650 members.
Article 170(1) of the Constitution currently stipulates that a state Assembly shall have a minimum of 60 and a maximum of 500 members, elected directly from territorial constituencies. The proposed amendment seeks to raise the upper limit to 650, while retaining the minimum strength of 60.
As with the Lok Sabha, the Bill provides for a 50 per cent increase in the number of seats in each state Assembly over its existing strength immediately before the delimitation exercise.
HOW WILL DELIMITATION BE CARRIED OUT?
The Bill seeks to amend Articles 81, 82 and 170 of the Constitution, which deal with the composition of the Lok Sabha, allocation of seats, delimitation of constituencies and the composition of state Assemblies.
The proposed delimitation exercise would involve two major changes: increasing the number of Lok Sabha seats allocated to each state and Union territory, as well as the total strength of their respective Assemblies, by 50 per cent; and redrawing territorial constituency boundaries using the latest published census figures available when the amendment comes into force.
The Bill's Statement of Objects and Reasons links the implementation of women's reservation to the "re-adjustment in the allocation of seats" and "re-drawing boundaries of territorial constituencies by the Delimitation Commission".
However, while the Bill lays down the constitutional framework for seat expansion and delimitation, it does not specify the detailed formula for redrawing constituency boundaries or provide a state-wise breakdown of the revised seats.
WHICH CENSUS FIGURES WILL BE USED?
The proposed amendment does not specify whether Census 2021 or Census 2027 will be used for the delimitation exercise. Instead, it repeatedly refers to the "latest published census figures available on the date of the commencement" of the Constitution (132nd Amendment) Act, 2026.
The provision would apply to population-based calculations and the readjustment of territorial constituencies. The Bill proposes to replace references to the 2001 Census in relevant constitutional provisions with the latest published census figures available when the amendment comes into force.
Consequently, the census data used for delimitation would depend on which census figures have been officially published by the time the amendment commences. The Bill does not specify a particular census year.
WHEN WILL WOMEN'S RESERVATION COME INTO EFFECT?
The Bill proposes to replace Article 334A of the Constitution, which governs the implementation of women's reservation.
Under the proposed provision, one-third reservation for women in the Lok Sabha, state Assemblies and the Legislative Assemblies of Delhi, Puducherry and Jammu and Kashmir would come into effect after the first delimitation exercise conducted following the commencement of the proposed amendment.
This effectively seeks to bring the women's quota into force after the first delimitation exercise under the new law, rather than waiting for the process envisaged under the existing 2023 legislation.
ONE-THIRD RESERVATION FOR WOMEN, INCLUDING SC/ST WOMEN
The proposed amendment provides for reservation of nearly one-third of seats in the Lok Sabha, state Assemblies and Union territory Assemblies for women, including those belonging to Scheduled Castes (SCs) and Scheduled Tribes (STs).
The Bill's Statement of Objects and Reasons refers to the Constitution (106th Amendment) Act, 2023, popularly known as the Nari Shakti Vandan Adhiniyam, which provided for one-third reservation for women in the Lok Sabha and Legislative Assemblies, including seats reserved for SC/ST women.
It states that the 2023 amendment "provided for reservation of nearly one-third of seats for women in the House of the People and the Legislative Assemblies (including women belonging to the Scheduled Castes and the Scheduled Tribes)".
The proposed amendment seeks to operationalise this reservation through the delimitation exercise, linking the implementation of the women's quota to the reallocation of seats and redrawing of constituency boundaries.
WOMEN'S RESERVATION TO CONTINUE FOR 15 YEARS
The Bill proposes that the reservation for women remain in force for 15 years from the commencement of the Constitution (106th Amendment) Act, 2023. However, Parliament would have the power to extend the period through legislation.
The proposed Article 334A states, "The reservation of seats for women... shall cease to have effect on the expiration of a period of fifteen years from the commencement of the Constitution (One Hundred and Sixth Amendment) Act, 2023 unless Parliament may by law extend the period for such further time as it may specify in this behalf."
The 15-year period would thus be calculated from the commencement of the 2023 amendment, rather than from the commencement of the proposed 132nd Amendment. Parliament could extend the reservation beyond this period through a law.
SEAT ALLOCATION, DELIMITATION FROZEN UNTIL 2051
The Bill proposes to extend the freeze on seat allocation and delimitation until 2051, replacing the existing constitutional provisions linked to the publication of census figures from the first census conducted after 2026. Under the proposed amendments, the revised allocation of seats and constituency boundaries following the delimitation exercise would remain in place until 2051.
It seeks to amend Articles 55, 81, 82 and 170 to replace the existing freeze period with 2051. The Statement of Objects and Reasons says that "the allocation of seats and the division into territorial constituencies so readjusted" would "continue until the year 2051".
This effectively means that there would be no further readjustment of seat allocation or territorial constituency boundaries before 2051 under the proposed framework.
WHAT HAPPENS TO SC/ST RESERVATION?
The Bill also proposes changes to the provisions governing reservation for Scheduled Castes (SCs) and Scheduled Tribes (STs) in the Lok Sabha and state Legislative Assemblies.
Under Article 330, the number of seats reserved for SCs and STs in the Lok Sabha is determined based on their population in the respective state or Union territory. The proposed amendment seeks to replace the existing reference to the 2001 Census with the latest published census figures available on the date the amendment comes into force.
The same change would apply to provisions governing SC/ST reservation in state Assemblies under Article 332.
Consequently, the population figures used to determine the allocation of SC/ST reserved seats would be updated based on the latest census data officially available when the proposed amendment commences.
WHAT WILL HAPPEN TO EXISTING LOK SABHA, ASSEMBLIES?
The Bill clarifies that the proposed changes would not affect the representation of members in the existing Lok Sabha, state Assemblies or Union territory Assemblies until the respective Houses are dissolved.
The proposed Article 334A(4) states, "Nothing in this article shall affect any representation in the House of the People, the Legislative Assembly of a State, the Legislative Assembly of the National Capital Territory of Delhi, the Legislative Assembly of the Union territory of Puducherry or the Legislative Assembly of the Union territory of Jammu and Kashmir until the dissolution of the then existing House of the People or the Legislative Assembly of a State or Union territory."
This means the revised seat allocation and reservation provisions would not alter the composition of the existing legislatures during their current terms. The changes would take effect for the respective legislatures following their dissolution.
WHAT DOES THE BILL MEAN IN NUTSHELL?
The proposed Constitution (132nd Amendment) Bill, 2026, seeks to implement one-third reservation for women through a delimitation exercise, while increasing the strength of the Lok Sabha and state and Union territory Assemblies by 50 per cent.
It proposes to raise the maximum strength of the Lok Sabha to 850 and state Assemblies to 650, redraw constituency boundaries using the latest published census figures available when the amendment comes into force and keep the revised seat allocation and boundaries in place until 2051.
The Bill also provides for one-third reservation for women, including SC/ST women, for 15 years from the commencement of the 2023 amendment, with Parliament empowered to extend the period. It also leaves the mechanism for rotating reserved constituencies to be determined through subsequent legislation.
While the Bill lays down the constitutional framework for the exercise, the final allocation of seats, constituency boundaries and rotation mechanism would be determined through the delimitation process and subsequent laws.

title: South's share won't shrink: Naidu urges Opposition to back 50% Lok Sabha seat hike
description: N Chandrababu Naidu backed the Centre039s proposed Lok Sabha expansion and urged parties to support women039s reservation He said the plan would preserve southern states039 parliamentary share while addressing demographic concerns
author: India Today News Desk
content:
South's share won't shrink: Naidu urges Opposition to back 50% Lok Sabha seat hike
N Chandrababu Naidu backed the Centre's proposed Lok Sabha expansion and urged parties to support women's reservation. He said the plan would preserve southern states' parliamentary share while addressing demographic concerns.
Andhra Pradesh Chief Minister N Chandrababu Naidu on Friday strongly backed the Centre's Delimitation Bill proposing a 50 per cent increase in Lok Sabha seats across states, asserting that it would not hurt southern states' representation, and urged Opposition parties to support the exercise and women's reservation.
Addressing a joint press conference in Delhi along with union minister HD Kumaraswamy, Naidu, who is part of the BJP-led NDA, appealed to political parties, including the opposition, to take a clear stand on the proposed legislation and avoid repeating what he described as mistakes made during the previous attempt to pass the Bills.
"I'm requesting all political parties to take a clear stand. Every political party must clearly and unequivocally state its position," he said.
Naidu's comments come after the government's announcement of a special Parliament session to pass the delimitation and women's reservation bills. The Opposition has opposed the delimitation exercise, arguing that it could alter the balance of political representation between states, give the BJP an electoral advantage and undermine federalism. One of their key concerns was that southern states, which have effectively implemented population control measures, could be disadvantaged in the delimitation exercise.
Responding to the Congress's stand that those who believe in the Constitution cannot support the Delimitation Bill, Naidu said the proposed seat increase would address concerns over southern states' representation while paving the way for women's reservation.
"Anybody who wants to support Nari Shakti, anybody who wants to recognise or respect women, they have to support (the Bill). Nobody can say no. This is a dream of 30 years... Now it is ready for execution, according to me. It is linked with delimitation," he said.
Naidu argued that increasing Lok Sabha seats by 50 per cent would remove objections to the implementation of 33 per cent women's reservation.
"If we increase by 50 per cent, nobody will have any grouse or objection to 33 per cent women's reservation. It is a win-win situation. There is no other formula except this. In democracy, one has to accept this," he said.
NAIDU EXPLAINS 50% SEAT INCREASE, CITES SOUTHERN STATES
Naidu said the proposed 50 per cent increase in Lok Sabha seats would ensure that southern states retain their existing share of parliamentary representation.
Giving state-wise figures, he said Andhra Pradesh's Lok Sabha seats would increase from 25 to 38, while Tamil Nadu's strength would rise from 39 to 59.
Karnataka's seats would increase from 28 to 42, Telangana's from 17 to 26, and Kerala's from 20 to 30, he said.
The combined strength of the five southern states would rise from 129 to 195 seats, while their share of total parliamentary representation would remain unchanged at 23.76 per cent, Naidu said.
He said Andhra Pradesh would retain a 4.6 per cent share, Tamil Nadu 7.18 per cent, Karnataka 5.16 per cent, Telangana 3.13 per cent and Kerala 3.68 per cent.
"Some arguments I want to answer very clearly. Andhra Pradesh, as on today, has 25 seats. Tomorrow, with 50% enhancement, it may be increased to 38, with 4.6% total proportionate, same ratio will continue," he said.
'SOUTH WAS WORRIED OVER POPULATION-BASED DELIMITATION'
Naidu said southern states had earlier feared losing their share of parliamentary representation because of their efforts to control population growth through family planning.
Recalling his efforts to promote family planning campaigns during his tenure as chief minister, he said female literacy and poverty eradication were essential to population control.
However, he argued that these issues needed to be addressed simultaneously rather than sequentially.
Citing a fertility rate of 1.6 against the replacement level of 2.1, Naidu said southern states were facing similar demographic challenges. He called for population management, incentives for larger families and measures to encourage people to have more children.
'DO NOT BE ON THE WRONG SIDE OF HISTORY'
Naidu urged Opposition parties to support the proposed legislation, saying women's reservation was a long-pending demand and women deserved to be equal partners in nation-building.
"Women's reservation is not new; it is a long-pending issue. It is well deserved. It is time for everybody to support and stand with women," he said.
He also appealed to political parties not to repeat the disruptions that he said had stalled the Bills during the previous attempt.
"Do not be on the wrong side of history. We are going to create history. It is going to happen. At this historical moment, all political parties, all leaders should be on the right side. Then India will have a glorious advantage," Naidu said.
The Centre is seeking to revive its delimitation-linked constitutional amendment and legislative package after an earlier attempt failed to secure the required two-thirds majority in April 2026.
The Union Cabinet on November 27 approved a revised delimitation proposal envisaging a 50 per cent increase in seats across states while maintaining their existing proportion of parliamentary representation until 2051.
The proposed expansion of the Lok Sabha is also linked to the implementation of the 33 per cent women's reservation under the Nari Shakti Vandan Adhiniyam.

title: From Nitish allies to JDU rebels: Political missteps of Anant Singh, Anand Mohan
description: Anand Mohan and Anant Singh039s political confrontations with the JDU leadership fuelled by personal grievances and ambitions appear to have cost them dearly with both now facing a return to jail
author: Rohit Kumar Singh
content:
From Nitish allies to JDU rebels: Political missteps of Anant Singh, Anand Mohan
Anand Mohan and Anant Singh's political confrontations with the JD(U) leadership, fuelled by personal grievances and ambitions, appear to have cost them dearly, with both now facing a return to jail.
Anand Mohan and Anant Singh, two prominent faces of Bihar's politics, are now set to return to jail after the Supreme Court withdrew relief in their respective cases and ordered them to surrender. While Anand Mohan's premature release was cancelled, Anant Singh's bail was revoked. However, beyond their legal troubles, the two leaders share an interesting political story -- both were once close to the ruling establishment, but their relations with the Janata Dal (United) and the government gradually soured.
How did their equations with JD(U) deteriorate? Where did they go wrong politically? And did their confrontations with the party leadership and the government ultimately come at a cost?
ANANT SINGH: A POLITICAL RETURN FOLLOWED BY A CLASH
Anant Singh, the former Mokama MLA popularly known as 'Chhote Sarkar', also has a long political association with Nitish Kumar and the JD(U). He was elected MLA from Mokama on a JD(U) ticket in 2005 and 2010. However, after becoming dissatisfied with the JD(U)-RJD alliance in 2015, he left the party and contested as an independent. He later joined the RJD and won the 2020 Assembly election on its ticket.
In 2024, his wife, Neelam Devi, joined the JD(U). During the February 2024 trust vote, she voted in support of the Nitish Kumar government. Anant Singh subsequently returned to the JD(U) as well.
He contested the 2025 Assembly election from Mokama on a JD(U) ticket and won, once again aligning himself with Nitish Kumar's party.
But his relationship with the party hit a roadblock over the Patna Graduate Constituency MLC election.
The JD(U) fielded its sitting MLC, Neeraj Kumar, and expected party leaders and legislators to campaign for the official candidate. Anant Singh, however, broke ranks and backed Jan Suraaj candidate Anuj Singh.
He openly campaigned against Neeraj Kumar, citing their past political rivalry. Anant Singh alleged that Neeraj Kumar had previously worked against him and said he wanted to settle old political scores.
The JD(U) leadership attempted to persuade him to fall in line, but he remained firm.
The party subsequently took disciplinary action. On October 25, the JD(U) expelled Anant Singh and his wife, Neelam Devi, for six years, accusing them of indiscipline, making objectionable remarks against senior leaders and campaigning against the party's official candidate. The party also sought action to terminate Anant Singh's Assembly membership.
But his troubles extended beyond politics.
During campaigning for the 2025 Assembly election, Dularchand Yadav was murdered in Mokama. Anant Singh was arrested in connection with the case and later secured bail from the Patna High Court. However, on October 30, the Supreme Court cancelled his bail and directed him to surrender by December 1. This would be five days after his daughter's lavish wedding, which had generated considerable buzz.
The court also directed Bihar Police to complete the investigation within four months.
ANAND MOHAN: FROM POLITICAL PROXIMITY TO CONFRONTATION
Anand Mohan, who has long been identified as a strongman in Bihar politics, was once counted among Nitish Kumar's political allies. His wife, Lovely Anand, joined the JD(U) and was elected MP from Sheohar in the 2024 Lok Sabha elections. Their son, Chetan Anand, had also become a JD(U) MLA, strengthening the family's political presence.
However, the family's political ambitions and its relationship with the JD(U) gradually began to diverge.
Chetan Anand was elected MLA in 2020 on an RJD ticket. In February 2024, when Nitish Kumar left the Mahagathbandhan and returned to the NDA, Chetan Anand also switched sides and supported the Nitish Kumar government.
After helping the government prove its majority in 2024, Anand Mohan was hopeful that his son would be made a minister in the new government following the 2025 Assembly elections. But that expectation remained unfulfilled.
Even after Samrat Choudhary became Chief Minister, Anand Mohan reportedly expected Chetan Anand to be accommodated in the Cabinet during the expansion. That, too, did not happen.
His disappointment soon turned into an open confrontation with the JD(U) leadership, particularly its working national president, Sanjay Jha. Anand Mohan launched an attack on Jha, accusing him of attempting to politically bury Nitish Kumar.
This raised questions over whether Anand Mohan's anger stemmed primarily from his son's failure to secure a ministerial berth. From that point, his distance from the JD(U) leadership and the government appeared to widen further.
However, Anand Mohan's current legal troubles have a separate history.
The case dates back to the 1994 murder of G Krishnaiah, the then District Magistrate of Gopalganj. Anand Mohan was convicted in the case and sentenced to life imprisonment. The Patna High Court commuted his death sentence to life imprisonment, and the Supreme Court upheld the life sentence in 2012.
In April 2023, the then Nitish Kumar government amended the prison rules, paving the way for Anand Mohan's premature release. The decision triggered considerable political controversy, and Krishnaiah's wife, Uma Devi, challenged it before the Supreme Court.
After nearly three years of legal proceedings, the Supreme Court on November 26, declared the Bihar government's rule change unconstitutional, cancelled Anand Mohan's premature release and directed him to surrender within a month.
WHERE DID THE POLITICAL EQUATIONS GO WRONG?
The trajectories of Anand Mohan and Anant Singh appear strikingly similar in some respects. Anand Mohan's confrontation with the JD(U) leadership intensified after his son was not accommodated in the Cabinet, while Anant Singh openly defied the party's official position over an MLC election, citing a personal political rivalry.
Both were once close to Nitish Kumar's political establishment. Both had families actively involved in Bihar politics. But their equations with the JD(U) leadership deteriorated over time.
Did they misread the political situation? Did personal grievances and political ambitions take precedence over party discipline? And does Nitish Kumar's political establishment have limited space for those who challenge its decisions?
Whatever the reasons, their political confrontations with the JD(U) leadership appear to have added another chapter to their turbulent political journeys. Both leaders are now facing a return to jail, even as their political equations with the party and the government have changed significantly.

title: Omar sees UP poll angle in Sheshnag row – ‘Stoking communal tension before elections’
description: The J&K Chief Minister accuses the BJP and PDP of trying to turn the controversy over excavation near Sheshnag Lake into a Hindu-Muslim issue, alleging that the timing is linked to the upcoming Uttar Pradesh Assembly elections
author: Arun Sharma
content:
Jammu & Kashmir Chief Minister Omar Abdullah on Friday claimed there were deliberate attempts to incite communal trouble over the Amarnath Yatra track in view of the Assembly elections in Uttar Pradesh.
The remarks come amid the row over excavation and road-widening work near the high-altitude glacial Sheshnag Lake on the Amarnath Yatra route. The Omar Abdullah-led Jammu and Kashmir government has defended the work, denied any ecological damage and ordered an internal inquiry into whether the Border Roads Organisation (BRO) deviated from the approved plan.
In his speech, Omar accused the Bharatiya Janata Party and “hardliners” of stoking communal tensions.
“Yeh BJP aur yeh garam jamat waley aaj dobara Jammu Kashmir mein Hindu-Musalman ke beech fasaad karbaney ke koshish kar rahey hein, Amarnath ke rastey ko le ke (This BJP and the hardliners are trying to incite communal tension between Hindus and Muslims over the issue of Amarnath track),” Abdullah said at a public meeting in Kathua district’s remote Bani town.
Omar said the Opposition claimed that broken stones and tarpaulin had been laid at the lake. “I dare them to go there and see for themselves. If even a foot of tarpaulin is found there, I’m prepared to face an enquiry,” he said.
In compliance with court instructions for a 12-ft-wide road, a machine was moving earth from one side of the track to the other at a spot away from Sheshnag Lake, he claimed.
“However, these people — the PDP [Peoples Democratic Party] and the BJP — keeping in mind the UP elections started making attempts to incite one community against the other by misleading people in Jammu and Kashmir,” he claimed.
Abdullah also dared the PDP and the BJP to approach either the courts or green tribunals if there was merit in the allegations.
“They won’t do that. Instead, they will try to play with public sentiment by misleading people through the media. The National Conference will not allow them to succeed, as it is determined to maintain communal harmony in Jammu and Kashmir,” he claimed.
The current row pertains to a video showing an excavator operating near Sheshnag Lake, at an altitude of 3,590 metres along the Pahalgam-Amarnath shrine track. Politicians, environmentalists and religious leaders have voiced concerns over the ecological and religious consequences of the work.
While the Border Roads Organisation and J&K Forest Minister Altaf Ahmad Wani have both said the work involved routine post-Yatra track maintenance and widening, PDP president Mehbooba Mufti tried to visit the site but was stopped by the police.
In a post on X, she later demanded to know why she had been stopped from visiting the site. “The JCBs wreaking havoc there are visible for all to see. To dispel all doubts, let the CM depute a team of political leaders and environmentalists to inspect the site and establish the truth. What is there to hide?” she asked.
Abdullah’s statement comes nearly two decades after the Amarnath land row rocked the state. A major political and communal crisis in J&K, the row was sparked by a government decision to transfer around 100 acres of forest land to the Shri Amarnathji Shrine Board (SASB) for temporary facilities for Hindu pilgrims.
The row divided the then state of J&K along communal lines, leading to the untimely fall of the Congress-PDP coalition government led by Ghulam Nabi Azad.

title: After 2 years of stalemate, J&K gets Advocate General. Who is Syed Faisal Qadri?
description: Syed Faisal Qadri has been practising law in Srinagar for over two decades. He was chosen from among a panel of three names
author: Naveed Iqbal
content:
Naveed Iqbal is a Senior Assistant Editor at The Indian Express, and reports from Jammu and Kashmir.... Read More
- Tags:
- Jammu and Kashmir
Jammu & Kashmir Lieutenant Governor Manoj Sinha on Friday approved the appointment of senior advocate Syed Faisal Qadri as Advocate General of the Union Territory. This ends over two years of stalemate over the issue between the L-G’s office and Chief Minister Omar Abdullah.
Qadri is a senior advocate practising in the High Court of J&K and Ladakh.
Following the swearing-in of the National Conference-led government in October 2024, the previous Advocate General, DC Raina, had submitted his resignation.
He was appointed to the post by former L-G Girish Chandra Murmu in November 2019, a day after J&K officially ceased to be a state.
When Raina called on Omar after his resignation, the CM asked him to continue in office. However, with confusion persisting over whether the L-G or the CM’s office would notify the appointment, and that Raj Bhawan had not cleared the continuation of Raina, the decision remained in limbo.
Qadri’s appointment was notified on Friday by the Department of Law, Justice and Parliamentary Affairs through an order dated November 27, issued under Section 79(1) of the Jammu and Kashmir Reorganisation Act, 2019.
Qadri has been practising law in Srinagar for over two decades. He was chosen from among a panel of three names. An alumnus of the University of Kashmir, he was designated senior advocate in December 2020.
The appointment of the AG for J&K remained a key contentious issue over the last two years alongside the finalisation of the Transaction of Business Rules, the concerns over rationalisation of reservation, nomination of members to the J&K Assembly, as well as control over institutions such as the Sher-e-Kashmir Institute of Medical Sciences.
While the L-G has asserted that he remains in charge of law and order as prescribed in the J&K Reorganisation Act (2019), the elected government has sought greater control over bureaucracy for effective functioning of government departments.
CM Omar has highlighted several times that a “dual power system” is an arrangement “built for failure” and unworkable in the long term.
“I did not know that attempts would be made to change the decisions of the Cabinet without the approval of the Cabinet. I did not know that decisions of the Cabinet would be stopped. They would not be approved. They would be locked up somewhere and forgotten,” Omar had said during his Independence Day address in 2025.
This year, his party has been exerting greater pressure to press its demand for statehood, taking their protests from the streets of Srinagar and Jammu to New Delhi.

title: Delimitation Bill full text:  850 Lok Sabha seats, women’s quota, 25-year freeze

title: Four directors of Hyderabad fertility centre detained in alleged human egg trafficking case
description: Police detained four directors of the company operating Oasis Fertility and Sadguru ART clinics after raids linked to an alleged illegal egg harvesting racket in Hyderabad. | India News
author: Srinivasa Rao Apparasu
content:
Srinivasa Rao is Senior Assistant Editor based out of Hyderabad covering developments in Andhra Pradesh and Telangana . He has over three decades of reporting experience.
Four directors of Hyderabad fertility centre detained in alleged human egg trafficking case
Police detained four directors of the company operating Oasis Fertility and Sadguru ART clinics after raids linked to an alleged illegal egg harvesting racket in Hyderabad.
Four directors of a Hyderabad-based fertility centre were detained on Friday in connection with an alleged illegal human egg harvesting and trafficking racket, police said.
The detentions followed overnight searches at the corporate offices of the company operating Oasis Fertility and Sadguru Assisted Reproductive Technology (ART) clinics in Begumpet, during which police seized laptops, financial records and documents.
A senior Malkajgiri police official said the four directors belonged to Sadguru Healthcare Services Private Limited, the parent company operating the two fertility clinic chains.
“They were taken into custody for questioning after overnight searches conducted by police teams led by assistant commissioner of police Gopalakrishna Murthy at the corporate offices of Sadguru Healthcare and Oasis Fertility at Center Point Apartments in Begumpet,” he said.
The police also sealed the premises after seizing laptops, financial records and other documents. “We are also on the lookout for the prime accused and founder-director, Venkata Surya Kiran Gedela. We are taking steps to secure a non-bailable warrant against him,” the official said.
The alleged exploitation came to light on October 31, when 43 women were rescued during simultaneous raids across Hyderabad. Women from economically weaker sections were allegedly offered between ₹20,000 and ₹30,000 for each egg donation cycle, while those operating the racket reportedly earned an average of around ₹3 lakh per cycle.
Malkajgiri police commissioner B Sumathi said nine people had been arrested in connection with the racket, which was allegedly being operated from Venkateswara Colony under the jurisdiction of Saroornagar police station.
She said the prime accused, identified as Durga Prasad, allegedly lured women from different states to Hyderabad with promises of money and accommodated them at Shetty Working Women’s Hostel in Venkateswara Colony. The women were allegedly made to undergo egg extraction every month.
Prasad supplied the eggs collected from the women to various corporate hospitals and fertility centres at high prices, Sumathi said.
“Acting on a tip-off, the Saroornagar police arrested Prasad and his eight associates. As many as 15 women from the hostel were taken to Osmania Hospital for medical check-up, from where they were sent to shelter homes,” she said.
The police also raided an apartment in Begumpet’s Prakash Nagar and rescued eight women from Bihar, Uttar Pradesh and Odisha, who were allegedly paid to donate eggs. “The racket was being run under the name of a working women’s hostel,” the commissioner said.
Following the arrests, police conducted a series of searches at fertility centres. Investigators suspect that Gedela Venkata Surya Kiran, founder-director and co-founder of Sadguru Healthcare, played a key role in the alleged egg procurement and sale network.
The investigation has also revealed, prima facie, that funds amounting to several crores of rupees were transferred from Oasis Fertility to Sadguru Healthcare Services Private Limited. Police are examining the transactions to establish the reasons for these transfers and determine whether they were linked to the alleged egg sale operations.

title: No State Left Behind? How Centre's New Three-Bill Formula Seeks To End Delimitation Divide
description: The three bills aim to clear the mandatory two-thirds parliamentary hurdle next week and set the stage for constituency redrawing ahead of the 2029 polls
author: Pathikrit Sen Gupta, Arunima
content:
No State Left Behind? How Centre's New Three-Bill Formula Seeks To End Delimitation Divide
The three bills aim to clear the mandatory two-thirds parliamentary hurdle next week and set the stage for constituency redrawing ahead of the 2029 polls
Got Question about the News?
In a decisive move to break the legislative deadlock over delimitation and 33 per cent women’s reservation, the Union government has circulated a three-bill legislative package to MPs ahead of Parliament’s reconvened sitting on Monday, November 30. Anchored by the Constitution (132nd Amendment) Bill, 2026, the draft legislation gives a written constitutional guarantee that every state’s proportional representation in the Lok Sabha will remain intact through a uniform 50 per cent seat expansion, while freezing inter-state seat readjustments until 2051.
The draft bills were circulated on Friday evening, hours after Tamil Nadu Chief Minister and DMK president MK Stalin reiterated on social media that any reduction in Tamil Nadu’s existing 7.18 per cent share of Lok Sabha seats would be unacceptable, and demanded that the 1971 Census-based distribution among states remain frozen for another 25 years. By writing both safeguards directly into the constitutional text, the Centre has moved to address the core objection that sank its earlier Constitution (131st Amendment) Bill in April 2026.
- Cabinet Clears Delimitation Bill Changes: Lok Sabha Seats To Rise 50%, State Share Frozen Till 2051
- From 543 To 815 MPs: How A 50% Increase In Lok Sabha Seats Will Change India's Parliament
- 67 Votes Short In April: How Modi Govt Plans To Turn The Tables On Delimitation-Women's Quota Bill In Parliament
- 888 Lok Sabha Seats, 543 MPs: How India's New Parliament Was 'Built-Ready' For Delimitation Shake-Up
Inside the Constitution (132nd Amendment) Bill, 2026
Unlike the earlier April draft, which relied on verbal assurances without codifying proportional protection, the newly circulated Constitution (132nd Amendment) Bill, 2026 amends Article 81 of the Constitution to raise the Lok Sabha’s maximum constitutional strength from 550 to 850—comprising up to 815 seats from states (up from the current cap of 530) and 35 seats from Union Territories (up from 20).
To guarantee that no state loses relative political weightage, the bill retains the 1971 Census as the baseline for inter-state seat allocation and mandates a uniform 50 per cent increase in Lok Sabha seats across every state and Union Territory during the first delimitation exercise after the amendment takes effect. Crucially, the bill freezes inter-state delimitation until 2051—substituting the existing constitutional reference to “the first census taken after the year 2026" with “until the year 2051".
At the same time, by amending Article 82, the government proposes using 2011 Census figures—rather than waiting for a post-2026 Census—to redraw internal constituency boundaries within each state and Union Territory. The bill also amends Article 170 to raise the maximum ceiling on state legislative assemblies from 500 to 650 seats, paving the way for larger states such as Uttar Pradesh—currently capped at 500—to see an expansion of around 150 seats alongside a uniform 50 per cent assembly hike across states.
How the Delimitation Bill and UT Laws Amendment Complete the Package
The Union government circulated a three-bill legislative package including the Constitution (132nd Amendment) Bill, 2026 to MPs.
The draft legislation proposes raising the Lok Sabha's maximum constitutional strength from 550 to 850 seats.
Inter-state seat readjustments are frozen until the year 2051 using the 1971 Census as the baseline.
The Delimitation Bill provides the statutory framework to implement a one-third reservation for women in the Lok Sabha and state assemblies ahead of the 2029 general elections.
Alongside the Constitution (132nd Amendment) Bill, the government is introducing two companion legislations on Monday to operationalise the expansion and women’s quota ahead of the 2029 general elections.
The second legislation, the Delimitation Bill, provides the statutory framework to give immediate effect to one-third reservation for women—including women from Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes—in the Lok Sabha and state and Union Territory legislative assemblies. It empowers a Delimitation Commission to readjust the allocation of seats and divide each state and Union Territory into newly drawn territorial constituencies, ensuring that women’s reservation is rolled out without reducing the existing pool of unreserved seats.
The third piece of legislation, the Union Territories Laws (Amendment) Bill, updates statutes governing Union Territories so that the 50 per cent seat expansion, boundary redrawing, and 33 per cent women’s reservation apply uniformly across Union Territories with legislatures. Together, the three bills aim to clear the mandatory two-thirds parliamentary hurdle next week and set the stage for constituency redrawing ahead of the 2029 polls.
Quick Answers
The Constitution (132nd Amendment) Bill, 2026 amends Article 81 to raise the Lok Sabha's maximum strength from 550 to 850 seats. It guarantees a uniform 50 per cent seat expansion across every state and Union Territory while freezing inter-state seat readjustments until 2051.

title: Explained: What is delimitation? Why is the Bill pending, and what is the debate about?
description: The Union Cabinet on Friday cleared a fresh bill linking the rollout of women's reservation to delimitation to effect a uniform 50 per cent rise in Lok Sabha seats in all states, which it is likely to introduce during the special sitting of Parliament next week.
author: PTI
content:
Explained: What is delimitation? Why is the Bill pending, and what is the debate about?
- Edited bysrabastee Biswas
- Published OnNov 27, 2026 | 21:19 IST
- Last Updated OnNov 27, 2026 | 21:19 IST
Linking women's reservation to constituency redrawing has sparked sharp political friction, with opposition parties raising concerns over boundary manipulation ahead of upcoming general polls. Discover how regional leaders plan to counter the proposed legislation in Parliament.
The Union Cabinet on Friday cleared a fresh bill linking the rollout of women’s reservation to delimitation to effect a uniform 50 per cent rise in Lok Sabha seats in all states, which it is likely to introduce during the special sitting of Parliament next week.
As the four-day special sitting brings the spotlight back on the delimitation debate, here’s an explainer on how Parliamentary and Assembly constituencies are redrawn following such an exercise.
1. What is delimitation?
Delimitation is the act or process of fixing limits or boundaries of territorial constituencies in a country or a province having a legislative body.
2. Who decides boundaries?
The task of delimitation is assigned to a high-powered body known as the delimitation commission or a boundary commission. In India, such commissions have been constituted four times under the Delimitation Commission Act – in 1952, 1963, 1973 and in 2002.
The Delimitation Commission of India is a high-powered body whose orders have the force of law and cannot be called in question before any court. The orders come into force on a date to be specified by the President. The copies of its orders are laid before Parliament and the state Assemblies concerned, but no modifications are permissible by them.
3. What is the debate about?
The government brought ‘The Delimitation Bill, 2026’ to replace the 2002 law during a special sitting of Parliament in April this year, under which the Centre would have the power to constitute a delimitation commission to distribute seats in the Lok Sabha and Assemblies based on the “latest census figures”.
4. Why is the Bill pending?
Since the Constitution Amendment Bill relating to the implementation of the women’s quota law before the 2029 general elections was defeated in the Lok Sabha in April due to a lack of numbers, the delimitation Bill never came up for voting. The government had decided to keep it pending in the Lower House.
5. What does the Bill say?
Several of the provisions of the new delimitation bill are similar to the 2002 law, which would be repealed. According to the Bill, the Central government may, from time to time, by notification, constitute a body to be called the Delimitation Commission.
The Commission shall comprise the following: one member, who shall be a person who is or has been a judge of the Supreme Court, to be appointed by the Centre as the chairperson of the Commission; the chief election commissioner or an election commissioner nominated by the chief election commissioner, ex officio; and the state election commissioner of the concerned state, ex officio.
The Central government may, by notification, specify the term of the Commission. It may, on the request of the Commission, extend its term by such further period as it may consider necessary.
The Election Commission shall act as the Delimitation Commission for the purpose of delimiting constituencies in the Assembly of Jammu and Kashmir falling under the occupation of Pakistan, when the area of the Union territory under the occupation of Pakistan ceases to be so occupied.
The Bill also states that the Commission shall associate with itself for the purpose of assisting it in its duties in respect of each state, 10 persons, 5 of whom shall be members of the House of the People representing that state and 5 shall be members of the Assembly of that state.
6. What is the Opposition’s stand?
The opposition parties have cited the delimitation exercises in Assam and Jammu and Kashmir to raise apprehensions over gerrymandering, which refers to the manipulation of constituency boundaries for electoral advantage.
The Lok Sabha Leader of Opposition, Rahul Gandhi, has accused the BJP of seeking to redraw the country’s electoral map to its advantage ahead of the 2029 general elections. The government has rejected the apprehensions.
Even if the existing share of states in the Lok Sabha is protected, the manner in which constituency boundaries are to be redrawn within states remains a point of contention for the opposition parties.
Rajya Sabha Leader of Opposition, Mallikarjun Kharge, has invited all the opposition floor leaders for a meeting at his residence on Saturday to devise a joint strategy in view of the government’s likely move to reintroduce the Constitution Amendment Bill in Parliament involving delimitation.
While the floor leaders of the INDIA bloc parties will be present at the meeting, the non-INDIA bloc parties such as the DMK, the AAP and the BJD, among others, have also been invited for the discussions.
7. What is the government’s argument for using the 2011 Census?
Union Home Minister Amit Shah had argued in the Lok Sabha in April that a delimitation exercise undertaken after a fresh census will take time and delay an early implementation of the women’s quota law. It will not be possible before the 2029 elections, given the extensive public consultations involved, he argued.

title: Assam government issues dress code for secretariat staffers; prohibits jeans, T-shirt, flip-flops

author: PTI
content:
Assam government issues dress code for secretariat staffers; prohibits jeans, T-shirt, flip-flops
- Published OnNov 27, 2026 | 21:18 IST
- Last Updated OnNov 27, 2026 | 21:18 IST
The order said the dress standards were being issued in the interest of maintaining a high level of dignity, discipline and decorum amongst employees of the secretariat complex, and would come into immediate effect.
The Assam government on Friday issued an "apparel advisory" for all officials serving at the state Secretariat Janata Bhawan, prohibiting casual attire such as jeans, T-shirts, leggings, tunics and flip-flops during office hours and in official engagements.
The advisory, issued by the General Administration (Secretariat Establishment) Department, said it has been noticed that certain dress codes being used by several government officials during the discharge of official duties were "deemed not decent to look at and are lowering the image of government servants in the public eyes, causing embarrassment to the government".
The order said the dress standards were being issued in the interest of maintaining a high level of dignity, discipline and decorum amongst employees of the secretariat complex, and would come into immediate effect.
The advisory will be applicable to all officials irrespective of cadres serving at Janata Bhawan, the government said, and advised all to attire with "appropriate dress code reflecting 'sense of decorum', 'decency', 'professionalism' and 'seriousness' during all official works and engagements".
For male officials, only "appropriate formal attire" -- formal pant-shirt and traditional Indian attire including kurta, dhoti-pyjama and other decent traditional clothing -- will be allowed.
Casual attire such as T-shirt and jeans has been barred, the advisory signed by General Administration Deputy Secretary Manash Jyoti Baruah said.
For female officials, "decent" salwar suit, saree and mekhela-chador have been prescribed. Casual attire such as T-shirt, jeans, tunics and leggings has been barred.
The dress standards will also apply while attending official training programmes conducted at the Secretariat Training School, Assam Administrative Staff College and other government training institutions, the advisory mentioned.
It also prescribed appropriate footwear, stating that "proper and decent footwear" suitable for a formal office environment should be worn.
Casual footwear such as flip-flops and informal footwear should be strictly avoided.
All officials have been asked to wear "clean, modest and decent looking clothes in sober colours", which should not look flashy, the instructions said.
Casual and party clothing should always be avoided while discharging official duties, attending training sessions, official meetings and other engagements, it added.
"Any violation in this regard will be viewed seriously and invite appropriate disciplinary action against the erring official(s) as deemed fit and proper," the advisory said.
The advisory has been circulated among the senior-most secretaries of all administrative departments for compliance by all officers and staffers serving in the Janata Bhawan.

title: Delimitation Bill: BJP confident of securing numbers as Opposition questions timing and intent

author: Ashmit Kumar
content:
Delimitation Bill: BJP confident of securing numbers as Opposition questions timing and intent
- Published OnNov 27, 2026 | 20:23 IST
- Last Updated OnNov 27, 2026 | 20:23 IST
The proposed delimitation Bill has triggered a fresh political debate ahead of the November 30 Parliament session, with the BJP expressing confidence of securing support. Congress and other Opposition leaders have questioned the timing, political intent and use of Census data in the exercise.
The proposed delimitation exercise has triggered a fresh political confrontation ahead of the Parliament session scheduled to resume on November 30, with the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) expressing confidence of securing the required numbers while Opposition parties have questioned the timing and intent behind the move.
The revised proposal reportedly includes a uniform 50% increase in Lok Sabha seats across states, with their share of representation frozen for the next 25 years. The government has linked the exercise to implementing 33% women's reservation.
BJP spokesperson Priyadarshini Singh defended the proposal, arguing that it would improve women's representation and give more opportunities to people outside established political families. She said the government was confident of building support across party lines.
"Let's wait for 30th November," Singh said, expressing confidence that the Bill would mark a significant change in Indian politics.
Samajwadi Party spokesperson Ghanshyam Tiwari questioned the government's approach, alleging that the delimitation exercise was being used to secure political advantage. He also raised concerns over linking delimitation with women's reservation, arguing that the two issues should be treated separately.
Senior journalist Sanjeev Srivastava offered a more cautious assessment, saying the BJP appeared to have learnt from its defeat in April and may have worked towards securing the required numbers this time. He noted that the proposed 50% increase across states could address some Opposition concerns, but questions over the timing and the use of older Census data remain.
Srivastava said the actual political arithmetic would become clear only when the Bill comes up for voting. The November 30 session is expected to be crucial in determining whether the government can secure the two-thirds majority needed to pass the constitutional amendment.
Congress spokesperson Chitra Batham Nishad, however, dismissed the BJP's confidence and maintained that the Opposition remained united. She said the Bill would not pass during the upcoming session.
Nishad also pointed to the DMK's position, saying the party had maintained two key demands: Tamil Nadu's existing 7.18% share of Lok Sabha seats should not decline, and the proportion of representation among states based on the 1971 Census should remain unchanged for another 25 years.
