title: 'करुणा की कमी ही दुनिया की हर समस्या की जड़', दिल्ली में बोले RSS प्रमुख मोहन भागवत- अब दुनिया को देने की बारी भारत की
description: RSS चीफ का मानना है कि दुनिया भर की समस्याओं की मुख्य वजह 'मैं और मेरा' वाली सोच है और इसका हल सिर्फ 'करुणा' में छिपा है. उन्होंने कैलाश सत्यार्थी की बुक 'करुणानायक राम' के लॉन्च इवेंट में भगवान श्रीराम के दयालु और करुणावान व्यक्तित्व पर जोर दिया.
author: भूपेंद्र राय
content:
RSS चीफ डॉ. मोहन भागवत ने तेजी से बढ़ रहे स्वार्थ, अहंकार और दुनिया भर में जारी लड़ाई पर चिंता जताई है. उन्होंने देश और दुनिया की हर बड़ी समस्या की असली जड़ 'करुणा की कमी' को बताया है. उनका मानना है कि मौजूदा वक्त में पूरी दुनिया में करुणा को फैलाने यानी 'ग्लोबलाइजेशन ऑफ कम्पैशन' की बहुत जरूरत है.
मोहन भावगत, नोबेल पुरस्कार विजेता कैलाश सत्यार्थी की किताब 'करुणानायक राम' का विमोचन कार्यक्रम में शिरकत करने पहुंचे थे. यह कार्यक्रम जनपथ स्थित डॉ. आंबेडकर इंटरनेशनल सेंटर में आयोजित हुआ. अपने संबोधन में उन्होंने कहा, चाहे कोई समस्या देश की हो या विदेश की, अतीत की हो, वर्तमान की हो या भविष्य की, सबकी जड़ एक ही जगह है और वह है करुणा का अभाव. उन्होंने आगे कहा कि मैंने 'करुणा के वैश्वीकरण' का विचार पहली बार कैलाश जी से सुना और आज इसकी सबसे ज्यादा जरूरत है.
#WATCH | Delhi: Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh (RSS) Chief Mohan Bhagwat says, "What was the difference between Ravana and Ram—one could say that Ravana was arrogant, while Ram was compassionate. But what is arrogance? It is the inability to look beyond 'I' and 'mine.' Why are we unable to move past this? It is because we remain unaware of a certain truth—or, even if we know it in words, we have not experienced it..."
— ANI (@ANI) November 27, 2026
मोहन भागवत ने रामायण का उदाहरण देकर भगवान राम और रावण के बीच का फर्क समझाया. उनका कहना है कि रावण में अहंकार कूट-कूटकर भरा था, जबकि भगवान राम करुणा की जीती-जागती मिसाल थे. 'मैं और मेरा' की सोच से आगे न बढ़ पाना ही असली अहंकार है. इंसान इस दायरे से बाहर इसलिए नहीं निकल पाता, क्योंकि वह परम सत्य को महसूस नहीं कर पाता. भागवत ने आगे कहा, दुनिया में जितने भी युद्ध और झगड़े हो रहे हैं, वे इसी 'मैं और मेरा' वाली छोटी सोच की देन हैं.
#WATCH | Delhi: Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh (RSS) Chief Mohan Bhagwat says, "... What else, truly, distinguishes a human from an animal? Biologically, a human is also an animal—sharing the same basic instincts. Yet, there exists something distinct—a special quality—which is compassion..."
— ANI (@ANI) November 27, 2026
भागवत ने इंसानी स्वभाव को लेकर कहा, आखिर इंसान को जानवर से अलग क्या बनाता है? जैविक रूप से देखा जाए तो इंसान भी एक जानवर ही है, जिसमें वही बुनियादी प्रवृत्तियां होती हैं, लेकिन इंसान के भीतर एक ऐसा खास गुण है जो उसे अलग बनाता है, और वह गुण 'करुणा' है. उनका मानना है कि लोग रूप, रंग और व्यवहार में अलग-अलग दिख सकते हैं, लेकिन बुनियादी सच्चाई यह है कि हम सभी भीतर से एक-दूसरे से जुड़े हुए हैं और एक ही इकाई का हिस्सा हैं. यह एकात्मता ही परम और स्थायी सत्य है. जब तक पूरी दुनिया और पर्यावरण खुशहाल नहीं होंगे, तब तक कोई भी व्यक्ति या देश सही मायने में खुश नहीं रह सकता.

title: Weather Update 28 November: तमिलनाडु-केरल में बरसेंगे बादल, दिल्ली-यूपी में घने कोहरे की मार, राजस्थान में चलेगी शीतलहर!
description: Weather Update 28 November: भारतीय मौसम विज्ञान विभाग (IMD) ने 28 नवंबर के लिए देश के अलग-अलग हिस्सों में मौसम के बदले मिजाज की चेतावनी जारी की है. आइए जानते हैं कहां कैसा मौसम रहेगा...
author: भूपेंद्र राय
content:
Weather Update 28 November: भारत में सर्दियों ने दस्तक दे दी है. कहीं बारिश तो कहीं घना कोहरा देखा जा रहा है. भारतीय मौसम विज्ञान विभाग का अनुमान है कि 28 नवंबर को देशभर में मौसम के दो अलग-अलग रंग देखने को मिलेंगे. एक तरफ जहां दक्षिण भारत के कई राज्यों में भारी बारिश, गरज-चमक और तेज हवाओं का दौर चलेगा, तो वहीं दूसरी तरफ उत्तर और पूर्वोत्तर भारत के मैदानी इलाकों में घना कोहरा परेशानी बढ़ाएगा. इसके अलावा राजस्थान के पूर्वी हिस्सों में शीतलहर चलने से ठिठुरन और बढ़ने की संभावना है.
28 नवंबर को पूर्वी हवाओं के प्रभाव के चलते तमिलनाडु, पुडुचेरी और कराईकल में कहीं-कहीं भारी बारिश हो सकती है. केरल, माहे, लक्षद्वीप में बारिश के साथ बिजली गिरने की आशंका जताई गई है. इन इलाकों में 30 से 40 किमी प्रति घंटे की रफ्तार से तेज हवाएं चल सकती हैं, जिनकी गति 50 किमी प्रति घंटे तक बढ़ सकती है.
मौसम संबंधी चेतावनी ! मुख्य बिंदु: पूर्वी हवाओं के प्रभाव के कारण, 27-28 नवंबर के दौरान तमिलनाडु, पुडुचेरी और कराईकल में; तथा 27 नवंबर को केरल और माहे में कहीं-कहीं भारी बारिश होने की संभावना है। Highlights: Under the influence of easterly waves, isolated heavy rainfall likely over Tamil Nadu, Puducherry & Karaikal during 27th-28th November; Kerala & Mahe on 27th November. East India: Isolated to Scattered rainfall likely over Andaman & Nicobar Islands during 27th-29th November.  Fairly Widespread to Widespread rainfall likely over Andaman & Nicobar Islands during 30th November- 3rd December. Isolated thunderstorm, lightning & gusty winds (speed reaching 40-50 kmph gusting to 60 kmph) likely over Andaman & Nicobar Islands during 29th November-2nd December, with gusty winds (speed reaching 30-40 kmph gusting to 50 kmph) likely over Andaman & Nicobar Islands on 3rd December.  Isolated heavy rainfall likely over Andaman & Nicobar Islands during 30th November-2nd December. South Peninsular India:  Isolated to Scattered rainfall likely over Tamil Nadu, Puducherry & Karaikal on 27th November and during 29th November-3rd December; Kerala & Mahe during 29th November-3rd December; Lakshadweep on 29th November and during 2nd-3rd December; Coastal Karnataka during 27th-28th November; North Interior Karnataka and Telangana on 27th November; South Interior Karnataka during 27th-28th November and during 2nd-3rd December; Coastal Andhra Pradesh & Yanam and Rayalaseema during 27th November-3rd December.  Fairly Widespread to Widespread rainfall likely over Tamil Nadu, Puducherry & Karaikal on 28th November; Kerala & Mahe and Lakshadweep during 27th-28th November.  Isolated thunderstorm, lightning & gusty winds (speed reaching 30-40 kmph gusting to 50 kmph) likely over Kerala & Mahe, Lakshadweep and Tamil Nadu, Puducherry & Karaikal during 27th-28th November.  Isolated thunderstorm & lightning likely over Coastal Karnataka, North Interior Karnataka and South Interior Karnataka on 27th November.  Isolated heavy rainfall likely over Tamil Nadu, Puducherry & Karaikal during 27th-28th November; Kerala & Mahe on 27th November. West and Central India:  No significant weather likely over West and Central India during the week. Cold Wave, Cold Day and Fog warning:  Dense fog conditions very likely over Assam & Meghalaya on 27th November; East Uttar Pradesh and West Uttar Pradesh during 27th-28th November; Haryana Chandigarh & Delhi, Nagaland, Manipur, Mizoram & Tripura and Punjab during 27th-29th November; Himachal Pradesh during 27th November-1st December. @moesgoi @airnewsalerts @DDNational @ndmaindia @ICRER_MHA #WeatherUpdate #IMD #RainfallAlert #HeavyRainfall #Kerala #TamilNadu #AndamanAndNicobarIslands #Lakshadweep #CoastalAndhraPradesh #Rayalaseema #Thunderstorm #Lightning #GustyWinds #ColdWave #DenseFog
— India Meteorological Department (@Indiametdept) November 27, 2026
तटीय आंध्र प्रदेश, यनम, रायलसीमा, तटीय और दक्षिण आंतरिक कर्नाटक में भी बारिश और तेज सतही हवाएं चलने का अनुमान है. IMD ने बताया है कि दक्षिण भारत के कई राज्यों में अगले सात दिनों (2 से 3 दिसंबर तक) रुक-रुककर बारिश का यह सिलसिला जारी रह सकता है.
अंडमान और निकोबार द्वीप समूह में 28 और 29 नवंबर को छिटपुट बारिश होगी, जो 30 नवंबर से 3 दिसंबर के बीच अपना दायरा बढ़ा सकती है. 29 नवंबर से 2 दिसंबर के बीच 40 से 50 किमी प्रति घंटे की रफ्तार से तूफानी हवाएं चलने और बिजली गिरने की चेतावनी जारी की गई है.
राजधानी दिल्ली में शनिवार को आसमान साफ रहने का अनुमान है, लेकिन सुबह के समय कुछ इलाकों में घना कोहरा छाया रह सकता है. दिल्ली में अधिकतम तापमान 24 से 26 डिग्री सेल्सियस और न्यूनतम तापमान 8 से 10 डिग्री सेल्सियस के बीच रहेगा. दिल्ली-एनसीआर के साथ ही हरियाणा, चंडीगढ़ और पंजाब में 28 और 29 नवंबर को सुबह के समय घने कोहरे का अलर्ट जारी किया गया है. हिमाचल प्रदेश में भी 1 दिसंबर तक घना कोहरा परेशान करेगा.
उत्तर प्रदेश में मौसम शुष्क रहेगा, हालांकि मॉर्निंग टाइम पूर्वी और पश्चिमी यूपी के कई इलाकों में घना कोहरा छा सकता है. रात और सुबह के तापमान में गिरावट के चलते ठंड भी बढ़ेगी, जिससे वाहन चालकों को कम दृश्यता के कारण सावधानी बरतना होगी.
बिहार में बारिश या शीतलहर का कोई बड़ा अलर्ट नहीं है. प्रदेश के ज्यादातर हिस्सों में मौसम शुष्क रहेगा. सुबह और रात के समय ठंड का असर महसूस होगा. पश्चिम और मध्य भारत के राज्यों में भी अगले एक हफ्ते तक मौसम शुष्क रहने की संभावना है.
पूर्वोत्तर भारत के राज्यों नागालैंड, मणिपुर, मिजोरम और त्रिपुरा में 28 और 29 नवंबर की सुबह घना कोहरा छाने का अलर्ट है. मॉर्निंग टाइम दृश्यता कम होने से सड़क और हवाई यातायात प्रभावित हो सकता है, इसलिए यात्रियों को सतर्क रहने की सलाह दी गई है.

title: फडणवीस की एक पोस्ट से छिड़ी मजेदार होड़: अवैध होर्डिंग पर पुणे-नागपुर मनपा की सोशल मीडिया जुगलबंदी वायरल
description: महाराष्ट्र के मुख्यमंत्री देवेंद्र फडणवीस के एक सोशल मीडिया पोस्ट के बाद अवैध होर्डिंग्स हटाने को लेकर पुणे (PMC) और नागपुर महानगरपालिका (NMC) के बीच दिलचस्प होड़ छिड़ गई है. जानें प्रशासनिक कार्रवाई और दोनों नगर निगमों की इस वायरल जुगलबंदी की पूरी कहानी.
author: अश्विनी कुमार पांडेय
content:
महाराष्ट्र के मुख्यमंत्री देवेंद्र फडणवीस के एक पोस्ट ने पुणे और नागपुर महानगरपालिका के बीच सोशल मीडिया पर ऐसी मजेदार नोकझोंक शुरू कर दी है, जिसे लोग खूब पसंद कर रहे हैं. मामला अवैध होर्डिंग और अतिक्रमण हटाने की कार्रवाई से जुड़ा है, लेकिन दोनों नगर निकायों के आधिकारिक हैंडलों ने जिस हल्के-फुल्के और चुटीले अंदाज में एक-दूसरे को जवाब दिया, उसने इस गंभीर मुद्दे को भी चर्चा के केंद्र में ला दिया है.
पुणे में अवैध होर्डिंग के खिलाफ चल रही मुहिम की तारीफ करते हुए मुख्यमंत्री ने जहां पुणे प्रशासन की पीठ थपथपाई, वहीं नागपुर प्रशासन को भी पहले से सचेत रहने का संकेत दिया. इसके तुरंत बाद पुणे और नागपुर महानगरपालिका के बीच शुरू हुआ संवाद देखते ही देखते शहर को होर्डिंग-मुक्त रखने की एक स्वस्थ और मजेदार प्रतिस्पर्धा जैसा दिखने लगा.
अतिक्रमण और खासकर अवैध होर्डिंग के विरुद्ध पुणे महानगरपालिका की कार्रवाई को लेकर देवेंद्र फडणवीस ने साफ शब्दों में कहा कि शहर की बुनियादी सुविधाओं का लाभ आम लोगों को मिलना चाहिए. उनके मुताबिक, सड़कों पर वाहनों की आवाजाही और फुटपाथ पर पैदल चलने वालों के लिए जगह बचना बेहद जरूरी है. उन्होंने यह भी स्पष्ट किया कि सरकारी नियम और आदेश केवल फाइलों या सरकारी प्रस्तावों (GR) में छपने के लिए नहीं होते, बल्कि उनका जमीनी स्तर पर पालन होना चाहिए ताकि नागरिकों की रोजमर्रा की जिंदगी आसान हो सके.
मुख्यमंत्री ने माना कि बिना अनुमति लगे होर्डिंग और फ्लेक्स की दिक्कत केवल पुणे तक सीमित नहीं है, बल्कि पूरे प्रदेश में इससे निपटने की जरूरत है. उन्होंने जोर दिया कि ऐसी कार्रवाई किसी एक दिन या अभियान तक सीमित न रहे, बल्कि लगातार और नियमित रूप से चलती रहे.
अपने पोस्ट में फडणवीस ने पुणे प्रशासन के काम करने के तरीके की खास सराहना करते हुए इसे ‘पुणेरी’ अंदाज से जोड़ा. बातचीत के हल्के-फुल्के लहजे को आगे बढ़ाते हुए उन्होंने यह चुटकी भी ली कि अगर आने वाले समय में उनके नाम का कोई अवैध होर्डिंग कहीं लगता है, तो कार्रवाई या पुरस्कार पाने वालों की सूची में उनका नाम भी दर्ज किया जाए.
मुख्यमंत्री की इस सराहना पर पुणे महानगरपालिका के आधिकारिक X हैंडल PMC Care ने बड़े ही दिलचस्प अंदाज में प्रतिक्रिया दी. पुणे मनपा ने लिखा कि मुख्यमंत्री की तारीफ के बाद एक पल के लिए फ्लेक्स लगाने का मन तो हुआ, लेकिन प्रशासन ने उस मोह को रोक लिया और ऐसा नहीं किया. इस एक लाइन के जवाब ने सोशल मीडिया यूजर्स का ध्यान खींच लिया.
पुणे मनपा के इसी पोस्ट को रीपोस्ट करते हुए नागपुर महानगरपालिका ने भी पीछे न रहते हुए मराठी में मजेदार जवाब दिया. नागपुर मनपा ने लिखा कि फ्लेक्स लगाने का मोह छोड़ देना अच्छी बात है, लेकिन मुख्यमंत्री की शुभकामनाएं देखने के लिए पुणे टीम 7 दिसंबर को नागपुर जरूर आए, जहां नागपुरकर सभी के स्वागत के लिए तैयार हैं.
इस न्योते के पीछे एक खास वजह है. दरअसल, 7 दिसंबर से नागपुर में राज्य विधानमंडल का शीतकालीन अधिवेशन शुरू होने जा रहा है. अधिवेशन के दौरान राजनीतिक सरगर्मी बढ़ने के साथ शहर में होर्डिंग और बैनर लगने की आशंका रहती है. इसी को देखते हुए मुख्यमंत्री ने नागपुर प्रशासन को पहले से जागरूकता अभियान चलाने और यह पक्का करने को कहा था कि शहर अवैध होर्डिंग से खराब न दिखे.
अपने संदेश के आखिर में देवेंद्र फडणवीस ने नेताओं और कार्यकर्ताओं को भी सीधा संदेश दिया. उन्होंने कहा कि जनप्रतिनिधि हों या कार्यकर्ता, उनकी मौजूदगी सड़कों और चौराहों पर लगे अवैध होर्डिंग के बजाय सीधे जनता के बीच होनी चाहिए. फिलहाल, अवैध होर्डिंग हटाने की गंभीर प्रशासनिक कवायद के बीच पुणे और नागपुर महानगरपालिका की यह सोशल मीडिया जुगलबंदी लोगों के बीच चर्चा का विषय बनी हुई है. एक तरफ शहर को साफ-सुथरा रखने की चुनौती है और दूसरी तरफ दोनों निकायों की इस हल्की-फुल्की नोकझोंक ने इस मुहिम में नया रंग भर दिया है.

title: ‘Compassion & Dignity Are Inherent in the Character of Lord Ram’: Mohan Bhagwat Urges All To Rise Above Ego For Public Welfare
description: “What else, truly, distinguishes a human from an animal? Biologically, a human is also an animal – sharing the same basic instincts. Yet, there exists something distinct, a special quality, which is compassion,” RSS chief Mohan Bhagwat said.
author: Ankita Paul
content:
‘Compassion & Dignity Are Inherent in the Character of Lord Ram’: Mohan Bhagwat Urges All To Rise Above Ego For Public Welfare
“What else, truly, distinguishes a human from an animal? Biologically, a human is also an animal – sharing the same basic instincts. Yet, there exists something distinct, a special quality, which is compassion,” RSS chief Mohan Bhagwat said.
- India News
- 5 min read
New Delhi: Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh (RSS) chief Mohan Bhagwat on Friday underlined the enduring relevance of Lord Ram’s compassion, dignity and sense of public welfare, stating that these qualities form the essence of his character and offer a guiding ideal for contemporary society.
Speaking at the launch of the book Karunanayak Ram by Nobel Peace Prize laureate Kailash Satyarthi, Bhagwat said compassion is an innate human impulse that moves one to alleviate another’s suffering.
“Compassion, dignity and the spirit of public welfare are inherent in the character of Lord Ram. The fundamental difference between Ram and Ravan was that Ravana remained confined to the ego of ‘I’ and ‘mine’, whereas Ram’s life represents the ideal of compassion and the practice of Dharma,” he observed.
He elaborated that ego prevents individuals from recognising the deeper interconnectedness of all beings.
Advertisement
“Until we rise above this attachment, we cannot experience the eternal truth that we are all interconnected at our core,” he said.
Compassion, he added, is not a special virtue but a natural expression of humanity: “It manifests when another person’s suffering becomes our own, and we act, to the best of our ability, to alleviate it. Merely expressing sympathy is not compassion; compassion inspires us to serve and work for the welfare of all.”
Advertisement
Bhagwat stressed that true faith in Ram requires following his ideals rather than mere belief. Many of the problems confronting the country and the world today, he noted, arise from the insistence on ‘I’ and ‘mine’ and the absence of compassion. “What else, truly, distinguishes a human from an animal? Biologically, a human is also an animal – sharing the same basic instincts. Yet, there exists something distinct, a special quality, which is compassion,” he said.
In this context, he called for the globalisation of compassion. “Only when we rise above our limited self-interest and develop a sense of belonging towards the entire creation can we truly move towards humanity and global welfare,” the RSS chief said.
Reflecting on the nature of Dharma, Bhagwat remarked that people often revere figures only after witnessing miracles, even though many great souls have lived without performing any.
“In reality, what a person ends up doing is often a matter of destiny – one acts according to the circumstances one is placed in,” he said.
The book Karunanayak Ram presents Lord Ram’s personality, life philosophy and ideals in the broader framework of compassion, human sensitivity, social justice and moral responsibility. Author Kailash Satyarthi said the central idea of the work is that compassion is an active moral force capable of bringing positive change in individuals, society and systems of governance. “For me, compassion is not merely an emotion, but a force that arises when we regard another person’s suffering as our own and inspires us to take action to alleviate it,” he noted, adding that the book examines this dimension of Ram’s life at four levels – family, society, systems and the self.
Princess Sonam Dechan Wangchuk of Bhutan, who attended as Guest of Honour, expressed pride that Satyarthi had described Bhutan as a good example of Ram Rajya. She also appreciated the growing interest among young people in understanding Lord Ram’s ideals.
Union Minister for Culture and Tourism Gajendra Singh Shekhawat, the Chief Guest at the event, described the title Karunanayak Ram as a profound philosophical expression.
“Power becomes meaningful only when it is inspired by compassion. The character of Rama presents an ideal synthesis of duty and sensitivity. Rama is an inspiration for India’s culture, ideals and public life, and a symbol of the collective consciousness that connects individuals and society. To understand Rama is to understand India,” he said.
He further observed that compassion is a transformative force and that even taking up a single thread of Ram’s character – his leadership, fearlessness, conduct as a son or the dignity he upheld in relationships – can open infinite dimensions of his personality.

title: NEET UG Paper Leak Case: Dhananjay Lokhande Seeks Bail, Rouse Avenue Court Seeks CBI's Response
description: Dhananjay Lokhande, an accused in the NEET-UG 2026 paper leak case, has sought bail. The Rouse Avenue court has issued notice to the CBI seeking its response.
author: Asian News International
content:
NEET UG Paper Leak Case: Dhananjay Lokhande Seeks Bail, Rouse Avenue Court Seeks CBI's Response
In the NEET-UG 2026 paper leak case, accused Dhananjay Lokhande has moved a bail application before the Rouse Avenue court. The court has sought the CBI's response and listed the matter for arguments in the first week of December.
- India News
- 3 min read
New Delhi: The Rouse Avenue court on Friday sought a response from the Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) on Dhananjay Lokhande. He is one of 14 accused in the NEET UG Paper leak case and has been charge-sheeted by the CBI. The Court has framed charges against all accused persons.
Special Exclusive Court Judge Ajay Gupta issued notice to the CBI and sought a reply. The matter has been listed for reply and arguements in the first week of December.
Lokhande has filed a bail application through advocate Vikram Singh in view of the material changes in the case as the charge sheet has been filed and charges have also been framed. The matter is at the stage of recording of Prosecution evidence.
On November 25, the court sought a reply from the Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) on the bail application of PV Kulakarni. He is one of the subject experts engaged by the National Testing Agency (NTA). He has been put on trial alongwith 13 other accused.
Advertisement
In its earlier order, the court had observed that the accused had, in one way or another, shared or distributed confidential examination material on a large scale, resulting in its circulation across the country well before the scheduled examination.
The court had said the alleged dissemination of confidential material led to the cancellation of the NEET-UG 2026 examination, causing an unnecessary loss of several crores of rupees to the public exchequer and financial as well as mental distress to lakhs of aspirants.
Advertisement
The judge had further observed that the question paper sets entrusted by the National Testing Agency (NTA) to the accused for translation, back-translation and proofreading constituted the agency’s copyright-protected intellectual property.
The NEET-UG 2026 examination was conducted on May 3, with approximately 22 lakh candidates appearing for it. The NTA cancelled the examination on May 12 following allegations of a question paper leak and subsequently held a fresh examination on June 21.
The CBI registered the case on May 12 following a complaint from the Department of Higher Education under the Union Education Ministry. The agency made its first arrests on May 13, and the investigation subsequently extended to Maharashtra, Rajasthan and Haryana.
The agency filed its main chargesheet on July 28 against 13 accused, including three subject experts associated with the NTA, two persons linked to coaching institutes and several alleged intermediaries. A supplementary chargesheet was subsequently filed against the 14th accused, Sheshrao Bajrang Suryawanshi alias Raj Suryawanshi, on October 14.
The CBI has relied on 360 witnesses, 422 documents and 43 material objects to substantiate its allegations against the accused.
The agency has invoked provisions relating to criminal conspiracy, cheating, criminal breach of trust and destruction of evidence, besides offences under the Prevention of Corruption Act and the Public Examinations (Prevention of Unfair Means) Act, 2024.
No government official or NTA office-bearer has been named as an accused in the chargesheets filed by the CBI. The agency’s case centres on the alleged involvement of subject experts and a network of private individuals in the paper leak conspiracy.

title: Pakistan Funding Row: CJP's Ashutosh Ranka Sends Rs 3 Crore Defamation Notice To Jitendra Singh
description: Cockroach Janta Party's Ashutosh Ranka has sent a defamation notice to Union Minister Jitendra Singh over alleged remarks linking him to Pakistani funding. Ranka has demanded an unconditional public apology, retraction of the claims and Rs 3 crore in damages for reputational harm.
author: Asian News International
content:
Pakistan Funding Row: CJP's Ashutosh Ranka Sends Rs 3 Crore Defamation Notice To Jitendra Singh
Cockroach Janta Party's Ashutosh Ranka has sent a defamation notice to Union Minister Jitendra Singh over alleged remarks linking him to Pakistani funding. Ranka has demanded an unconditional public apology, retraction of the claims and Rs 3 crore in damages for reputational harm.
- India News
- 3 min read
New Delhi: The legal cell of the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) has served a defamation notice to Union Minister Jitendra Singh on behalf of party co-convenor Ashutosh Ranka over his alleged remarks linking Ranka to funds received from Pakistani politicians and a purported handler.
The notice, sent by Advocate Abhik Chimni, concerns remarks allegedly made by Singh during a Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) press conference in Bengaluru on November 3, 2026.
According to the notice, Singh had stated: "Ashutosh Ranka was paid by Pakistani politicians, and also receiving funds from his handler Sania, even while Operation Sindoor was receiving funds."
Ranka has rejected the allegations, describing them as false, malicious and without factual basis. The notice states that his financial records are transparent and that all remittances received over the past two years constitute legitimate professional income, routed through regulated banking channels, declared in his Income Tax Returns (ITRs) and assessed to tax.
Advertisement
It also refers to Ranka's consulting project with Gavi, describing it as a reputed global public health organisation to which the Government of India has been a regular donor and with which it has a strong bilateral relationship.
Questioning the evidence behind Singh's remarks, the notice states: "You did not name a single Pakistani politician who is using their personal or party funds to remit money to my client. You did not state a single amount, date, transaction, account, document, or source. The allegation was deliberate while being unsubstantiated. An attempt has been made to pass these allegations off as official facts issued from a press conference. An imputation of being anti-national and committing treachery, made by a Union Minister without a single supporting particular, is not a mere careless remark, but a calculated design to malign our client's reputation."
Advertisement
Through the notice, Ranka has called upon Singh to produce the purported evidence supporting his claims, retract the statements and issue an unconditional public apology.
The notice also seeks Rs 3 crore in damages for the alleged injury to Ranka's reputation, with the stipulation that the entire amount be donated to a charitable organisation working towards primary education in India.
The CJP has said it will not accept what it described as reckless and defamatory attacks aimed at intimidating individuals engaged in community welfare and raising issues of public interest.
The notice states that Ranka will pursue appropriate remedies under civil and criminal law if Singh fails to comply with the demands.
Ranka, an alumnus of the Indian Institute of Technology (IIT) and the London School of Economics (LSE), had relinquished a consulting career with McKinsey & Company in London to return to India for grassroots public work, according to the notice.

title: Indian Navy gets final P17A frigate Vindhyagiri, equipped with BrahMos and Barak-8 missiles
description: The 6,670-tonne warship, equipped with BrahMos and Barak 8 missiles, completes the shipyard’s six-frigate programme and marks a milestone in indigenous naval construction.
author: Snehesh Alex Philip
content:
Indian Navy gets final P17A frigate Vindhyagiri, equipped with BrahMos and Barak-8 missiles
The 6,670-tonne warship, equipped with BrahMos and Barak 8 missiles, completes the shipyard’s six-frigate programme and marks a milestone in indigenous naval construction.
The Indian Navy has received delivery of Vindhyagiri, the sixth and final Advanced Guided-Missile Frigate under the P17A programme, completing a Rs 45,000-crore project ordered in 2019.
The six frigates were ordered in 2019 under a contract worth approximately Rs 45,000 crore. The construction programme was divided between two state-run defence shipyards — Garden Reach Shipbuilders & Engineers Ltd (GRSE) and Mazagon Dock Shipbuilders Ltd (MDL).
Designed by the Warship Design Bureau (WDB) and overseen by the Warship Overseeing Team (Mumbai), the P17A frigates represent a significant advancement in India's indigenous warship design. The class incorporates improvements in stealth, survivability and combat capabilities, strengthening the Navy's ability to undertake a wide range of maritime operations.
With more than 75 per cent indigenous content, Vindhyagiri has a displacement of approximately 6,670 tonnes and can attain speeds of up to 28 knots. The 149-metre-long warship is equipped with supersonic surface-to-surface missiles, medium-range surface-to-air missiles, anti-submarine warfare systems and an embarked multi-role helicopter.
Its advanced stealth features, modern sensors, network-centric combat systems and sophisticated weapon suites are designed to enhance its operational effectiveness across multiple threat environments.
The delivery on Friday marks the successful completion of GRSE's P17A frigate-building programme. It comes less than eight months after the shipyard handed over Dunagiri, the second frigate of the series.
Vindhyagiri is the 811th vessel built and delivered by GRSE and the 121st warship constructed by the shipyard. The frigates are the largest and most sophisticated guided-missile warships built by GRSE in its more than six decades as a Defence Public Sector Undertaking.
The vessel is armed with BrahMos anti-ship and land-attack cruise missiles, along with Barak-8 surface-to-air missiles, providing it with formidable offensive and defensive capabilities. Its weapon systems enable it to engage surface targets and defend against aerial threats.
The frigate is powered by a combination of diesel engines and gas turbines and features advanced active electronically scanned array (AESA) radar and modern combat management systems. It is capable of conducting anti-air, anti-surface and anti-submarine warfare operations, while its enhanced survivability features are intended to improve its resilience in combat.
The ship can accommodate 225 personnel and has comprehensive aviation facilities to support helicopter operations, extending its surveillance, reconnaissance and anti-submarine warfare capabilities.
Named after the Vindhyagiri mountain range in Karnataka, the warship carries forward the legacy of the erstwhile INS Vindhyagiri, a Leander-class frigate that served in the Indian Navy from July 8, 1981, to June 11, 2012. The earlier vessel completed 31 years of service to the nation.
The P17A frigates are the successors to the Shivalik-class stealth frigates, developed under the earlier P17 programme. The newer class incorporates more advanced design features and combat systems, reflecting the Navy's continuing push towards modernisation and greater self-reliance in defence manufacturing.
In addition to these naval platforms, the GRSE is currently engaged in the construction of 11 frontline naval platforms, comprising two ASW-SWCs, four Next Generation Offshore Patrol Vessels and five Next Generation Corvettes. In addition, the shipyard is constructing 36 other vessels, including 13 export platforms.
The completion of the P17A programme is a significant milestone in the Navy's modernisation efforts and in the country's drive to strengthen indigenous capabilities in the design and construction of advanced warships.

title: India set for 33% women lawmakers, 50% bigger Lok Sabha: Modi Cabinet clears delimitation bill
description: The proposal seeks to maintain the existing balance of representation among states while expanding the Lok Sabha, addressing concerns over delimitation and paving the way for 33 per cent women's reservation ahead of the 2029 elections
author: FP News Desk
content:
India set for 33% women lawmakers, 50% bigger Lok Sabha: Modi Cabinet clears delimitation bill
The proposal seeks to maintain the existing balance of representation among states while expanding the Lok Sabha, addressing concerns over delimitation and paving the way for 33 per cent women's reservation ahead of the 2029 elections
The Union Cabinet, chaired by Prime Minister Narendra Modi, on Friday approved a proposal to increase the number of Lok Sabha seats by 50 per cent across all states, in a big step towards reviving the government's delimitation exercise and implementing women's reservation.
The decision, as reported by news agency PTI, was taken at a Cabinet meeting at the Sewa Teerth complex in New Delhi, ahead of Parliament's special sitting scheduled to begin on November 30.
Under the proposed formula, every state would get a uniform 50 per cent increase in its existing Lok Sabha seats. This would take Uttar Pradesh's representation from 80 to 120 seats, while Tamil Nadu's strength would rise from 39 to around 58 seats.
The move is aimed at addressing concerns, particularly among southern states, that a delimitation exercise based on population could reduce their relative political representation because of their progress in population control.
What the proposed changes mean
The proposal is part of the government's broader plan to amend the delimitation framework and bring forward the implementation of 33 per cent reservation for women in the Lok Sabha and state legislative assemblies.
The government also plans to extend the freeze on changes to the inter-state allocation of Lok Sabha seats for another 25 years. This would preserve the existing balance of representation among states while allowing constituencies to be redrawn within individual states.
The proposed framework is expected to help implement the women's quota ahead of the 2029 Lok Sabha elections.
The Women's Reservation Act provides for 33 per cent reservation for women in the Lok Sabha and state assemblies. However, its implementation is linked to a delimitation exercise following a Census.
The government is now seeking to amend the existing framework to speed up the process.
Parliament to reconvene from November 30
The Cabinet decision comes days before Parliament resumes its sitting.
The Lok Sabha will reconvene on November 30, while the Rajya Sabha will meet from December 2. The sittings of both Houses may conclude on December 3, depending on government business.
In a report on Thursday, PTI said the special sitting had been convened amid indications that the government could bring back the constitutional amendment linking women's reservation with delimitation.
PTI also reported that the Union Cabinet was scheduled to meet on Friday and was likely to discuss the proposed changes.
Parliamentary Affairs Minister Kiren Rijiju had said the government had requested the Lok Sabha Speaker and the Rajya Sabha Chairman to reconvene the Houses to transact 'essential government business'.
The proposed constitutional amendment will need a special majority in Parliament, requiring the support of at least two-thirds of members present and voting in each House.
Why the proposal matters
The government had attempted to push through the delimitation-linked constitutional amendment earlier this year, but the legislation failed to secure the required majority in the Lok Sabha in April.
The Opposition had raised concerns over linking women's reservation with delimitation, arguing that states which had successfully controlled population growth could be disadvantaged in the redistribution of parliamentary seats.
Southern states, particularly Tamil Nadu and Kerala, had warned that using population figures to determine representation could shift the balance of political power towards more populous northern states.
The proposed uniform 50 per cent increase is intended to address some of these concerns by ensuring that every state gets the same percentage increase in its existing representation.
However, the government will still need to secure the support of opposition parties and regional players to pass the constitutional amendment when Parliament meets next week.

title: Gujarat ATS arrests suspected Jaish-e-Mohammed operative in Vadodara, seizes AK-47 and 23 cartridges
description: Acting on specific intelligence inputs, Gujarat ATS stopped a vehicle in Vadodara and recovered an AK-47 rifle and 23 rounds of live ammunition
author: FP News Desk
content:
Gujarat ATS arrests suspected Jaish-e-Mohammed operative in Vadodara, seizes AK-47 and 23 cartridges
Acting on specific intelligence inputs, Gujarat ATS stopped a vehicle in Vadodara and recovered an AK-47 rifle and 23 rounds of live ammunition
The Gujarat Anti-Terrorism Squad (ATS) has arrested a man named Md Saharul Islam Assam, suspected of having links with Pakistan-based terror outfit Jaish-e-Mohammed (JeM) in Vadodara district. An AK-47 rifle and 23 live cartridges were recovered during the operation, as per officials cited by news agency ANI.
The suspect was intercepted near Jarod bus stand in Vadodara on Friday following specific intelligence inputs. The ATS team stopped the vehicle he was travelling in and searched it, recovering the rifle and ammunition.
Acting on a tip-off, Gujarat ATS personnel set up an operation near Jarod bus stand, which falls under the jurisdiction of Jarod police station in Vadodara district.
Probe underway to trace weapon's origin
Following the arrest, investigators began questioning the accused to determine where the AK-47 came from and who was supposed to receive it.
The ATS is also examining whether other individuals were involved in procuring or transporting the weapon. Investigators are looking into the nature of the suspect's alleged links with Jaish-e-Mohammed and whether the seizure points to a wider network.
However, officials have not yet disclosed whether the weapon was being transported for delivery to another person or what its intended use may have been.
Further details are expected as the investigation progresses.

title: Gavai writes to President, flags community bias in judicial appointments
description: Former Chief Justice of India B R Gavai has questioned recent Collegium recommendations, urging President Droupadi Murmu to uphold diversity, inclusivity, and merit
author: Bhavini Mishra
content:
Gavai writes to President, flags community bias in judicial appointments
Former Chief Justice of India B R Gavai has questioned recent Collegium recommendations, urging President Droupadi Murmu to uphold diversity, inclusivity, and merit
Listen to This Article
Justice B R Gavai, the first Buddhist and second Dalit to head the Indian judiciary, on Friday alleged discrimination against marginalised communities in the appointment and transfer of judges to the higher courts as he urged President Droupadi Murmu to uphold “diversity, inclusivity and merit”. 
"Candidates belonging to one particular section of the society are being favoured for recommendation/elevation to the exclusion of everyone else including marginalised communities including scheduled castes, tribes, other backward classes, minorities, women and even persons from forward sections of the society who are not from a particular community," the former Chief Justice of India (CJI) said without naming that section.
In a three-page letter to Murmu, who is India’s first tribal head of state, Justice Gavai also questioned the functioning of the Supreme Court collegium, alleging that its recent recommendations appeared to favour members of a particular community at the expense of candidates from marginalised backgrounds.
While he did not identify the community, the former CJI said a group accounting for less than 5 per cent of the country's population now constitutes more than 40 per cent of the Supreme Court's strength, with its representation having increased substantially in recent years.
Justice Gavai urged the President to "acknowledge the issue at hand and intervene in the matter" to ensure that all are reminded of the constitutional duty of equal representation in the higher judiciary.
Also Read
Citing Article 124(2) of the Constitution, Justice Gavai said the primacy accorded to collegium recommendations did not absolve the President of constitutional responsibilities. He maintained that the executive remained an equal stakeholder in the appointment and transfer of judges to constitutional courts. Article 124(2) governs the appointment, tenure, resignation, and removal of judges of the Supreme Court of India.
The former CJI cited government data to say that out of 715 high court judges appointed since 2018, only 22 belonged to Scheduled Castes (SCs), 16 to Scheduled Tribes (STs), 89 to Other Backward Classes (OBCs) and 37 to minorities.
Roughly three of every four judges of constitutional courts came from the general category, he added.
"For appointments between January 2021 and January 2026, the reported share of the forward communities is close to 80 per cent," he said, adding that OBCs, perhaps 40 to 50 per cent of the total population, have received under 14 per cent share in higher judiciary.
Copies of the letter, seen by Business Standard, were also sent to Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Union Minister of State (independent charge) for Law and Justice Arjun Ram Meghwal.

title: PM Surya Ghar nears 7 million homes as solar rooftop adoption gathers pace
description: PM Surya Ghar: The rooftop solar scheme has covered 6.91 million households and disbursed ₹37,989 crore in subsidies, with just over three million households remaining to meet its target
author: Unis Ahmad Dar
content:
PM Surya Ghar nears 7 million homes as solar rooftop adoption gathers pace
The rooftop solar scheme has covered 6.91 million households and disbursed ₹37,989 crore in subsidies, with just over three million households remaining to meet its target
Listen to This Article
The Centre's flagship rooftop solar scheme, PM Surya Ghar: Muft Bijli Yojana, is nearing the seven-million-household milestone, with 6.91 million households covered as of November 26, according to the latest data cited by the Ministry of New and Renewable Energy (MNRE).
The scheme has disbursed ₹37,989 crore in subsidies and added 20.2 gigawatts (GW) of rooftop solar capacity. With 3.09 million households still to be covered, the government has to accelerate installations to meet its March 2027 target.
Under the PM Surya Ghar scheme, residential consumers can receive central financial assistance of up to ₹78,000 for rooftop solar systems of up to 3 kilowatts (kW). The programme aims to reduce household electricity bills while expanding India's renewable energy capacity.
Scheme is on track
Launched in February 2024 with an outlay of ₹75,021 crore, Surya Ghar aims to cover 10 million households by March 2027. Officials quoted by the Hindustan Times said the scheme is on track and gaining momentum with the help of a recently launched QR-based tool, meant to simplify installation for users. 
Also Read
The tool has recorded 4,57,561 scans in the three months since its launch on August 20. Of these, 98,110 users generated customised solar plans, while 46,369 contacted empanelled vendors, Moneycontrol reported, citing government data released on Thursday.
The tool allows households to generate customised rooftop solar plans, including estimates of installation costs, system capacity, payback periods and potential electricity savings.
At the Bharat Renewable Energy (BRE) Summit and Expo 2026 in Delhi on November 2, Prime Minister Narendra Modi said the scheme was adding nearly 1 lakh new households every six days. He also said it had reduced electricity bills by around 76 per cent.
State-wise installation trends
The national figures mask significant differences in implementation across states.
According to Solentra's state-wise PM Surya Ghar dashboard, based on data from the National Portal for Rooftop Solar, Uttar Pradesh led with around 9.89 lakh installations as of November 27. Gujarat followed with 9.56 lakh and Maharashtra with 9.43 lakh. Together, the three states accounted for nearly half of the installations recorded in the dashboard.
Kerala, Madhya Pradesh and Tamil Nadu reported relatively high application-to-installation conversion rates of 77.6 per cent, 75.5 per cent and 82.6 per cent, respectively.
Bihar and West Bengal, however, recorded conversion rates of just 17.6 per cent and 15.2 per cent. Delhi's rate stood at 22.1 per cent.
The government estimates that installations across 10 million households could generate around 1,000 billion units of renewable electricity over their lifetime and reduce carbon dioxide equivalent emissions by 720 million tonnes over 25 years.

title: India ranks 40th in AI-Human Skills Synergy Index: Coursera report
description: AI micro-credential enrolments in India rose 181 per cent year-on-year, but growth in critical thinking, problem-solving and innovation learning trailed global rates, says Coursera
author: Our Bureau
content:
India ranks 40th in AI-Human Skills Synergy Index: Coursera report
AI micro-credential enrolments in India rose 181 per cent year-on-year, but growth in critical thinking, problem-solving and innovation learning trailed global rates, says Coursera
Listen to This Article
India ranked 40th globally and 12th in the Asia-Pacific region in the inaugural AI-Human Skills Synergy Index, highlighting a gap between the country’s rapid adoption of artificial intelligence (AI) learning and the development of human skills needed to apply the technology effectively, according to Coursera’s Global Skills Report 2026.
While AI micro-credential enrolments in India grew 181 per cent year-on-year (Y-o-Y), significantly ahead of the global growth of 122 per cent, the country lagged global growth rates in enrolments for critical thinking, complex problem-solving and innovation.
Overall AI course enrolments in India rose 57 per cent Y-o-Y.
The index, introduced in the eighth edition of Coursera’s Global Skills Report, ranks 98 countries on how effectively learners are developing AI and human skills together, while also taking into account each country’s broader AI readiness. It draws on a subset of learning data from over 300 million Coursera and Udemy learners and incorporates Oxford Insights’ Government AI Readiness Index.
Critical thinking enrolments in India grew 65 per cent Y-o-Y, compared with 107 per cent globally. Similarly, complex problem-solving enrolments rose 55 per cent, against 126 per cent globally, while innovation-related enrolments grew 62 per cent, compared with 74 per cent globally.
Also Read
“India has the scale and ambition to become a global hub for AI talent, building capabilities that serve both our economy and the world,” said Ashutosh Gupta, managing director, India and Asia-Pacific, Coursera.
“India leads the world in AI learning on Coursera. Building on this momentum means deepening specialist and domain-specific AI expertise while strengthening the human skills that give our workforce a competitive edge. Investing in both will be essential to turning AI adoption into productivity and growth,” he added.
The report also pointed to a shift towards more specialised and applied AI learning in India. Learners across Coursera and Udemy are enrolling in generative AI (GenAI) courses at a rate of 12 enrolments per minute, double the six enrolments per minute recorded in 2025.
AI security emerged as a fast-growing area, with enrolments rising 296 per cent, followed by agentic workflows at 238 per cent and GenAI at 125 per cent. Other areas gaining traction include AI and machine learning foundations, large language model (LLM) applications and modelling, and prompting and AI interaction.
The report found that Indian learners are increasingly combining AI capabilities with human skills such as communication, presentation and innovation. For instance, learners are pairing prompting and AI interaction with communication skills to improve instructions and evaluate AI-generated content. Similarly, AI workflow integration and orchestration are being combined with innovation and ideation skills to develop practical applications.
The need to bridge the gap between AI and human skills assumes significance given the scale of workforce transformation expected in India. According to EY, GenAI could transform 38 million jobs in India by 2030, while Bain & Company has projected an AI talent shortfall of one million people by 2027, the Coursera report highlighted.
The Coursera report recommended that businesses, educational institutions and governments align learning programmes with specific job roles and workflows, and assess AI and human capabilities together to prepare the workforce for changing employment requirements.
The AI-Human Skills Synergy Index assigns a 60 per cent weightage to learning behaviour and 40 per cent to government AI readiness. The learning component assesses proficiency, the proportion of learners developing both AI and human skills, and the breadth of skills being acquired.

title: Airline cancels Delhi-Bengaluru flight; passenger spends  ₹48,719 on new ticket, court orders  ₹66,491 compensation
description: According to the complaint, the passenger booked a Delhi-Bengaluru flight on November 4, 2025, for travel on December 5, paying  ₹7,497 for the ticket.
author: Kanishka Singharia
content:
A West Bengal Consumer Commission has directed an airline to pay ₹56,491.78, along with 9% annual interest, to a passenger after cancelling her Delhi-Bengaluru flight without providing an adequate explanation for the decision. The passenger had to arrange another flight at a higher cost and spend two days at a hotel in Gurugram. The commission also ordered the airline to pay ₹10,000 towards litigation expenses, according to a report by Indian Express. The bench, comprising President Shivarama K and members Suma Anil Kumar and Rekha Sayannavar, held that the airline could not avoid responsibility as it had failed to explain the operational difficulties that led to the cancellation. Observing that “the unforeseen operational exigencies have not been explained”, the commission concluded that the airline was guilty of deficiency in service. In its November 19 order, the commission said, “It is not explained as to what kind of unforeseen operational exigencies it has faced. Therefore, mere saying that, because of unforeseen operational exigencies, it has affected the travel and theflight did not take off is not sufficient”. According to the complaint, the passenger booked a Delhi-Bengaluru flight on November 4, 2025, for travel on December 5, paying ₹7,497 for the ticket, Indian Express reported. The complainant asserted that the flight was cancelled without prior notice or alternative arrangements. She also claimed that the crew did not provide any assistance to help her reach her destination by another mode of transport. The cancellation disrupted her doctor's appointment and also resulted in a financial loss of ₹50,000. She also had to stay in Gurugram, Haryana, for two days before undertaking her return journey. The passenger said she stayed at a hotel from December 5 to December 6 and paid ₹15,269 for the accommodation. She later booked another flight for December 7, 2025, and paid ₹48,719 for the replacement ticket. After incurring these losses, she approached the consumer commission seeking compensation. The airline claimed that the flight was cancelled on December 5, 2025, due to operational reasons and that the passengers had been informed immediately. It further alleged that the passenger had refused to travel on the alternative flight offered by the airline and that the full ticket amount had been refunded, the report added. The airline also argued that the circumstances leading to the cancellation were unforeseen and beyond its control. The commission observed that the passenger's flight ticket showed that she had travelled on another flight on December 7, 2025. It also noted that the hotel invoice submitted by her covered accommodation expenses alone. After examining the documents, the bench held that she was entitled to reimbursement of the additional expenses incurred because of the cancellation. title: Jio partners with WhatsApp for international travel eSIMs: Will Indian travellers benefit? What we know so far
description: WhatsApp is partnering with Reliance Jio and other telecom operators to let users buy international travel eSIMs within the app. But will Indian travellers get access to the service, and could it be cheaper than existing roaming plans?
author: Trisha Bhattacharya
content:
WhatsApp is planning to make international travel a little easier with a new feature that will let users buy travel eSIM plans directly through the app. The Meta-owned platform has partnered with several telecom operators and eSIM providers for this service, including India's Reliance Jio. Announced on November 26, the feature will help people travelling abroad get mobile internet without having to buy a local SIM card after landing or pay for expensive international roaming plans. Users will be able to buy and install a travel eSIM in just a few steps without leaving WhatsApp. They can also continue using their existing WhatsApp number while getting internet through the travel eSIM. Jio's involvement has raised interest among Indian travellers. However, WhatsApp has not confirmed whether India will be among the first countries to get the feature. The company says the service will start rolling out in select countries soon. It has not shared a launch date, the list of countries or the prices of the plans yet. WhatsApp has named Reliance Jio, Smart Axiata, Smart Communications and Verizon among its partners for the new service. It is also working with other telecom operators and eSIM providers to make the feature available in more countries. Jio's involvement is important for Indian users who often travel abroad. However, this does not mean that Indian customers will get access to the feature as soon as it launches. WhatsApp has not confirmed whether India will be part of the first phase. It has also not explained which partners will provide network coverage in different countries. There are a few other details that remain unknown. The company has not shared how much the plans will cost, how much data users will get or how long each plan will remain active. Once the feature is available, users will be able to find the option directly inside WhatsApp. The idea is to make it easier for people to get mobile internet when they travel to another country. Currently, travellers have a few options. They can buy a local SIM card at the airport, activate an international roaming pack with their regular operator or purchase an eSIM through another app or website. WhatsApp wants to bring this entire process into its app. This means users will be able to buy and install a travel data plan without having to visit a separate website or download another app. An eSIM is simply a digital SIM card. It allows a compatible smartphone to connect to a mobile network without inserting a physical SIM card. Depending on the phone, users can also keep their regular SIM active while using an eSIM. One of the biggest advantages is that travellers will not have to change their WhatsApp number. They can continue using their existing account for messages and calls while the travel eSIM provides mobile internet. It could also reduce the need to depend on public Wi-Fi at airports, hotels and cafes. Jio's partnership with WhatsApp has raised hopes that Indian travellers could also get access to the service. However, there are still some important questions. The first is availability. WhatsApp has not confirmed whether Indian users will be able to buy travel eSIMs when the feature first launches. The second is pricing. The new service could give travellers another option besides international roaming packs and third-party eSIM services. However, it is too early to say whether it will actually be cheaper. That will depend on how much WhatsApp charges, how much data each plan offers and how long the plan remains active. Users will also need a smartphone that supports eSIM technology to use the service. For now, Indian travellers will have to wait for WhatsApp to share more details about the launch and the countries covered by its partners. The announcement is another step in WhatsApp's effort to offer more services beyond messaging and calling. The company pointed out that people already use WhatsApp while travelling to receive boarding passes, arrange airport pick-ups and let family members know when they reach their destination. Having mobile internet as soon as they land could make these things easier. WhatsApp head Kunal Shah also spoke about the new feature in a post on X. He described it as an early step towards offering eSIM services and invited more telecom operators and eSIM providers to join the initiative. For now, the feature is still in its early stages. Whether it becomes a cheaper option for Indian travellers will depend on its availability and pricing once WhatsApp shares more details. title: Who is Raul John Aju? India’s ‘AI Kid’ who made his first video at 9 and clicked a selfie with Vladimir Putin
description: Kerala-born AI entrepreneur Raul John Aju, popularly known as India's 'AI Kid', recently met Russian President Vladimir Putin at the AI Journey 2026 conference in Moscow. From making his first video at nine to developing a humanoid robot at 12 and founding an AI company.
author: Anjali Thakur
content:
Indian AI innovator Raul John Aju recently shared a photograph with Russian President Vladimir Putin on Instagram after meeting him at the AI Journey 2026 conference in Moscow. Popularly known as the 'AI Kid of India', the young entrepreneur reflected on his journey, recalling how he started making videos at the age of nine. Sharing a selfie with Putin, Aju spoke about how his journey in technology and content creation had taken him to an experience he had never imagined as a child. “From making my first video in a bathroom at 9 to taking a selfie with President Putin, never in my wildest dreams did I think life would take me here,” he wrote. While meeting the Russian president was a significant moment, Aju also highlighted the personal growth and lessons he had gained along the way. “More than anything I’ve achieved, I’m grateful for the person this journey has helped me become.” Reflecting on his experience at the Moscow conference, the young innovator spoke about meeting professionals working in artificial intelligence and how their knowledge made him realise there was still much more to learn. “Meeting some incredible people at AI Journey (way smarter than me) made me realise how much more I have to learn.” Aju also acknowledged the people who supported him throughout his journey, expressing gratitude to the conference organisers, his parents, friends and others who helped him pursue his ambitions. “And to everyone who’s been part of this journey, thank you for making a little kid’s dreams come true.” Concluding his Instagram post, the young entrepreneur said that despite his achievements and experiences, he continues to approach life with the curiosity that first sparked his interest in technology. “Still a curious kid, just with a few more stories to tell.” He also shared a photograph of himself posing alongside Vladimir Putin, offering his followers a glimpse of the meeting in Moscow. Originally from Kerala, Raul John Aju is a teenage AI entrepreneur, developer and educator who is popularly known as the 'AI Kid of India'. His interest in technology reportedly began at a young age. At just 12, he developed his first humanoid robot, marking an early milestone in his journey as a technology enthusiast and innovator. Aju later ventured into entrepreneurship by founding AI Realm Technologies. The venture marked his entry into the business world at the age of 16. His journey from experimenting with content creation as a nine-year-old to developing technology and building an AI venture has made him a notable young name in India's artificial intelligence space. Anjali Thakur is a Senior Assistant Editor with Mint, reporting on trending news, entertainment and health, with a focus on stories driving digital conversations. Her work involves spotting early signals across news cycles and social media, sharpening stories for SEO and Google Discover, and mentoring young editors in digital-first newsroom practices. She is known for turning fast-moving developments—whether news-driven or culture-led—into clear, tightly edited journalism without compromising editorial rigour.

title: Delhi makes Aadhaar mandatory for Lakhpati Bitiya scheme beneficiaries
description: Delhi's government has made Aadhaar mandatory for beneficiaries of the Lakhpati Bitiya Scheme to access financial assistance. Applicants who do not have an Aadhaar number can use alternative identity documents during enrollment. The scheme provides financial support stages including Rs 11,000 at birth and payments for education. Assistance for higher education also includes Rs 20,000 for three-year courses and Rs 25,000 for four-year courses.
author: ET Online
content:
Under a November 19 notification issued by the Women and Child Development Department, eligible applicants must furnish proof of an Aadhaar number or undergo Aadhaar authentication to access the scheme. Girls who do not have an Aadhaar number or have not enrolled for one must apply for enrolment before registering.
However, applicants awaiting their Aadhaar numbers can submit their enrolment identification slip along with any one of several alternative documents, including a bank or post office passbook bearing a photograph, PAN card, passport, ration card, voter ID, MGNREGA card or driving licence.
The department's district offices will facilitate Aadhaar enrolment for beneficiaries who have not registered. Where no enrolment centre is available locally, the department will arrange facilities at convenient locations in coordination with the Unique Identification Authority of India (UIDAI).
The notification also provides for alternative authentication arrangements if biometric verification fails because of poor fingerprint quality or other reasons.
The Lakhpati Bitiya Scheme aims to strengthen the social and financial security of girl children and encourage them to continue their education. Under the scheme, financial assistance is invested in the name of the beneficiary at different stages of her life and education, with the accumulated amount and returns paid out upon maturity after the lock-in period.
The assistance includes Rs 11,000 at birth and Rs 5,000 each on admission to Classes I, VI, IX, XI and XII. Beneficiaries pursuing higher education receive Rs 20,000 for a three-year graduation course and Rs 25,000 for a four-year course, disbursed in instalments.
The final maturity amount depends on the stage at which the girl child enters and registers under the scheme, PTI reported.

title: India announces $500,000 financial grant to IORA for capacity building
description: The Indian Ocean Rim Association (IORA), at an India-hosted ministerial conclave in New Delhi, also voiced  concern  over the undermining of maritime safety and security of vessels and seafarers and called for ensuring their safety.
author: PTI
content:
New Delhi: A grouping of Indian Ocean littoral countries on Friday vowed to work towards peace and prosperity in the region while underlining the need for ensuring freedom of navigation, unimpeded commerce and peaceful settlement of disputes amid increasing concerns over China's increasingly assertive behaviour in strategic maritime zones.
The Indian Ocean Rim Association (IORA), at an India-hosted ministerial conclave in New Delhi, also voiced "concern" over the undermining of maritime safety and security of vessels and seafarers and called for ensuring their safety.
Reaffirming its commitment to strengthen IORA, India announced a grant of USD 500,000 towards the grouping's institutional and financial capacity-building, according to the Ministry of External Affairs (MEA).
India hosted the conclave in New Delhi in its capacity as the current chair of the IORA that comprises 23 nations including Australia, Indonesia, South Africa, Kenya, Tanzania, Mozambique, Somalia, Oman, Yemen, Bangladesh, Malaysia and Thailand. The US, the European Union and several other dialogue partners of the IORA also joined the gathering.
Chairing the conclave, External Affairs Minister S Jaishankar said the Indian Ocean is central to global trade, energy security and connectivity and all littoral states in the region must jointly work towards its safety.
In a communique, the grouping resolved to strengthen IORA in view of rapid pace of geopolitical developments and the challenges facing the international rules-based order.
"We reaffirm our commitment to maintaining the Indian Ocean as a region of peace, stability and prosperity, and to upholding applicable international law, including applicable international law of the sea to ensure freedom of navigation and overflight, unimpeded commerce, peaceful settlement of disputes and other lawful uses of the sea," the Delhi Communique said.
The IORA said it is steadfast in its commitment to the vision of a peaceful, stable and prosperous Indian Ocean and to the fundamental principles of the grouping's charter, namely, sovereign equality, territorial integrity, political independence, non-interference in internal affairs, peaceful co-existence, and mutual benefit.
The grouping said it will work towards sustained growth and balanced development of the region through promoting trade and investment, the freer flow of goods, services, technology and people.
"We reaffirm the urgency of strengthening IORA, recognising the rapid pace of recent geopolitical developments and the challenges facing multilateralism and the international rules-based order, as well as the pressing challenge of climate change for the region," according to the communique.
"As a pivotal multilateral platform, IORA remains central to fostering sustained growth and balanced regional development. In this context, we underscore the urgent need for enhancing the availability of financial resources for IORA, and to ensure their efficient, effective and transparent utilisation to support the long-term sustainability of IORA," it added.
The grouping expressed concern over the undermining of maritime safety and security of vessels and seafarers and called for ensuring their safety and security.
The remarks came against the backdrop of mounting global concerns over attacks on merchant shipping in West Asia as well as in the Black Sea in which several Indian sailors were killed.
The MEA said the ministers exchanged views on regional and global developments, with a focus on the Indian Ocean Region.
"They discussed ways to strengthen cooperation among IORA member states in areas of mutual interest. Ministers also deliberated on IORA's forthcoming Action Plan for 2028-2032 and engaged with dialogue Partners on potential areas of cooperation," it said.
The IORA has been focusing on boosting the blue economy through a common vision for balanced economic development in the Indian Ocean region besides working on maritime security.
The IORA's foundation charter sets the guiding principles for it to facilitate economic cooperation, in a spirit of multilateralism, and expand understanding and mutually beneficial cooperation through a consensus-based, evolutionary and non-intrusive approach.
