'इंडियन एक्सप्रेस'च्या वृत्तानुसार, डीएमकेच्या एका नेत्याने सांगितलं की, केंद्र सरकारने पक्षाशी संपर्क साधला होता. तामिळनाडूच्या लोकसभेतील सध्याच्या 7.2 टक्के जागा कायम राहतील, अशी हमी मिळाल्यास डीएमके मतदारसंघ पुनर्रचनेच्या विधेयकाला पाठिंबा देऊ शकते.
राष्ट्रवादी काँग्रेसच्या (शरद पवार गट) नेत्या सुप्रिया सुळे यांनी यापूर्वी या विधेयकाला पाठिंबा देण्याचे संकेत दिले होते. परंतु, शुक्रवारी (27 नोव्हेंबर) त्यांनी यावर कोणतीही प्रतिक्रिया देण्यास नकार दिला. लोकसभेत या पक्षाचे 8 खासदार आहेत.
सुप्रिया सुळे यांनी गेल्या बुधवारी पत्रकारांशी बोलताना म्हटलं होतं, "विरोधकांनी यापूर्वीही अनेक मुद्द्यांना पाठिंबा दिला आहे. पहलगामचा मुद्दा, जीएसटी विधेयक आणि महिला आरक्षणाचं विधेयक यांसारख्या विषयांना आम्ही एकमताने पाठिंबा दिला होता. देशाच्या हिताच्या मुद्द्यांवर चर्चा झाली पाहिजे."
लोकसभेमध्ये हे विधेयक मंजूर झालं, तर ते राज्यसभेत मांडलं जाण्याची शक्यता आहे. राज्यसभेत एकूण 245 सदस्य असून, त्यापैकी 142 खासदार एनडीएचे आहेत. घटनादुरुस्ती विधेयक मंजूर होण्यासाठी 161 खासदारांच्या पाठिंब्याची गरज आहे. त्यामुळे सत्ताधारी आघाडीला आणखी 19 खासदारांच्या पाठिंब्याची गरज आहे.
राज्यसभेत डीएमकेचे 8, तर राष्ट्रवादी काँग्रेसचा (शरद पवार गट) 1 खासदार आहे. प्रादेशिक पक्षांसह एनडीएबाहेरील पक्षांचे सुमारे 100 खासदार आहेत. या खासदारांचा पाठिंबा मिळवून आवश्यक संख्याबळ जमवण्यात यश येईल, असा भाजपला विश्वास आहे.
स्टॅलिन काय म्हणाले?
तामिळनाडूचे माजी मुख्यमंत्री आणि डीएमकेचे नेते एमके स्टॅलिन म्हणाले की, मतदारसंघ पुनर्रचनेचे संभाव्य परिणाम काय होऊ शकतात, याबाबत आवाज उठवणारा डीएमके हा भारतातील पहिला पक्ष होता.
त्यांनी 'एक्स'वरील पोस्टमध्ये लिहिलं की, निष्पक्ष मतदारसंघ पुनर्रचनेची मागणी करण्यासाठी देशातील प्रमुख नेत्यांना एकत्र आणणारी पहिली बैठकही चेन्नईतच झाली होती.
तामिळनाडू विधानसभेत मंजूर झालेला ठराव आणि निष्पक्ष मतदारसंघ पुनर्रचनेसाठी संयुक्त कृती समितीच्या बैठकीत मंजूर झालेल्या ठरावांनुसार आमच्या 2 स्पष्ट मागण्या होत्या-
"जर लोकसभेतील जागांची संख्या वाढवली, तर कोणत्याही परिस्थितीत तामिळनाडूचा सध्याचा 7.18 टक्के वाटा कमी होता कामा नये."
"आणि, 1971 च्या जनगणनेनुसार निश्चित केलेलं आणि राज्यांमधील लोकसभेतील प्रतिनिधित्वाचं सध्याचं प्रमाण पुढील 25 वर्षेही कायम ठेवलं पाहिजे."
स्टॅलिन यांनी लिहिलं, "डीएमके आजही या दोन्ही मागण्यांवर ठाम आहे आणि यापुढेही ठाम राहील. आमच्या भूमिकेत कोणताही बदल झालेला नाही आणि कोणत्याही प्रकारची तडजोड करण्याचा प्रश्नच उद्भवत नाही. प्रसारमाध्यमांमधून केल्या जाणाऱ्या चर्चा आणि विश्वासघात करणाऱ्यांची विधानं यामुळे आमच्या भूमिकेवर कोणताही परिणाम होणार नाही."
विरोधकांनी काय म्हटलं?
विरोधी इंडिया आघाडीच्या नेत्यांनी डीलिमिटेशन विधेयकावर तीव्र प्रतिक्रिया दिली असून सरकारला इशाराही दिला आहे.
काँग्रेस नेते जयराम रमेश म्हणाले की, संसदेचं विशेष अधिवेशन महिला आरक्षणासाठी बोलावलेलं नाही, हे आता स्पष्ट झालं आहे. कारण महिला आरक्षणाचा कायदा आधीच मंजूर झाला आहे.
जयराम रमेश यांनी 'एक्स'वरील पोस्टमध्ये म्हटलं, "लोकांचा आवाज दाबण्यासाठी मतदारसंघांची मनमानी पद्धतीने पुनर्रचना करणं, हा या विशेष अधिवेशनाचा खरा उद्देश आहे."
"मतदारसंघांच्या सीमा ठरवण्याची जबाबदारी कोणाकडे दिली जाणार आहे?" असा प्रश्न त्यांनी विचारला.
कॉकरोच जनता पार्टीचे आशुतोष रांका म्हणाले की, 30 नोव्हेंबरला होणाऱ्या संसदेच्या कामकाजाकडे संपूर्ण देशाचं लक्ष असेल.
समाजवादी पक्षाचे अध्यक्ष अखिलेश यादव यांनी डीलिमिटेशन विधेयकाला मोदी सरकारची सर्वात मोठी चूक म्हटलं आहे.
त्यांनी 'एक्स'वर लिहिलं, "डीलिमिटेशन ही भाजपच्या राजकारणातील सर्वात मोठी चूक ठरेल."
राष्ट्रीय जनता दलाचे खासदार आणि राष्ट्रीय प्रवक्ते मनोज झा यांनी डीलिमिटेशनच्या नावाखाली राजकीय पक्षपात केला जात असल्याचा आरोप केला आहे.
त्यांनी 'एक्स'वर लिहिलं, "प्रस्तावित डीलिमिटेशनची प्रक्रिया केवळ जागांची संख्या वाढवण्यापुरती मर्यादित नाही, हे स्पष्ट झालं पाहिजे. राजकीय फायद्यासाठी मतदारसंघांच्या सीमा बदलल्या जातील, ही त्याहून मोठी चिंता आहे."
"घटनात्मक तत्त्वं आणि लोकशाहीतील निष्पक्षतेचा विचार न करता राजकीय पक्षपातातून ही प्रक्रिया राबवली गेली, तर लोकशाहीतील लोकांचं प्रतिनिधित्व, केंद्र आणि राज्यांमधील समतोल आणि देशाच्या एकतेला मोठा धक्का बसू शकतो, नुकसान होऊ शकतं."
ममता बॅनर्जी गटाच्या तृणमूल काँग्रेसच्या खासदार सागरिका घोष यांनी 'एक्स'वर लिहिलं, "नरेंद्र मोदी सरकार डीलिमिटेशन विधेयक आणत आहे. या विधेयकाच्या माध्यमातून भाजपला आपल्या निवडणुकीच्या फायद्यासाठी सर्व मतदारसंघांची नव्याने आखणी करण्याची संधी देण्यासारखं आहे. मात्र, हे सर्व 'महिला शक्ती' आणि 'महिलांना प्रतिनिधित्व देण्यासाठी' केलं जात असल्याचा दावा सरकार करत आहे."
त्यांनी लिहिलं, "मतदारसंघ पुनर्रचनेचं विधेयक म्हणजे सत्तेवर निर्लज्जपणे ताबा मिळवण्याचा प्रयत्न आहे. पण, हा प्रयत्न महिलांच्या आडून केला जात आहे. या विधेयकातून भाजपचा लोकशाहीबद्दलचा अनादर तर दिसून येतोच, पण महिलांबद्दलची तुच्छतेची आणि अपमानास्पद वागणूकही दिसते."
राजकीय विश्लेषक योगेंद्र यादव यांनी 'एक्स' वर आपला एक लेख शेअर करताना लिहिलं, "एप्रिलमध्ये भाजपचा पहिला प्रयत्न विरोधकांनी हाणून पाडला होता. आता सत्ताधारी पक्षाच्या दुसऱ्या योजनेला म्हणजेच 'प्लॅन बी'ला सामोरं जाण्याची तयारी विरोधकांना करावी लागेल. या योजनेनुसार, राज्याच्या लोकसभेतील जागांची टक्केवारी बदलली जाणार नाही. परंतु, मतदारसंघांची नव्याने अशी रचना केली जाईल की, त्याचा भाजपला दीर्घकाळ निवडणुकीत फायदा मिळत राहील."
आसाम आणि जम्मू-काश्मीरमध्ये डीलिमिटेशन केल्यानंतर सत्ताधारी पक्षाला निवडणुकीत मोठा फायदा झाल्याचं या पूर्वी दिसून आलं आहे. एखाद्या विशिष्ट पक्षाला निवडणुकीत फायदा व्हावा, यासाठी मतदारसंघांच्या सीमा जाणीवपूर्वक बदलण्याच्या प्रक्रियेला 'गेरिमँडरिंग' म्हणतात.
(बीबीसीसाठी कलेक्टिव्ह न्यूजरूमचे प्रकाशन)

title: जगातील पहिल्या सुपरमॉडेल्सपैकी एक असलेल्या वेरुश्का यांचं निधन; पाहा त्यांचे 8 गाजलेले फोटो
description: 1960 च्या दशकात फॅशनविश्वातील पहिल्या आंतरराष्ट्रीय स्टारपैकी एक बनलेल्या मॉडेल आणि कलाकार वेरुश्का यांचं वयाच्या 87 व्या वर्षी निधन झालं.
author: इयान यंग्स
content:
जगातील पहिल्या सुपरमॉडेल्सपैकी एक असलेल्या वेरुश्का यांचं निधन; पाहा त्यांचे 8 गाजलेले फोटो
  - Author, इयान यंग्स
  - Role, सांस्कृतिक प्रतिनिधी
- Published
- वाचन वेळ: 3 मिनिटे
1960 च्या दशकात फॅशनविश्वातील पहिल्या आंतरराष्ट्रीय स्टारपैकी एक बनलेल्या मॉडेल आणि कलाकार वेरुश्का यांचं वयाच्या 87 व्या वर्षी निधन झालं.
त्यांचे अनेक कल्पक आणि वेगळ्या पद्धतीने केलेले फोटोशूट्स गाजले. या फोटोशूट्समुळे 1960 आणि 70 च्या दशकात फॅशन आणि सौंदर्याच्या कल्पनांना नवीन दिशा मिळाली, त्यांच्या सीमा विस्तारण्यास मदत झाली. वेरुश्का अमेरिकेतील 'व्होग' मासिकाच्या मुखपृष्ठावर तब्बल 13 वेळा झळकल्या होत्या.
'व्होग' मासिकाने श्रद्धांजली वाहताना वेरुश्का यांचा उल्लेख "एका संपूर्ण युगावर ठसा उमटवणारी सुपरमॉडेल" असा केला.
"पहिल्या सुपरमॉडेलपैकी एक असलेल्या वेरुश्का यांनी फॅशनविश्वात परफॉर्मन्स आर्टिस्ट म्हणूनही मोठं नाव कमावलं होतं."
त्यांनी 1960 च्या दशकात गाजलेला स्विंग चित्रपट 'ब्लो अप' आणि 2006 मध्ये आलेल्या जेम्स बाँडच्या 'कॅसिनो रॉयल' या चित्रपटातही काम केलं होतं.
वेरुश्का (व्हेरा वॉन लेन्डॉर्फ) यांचा जन्म 1939 मध्ये कोनिग्सबर्ग येथील एका श्रीमंत आणि प्रतिष्ठित कुटुंबात झाला. त्यावेळी हे शहर जर्मनीत होतं. आता हे शहर रशियातील कॅलिनिनग्राड या नावाने ओळखलं जातं.
त्यांचे वडील काउंट हेनरिक वॉन लेन्डॉर्फ यांना ॲडॉल्फ हिटलरच्या हत्येचा कट रचल्याप्रकरणी 1944 मध्ये फाशी देण्यात आली होती. हा कट यशस्वी झाला नव्हता.
त्यांनी हॅम्बर्ग आणि फ्लॉरेन्स येथे कलेचं शिक्षण घेतलं. त्यानंतर मॉडेल म्हणून करिअरला सुरुवात केली आणि लवकरच त्या एक दिग्गज मॉडेल बनल्या, असं त्यांची बहीण काउंटेस कॅथरिना वॉन लेन्डॉर्फ यांनी लिहिलं आहे.
त्यांनी इव्ह सेंट लॉरेंट, कार्ल लेगरफेल्ड आणि व्हॅलेंटिनो यांसारख्या प्रसिद्ध फॅशन डिझायनर्ससोबत काम केलं.
याशिवाय, वेगळ्या धाटणीच्या फोटोशूटमध्येही त्या सहभागी झाल्या. या फोटोशूटमध्ये त्या स्वतःच्या शरीरावर चित्रं काढायच्या, वेगवेगळे प्रयोग करायच्या आणि शरीराचा वापर करून नवनवीन कलाकृती साकारायच्या.
"वेरुश्का केवळ मॉडेल नव्हत्या, तर त्या एक कलाकार आणि बंडखोर वृत्तीच्या स्त्री होत्या. त्यांच्या कलाकृतींना स्त्रीवादी विचारांवर आधारित परफॉर्मन्स कलेची सुरुवात मानलं जातं."

title: पाण्यासाठी वणवण, तरीही मराठवाड्यातले शेतकरी लाखो एकर क्षेत्रावर उसाची लागवड का करतात? – ग्राऊंड रिपोर्ट
description: मराठवाड्याला दुष्काळी भाग म्हणून ओळखलं जातं. कारण इथं पाऊस कमी पडतो. पण, याच मराठवाड्यात जास्त पाणी लागणारं उसाचं पीकही घेतलं जातं. तेही तब्बल साडेतीन लाख हेक्टर क्षेत्रावर.
author: श्रीकांत बंगाळे
content:
पाण्यासाठी वणवण, तरीही मराठवाड्यातले शेतकरी लाखो एकर क्षेत्रावर उसाची लागवड का करतात? – ग्राऊंड रिपोर्ट
  - Author, श्रीकांत बंगाळे
  - Role, बीबीसी मराठी प्रतिनिधी
- Published
- वाचन वेळ: 5 मिनिटे
"2025 चा पाऊस झालेला होता, त्याच्यात पाण्याची भरपूर क्षमता होती. त्याच्यामुळे आम्ही ऊस लावलेला होता. पहिले कापूस होता."
गेल्यावर्षी पाऊस चांगला झाल्यामुळे रणजित तिपाले यांनी अडीच एकर क्षेत्रावर उसाची लागवड केली. रणजित मराठवाड्यातल्या बीड जिल्ह्यातले शेतकरी.
याच मराठवाड्याला दुष्काळी भाग म्हणून ओळखलं जातं. कारण इथं पाऊस कमी पडतो. पण याच मराठवाड्यात जास्त पाणी लागणारं उसाचं पीकही घेतलं जातं.
2012-13 साली 2 लाख 16 हजार हेक्टर क्षेत्रावरील उसाची लागवड, 2026 मध्ये जवळपास साडेतीन लाख हेक्टरवर, म्हणजे जवळपास 9 लाख एकर क्षेत्रावर पोहचलीय. त्यामुळे पाण्याचं दुर्भिक्ष्य असूनही मराठवाड्यातले शेतकरी ऊस लागवडीकडे का वळाले? असा प्रश्न पडणं साहजिक आहे.
छत्रपती संभाजीनगर बाभुळगाव खुर्दचे शेतकरी प्रकाश चौधरी उसाला पाणी देत होते.
ते सांगायला लागले, "उसाकडं वळायचं कारण एक आहे, याला हमीभाव आहे. आपल्या जवारी, मका, यालाही हमीभाव आहेत. पण त्याचे असे कारखाने नाहीत की जाऊन माल लगेच द्यायचाय."
उसामुळे आर्थिक सुरक्षितता आणि सामाजिक प्रतिष्ठा
ऊस उत्पादकांना हमीभाव मिळावा यासाठी दरवर्षी साखर हंगाम सुरू होण्यापूर्वी केंद्र सरकारकडून उसाचा FRP म्हणजेच 'फेअर रेम्युनरेटीव्ह प्राइस' – 'रास्त आणि किफायतशीर दर' जाहीर केला जातो.
उसातून मिळणारी आर्थिक सुरक्षिततेची हमी आणि ऊसाला असणारी सामाजिक प्रतिष्ठा, या कारणांमुळे मराठवाड्यातील शेतकऱ्यांचा उसाकडे कल वाढलाय.
शेती क्षेत्राचे अभ्यासक डॉ. सोमिनाथ घोळवे यांच्या मते, "उसाचं कसं टिपरू न टिपरू विकलं जातं. हे इतर पिकांचं विकलं जातं का, तर नाही जात विकलं. हमीभाव किंवा संरक्षण इतर पिकांना मिळालं, तर शेतकरी ऑटोमॅटिक त्याच्याकडे वळताना दिसतील."
पर्यावरणतज्ज्ञ अतुल देऊळगावकर हाच मुद्दा पुढे नेत म्हणतात, "सरकारनं एक अघोषित वर्णव्यवस्था पिकांमध्ये केलेली आहे. त्यातलं ऊस हे अतिशय उच्चवर्णीय पीक आहे. त्यामुळे ते सगळ्यांना हवहवसं वाटतं. त्याचं कारण काय आहे, ऊस जर मी लावला, तर मला एक खात्री आहे, माझ्या शेतातनं तो कुणीतरी तोडून नेणार आहे आणि माझ्या बँकेच्या खात्यावर त्याचे पैसे जमा होणार आहेत. यात फार कष्ट करायची गरज नाही."
मराठवाड्यात 67 साखर कारखाने
गेल्या काही वर्षांत मराठवाड्यात अनेक साखर कारखाने सुरू झाले. त्यामुळेही शेतकऱ्यांचा ऊस लागवडीकडे कल वाढलाय.
साखर आयुक्तालयाच्या आकडेवारीनुसार, मराठवाड्यातील छत्रपती संभाजीनगर, परभणी, जालना, बीड, धाराशिव, लातूर, नांदेड आणि हिंगोली, या 8 जिल्ह्यांमध्ये तब्बल 67 साखर कारखाने आहेत. यातील 14 कारखाने बंद, तर 19 कारखाने अवसायनात निघालेत.
मराठवाड्यातल्या 67 साखर कारखान्यांपैकी, सर्वाधिक 14 साखर कारखाने धाराशिव जिल्ह्यात आहेत. मराठवाड्यातील राजकारणावर साखर कारखानदारीचा मोठा प्रभाव आहे.
सोमिनाथ घोळवे सांगतात, "उसाकडे आपल्याला एक राजकीय पीक म्हणून बघावं लागतं. जसं पश्चिम महाराष्ट्रात सहकाराच्या माध्यमातून ऊसाच्या पिकाचा विकास झाला, त्याला मूल्यसाखळी मिळत गेली. बॉर्डरवरचे जे जिल्हे होते, म्हणजे नदीच्या काठचे. जसं की गोदावरी असेल, खाली कृष्णा असेल. इथलं राजकारण हळूहळू उसावर संघटित होत होतं, सहकाराच्या माध्यमातून. त्याचा प्रभाव मराठवाड्यावर पडलेला दिसतो."
मराठवाड्यातल्या नांदेड, हिंगोली, परभणी, लातूर या 4 जिल्ह्यांमध्ये 2024-25 साली उसाखालील क्षेत्र 1 लाख 25 हजार हेक्टर होतं. 2026-27 मध्ये ते 70 हजार हेक्टरने वाढून 1 लाख 96 हजार हेक्टरवर पोहचलंय.
उसाचा भूजल पातळीवर परिणाम
पाऊस चांगला पडला, की उसाच्या लागवडीखालील क्षेत्रात वाढ होते. शेतकरी उसाला धरणं, विहिरी, बोअरचे पाणी वापरत आहेत. पण, उसासाठी भूजलाचा अधिकाधिक उपसा केला जातो आणि त्याचा भूजल पातळीवर विपरित परिणाम होतोय.
डॉ. शंकरराव नागरे हे जलतज्ज्ञ आणि मराठवाडा वैधानिक विकास मंडळाचे माजी तज्ज्ञ सदस्य आहेत.
ते सांगतात, "उसाच्या पाळ्या 10 ते 11 महिने म्हणजे जवळजवळ वर्षभर चालतात. उसाला जे आपण पाणी देतो, ते जर आपण मोजलं उभं तर सव्वा दोन मीटर पाणी होतं ते. म्हणजे जवळजवळ 8 किंवा 7 फूट पाणी उसाला लागतंय. जनरल पिकाला आपण जे पाणी घेतो ते दीड फूट लागतं. जे बारमाही पिके आहेत, त्यातल्या त्यात ऊस हा जास्त महत्त्वाचा आहे. उसाने जास्त पाणी पातळी खाली जाते."
याचं एक उदाहरण पाहायचं झालं, तर धाराशिव जिल्ह्यात 2025-26 मध्ये, ऊस लागवडीखालील क्षेत्र 54,188 हेक्टर होतं. 2026-27 मध्ये ते 79,759 हेक्टरवर पोहचलंय. याच धाराशिव जिल्ह्यात मागील 5 वर्षांच्या तुलनेत यंदाच्या सप्टेंबर महिन्यात भूजल पातळीत 8.86 मीटरने घट झाल्याचं भूजल सर्वेक्षण विभागाची आकडेवारी सांगते.
नीती आयोगाच्या अहवालानुसार, मराठवाडा आणि विदर्भात शेतीसाठी वापरल्या जाणाऱ्या एकूण पाण्यापैकी जवळपास 70 % पाणी उसाच्या पिकासाठी वापरलं जातं. यंदा पावसाच्या कमरतेचा फटका ऊसालाही बसलाय.
तरुण शेतकरी चेतन तुपे म्हणतो, "उसाला दर 10 दिवसाला 1 पाणी बसलं पाहिजे. पण, यावर्षी स्वत:ला पाणी प्यायला राहिलेलं नाहीये, तर उसाला कुठून देणार, अशी परिस्थिती झालेली आहे."
पावसाअभावी यंदा उसाच्या उत्पादनात घट होईल, अशी शक्यता शेतकरी व्यक्त करताहेत.
बीडच्या पारगाव जप्ती गावातील शेतकरी त्यांच्या शेतातील ऊस दाखवायला लागले.
गेल्यावर्षी या परिसरात पाण्याची चांगली व्यवस्था असल्यामुळे उसाला 25 कांड्या होत्या. यंदा मात्र सातच कांड्या दिसत होत्या. यंदा पाण्याअभावी उसाच्या मापावर परिणाम झाल्याचं इथले शेतकरी सांगत होते.
'उसबंदी पर्याय नाही'
उसाला प्रतिहेक्टर सरासरी 196 लाख लीटर पाणी लागतं. हे पाणी तेलबिया किंवा डाळवर्गीय पिकांना वळवलं, तर त्याचा फायदा 31 लाख हेक्टर क्षेत्राला होऊ शकतो, त्यामुळे मराठवाड्यामध्ये उसाच्या लागवडीवर पूर्णपणे बंदी घालावी, अशी शिफारस विभागीय प्रशासनानं 2019 साली मुख्यमंत्र्यांकडे केली होती.
पण उसशेतीवर हजारो लोक अवलंबून आहेत. साखर कारखाने, ऊसतोडणी आणि त्याची वाहतूक यातून हजारो हातांना रोजगार मिळतो. त्यामुळे उसबंदी हा पर्याय नसून मराठवाड्यात ऊस शेतीसाठी पाणी व्यवस्थापनाच्या पद्धती सुधारणं आणि ठिबक सिंचनाचा वापर वाढवण्यावर भर देणं, आवश्यक असल्याचं मत जाणकार नोंदवतात.
यासोबतच, प्रत्येक गावामध्ये पाण्याचा ताळेबंद मांडून त्याच्या उपलब्धतेनुसारच पीक पद्धतीची रचना करणं गरजेचं असल्याचंही म्हटलं जातंय.
(बीबीसीसाठी कलेक्टिव्ह न्यूजरूमचे प्रकाशन.)

title: 50% More Lok Sabha Seats For Every State, House Capped At 850: What's Inside Delimitation Bill
description: The amendment would raise the Lok Sabha’s maximum strength to 815 members from states and 35 from Union Territories. It would also raise the maximum size of a state Assembly from 500 to 650 members.
author: Outlook News Desk
content:
- The Bills before Parliament’s special sitting propose a fresh delimitation exercise; they have not yet been passed.
- They propose a 50% increase in seats for every state and Union Territory, with the Lok Sabha’s maximum strength rising to 850.
- Women’s reservation—about one-third of seats, including SC/ST-reserved seats—would take effect after delimitation.
Parliament’s special sitting beginning November 30 will take up a delimitation Bill that proposes a 50% increase in Lok Sabha and Assembly seats across states and Union Territories.
The accompanying Constitution amendment would link constituency redrawing to the implementation of women’s reservation.
The Constitution (132nd Amendment) Bill proposes that women’s reservation take effect after the first delimitation exercise conducted once the amendment comes into force. It provides for about one-third of seats in the Lok Sabha and state and specified Union Territory Assemblies to be reserved for women, including women from Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes.
The reserved seats would rotate under a system Parliament would determine by law. The Bill says the reservation would operate for 15 years from the commencement of the 106th Amendment Act, 2023, unless Parliament extends it. It also provides that the membership of existing Houses would not change before they are dissolved.
Lok Sabha Strength Could Rise To 850
The amendment would raise the Lok Sabha’s maximum strength to 815 members from states and 35 from Union Territories. It would also raise the maximum size of a state Assembly from 500 to 650 members.
The Delimitation (Second) Bill requires a 50% increase in the seats allocated to each state and Union Territory in the Lok Sabha and in the total strength of their Assemblies. The proposed maximums are ceilings; the final seat count for each legislature would be determined through delimitation.
2011 Census Data To Guide Boundaries
The amendment proposes using the latest published Census figures available when it comes into force. It would replace the existing provision tied to publication of the first Census after 2026 and keep the resulting seat allocation and constituency boundaries in place until 2051.
The figures used would depend on what Census data had been published when the amendment commenced.
The proposal also revises constitutional provisions on SC and ST seats. Certain existing arrangements for tribal representation in northeastern state Assemblies would continue until a readjustment taking effect after 2051.
Commission To Redraw Constituencies
The Delimitation (Second) Bill provides for a commission to be set up by the Centre after the law comes into force. Its chairperson would be a current or former Supreme Court judge appointed by the Centre. The other members would be the Chief Election Commissioner or a nominated Election Commissioner, and the State Election Commissioner of the state concerned. The Centre would set the commission’s term and could extend it.
For each state, the commission would be assisted by up to ten associate members: five Lok Sabha MPs representing the state and five state legislators. Speakers of the respective Houses would nominate them. The associate members would not vote or sign the commission’s decisions.
The commission would determine seat allocations, SC/ST reservations and women’s reserved seats, then divide states and Union Territories into constituencies. The Bill says constituency boundaries should, as far as practicable, account for geographic features, administrative borders, communication links and public convenience. Each Assembly constituency would have to fall wholly within one parliamentary constituency.
Draft Boundaries Open To Objections
The commission would publish its proposed boundaries and invite objections and suggestions. It would hold public sittings in the states before issuing final orders. It could also summon witnesses, require documents and call for public records.
Once published in the Gazette of India, the commission’s final orders would have the force of law and could not be challenged in court under the Bill. The new boundaries would apply to elections held after publication, while the existing Lok Sabha and Assemblies would continue until their dissolution. The Bill would repeal the Delimitation Act, 2002.

title: Supriya Sule Clarifies NCP(SP) Yet To Take Decision On Delimitation Bill After MLA Says Party Will Support It
description: Awhad said the party’s support was based on the revised proposal cleared by the Union Cabinet, which provides for a 50% increase in Lok Sabha seats across states
author: Outlook News Desk
content:
- NCP(SP) leader Jitendra Awhad said the party would support the Centre’s delimitation Bill after meeting party chief Sharad Pawar.
- The party’s backing is tied to women’s reservation, a uniform 50% increase in Lok Sabha seats across states and Opposition representation on the Delimitation Commission.
- Supriya Sule will skip Saturday’s INDIA bloc meeting because her father is unwell; the party will send its MPs.
Soon after NCP (SP) leader Jitendra Awhad announced that the party will back Centre's Delimitation Bill, working president Supriya Sule clarified that the no decision will be taken before reading the draft of the bill.
Sule said that the party will make its stand on the bill clear on the floor of the Lok Sabha on Monday. "No decision would be taken without reading the draft of the bill. We will sit together and discuss. Awhad probably spoke in the context of 50% increase in seats and reservation for women," she said in a statement.
This comes after Jitendra Awhad said that the party will support the bill after meeting party chief Sharad Pawar, who is admitted to Breach Candy Hospital in Mumbai.
“Pawar saheb told me that as per constitutional provisions, delimitation has to be done. Supriya tai and the MPs have taken a decision. Our party will support the delimitation,” he told reporters.
Awhad said the party’s support was based on the revised proposal cleared by the Union Cabinet, which provides for a 50% increase in Lok Sabha seats across states while maintaining their relative share. “There is absolutely no confusion. It has been decided that we will support delimitation. We will support it,” he said.
Sule's Conditions For Party Support
NCP(SP) working president Supriya Sule had earlier set out three conditions for the party’s backing: implementation of women’s reservation, a uniform 50% increase in seats in every state, and adequate representation for Opposition parties on the Delimitation Commission, which will redraw constituency boundaries.
Sule said she would miss Saturday’s INDIA bloc meeting on the Opposition’s floor strategy because her father was unwell. The party will send its MPs to the meeting.
The NCP(SP) also issued a whip directing its Lok Sabha MPs to remain present in the House from November 30. The party has eight members in the Lok Sabha and one in the Rajya Sabha.
Sule To Miss INDIA Bloc Strategy Meeting
NCP(SP) working president Supriya Sule said she would skip the INDIA bloc’s meeting on Saturday, November 28, to discuss the Opposition’s floor strategy for Parliament’s special sitting. The Baramati MP said she would remain in Mumbai over the weekend as her father, Sharad Pawar, was hospitalised.
Cabinet Clears Revised Delimitation Bill
The Union Cabinet on Friday approved a Constitution amendment Bill linking women’s reservation to delimitation. The proposal provides for a uniform 50% increase in Lok Sabha seats across states while keeping each state’s share of seats unchanged until 2051.
The move comes ahead of the special sitting, expected to run from November 30 to December 3, and addresses a key criticism of the government’s earlier proposal in April. Opposition parties and several southern states had argued that the assurance of an equal increase in seats across states had been made publicly but was absent from the Bill.
Prime Minister Narendra Modi chaired the Cabinet meeting a day after the government announced the proposed dates for Parliament’s sitting. Parliamentary Affairs Minister Kiren Rijiju said the Bill would be introduced in the Lok Sabha on November 30 and urged the Opposition to participate in the debate.

title: Delimitation: The Battle That Could Pit North India Against The South
description: As South India opposes changes like delimitation and the push for Hindi, fearing a loss of political power and cultural harm, the  struggle raises larger concerns about fairness and regional rights in India
author: Outlook Bureau
content:
“Women and children have no part in war, yet they pay the highest price.”
—Leymah Gbowee, Liberian peace activist & Nobel Prize winner
In India’s ongoing North-South cultural divide, women and children have, as always, been drawn into the frontlines, not by choice, but by consequence. As southern states push back against fiscal injustice and linguistic imposition, a peculiar battle cry has emerged from Tamil Nadu: have more children.
At a wedding event in Nagapattinam on March 3 this year, Chief Minister MK Stalin urged people to expand their families as a strategic counter to the looming threat of delimitation. “I will not tell you to not have children hastily; have children immediately,” he declared, linking reproduction to political representation.
His message was clear. Tamil Nadu, and, by extension the South, must strengthen its numbers to retain its voice in Delhi.
But not everyone down South is rallying to the call.
Many women, in particular, question why they must bear the brunt of political calculations. “Do women have to pay the price for the wrong policies?” asks Shalin Mariya, a lawyer and feminist activist in Chennai. She likens Stalin’s call to the RSS’ long-standing rhetoric urging Hindu families to have more children. “He said it more than once, so this isn’t sarcasm. It’s an overreach into the autonomy and liberty of women.”
The resistance to delimitation isn’t just about numbers. It highlights growing fault lines in India’s federal structure.
On March 22, 2025, Tamil Nadu Chief Minister MK Stalin convened the first meeting of the Joint Action Committee (JAC) on Fair Delimitation in Chennai to address concerns over the proposed Lok Sabha seat delimitation based on population. The meeting saw participation from key leaders, including Kerala CM Pinarayi Vijayan, Telangana CM Revanth Reddy, Punjab CM Bhagwant Mann and Karnataka Deputy CM DK Shivakumar. KT Rama Rao, the BRS leader, and former Odisha CM Naveen Patnaik (via video call) also joined, along with representatives from the Yuvajana Sramika Rythu Congress Party (YSRCP), Congress, CPI(M), CPI and the Aam Aadmi Party.
Telangana CM Revanth Reddy warned that delimitation without equitable policies would be an irreversible injustice to the South. Karnataka’s Shivakumar echoed this, accusing the BJP of tilting power toward the Hindi belt. Union Home Minister Amit Shah countered, insisting in Coimbatore last month that “no (TN) seats will be lost.” However, without specifics, anxieties remain. The issue reached Parliament, where opposition parties staged protests against the Centre’s stance. Shah accused the DMK of scaremongering and using the Hindi imposition debate to “hide your corruption.” Opposition MPs, meanwhile, charged the government with attempting to suppress regional languages, deepening the North-South political divide.
The BJP-led Union government dismissed the JAC meeting as mere political theatrics, but the tremors of southern resistance are beginning to reshape India’s federal discourse.
At the heart of this pushback from the collective southern political leadership is a simple demand: fairness.
The JAC has called for a 25-year freeze on parliamentary seats and a system that rewards states for fiscal prudence and population control. But as the debate rages on, the larger question remains. Will the South’s fight for parity end in a truce or deepen the battle lines?
Seething South
Last year, in one of Tamil Nadu’s most high-profile electoral contests for the Coimbatore seat, signs of Southern rhetoric were already in play. The keenly watched battle between Ganapathy Rajkumar P of the DMK and Annamalai K of the BJP—who eventually lost by a huge margin—offered a glimpse into the South’s growing discomfort. At a joint Congress-DMK poll rally in Coimbatore on April 12, 2024, the stage itself was a replica of India’s older, now-defunct Parliament building.
The new and much larger Parliament building, the new apex temple of Indian democracy, can accommodate 888 Lok Sabha MPs and 384 Rajya Sabha MPs, compared to the old building’s capacity of 543 Lok Sabha MPs and 250 Rajya Sabha MPs. The anxiety among the South’s political leadership stems from this potential increase in parliamentarians after the long-drawn delimitation process concludes.
While natural barriers and geographic compactness are key factors in delimitation, the most contentious parameter for southern politicians is population. Will a more populous northern India corner more seats, despite its poor performance on social indices?
Kerala Chief Minister Pinarayi Vijayan termed the proposed delimitation a “Sword of Damocles” hanging over the southern states. “When smaller or less populous states lose political clout, their capacity to safeguard their cultural traditions diminishes. A homogenised Parliament dominated by populous states could sideline regional priorities, eroding the pluralism envisioned by modern India’s founders,” he said at the JAC meeting. He also stressed that federalism is not a gift from the Union but a right of the states. “Our collective resistance is not just about seats; it is a fight to preserve India’s pluralism and diversity.”
“It is an attempt to expedite the establishment of a theocratic state,” says MA Baby, a politburo member of the CPI(M). “Delimitation in its current form would only strengthen the BJP’s power in Parliament. Any single party gaining absolute dominance would be lethal to our democracy,” he warned.
Stalin described the JAC as a “national movement” for fair representation in the Lok Sabha, calling it a “historic day for Indian federalism.” On March 21, the day before the meeting, he posted on X that it was more than just a meeting. It was the beginning of a movement.
Stalin and the DMK have taken pole position in articulating southern angst over delimitation, pushing back against what they see as a raw deal for states south of the Vindhyas. Yet, within Tamil Nadu, the party faces criticism from opposition parties like the AIADMK, which mocks its stance. “Do you remember when DMK staged a protest against the union government? All the black flags have gone. When Modi came to Tamil Nadu last year, Stalin went to welcome him with a white umbrella. They do not want to antagonise the government,” says AIADMK spokesperson Babu Murugavel, referring to Stalin’s welcome for Modi in Tamil Nadu at the time. The reason? Enforcement Directorate (ED) cases against DMK ministers, claims Murugavel. The DMK calls the ED action a political vendetta. But while treading carefully, the party has managed to keep the ‘Centre versus State’ fire burning.
The Hindi Headache
Tamil Nadu’s resistance to Hindi stems from its strong Tamil identity. In 1937, EV Ramaswamy, alias Periyar, led protests against compulsory Hindi in schools. The movement peaked in 1965 when plans to make Hindi India’s sole official language sparked violent agitations, self-immolations and mass protests, cementing Tamil Nadu’s defiance against linguistic imposition. Now, the National Education Policy (NEP) 2020 has rekindled old tensions. Stalin rejects it outright: “Let BJP states teach 30 languages, just leave Tamil Nadu alone.”
But local opposition outfit, Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam’s deputy general secretary CTR Nirmal Kumar accuses the DMK of theatrics and not doing enough to take on the centre. “Where are the black balloons now?” he asks, referring to a unique protest in 2018 featuring ‘Go Back Modi’ slogans by the DMK during Modi’s visit to Chennai.
Meanwhile, Stalin’s son and Deputy Chief Minister, Udhayanidhi, has warned of another language war, while BJP’s Annamalai has called out the DMK’s hypocrisy, pointing to private schools that teach Hindi. The DMK contends that the NEP lacks legitimacy as it was never debated in Parliament. The battle over language, much like Tamil Nadu’s defiance, refuses to fade.
Fiscal Folly
Tamil Nadu, a key economic powerhouse, contributes significantly to national tax revenues but receives a disproportionately lower share in return from the Centre. This fiscal imbalance, driven by the Finance Commission’s focus on equity over efficiency, has long fuelled concerns over unfair resource allocation between industrialised southern states and their northern counterparts.
Tamil Nadu’s Fiscal Contribution and Devolution Share
Rs 6.23 lakh crore: Tamil Nadu’s tax contribution to the Centre (2014-23)
Rs 4.75 lakh crore: Funds received from the Centre (2014-23)
29 paise: Return per Rs 1 contributed
Declining Share in Central Tax Devolution
- 12th FC* (2005-10) – 5.305 per cent
- 13th FC (2010-15) – 4.969 per cent
- 14th FC (2015-20) – 4.189 per cent
- 15th FC (2021-26) – 4.079 per cent
*FC = Finance Commission

—Edited by Mayabhushan Nagvenkar
This article is a part of Outlook's April 11, 2025 issue 'Viksit South', which explores the growing north-south divide in India. It appeared in print as 'A Southern Storm'.

title: Maharashtra Congress Calls NCP (SP)’s Support for Delimitation Bill ‘Unfortunate’
description: The Congress also questioned the rationale behind the proposed exercise in the absence of a fresh Census.
author: Our Correspondent
content:
Maharashtra Congress Calls NCP (SP)’s Support for Delimitation Bill ‘Unfortunate’
The Congress also questioned the rationale behind the proposed exercise in the absence of a fresh Census.
Mumbai: The decision of the Sharad Pawar-led NCP (SP) to support the Narendra Modi government's delimitation bill is unfortunate and will help a ruling dispensation with an authoritarian mindset, the Maharashtra Congress said on Friday.
The government's intention behind the bill is not genuine and is aimed at further tightening its grip on power, Congress spokesperson Sachin Sawant said.
The Congress also questioned the rationale behind the proposed exercise in the absence of a fresh Census.
Asking why the 2011 Census was being used for the exercise when a fresh Census had not been conducted, Sawant cited delimitation in Assam, alleging that constituency boundaries were redrawn to suit the BJP's political interests.
"This is called gerrymandering. There is no doubt that the government intends to replicate this experiment at the national level," Sawant claimed. Gerrymandering is the deliberate manipulation of constituency boundaries to give a political party an unfair advantage.
Referring to NCP (SP) leader Jitendra Awhad's statement on (the party) supporting delimitation, Sawant said such a decision should have been taken at a meeting of the Opposition INDI bloc.
The INDI bloc had opposed the same bill earlier, the Congress leader pointed out.
Earlier in the day, Awhad, a senior MLA and NCP (SP) spokesperson, told reporters that Pawar had termed delimitation as a constitutional exercise that has to happen sooner or later. A decision has been taken to support it, Awhad said.
Questioning the reason for the change in the stand, Sawant referred to Leader of Opposition in the Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi's remarks that smaller parties were being pressured.
Emphasising the importance of opposition unity and collective decision-making, Sawant said, "Whether the NCP (SP) decision was taken under pressure or was driven by political calculations will become clear with time."
Asserting that Sharad Pawar's political journey had been associated with secular and democratic values, Sawant expressed surprise on the decision of the NCP (SP) to support the delimitation exercise.
The Congress has maintained that Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Home Minister Amit Shah want to carry out the delimitation exercise under the garb of implementing women's quota, and their ultimate objective is to change the Constitution.
The Congress' assertions came after the Union Cabinet, chaired by Modi, on Friday cleared the delimitation-linked Constitution amendment bill for early implementation of the women's quota law. The government is likely to bring it during the special sitting of Parliament beginning next week.
The government has called for a four-day special sitting -- November 30 and December 1 in the Lok Sabha, and December 2 and 3 in the Rajya Sabha.
( Source : PTI )

title: Delhi Govt Displays Kejriwal’s ‘Sheesh Mahal’ With Jacuzzi & Sauna
description: The "Sheesh Mahal" display comes just months ahead of assembly polls in Punjab, where AAP is in power.
author: Our Correspondent
content:
Delhi Govt Displays Kejriwal’s ‘Sheesh Mahal’ With Jacuzzi & Sauna
The "Sheesh Mahal" display comes just months ahead of assembly polls in Punjab, where AAP is in power.
New Delhi: The Delhi government on Friday put on display the bungalow at 6 Flagstaff Road in Civil Lines area where Arvind Kejriwal lived for nine years during his tenure as chief minister, accusing him of turning the official residence into a "Sheesh Mahal" fitted with a jacuzzi, sauna, massage table, lavish interiors and furniture and drapes worth crores.
PWD Minister Parvesh Sahib Singh Verma and Tourism Minister Kapil Mishra accompanied mediapersons on a tour of the 20-room bungalow, featuring eight bedrooms, two kitchens, a 'baithak' (lounge), a wellness suite and a gym.
There was no official reaction from the Aam Aadmi Party (AAP).
The "Sheesh Mahal" display comes just months ahead of assembly polls in Punjab, where AAP is in power.
Chief Minister Rekha Gupta said it was "necessary" to open the bungalow for public viewing, alleging that AAP looted Delhi and are doing the same in Punjab.
The bungalow -- BJP's prime target to corner AAP over alleged corruption during last year's Delhi Assembly polls -- was opened to mediapersons on Friday.
A large board bearing the words "Sheesh Mahal" has been put up at the entrance of the premises, spread over 1,905 square metres and maintained by the PWD. It mentions that Rs 58 crore was allegedly spent on renovation and interiors, and the property was occupied by Arvind Kejriwal between 2015 and October 2024.
In a statement, the government claimed Rs 82.56 lakh had been spent on the 11 televisions in the bungalow, including one kept in the lobby with a price tag of Rs 28.92 lakh and another in the lounge worth Rs 17.53 lakh.
It also claimed Rs 1.07 crore had been spent on drapes. Curtains for one master bedroom alone cost Rs 12.02 lakh, it said.
Every item on display has been price-tagged. In its statement, the government also mentioned the cost of most of the items procured by the PWD, along with their invoice numbers.
The staircase of the bungalow includes a designer ornamental railing worth Rs 25.16 lakh and a chandelier worth Rs 8.20 lakh, the statement said.
The first stop during the media tour was the 'baithak', where the sliding door alone is valued at Rs 2.4 lakh. The curtains are listed at Rs 7.94 lakh, the carpet at Rs 5.53 lakh and a lamp at Rs 2.66 lakh, the PWD said.
Across the lounge is an office or waiting area, with a centre-table costing Rs 6.79 lakh, single-seater sofas worth Rs 4.14 lakh and a chair valued at Rs 1.81 lakh. The curtains in the room are listed at Rs 16.96 lakh, an official claimed.
In the dining area, a table is listed at Rs 13.7 lakh and 14 chairs together at Rs 17.45 lakh, according to the government statement.
Two chandeliers hanging above the table are valued at Rs 23.12 lakh, taking the total fitting cost of the room to Rs 68.48 lakh, a government official claimed.
Attached to the dining area is a modular kitchen, with fittings listed at Rs 61.13 lakh. Its construction and interior work alone accounts for Rs 31.62 lakh, while a dumbwaiter, used to transport food between floors, is valued at Rs 7.2 lakh, he said.
The kitchen also features a double-door refrigerator imported from South Korea, costing Rs 3.17 lakh, a chimney valued at Rs 5.41 lakh and laundry fittings worth Rs 3.07 lakh. An automatic sliding door is listed at another Rs 3.07 lakh.
The ground floor also has two master bedrooms, with fittings valued at Rs 75.74 lakh and Rs 85.89 lakh, respectively. In the first, interior work is listed at Rs 34.50 lakh, curtains at Rs 12.01 lakh and a television at Rs 6.90 lakh.
The second master bedroom features interior work valued at Rs 33.70 lakh, a bed costing Rs 6.50 lakh, curtains worth Rs 5.84 lakh and a wardrobe priced at Rs 5.56 lakh. The total fitting cost of the room is listed at Rs 85.89 lakh.
A family lounge, also described as the middle room, has fittings valued at Rs 61.36 lakh. Its interior work is listed at Rs 24.01 lakh, while a round bed costs Rs 9.36 lakh, curtains Rs 5.38 lakh and a console table Rs 3.99 lakh.
The staircase is another section with a substantial price tag, with its total fitting cost listed at Rs 75.61 lakh. The inlay work is valued at Rs 42.25 lakh, the designer ornamental railing at Rs 25.15 lakh and a chandelier at Rs 8.19 lakh.
The living room lounge, meanwhile, has the highest listed fitting cost among the rooms on display -- at Rs 1.48 crore. Its interior work is valued at Rs 62.74 lakh, while a television cost Rs 17.52 lakh and a TV console Rs 13.19 lakh.
A temple in the lounge is listed at Rs 6.71 lakh, while an L-shaped sofa is valued at Rs 6.40 lakh and round centre-tables at Rs 5.65 lakh. The official said the total cost of fittings in the room is Rs 1.48 crore.
The two guest bedrooms had fittings valued at Rs 72.88 lakh and Rs 73.68 lakh, respectively.
In the wellness room, visitors could see facilities including a steam room, sauna and jacuzzi. The total fitting cost of the room is listed at Rs 31.75 lakh, with the steam room valued at Rs 11.38 lakh, the sauna at Rs 8.68 lakh and the jacuzzi at Rs 5.95 lakh.
Officials said the bungalow is expected to open to the public next month, with an online booking system. The entry ticket is likely to cost around Rs 20, while senior citizens and college students are expected to be allowed free entry.
The government has also announced plans to rope in a private hospitality firm to manage the property, which it intends to use for official conferences, lunches and meetings, officials said.

title: 39 Naga Ancestral Remains Return Home After Six-Year Repatriation Process
description: The remains had been taken from the Naga homeland during the British colonial period, largely between 1910 and 1940, by colonial administrators and collectors, and had remained in the museum for decades.
author: Our Correspondent
content:
39 Naga Ancestral Remains Return Home After Six-Year Repatriation Process
The remains had been taken from the Naga homeland during the British colonial period, largely between 1910 and 1940, by colonial administrators and collectors, and had remained in the museum for decades.
Dimapur: Thirty-nine ancestral human remains of Nagas, repatriated from the Pitt Rivers Museum at the University of Oxford in the United Kingdom, arrived in Nagaland on Friday afternoon.
The remains were brought to Dimapur from New Delhi, where they had arrived from the UK on November 25, marking the culmination of a six-year-long effort to bring the remains of the ancestors back to their homeland.
On arrival at Dimapur airport, the remains were received by representatives of various Naga tribes led by Naga Tribes Hoho (NTH) and the Forum for Naga Reconciliation (FNR), as well as other non-Naga communities extending a rousing welcome to the remains of the Naga ancestors that had been kept in a foreign country for more than a century.
A prayer service was held outside the airport after which they proceeded to Kohima for further rites.
The repatriation process began in 2020 after the Pitt Rivers Museum removed human remains from public display and initiated discussions on their future care and return.
The Forum for Naga Reconciliation (FNR) played a key role in facilitating dialogue between the museum and Naga communities.
In 2021, the FNR constituted the Recover, Restore and Decolonise (RRaD) team to coordinate the initiative through community engagement, participatory research, historical documentation and public awareness.
The process involved Naga tribal Hohos, elders, churches, civil society organisations and communities across the Naga homeland.
A series of consultations and dialogues were organised to establish a collective Naga position on the return and dignified burial of the ancestral remains.
A Naga delegation comprising tribal leaders and representatives also visited Oxford in June 2025 to formally advance the repatriation process.
In June 2025, a unanimous inter-tribal declaration, known as the Naga-Oxford Declaration, was presented, affirming the commitment to bring the ancestors home and provide them a common memorial resting place as a symbol of healing, reconciliation and Naga unity.
The University of Oxford Council approved the return of 39 ancestral human remains in July 2026.
The formal transfer of custodianship to the Naga people through the FNR and Naga Tribe Hoho took place at the Pitt Rivers Museum on November 9.
The remains had been taken from the Naga homeland during the British colonial period, largely between 1910 and 1940, by colonial administrators and collectors, and had remained in the museum for decades.
The return is being regarded as a significant moment of historical remembrance, restoration of ancestral dignity and reconciliation for the Naga people.
A public homecoming programme will be held at the NBCC Convention Centre, Kohima, on November 28 at noon.
Members of the public can pay their respects, offer prayers and lay wreaths at the venue from 9 am on November 29.
The final burial rites will be held at Naga Solidarity Park, Kohima, on November 30 at 2 pm.
( Source : PTI )

title: Vijayawada Metro HR Policy Should Address Long-Term Needs
description: VMC commissioner H.M. Dhyanachandra has called for a comprehensive HR policy to ensure the smooth operation and maintenance of the proposed Vijayawada Metro Rail project.
author: DC Correspondent
content:
Vijayawada Metro HR Policy Should Address Long-Term Needs
VMC commissioner H.M. Dhyanachandra has called for a comprehensive HR policy to ensure the smooth operation and maintenance of the proposed Vijayawada Metro Rail project.
Vijayawada Municipal Corporation (VMC) commissioner H.M. Dhyanachandra has stressed the need for a comprehensive human resources (HR) policy to ensure the efficient operation and maintenance of the proposed Vijayawada Metro Rail project.
He was speaking at a meeting with members of the subcommittee constituted to prepare the HR policy and manual for the Andhra Pradesh Metro Rail Corporation Limited (APMRCL). The meeting was held at the Command Control Room at the VMC headquarters on Friday.
Dhyanachandra said advance planning was essential to ensure the smooth administration and operation of the metro rail system after the project was completed and services commenced.
He asked the subcommittee to study recruitment policies followed by operational metro rail systems in other states, workforce requirements across departments, staff allocation based on corridor length, salary structures and other service conditions. He said these aspects should be examined in detail before framing a policy suited to Vijayawada Metro’s requirements.
The commissioner said there should be no shortcomings in recruitment, allocation of duties, administration and maintenance when metro services became operational.
He called for a long-term approach while preparing the HR policy and manual, taking into account the possibility of increased passenger numbers and future expansion of metro services. He said the workforce structure should be capable of meeting growing operational requirements.
APMRCL managing director N.P. Ramakrishna Reddy, Andhra Pradesh finance department representative J. Shivaiah, APMRCL director (Projects) Sahadev Singh, VMC chief engineer P. Satyakumari, city planner Sanjay Ratna Kumar and Nitin Kothari, representative of Ernst & Young LLP, Gurugram, attended the meeting.

title: Karrasamu Set for Khelo India Debut
description: The move comes as traditional rural sports and skills passed down through generations are losing ground to modern sports.
author: L. Venkat Ram Reddy
content:
Karrasamu Set for Khelo India Debut
The move comes as traditional rural sports and skills passed down through generations are losing ground to modern sports.
Hyderabad: Telangana’s traditional martial art, karrasamu (stick fighting), is set to make its national debut at the Khelo India Youth Games 2026, which the state will host from December 11 to 22. The government will organise demonstrations at the Telangana State Sports School in Hakimpet, introducing the art to young sportspersons and sports officials from across the country.
The move comes as traditional rural sports and skills passed down through generations are losing ground to modern sports. Once practised for self-defence, Karrasamu later became a feature of village festivals, jataras and processions. In some regions, it is also known as Karraseva.
The art calls for agility, concentration, quick thinking and coordination, as well as practice to maintain balance while performing rapid stick movements. It requires no expensive equipment or large playing field, making it accessible for training children in villages and helping them build fitness, confidence and discipline.
Sports Authority of Telangana (SATG) chairman Shiva Sena Reddy said Karrasamu has two main forms: alankaram (demonstration) and yuddham (combat). In alankaram, individual performers display speed, skill and coordination through a series of stick movements. Yuddham features two performers facing each other under prescribed rules. Both forms will be showcased at Hakimpet. Karrasamu has been included as a demonstration sport this year, with no medal competition, he said.
The Khelo India Youth Games feature traditional sports from across the country, including Mallakhamb from Maharashtra, Kalaripayattu from Kerala, Gatka from Punjab and Thang-Ta from Manipur. This year, Mallakhamb will have nine events; Kalaripayattu, Thang-Ta and Yogasana will have eight each; and Gatka will have six, bringing the total across the five traditional disciplines to 39.
The Centre has a dedicated component under the Khelo India scheme to promote indigenous, rural and tribal sports through equipment, training facilities and coaches.
The Telangana government is also seeking national recognition for the State’s traditional sports. Chief Minister A. Revanth Reddy recently unveiled an information booklet on Karrasamu during a review of preparations for the Games. The demonstrations are expected to help identify skilled practitioners in villages and create opportunities to train young people in the art.
After remaining largely within village jataras and festivals, Karrasamu is set to gain a national platform and showcase Telangana’s rural sporting heritage.

title: Elusive Goon Hurt In Police Encounter, Held In WB
description: A cyber crime accused, who had fled after opening fire on the police during a raid: Reports
author: Rajib Chowdhuri
content:
Elusive Goon Hurt In Police Encounter, Held In WB
A cyber crime accused, who had fled after opening fire on the police during a raid: Reports
KOLKATA : A cyber crime accused, who had fled after opening fire on the police during a raid at Asansol in Burdwan West of West Bengal two days ago, was injured in an encounter with cops and was arrested amidst a high drama on Friday morning.
Pratap Das, the culprit, was seen getting dragged away from a lane to a bylane at Ismail area in Hirapur and then carried by the gun-toting police personnel for his treatment. He was admitted to Asansol District Hospital with bullet injuries on his right leg.
On the way, Pratap was heard alleging, “I have been framed by Musafir. He gave me a contract to kill a man but I failed. So he did it.” His wife Rina however claimed that her husband got in touch with the police over phone through a relative on Thursday night to surrender.
She argued that the cops rejected his wish to appease the government which has been defending the trend of encounter. In the morning, a dramatic scene unfolded in the area. The cops in uniform and plainclothes were seen roaming around wielding revolvers. Suddenly sounds of firing gripped the locality before Pratap was nabbed.

title: India eyes price relief as Gulf oil supplies recover
description: A looming global oil surplus in 2027 could ease India's rising crude import costs, with Goldman Sachs forecasting Brent prices to drop to $78 per barrel, hinging on OPEC+ decisions and Gulf supply recovery.
author: Saurav Anand
content:
A looming global oil surplus could bring much-needed relief to India’s soaring crude import bill in 2027, with Goldman Sachs forecasting Brent prices to fall to $78 per barrel by December. However, much will depend on Sunday’s crucial OPEC+ meeting in Vienna, where major producers face a difficult choice between restricting supplies to support prices and allowing more oil into the market as Gulf exports recover from months of disruption.
The November 29 meeting assumes significance as India’s crude import bill surged 53.5% to $111 billion during April-October FY27, even as volumes rose just 2.7% to 146.6 million tonnes, according to Petroleum Planning and Analysis Cell (PPAC) data. With imports meeting nearly 89% of the country’s crude requirements, the production strategy adopted by OPEC+ could have significant implications for India’s oil import costs next year.
The Indian crude basket averaged $119.9 per barrel in October, compared with $65.08 a year earlier, underscoring the impact of elevated international prices.
Rystad Energy projects a global liquids surplus averaging around 5 million barrels per day (bpd) in 2027, equivalent to nearly 5% of global demand, even if Gulf supplies recover only partially. A surplus of this magnitude could put downward pressure on crude prices as supplies outpace consumption.
Goldman Sachs has also projected an oversupplied market, although its estimate is lower at 2 million bpd. The investment bank expects Brent to average $88 per barrel in 2027 before easing to $78 by December, as recovering supplies and reduced geopolitical risk premiums weigh on prices.
The forecasts raise a crucial question for OPEC+: whether to restrict production to prevent prices from falling further or protect market share by allowing more barrels into the market.
“Vienna will witness one of the most complicated OPEC+ meetings in years, and this time, the difficulty is structural rather than political,” said Jorge León, senior vice-president and head of geopolitical analysis at Rystad Energy.
At its 42nd ministerial meeting, OPEC+ must address two contentious issues: determining the sustainable production capacity of individual members and deciding how much oil the grouping should pump in 2027, with existing group-wide quotas expiring in December.
However, the grouping could retain current output targets for at least the first quarter of 2027, according to a Reuters report citing people familiar with the discussions, as disagreements over production capacity persist.
The challenge stems from the widening gap between permitted production and actual output following nine months of Gulf disruptions.
OPEC+ output rose from 31.3 million bpd in March 2025 to around 33.3 million bpd before the Middle East conflict, before plunging to 24.4 million bpd in April 2026. Production recovered to 31.1 million bpd by October, but remained more than 3 million bpd below combined quotas.
This means substantial additional supplies could enter the market next year even without higher production ceilings, provided disrupted oilfields and export routes resume operations.
Goldman Sachs expects Middle Eastern producers to adapt further to shipping disruptions, with an additional 3.8 million bpd of pipeline capacity projected to come online over the next year. Such infrastructure would allow more crude to bypass the Strait of Hormuz, reducing dependence on the strategic waterway.
Nevertheless, the outlook remains highly uncertain. Goldman Sachs estimates that Brent could reach $130 per barrel and average around $120 in 2027 if Gulf production remains substantially below pre-war levels. Conversely, stronger-than-expected recovery could push prices into the $60s.
Complicating OPEC+’s decision is the dispute over production allocations. Russia pumped around 8.4 million bpd in October against a quota of nearly 10 million bpd, while Iraq and Kazakhstan are seeking higher capacity assessments.
The UAE’s departure from OPEC+ in May has further weakened the grouping’s ability to manage global supplies. Abu Dhabi can now expand production independently, potentially gaining customers from producers that agree to restrict output.
“Every barrel OPEC+ holds back to support prices is a barrel the UAE can sell instead,” León said.
Saudi Arabia, meanwhile, has partially cushioned export disruptions by diverting supplies through its East-West pipeline to the Red Sea, while other Gulf producers face pressure to recover lost revenues and finance infrastructure repairs.
“For India, the eventual impact will depend not only on OPEC+’s production decision but also on the pace of Gulf supply recovery and shipping conditions. While a sustained surplus could reduce crude procurement costs, renewed disruptions or deeper production restrictions could limit the benefit,” said an analyst, who is tracking the sector.
“The Vienna meeting will therefore be a key test of whether producers prioritise defending prices or preserving market share at a time when the global oil market is moving towards a potentially substantial surplus.” the person added.

title: High oil prices cost India Rs 7 lakh crore a year: PM’s adviser
description: Elevated global crude oil and natural gas prices cost India Rs 6-7 lakh crore annually, impacting imports, transport, fertilisers, and essential goods, urging diversification and renewable energy adoption for energy security.
author: Saurav Anand
content:
Elevated international crude oil and natural gas prices are imposing an additional burden of Rs 6-7 lakh crore annually on the Indian economy, with rising import costs affecting transportation, fertilisers and essential commodities, said Tarun Kapoor, advisor in the Prime Minister’s Office (PMO), on Friday.
The government and oil marketing companies have absorbed a substantial portion of the increase in international energy prices to prevent the entire burden from being passed on to consumers, Kapoor said at the Confederation of Indian Industry’s (CII) 16th Energy Security Conference.
“Just this high price of crude and natural gas is costing us at least ₹6-7 lakh crore extra every year,” Kapoor said, highlighting India’s vulnerability to international energy markets.
The remarks come amid elevated global energy prices and disruptions linked to the West Asia conflict, which have sharply increased India’s import expenditure. Oil and natural gas account for around 35% of the country’s total energy consumption.
According to Petroleum Planning and Analysis Cell (PPAC) data, India imported over 293 million tonnes of crude oil and petroleum products in FY26, costing more than Rs 13 lakh crore. During April-October FY27, imports stood at 161 million tonnes, with expenditure reaching Rs 11.4 lakh crore.
Kapoor said diversifying suppliers and securing long-term contracts were necessary but offered limited immediate relief given India’s substantial energy requirements. He stressed the need to develop strategic storage capacity while reducing avoidable fuel consumption.
He noted that although storage could provide flexibility in procurement during periods of price volatility, the country could not build reserves sufficient to cover several years of consumption.
Referring to the Prime Minister’s appeal to reduce energy consumption, Kapoor said initial savings had been offset by rising demand from economic growth, higher incomes and increased transportation.
He called for structural changes in transport, including greater use of electrified railways for passenger and freight movement and faster adoption of electric vehicles, particularly electric trucks.
On domestic energy alternatives, Kapoor identified coal gasification as an opportunity to produce syngas for fertilisers and industrial applications, alongside carbon capture technologies to address environmental concerns.
He also called for expanding biofuels beyond ethanol blending in petrol to diesel, given its substantial share in petroleum consumption. Compressed biogas production, supported by capital subsidies and assured procurement under the GOBARdhan scheme, could help reduce dependence on imported gas.
Kapoor emphasised accelerating renewable energy deployment and pumped storage hydropower projects to improve grid flexibility and ensure reliable electricity supply.
PNGRB Chairperson Anil Kumar Jain outlined five key strategies for strengthening energy security: diversification of energy imports, securing long-term LNG supply contracts, acquiring equity oil and gas assets abroad, enhancing domestic exploration and developing transnational gas pipelines.
He further stressed the importance of encouraging greater industry participation, promoting competition in the energy sector, and accelerating the electrification of transport, households, and industrial processes, supported by renewable energy, to enhance energy efficiency and long-term sustainability.

title: Artificial intelligence opens up new opportunities for cooperation between India and Russia
description: Andrey Belevtsev, senior vice president and head of Technological Development at Sberbank, notes that the key factor for businesses is not the technology per se, but rather its impact — namely, faster processes and higher productivity
content:
Companies are increasingly integrating generative AI into their business processes and delegating a widening range of tasks to AI agents, from analyzing information and handling documentation to interacting with customers. For the Indian market — characterized by a combination of digital transformation, a large-scale local economy, linguistic diversity, and the rapid growth of technology firms — such solutions are particularly relevant. They help automate repetitive operations, personalize services, and accelerate the time to market for new products.
The AI Journey conference in Moscow will cover a comprehensive spectrum of applied topics, ranging from the global AI development agenda to highly specialized, industry-specific solutions that could prove valuable to Indian companies today. Russia and India have the potential to exchange both finished products and implementation expertise, sharing Russian computer vision solutions, speech interfaces, industrial AI, and enterprise AI agents, alongside Indian case studies on scaling digital services, fintech, logistics, and customer-facing platforms.
Andrey Belevtsev, senior vice president and head of Technological Development at Sberbank, notes that the key factor for businesses is not the technology per se, but rather its impact — namely, faster processes and higher productivity. This is precisely why cooperation between the two countries in the field of AI may evolve from a simple exchange of ideas into joint pilot projects, the localization of solutions, and the creation of products that are sought-after both across the Russian and Indian markets.
Andrey, this year’s AI Journey will bring together the world’s top experts and showcase the most relevant AI adoption cases. Why is this conference worth attending, and what should participants keep an eye on?
AI Journey is an opportunity to look beyond individual technologies and gain a comprehensive view of how AI is transforming society, business, and science. I invite you all to join the live stream. This year, the conference will bring together professionals from China, India, Serbia, Brazil, Kenya, Kazakhstan, Egypt, and other nations, giving us a chance to compare global trends with national approaches and actual adoption practices.
India’s experience is of particular value to us. The country possesses a vast domestic market and a mature Digital Public Infrastructure, including platforms like UPI, AADHAAR, and ONDC, alongside various government frameworks. Indian companies have demonstrated a strong capacity for building digital platforms and financial services for massive user bases. This experience provides valuable insight into how AI can be integrated into products and processes designed for large-scale adoption.
The experience of India and other countries will be showcased during the Business track. Participants will learn how companies transition from pilot projects to scalable AI solutions. The program covers AI agents, cloud platforms, industrial AI, and data infrastructure, featuring case studies from sectors such as construction, manufacturing, and retail. For Indian partners, this is an opportunity to evaluate how such solutions can be adapted to local needs, ranging from multilingual customer service and document workflow automation to supply chain management and the development of industrial enterprises.
Crucially, the conference is more than just an overview of technologies; it offers practical guidance on building AI infrastructure, preparing processes and teams for transformation, and turning AI agents into a source of business value.
What themes and technologies will shape the agenda for the Science and Business days, and what changes might they bring across industries and society in the coming years?
A central theme is the evolution of AI agents, meaning systems capable of responding to queries but also of executing tasks, coordinating processes, and working in tandem with humans. This is transforming product development, service operations, and the organization of business processes.
The Business Day will focus on practical solutions for key economic sectors, ranging from AI agents and generative AI to cloud platforms and industrial implementations. This is particularly relevant for India in financial services, retail, logistics, healthcare, and education, i.e. sectors where digitalization has already laid the groundwork for the rapid adoption of intelligent tools.
A highlight of the Business Day will be a presentation by Raul Aju, a 16-year-old Indian entrepreneur and AI developer, who will share how AI has helped him grow his business. Despite his young age, he is a student, a content creator with millions of views and over 500,000 followers, and an educator who has taught more than 500,000 people in schools and universities.
The Science Day will be dedicated to fundamental research and breakthrough designs, including generative models, agent-based systems, and robotics, along with their real-world applications. Special attention will be given to the role of humanoid robots in manufacturing, logistics, and urban environments, a prime example of how AI is moving beyond software to reshape the physical world.
Andrey, has corporate AI moved beyond the experimental stage? What is the best indicator of market maturity?
You shouldn’t look at the number of experiments, but rather at how regularly companies incorporate AI into their workflows, how the number of users is growing, and — most importantly — what measurable impact the technology delivers to businesses. A market reaches maturity when AI is no longer just a pilot but is instead integrated into the operational environment.
This transition is already underway. Sber currently has over a thousand initiatives involving generative AI agents, many of which have reached the stage of full-scale industrial deployment. Our product teams are implementing these agents where AI proves effective, and its impact can be quantified. In our corporate client contact center, for instance, AI agents handle a portion of the tasks, enabling us to respond to clients both faster and more accurately. This is a hallmark of market maturity: agents are being used on an ongoing basis, with a proven business impact.
At the same time, we remain open to collaboration with friendly nations, and India stands out as one of the most promising partners in this regard. Furthermore, India is a market where Sber already has a presence and is successfully growing its banking operations.
How do you assess the generative AI market? At what pace is it growing?
The generative AI segment is one of the fastest-growing areas. While the IT market as a whole is expanding at a rate of 20–25% per year, generative AI is seeing tenfold growth. According to our estimates, the entire market for generative artificial intelligence in Russia is set to reach RUB 1.8 tn by 2029.
AI agents that can be tasked with multistep, sequential workflows is one area of development in this market. For instance, GigaAgent can analyze a company’s financial reports, cross-reference the data, and draw conclusions. This provides the user with an analysis to support decision-making, while significantly reducing the time spent on preparation.
A major barrier to the widespread adoption of such tools is still the high cost of executing tasks. However, this cost is falling rapidly. In just a few months, we have reduced the expense of performing a given task with GigaAgent by a factor of ten. As the cost of achieving results decreases, an increasing number of AI use cases become economically viable for companies.
In September, you spoke about a new way of working with generative AI, shifting from a personal agent model to team-based collaboration and agentic development. What does this change for an individual employee?
In the past, being proficient with a PC was a distinct skill to highlight on a resume; today, it’s a default competency. We’re seeing a similar transition with generative AI: the ability to define a task, give the necessary context, and integrate AI into one’s workflow is becoming a foundational skill.
The next level involves tasking an agent with a sequence of actions — working with corporate data and systems — allowing AI to assist in executing entire workflows.
At Sber, we were among the first to recognize this, and we created GigaCowork, a platform designed to handle various tasks by leveraging a range of skills and tools. It integrates with documents, email, and other systems, providing a single interface instead of a dozen separate ones. The underlying systems remain, but the way you interact with them changes. Although it was only launched in May, the platform is already being used by thousands of companies and dozens of thousands of employees.
Another significant shift is agent-based development. Previously, creating any in-house tool — whether a dashboard, a calculator, or an application — required a developer. Now, a user simply describes the desired outcome, provides the necessary data and calculation rules, and the AI builds the tool itself. We are already advancing this approach with GigaCode. The next step is to integrate GigaAgent, GigaCowork, and GigaCode into a single interface.
Agents can also facilitate interaction between companies. For such scenarios, we are developing GigaNetwork, a platform for autonomous transactions between corporate agents. This solution could help Russian and Indian companies more quickly negotiate order terms, process documentation, and handle settlements. It is an example of how AI is evolving from a mere internal enterprise tool into an infrastructure facilitating international business collaboration.
Andrey, Physical AI is considered a central line of AI development. What will Sber present at AI Journey in this field?
Physical AI is the next step in the development of AI: technology ceases to be just a digital tool and begins to perceive the environment, make decisions and act in the real world through robots, unmanned vehicles and smart devices. Unlike classical robots with rigid scenarios, such systems adapt to conditions and learn from feedback.
At AI Journey, we will unveil new Physical AI solutions and continue the development of our line of humanoid robots, an initiative spearheaded by Sber’s Robotics Center. Our proprietary model, Green-VLA, enables robots to perceive their environment, interpret natural-language commands, break down tasks into specific actions, and evaluate outcomes. This model serves as the foundation for our anthropomorphic robot, Green.
For businesses, this is an opportunity to automate physical operations across manufacturing, logistics, construction, and urban infrastructure. Such solutions can also assist individuals in their daily lives, as well as in the fields of education and healthcare.
However, Physical AI demands a rigorous focus on safety, security, reliability, and predictability; the cost of an error in the physical world is far higher than in the digital realm. Consequently, Sber is advancing both the robots and the methodologies for training, testing, and safely integrating them. This commitment to the responsible development of technology could serve as another point of alignment between Russia and India, two nations that view AI not merely as a commercial opportunity, but as a vital tool for addressing challenges of national significance.

राजस्‍थान की जोजरी, बांडी और लूनी नदियों में प्रदूषण का मुद्दा एक बार फिर सुप्रीम कोर्ट की दहलीज पर पहुंचा. बेंच ने राजस्‍थान सरकार के ढीले रवैये पर नाराजगी जताई. जस्टिस विक्रम नाथ और जस्टिस संदीप मेहता की बेंच ने अफसरों के रवैये पर सवाल उठाए. कोर्ट ने कहा कि जमीनी स्तर पर काम नहीं हो रहा है. अधिकारियों को अब अपनी जिम्‍मेदारी समझनी होगी. पीठ ने सख्त लहजे में कहा कि अफसरों को कुंभकर्णी नींद से जगाने के लिए कड़े कदम उठाने पड़ेंगे. अदालत ने यह भी चेताया कि आदेशों पर अमल नहीं हुआ तो संबंधित अधिकारियों के खिलाफ अवमानना की कार्रवाई हो सकती है. सुनवाई के दौरान कोर्ट ने नौकरशाही की अड़चनों और काम में हो रही देरी पर भी नाराजगी जताई. पीठ ने अतिरिक्त सॉलिसिटर जनरल से कहा कि वे सरकार को इस मामले में सही सलाह दें.
अधिकारी कुछ भी करना नहीं चाहते
बेंच ने कड़ी नाराजगी जताते हुए कहा, ‘‘वे (अधिकारी) कुछ भी करना ही नहीं चाहते. उन्हें नींद से जगाने के लिए हमें निश्चित रूप से कोई कड़ा कदम उठाना पड़ेगा. हम लालफीताशाही या नौकरशाही की अड़चनों के कारण इस मामले को यूं ही नहीं जाने देंगे. यदि वे नींद से जागकर कार्रवाई नहीं करेंगे, तो हम उनके खिलाफ सख्त कदम उठाएंगे.’’ शीर्ष अदालत जोजरी नदी में प्रदूषण से जुड़े मामले की स्वतः संज्ञान लेकर सुनवाई कर रही है. पीठ ने बांडी और लूनी नदियों में प्रदूषण के मुद्दे को भी गंभीरता से लिया था.
नए औद्योगिक प्रतिष्ठानों की स्थापना पर रोक
जोजरी नदी जोधपुर से होकर गुजरती है, जबकि बांडी नदी पाली और लूनी नदी बालोतरा से होकर बहती है. बांडी और जोजरी नदियां बालोतरा शहर के पास लूनी नदी में मिल जाती हैं. मामले में अदालत की सहायता कर रहे वरिष्ठ अधिवक्ता बलबीर सिंह ने शुक्रवार को सुनवाई के दौरान शीर्ष अदालत के 26 अक्टूबर के आदेश का हवाला दिया. उन्होंने शीर्ष अदालत के उस निर्देश का उल्लेख किया, जिसमें राज्य सरकार को नदी पारिस्थितिकी तंत्र यानी इकोसिस्‍टम के आसपास या उसके निकट नए औद्योगिक प्रतिष्ठानों की स्थापना की अनुमति देने से रोक दिया गया था. यह रोक तब तक लागू रहेगी, जब तक बाढ़ के उच्चतम स्तर और बफर जोन का वैज्ञानिक तरीके से निर्धारण नहीं कर लिया जाता.
Advertisement
अवैध खनन की जांच के लिए एसअईटी
जब वरिष्ठ अधिवक्ता ने इस मामले में राज्य सरकार के जवाब का जिक्र किया, तो पीठ ने टिप्पणी की, ‘‘यह पूरी तरह से लचर कार्रवाई का मामला है.’’ उन्होंने बताया कि शीर्ष अदालत के 26 अक्टूबर के निर्देश के अनुसार, राज्य सरकार ने लूनी, जोजरी और बांडी नदियों तथा उनकी सहायक नदियों को प्रभावित करने वाले संगठित अवैध बजरी खनन की व्यापक जांच के लिए एक विशेष जांच दल (एसआईटी) का गठन किया है.
सरकार पाइपलाइन क्‍यों नहीं बिछाती
उन्होंने बताया कि अदालत में दाखिल वस्तुस्थिति रिपोर्ट के अनुसार, इस संबंध में कुछ प्राथमिकी भी दर्ज की गई हैं. इस पर राज्य सरकार की ओर से पेश विधि अधिकारी ने पीठ को मामले में राज्य के अधिकारियों द्वारा की गई कार्रवाई की जानकारी दी. शीर्ष अदालत ने बालोतरा में पेयजल की गंभीर कमी का मुद्दा भी उठाया. पीठ ने टिप्पणी की, ‘‘सरकार इस क्षेत्र में रहने वाले लाखों लोगों को पीने का पानी उपलब्ध कराने के लिए पाइपलाइन क्यों नहीं बिछा सकती?’’ शीर्ष अदालत ने इसके लिए नर्मदा नहर से करीब 100 किलोमीटर लंबी पाइपलाइन बिछाने का सुझाव दिया. पीठ ने कहा, ‘‘यदि केंद्र और राज्य सरकार मिलकर यह काम कर पाती हैं, तो यह इस क्षेत्र के लोगों के लिए बेहद सराहनीय कदम होगा.’’ शीर्ष अदालत ने इस मामले में आदेश पारित करने के लिए सुनवाई की अगली तारीख 10 दिसंबर तय की.

content:
परिसीमन विधेयक: शरद पवार की NCP पर कांग्रेस का शक गहराया, आखिरी वक्त तक सुप्रिया सुले का इंतजार
Last Updated:
Sharad Pawar Delimitation Bill: शरदचंद्र पवार (एनसीपी-एसपी) की सांसद सुप्रिया सुले ने कहा कि जब तक सरकार प्रस्तावित परिसीमन विधेयक का ड्राफ्ट जारी नहीं करती और संसद के आगामी विशेष सत्र का एजेंडा साझा नहीं करती, तब तक वह इस पर कोई टिप्पणी नहीं कर सकतीं. केंद्र सरकार ने 30 नवंबर से 4 दिसंबर तक संसद का विशेष सत्र बुलाया है. ऐसी अटकलें लगाई जा रही हैं कि सरकार एक संशोधित परिसीमन विधेयक पेश कर सकती है.
Sharad Pawar Delimitation Bill: परिसीमन बिल को लेकर विपक्षी गठबंधन ‘इंडिया’ ब्लॉक में दरार की खबरें सामने आ रही हैं. इस बीच कांग्रेस सूत्रों ने उम्मीद जताई है कि शरद पवार की अगुवाई वाली एनसीपी (एसपी) का साथ उन्हें मिल सकता है. कांग्रेस सूत्रों के मुताबिक, पार्टी आखिरी पल तक इंतजार करेगी और चाहती है कि सुप्रिया सुले खुद सामने आकर स्थिति स्पष्ट करें, क्योंकि संवाद की जिम्मेदारी वही संभालती रही हैं. हालांकि, सूत्रों ने यह भी साफ कर दिया है कि अगर एनसीपी (पवार) आखिरकार इस बिल के पक्ष में वोट देती है, तो कांग्रेस उन्हें ‘इंडिया’ गठबंधन से बाहर मानेगी.
कांग्रेस सूत्रों ने 27 नवंबर को बताया कि एनसीपी (पवार) के एक नेता के जरिए उन्हें यह संदेश मिला है कि पार्टी के ज्यादातर सांसद पहले से ही सरकार के संपर्क में हैं और इस बिल का समर्थन करने के पक्ष में हैं. ऐसे में पार्टी को टूटने से बचाने के लिए उनके पास सरकार का समर्थन करने के अलावा कोई दूसरा विकल्प नहीं बचा है. इस सियासी हलचल के बावजूद कांग्रेस खेमे को अब भी उम्मीद है कि सुप्रिया सुले स्थिति साफ करेंगी और एनसीपी (पवार) का कोई न कोई प्रतिनिधि 28 नवंबर को होने वाली विपक्ष की बैठक में जरूर शामिल होगा, क्योंकि इस बात का आश्वासन दिया गया है.
एनसीपी (एसपी) ने जारी किया व्हिप
दूसरी ओर, राष्ट्रवादी कांग्रेस पार्टी (शरदचंद्र पवार) ने 27 नवंबर को अपने लोकसभा सांसदों के लिए व्हिप जारी किया और उन्हें 30 नवंबर से संसद के आगामी विशेष सत्र के दौरान सदन में अनिवार्य रूप से उपस्थित रहने का निर्देश दिया. पार्टी के मुख्य सचेतक अमोल कोल्हे की ओर से जारी व्हिप में कहा गया है, “लोकसभा में 30 नवंबर से चार दिसंबर तक अत्यंत महत्वपूर्ण कामकाज होने वाला है इसलिए एनसीपी (एसपी) के सभी लोकसभा सदस्यों से अनुरोध है कि वे बिना किसी चूक के सदन में उपस्थित रहें और पार्टी के रुख का समर्थन करें.”
सुप्रिया सुले ने क्या कहा?
एनसीपी (एसपी) की कार्यकारी अध्यक्ष सुप्रिया सुले ने कहा है कि उनकी पार्टी इस प्रस्ताव पर विचार कर सकती है, बशर्ते सभी राज्यों में लोकसभा सीट की संख्या समान रूप से 50 प्रतिशत बढ़ाई जाए. पार्टी के लोकसभा में आठ सांसद हैं. सुले ने यह भी कहा है कि विधेयक पेश किए जाने के बाद उनकी पार्टी इस मुद्दे पर विपक्षी गठबंधन ‘इंडिया’ के घटक दलों के साथ चर्चा करेगी.
संसद का विशेष सत्र 30 नवंबर से बुलाया गया है, जिसमें महत्वपूर्ण विधायी कामकाज किया जाएगा. ऐसे संकेत हैं कि सरकार महिला आरक्षण लागू करने को परिसीमन से जोड़ने वाले संविधान संशोधन विधेयक को फिर से पेश कर सकती है. लोकसभा की बैठक 30 नवंबर को और राज्यसभा की बैठक दो दिसंबर को फिर से बुलाई गई है.
यह घटनाक्रम प्रधानमंत्री नरेन्द्र मोदी के 26 नवंबर को दिए गए उस बयान के बाद सामने आया है, जिसमें उन्होंने कहा था कि महिलाओं को न्याय मिलने से कोई ताकत नहीं रोक सकती. साथ ही, उन्होंने अप्रैल में संसद में परिसीमन से जुड़े संविधान (131वां संशोधन) विधेयक, 2026 के पारित नहीं होने के लिए ‘विपक्ष के एक दल’ को जिम्मेदार ठहराया था. इस विधेयक में विधायिकाओं में महिलाओं को 33 प्रतिशत आरक्षण देने का प्रावधान था.

राकेश रंजन कुमारराकेश रंजन कुमार को डिजिटल पत्रकारिता में 10 साल से अधिक का अनुभव है. न्यूज़18 के साथ जुड़ने से पहले उन्होंने लाइव हिन्दुस्तान, दैनिक जागरण, ज़ी न्यूज़, जनसत्ता और दैनिक भास्कर में काम किया है. वर्तमान में वह h...और पढ़ें

title: परिसीमन: 30 नवंबर को संसद में आएंगे 2 संविधान संशोधन बिल, 50% सीटें बढ़ेंगी और 33% महिला आरक्षण लागू होगा
